title: memVar: an integrated resource for interpreting human membrane protein variation in molecular and disease contexts
abstract: Interpreting membrane protein variation requires connecting clinical evidence to the membrane environments and molecular interactions that govern protein functions. Here, we introduce memVar (https://memvar.sunnylab.org), an integrated database of 10,906,688unique single-nucleotide variants from ClinVar, COSMIC, and gnomAD across 7,732 human membrane-associated proteins. memVar reconciles genomic, transcript, and protein coordinates to link variants with membrane topology, bilayer depth, lipid contacts, functional sites, partner-specific interaction interfaces, and variant-effect predictions, alongside disease, tissue-expression and regulatory annotations. Coordinated sequence, structure and variant views retain source provenance and distinguish clinical assertions, experimental observations, and computational predictions. Our analysis reveals that pathogenic/likely pathogenic missense substitutions are enriched in transmembrane segments and predicted protein-protein interaction sites relative to benign/likely benign substitutions, with pooled odds ratios of 2.47 and 6.67, respectively. IntAct-derived interaction loss or decrease was experimentally recorded for 57.9% of pathogenic/likely pathogenic substitutions versus 7.4% of benign/likely benign substitutions. CFTR examples contextualize the established G551D gating defect and prioritize W202R, a variant of uncertain significance, for tests of protein maturation, surface abundance and channel activity. By connecting variant records to specific molecular questions, memVar potentially supports mechanism-oriented investigation and prioritization of functional experiments.
authors: Xu Y, HUANG S, Zhao J, Sun J.

title: WheatPanRef: a unified linear pan-reference genome for wheat genomics
abstract: Linear reference genomes provide coordinates for read mapping, variant discovery and multi-omics data integration, yet assembly-specific coordinate systems limit data reuse, particularly in the large, repetitive and polyploid wheat genome. Here, we present WheatPanRef, a scalable linear pan-reference and coordinate framework that integrates wheat sequence diversity within a stable coordinate system. We reconciled independent Chinese Spring assemblies by resolving structural and sequences discrepancies to constructed a 14.50-Gb consensus sequences CS-NP. Using CS-NP as backbone, we incorporated 4.37 Gb of non-redundant non-CS sequences from 37 diverse wheat accessions, generating WheatPanRef (18.87 Gb). WheatPanRef improves read-alignment performance and captures putative wild-relative introgressions and sequences absent or unanchored in conventional references. Bidirectional coordinate-translation system enables accurate projection between WheatPanRef and individual assemblies without remapping, facilitating genomic resource integration and reuse. WheatPanRef provides a common sequence and coordinate foundation for population-scale wheat genomics, with potential utility for genomic resource integration in other complex crops.

title: An end-to-end in silico framework for truth-based validation and regression testing of clinical genome sequencing pipelines, from simulated reads to reportable findings
abstract: Clinical genome sequencing pipelines change often, and each change requires proportionate revalidation. Guidelines accept in silico data as a supplement but leave variant interpretation outside pipeline validation, and, to our knowledge, no framework tests a pipeline against a known truth up to the reportable finding, so report specificity is not measured. We present a source-available framework that tests a pipeline end to end, from sequencing reads to the report, against a truth fixed before any run. It plants expert-curated pathogenic and benign variants from the same genes, and optionally synthetic variants that no database holds, into the GIAB HG002 germline background and records the expected class and report decision of each variant. It then simulates reads and runs secondary and tertiary analysis as black boxes through exchangeable adapters. Findings are compared with the truth at the call-set and report levels, each failure is assigned to the first pipeline stage where it appears, and a variant-by-variant comparison of two runs serves as a regression test. We applied the framework to nf-core/sarek with DeepVariant and to the ACMG/AMP classifier BIAS-2015, using 243 ClinGen-curated variants in five test sets. Single-nucleotide variant recall against the HG002 benchmark was 99.5% on simulated and 99.3% on real reads, and every planted variant was present in the reads and called with the correct genotype. The report included 115 of 117 pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants (98.3%) but withheld only 106 of 126 variants that must not be reported (84.1%), mainly because variants of uncertain significance were upgraded and recessive carriers were reported. Without ClinVar-derived criteria, report sensitivity fell to 74.4%. Most false reports of one test set came from diploid calling of the male chromosome X, and haploid calling removed them without side effects. In supplementary experiments, indels were called completely up to 20 bp, and BIAS-2015 left 74% of synthetic loss-of-function variants unreported because it combined criteria by the 2015 rules. The framework measures report-level sensitivity and specificity and localizes regressions, so it can supplement validation on human samples and support change control.
authors: Dvorský B, Komárková M, Kollinová K, Klempíř O, Krupička R.

title: High-throughput sequencing of unmethylated DNA (UMR-seq) reveals extensive epigenetic variation in the hypomethylome of diverse plant species
abstract: ABSTRACT  The unmethylated regions (UMRs) in a genome can reveal the location of genes and gene regulatory loci. However, discovering UMR variation across and between entire genomes and disentangling the contribution of genetics and epigenetics to traits are challenging because they require separate and costly whole-DNA methylome and whole-genome genetic analyses. In many species this is prohibitively expensive for even a small number of samples, curtailing analysis on a population or breeding scale. Here we introduce UMR-seq, a method for the specific capture of UMRs from a genome and simultaneous sequencing of genetic variants in a single economical and scalable assay. UMR-seq charts the hypomethylome, revealing that it is highly enriched with functionally important regulatory loci. While UMRs are highly stable between vegetative tissues in plants, we find they are dynamic in the endosperm and vary substantially between accessions. Adaptable to diverse species, using this method we uncover a positive correlation between gene number in a species and UMR content, reflecting gene regulatory space in a genome. At 1/50  th of the conventional cost of methylome sequencing in wheat, UMR-seq enables simultaneous population scale analysis of genetic and epigenetic variation in the functional genomic space. We reveal that in a panel of 187 elite wheat cultivars, profiling UMR variation improved genomic prediction across population groups, and UMR-based association mapping identified trait associations that were largely distinct from those detected with SNPs, providing new opportunities to understand trait biology and to enhance predictive breeding.

title: Filling the gaps in Australian angiosperm genomes.
abstract: The Genomics for Australian Plants Initiative (GAP) reference genome project aimed to provide high quality angiosperm genomes for previously underrepresented taxonomic groups with evolutionary significance, cultural value, biogeographic importance, and concerning conservation status in Australia. Here we present the results of long-read genomic sequencing and assembly for 29 selected angiosperm species, including analyses of genome completeness, contiguity, ploidy, gene annotations, and repeat content. Plastid and mitochondrion genomes were also assembled and annotated. The data provided a diverse selection of genome size, ploidy and complexity, which were compared. The long read sequencing methods, PacBio HiFi, and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT), used in tandem and individually where appropriate, provided high quality near complete telomere to telomere assemblies. These genomes provide valuable genomic resources for Australian plants that will enable and extend research in evolution, conservation, functional adaptation, and comparative genomics.
authors: Allnutt TR, McLay TGB, Jones A, Edwards R, Holmes GD, Schmidt-Lebuhn AN, Andrew RL, Fowler RM, Jackson C, Lum M, Bruhl JJ, Ferguson S, Fournier-Level A, Lewsey MG, Roach M, Shaldoom T, Cantrill DJ.

title: Holistic integration of protein interaction datasets establishes a framework for exploring the organization and composition of Caenorhabditis elegans germ granules.
abstract: Spatiotemporal organization of biological molecules is a key driver of cellular processes, including many post-transcriptional epigenetic processes. The germline-specific germ granules are biomolecular condensates that act as hubs for mRNA and small RNA processing and are core regulators of germline gene expression programming. Germ granules have been studied extensively in Caenorhabditis elegans, and recent developments have led to many subdivisions of the germ granule into specialized compartments. Rapid advancements in microscopy and protein-protein interaction (PPI) screening techniques have produced a large amount of data towards characterizing the localization of proteins to specific granules. However, common methods used to probe PPIs are limited in their ability to robustly detect valid interactions, especially the multivalent and sometimes transient ones observed in granule environments. Here we perform a meta-analysis of granule protein interaction screens. While these experiments generally enrich for proteins matching the profile of granule-associated proteins, we find that when considering screens individually, reproducibility is surprisingly low, highlighting not only the variability inherent in these methods but also the dynamic nature of the PPI networks present in granules. We developed an algorithm to provide a measure of each protein's association with specific granules across various experiments (a "granule association metric" or GAM). By further clustering and investigation of the GAM matrix, we demonstrate the power of this holistic approach to provide deeper insights into germ granule organization, highlight novel candidates, and act as a resource to inform future investigations into granules and their constituent proteins.
authors: Wills C, Ashe A.

title: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction.
abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. Here, to address this, we present a framework that enables systematic genome-wide analysis of methylation and sequence-based prediction of context-specific methylation effects of variants. Our data-driven discovery of methylation classes reveals context-dependent roles for methylation across tissues, cell types and regions of the genome. The framework also includes Wreath, a deep learning-based sequence model specifically designed to accurately predict the context-dependent impact of any genetic variant on methylation. These developments leverage a compendium that harmonizes disparate methylation profiles from disparate studies including over 90 tissues and cell types. Using Wreath, we systematically characterized the impact of noncoding pathogenic variants on tissue-specific methylation, generating mechanistic hypotheses for individual regulatory variants. We make the full framework, including the compendium, the methylation classes and the model, available for use by the community.
authors: Mao W, Chen KM, Park CY, Theesfeld CL, Troyanskaya OG.

title: LOTUS: lineage-aware optimal transport reconstructs continuous clonal fate dynamics
abstract: Destructive sampling in single-cell sequencing obscures ancestor–descendant relationships, limiting the continuous reconstruction of cell-fate dynamics. Here we present Lineage-aware optimal transport for unbalanced single-cell dynamics (LOTUS), a framework that integrates time-resolved transcriptomic snapshots with clonal lineage information from engineered barcodes or endogenous T cell receptor clonotypes. LOTUS couples clone-level optimal transport with neural unbalanced transport to model continuous cellular state change, population growth and clonal propagation under lineage-consistent constraints. In branching simulations, LOTUS reduced lineage-inconsistent transport relative to benchmark methods, lowering off-target routing from 4.94–14.84% to 1.10%. On LARRY lineage-barcode scRNA-seq of hematopoiesis, LOTUS reconstructed branching trajectories, improved early neutrophil–monocyte fate-boundary prediction, and inferred multi-fate progenitors and fate-biased meta-clones, linking their distinct fate potentials to inferred epigenetic priming. On CellTagging scRNA-seq of fibroblast reprogramming, it distinguished reprogrammed from failed trajectories and prioritized fate-associated perturbation genes. In longitudinal scRNA-seq and TCR-seq of malaria-responsive memory (CD45RA-) CD4+ T cells, it preserved endogenous clonotype structure and reconstructed TR1 dynamics and regulatory networks. LOTUS thus converts lineage-resolved single-cell snapshots into interpretable, continuous models of fate dynamics and their regulatory programs.
authors: Lu J, Hou H, Zhang Z, Lin Y, Lin Y, Zhou P.

title: TSNR: Protein-Specific Signals with Broad Molecular Context for Spatial Protein Prediction
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures transcriptome-wide gene expression while preserving tissue organization, enabling prediction of spatial protein abundance beyond directly measured antibody panels. Such prediction draws on protein-specific transcript signals at the center spot and broader molecular context from the surrounding tissue. Existing spatial methods increasingly use context, but what molecular information the context should retain and how reliably it transfers across tissue environments remain unclear. We compare predictors that share a protein-specific center representation but differ in contextual molecular scope. Their transferred risk difference admits a value-mismatch characterization: broader context is favored when its target-side value advantage exceeds the corresponding change in source-to-target transfer mismatch. For convex prediction objectives, we further relate mismatch to cross-environment estimating-score variation; squared loss yields an explicit covariance geometry. This analysis motivates broad molecular context together with bounded-score robust regression. We develop Target-Specific Niche Regression (TSNR), which combines a protein-specific center representation, compact broad molecular context, and a protein-specific Huber regressor. On the six-section Spatial-CITE-seq benchmark, TSNR achieves the highest mean macro Spearman correlation among the reproduced methods under matched biological holdout evaluation. Controlled analyses support both broader context and robust regression. Across two independent external cohorts, protein-level broad-context gains are positively rank-correlated with the value-mismatch balance in all 11 held-out biological folds.
authors: Zhang X, Zhang J.

title: Comparison Study of Data Processing Workflows for Label-Free DIA Quantitative Proteomics.
abstract: Data processing tools for the data-independent acquisition method, rapidly gaining popularity in proteomics in recent years, are crucially important for this method's efficiency. Quite a number of them, serving both the identification and quantitation of proteins, have been developed over the past decade, yet the issue is still in its infancy, and the research on their comparison and integration is scarce. In this study, we collected four DIA search workflows─DIA-NN, DIA-Umpire, diaTracer, and MSFragger-DIA─as well as four protein quantitation utilities─directLFQ, AlphaPeptStats, Triqler, and simple t test─to evaluate the efficiencies of quantitation workflows integrating these tools in different combinations. The combinations were evaluated in terms of the number of protein identifications, differential expression sensitivity, fold change accuracy, and quantitative false discovery rate control, using two spike-in benchmark data sets. The study provides insights into the compatibility of the evaluated software pairs and practical recommendations for improving the data analysis pipeline for DIA proteomics.
authors: Postoenko VI, Gorshkov MV, Ivanov MV.

title: Benchmarking ZenoSWATH-DIA and Rapid-Gradient Workflows for Plasma Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics is the large-scale study of proteins. Mass spectrometry (MS) is one of the most informative techniques for analyzing proteins. Proteomics-based MS examines biological changes in diseases. It also identifies potential biomarker candidates in early disease stages, enabling the diagnosis, prognosis, and evaluation of therapeutic efficacy. Developing efficient and high-throughput proteomics techniques enables comprehensive exploration of the human plasma proteome. In this study, we compared the performance of various MS instruments and software tools for analyzing data-independent acquisition plasma proteomics data. We employed a "mixed species" approach, spiking three different amounts of Escherichia coliproteins into a constant amount of human plasma proteins to evaluate various LC-MS run length and data analysis workflows (DIA-NN and Spectronaut) for their ability to detect differential abundance. Assessing the power of the method to detect differences provides a more informative evaluation of workflow performance than relying solely on CVs. Our research shows that the ZenoTOF 7600 MS workflow, combined with DIA-NN in library mode, was most effective at detecting true-positive changes in protein abundance in our spiked samples. DIA-NN in library mode using the 21 min gradient method outperformed Spectronaut in detecting true-positive change. These results hold promise for detecting differentially abundant proteins in plasma.
authors: Alharbi H, Campbell A, Unwin RD.

title: Telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of the endangered Jacktree (Sinojackia xylocarpa Hu) reveals its centromeric landscape and evolutionary dilemma as a small population.
abstract: The endangered status of many plant species is often attributed to a decline in fitness, which drives a sustained decrease in population size under natural conditions. However, the role of highly repetitive genomic regions in the decline of endangered plants remains poorly understood. Here, we present the gap-free telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome for the endangered Jacktree (Sinojackia xylocarpa Hu). It has a genome size of 961.94 Mb, an N50 of 78.05 Mb, and 36 446 predicted protein-coding genes. Using CENH3 chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), we identified centromeric regions across all 12 chromosomes and revealed that S. xylocarpa centromeres are composed of diverse transposable element (TE) families, with long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons and LINE elements as major components. Notably, the right arm of chromosome 1 exhibited ectopic CENH3 enrichment and a TE accumulation similar to that of centromeric regions, suggesting the formation of a centromere-like chromatin domain. In addition, we detected inversion polymorphisms and inversion heterozygotes in natural populations, predominantly concentrated on the same chromosomal arm. These features may be associated with meiotic abnormalities. Using a high-quality T2T genome assembly, we identified a pattern of genomic erosion facing these small populations characterized by local suppression of recombination linked LTR proliferation and by the accumulation of deleterious mutations in DNA repair genes. This genomic erosion creates an evolutionary dilemma that impairs the purging of deleterious alleles, ultimately threatening long-term adaptability and survival. This study highlights the utility of T2T genome assembly for the conservation of endangered plants.
journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
authors: Liang SD, Zheng SS, Wu L, Liu A, Meng HH, Jiang Y, Wang ZW, Ge BJ, Zou WL, Wan Q, Dai XL, Kozlowski G, Li NW, Yan XL, Song YG.

title: IsoPrism predicts isoform usage from short-read transcriptomes through structure-guided competitive allocation.
abstract: Short-read (SR) single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterize gene expression but provide limited resolution of within-gene isoform usage. Here we present IsoPrism, a structure-guided competitive allocation framework that predicts isoform proportions from gene-level expression. IsoPrism combines individual expression and local expression context with transcript structural annotations, using shared iterative updates to preserve non-negative, gene-normalized proportions. Joint supervision from individual long-read (LR) counts and group-level isoform usage enables prediction in samples without matched LR measurements. Across five transfer scenarios derived from three paired transcriptomic resources, IsoPrism achieved the highest mean dominant isoform accuracy, compositional similarity, and cluster-level allocation correlation among eight evaluated methods. Ablation analyses supported complementary contributions from structural queries, expression context, iterative allocation, and dual-resolution supervision. Applied to a developing mouse cortex atlas, IsoPrism identified stage- and cell-type-associated isoform-usage patterns, including variation in the predicted relative usage of two Pkm transcripts. IsoPrism enables isoform-usage analysis of SR transcriptomes by transferring information from paired LR references, extending the analytical value of existing single-cell and spatial gene-expression atlases.
authors: Yan P, Liu J, Cui X, Liu X, Shi L, Cheng L.

title: ProteinExt3: Adaptive Fusion of Protein Language Models for Protein Function and Target Annotation.
abstract: Introduction/objectiveProspective protein function prediction requires evaluation designs that control for temporal leakage and sequence homology while accounting for the strong imbalance of Gene Ontology (GO) labels. We developed ProteinExt3 to integrate complementary sequence- derived evidence for GO-based protein function prediction under a temporally separated and homology-controlled evaluation protocol.MethodsProteinExt3 is a late-fusion framework that combines representations extracted from ESM- 2 layers 20 and 33, ProtT5 representations, 63 sequence-derived physicochemical features, and BLASTp homology transfer. Fusion weights were learned from out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, and final scores were propagated through the GO directed acyclic graph. The benchmark used experimentally supported GO annotations, a temporal split based on the earliest experimental annotation date, and MMseqs2 filtering between training and prospective test proteins.ResultsProteinExt3 reached Fmax values of 0.226 for Biological Process (BP), 0.547 for Cellular Component (CC), and 0.669 for Molecular Function (MF). Among the evaluated learning-based methods, ProteinExt3 achieved the highest Fmax in all three namespaces. For CC, the frequencybased Naive baseline retained the highest Fmax (0.569), whereas ProteinExt3 achieved higher AUPR and lower Smin. Ablation results showed that the effects of homology transfer, handcrafted features, and pooling differed across namespaces and metrics.DiscussionMost of the OOF gain came from combining prediction branches; optimizing their weights provided a smaller improvement. Component effects varied across GO namespaces and evaluation metrics.ConclusionProteinExt3 combines complementary sequence-derived evidence to support protein function annotation and downstream target prioritization.
authors: Wang J, Jiang P, Sun R, Chen X, Hou J, Si D, Zhang L, Cao R.

title: From long-term progeny trials to genomic selection: empirical prediction and simulation-guided redesign of Scots pine breeding in Germany.
abstract: In Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.), long generation intervals limit genetic gain, but mature progeny trials may provide reference populations for genomic selection. We combined repeated phenotypes from two German trials established in 1990 with single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotypes, parentage auditing, duplicate filtering, and empirically calibrated forward simulations. Of 1,986 phenotype-matched genotyped trees, 1,651 remained after quality control. Across 14 trait-by-age combinations, genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) gave modest but consistent improvements in predictive ability for diameter and volume from age 20 onwards. For volume at age 20 (V20), repeated leave-progeny-out predictive ability increased from 0.233 with pedigree-based additive best linear unbiased prediction (ABLUP) to 0.268 with GBLUP, and GBLUP exceeded ABLUP in all 20 matched partitions. Paired jackknife intervals did not establish systematic differences in narrow-sense heritability. ABLUP and GBLUP rankings were highly correlated, but only 75.9% of the top 10% V20 candidates overlapped. Simulations calibrated to empirical V20 variance components and family relationships compared phenotypic selection, ABLUP, progeny testing, direct genomic selection, and genomic selection followed by phenotypic thinning. After five cycles, progeny testing produced the greatest cumulative additive genetic gain (163.3%), whereas direct genomic selection produced the greatest annual gain (1.208% yr-1) because of shorter cycles. Faster genomic pathways accumulated more kinship, and a kinship-aware penalty reduced relatedness with pathway-specific effects on gain. These results support staged genomic implementation with continual reference-population updating, field validation, and explicit coancestry management.
authors: Degen B, Leite Montalvão AP, Schneck V.

title: OsGAT2 modulates nitrogen allocation and heading date in rice through amino acid transport.
abstract: Heading date (or flowering time) is one of the most important agronomic traits in rice, as it determines regional adaptability and grain yield. Its regulation is influenced by multiple factors, including photoperiod, nutritional status, and endogenous phytohormones. However, the roles of amino acids and their transporters in regulating heading date remain largely unclear. In this study, we identified four haplotypes in the promoter region of the rice amino acid transporter gene OsGAT2 among diverse germplasm resources. Haplotypes associated with lower OsGAT2 expression exhibited earlier heading date, longer grain length, and reduced nitrogen content. Further analyses showed that OsGAT2 is mainly expressed in basal tissues, stems, and leaf sheaths, and is localized to the plasma membrane. Substrate assays in yeast demonstrated that OsGAT2 is capable of transporting multiple amino acids, including GABA, Ser, Leu, Glu, Val, Gly, and Ala. Functional analyses revealed that knockout of OsGAT2 promoted earlier heading date, whereas overexpression lines exhibited delayed heading date. Consistently, the contents of GABA, several amino acids, and total nitrogen in the leaves and panicles were significantly higher in OsGAT2 overexpression lines than in the wild-type, whereas OsGAT2 CRISPR knockout lines exhibited tissue-dependent changes, with increased stem nitrogen content but reduced nitrogen content in leaves and panicles. Moreover, exogenous application of these amino acids further enhanced the delayed heading date phenotype in overexpression lines, while mutants headed earlier than the wild-type. Transcriptome analysis revealed that altered expression of OsGAT2 affects the regulatory network controlling heading date. The heading repressors Ghd7 and Ghd8 were significantly upregulated in OsGAT2 overexpression lines but downregulated in mutants. In contrast, heading-promoting genes, including OsGI, Hd17, and Ehd2, were markedly upregulated in the mutants. Taken together, these results demonstrate that the amino acid transporter OsGAT2 regulates rice heading date by mediating amino acid transport and modulating the expression of key heading regulatory genes. This study provides important insights and potential targets for shortening heading time and improving regional adaptability of rice through gene editing. KEY MESSAGE : The amino acid transporter gene OsGAT2 regulates rice heading date by modulating amino acid transport and the expression of heading date-related genes, thereby improving regional adaptability.
journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
authors: Yang X, He C, Ming Z, Wu B, Luo H, Huang W, Fang Z.

title: SSUplex: fast, both-strand extraction and origin-sorting of small-subunit rRNA for environmental DNA metabarcoding.
abstract: MotivationLong-read sequencing has made full-length small-subunit ribosomal RNA metabarcoding routine, but broadly conserved primers also amplify organellar and cross-domain sequences, which distort profiles when sent to a target-domain classifier.ResultsSSUplex detects small-subunit ribosomal RNA on both strands with conserved-region profile hidden Markov models, assigns each read to one of five origins (bacteria, archaea, eukaryota, mitochondria, chloroplast) and extracts the gene region. It reimplements Metaxa2's extraction step but ranks origins by summed rather than mean per-region score. On 5000 ZymoBIOMICS Nanopore reads, this raised accuracy from 54.9% for Metaxa2's extraction step to 95.9%, against 99.96% for Metaxa2's full pipeline with similarity-search classification. On reads simulated from sources outside the Metaxa2 database, SSUplex was 93 to 98% accurate for bacteria-dominated and plant-root-like compositions (Metaxa2's full pipeline: 96 to 99%), with mitochondria the weakest origin. In a rice-root 16S sample, about 40% of reads were organellar. SSUplex ran 3.2× faster than Metaxa2's extraction step from 200 000 reads upward, with about 45% less peak memory, and 65 to 134× faster than Metaxa2's full pipeline.Availability and implementationSSUplex is implemented in Rust and freely available at https://github.com/ayobi/ssuplex and from Bioconda; version 0.2.0 is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23246210.
authors: O'Brien A, Vargas Botia J, Acuña I, Restovic F, Martínez P, Parada P.

title: MultiPepGen: A conditional generative framework for the de novo design of function-specific antimicrobial peptides.
abstract: The accelerating global crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has intensified the need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Although antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics, their experimental discovery remains costly and time-intensive. Computational approaches have accelerated AMP candidate discovery; however, the ability to specifically target distinct biological activities remains a critical challenge for optimizing downstream experimental validation. Addressing this need, we introduce MultiPepGen, a conditional generative framework integrating adversarial learning with recurrent sequence modeling under explicit functional conditioning. Its architectural design is systematically examined through ablation analysis across recurrent variants. A multi-criteria evaluation framework combining distributional fidelity, statistical descriptor analysis, and external classifier-based functional prediction indicates that MultiPepGen preserves key distributional characteristics of natural AMPs while balancing sequence diversity with predicted functional enrichment. Crucially, our analysis reveals a potency-diversity trade-off: models selected for high classifier confidence exhibit a measurable contraction of the physicochemical descriptor space, whereas models favoring stable generative dynamics preserve broader exploratory capacity. Downstream candidate filtering identified top de novo candidates exhibiting high predicted potency and less than 45% sequence identity to the training AMP set, indicating substantial sequence-level novelty. By providing both an open-source implementation and an intuitive graphical interface, MultiPepGen offers an accessible computational pipeline for targeted antimicrobial peptide design.
authors: Orrego-Perez A, Mera-Banguero C, Orduz S, Branch-Bedoya JW.

title: SpaceBlocks: an expert-supervised workflow for cohort-level spatial transcriptomics analysis
abstract: Summary  Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has become a central tool in tissue biology, with multiple technologies addressing the issue from a different angle. Each platform imposes its own raw data format conventions, and few workflows address reproducible, scalable, cohort-level analyses while integrating expert-supervised decisions to strengthen computational and biological provenance. In this work, we present SpaceBlocks, a Snakemake workflow for reproducible cohort-level analysis of single-cell resolution-ST data that prioritizes expert supervision over full automation. SpaceBlocks homogenizes heterogeneous platform outputs into a common data format, whose structure is validated to ensure downstream processing. Comprehensive expert supervision is facilitated through per sample quality control and cell type annotation diagnostic visualizations, after which downstream analyses automatically follow. SpaceBlocks also allows the ingestion of technology-agnostic externally formatted data and provides interoperability with existing tools and technologies. We demonstrate the use of SpaceBlocks through the reanalysis of 37 samples from public Visium HD, Xenium 5K and MERSCOPE datasets. SpaceBlocks exhibited processing scalability across the three platforms. This reanalysis identified previously missed cell types in Visium HD and heterogeneous marker gene expression in MERSCOPE, highlighting the need for expert-supervised annotations. Moreover, SpaceBlocks facilitated the identification of differentially expressed genes associated with previously defined multiple sclerosis (MS) spatial domains in MERSCOPE, and transcriptional differences between healthy and malignant colorectal tissues in Visium HD. Together, these findings establish SpaceBlocks as a flexible and reproducible workflow for expert-supervised spatial transcriptomics analysis across technologies and biological cohorts. Availability and Implementation  SpaceBlocks is freely available under the MIT license on GitHub  https://github.com/cbib/SpaceBlocks and the official Snakemake catalog  https://snakemake.github.io/snakemake-workflow-catalog/docs/workflows/cbib/SpaceBlocks.html . SpaceBlocks v0.5.1 code, config files, and the public data formatting scripts used to reproduce the results from this study have been deposited in Zenodo (doi: 10.5281/zenodo.23378236).  Contact  macha.nikolski@u-bordeaux.fr ;  sergiooterino@usal.es Supplementary information  Supplementary information is available online. Conflict of interest: None declared.
authors: Oterino-Sogo S, Mechkouri N, García-Ruano D, Groppi A, Rezvani H, Nikolski M.

title: VaccineScout: A Computational Framework for Guiding the Composition and Valency of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Updates
abstract: The continual evolution of SARS-CoV-2 necessitates periodic vaccine updates to maintain immunity against newly emerging variants. However, vaccine design remains largely guided by experimental serological studies, and there is no publicly available computational framework to help systematically prioritize vaccine variants and guide valency selection. Here, we analyze over 14 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected globally between 2021 and 2025 and find that over half of spike amino acid sequences (primary vaccine target) observed during the first six months after vaccine selection were already circulating at the time of selection, compared with only 5-10% of sequences during the subsequent six months. These findings provide quantitative support for annual COVID-19 vaccine updates. We further show that circulating variant prevalence and open-source variant fitness predictors can both effectively rank circulating variants by their future prevalence. Motivated by these findings, we developed VaccineScout, a computational framework that recommends vaccine candidates by minimizing the average spike amino acid substitution distances to the forecasted prevalence of circulating variants. VaccineScout also helps determine vaccine valency by quantifying diminishing returns as additional variants are introduced. Retrospective analyses showed that VaccineScout-recommended candidates either matched U.S. Food and Drug Administration recommendations or had lower average spike sequence distances to future variants and higher fitness. In addition, their spike distances to future variants were comparable to an oracle selection informed by future prevalence, indicating near-optimal performance by this metric. Together, VaccineScout introduces an in silico framework for systematically prioritizing SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidates for costly downstream experimental validation.
authors: Gangwar P, Khanna S, Wertheim J, Lin B, Turakhia Y.

title: A linear-transformer hybrid for single-nucleotide polymorphism-based genotype-to-phenotype prediction in grapevine.
abstract: Robust genotype-to-phenotype (G2P) prediction is essential for accelerating grapevine (Vitis spp.) breeding decisions and genetic gain. However, it remains challenging to measure complex traits under variable field conditions and across years. In this study, we propose a linear-Transformer (LiT)-G2P, an automated predictive framework that integrates additive genetic variance effects with Transformer-based nonlinear interactions using genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) data. We evaluated LiT-G2P on a panel of diverse grape accessions, genotyped with SNP markers and measured for phenotypes across three consecutive years. Target phenotypic traits include leaf hair density and trichome density of grapevines. Across both single-year and cross-year testing scenarios, LiT-G2P consistently improves prediction performance compared with baseline models. For leaf hair density, LiT-G2P achieved the lowest prediction errors in both single-year and cross-year evaluations, with root mean square error (RMSE) values of 0.475 and 0.460 and ± 0.5 accuracies of 78.6% and 72.9%, respectively. For trichome density, LiT-G2P achieved RMSE values of 0.637 and 0.766 and corresponding accuracies of 62.6% and 58.2%. In addition, we extracted model-prioritized SNPs from attention weights and applied genotype-stratified analysis to provide interpretable candidate marker for downstream validation. These results support practical SNP-based predictive modeling for genomic selection and identify the remaining need for more detailed field data, larger multi-year grapevine panels, and independent grapevine validation before broader deployment.
authors: Wang Y, Jayakodi M, Kirubakaran S, Chandra A, Zahid A.

title: Should Dietary Planning Start from Energy? An Essential Amino Acid–First Framework
abstract: Amino acids serve functions beyond protein synthesis. Genetic information is expressed largely through proteins assembled from them; they constitute structural proteins, enzymes and immune proteins, serve as precursors of neurotransmitters and act as signalling molecules. Nine of them, the essential amino acids (EAAs), cannot be synthesised by the human body and have no dedicated store, so the diet must supply them every day. Nevertheless, dietary planning starts from an energy target, partitioned among carbohydrate, fat and protein, and assumes that EAA requirements are met within the protein allowance. We argue that dietary planning should start from the EAAs. An energy-first plan is easily met with energy-dense foods that often lack other essential nutrients, and can leave one or more EAAs below requirement. Such diets may meet the EAA requirements only when much more food, and therefore energy, is eaten. Under energy restriction, as during weight loss, and in older adults or those eating only plant foods, the same sequence can leave the limiting EAA short. Starting from the EAAs removes this dependence. Meeting all nine from a single food with a high EAA content takes 10–53% of daily energy (2,000 kcal) in our examples; the remaining energy can be adjusted to individual needs and goals. This sequence also fits physiology: energy requirements fluctuate from day to day and are buffered by glycogen and adipose tissue, whereas EAA requirements scale with body weight. A plan should be anchored to the more stable target, with the more variable one adjusted to it. The framework has four steps: Select, Combine, Complete and Adjust. It concerns the sequence in which a diet is planned, not the order in which foods are eaten; it is neither a high-protein nor a supplement-based diet and uses ordinary foods within any dietary pattern.
authors: Duygu A.

title: Hsa_Circ_0000615-Encoded 250-Amino Acid Polypeptide Suppresses Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Progression via Promoting HMGB1 Nuclear Accumulation.
abstract: Objectives: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) can encode functional peptides to regulate tumor progression, yet the roles of circRNA-encoded peptides in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the function of hsa_circ_0000615 (circ_0615) and its encoded polypeptide in EOC and explore its potential pre-clinical value as a candidate therapeutic target. Methods: We detected circ_0615 expression in EOC clinical tissues and cell lines. In vitro functional assays, in vivo xenograft and Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models with adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated overexpression were used to assess tumor-suppressive phenotypes. Mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, western blotting, immunofluorescence, and chromatin immunoprecipitation were applied to characterize the circ_0615-encoded polypeptide Zinc Finger Protein 609-250-amino acid (ZNF609-250aa) and its interaction with high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). Results: circ_0615 was downregulated in EOC tissues and cell lines. Circ_0615 overexpression suppressed EOC proliferation and migration in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circ_0615 promoted translation of ZNF609-250aa via eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit 1 (eIF2α). ZNF609-250aa bound HMGB1, reduced its ubiquitination, and promoted HMGB1 nuclear accumulation, which may contribute to repression of aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 family member A1 (ALDH1A1) transcription. AAV2/8-ZNF609-250aa restrained tumor growth in PDX models. Conclusion: Circ_0615-encoded ZNF609-250aa acts as a tumor suppressor in EOC, partially through modulating ZNF609-250aa-HMGB1-related molecular events. This study provides novel mechanistic insights and promising pre-clinical candidate targets requiring further validation for EOC intervention.
authors: Guo Z, Deng S, Meng J, Zhang X, Wang Y, Huang J, Li T, Liu M, Yang H, Chen F, Wang Y, Meng W, Wang S, Li Y.

title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica.
abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences between subgenome groups. Chromosome location, transposon density, and chromatin-associated features, including the proximity of accessible chromatin regions to genes and active histone marks such as H3K9ac and H3K27ac, consistently ranked among the top contributors to subgenome classification. XAI-derived covariation and interaction networks further revealed recombination rate as the central node connecting significant features. Together, these results highlight recombination and chromatin environment as major predictors of subgenome divergence in polyploid genomes.
authors: Schuster LA, Liu B, Silva JCF, Cheng X, Dias R, Zhao M.

title: Sequence-based coevolutionary prediction of species-specific interactomes.
abstract: Evolutionarily conserved protein-protein interactions (PPIs) reveal fundamental biological processes. However, predicting protein function solely from these interactions provides an incomplete picture of biological systems. Computational methods for predicting PPIs often struggle due to limited functional annotations in databases, making it difficult to fully understand unique biological systems. This study introduces ContextMirror2.0 (CM2.0), a coevolution-based method designed to address these limitations. Coevolutionary approaches, unlike supervised machine learning methods, do not rely on labelled datasets, proving valuable in addressing the scarcity of data for species-specific PPIs. Around 40% of CM2.0's top-1000 predicted PPIs for E. coli, S. enterica, and S. aureus are supported by experimental PPI databases. However, comparative analysis of the resulting functional communities further revealed both highly conserved interaction patterns and species-specific interactions. CM2.0 leverages coevolutionary information at the phylogenetic level to explore protein interaction dynamics and understand the functional consequences of species-specific variations. This information can inform further studies on the emergence of novel functions, adaptation to specific environments, and the development of targeted therapies.
authors: Fernandez-Martin M, Pontes C, Ruiz-Serra V, Valencia A.

title: Learning interpretable compositional features associated with continuous covariates
abstract: Compositional variation as a function of continuous covariates, such as time, presents challenges for learning interpretable features and accounting for their construction in subsequent inference. Motivated by temporal change in isoform usage in genomics, we introduce IsoVita, a statistical framework integrating covariate-informed balance learning designed for compositional data with complementary tests for abrupt and gradual compositional variation. IsoVita estimates a dominant covariate-dependent direction in the log-ratio coordinates and approximates it as a log ratio of their geometric mean proportions between two learned component groups, linking statistical evidence to explicit component membership. Change point and spline tests evaluate this interpretable feature, while a selection-aware permutation procedure repeats feature construction and testing under each permutation. In transcript-level simulations, IsoVita maintained low empirical false discovery proportions with power to detect differences and change point accuracy improving as temporal signals strengthened. However, the performance depended on trajectory shape and study design. Applications to two human brain bulk RNA-sequencing datasets identified widespread temporal variation in isoform composition while retaining transcript-level interpretability. IsoVita integrates interpretable compositional feature learning with inference along continuous covariates, with potential applications beyond transcriptomics. IsoVita is available as a PyPI package (https://pypi.org/project/isovita).
authors: Chen X, Hicks SC.

title: Deducing splicing events from transcript sets with splicelogic
abstract: Long-read RNA sequencing captures a greater proportion of full-length transcripts, enabling more accurate isoform identification, discovery of novel isoforms, and more precise differential transcript usage analysis. However, comparing transcripts, whether between conditions or between sets such as novel and annotated isoforms, yields complex isoform changes that are hard to manipulate, summarize, and visualize. This is compounded by vertical integration of some tools, where downstream analysis depends on the specific output of a particular upstream tool. To address this gap, we have developed splicelogic, an R/Bioconductor package that makes transcript-set comparisons biologically interpretable by turning them into discrete splicing events, such as exon skipping, alternative splice sites, intron retention, and alternative transcription start and end sites. We designed splicelogic to integrate easily with existing RNA-seq workflows and tools. The splicelogic functions are modular, readable, and extensible, making it easy for users to adapt core logic to their own custom scientific questions or novel splicing definitions. By obtaining interpretable splicing events from transcript changes, splicelogic enables downstream analyses, including annotation of RNA-binding protein recognition sites, alongside summary statistics and visualization. The splicelogic package is publicly available and distributed through Bioconductor.
authors: Campillo B, Love MI.

title: Molecular Classification of Breast Cancer Using a Cuproptosis Related Gene Panel and a Robust REO Ensemble Classifier
abstract: Abstract  Background  Cuproptosis is a mitochondria-dependent form of regulated cell death. Its interplay with cancer metabolism can modulate tumor aggressiveness. We hypothesized that cuproptosis-related gene expression defines distinct breast cancer (BRCA) subtypes and that a relative expression ordering (REO) ensemble classifier built on a 19-gene panel (CRG19) yields a technically robust, clinically translatable tool. Methods  We curated a mechanistically grounded 19-gene panel (CRG19) and analyzed primary BRCA RNA-seq samples from TCGA (n = 986, split into training n = 838 and testing n = 148). Consensus clustering (k = 3) identified molecular subtypes. From 171 pairwise gene relations, the top 100 discriminative REO pairs (chi-square ranking) were used to build an ensemble of four machine-learning models (SVM, Random Forest, Elastic Net, XGBoost) within a nested 5x5 cross-validation framework. Tumor microenvironment (CIBERSORTx), pathway activity (GSVA), and drug sensitivity (oncoPredict/CTRP2) were evaluated. External validation was performed on an independent cohort (GSE202203, n = 3,207). Results  Consensus clustering defined three reproducible subtypes (A, B, and C) with distinct biology and clinical outcomes (p = 0.035). Subtype A was enriched for basal-like/HER2-enriched PAM50 classes, showing pronounced cell cycle activation and poorer early survival. Subtype B was predominantly luminal with active hormone signaling. Subtype C exhibited a quiescent state and the best long-term prognosis. The REO ensemble achieved high probability calibration and stability between training and test sets (KS statistics 0.12–0.14). Subtype A showed higher predicted chemosensitivity, whereas Subtypes B/C were predicted to respond better to endocrine therapy. In external validation, differential pathway patterns across subtypes were highly reproducible (all-pathway Spearman r = 0.838–0.925, weighted direction consistency = 0.947). Conclusion  The CRG19 taxonomy defines biologically and clinically distinct breast cancer subtypes. The accompanying REO ensemble classifier provides a technically robust, cross-platform tool suitable for clinical risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making.
authors: Shi Y.

title: Educational framework to strengthen the variant scientist workforce in clinical genomics.
abstract: BackgroundThe integration of genomics into clinical care has created an urgent need for accurate, standardized variant interpretation. Variant Scientists (VSs) play a central role in translating sequencing results into clinically actionable findings, yet formal education and standardized training pathways for this emerging profession are still evolving internationally. This study aimed to describe educational needs of practicing VSs and to develop a structured training program informed by those needs.MethodsA national survey was distributed to practicing VSs across Israeli clinical genetics centers to assess training background, learning, access to interpretation tools, and professional challenges. Survey findings informed the definition of core competencies and the development of a phased training program by a multidisciplinary working group.ResultsThirty-eight respondents were included. Professional training was mostly acquired through observation of expert analysts (42.1%), followed by hands-on experience (39.5%). Only 18.4% participated in a dedicated VS course. Key challenges included keeping pace with evolving guidelines (55.3%) and copy number variant (CNV) analysis (47.4%). The survey identified substantial variability in training pathways and highlighted priority areas for structured education. Based on these findings, a structured training program was developed, combining theoretical modules, practical training, and assessment via a standardized proficiency test, supported by institutional forums and national meetings.ConclusionThis study presents a structured, scalable VS training program informed by a national needs assessment. By aligning the curriculum with identified educational needs, it provides a practical model that may support more standardized VS training and inform similar initiatives in clinical genomics internationally.
authors: Marek-Yagel D, Greenberg R, Naftali M, Isakov O, Ben-Shachar S.

title: OncoSpot enables benchmarking of cancer spatial transcriptomics methods across tumor evolutionary modes
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is increasingly used to map clonal architecture within tumors, yet methods for analyzing cancer ST data are difficult to evaluate because real tumors lack ground truth for copy-number alterations (CNAs), subclonal identity, and malignant cell fraction. Existing ST simulators model normal tissue and do not represent tumor evolution, CNA-driven expression, or the spatial organization of malignant subclones. We present OncoSpot, a cancer-aware simulator of Visium-like spot-based ST data. OncoSpot combines a spatial evolutionary scaffold from DEMON, CNAs generated along the resulting clonal phylogeny with CNAsim, cancer-type-specific malignant transcriptional programs, and spatially clustered nonmalignant cell types, and aggregates cells into spots with known malignant fraction, subclone, and copy-number profiles. We demonstrate OncoSpot on high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, which represent three distinct modes of tumor evolution. Simulated subclones were spatially clustered and showed stronger phylogeny–space concordance than those generated by scCube under matched subclone populations. Benchmarking CopyKAT, CancerFinder, Clonalscope, and RCTD revealed cancer-dependent performance: Clonalscope recovered copy-number signals more accurately in ovarian and colorectal cancer, whereas CopyKAT performed better in hepatocellular carcinoma, reflecting both the assumptions of each method and the copy-number landscapes of the three cancers. OncoSpot's ground truth also exposed a failure mode in Clonalscope's malignant spot identification, in which tumor and normal labels were inverted, and allowed us to trace its cause. These method-dependent behaviors would be difficult to detect in real data. OncoSpot provides a framework for benchmarking CNA inference, subclone detection, malignant spot identification, and normal spot deconvolution, and its modular design and guidelines allow extension to additional cancer types. OncoSpot is freely available at https://github.com/compbio-mallory/OncoSpot.
authors: Bhattarai P, Yuan W, Zhou XM, Mallory X.

title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction
abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17,951 domain and 1,383 site classes. Across 2.3 million held-out proteins, PALM achieved domain- and site-occurrence F1 scores of 0.941 and 0.877, respectively, and retained substantial performance in proteins with <20% sequence identity to the training and validation data. PALM also substantially outperformed ESM3 annotation baseline. Without training on variant-pathogenicity labels, PALM embedding disruption distinguished 151,823 ClinVar missense variants more accurately than ESM2 embedding disruption (AUROC 0.835 versus 0.710), and combining PALM embedding disruption with the ESM2 likelihood-ratio signal reached an AUROC of 0.877. The same combined zero-shot score outperformed AlphaMissense on a benchmark dataset on 128,161 missense variants, that were derived from literature but not present in ClinVar database. At the protein level, PALM embeddings showed stronger CATH-Gene3D superfamily organization than frozen ESM2 and ESM3 embeddings, and improved prediction of experimental activation and repression effects when combined with ESM2. In a downstream case study, we demonstrated the ability to use PALM-derived embedding as proxy of deep mutational scanning (DMS), showcasing the broad application of PALM. Together, PALM converts curated residue-level knowledge into transferable and mechanistically interpretable representations that connect protein sequence, function, and variant consequence.
authors: Wang P, Ahsan MU, Chen T, Wang K.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics of enriched rare neural lineages of  Tribolium castaneum
abstract: Background  Single-cell transcriptomic atlases have transformed our understanding of cell diversity. However, studies designed to profile entire tissues or organisms often omit or underrepresent rare cell populations. Enriching selected populations before sequencing offers a powerful approach to overcoming this limitation, but its application in insects has largely focused on  Drosophila , limiting opportunities for comparative studies. Here, we establish complementary workflows for targeted transcriptomic profiling of rare neural populations in the red flour beetle,  Tribolium castaneum .  Results  We developed two workflows combining population enrichment with single-cell or single-nucleus RNA sequencing. First, we generated cell suspensions from a transgenic reporter line labelling embryonic neuroblasts, enriched fluorescently labelled cells by fluorescence-activated cell sorting, and performed single-cell RNA sequencing. Second, we immunolabelled first-instar larval brains with an antibody against the nuclear transcription factor Rx, isolated and sorted labelled nuclei, and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Both workflows yielded material suitable for transcriptomic profiling, demonstrating complementary reporter-based and antibody-based strategies for accessing selected neural populations at different developmental stages. Conclusions  These workflows establish a methodological framework for targeted single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic studies of rare or specific neural populations in  Tribolium . They provide practical starting points for adaptation to other insect systems, expanding opportunities for comparative investigations of neural development and cell-type evolution.
authors: Cabañas N, Veloso A, Zinzen R, Bucher G, Mau C.

title: Spectral Adaptive Repositioning for Flow-Based Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
abstract: Predicting transcriptome-wide cellular responses to genetic and biomolecular perturbations is central to functional genomics and therapeutic target discovery. Existing methods assign gene positional encodings derived from arbitrary orderings or static co-expression masks built from unperturbed cells, and cannot capture the functional rewiring induced by perturbations. We present  SPEAR , a generative framework built on two complementary positional mechanisms. Spectral positional encoding grounds each gene’s position in the geometry of the co-expression network via continuous coordinates derived from the graph Laplacian. Adaptive repositioning then derives each gene’s position from its perturbation-conditioned hidden state at every layer, allowing the attention genes exert on one another to reorganize without explicit supervision. Evaluated on genetic, pharmacological, and cytokine perturbation benchmarks, SPEAR demonstrates excellent recovery of differential gene-expression, distributional structure, and perturbation-specific identifiability. SPEAR also captures latent positional relationships that closely map to known transcription factor-target interactions.  https://github.com/shouryaverma/SPEAR
authors: Verma S, Wang M, Kadadi S, Lanman NA, Mohammadi S, Grama A.

title: De novo genome assembly of the floating-hook moss Warnstorfia fluitans
abstract: The floating-hook moss Warnstorfia fluitans is a natural species dominant in subarctic and Arctic aquatic ecosystems. It is adapted to cold, acidic, and nutrient-deficient environments and possesses great potential for bioremediation by removing contaminants from polluted water in cold climate conditions. Here, we present the first de novo genome assembly of W. fluitans generated from pooled male and female gametophytes. The assembly is 725.04 Mb, has a N50 of 193.5 kb, a BUSCO completeness of 97.6% against the Viridiplantae lineage and 82% against the Embryophyta lineage. The whole assembly has Merqury quality value of 37 and Merqury completeness of 92%. A total of 30421 protein coding genes were predicted, with 78.62% completeness by compleasm and 87% OMArk completeness against the Embryophyta lineage. Repetitive sequences comprise 56.16% of the genome. We also present here the two complete circular chloroplast genomes and a linear mitochondrial genome of W. fluitans. This genomic resource will facilitate studies of ecological adaptation and a wide range of biological and evolutionary studies in bryophytes.
authors: Nguyen M, Galarza JA, Koskimäki JJ, Mian AH, Podolich O, Ahonen SH, Pirttilä AM, Lehosmaa K.

title: Unified cell segmentation for spatial transcriptomics via transcript reassignment
abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression as individually localized molecules on imaging-based platforms or as counts in subcellular bins on sequencing-based platforms, and both must be assigned to cells before cell-level analysis. Existing segmentation methods focus on delineating cell boundaries, yet transcripts that diffuse beyond their cell of origin, fall where cells overlap, or lie in bins that cells only partially cover are still misassigned. Here we present Tracel, a two-stage optimal transport framework that assigns spatial observations to cells under the guidance of a matched single-cell RNA-sequencing reference. Tracel first aligns reference cells to spatial cells to estimate the expected expression profile at each cell location, and then maps transcripts to cells against these profiles. The same formulation assigns transcripts from imaging-based platforms (e.g., Xenium, CosMx) and bin counts from sequencing-based platforms (e.g., Visium HD). Across five human datasets spanning three platforms and three tissues, Tracel improves the separation of cell types over existing methods, assigning cell-type markers to their correct cells, retaining more cell-intrinsic transcripts and reducing contamination from neighboring cells. Tracel also preserves variation within cell types, yielding more accurate differential expression across spatial locations, and its expression profiles attribute ligand-receptor interactions to the correct cell-type pairs in cell-cell communication analysis. Tracel can enter the segmentation workflow at different stages, either refining an existing segmentation or segmenting cells starting from nucleus segmentation. title: RNA accessibility sequencing reveals transcriptome-wide RBP binding and RNA structure
abstract: We introduce RAD-seq (RNA Accessibility via Deamination sequencing), a simple and scalable method that quantifies RNA accessibility by protein binding in vivo. RAD-seq uses TadA8.20-mediated adenosine deamination to report the local exposure of each adenosine to its molecular environment, integrating the combined effects of base pairing, RNA folding, and RNA-binding protein (RBP) occupancy in a single experiment. RAD-seq profiles recapitulate known structural signatures, reveal high-resolution RBP footprints, report on the influence of RNA modifications, and capture dynamic remodeling of RNA accessibility during oxidative and heat-shock stress. By integrating RAD-seq with RNA Bind-n-Seq motifs, we detected local enrichment of the RNA  N 6 -methyladenosine (m  6 A) methyltransferase recruiter TRA2A following knockdown of the exon junction anchor protein EIF4A3, revealing a potential mechanism that links RNA accessibility to enhanced TRA2A recruitment and m  6 A deposition. Extending this framework, we introduce an unsupervised statistical model that combines RAD-seq with motif priors to infer binding landscapes for multiple RBPs, reproducing the information from numerous CLIP-seq datasets from a single RAD-seq experiment. These results indicate RAD-seq as a generalizable approach for joint profiling of RNA structure and protein occupancy, defining enzymatic RNA accessibility as a new dimension to investigate regulatory elements on RNA.
authors: Li Y, Ye C, Ge R, Ju C, Xiao Y, Tang W, Chen M, He C.

title: Algorithm Verification of the Wind Power Generation Modelling System Using Scada and Open Meteorological Data
abstract: Reliable software verification is a prerequisite for developing information systems intended for renewable energy modelling. This paper presents an information system for modelling wind power generation together with a methodology for verifying its computational algorithms using heterogeneous data from open meteorological sources and operational SCADA measurements. The system integrates NASA POWER meteorological data, wind turbine technical characteristics, and SCADA operational records to calculate theoretical power generation based on the turbine power curve. The proposed verification framework combines statistical performance metrics, correlation analysis, empirical power-curve comparison, time-series analysis, and error distribution assessment to distinguish algorithmic errors from uncertainties caused by meteorological input data. Experimental verification was performed using publicly available SCADA data from the Penmanshiel Wind Farm equipped with Senvion MM82 wind turbines. The results confirm the correctness of the implemented calculation algorithms, achieving a correlation coefficient of r = 0.968 when validated against theoretical SCADA-based calculations. At the same time, simulations using NASA POWER meteorological data exhibited substantially lower accuracy (RMSE = 432.1 kW), demonstrating that modelling performance is primarily constrained by the quality of meteorological input rather than by the software implementation itself. The proposed verification methodology improves the reliability assessment of renewable energy information systems and can be applied to the validation of software tools that integrate heterogeneous environmental and operational datasets.
authors: Zaporozhets A, Verpeta V, Matushkin D.

title: From DNA Detection to Reliable Biodiversity Assessment: Methodological Priorities for Environmental DNA Metabarcoding in the African Great Lakes Region
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding can broaden freshwater biodiversity assessment by detecting genetic material released by organisms into water. Its value for conservation, however, depends on how confidently sequence detections can be linked to taxa and interpreted in space and time. This narrative mini review examines methodological priorities for tropical African freshwater monitoring, using the Lake Albert study in the Albertine Rift as a geographically direct example and the Rufiji River catchment in Tanzania as a comparative East African river-system case. A targeted, non-systematic literature search was used to identify these focal studies and methodological literature on reference libraries, marker resolution, eDNA transport and persistence, replication, contamination control, and taxonomic assignment. The review distinguishes two related but different identification problems: missing or unreliable reference sequences and markers that cannot separate closely related species even when reference sequences are available. It also explains why DNA transported downstream or persisting after release can indicate genetic material without proving that a living population occupies the precise sampling point. Practical recommendations are presented for interpreting negative controls, replicate agreement, and assignment confidence without imposing universal thresholds that are not supported across assays and ecosystems. The main contribution is a focused inference framework for moving from sequence detection to defensible biodiversity claims in the African Great Lakes region. Priorities for Rwanda and neighbouring countries include regionally curated reference libraries, spatially and temporally appropriate sampling, transparent quality assurance, conservative taxonomic reporting, and validation against complementary surveys.
authors: Habiyakare JdD, Niyonsaba D, Munezero V, I. Mudahunga O.

title: Pediatric nephrotic syndrome: a mini-review of genetic diagnostic methods.
abstract: Idiopathic nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a prevalent glomerular disease that presents as either steroid sensitive (SSNS) or steroid resistant (SRNS), according to whether complete remission is achieved following corticosteroid treatment. SRNS is by definition only diagnosed after a failed 6-week steroid trial, exposing children to significant adverse effects. Moreover, SRNS confers an increased risk of progression to kidney failure, prompting early personalized treatment. Accordingly, clinically actionable tools that identify SRNS at disease onset are urgently needed to enable early risk stratification and guide precision therapy-distinguishing immune-mediated SRNS, which may respond to intensified immunosuppression, from monogenic forms that are typically multidrug-resistant and warrant avoidance of ineffective therapies and earlier implementation of targeted management strategies. Advances in genetics offer the potential to predict steroid resistance at presentation, enabling a paradigm shift toward personalized care. Established clinical diagnostics such as whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing are increasingly complemented by emerging research tools such as genome-wide association studies, epigenetic profiling, proteomics, microRNA analysis, and polygenic risk scores, although these remain largely investigational and not yet routinely implemented in clinical practice. This review highlights current and emerging genetic approaches for early NS stratification and their clinical applicability. Furthermore, we analyze key podocyte genes central to NS pathogenesis (NPHS1, NPHS2 and WT1). NPHS1 biallelic pathogenic variants are the main cause of congenital NS, particularly in Finnish populations, while NPHS2 mutations mostly underlie early SRNS onset. Monoallelic WT1 mutations cause both isolated and syndromic SRNS and necessitate oncologic surveillance. Accurate variant interpretation is essential for prognosis, therapeutic decision-making, and genetic counseling. IMPACT: The current review highlights various genetic diagnostic modalities that can be used to detect and differentiate steroid resistant and steroid sensitive nephrotic syndrome in children. The review analyzes key podocyte genes and their role in nephrotic syndrome disease characterization and importance of variant interpretation for prognosis and treatment planning. The review discusses the emerging role of non-invasive biomarkers and epigenetic mechanisms in distinguishing SRNS and SSNS and predicting disease progression.
authors: Sathik N, Parashar S, Grden A, Hu J, Datta D, Sinha R, Chan EY, Boyer O, Raina R.

title: Multi-platform framework for mapping somatic retrotransposition in human tissues.
abstract: Mobile element insertions (MEIs) shape the human genome in both germline and somatic tissues. While inherited MEIs are well characterized, identifying somatic MEIs (sMEIs) in non-cancer tissues remains challenging due to their low allelic fraction and repetitive nature. Here, we present an integrative framework for sMEI mapping that leverages modern sequencing technologies and analytical innovations. We first benchmarked sMEI detection methods, demonstrating advantages of long-read and MEI-targeted sequencing for ultra-rare events, and established an effective cross-platform integrative approach using a mixture of well-established cell lines. Haplotype phasing and donor-specific genome assemblies further refined sMEI calls by distinguishing germline and false signals in in silico tumor-normal mixtures. We also developed a source-tracing approach based on sequence variation within MEIs, expanding the catalog of active source elements beyond traditional transduction-based inference. Applying this framework to benchmark donor tissues, we detected rare somatic L1 insertions in all four tissue types examined, revealing structural and source diversity. Our work provides a foundational framework and biological insight into somatic retrotransposition in the human body.
authors: Wang S, Bae M, Wang J, Zhao B, Nguyen K, Mallett S, Switzenberg JA, Losh SJ, Sexton CE, Miao B, Dong S, Zeng X, Wang Z, McDonald TL, Mumm C, Gadde RK, Tariq AM, Chen Z, Feng WC, Burn A, Park J, Chu C, Shen H, Wang T, Urban AE, Zhu X, Li H, Burns KH, Chun HE, Park PJ, SMaHT MEI Working Group, Boyle AP, Mills RE, Zhou W, Lee EA.

title: Volumetric Chest CT Report Generation via State-Space Visual Prompting and Clinical-Fact Alignment.
abstract: ObjectiveTo address the memory bottlenecks of 3D sequence modeling and the factual hallucinations associated with cross-entropy optimization in automated 3D chest CT report generation.ApproachWe propose an end-to-end framework that couples perception refinement with clinical-fact alignment. First, a hybrid perception module integrates spatial visual encoding with a bidirectional state-space model to capture global anatomical topology at linear computational complexity. Second, a lesion-aware visual prompting module extracts key pathological signals through cross-view synergy and adaptive residual gating. Finally, the text decoder is fine-tuned with the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) algorithm under an asymmetric composite reward, reducing its reliance on normal templates.Main resultsExperiments on the CTRG-Chest-548K dataset show that the proposed method achieves competitive natural language generation performance and, more importantly, a substantial improvement in clinical accuracy. The RadGraph F1 score increases from 41.89 to 44.63 relative to the strongest baseline, indicating reduced factual hallucination.SignificanceCombined with a 71% reduction in peak inference memory, these results indicate that the framework is a practical step toward deployable and clinically reliable automated CT interpretation.
authors: Li Z, Yang D, Li R, Zhang J.

title: Investigating the Distinctive Clinical and Genetic Landscape of PPA2 Deficiency.
abstract: BackgroundPPA2 encodes for inorganic pyrophosphatase 2, a mitochondrial enzyme that hydrolyzes inorganic pyrophosphates into orthophosphate. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause PPA2 deficiency, an emerging recessive cardiac condition that causes heart failure and sudden cardiac death in infants and young people.MethodsUsing published case reports and large-scale genomics resources, we defined the clinical and molecular spectrum of this disease, classified variants using a customized American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics pipeline, assessed genotype-phenotype correlations, calculated predicted prevalence using the gnomAD GenIE tool, and investigated monoallelic associations in the UK Biobank.ResultsA total of 63 cases from 37 families were identified from 12 publications. The natural history of this disease is characterized by clinical heterogeneity and high mortality (79% by 20 years of age), typically presenting as a highly arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with 2 distinct risk periods: in infancy, where viral infections can lead to heart failure, and in adolescence, where minimal alcohol exposure can trigger sudden cardiac death. The disease is genetically heterogeneous, with 29 distinct variants described (18 of which were classified as [likely] pathogenic), usually in compound heterozygosity. As complete gene knockout appears to be incompatible with life, PPA2 deficiency is caused by biallelic variants within a particular loss-of-function window, with deficiency mitigated by hypomorphic effects, variants in nonconstitutive exons, and particular compound heterozygous combinations. The spectrum of phenotypic effect extends to monoallelic carriers of pathogenic variants, which demonstrate an apparent mitohormesis-like compensatory protection from heart failure. The disease has an estimated prevalence of at least 1/135 000 in European ancestry populations.ConclusionsPPA2 deficiency is a genetically complex and clinically severe disease. Given the potential for effective life-saving interventions, PPA2 may warrant inclusion in emerging newborn genomic screening programs.
authors: Low BSH, Corver ME, Lipov A, Wardle JPR, Mazzarotto F, Bezzina CR, Behr ER, Jurgens SJ, Carroll CJ, Walsh R.
