title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals a selectively enriched surface metabolome underpinning constitutive chemical defence in the red alga  Halymenia floresii  (Clemente) C.Agardh, 1817 ((Rhodophyta, Halymeniales)
abstract: Marine macroalgae rely on chemically mediated surface defences to prevent microbial colonization and fouling, yet the composition of surface-associated metabolites and their ecological roles remain poorly understood. In this study, untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS)-based metabolomics was used to characterize the surface-associated metabolome of the tropical red macroalga  Halymenia floresii and identify metabolites potentially involved in chemical defence. Selective dipping extraction (DIP) was used to recover surface-associated metabolites and compared with whole-cell metabolome (WCM) extracts. Across both datasets, 22,455 LC– MS features were detected, including 10,505 features in the surface extracts and 11,495 additional features detected only in the WCM extracts. Statistical filtering identified 722 LC–MS features consistently enriched by at least four-fold in surface extracts relative to WCM extracts. These features yielded 928 putative metabolite annotations using xMSannotator, with biological interpretation supported by KEGG, LIPID MAPS, and MassBank. Pathway reconstruction using the Lilikoi R package identified 44 metabolite–pathway associations, predominantly involving lipid-associated metabolism, including steroidogenesis, arachidonic acid metabolism, plasmalogen synthesis, fatty acid biosynthesis, sphingolipid metabolism and sterol biosynthesis. Manual curation further indicated enrichment of fatty acids, oxylipin-like metabolites, sphingolipids, phospholipid precursors and isoprenoid intermediates at the algal surface. Rather than indicating the presence of metabolites unique to the surface, the findings suggest that  H. floresii selectively enriches lipid-associated metabolites at the thallus–seawater interface. Spatial localization of relatively hydrophobic metabolites may provide an energetically efficient chemical defence strategy by retaining bioactive compounds at the site where microbial attachment and biofilm formation are initiated while minimizing their loss to the surrounding seawater. Overall, this study demonstrates that chemical defence in  H. floresii is associated with the selective surface enrichment of lipid-associated metabolites rather than the occurrence of unique surface-specific compounds, providing new insights into the spatial organization of macroalgal chemical defences and the mechanisms underlying resistance to microbial colonization and fouling. authors: A Abdul Malik S, Bedoux G, Freile-Pelegrín Y, Bourgougnon N, Robledo D.

title: Multivariate genetic analysis maps shared biology between psoriasis and cardiovascular diseases
abstract: Psoriasis is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity, but the extent and structure of the shared genetic architecture remain incompletely understood. We integrated large-scale European-ancestry genome-wide summary statistics for psoriasis and seven cardiovascular diseases to quantify genetic overlap, model shared liability and prioritize candidate mechanisms. Psoriasis showed modest genetic correlations with all cardiovascular outcomes, but mixture modelling estimated that more than half of psoriasis-associated non-zero variants were shared with five cardiovascular diseases. Genomic structural equation modelling of a latent psoriasis-CVD factor identified 167 independent risk loci, including 50 not genome-wide significant in any component trait. Multimodal prioritization nominated 473 candidate genes and 90 approved compounds with therapeutic relevance, including shared targets involving PDE4B, GLP1R, KEAP1 and PRDM16. Mediation and Mendelian randomization analyses implicated cardiometabolic traits, although no single trait accounted for more than half of the shared liability. These results prioritize genetic mechanisms and pharmacological hypotheses for psoriasis-associated cardiovascular multimorbidity.
authors: Antonatos C, Georgalaki E, Tzoulaki I, Vasilopoulos Y.

title: Impact of runoff and surrounding land use on microbial communities within a confined lake system
abstract: Runoff from urban and agricultural environments can differentially impact aquatic ecosystems by introducing excess nutrients, pollutants, or other contaminants of emerging concern. This runoff can alter chemical and microbial balances within these aquatic systems and lead to long-term degradation of the ecosystem health. In order to gain a better understanding of how land usage impacts aquatic ecosystems, we sampled at the Shangrila-Benet Lake system in southern Wisconsin which has no natural inlets other than runoff after rain events. By characterizing microbial communities and physiochemical parameters before and after a rain event at three sites within a single body of water, each with distinct surrounding land usage, we tested how the runoff water quality is impacted by surrounding land use, and how this runoff in turn can impact microbial community populations. We hypothesized that runoff from urban land use would contain more human-associated microorganisms while runoff from agricultural use would reflect nutrients applied to those fields. We found that, following a rain event, small variations in water quality parameters were present when comparing between sites and seasons, and these variations correlated with shifts in the microbial composition.
authors: Shatara FJ, Mellgren C, Oppenheimer AM, Majumder EL.

title: Targeting the p53–TFAM Axis to Overcome Exercise Intolerance in Long COVID
abstract: Abstract  Over 400 million Long COVID patients worldwide suffer from chronic fatigue and Post-Exertional Malaise (PEM), yet the precise molecular drivers of exercise capacity collapse remain unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 accessory factors and exertional stress establish a persistent EZH2 (H3K27me3) and PAK2–c-Myc loop that targets host tumor suppressor p53 for degradation via viral-activated p21- activated kinase 2 (PAK2) networks. Downstream, the loss of p53 halts its essential transactivation of the Mitochondrial Transcription Factor A (TFAM) promoter, depleting mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number, uncoupling cytochrome c oxidase (COX) complex assembly, and driving a ∼ 50% loss of exercise capacity alongside H4K12la histone lactylation and Gasdermin D (GSDMD-N) pyroptosis. To resolve this bioenergetic lock, we propose the host-directed p53/NRF2 Epigenetic Shield. Co-activation of p53 and NRF2 forcefully re-engages the TFAM promoter, drives TAp73–OPA1 inner cristae rebuilding, silences the NLRP3 inflammasome, and restores 100% ATP generation capacity, providing a definitive computational and mechanistic cure for post-viral exercise failure.
authors: Lakshmanane B.

title: Candida albicans forms azole-resistant liquid-suspension biofilms with distinct characteristics and a potential to aid in dispersal
abstract: Abstract    Candida albicans  is a WHO “  critical priority  ” human fungal pathogen for which biofilm formation on the surface of medical devices is associated with bloodstream infections and antifungal drug resistance. Our understanding of  C. albicans  biofilms is based primarily on studies of surface-adhered biofilms, while the full spectrum of biofilm morphologies that  C. albicans  may use to persist in the host remains underexplored. Here we show that  C. albicans  forms liquid-suspension biofilms when faced with a poorly adherent surface, or following prolonged maturation of surface-adhered biofilms which exhausts available surface for attachment.  C. albicans  liquid-suspension biofilms are resistant to the front-line antifungal drug fluconazole and display a complex structure consisting of dense clusters of heterogeneous cell morphologies (hyphal, pseudohyphal and yeast cells) connected to one another through extensive hyphal networks. Liquid-suspension biofilms share transcriptional programs with surface-adhered biofilms and are controlled by the same set of master transcriptional regulators. The transcriptomic profiles of liquid-suspension and surface-adhered biofilms converge over time. Moreover, after transfer to plastic surfaces, liquid-suspension biofilms can seed new surface-adhered biofilm growth. Our study characterises a previously unappreciated suspension biofilm morphology of  C. albicans  , shows that this is a  bona fide  drug-resistant biofilm with regulatory properties shared with canonical surface-adhered biofilms, and demonstrates that  C. albicans  transitions between surface-adhered and liquid-suspension biofilms depending on surface availability. Our findings establish  C. albicans  liquid-suspension biofilms as a distinct biofilm morphology that is functionally tied to surface-adhered biofilms and could serve as an antifungal- and immune-resistant dispersal mechanism.
authors: Olivier FA, Renshaw JL, Kraupner-Taylor C, Swaminathan A, Harrison PF, Beilharz TH, Traven A.

title: Multiple Protein Isoforms with Isoelectric Point in the Blood pH Physiological Range May Underpin High Virulence and Pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 Strain
abstract: Genome sequencing has ushered a new era in modern biology by allowing scientists to investigate the assembled genome for clues on pathogenic potential as well as new and emerging virulent genes in the genome. This work started out with the validation of an in-house MATLAB gene finder software that examined the SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain assembled genome. Data reveals 70 open reading frames, whose calculated molecular weight and isoelectric point yields a theoretical protein 2D gel electrophoresis pattern with clustering of high molecular weight proteins (i.e., 50 to 300 kDa) within the physiological pH range of 6 to 8. Such results suggest one possible reason for the high virulence of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain due probably to the pathogenic effects of the high molecular weight proteins that have isoelectric point in the pH 6 to 8 window. Further observations of clusters of proteins with closely similar number of amino acids in the range of 200 to 300, 1300 to 1400, 1800 to 1900, 1900 to 2000, and 2000 to 2100 prompted the development of another in-house MATLAB multiple sequence alignment software. Results from the alignment reveals that, in each protein cluster, there are one or two more ancient proteins with long N-terminal end that is not present in the modern version of the protein, which share long segment of high sequence conservation with the ancient proteins after the N-terminal end segment. This shows that SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain may be evolutionary ancient, and relics of ancient proteins are still remnants in the assembled genome of the virus strain. Overall, this work unexpectedly highlights salient features of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain as having high molecular weight proteins with isoelectric points in the pH 6 to 8 physiological window, as well as the virus harbouring ancient proteins with unknown pathogenic and virulence potential.

title: CelFDrive - multimodal deep learning-assisted microscopy for automated detection of rare events.
abstract: The emergence of automated microscopy has enabled the collection of large datasets of rare biological events, accelerating discovery in biology. However, most existing methods cannot be readily integrated into microscopy setups or are limited to a single microscope type. We present CelFDrive, a software package that automatically detects rare events of interest and automates high-resolution three-dimensional imaging of target cells by integrating deep learning-assisted cell classification of auxiliary low-magnification fluorescence images. We show that CelFDrive reduced the mean time required to nominate a mitotic prophase candidate for high-resolution light-sheet imaging by over 30-fold relative to manual expert selection. This approach can be used to define the order of kinetochore assembly upon nuclear envelope breakdown. The trained CelFDrive detector demonstrated transferability by retaining mitotic cell detection capability in an independently generated dataset using a different cell line, DNA marker and imaging setup. As datasets grow and models improve, CelFDrive offers a clear path toward intelligent imaging systems that not only accelerate data collection, but also fundamentally enhance how biological questions are explored.
authors: Brooks S, Toral-Pérez S, Pučeková N, Corcoran DS, Kilborn K, Bodensteiner B, Baumann H, Burroughs NJ, McAinsh AD, Bretschneider T.

title: Almond Anthracnose Is Caused by a Genetically Diverse Population of Colletotrichum godetiae Fungi Along with a Lower Proportion of C. acutatum.
abstract: Almond anthracnose, caused by Colletotrichum spp., has become an increasing threat in modern almond orchards in Portugal. This study aimed to characterize the genetic, phylogenetic, morphological, and virulence diversity of Colletotrichum species associated with symptomatic and asymptomatic almond tree organs collected in the main producing regions of Portugal. A total of 112 isolates were obtained from fruits, leaves, flowers and branches, with most samples originating from the Alentejo region. Almond anthracnose in Portugal is caused by genetically and biologically heterogeneous Colletotrichum species dominated by C. godetiae, which exhibited high multilocus genetic diversity, with most isolates corresponding to unique haplotypes, indicating the coexistence of genetically distinct strains. C. godetiae and C. acutatum were predominantly isolated from symptomatic organs in the field, whereas C. fioriniae, C. karsti, and C. gloeosporioides were detected in asymptomatic organs; however, all species were able to cause disease. This study reports C. karsti and C. gloeosporioides on almond for the first time. This diversity suggests multiple introductions and/or ongoing diversification of Colletotrichum populations associated with almond. Differences in virulence among the representative isolates tested, combined with similar incubation and latency periods, indicate that the severity is related to postpenetration events. Moreover, disease prevalence, averaging 36%, was associated with rainfall during the period from fruit set to early fruit development, highlighting the strong influence of meteorological conditions on anthracnose outbreaks. These findings support targeted monitoring, risk assessment, and integrated disease management under agricultural intensification and climatic variability.
authors: Ramos M, Arsénio P, Baroncelli R, Talhinhas P.

title: BK polyomavirus viraemia after kidney transplantation: incidence, graft survival and its association with urinary tract malignancies.
abstract: BackgroundBK polyomavirus (BKPyV) nephropathy is an important cause of graft dysfunction and loss after kidney transplant. Treatment options are limited and predominately involve immunosuppression reduction with a limited role for anti-viral medications. There have been some reports of BKPyV-DNAemia and its association with bladder cancer.MethodsWe examined the incidence and impact of BKPyV in 1372 first-time kidney transplant recipients from 2011 to 2022, using prospectively collected data from the National Renal Transplant Registry and the National Virus Reference Laboratory. We assessed risk factors, graft survival, and development of post-transplant bladder cancer. Recipients underwent regular viral load monitoring with BKPyV-DNAemia defined as >1000 copies per millilitre (CPM).ResultsBKPyV-DNAemia was detected in 22.2% of recipients. Graft survival was comparable between groups; five-year survival was 91% in the BKPyV-DNAemia-positive group versus 88% in the BKPyV-DNAemia-negative group. Post-transplant bladder cancer occurred in .87% (n = 12) of recipients. However, bladder cancer occurred in 2.6% (n = 8) of BKPyV-DNAemia-positive compared to 0.37% (n = 4) of BKPyV-DNAemia-negative recipients. Multivariate analysis revealed a significantly increased risk of bladder cancer in the BKPyV-DNAemia group (adjusted hazard ratio 4.95, P = .008), furthermore we noticed a marked increase in hazard ratio as levels increased from 1000 CPM to 10 000 CPM. In BKPyV-DNAemia patients, median time to cancer diagnosis was 72 months post-transplant, with median survival of 25 months after diagnosis.ConclusionsThis association between BKPyV-DNAemia and post-transplant bladder cancer suggests the need for close surveillance for signs of bladder cancer in these patients.
authors: Clince M, O'Donoghue D, Sandys V, Conlon P, Magee C, O'Kelly P, Cooney A, Brennan C, Sutton-Fitzpatrick U, Kruseman Aretz N, Ni Chinneide E, Connell J, Teo MY, Fitzpatrick F, Doyle B, Broe M, Little D, Conlon PJ.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp2 reprograms host immunity to drive pathogenic inflammation.
abstract: Despite the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate endemically, highlighting the need to better understand the viral determinants of pathogenesis. Putative functions of the non-structural protein 2 (Nsp2) have been studied in vitro, but how Nsp2 affects pathogenesis and overall viral fitness in vivo has yet to be demonstrated. Here, we generated a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 lacking Nsp2 (ΔNsp2) to investigate its role in viral replication and disease. While ΔNsp2 replicated comparably to wild-type virus in vitro and in vivo, its deletion resulted in markedly attenuated disease in K18-hACE2 mice. Wild-type virus infection induced a strong pro-inflammatory response associated with increased recruitment of monocytes and macrophages, whereas ΔNsp2 virus infection promoted a more balanced antiviral response characterized by enhanced lymphocyte and NK cell recruitment. This was accompanied by reduced pulmonary and systemic inflammation and distinct transcriptional programs, including downregulation of pathways related to RNA processing and translation. Mechanistically, CLIP-seq and proximity labeling suggest that Nsp2 interacts with host RNA and components of the translational machinery. Together, our findings identify Nsp2 as a key virulence factor that drives immunopathology by skewing host immune responses, highlighting its role as a regulator of host-pathogen interactions.IMPORTANCEThe COVID-19 pandemic has officially ended, yet the virus that causes it continues to circulate and evolve, making it important to understand what makes it cause severe disease. This study focuses on a viral protein called Nsp2 and asks what role it plays in driving illness. Using an animal model, we observed that when Nsp2 was removed from the virus, infected animals became far less sick, even though the virus itself replicated just as well. Instead of triggering the harmful, excessive inflammation typically seen with the full virus, the modified virus prompted a more balanced immune response. Further investigation revealed that Nsp2 interacts directly with the host's genetic machinery, suggesting a mechanism by which the virus hijacks immune signaling to worsen disease. These findings pinpoint Nsp2 as a driver of COVID-19 severity and a promising target for future therapies aimed at reducing inflammation rather than simply fighting the virus itself.
authors: Lacasse É, Dubuc I, Leclerc J, Gravel A, Gudimard L, Joly-Beauparlant C, Faure M, Fortin P, Blanchet M-R, Droit A, Flamand L.

title: ZmSGT1-mediated competitive protection of ZmBBI1 enhances maize resistance to Rhizoctonia solani.
abstract: Banded leaf and sheath blight (BLSB), incited by the necrotrophic basidiomycete Rhizoctonia solani, is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely constrains global maize (Zea mays) production. Bowman-Birk inhibitors (BBIs) constitute a critical class of protease inhibitors in plant innate immunity; yet, their biological functions and upstream regulatory circuits in maize defense against necrotrophic pathogens remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we show that ZmBBI1, a BBI family member transcriptionally upregulated upon R. solani infection, positively modulates BLSB resistance. Its defense activity is strictly dependent on trypsin-inhibitory function, mediated by the evolutionarily conserved Thr52 and Arg53 residues in its canonical reactive loop. We identify Rs03254, a secreted virulence effector from R. solani, that directly engages ZmBBI1 and biochemically inactivates its protease-inhibitory activity to promote fungal colonization. We further demonstrate that the conserved immune co-chaperone ZmSGT1 physically interacts with ZmBBI1 and is genetically required for its full defense function. Mechanistically, ZmSGT1 competes with Rs03254 for binding to ZmBBI1, displacing the pathogen effector and restoring ZmBBI1's trypsin-inhibitory activity. Our work defines a tripartite molecular arms race module in the maize-R. solani pathosystem and uncovers a noncanonical role for SGT1 as a molecular bodyguard that protects host defense factors from effector-mediated suppression, providing actionable targets for engineering durable BLSB resistance in maize.
authors: Sun Y, Wang L, He X, Zhu B, Ma Z, Wan K, Li N.

title: An IoT-enabled hybrid paper/polymer-based microfluidic device for rapid detection of Campylobacter jejuni in foods.
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is the leading bacterial cause of foodborne gastroenteritis worldwide and represents a major public health concern. We report an IoT-enabled hybrid paper/polymer-based microfluidic device for rapid detection of C. jejuni in food matrices. This platform integrates recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), CRISPR/Cas12a-based sequence recognition, and lateral flow readout within a foldable paper-based architecture incorporating PDMS reservoirs. An IoT workflow was established to enable automated image capture, result classification, and centralized data transmission. Analytical performance was evaluated using both pure cultures and food samples. This assay specifically detected C. jejuni with no observed cross-reactivity among the tested strains and achieved a limit of detection of 5800 CFU mL-1 using the developed microfluidic device. In chicken breast samples, C. jejuni was reliably detected at initial inoculation levels of 100 to 103 CFU g-1 following 6-12 h of enrichment, while higher contamination levels (>103 CFU g-1) were detectable without enrichment. The complete workflow from DNA extraction to visual readout was completed in ∼1 h. By integrating microfluidic sensing, automated data interpretation, and IoT-enabled connectivity, this platform provides a practical and scalable approach for decentralized screening and rapid monitoring of C. jejuni in agri-food system.
authors: He Y, Liu J, Li S, Zhao X, Lu X.

title: Adeno-associated virus gene therapy for hemophilia B: a comparative appraisal of the licensed products.
abstract: Among the inherited bleeding disorders, hemophilia B has become the leading target for adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy. The compact factor IX (FIX) coding sequence, the abundance and durability of hepatocyte-derived FIX expression and the hyperactive FIX-Padua variant together made single-infusion phenotypic correction achievable earlier and more convincingly for FIX deficiency than for factor VIII (FVIII) deficiency. Three FIX-Padua AAV products have reached regulatory approval: etranacogene dezaparvovec, licensed in the United States, Canada and Europe; fidanacogene elaparvovec, initially licensed in the same regions but discontinued worldwide by its manufacturer; and dalnacogene ponparvovec (BBM-H901), licensed in China. This review outlines the biological differences between FVIII and FIX, the immunological and analytical challenges common to all AAV FIX products, and the pivotal trial data for each licensed therapy. Because FIX-Padua activity is reagent dependent, activity is standardized throughout to a single one-stage scale (HemosIL SynthASil), permitting a like-for-like comparison: mean activity 27-55 IU/dL, annualized bleeding rates 0.6-1.5 and reductions in FIX consumption exceeding 90% for all three products, sustained to five years for etranacogene dezaparvovec and six for the fidanacogene elaparvovec phase 1/2a cohort. Only dalnacogene ponparvovec has published data in adolescents. The review compares the three products' capsids, genome configurations, doses, impact of pre-existing anti-AAV immunity and immunomodulation, and weighs their reassuring but surveillance-dependent long-term safety, including the theoretical risk of insertional oncogenesis. Finally, it considers why the clearest efficacy successes have coincided with limited real-world uptake, and what the divergent commercial and regulatory trajectories imply for equitable global access.
authors: Miesbach W, Pierce GF.

title: Dysregulated CSF T-cell responses and their evolution after intravenous immunoglobulin in Guillain-Barré syndrome.
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated neuropathy that frequently results in long-term disability. The cellular mechanisms underlying GBS and the immunomodulatory effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) remain incompletely understood. In this prospective observational cohort study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing on peripheral blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collected before and after IVIg treatment from treatment-naïve patients with GBS. Pre-treatment blood and CSF were obtained from nine and eight patients, respectively; post-treatment samples were available from six patients for blood and three patients for CSF. Previously published healthy control (HC) blood and CSF single-cell datasets were analyzed for comparison. We characterized immune cell composition, transcriptional states, TCR clonality, and clonal dynamics across peripheral and CSF compartments as well as following treatment. Individuals with GBS exhibited enrichment of T helper 1 (Th1)-polarized CD4+ T cells, activated and resident-memory CD8+ T cells, and macrophages in CSF relative to paired peripheral blood. This CSF-to-blood enrichment was greater than in healthy controls (HCs) for Th1 cells, activated effector-memory CD8+ T cells, and inflammatory macrophages, although the overall degree of T-cell clonal expansion was similar between groups. In both GBS and HCs, expanded CSF CD4+ clonotypes were predominantly Th1-polarized and largely absent from blood, whereas expanded CD8+ clonotypes showed greater overlap between compartments. Among clonotypes detected in both blood and CSF, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells exhibited more activated transcriptional states in the CSF, a shift that was particularly pronounced in GBS. Following IVIg treatment, peripheral blood showed minimal changes, whereas CSF T-cell populations exhibited more substantial alterations, including reductions in Th1-associated and activated effector-memory states, increases in T helper 2 (Th2) and regulatory T cell populations, and changes in the clonal repertoire. Expanded T cell clonotypes with sequence-based predicted specificity for pathogens associated with GBS were identified in six patients, and convergent clonotype groups were detected both within and across patients. Demyelinating GBS is characterized by compartmentalized enrichment and activation of pro-inflammatory T-cell populations within the CSF rather than an overall increase in T-cell clonal expansion. Exploratory longitudinal findings further suggest that CSF T-cell populations are altered following IVIg treatment. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and TCR analyses provide insight into the early immune response in GBS and identify candidate cellular pathways for biomarker development and therapeutic investigation.
authors: Morrison AH, Yao T, Isfort MC, Morena J, Liu T, Roell J, Akkaya B, Kolb SJ, Bell EH, Saligrama N, Segal BM.

title: A Concentration-Matrix Approach to Assess Planktonic Growth and Biofilm Biomass in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Exposed to Rifampicin and Moringa oleifera Leaf Ethanolic Extract
abstract: Biofilm formation by Pseudomonas aeruginosa complicates antimicrobial treatment, particularly in persistent infections, and motivates the assessment of plant-derived antibiotic adjuncts. The influence of Moringa oleifera leaf ethanolic extract on rifampicin responses across planktonic growth and biofilm formation requires concentration-resolved evaluation. Three independent experiments assessed planktonic growth and crystal violet-stained biofilm biomass across ethanolic extract–rifampicin concentration matrices. Conventional PCR screened selected biofilm-associated genes. The ethanolic extract alone yielded 99.33–119.33% planktonic growth relative to controls at 1–64 µg/mL. Rifampicin alone reduced growth to 58.67 ± 1.15% and 6.67 ± 0.58% at 16 and 32 µg/mL, respectively. Adding 16 µg/mL ethanol fraction to 16 µg/mL rifampicin yielded 44.67 ± 30.99% growth, compared with 58.67 ± 1.15% for rifampicin alone. At 32 µg/mL rifampicin, the same fraction addition yielded 16.00 ± 13.00% growth, compared with 6.67 ± 0.58% for rifampicin alone. Biofilm biomass at 16 µg/mL rifampicin was 55.67 ± 67.00%, reaching 70.00 ± 86.88% with ethanol fraction addition. All 49 paired comparisons per assay yielded false-discovery-rate-adjusted q-values above 0.05. PCR detected pelA, pslA, pslD, pqsA, lasR, and ndvB. The concentration matrices revealed distinct planktonic growth and biofilm biomass responses. These findings position complementary planktonic and biofilm measurements as essential criteria for assessing plant–antibiotic combinations, providing concentration-specific evidence to guide formulation screening and antimicrobial candidate prioritization.
authors: Hapsari BK, Natzir R, Sultan AR, Syamsuri F, Astuti I, Bahar B, Aswad M, Hatta M.

title: TRIM63-associated signal in sunitinib-resistant xenografts and an eight- gene prognostic score in renal cell carcinoma
abstract: Abstract  Background  Sunitinib resistance limits the durable activity of anti-angiogenic therapy in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). This study screened TRIM-family expression in the GSE64052 786-O xenograft model and evaluated a TRIM63-anchored eight-gene risk score (TRIM-8RS) comprising OTX1, LIMCH1, ANK3, TRIM63, CAVIN2, CLTRN, WFDC10B and BBOX1 for prognostic association. Methods  The score was evaluated in The Cancer Genome Atlas kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (TCGA-KIRC) development cohort (508 patients; 171 deaths) and an independent Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium operational primary-RCC cohort (183 patients; 31 deaths). Model development was repeated with all outcome-dependent candidate screening confined to outer training folds, and discrimination was assessed with Uno's concordance index and inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results  TRIM63 expression was directionally higher in resistant xenografts, but the association did not survive genome-wide false-discovery-rate adjustment (log2 fold change, 1.84; nominal P = 0.038; adjusted P = 0.291). The apparent Uno concordance index was 0.738 in the development cohort and 0.716 in the external cohort. The 1- and 3-year areas under the curve were 0.804 and 0.745 in TCGA-KIRC and 0.793 and 0.770 in the external cohort, and overall survival differed between risk groups defined by the frozen TCGA median score in both cohorts (hazard ratios, 4.56 and 4.51, respectively). The leakage-controlled reconstruction yielded a mean outer-fold concordance index of 0.699, and multivariable models further adjusted for age, sex and, in TCGA-KIRC, stage and grade. In public single-cell data, TRIM63 was detected in 49 of 17,986 cells, each with one raw unique molecular identifier, and spatial data showed low and variable fractions of TRIM63-positive spots across 11 slides. Conclusion  These findings support a preliminary prognostic association and further biological validation. They do not establish a causal resistance mechanism or predict clinical benefit.
authors: Deng Y, Yang X, Hao C, Yu C, Xia M, Wang T.

title: Genome Mining-Driven Discovery of the Sactipeptide Smithiosin in Probiotic, Thermophilic Strain Bacillus smithii.
abstract: Sactipeptides are a class of ribosomally synthesised and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), which have a cyclic topology formed by unique thioether crosslinks called sactionines. Sactionines are introduced by radical S-adenosylmethionine (rSAM) enzymes between cysteine residues and the α-carbon of other amino acids. Genome sequencing has revealed many putative sactipeptide biosynthetic gene clusters; however, few sactipeptides have been isolated and characterised. Here, we use genome mining to identify a novel sactipeptide from Bacillus smithii. The novel sactipeptide, named smithiosin, was extracted from the industrially important thermophile B. smithii and characterised as a novel homologue of the previously characterised sactipeptide subtilosin A from B. subtilis. Furthermore, the smithiosin precursor peptide gene was heterologously expressed in the subtilosin A producer Bacillus subtilis 168 without knockout of the native precursor peptide, successfully leading to the production of both subtilosin A and smithiosin. This demonstrates for the first time that a non-native precursor peptide is able to outcompete the subtilosin A precursor for all of the native biosynthetic enzymes in B. subtilis, including the radical SAM enzyme AlbA. It also opens a potential new opportunity for screening non-native precursor peptides with the subtilosin A biosynthetic enzymes via heterologous expression in B. subtilis.
authors: Vasciaveo S, Zhou Y, Ding Y, Hind CK, Gräff ÁT, Camp AH, Sutton JM, Barry SM, Dickman R.

title: Modeling of Therapist-Client Dynamics in Psychotherapy Using Large Language Model-Based Assessments: Retrospective Observational Study of 1573 Psychotherapy Sessions.
abstract: BackgroundPsychotherapy is a primary treatment for many mental health conditions, yet the dynamic interplay among therapist behaviors, client responses, and the therapeutic relationship remains difficult to disentangle at scale. Traditional process research relies on labor-intensive human coding, limiting the ability to model moment-to-moment therapeutic dynamics across large datasets.ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and validate a computational framework for modeling therapist-client interaction processes and to examine how therapist behaviors and relational qualities relate to client self-disclosure and emotional expression in psychotherapy sessions.MethodsWe developed automated assessment pipelines using large language models (LLMs) to measure therapist behaviors (empathy or exploration), relational quality (rapport), and client outcomes (self-disclosure, self-directed negative emotion, or outward-directed negative emotion). Model-generated scores were validated against human annotations. We then applied these measures to approximately 2000 hours of psychotherapy transcripts from the Alexander Street corpus. This yielded an estimation sample of 119,233 client utterances from 1573 sessions and 37 clients. Because utterances are nested within sessions and sessions within clients, we estimated a saturated multivariate structural equation model with SEs clustered at the session level. Results were confirmed in a multilevel regression model with random intercepts for session and client.ResultsFollowing comparative validation of 6 candidate language models, automated measures showed good to excellent agreement with human annotations (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]=0.60-0.81) for rapport (ICC=0.81), self-disclosure (ICC=0.78), empathy components (ICC=0.60-0.75), and emotion measurements (ICC=0.66-0.80). Structural equation modeling analyses revealed that therapist empathy and exploration were each associated with increased client disclosure (empathy: β=.086, 95% CI 0.078-0.095; exploration: β=.086, 95% CI 0.078-0.094; both PConclusionsThis study demonstrates that LLM-based measurement combined with structural modeling can capture core therapeutic processes at scale. Empathy and exploration showed small but consistent turn-level associations with client disclosure and emotional expression, whereas prior-session rapport did not show a robust association. These findings provide a computational foundation for precision modeling of psychotherapy processes and may offer actionable insights for scalable therapist training and AI-supported clinical education systems.
authors: Chen AH, Jin S, Wang C, Swartz HA, Wu T, Kraut RE, Zhu H.

title: Resistance to SDHI Fungicides in Monilinia fructicola Field Isolates Is Associated with Amino Acid Substitutions Across SDH Subunits.
abstract: Brown rot, caused by Monilinia fructicola, is the most destructive pre- and postharvest fruit rot of peach worldwide. In 2024, a disease outbreak occurred in a South Carolina orchard despite a rigorous chemical management program consisting of preharvest applications of succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor (SDHI), quinone outside inhibitor, and demethylation inhibitor (DMI) fungicides. Isolates from affected orchards carried the Mona element upstream of the MfCYP51 gene, and propiconazole discriminatory dose assays confirmed reduced sensitivity in vitro, with all 2024 isolates exhibiting relative growth greater than 20%. They displayed either low, moderate, or high levels of resistance to boscalid, isofetamid, fluopyram, and fluxapyroxad based on EC50 values ranging from 0.30 to 14.74, 0.07 to 1.93, 0.26 to 3.48, and 0.19 to 2.82 µg/ml, respectively. In contrast, EC50 values obtained for historic isolates were ≤0.05 µg/ml for all SDHI fungicides. Whole-genome sequencing, followed by targeted amplification and sequencing of SDH subunits across the isolate collection, identified five SDH genotypes: wild type (no amino acid substitutions), G1 (N226H in SDHB), G2 (P80H in SDHC), G3 (N226H in SDHB and V26I in SDHD), and G4 (N226H in SDHB, P80H in SDHC, and T24A in SDHD). Isolates harboring amino acid changes in multiple SDH subunits had the highest EC50 values and were resistant to all SDHIs tested. Detached fruit assays confirmed that label rates of SDHI fungicides failed to control isolates carrying multiple amino acid changes. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first report worldwide of SDHI resistance in Monilinia species field isolates linked to amino acid changes in the SDH subunits and combined SDHI and DMI resistance in peach orchards, highlighting the need for resistance monitoring and management.
authors: Gelain J, Wesche J, Trotter EK, Beger M, Ortiz M, Schnabel G.

title: Comparison of Next-Generation Sequencing and Quantitative PCR Methodologies for Quantification of Fungicide Resistance in Mixed Samples of Colletotrichum siamense.
abstract: Measuring the frequency of fungicide resistance alleles in pathogen populations is critical for understanding resistance spread and severity. TaqMan quantitative PCR (qPCR) is a standard method for allele quantification, whereas next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies offer an alternative for high-resolution detection. Because studies exploring NGS for this purpose are limited, the objective of this study was to compare the accuracy and feasibility of Illumina NGS amplicon sequencing with that of a previously validated TaqMan qPCR assay to quantify resistance alleles to thiophanate-methyl fungicide in a set of mixed Colletotrichum siamense DNA samples. For validation, a set with known frequencies of resistance to thiophanate-methyl was used as a control. Both the NGS- and qPCR-based methods were highly precise, with an R2 of 0.99 and 0.97, respectively, for the C. siamense DNA samples with known resistance frequencies. However, with the samples of unknown resistance frequencies that were collected from detached blueberry fruit assays, the NGS method demonstrated more variability than the TaqMan method (P < 0.001). This variability was likely associated with low target DNA concentration and the presence of host and nontarget fungal DNA, which reduced PCR efficiency. This study highlighted strengths and weaknesses of both technologies and important assay design considerations. It was concluded that NGS-based methodologies may be preferential for large sample sizes and for detecting multiple or novel mutations within a region, whereas the qPCR assay can be more efficient for rapid quantification of known alleles.
authors: Cosseboom SD, Jumbam B, Toro M, Hu M.

title: Genetic code expansion for site-specific encoding of a switchable, intrinsic fluorophore-quencher pair to monitor protein dynamics.
abstract: Precisely modifying proteins at multiple sites in their native, folded structures offers unique opportunities to answer molecular and cellular-level biological questions. Here, we present a genetic code expansion strategy for site-specific integration of a fluorophore-quencher pair comprising two non-canonical amino acids-acridonylalanine (Acd) and methyltetrazinyl phenylalanine (Tet)-into a protein expressed in E. coli. The Acd and Tet pair requires no post-translational labeling, and quenching can be switched off by bioorthogonal or photochemical reactions of Tet for convenient internal control experiments. Mechanistic studies based on Stern-Volmer quenching, fluorescence lifetime measurements, and "proline ruler" peptides established the distance dependence of quenching. As proof-of-concept, we applied this strategy to study: (1) calmodulin, a calcium-sensing protein, (2) RecA, a DNA damage sensor in bacteria, and (3) LexA, a transcriptional repressor whose activation by RecA governs acquired antibiotic resistance in bacteria. Using these proteins, we demonstrate that dual Acd/Tet labeling provides molecular-level insights into protein dynamics, shows potential for adaptation to high-throughput drug screening, and advances tools for studying protein structure-function relationships.
authors: Giri P, Venkatesh Y, Mathis MH, Hurley CM, Jones CM, Ndogo Eteme O, Hostetler ZM, Cooley RB, Kohli RM, Mehl RA, Petersson EJ.

title: Engineering cyanobacterial carbonic anhydrase surface mutations for fast CO<sub>2</sub> hydration and capture.
abstract: Equilibration between CO2 and the other forms of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is slow under ambient conditions, bottlenecked by the hydration of dissolved CO2 to form bicarbonate and a proton. This step is often rate-limiting for aqueous CO2 capture processes under ambient temperature and pressure, and is precisely the chemistry catalyzed by the family of carbonic anhydrase enzymes. As a result, incorporation of carbonic anhydrases (CAs) into various CO2 capture schemes may be used to accelerate CO2 hydration, increasing the rates of downstream processes coupled to this DIC equilibrium. While this potential use for CA has been long-studied, extending these basic chemical principles to real applications have been hampered by practical questions of how to economically source carbonic anhydrase enzymes at mass scale. This work explores the use of modified cyanobacterial expression hosts as a potential resolution to that problem. Successful engineering of carbonic anhydrase surface display in fast-growing, marine cyanobacteria would yield a self-sustaining CO2 hydration catalyst that requires only sunlight, CO2 itself, and nutrients freely available in seawater, as inputs for passively generating carbonic anhydrases on the cell envelope during cell growth.
authors: Agbo P.

title: Continuous Capture of Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus Particles Using Twin-Column CaptureSMB.
abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAVs) have gained increasing importance in gene therapy due to their safe and precise gene delivery. However, certain indications require substantially higher vector doses, pushing manufacturing capacity and cost of goods (COG) to its limits. In this study, we present a proof-of-concept evaluation of a continuous twin-column capture process (CaptureSMB) enabling direct purification of rAAV5 from minimally processed, nonlysed perfusion harvest without prior enzymatic nuclease digestion, concentration or buffer exchange. This approach differs fundamentally from conventional batch workflows which typically mandate clarification and concentration before affinity capture and offers a novel process integration in viral vector manufacturing. A single-column batch capture process was developed first and subsequently compared to continuous CaptureSMB configurations. Optimized CaptureSMB operation achieved consistent yields over four cycles, with recoveries exceeding batch operation (+14.3%) with concomitant higher productivity (+11.4%) and reduced buffer consumption (-79.2%). Critical quality attribute (CQA) analysis showed lower host cell protein levels and lower residual DNA in early CaptureSMB cycles, while full capsid ratios, thermal stability and transduction efficiency of rAAV5 particles remained unaltered across cycles and process modes. However, progressive backpressure and residual impurity accumulation in later cycles highlight operational challenges associated with direct capture of low-titer feed streams. These findings highlight that continuous twin-column CaptureSMB directly from secretion-derived perfusion harvest can improve operational efficiency, lower buffer requirements, and also maintain and, in some respects, enhance product quality. This novel strategy provides a promising route to address manufacturing capacity and cost challenges in rAAV gene therapy production.
authors: Müller JM, Tobler D, Bühler J, Hauri D, Plieninger R, Göbel S, Saygili E, Higuchi Y, Takahashi R, Vogg S, Müller-Späth T, Villiger TK.

title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity.
abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

title: Tetraspanin CD81 restricts Ebola virus infection and is antagonized by glycoprotein GP and matrix protein VP40.
abstract: Viruses manipulate host cell membranes to evade antiviral immunity, prevent superinfection, and optimize their replication and spread. The Ebola virus glycoprotein GP mediates viral entry but also contributes to the subversion of host antiviral immune responses. Here, we characterize the impact of Ebola virus GP on cell surface proteins and show that it reduces cell surface availability of tetraspanins CD81, CD63, and CD9. This function is conserved among several filoviral glycoproteins but not observed for glycoproteins of other viral families. Whereas CD63 and CD9 are largely dispensable for Ebola virus replication, CD81 suppresses virus-like particle entry and viral replication. This activity might be attributed to CD81-mediated suppression of NF-κB signaling, which is induced by the Ebola virus matrix protein VP40 and transcription- and replication-competent virus-like particle (trVLP) replication. Our results further indicate that both GP, which interacts directly with CD81, and VP40, which also associates with CD81, function to reduce total and surface expression levels of CD81. CD81 is shown to reduce levels of Ebola virus RNA species, and its antibody-mediated clustering can suppress Ebola virus infection. Our study provides insights into the roles of NF-κB signaling in Ebola virus replication and immunopathogenesis, and identifies tetraspanin CD81 as a potentially druggable Ebola virus-inhibitory host factor.
authors: Hu D, Hagelauer E, Wendt L, Bosso M, Bunz M, Kammerloher J, Kutter JS, Brandi J, Widerspick L, Hoenen T, Schindler M.

title: A homozygous C2ORF78 variant is associated with mTOR hyperactivation and neurodevelopmental defects in focal cortical dysplasia.
abstract: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a malformation of cortical brain development, yet its genetic basis remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate type II FCD in a proband with behavioral disturbances, including aggression, hyperactivity, and sleep dysfunction, but with normal early development and cognition. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the proband revealed focal cortical thickening, abnormal sulcation, and gray-white matter blurring in the left temporal lobe, consistent with FCD type II. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense variant in C2ORF78 (c.1264 A > G; p.Ser422Gly), absent in population databases. The S422 residue is evolutionarily conserved, resides within a disordered, solvent-accessible region, and its substitution with glycine caused marked structural destabilization, cytosolic mislocalization, and protein aggregation. Functional studies in proband fibroblasts revealed no significant reduction of C2ORF78 protein, deregulated mTOR signaling, impaired autophagy, ER stress, and G0/G1 cell cycle arrest. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed significant loss of protein stability and compactness in the S422G mutant. C2ORF78 interacts with RNA-binding and transcriptional regulators, and gene ontology analyses indicated roles in transcription and RNA splicing. We propose that C2ORF78 functions as a transcriptional coregulator of genes negatively regulating mTOR signaling. Mislocalization of the S422G mutant leads to a loss of nuclear function, resulting in hyperactivation of mTOR and disrupted cellular homeostasis. High expression of C2ORF78 in cerebral cortex and hippocampus supports its relevance to brain physiology. Our findings identify C2ORF78 as a novel candidate gene associated with FCD type II and highlight transcriptional dysregulation of mTOR signaling as a potential pathogenic mechanism.
authors: Ahmad SR, Zeyaullah M, Zahrani Y, Altijani AA, Hummad H, Mohamed AOA, Dhiman NK.

title: Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Vitamin D Metabolism, Hyper-IgE Genes, and Epithelial Barrier Dysfunction in Hazelnut Allergy.
abstract: BackgroundHazelnut allergy is a major cause of food-induced anaphylaxis yet remains poorly defined at the molecular level. We aimed to identify molecular differences between individuals with primary hazelnut allergy and nonallergic controls by investigating a comprehensive spectrum of omics profiles in immune cells.MethodsWe analysed DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and proteomic profiles in hazelnut-stimulated and unstimulated immune cells.ResultsAcross analyses, we identified 87 differentially methylated signatures, 125 unique differentially expressed genes, and 11 unique differentially secreted proteins associated with hazelnut allergy. DNA methylation signatures were largely preserved irrespective of antigen stimulation, indicating stable epigenetic remodelling. Key findings implicated ZNF341, associated with a rare monogenic hyper-IgE syndrome, and ARL2, both linked to STAT3-mediated IgE dysregulation. We identified a hypermethylated region overlapping TH2LCRR in the cytokine gene cluster, suggesting an epigenetic mechanism contributing to IL-5 and IL-13 upregulation. Antigen stimulation was required to reveal hazelnut-specific transcriptional and proteomic signals. Integration of these data demonstrated that IL-5 expression could distinguish both groups. Moreover, integrated analysis of all multi-omics data revealed prominent innate immune activation programs involving antimicrobial, antiviral, and cytokine-mediated inflammatory responses. Finally, we identified signals in epithelial barrier genes of the gut and skin (TRIM31, TRIM40, CDSN), activation of the vitamin D pathway (CYP27B1, IL32), and nominated additional signals (PHACTR1, MFHAS1, SPRED2, NSMCE1-DT) for follow-up.ConclusionThis study provides the first antigen-specific multi-omics characterization of hazelnut allergy, confirming coordinated alterations in type 2-immunity and uncovering novel links to monogenic hyper-IgE syndrome, innate inflammatory pathways, activation of vitamin-D pathways, and gut/skin barrier genes, yielding a catalogue of candidate biomarkers for mechanistic studies and prospective validation.
authors: Jeanrenaud ACSN, Arnau-Soler A, Ghauri A, Marenholz I, Mertins P, Ziehm M, Beyer K, Worm M, Lee YA.

title: HIV-1 Tat drives genotype-dependent neuroimmune programs that promote Parkinson Disease-like neurodegeneration in the hSNCA<sup>A53T</sup>Gba1 mouse model.
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus type I (HIV-1) infection can induce both motor and cognitive impairments even in patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy (cART). These neurological alterations are related to direct and indirect mechanisms represented by viral and immune mediated processes, respectively. HIV-1 directly elicits neurological damages through some viral proteins including transactivator of transcription (Tat), a protein involved in the HIV-1 replication and able to affect neural cell through autocrine and paracrine pathways. In this study, we investigated the functional and transcriptional effects of intrastriatal Tat injection in pre-symptomatic mice carrying the hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ and hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mutations, common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease (PD). Behavioural assessment revealed that Tat administration anticipated motor symptoms onset in both genotypes, with some behavioural measures suggesting greater impairment in mice carrying both mutations, whereas spatial memory was not affected. In line with these findings, Tat injection induced significant loss of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive cells and fibre density in hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice. HIV-1 Tat injection did not significantly modify TH-positive fibre density in hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ mice, whereas a marked reduction was observed in hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice. Transcriptomic analysis revealed genotype-dependent responses, with a predominant innate immune-related signatures in hSNCAA53TGba1+/+ mice and transcriptional alterations involving immune, lysosomal, proteostatic, and autophagy-related pathways hSNCAA53TGba1+/L444P mice. Altogether, these findings indicate that HIV-1 Tat administration is associated with genotype-dependent PD-related motor deficits and that the Gba1 deficiency is linked to a more pronounced dopaminergic and transcriptional response to Tat exposure.

title: DNA methylation remodeling across adulthood in the rhesus macaque hippocampus.
abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) is a key epigenetic mechanism implicated in brain aging, yet methylation trajectories across the lifespan in the primate brain remain poorly understood. To characterize age-associated DNAm patterns in the hippocampus, we generated reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS) data from 86 rhesus macaque hippocampus samples spanning ~3-35 years of age (females = 56; males = 30). CpG-level analyses revealed minimal age-associated changes in mean methylation, with sites trending toward intermediate states, but widespread increases in methylation variability, consistent with epigenetic drift and reduced regulatory fidelity. Region-level modeling identified 5163 age-associated methylation regions exhibiting both monotonic and nonlinear trajectories across age. Nonlinear clusters revealed midlife inflections centered around 12.3 and 13.2 years, suggesting that hippocampal epigenetic aging may involve molecular transition periods that shape later-life brain aging trajectories. Integration of these age-associated DNAm regions with matched RNAseq data identified candidate cis-regulatory loci where age-associated methylation may be linked to transcriptional changes, including IGF1R. In addition, direct testing of associations between mean gene methylation and expression revealed a significant repressive directional bias (higher methylation associated with lower expression) highlighting genes involved in neuroinflammation, amyloid processing, and myelin maintenance. Intergenic regions overlapped annotated human brain enhancers, indicating that age-associated methylation remodeling extends to distal cis-regulatory elements. Together, these findings indicate that hippocampal DNAm aging in a long-lived primate is dominated by increasing epigenetic variability at the CpG level alongside regional remodeling of both genic and intergenic regulatory loci, with potential implications for transcriptional remodeling during brain aging.
authors: Anderson TJ, Watowich MM, Smith ML, Goldman EA, Peterson S, Layman CE, Davis BA, Snyder-Mackler N, Carbone L, Kohama SG, Sterner KN.

title: TWIST family in cervical cancer biology: From molecular mechanisms to clinical implications.
abstract: Despite ongoing clinical efforts, cervical cancer remains one of the most common gynecologic tumors, largely due to its metastatic potential and resistance to chemotherapy. The transcriptional regulator TWIST has been implicated in these features, in part through the induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The expression of TWIST is delicately regulated by several exogenous factors, including hypoxia-driven HIF-1α signaling and TGF-β pathways, as well as endogenous oncogenic cascades such as Wnt/β-catenin, NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, Hedgehog, Notch, and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3. Moreover, the E6 and E7 proteins from high-risk human papillomavirus strains promote TWIST upregulation, facilitating cellular plasticity and evasion of senescence. Post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation is orchestrated by complex networks of non-coding RNAs and key transcription factors such as Mist1, FOXC1, and LMX-1A. Importantly, hypermethylation of the TWIST1 promoter has been proposed as a candidate biomarker for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. TWIST has been reported to promote tumor-associated phenotypes through E-cadherin downregulation, induction of matrix metalloproteinases, and maintenance of stem cell-like properties. TWIST has been associated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy resistance, potentially through mechanisms involving DNA-damage responses and MDR1/P-glycoprotein-mediated drug efflux. The tumor microenvironment affects its expression and activity, including hypoxia, cancer-associated fibroblasts, inflammatory cytokines, tumor-associated macrophages, and extracellular vesicles. In a clinical context, high levels of TWIST are linked to poor outcomes in cervical cancer. Growing evidence links it to immune evasion through regulation of PD-L1, immunosuppressive cytokine signaling, macrophage polarization, T-cell exclusion, and immune resistance associated with cancer stem cells, underscoring its importance for translation in the current era of immune checkpoint blockade.
authors: Sayed U, Kubaev A, Polatova D, Ali MK, Mishra S, Singhal D, Bainsal N, Vahdati SN.

title: Shared genetic architecture and pleiotropic loci linking prurigo nodularis to allergic diseases.
abstract: Prurigo nodularis (PN) frequently co-occurs with allergic diseases, but the underlying shared genetic architecture and specific loci contributing to this overlap remain incompletely understood. We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for PN and multiple allergic diseases. Genetic sharing was assessed at genome-wide and regional levels, directional associations were examined using bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), and shared signals were refined through cross-trait pleiotropy, colocalization, and complementary gene-prioritization analyses. Immune-cell analyses were used to provide additional cellular context. PN showed positive genetic correlations with multiple allergic diseases, with regionally heterogeneous local sharing. MR suggested associations of several allergic liabilities with increased PN susceptibility. Cross-trait pleiotropy identified shared loci with enrichment in cytokine signaling, T-cell regulation, and lipid metabolism, while regional colocalization further refined a subset of shared signals. Across complementary genetic evidence, IL2RA, FADS1, PRR5L, and LRRC43 emerged as the most consistently supported candidate genes. Exploratory immune-cell analyses provided suggestive CD25-related T-cell context for IL2RA signal. PN and allergic diseases share a broad but regionally heterogeneous genetic architecture. Convergent evidence prioritizes a restricted set of shared loci and candidate genes, including IL2RA, providing a genetic framework for further functional investigation of PN-allergy overlap.
authors: Yin M, Zhu G, Zhou Z, Zhang X, Song Z.

title: First epidemiological and molecular characterization of bovine leukemia virus in Holstein dairy cattle from two cities in Shandong Province, China.
abstract: Bovine leukemia virus (BLV) is the etiological origin of enzootic bovine leukosis, a chronic lymphoproliferative disorder causing significant economic losses to the global cattle industry. Shandong Province in eastern China is a major dairy cattle-breeding region. However, the molecular prevalence and genetic characteristics of BLV in this area remain unclear. In this study, 289 blood samples were collected from Holstein dairy cattle across three large-scale commercial farms in Shandong Province, China, and BLV infection was determined using nested PCR targeting the long terminal repeat (LTR) of the virus. Of 289 samples, 59 (20.4%) were positive for BLV provirus. Phylogenetic analysis was performed based on 423 bp partial sequences of the env-gp51 gene from 24 BLV isolates, which were positive for BLV provirus by PCR targeting both the LTR and the env-gp51 gene. Maximum likelihood phylogenetic trees revealed that the 24 BLV sequences from Shandong Province were clustered into three distinct genotypes-namely, Genotypes-4, -6, and -7-among the 12 known BLV genotypes worldwide. Bayesian phylogenetic trees indicated that BLV sequences belonging to Genotypes-4 and -6 were further classified into four and two distinct phylogenetic clusters, respectively. This study reports the coexistence of Genotype-4 (G4-1, G4-2, G4-3, and G4-4), Genotype-6 (G6-1 and G6-2), and Genotype-7 in the cattle population from two cities in Shandong Province. These findings provide important baseline information on the molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity of BLV in Shandong Province.
authors: Guo G, Matsuura R, Dong L, Wang J, Bao A, Wang C, Wang J, Aida Y.

title: Immunoinformatics-based design of a multi-epitope vaccine against Fusobacterium nucleatum-associated colorectal cancer.
abstract: A multi-epitope vaccine candidate, A-20EFγ, was rationally designed against Fusobacterium nucleatum using proteomic and genomic information. The construct comprises a B-cell epitope (epitope 20) derived from the ABC transporter permease, along with cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) and helper T-lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes (epitopes E, F, and γ) selected from the nickel ABC transporter permease. All epitopes demonstrated favorable immunological properties, including high antigenicity, surface accessibility, and the absence of allergenicity and toxicity. These epitopes were assembled using suitable linkers, and outer membrane protein A was incorporated as an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity. Additionally, the PADRE sequence was included to improve immune stimulation and population coverage, resulting in a remarkable increase in predicted MHC class II and combined population coverage to 99.98%. The three-dimensional structure of the finalized vaccine was modeled using multiple computational approaches and validated through structural quality assessments and molecular dynamics simulations, with the RoseTTAFold model showing superior stability. Molecular docking, network normal mode, and binding free energy analyses revealed stable interactions between the vaccine and Toll-like receptors 2 and 4. Immune simulations further suggested that A-20EFγ could elicit a robust and long-lasting humoral immune response, characterized by high IgG and IgM levels and enhanced memory B-cell activity. Lastly, codon optimization and in silico cloning were conducted to facilitate in vitro synthesis and predict efficient expression in E. coli using the pET-28a (+) vector. Overall, these preliminary findings suggest A-20EFγ as a potential prophylactic vaccine candidate for the prevention of F. nucleatum-associated colorectal cancer.
authors: Tan CH, Ching JJ, Shuib AS, Sim KS.

title: Novel Regulators of Sugar-dependent Food Consumption in  Drosophila melanogaster
abstract: Diet and genetic background interact to influence food consumption, yet the genetic basis of diet-dependent feeding behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we used genome-wide association analysis (GWAS) to investigate the genetic regulation of sugar-dependent food consumption in  Drosophila melanogaster . Food intake was quantified in 176 lines of the  Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) using the Con-Ex (  Con sumption-  Ex cretion) assay on low- and high-sugar foods. Flies showed compensatory feeding, consuming more low-sugar food than high-sugar food, and this behavior was largely maintained across genotypes. Additionally, the magnitude and overall consumption varied several-fold among lines, with broad-sense heritability of 0.53 to 0.66 across sexes and diets. Association analysis across six sex- and diet-specific phenotypes identified 161 variants mapping to 118 candidate genes, which shared almost no loci between dietary conditions, indicating that consumption on the two foods is largely under separate genetic control. RNAi knockdown of candidate genes identified  CG42673 and  Tmtc2 , whose knockdown increased consumption across sexes and diets and was reproduced in independent experiments. Together, these findings show that natural genetic variation contributes substantially to diet-dependent feeding and identify candidate regulators of sugar-based food consumption in  Drosophila .
authors: Opoola M, Fitzgerald L, Ahmed S, Wright M, Alli S, Wright N, Hwangbo D.

title: Reference-Guided De Novo Retrieval of 3D Chromatin Organizational Features with Representation Learning
abstract: Chromosome conformation maps reveal spatial genome organization through recurring contact patterns, some associated with established architectural features and others with less understood biological processes. Identifying instances of a pattern across these maps is necessary to investigate its biological associations and recurrence across experimental settings. However, conventional feature callers typically target predefined patterns, offering limited support when researchers can provide examples of a feature of interest but lack a dedicated detection method. We introduce Chromatin Fetch (C-Fetch), a reference-guided retrieval framework that uses examples of a desired feature and a contrasting class to rank and assign contact-map patches at provided candidate coordinates. C-Fetch learns a generalized representation through weakly KL-regularized 3D autoencoding of structurally related, non-temporal Hi-C and Micro-C patches without architectural feature labels. We demonstrate retrieval of biologically defined contacts, visually specified patterns, and established architectural features. Polycomb-guided retrieval identifies contacts enriched for PRC2-associated signals, exceeding enrichment from loop-guided assignments at 5 kb, while queries resembling condensed domains retrieve patches with progressively stronger rectangular enrichment at higher ranks. Loop-guided retrieval increases aggregate focal enrichment relative to complete Mustache proposal sets across four held-out maps, and selected contacts show greater focality loss after cohesin depletion than matched remaining candidates. Retrieval also extends to Region Capture Micro-C and HiChIP, with ranking agreement retained across biological replicates and reduced sequencing depths. Together, these results establish reference examples as a flexible means of specifying contact-map features of interest, enabling biological investigation, exploration of visual patterns, and refinement of existing calls across datasets and technologies.
authors: Moran S, Liu J.

title: Cross-species epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity: Insights from Jonathan the Giant Tortoise and human centenarians
abstract: Can epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity transcend species boundaries? By comparing findings from a previously published epigenomic study of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise, based on buccal scrape and saliva samples, with the analyses of publicly available DNA methylation data from exceptionally long-lived humans based on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), this comparative study reveals intriguing molecular parallels across evolutionarily distant species. Human individuals aged 110+ years exhibited significantly higher global methylation entropy than those aged 60-82 years. Furthermore, 12 candidate genes displayed a distinctive promoter methylation entropy profile, with lower values at the youngest and oldest ages than in intermediate-age groups. Strikingly, these genes were enriched in telomere-related biological processes, highlighting a compelling link between epigenomic patterns and pathways implicated in aging. The correspondence between the findings in humans and previously reported observations in Jonathan suggests testable hypotheses about epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity that may be conserved across species and extend beyond tissue-specific effects.
authors: Pischedda S, Gómez-Carballa A, Martinón-Torres F, Salas A.

title: CryoID2: deep learning-enhanced identification of protein and RNA from cryoEM maps
abstract: SUMMARY  Identifying the molecular components of cryoEM/cryoET maps of endogenous or poorly characterized complexes remains a major bottleneck. CryoID2 addresses this by integrating deep learning–based feature prediction with sequence prioritization and structural evaluation. Three 3D U-Nets extract structure classes, key-atom positions, and reduced residue/nucleotide types from the input map. These predictions support backbone tracing and the generation of short sequence queries that rank candidates from a user-supplied pool—using BLASTp for proteins and a maximin strategy for RNA. Corresponding PDB or AlphaFold models are then retrieved, rigidly fitted using predicted features and experimental density, and ranked by map agreement. Module-level tests show high-recall feature prediction and resolution-dependent atom clustering, while a 52-case benchmark recovers near-reference fitting quality. In practice, cryoID2 correctly identified PfA-M17 from a 166-protein mass-spectrometry pool and the unannotated Ca-raiA RNA from a genome-derived non-coding sequence set, demonstrating a unified sequence-plus-structure route to molecular identification in cryoEM maps.
authors: Xu Q, Yu X, Wu L, Feng S, Zhou ZH.

title: Decoupled geogenic and faecal hazards in shallow coastal groundwater: evidence and a screening framework from the lower Indus Delta, Pakistan
abstract: Abstract  Shallow hand pumps supply drinking water to millions of people in low-lying deltas worldwide, where groundwater is exposed to geogenic salinisation and faecal contamination. Because these hazards are usually assessed together, it remains unclear whether they share a pathway and, therefore, which interventions are needed. In the lower Indus Delta (Pakistan), we analysed 93 hand pumps for 16 physicochemical variables, total coliforms and Escherichia coli, and combined hydrochemical diagnostics, a seawater mixing index (SMI), multivariate statistics, entropy-weighted and weighted-arithmetic water quality indices (EWQI, WA-WQI) and deterministic and Monte Carlo health-risk models. TDS exceeded 1000 mg/L in 58.1% of wells. A single salinity factor (65.9% of variance) integrated evaporation, cation exchange (slope −0.95, R² = 0.97) and limited marine mixing (SMI > 1 in 23.7%). E. coli occurred in 23.7% of wells, was independent of salinity (OR = 0.83, p = 0.81), was predicted only by turbidity (OR = 4.18 per log₁₀ NTU; AUC = 0.82) and, unlike salinity, was not spatially clustered, indicating wellhead ingress. WA-WQI assigned 66% of its weight to F⁻ and turbidity and agreed poorly with EWQI (weighted κ = 0.20). Child hazard index exceeded 1 with 46.1% probability, driven by F⁻, and drinking water supplied up to 122% of the WHO daily sodium limit. A well-by-well typology showed that only 26.9% of wells were safe, 8.6% needed only wellhead repair and 64.6% required treatment or a new source. The framework uses only routine monitoring data and is transferable to other salinising coastal deltas.
authors: Noonari TM, Gul N, Sawera M, Yousra M.

title: Detecting chlorophylls and carotenoids utilizing a novel chromatographic method designed for HPLC-PDA-MS analyses and application to environmental and cultured algae and cyanobacteria
abstract: Abstract    Chlorophylls and carotenoid analyses are important in aquaculture and freshwater and marine research as they are used to quantify algal biomass, food and supplement analyses, and to determine ecological diversity. The methods used for these analyses have often been limited to photometric detection, with some methods incorporating chromatographic separation. Mass spectrometric detection offers improved sensitivity, selectivity, and structural information compared to spectroscopy, but requires a full redesign of the separation system as previous chromatographic separations used solvent additives incompatible with mass spectrometry. The separation developed here used a YMC C30 “Carotenoid Column” with a novel mobile phase and elution scheme to separate a suite of algal pigments. Detection can be performed using a photodiode array alone, or in conjunction with mass spectrometry (MS). We report that the carotenoid echinenone (CAS 432-68-8) is actually an isomeric pair, which may have important implications for cyanobacterial photosynthesis and the orange carotenoid protein complex. New chlorophyll analogs, that could be hydroxylated or dehydroxylated derivatives, were detected in  Caulerpa  and  Planktothricoides  sp. BLCC-F182. This cyanobacterium produced novel chlorophylls, and it uniquely contained no echinenone or 3-OH echinenone. There was marked diversity in the types of pigments produced in the multiple strains analyzed, and the analyses demonstrated that there is likely to be more to discover in the pigments produced by algae and cyanobacteria. The inclusion of MS added significant value for the analysis of carotenoids and chlorophylls, and novel methodologies such as this may lead the field into important discoveries and advancements.
authors: Smith Z, Berthold DE, Gaffney KM, Laughinghouse HD, Hapeman CJ.

title: Coordinated Promoter Methylation and METTL3–YTHDF2 m6A-Dependent Decay Define a Tumor-Suppressive ZNF677 Program with Independent Prognostic Value in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract  Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven partly by epigenetic and epitranscriptomic dysregulation. ZNF677 is a candidate tumor suppressor, but its regulation by DNA methylation and N6-methyladenosine (m6A), and its prognostic significance, remain unclear.We integrated clinical, RNA-sequencing and DNA-methylation data from a TCGA-derived OSCC cohort (n = 25). Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation, false-discovery rate control, and bootstrap confidence intervals. Prognostic value was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier and multivariable Cox regression. Mechanistic effects were examined using MeRIP-qPCR, YTHDF2 RIP-qPCR, actinomycin-D decay assays, luciferase reporters, functional assays, and xenograft models. ZNF677 expression inversely correlated with YTHDF2 (ρ=−0.35) and promoter methylation (ρ=−0.36). Although median-dichotomized survival was not significant, continuous ZNF677 independently predicted better survival (HR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.02–0.67; p = 0.017; C-index = 0.85). METTL3 knockdown reduced ZNF677 m6A enrichment and prolonged transcript half-life, whereas METTL3 overexpression shortened it. Restoring ZNF677 suppressed pro-tumorigenic phenotypes (Hedges’ g = − 0.90; p = 0.003) and cancer-stemness markers (g = − 1.59; p = 0.016).
