title: Early treatment with tecovirimat against mpox disease in cynomolgus macaques.
abstract: BackgroundTecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation.MethodsIn this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures.FindingsTreatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P  0.99).InterpretationIn this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates.FundingThis study was supported by SIGA Technologies.
authors: Rössler A, Aid M, Ayala-Bernot J, Liu J, Russo AT, Grosenbach DW, Lovejoy C, Cook A, Andersen H, Hruby DE, Barouch DH.

title: Life Histories, Breeding Systems, and Life Cycles in Brood-Site Pollination Mutualisms.
abstract: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.
authors: Borges RM.

title: Wolbachia outcompetes mosquito-borne viruses by reprogramming host ATPSβ1-driven ATP metabolism toward symbiotic proliferation.
abstract: Wolbachia endosymbionts confer broad-spectrum resistance to mosquito-borne viruses. While the antiviral metabolites in Wolbachia-Aedes have been identified during viral replication, the core metabolic gene underlying this defense across the entire viral infection cycle remains undefined. Here, we demonstrated for the first time that Wolbachia strongly suppressed the emerging alphavirus Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, extending its known antiviral spectrum. Transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed ATP synthase beta subunit 1 (ATPSβ1) as a key metabolic hub hijacked by both MBV and the symbiont. Without Wolbachia symbiosis, dengue virus and VEEV induced ATPSβ1 to promote viral binding via the viral envelope protein and increased intracellular ATP production for viral replication. Conversely, Wolbachia overrode ATPSβ1-mediated viral binding and redirected ATPSβ1-driven ATP synthesis to fuel its proliferation, strengthening antiviral activity. Pharmacologically, adenosine increased Wolbachia wAlbB density and potently suppressed viral infection in Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus cells. Oligomycin reduced intracellular ATP and inhibited viral infection in Wolbachia-free Ae. aegypti cells. Collectively, Wolbachia repurposes dual-functional ATPSβ1, which governs MBV binding and replication, into a potent antiviral effector through a metabolic tug-of-war over host ATP during symbiont-virus competition. Moreover, we highlight interventions targeting the ATPSβ1-driven metabolism as promising strategies to curb MBV transmission.
authors: Yuan H, Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Wang C, Zhou Y, Ni Q, Li X, Zhang B, Wang Y, Cai L, Liu H, Wang J, Gong J, Zhang M, Xi Z, Pan X.

title: Lyssavirus matrix protein stabilizes RGS4 to suppress ferroptosis via incomplete autophagy and iron metabolic reprogramming.
abstract: Rabies virus (RABV), the prototypical lyssavirus, suppresses neuronal ferroptosis through lipid droplet (LD) biogenesis, which is a critical immune evasion strategy we previously identified. However, the mechanistic link between LD formation and ferroptosis regulation during RABV infection remains poorly defined. Here, we report that RABV upregulate Regulator of G Protein Signaling 4 (RGS4), a ferroptosis-associated regulator, and this induction is strictly dependent on triglyceride synthesis and subsequent LD formation. Functionally, genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RGS4 elevates ferroptosis susceptibility, thereby restricting viral replication. Mechanistically, RGS4 depletion reduces HERC2, impairing the assembly of branched K48/K63 ubiquitin chains on NCOA4, which is essential for its proteasomal degradation, thereby enhancing NCOA4 stability. Stabilized NCOA4 promotes ferritinophagy, leading to degradation of ferritin heavy chain (FTH) and ultimately inducing ferroptosis. Critically, we identified that the lyssavirus matrix (M) protein directly counteracts this pathway: M protein inhibits RGS4 degradation via the Cys/N-degron system through incomplete autophagy, stabilizing RGS4 to maintain HERC2 expression, promote NCOA4 ubiquitination, and attenuate ferritinophagy. This mechanism reduces ferroptosis susceptibility and enables viral replication. Our findings unveil a novel lyssavirus-specific regulatory axis, RGS4-HERC2-NCOA4-FTH, that modulates ferroptosis, highlighting the critical role of ferroptosis in lyssavirus infection and pathogenesis.
authors: Zhao J, Chen P, Sun M, Liang C, Fu ZF, Zhao L, Zhou M.

title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Integration, and the PACA Framework.
abstract: Particulate matter exposure, particularly PM2.5 and ultrafine particles, is a well-established risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity. However, whether pollution-associated cardiovascular abnormalities represent transient toxicity, cumulative injury, developmental programming, aging-like phenotypes, or a genuine alteration in the trajectory of cardiovascular aging remains unresolved. Here, we propose the Pollution-Accelerated Cardiovascular Aging (PACA) framework as a conceptual, hypothesis-generating approach for interpreting this distinction. Rather than proposing new molecular mechanisms, we integrate established pathways, including mitochondrial and redox dysfunction, genomic and epigenetic alterations, cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype signaling, impaired proteostasis, endothelial dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation within an explicit evidentiary framework. We also consider the pulmonary neural cardiac axis as a potential route through which pulmonary sensory activation may influence autonomic regulation, calcium handling, and cardiac electrophysiological function. To distinguish exposure-associated toxicity from evidence consistent with altered cardiovascular aging, we introduce a Temporal-Evidence Matrix that integrates exposure kinetics, life-course timing, persistence and recovery after exposure cessation, exposure response relationships, and longitudinal change relative to age-referenced comparators. Persistence, incomplete recovery, or cumulative loss of cardiovascular reserve support chronic or sustained injury but do not independently establish accelerated aging. Stronger evidence for PACA requires repeated longitudinal demonstration that particulate exposure is associated with a greater rate or altered trajectory of aging-related cardiovascular or biological change than expected from chronological aging. Finally, we propose a tiered biomarker framework that separates candidate biological-aging integrators from mechanistic stress and injury indicators and contextual inflammatory markers, while treating vascular and cardiac functional or imaging measures as complementary cardiovascular phenotypes. The principal contribution of PACA is therefore evidentiary rather than mechanistic, providing a structured approach for testing whether particulate exposure is associated with cardiovascular toxicity alone or with an altered cardiovascular-aging trajectory.
authors: Yadav P, Bhakta-Guha D, Nagarajan D, Mani KP, Mondal R, Guha G, Kurian GA.

title: Myco-degradation of anthraquinone dyes by immobilized white-rot fungal consortium and toxicity assessment.
abstract: Anthraquinone (AQ) dyes widely used in textile industries cause serious environmental and health risk due to their persistence and toxicity. In this context, myco-remediation using white-rot fungal consortium (WRFC) immobilized in chitosan beads demonstrated mixture of AQ dyes (MAQD) biodegradation with enhanced dye decolorization efficiency (97.35%) within 8 h. Further, FTIR analysis confirmed structural disruption of MAQD, including aromatic ring cleavage and functional group transformation. Moreover, LCMS analysis revealed formation of several low molecular weight intermediate organic acids such as phthalic, oxalic, malonic, succinic, fumaric, malic, citric and isocitric acids, suggesting progressive degradation of MAQD and possible microbial transformation of the degradation products. The findings were also validated by SEM and TEM analysis of the chitosan beads which evidenced WRFC immobilization and ultrastructural changes on post exposure to MAQD. The decolorization data were described using a first-order kinetic model, with the highest rate constant observed at 200 ppm. Toxicity assessment of treated (using WRFC immobilized in chitosan beads) MAQD water demonstrated substantial detoxification evidenced by 80% survival of Danio rerio in acute tests, HeLa cell line maintained 84% viability even after 24 h, comet assays indicated reduced DNA damage, and Vigna radiata exhibited normal germination and growth. These findings confirm the synergistic action of enzymatic degradation and biosorption by immobilized WRFC and highlight chitosan beads as a robust carrier matrix. This eco-friendly strategy effectively reduces dye toxicity, offering a promising approach for sustainable industrial wastewater management.
authors: Sahoo PP, Raut S, Sahoo AA, Panda AK, Sen SK.

title: Rifampicin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis implant-associated infections: the therapeutic potential of ceftaroline and daptomycin combinations.
abstract: Rifampicin-resistant (RIF-R) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) pose a significant challenge in managing implant-associated infections (IAIs). However, the functional consequences of rpoB mutations leading to RIF resistance remain poorly characterized, particularly their impact on bacterial fitness and treatment response. We analyzed clinical RIF-R and RIF-susceptible (RIF-S) MRSE isolates from a single-center IAI cohort. RIF-R strains showed delayed exponential growth and exhibited a reduced growth rate during the exponential phase, while biofilm formation remained largely unchanged. To investigate resistance-associated phenotypes, we induced RIF resistance in three clinical RIF-S strains using subinhibitory exposure in a murine tissue cage model. Sequencing revealed rpoB mutations in cluster I, frequently at codons 481 and 486. One mutant, R611 (Ser486Tyr), mirrored mutations from a clinical isolate and exhibited slower growth, reduced cell density, and markedly increased biofilm production with unchanged susceptibilities to vancomycin or daptomycin compared to its RIF-S parent, S611. In vivo, R611 was more competitive in the planktonic phase, while S611 dominated the adherent fraction. Time-kill assays demonstrated strong bactericidal activity of daptomycin combined with ceftaroline or fosfomycin. In the murine model, ceftaroline monotherapy was partially effective, whereas daptomycin/ceftaroline achieved the highest cure rates even against clinical RIF-R strains at the minimum infective dose, with efficacy decreasing markedly at higher bacterial inocula. These findings reveal fitness trade-offs linked to rpoB-mediated resistance and support ceftaroline-based combinations as a potential treatment strategy for RIF-R MRSE in IAIs, particularly when bacterial burden can be reduced.
authors: Woischnig A-K, Kuehl R, Cornillet D, Iizuka A, Schumacher M, Lang C, Egli A, Keller PM, Giulieri SG, Morgenstern M, Clauss M, Khanna N.

title: Novel approaches to target prostate cancer stem cells driving therapy resistance and cancer progression.
abstract: Prostate cancer remains one of the most common malignancies in men, and its global burden continues to rise. Although androgen deprivation therapy and other standard treatments can provide substantial disease control, advanced tumors may progress to castration-resistant prostate cancer, which is associated with poor outcomes. Preclinical and translational evidence implicates prostate cancer stem-like cells (PCSCs) in treatment persistence, progression, and relapse, without establishing them as the sole cause of resistance in patients. PCSC-associated states share functional traits with normal stem cells, including self-renewal and survival under stress; reduced androgen receptor activity occurs in some, but not all, stem-like populations. Their behavior is influenced by the genomic context, including PTEN loss, TP53/RB1 alterations, SPOP mutations, and TMPRSS2-ERG rearrangements, as well as hypoxia, stromal interactions, and inflammatory signaling. These alterations are not specific markers of PCSC identity. Multiple interconnected pathways, notably PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RAS/MAPK, Hedgehog, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo, JAK/STAT, Notch, EGFR, and hypoxia-driven HIF signaling, provide candidate therapeutic targets. Additional strategies include modifying the microenvironment to suppress epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, restoring tumor-suppressive microRNAs, and developing checkpoint inhibitors, vaccines, and CAR-T cells against relevant tumor-associated antigens. Most PCSC-specific evidence remains experimental, even when a pathway-directed agent has clinical activity or regulatory approval in a molecularly selected prostate cancer population. Clinical tumor responses do not by themselves demonstrate selective PCSC depletion. This narrative review distinguishes mechanistic findings from clinical outcomes and considers limitations involving marker specificity, model selection, drug delivery, toxicity, and therapeutic escape. Functionally validated biomarkers and appropriately designed combination trials are needed to determine whether targeting PCSC-associated states can improve durable disease control.
authors: Alatawi FS.

title: Complete genome sequence of Cellulosilyticum lentocellum HNost1007, a cellulolytic strain isolated from ostrich feces.
abstract: The complete genome sequence is described from Cellulosilyticum lentocellum HNost1007, cellulolytic bacteria isolated from ostrich feces. The genome contains a 4,639,609 bp chromosome, 34.4% GC content, 4,262 coding sequences, 25 ribosomal RNAs, and 103 transfer RNAs.
authors: Ogawa Y, Fujita M, Ban-Tokuda T, Matsui H.

title: Complete genome sequence of a co-cultured Phycisphaerae bacterium of the phylum Planctomycetota, strain 2_2a_38c.
abstract: We report the 4.1-Mb complete genome sequence of a novel member from the class Phycisphaerae (Phycisphaerae bacterium strain 2_2a_38c) of the phylum Planctomycetota, which was sequenced from a co-culture with Nocardioides sp. strain 2_2a_38e, originated from the forest soil in Hiroshima, Japan.
authors: Peng Z, Shimomura Y, Mori K, Kato S, Nakashimada Y, Tashiro K, Aoi Y.

title: Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL mapping enables high-sensitivity detection of candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19
abstract: Host genetic variation influences heterogeneity in infectious disease severity. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified 69 lead single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with critical COVID-19, but most lack known regulatory mechanisms. To date, the genetic cis-regulatory effects of critical COVID-19 GWAS lead SNPs have not been systematically characterized across acute illness and convalescent phases in a COVID-19 specific cohort. Here, performing severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTL) mapping and colocalization with critical COVID-19 GWAS signals, we find that host cis-regulatory effects vary across clinical severity and disease phase. We analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,031 patients in the Immunophenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort (IMPACC), a prospective multicenter study of adults hospitalized with COVID-19, profiled across 10 timepoints spanning acute illness and convalescence. We identified 23 GWAS lead SNPs that colocalized with cis-eQTLs at 26 candidate causal genes, with 16 detectable only when severity stratification and longitudinal sampling were incorporated. A colocalized, protective allele (chr19:4,717,660) at the TMIGD2 locus upregulated TMIGD2 expression exclusively during the acute phase in the prolonged-critical/fatal cohort, with no detectable effect in the rapid-recovery cohort. Our results show that host genetic effects on critical COVID-19 can be context-dependent, with cis-regulatory effects varying across clinical severity and disease phase. Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL designs have greater sensitivity to identify candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19 GWAS associations than single-timepoint cross-sectional studies.

title: Snail restricts SARS-CoV-2 entry by limiting ACE2 expression as part of broader remodelling of epithelial determinants of viral tropism
abstract: ABSTRACT  Pre-existing state of the host cell is a major determinant of the host susceptibility to viral infection. Here, we identify the epithelial-mesenchymal transition transcription factor Snail as a host restriction factor for SARS-CoV-2. Snail loss markedly increased SARS-CoV-2 replication, whereas Snail overexpression and complementation restricted viral replication. Transcriptomic analysis of Snail knockout cells revealed remodelling of epithelial surface-associated programs, including apical membrane, brush border, and junctional pathways. ACE2, the cellular receptor for SARS-CoV-2, was among the genes upregulated in Snail knockout cells. Snail negatively regulated  ACE2 transcription, leading to reduced ACE2 transcript and protein abundance and, consequently, lower SARS-CoV-2 entry. Consistent with this,  ACE2 promoter activity was higher in Snail knockout cells, which was reduced following Snail complementation. As a means to counter Snail’s antiviral functions, SARS-CoV-2 infection progressively depleted Snail protein in different cell culture models, while  SNAI1 transcript abundance was surprisingly maintained or increased under the same conditions. Proteasome inhibition and protein-turnover analyses failed to account for this depletion. We find that SARS-CoV-2 infection resulted in reduced association of  SNAI1 with polysomes at later stages of infection coinciding with virus-induced host translational suppression, resulting in lower protein synthesis. Together, these findings identify Snail as a regulator of the epithelial entry landscape that limits ACE2-associated SARS-CoV-2 entry and shapes cellular permissiveness, with broader implications for cellular determinants of viral tropism. SARS-CoV-2, in turn, progressively depletes this short-lived antiviral regulator, revealing how virus-induced translational shutoff can remodel pre-existing host cell states and thereby alter cellular susceptibility during infection.  IMPORTANCE  Cellular permissiveness is a major determinant of viral tropism. Host transcriptional programs are well known to shape cellular identity and surface composition, but their contribution to viral susceptibility is less often viewed as a form of host restriction. We previously showed that the epithelial-mesenchymal transition transcription factors Snail and Slug restrict multiple RNA viruses. Here, we show that Snail also limits SARS-CoV-2 infection by restricting ACE2 expression and by remodelling the epithelial surface landscape. SARS-CoV-2 neutralizes this threat by translationally repressing  SNAI1 as part of the global translation suppression. We show that loss of Snail remodels surface-associated cellular programs and establishes a more permissive state. Together, these findings connect two aspects of host-virus interaction: transcriptional programs that establish cellular permissiveness and viral processes that can subsequently alter them. They position Snail as a broader regulator of the cellular landscape that influences viral entry and tropism.
authors: Sahoo PP, Sah V, Harshan KH.

title: Dynamics and activation of the  Legionella  Type IV secretion system
abstract: Legionella pneumophila uses the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system (T4SS) to translocate hundreds of effector proteins into host cells, yet how this transenvelope machine assembles and becomes secretion competent remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and  in situ single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we resolve distinct structural and functional states of the native Dot/Icm T4SS. Unexpectedly, the T4SS predominantly occupies a resting state containing the outer-membrane core complex but lacking the inner-membrane complex, including DotA. Recruitment of inner-membrane components establishes a fully assembled but secretion-inactive primed state. A 3.6-Å cryo-EM structure of the DotO–DotI–DotJ–IcmT complex, integrated with  in situ reconstructions, reveals how membrane-associated components organize DotO into a hexamer-of-dimers ATPase platform. Upon host contact, the T4SS undergoes extensive conformational remodeling while preserving its transenvelope scaffold. Activation involves dilation of the DotG outer-membrane gate and transformation of the DotA–IcmX protochannel into an open translocation conduit that extends beyond the bacterial surface. Substrate-associated state exhibit further channel expansion, revealing structural plasticity associated with effector translocation. During macrophage infection, the extracellular conduit bridges the bacterial and host membranes, establishing a direct pathway for effector delivery. Together, our findings reveal a stepwise mechanism of Dot/Icm T4SS channel assembly and activation, in which coordinated remodeling of the secretion channel converts a resting apparatus into a host-engaged translocation machine.
authors: Heydari S, Yue J, Yang Z, Shu S, Wang H, Mi W, Roy C, Liu J.

title: Genotyping of Indian Himalayas wild-growing cannabis reveals population structure along varying environmental gradients
abstract: Cannabis sativa L. is a multipurpose crop regaining interest after decades of prohibition, highlighting the need to better characterize and conserve its genetic diversity . This study focuses on wild-growing cannabis populations from northern India, a region where the species has been present for thousands of years but remains understudied. We genotyped 478 individuals from different locations using genotyping by sequencing. Four geographically structured genetic clusters were identified and associated with different environmental conditions. The population structure appeared shallow with no significant difference in heterozygosity and nucleotide diversity between inferred clusters, which suggested an unrestricted gene flow between populations in this highly mountainous region. Northern Indian samples were associated with the previously described drug-type feral population and exhibited a higher heterozygosity and nucleotide diversity than cultivated populations which is typical for wild-growing open pollinated plants. A genome wide association study was performed based on traits of interest recorded in the field and allowed to identify a candidate marker potentially associated with inflorescence density. This study provides a first perspective on how wild-growing cannabis populations are structured in northern India according to environmental conditions and highlights the need for conservation of wild and feral populations as a valuable reservoir of genetic diversity.
authors: Devèze T, de Ronne M, Maire V, Chauhan R, Letanneur C, Gazal S, Sharma N, Rathore M, Baliyan S, Rhéaume K, Lamara M, Torkamaneh D, Chauhan H, Germain H.

title: Gene Therapy for Ovarian Cancer: From Bench to Bedside: Overcoming Barriers to Clinical Translation
abstract: Gene therapy has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for ovarian cancer (OC), with the potential to complement current treatments by targeting mechanisms that sustain residual and treatment-resistant diseases. Recent advances in genome editing, RNA therapeutics, viral and non-viral delivery systems, and engineered immune cell therapies have expanded the investigation landscape. However, despite encouraging preclinical progress, clinical translation remains limited by tumor heterogeneity, incomplete delivery across disseminated lesions, insufficient transgene expression or cellular persistence, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, modality-specific safety risks, and, particularly, biological challenges posed by peritoneal metastases (PMs), the dominant manifestation of advanced OC. This critical narrative review examines the molecular context, therapeutic platforms, delivery strategies, and clinical barriers relevant to gene therapy for OC. Particular emphasis is placed on PMs, functional target engagement across heterogeneous lesions, integration with established therapies, and biomarker-guided clinical developments. We also consider the translational requirements for genome editing, RNA therapeutics, viral and non-viral delivery systems, and engineered immune cell therapies. Clinical translation will depend on matching patient and target selection to the delivery platform and route while prospectively defining treatment timing, combination strategies, and pharmacodynamic endpoints.
authors: Tamura K, Koyanagi T, Takahashi K, Takahashi Y, Taneichi A, Saga Y, Takei Y, Fujiwara H.

title: Commercial and Novel Drug-Loaded Coatings with Anticoagulant and/or Antibacterial Functions for Clinical Applications.
abstract: Drug-loaded coatings significantly improve the bioactivities of multiple medical devices. The most widespread applications are assembling anticoagulant coatings on blood-contacting medical devices to enhance blood compatibility and applying antibacterial coatings to prevent device-induced infection. Notably, a vicious cycle between bacterial infection and thrombosis may result in deterioration of condition and even lead to treatment failure. Thrombosis caused by blood incompatibility of medical devices provides niduses for bacterial colonization, whereas bacterial endotoxins accelerate thrombosis by activating platelets. In some situations, the interactional process can also trigger inflammatory responses and calcification processes. Therefore, the demands for anticoagulant and antibacterial are necessary and mutually influenced. This review presents a summary of current commercial drug-loaded anticoagulant coatings and a detailed report on novel drug-loaded coatings with anticoagulant and/or antibacterial effects. We highlight the synthesis and assembly techniques, drug-release duration, and biofunctional behavior of referenced coatings. Based on careful comparison and comprehensive summary of the state-of-the-art literature, this review reveals the difficulties in large-scale production of the emerging coatings and the functional differences compared to the existing commercial coatings, and predicts the general process for manufacturing and commercialization.
authors: Yu Q, Sheng K, Long J, Gao Y, Peng P, Bao T, Yan Y, Zheng X.

title: Adenovirus as a Causative Agent of an Acute Gastroenteritis Outbreak in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Introduction  Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a cause of childhood morbidity and may be associated with human adenovirus (HAdV) infection. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of HAdV in fecal samples from children with AGE in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, as well as to molecularly characterize the identified strains and evaluate their cytopathic effects in cell culture. Methods  A total of 131 samples were analyzed using the nested polymerase chain reaction (Nested-PCR) technique. Molecular characterization was performed through Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, while Vero cell cultures were used to investigate the occurrence of cytopathic effects. Results  Of the samples analyzed, 13 (9.9%) tested positive for HAdV, while 118 (90.1%) were negative. The highest detection frequency was observed in children aged three years or younger, particularly those under one year of age. Phylogenetic analysis identified variants related to HAdV-F41 and HAdV-B3, revealing genetic differences and distinct clustering patterns compared with reference sequences. In cell culture, cytopathic effects were observed four days after inoculation, although further analyses are required to confirm productive viral replication. Conclusion  These findings demonstrate the presence of HAdV in the samples studied and contribute to understanding its genetic diversity and circulation in Salvador, highlighting the importance of epidemiological surveillance and further studies on its role in the etiology of childhood AGE.
authors: Vidal BP, Neves SO, Santos IP, Sardi SI, Campos GS.

title: Detection and Characterization of Human Bocavirus in Stool Samples from an Acute Gastroenteritis Outbreak in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, in 2024
abstract: Introduction  Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a global public health problem and a major cause of mortality in low- and lower-middle-income countries. Human bocavirus (HBoV) is among the viral agents associated with this condition. Therefore, investigating the presence of HBoV in cases of AGE in Salvador, Bahia, as well as its prevalence and circulating strains, is important. Objective  To investigate the occurrence of HBoV infection during an AGE outbreak in Salvador. Methods  A total of 178 samples were analyzed for HBoV using nested polymerase chain reaction (nested PCR), and the amplification products were visualized by agarose gel electrophoresis. HBoV was detected in 5.7% of the samples analyzed. Conclusion  This study contributes to the understanding of HBoV epidemiology as a secondary agent associated with acute gastroenteritis during a norovirus outbreak in Salvador. Continued investigation and identification of the etiological agents involved in outbreaks are essential for evaluating the causes of AGE. These findings also highlight the need for broader diagnostic approaches and the importance of phylogenetic analysis for monitoring and controlling viral infections.
authors: Vidal BP, Neves SO, Santos IP, Sardi SI, Campos GS.

title: Hexosyl transfer  via  a covalent intermediate within a dual retaining and inverting enzyme
abstract: Bifunctional glycosyltransferases underpin biosynthesis of essential glycans, including bacterial capsular antigens, and eukaryotic glycosaminoglycans. Typically, these enzymes transfer hexose sugars from activated nucleotide-phosphate donors, forming new glycosidic bonds with either retention or inversion of anomeric stereochemistry. Retaining hexosyl transfer typically proceeds  via non-covalent  S  N i  -type pathways, but recent studies of octulosyl Kdo-transferases have reignited debate over covalent mechanisms. Here we comprehensively dissected the activity of the archetypal bifunctional glycosyltransferase PmHS2, providing X-ray structures of ligand complexes alongside atomistic simulations to delineate full substrate-to-product reaction trajectories. Combined computational, biochemical and evolutionary evidence suggests that PmHS2 retaining GlcNAc-transfer likely proceeds  via a previously undescribed covalent mechanism, involving considerable assistance from departing nucleotide-phosphate rotation. In mapping reaction pathways, we also report the first example of a glycosyl donor substrate coopted as an acceptor, which enables enzymatic self-priming for polymerization. These new covalent and self-priming functionalities highlight unexplored routes to modulate or inhibit polysaccharide biosynthesis.
authors: Sağıroğlugil M, Piniello B, Leanca MA, Kitano ES, Mycroft-West CJ, Papadakis G, Gafitescu MA, Mohammed S, Davis BG, Rovira C, Wu L.

title: Molecular mechanism of albicidin-dependent transcription activation by the antibiotic resistance factor AlbA
abstract: The escalating spread of antimicrobial resistance demands antibiotics with novel mechanisms of action. Albicidin is a potent DNA gyrase inhibitor produced by  Xanthomonas species, and bacteria counter its activity through resistance mechanisms including the albicidin-sequestering protein AlbA from  Klebsiella oxytoca . AlbA is a MerR family transcription activator that binds albicidin and stimulates expression of the  albA gene, but how ligand recognition is coupled to transcription activation has remained unclear. Here, we use cryogenic electron microscopy and complementary biochemical assays to define the mechanism of AlbA-dependent transcription activation. Structures of transcription complexes reveal that AlbA remodels the promoter, repositioning the −35 element for productive σ  70 recognition and RNA polymerase engagement. Albicidin does not measurably alter AlbA’s DNA affinity or the architecture of the mature open complex. Instead, transcription kinetics and experiments bypassing promoter opening indicate that albicidin selectively facilitates a promoter opening-dependent transition. AlbA is released upon synthesis of approximately five nucleotides, concomitant with downstream DNA melting, bubble translocation and upstream DNA rewinding rather than DNA scrunching. Together, these findings establish a sequential mechanism in which AlbA remodels promoter architecture, while albicidin tunes the kinetic transition to promoter opening, linking antibiotic recognition to induction of its sequestration machinery.
authors: Helmer CP, Hilal T, Said N, Boyakova Y, Eulberg T, Schnoor SB, Bodescu M, Mainz A, Milles S, Loll B, Süssmuth RD, Wahl MC.

title: Sodium nitrophenolates as a potential tool for the management of grapevine trunk diseases
abstract: Fungal trunk diseases represent a major constraint on the production of grapevine and other perennial crops, while effective curative control methods remain limited. This study evaluated the antifungal and defence-modulating effects of the sodium nitrophenolate based product Atonik® against selected fungi associated with trunk diseases.  In vitro efficacy was tested against ten fungal pathogens, and its effect against  Eutypa lata was further evaluated in grapevine under  in planta conditions. Atonik® inhibited mycelial growth in a pathogen and concentration dependent manner, with the strongest effects at the highest tested concentration observed against  Cadophora luteo-olivacea ,  E. lata , and  Phaeoacremonium minimum . In grapevine,  E. lata caused a mean lesion length of 48.38 mm, whereas Atonik® treatment reduced it to 12.29 mm. Absolute qPCR indicated higher  VvSOD transcript abundance in treated plants. RNA-seq analysis identified 168 genes associated with infection and 43 genes associated with treatment. The results suggest that sodium nitrophenolates may reduce wood necrosis caused by  E. lata through a combination of direct antifungal activity and modulation of grapevine defence responses.
authors: Čechová J, Štůsková K, Přinosilová P, Holcová L, Homolová D, Špetík M, Babuška P, Dvořák O, Eichmeier A.

title: Cytoplasmic localization of 5hmC reveals RNA hydroxymethylation in breast cancer
abstract: DNA methylation (5-methylcytosine, 5mC) is a major repressive epigenetic mark that can be iteratively oxidized by ten-eleven-translocation (TET) enzymes to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC); beyond DNA, modifications of RNA can also affect transcript stability and processing, yet RNA hydroxymethylation remains unexplored in breast cancer (BC). Here, we identify a quantifiable cytoplasmic 5hmC signal in BC cell lines and, more prominently, in human BC tissue, using immunoassays and digital pathology, and confirm with an adapted, RNase-sensitive, RNA-specific ELISA that this signal reflects hydroxymethylation of total RNA and mRNA. Cytoplasmic 5hmC was significantly enriched in triple-negative (ER-/PR-/HER2-) and grade 3 tumors, and correlated with increased cytoplasmic TET2/TET3 in tissue and  TET3 upregulation in TCGA. As a leading candidate mechanism,  TET3 expression was associated with RNA-processing/spliceosomal transcripts, and  TET3 knockdown in three TNBC cell lines reduced a subset of these targets, independently supported across 70 DepMap breast cancer lines.
authors: Wen J, Del Bel Belluz L, Ottaviani S, Poyia F, Yu H, Sachdev S, El Eid L, Garner K, Mistry K, Hayes E, Moderau N, Chandrasinghe P, Stebbing J, Cereser B.

title: Reconstruction of a rare Δ10 desaturation pathway enables production of yellow peach moth pheromone precursors in  Camelina sativa
abstract: ABSTRACT  Sex pheromones are environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional insecticides for pest control. The high synthesis cost, however, has restricted large-scale application. Plant-based biofactories provide a promising, sustainable route for cost-effective production that could facilitate the broader use of pheromone-based pest control. Mating disruption of the yellow peach moth,  Conogethes punctiferalis –a serious pest of fruit trees and field crops in East Asia–can be achieved using (  E )-10-hexadecenal and (  Z )-10-hexadecenal, two components of its sex pheromone. To enable rational reconstruction of the biosynthetic pathway towards these unusual fatty acid derivatives in heterologous production systems, we first elucidated their biosynthesis by combining  in vivo labeling experiments, transcriptomics and functional characterization of candidate desaturase and reductase genes using  Nicotiana benthamiana and yeast expression systems. We identified a rare Δ10 fatty acyl desaturase that catalyzes the production of both (  E )- 10- and (  Z )-10-hexadecenoic acids, along with a downstream fatty acyl reductase with higher activity on the  E isomer. We further introduced this Δ10 desaturase together with an acyl-ACP thioesterase-1 into  Camelina sativa to redirect seed lipid metabolism towards the accumulation of the pheromone precursor fatty acids. After four generations of selection, we obtained stably inherited Camelina lines accumulating up to 4.7% of target fatty acids in total seed lipids, with individual seeds containing up to 8.3 μg, without significant effects on plant growth or seed viability. These findings demonstrate how elucidating moth pheromone biosynthetic pathways can support the development of sustainable biotechnological production systems for pheromone-based pest management.
authors: Hou X, Wang H, He P, Jin Y, Gao X, Lassance J, Löfstedt C, Ding B.

title: Closing the conformational cycle of the beta-barrel assembly machinery
abstract: The β-barrel assembly machinery (BAM) catalyzes the folding and insertion of β-barrel outer membrane proteins (OMPs) in Gram-negative bacteria without an external energy source. BAM comprises the central subunit BamA and associated lipoproteins, with BamA forming a conformationally dynamic lateral gate. Although substrate-engaged structures have revealed key steps in OMP assembly, how substrate-free BamA closes its lateral gate and which conformations it adopts in a lipid bilayer remain unclear. Here, we determined cryo-EM structures of the  Escherichia coli (E.coli) BAM complex in three detergents and in Saposin A nanodiscs composed of  E. coli polar lipids. In addition to the canonical outward-open (OO) state, we identified an occluded (OC) state in which both the lateral gate and the periplasmic opening of the BamA barrel are closed. OC predominated in lipid-reconstituted BAM that retained OMP-folding activity, indicating that this state is substantially populated in a functional BAM ensemble within a lipid bilayer. We also identified a semi-occluded (sOC) state in which β1–β2 adopts an OC-like closed position while rearrangement of β16 remains incomplete. Comparison of OO, sOC, and OC reveals asynchronous rearrangements of the β1–β2 and β16 regions, with β1–β2 movement can occur without complete repositioning of β16. Re-examination of previously reported lipid-embedded BAM structures further highlights the importance of local map quality at the gate region for conformational assignment. Together, our findings expand the BamA conformational landscape beyond the conventional OO–inward-open (IO) framework to include OC and sOC as distinct structural states associated with lateral-gate closure following OMP insertion.
authors: Kato T, Shigematsu H, Takeuchi K, Suzuki M, Nitta R, Imasaki T.

title: Source-linked multispecialty clinical reasoning and tumour-board decision-making in colorectal cancer
abstract: Clinical records preserve patient findings and final recommendations but rarely capture how specialists select evidence, develop alternative interpretations, disagree, and converge on a management strategy. We describe a dataset derived from ten retrospectively selected, completed cases of histologically confirmed colorectal cancer. For each case, an administrator uploaded de-identified textual clinical records to an authenticated web-based annotation platform. A medical oncologist, surgical oncologist, and radiation oncologist, each with more than ten years of clinical experience, independently linked relevant source fragments to patient-specific interpretations and documented clinical problems, differential hypotheses, uncertainty, and diagnostic and treatment strategies. After the three records were locked, a large language model generated candidate questions for review by the tumour-board chair. The four physicians then discussed each case online; recordings were automatically transcribed and verified by two medical residents. The dataset comprises 30 source-linked specialist reasoning records, 10 verified case-level discussion transcripts, 10 final tumour-board decisions, and associated provenance and quality-control metadata. It supports research on evidence-grounded reasoning, cross-specialty disagreement, multidisciplinary decision-making, and multi-agent clinical decision support.

title: Difficult-to-Treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa Harboring Tandem Guiana Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamases: A Case Report​
abstract: We report a case of a patient, who had recently been hospitalized outside the United States and developed a difficult-to-treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) identified tandem Guiana extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (blaGES-19/20). We highlight the value of WGS and the challenges faced in managing infections with organisms displaying unexpected resistance mechanisms.

title: Intratumoral influenza A virus infection drives platinum resistance and invasive reprogramming in NSCLC
abstract: Abstract  Respiratory viral infections are frequent in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet whether intratumoral viral presence directly influences tumor behavior and therapeutic response remains unknown. Here, we identify a respiratory virus-associated drug metabolism program (REVIS-DM), predominantly expressed by tumor cells and linked to poor clinical outcome. Across multiple NSCLC cohorts, a subgroup of tumors with concurrent high REVIS-DM, interferon-stimulated gene and antiviral signatures was associated with reduced survival and increased relapse after chemotherapy. Consistent with this antiviral profile, Influenza A virus (IAV) transcripts were detected in NSCLC and associated with poor outcome and relapse. Mechanistically, IAV infection induced xenobiotic detoxification, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, invasion, and platinum resistance in vitro and in vivo. These effects required viral sensing and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling but were independent of type I/III interferon pathways. Together, our findings establish intratumoral IAV infection as a previously unrecognized driver of tumor-cell plasticity and chemoresistance in NSCLC, revealing virus-induced metabolic vulnerabilities with potential therapeutic relevance.

title: Whole-Genome Profiling of Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci and Mammaliicoccus from Broiler Chickens: Insights into Mobilome and Resistome Diversity
abstract: Abstract    Staphylococcus  species in poultry are emerging opportunistic pathogens and significant reservoirs of virulence and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In this study, whole-genome sequencing of eight isolates (  Staphylococcus simulans  ,  S. shinii  ,  S. arlettae  ,  S. gallinarum  ,  Mammaliicoccus sciuri  , and  M. lentus  ) isolated from infected broiler chickens in India was conducted to analyze their genome comparison and identify plasmids, phages, mobile genetic elements, CRISPR-Cas, antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes. An open pan-genome with 12,200 pan-genes, 243 core genes, and 7,077 strain-specific genes was observed by pan-genome analysis. Plasmid profiling revealed a variety of replicons, including substantial plasmid diversity in  S. gallinarum, S. arlettae, S. shinii  , and  M. lentus  and conserved rep10 and rep7a were found in all isolates. There were 150–193 MGE–associated genes per genome found by mobile genetic element analysis.  Siphoviridae  prophages were only found in  Staphylococcus  species. CRISPR arrays were found in all eight genomes and Type II system (cas1, cas2, cas9) was found in  S.simulans  but  S. shinii, S. arlettae, S. gallinarum  , and  M. sciuri  had Type I systems (cas3). On the other hand, the absence of cas proteins in  M. lentus  suggested a degraded immunological locus. In antimicrobial resistance gene analysis there are 133 AMR genes covering key antibiotic classes were found, and 26 of the genes were conserved in all six species. Additionally, a wide range of virulence factors were found, with S. simulans exhibiting the largest profile. These factors included capsular polysaccharides (  cap  ), iron-acquisition systems (  sbn  ,  isd  ), toxins, and secretion machinery (Types II, VI, and VII). All things considered, poultry-derived CoNS and  Mammaliicoccus  have large mobilomes, a variety of AMR genes, and fluctuating immunological responses, highlighting their function as hyper-permissive, multidrug-resistant reservoirs with serious zoonotic and veterinary concerns.
authors: Gopalram VT, Rengaraj K, Uthandakalaipandian R, Mariakuttikan J.

title: Assessment and Evolution of Surface-Subsurface Landform Connectivity of Jabal Al Qarah in Saudi Arabia: A Potential World-Class Geomorphological Heritage
abstract: Abstract  Worldwide, surface and subsurface connectivity of geomorphic processes, landform diversity, and their geoheritage importance are very interesting topics. Jabal Al Qarah is a mesa (residual hill), located in Al Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. This mesa offers unique diversity in surface and subsurface landforms. Therefore, the scope of this paper is a detailed geomorphological heritage assessment of Jabal Al Qarah, which was a gap. The geomorphological heritage assessment is considered based on scientific and additional value. The key landforms in Jabal Al Qarah are vertical slots, a rill network, a rectangular fault system, a rectangular cave system, a rock pillar, and an in-situ boulder, which belong to the IUCN Geoheritage Theme: Erosional, Cave and Karst System. Jabal Al Qarah comprises a deposition of marine sedimentation, which is followed by the orogeny of the tablelands and plateaus in the eastern part of Saudi Arabia. Due to weathering and denudation, this mesa unit detached from the Shedgum Plateau and formed the mesa. Following the rectangular fault system that is exposed at the surface, weathering forms a rectangular cave system. Jabal Al Qarah is a unique example with spectacular surface and subsurface landform diversity, high representation, well accessible, and a global example of the complex geomorphic process associated with cave formation. Therefore, Jabal Al Qarah is a strong candidate for inclusion in the world-class geomorphological heritage.
authors: Sen S.

title: Artificial Lemming Algorithm-Optimized CrossKAN for Multi-Energy Load Forecasting
abstract: Abstract  Accurate multi-energy load forecasting requires models that capture nonlinear, cross-variable and time-varying dependencies without imposing excessive computational cost. Here we present CrossKAN, a lightweight forecasting model whose hyperparameters are optimized using the Artificial Lemming Algorithm (ALA). A triple-correlation analysis first combines the Maximal Information Coefficient, SHAP importance and sliding-window correlation to rank candidate inputs according to statistical dependence, predictive contribution and temporal stability. CrossKAN retains the cross-correlation and patch-embedding backbone of CrossLinear, but replaces its linear forecasting head with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network that learns nonlinear spline mappings. Across electricity, heating and cooling forecasting tasks, CrossKAN reduced MAE, RMSE and MAPE by 13.2–17.6% relative to the strongest baseline for each metric on the primary dataset. On Building Data Genome 2, the model reduced six MAE and RMSE measures by 1.2–12.0%. These results suggest that concentrating nonlinear modelling in the forecasting head can improve accuracy while preserving a lightweight encoder, within the datasets and evaluation settings considered here.
authors: Lv Z, Yan J, Hou F, Li Y, Sun P.

title: varianTalker: a Nextflow Framework for Scalable, Portable and Clinically Oriented Variant Annotation, Prioritization, and Review
abstract: Abstract  Accurate variant interpretation is essential for molecular tumour boards and precision oncology, yet available tools are often fragmented, proprietary, or difficult to maintain. We present varianTalker, a framework implemented in Nextflow DSL2 that integrates ten complementary annotation resources (Funcotator, ANNOVAR, CancerVar, InterVar, ReNOVo, CIViC, AlphaMissense, PharmGKB, ESCAT, and ClinVar) within a containerised, batch-capable workflow. The pipeline supports somatic and germline variants, applies the appropriate classification framework, and accepts outputs from Thermo Fisher Ion Torrent/Oncomine, Illumina DRAGEN, and nf-core Sarek. Consistent consequence reporting is achieved through MANE Select transcripts, while dedicated update modules, custom institutional annotations, and explicit resource versioning support reproducible analyses. A PostgreSQL-backed variant store reuses previously computed annotations, reducing analysis time by an average of 92% when queried variants have already been annotated. Integration of multiple sources provided additional complementary evidence to 47.1% of somatic and 86.9% of germline variants of uncertain significance. In addition, configurable filtering reduced thousands of annotated variants to tens of clinically relevant candidates for interactive review in a Streamlit application. Applied to retrospective cohorts, varianTalker offers a scalable, transparent framework for reproducible variant interpretation.
authors: Mariani GA, Barreca M, Belloni E, Fassi V, Maria R, Nero C, Derenzini E, Tarella C, Mazzarella L, Pelicci PG, Ronchini C, Frigè G, Zhan Y.

title: CNV-GWAS identifies 14 novel Autism-associated loci and distinct effects on Cognitive Ability
abstract: Abstract  Copy number variants (CNVs) are well-established risk factors for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Prior rare-variant association studies have predominantly relied on family-based cohorts, limiting statistical power and identification of novel loci. In addition, it has been challenging to distinguish the effects of CNVs for ASD from the impact on cognitive ability. Here we present a large CNV association study of ASD, analyzing 29,696 autistic and 528,576 control individuals, with cognitive ability data available for over half of the participants. We used two complementary designs, leveraging related and unrelated controls. The unrelated case-control analysis yielded substantially more associations than the family-based design, while effect estimates remained concordant across approaches and showed no evidence of stratification bias. Among recurrent neurodevelopmental CNVs, we identified 19 ASD associations, 8 of which had not been previously linked to ASD, including duplications at 7q11 (ZNF92) and 9p24 (DMRT1), previously associated with schizophrenia. Across the genome, we identified 14 novel candidate CNV loci, several previously associated with risk for schizophrenia, ADHD, or other psychiatric conditions by common and rare variant studies. Cognitive ability data allowed us to delineate two distinct genetic architectures: CNVs predominantly associated with ASD and other mental health conditions, which were enriched for duplications and encompassed less-constrained genes; and CNVs affecting both ASD and cognition, which were enriched for deletions. Together, these findings suggest that classes of variants, rather than genes, may show preferential phenotypic associations.

title: High seroprevalence of Brucella spp. antibodies in small-ruminant milk and poor brucellosis-related awareness among herders in Maiduguri, northeastern Nigeria
abstract: Abstract    Background:  Brucellosis is an important bacterial zoonosis affecting livestock production and public health, particularly in resource-limited settings where contact between humans and infected animals and consumption of unpasteurized animal products are common. In Nigeria, information on  Brucella  exposure among small ruminants and the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAPs) of their handler’s remains limited. This study assessed the seroprevalence of anti-  Brucella  antibodies in milk from sheep and goats and evaluated brucellosis-related KAPs among small-ruminant herders in Maiduguri, northeastern Nigeria.  Methods:  A cross-sectional study was conducted among small-ruminant flocks and herders in Maiduguri. A total of 184 fresh, unpasteurized milk samples, comprising 92 from sheep and 92 from goats, were collected from 14 purposively selected flocks using simple random sampling within flocks. Samples were screened for anti-  Brucella  antibodies using a commercial indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (iELISA). Because the iELISA does not differentiate among  Brucella  species, species-specific molecular confirmation was undertaken on 14 randomly selected ELISA-positive samples using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), owing to financial constraints. A separate KAP survey was conducted among 360 randomly selected small-ruminant herders drawn from a broader operational sampling frame comprising herders associated with the 60 identified flocks and additional larger flocks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary and multivariable logistic regression.  Results:  Anti-  Brucella  antibodies were detected in 32.1% (95% CI: 25.4–39.3) of the 184 milk samples, with significantly higher seroprevalence among goats (54.4%; 95% CI: 43.6–64.8) than sheep (10.0%; 95% CI: 4.6–17.8). At the flock level, 71.4% (95% CI: 41.9–91.6) of the 14 sampled flocks had at least one ELISA-positive animal. Seropositivity was significantly associated with species, source of animals, parity, history of abortion, body condition score, and reported flock-level antibiotic use. However, these associations should be interpreted cautiously because the study was cross-sectional, antibiotic use was assessed at flock level based on herder recall, and the animal-level regression analysis did not explicitly account for clustering within flocks. Of the 14 ELISA-positive samples tested by PCR, four (28.6%) were positive for  B. melitensis  DNA, all from sheep, while 10 were PCR-negative. Thus, molecular evidence of  B. melitensis  was restricted to the tested subset and was not used to estimate population-level  B. melitensis  prevalence. The KAP assessment revealed generally poor levels, with only 20.8%, 17.2%, and 16.9% of herders demonstrating good knowledge, positive attitudes, and appropriate practices, respectively. Breeding system, years of experience, economic status, educational level, and farming system were independently associated with KAP outcomes.  Conclusions:  The high seroprevalence of anti-  Brucella  antibodies indicates substantial  Brucella  exposure among small ruminants in the study area, while detection of  B. melitensis  DNA in a limited subset provides species-specific molecular evidence of  B. melitensis  among some tested animals. The combination of substantial serological evidence and poor brucellosis-related KAPs highlights an important One Health concern, particularly in relation to raw milk consumption and unsafe handling of potentially infectious materials. Strengthening veterinary extension and surveillance services, improving herder awareness, promoting milk pasteurization and safer handling of abortion materials, and strengthening collaboration between veterinary and public health services are warranted to reduce the potential risk of brucellosis transmission in the study area.
authors: Tijjani B, Jajere SM, Tijjani AO, Sadiq MA, Beauvais WA.

title: Five-Year Analysis (2019-2023) of Anatoxin-a (ATX-a) concentrations in Lake Anna, Virginia, USA: Implications for Future Freshwater Cyanotoxin Monitoring
abstract: Abstract  Harmful algal blooms (HABs) are an increasing concern for the health of freshwater systems worldwide. Cyanobacterial HABs (cyanoHABs) have recently been reported in Lake Anna, Virginia, and low levels of the neurotoxin anatoxin-a (ATX-a) have been observed. Here, we provide a comprehensive report of ATX-a concentrations at multiple locations in the upper tributaries and northern sections of Lake Anna over five consecutive years (2019–2023). ATX-a concentrations ranged from 0.053 to 1.64 ppb, and 14% (13/91) of samples exceeded Virginia’s drinking water advisory threshold of 0.4 ppb. Elevated ATX-a concentrations were most frequently observed in shallow northern tributaries during summer, coinciding with periods of increased cyanobacterial abundance. ATX-a was quantified using two different methods, each with a distinct limit of detection (LOD). title: 4-Diketopyrrole-2-carboxamide derivatives affecting HBV capsid assembly: structure-activity relationship around the GLP-26 scaffold.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden with limited curative options. Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) have emerged as a promising antiviral strategy by disrupting nucleocapsid formation and suppressing cccDNA amplification. In this study, we discuss the structure-activity relationship (SAR) around the 4-diketopyrrole-2-carboxamide scaffold of GLP-26, focusing on modifying the aniline moiety and the oxoacetamide region, and introducing alternative acetamide groups. Compounds were synthesized through efficient coupling strategies, including microwave-assisted amidation, and several analogs exhibited potent inhibition of HBV DNA replication in HepAD38 cells, with EC50 values in the low nanomolar range and minimal cytotoxicity. This work broadens the chemical space surrounding GLP-26 and provides a valuable roadmap for designing new scaffolds for next-generation HBV CAMs.
authors: Chen Z, Zhou S, Liu P, Wiseman J, Zhou L, Fan CV, Bowers HB, Salman M, Verma K, Monroe DR, Downs-Bowen J, Patel D, Bassit L, Schinazi RF, Amblard F.

title: Upregulation of NKAIN1 Predicts Poor Prognosis and Shapes Immune Infiltration in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma: An Integrated Bioinformatic and Experimental Study.
abstract: IntroductionThis research sought to explore the expression profile, prognostic relevance, and immune- related functions of Sodium/Potassium Transporting ATPase Interacting 1 (NKAIN1) in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC) through integrated bioinformatic approaches followed by experimental validation.MethodsRNA-seq data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed to assess NKAIN1 expression across cancer types, with a specific comparison between UCEC and healthy tissues. Differential expression, survival outcomes, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration patterns, Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB), mRNA stemness index (mRNAsi), and drug sensitivity correlations were evaluated using R packages. Samples with missing clinical data were excluded from the respective clinical correlation analyses. Protein- level expression was confirmed via the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) database, while mRNA levels were measured in UCEC cell lines (Ishikawa, KLE) and Endometrial Stromal Cells (ESC) by qRT-PCR.ResultsNKAIN1 was markedly elevated in UCEC tissues and cell lines compared to normal controls (p DiscussionThe correlative findings suggest that NKAIN1 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker in UCEC, with potential roles in tumor progression, immune evasion, and stemness maintenance. The correlations with immune infiltration and checkpoint genes highlight its relevance in tumor immunology. It is important to note that these are hypotheses generated from the correlative data, which require rigorous testing in future functional experiments. However, limitations include reliance on public databases, small experimental sample size, the retrospective nature of TCGA analyses, and lack of mechanistic validation. Additional studies are needed to clarify the functional routes and therapeutic relevance of NKAIN1 in UCEC.ConclusionNKAIN1 is overexpressed in UCEC and correlates with unfavorable prognosis, an altered immune microenvironment, and treatment sensitivity. It stands as a promising biomarker for risk stratification and a possible candidate for further investigation in the context of personalized immunotherapy. Future research should focus on mechanistic insights and clinical validation of NKAIN1 in UCEC management.
authors: Chang R, Wu Y, Cui A, Jiang L, Jia Q.

title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection.
abstract: The rapid evolution and emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have posed significant public health challenges due to enhanced transmissibility and diverse clinical outcomes. While the effects of these variants in humans have been extensively investigated, their impact on domestic animals remains insufficiently understood. Given the close interaction between humans and dogs, along with documented cases of human-to-animal transmission and the potential role of companion animals as reservoirs for viral evolution, understanding the molecular dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs is of considerable importance. However, in vivo infection studies in non-laboratory animal species are highly resource intensive, time-consuming, require ABSL3 facilities, and involve ethical constraints, limiting their widespread application. In this context, ex vivo culture systems provide a practical and physiologically relevant alternative. Therefore, in the present study, we employed an ex vivo lung explant culture model derived from domestic dogs to investigate host responses to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants. Comprehensive transcriptomic profiling across multiple time points post-infection revealed significant alterations in genes associated with cell adhesion, structural components, extracellular matrix (ECM) organization and regulation, immune responses, mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and ribosomal function. Both variants induced marked downregulation of ECM-associated and T-cell-related genes, suggesting disruption of tissue integrity and suppression of adaptive immune responses. The Delta variant was characterized by early and sustained suppression of immune-associated signaling pathways, particularly T-cell receptor signaling, whereas the Omicron variant induced stronger activation of genes associated with mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and translational responses. At later stages of infection, especially at 24 h post-infection (hpi), canine lung explants exhibited increased expression of genes related to tissue repair, epithelial maintenance, mitochondrial function, and ribosomal activity, suggesting activation of compensatory responses aimed at maintaining cellular stability under viral stress. Notably, several hub genes were identified, including CD2, CD3D, CD3E, CD27, PTPRC, ZAP70, SYK, and LCP2 in Delta infection, and FLT3LG, MRPL2, MRPL4, MRPS11, MRPS12, RPS13, and RPS5 in Omicron infection, which are involved in critical pathways associated with immune signaling, mitochondrial function, metabolic regulation, and protein synthesis. Furthermore, the observed mitochondrial and ribosomal responses may indicate that therapeutic strategies aimed at supporting mitochondrial function and modulating excessive inflammation could potentially help reduce lung damage during severe infection. Overall, this study provides important insights into the transcriptomic response of dog lung explants following exposure to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants and also highlights the utility of ex vivo canine lung explant cultures as a valuable platform for studying host-pathogen interactions.
authors: Panwar A, Raut AA, Kumar A, Sharma S, Jangir A, Saran S, Kumar P, Joshi P, Singh RK, Mishra A.

title: Euscaphic Acid from Rosa roxburghii Tratt Fruit Ameliorates Ulcerative Colitis by Modulating Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Gut Microbiota, and Metabolism.
abstract: Although euscaphic acid (EA)-the main active component of Rosa roxburghii Tratt fruit-possesses potential antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and intestinal protective effects, the mechanisms underlying these properties remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether EA can alleviate dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced ulcerative colitis (UC) through multiple mechanisms such as inhibiting oxidative stress, regulating inflammation, remodeling the gut microbiota, and restoring metabolic disturbances. Using a DSS-induced mouse model of UC and integrating histopathological examination, Western blotting, 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, transcriptome sequencing, and fecal microbiota transplantation, EA's mechanisms of action were investigated at multiple levels, including the tissue, microbial, and metabolic levels. EA counteracted DSS-induced alterations in MPO, SOD, MDA, IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α. In addition, EA intervention improved UC and reversed the reduction in Bacteroides uniformis (B. uniformis) in UC mice. Further studies confirmed that B. uniformis is a key species mediating the UC-alleviating effects of EA. Metabolomics analysis indicated that EA could mitigate the effects of metabolic disorders; transcriptomic analysis indicated that it inhibits inflammatory signaling pathways; and multi-omics analysis further revealed that it alleviates UC by restoring the gut microbiota and correcting metabolic disorders while simultaneously inhibiting oxidative and pro-inflammatory pathways.
authors: Liu J, Wang Q, Bian X, Han Y, Liang J, Zhang R, Xiao Y, Chen Q, Zhang X, Sun X.

title: MAFF Expression Reshapes Key Stress-Response Proteins During Light-Induced Injury.
abstract: MAFF is a small MAF family transcription factor involved in antioxidant signaling and cytoprotective gene regulation. MAFF is differentially expressed across retinal regions, with particularly low expression in macular Müller cells, which play a central role in retinal redox balance. Reduced MAFF expression may weaken macular resilience to oxidative stress (OS), increasing susceptibility to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and macular telangiectasia type 2. However, the function of MAFF in Müller cells remains unclear. Human primary Müller cells (huPMCs) from non-diseased human donor eyes were used to investigate MAFF modulation under stress. Cells were transfected with MAFF plasmid DNA to evaluate intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) following H2O2-induced stress. For functional and proteomic analyses, MAFF was overexpressed using mRNA or knocked down using siRNA and validated by Western blot. huPMCs were exposed to light stress and cell viability was assessed using the AlamarBlue assay. Molecular changes were characterized by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based quantitative proteomics. MAFF upregulation significantly reduced intracellular ROS following H2O2-induced stress. MAFF protein expression decreased following siRNA-mediated knockdown (KD) and increased following mRNA-mediated overexpression (OE). MAFF OE improved Müller cell viability under light stress, whereas MAFF KD reduced viability. Exploratory proteomic profiling quantified 5907 proteins and identified candidate molecular changes associated with MAFF expression. Pathway analyses suggested that reduced MAFF expression was associated with oxidative-stress response signatures, whereas elevated MAFF expression was associated with changes in mitochondrial and immune/inflammatory pathways. KEAP1, BMP2K, VPS28, and PDCD4 were negatively associated with MAFF expression, suggesting potential regulation of antioxidant defense, vesicle trafficking, and apoptosis-related processes. Elevated MAFF expression was associated with reduced ROS accumulation and improved cell viability, while exploratory proteomic analysis identified changes in mitochondrial, oxidative-stress, and immune/inflammatory pathways. These findings support further investigation of MAFF as a contributor to macular stress susceptibility and as a candidate for future therapeutic studies.
authors: Zhang J, Zhang T, Arafah ADB, Lee S, Yam M, Zeng J, Chang CC, Wang X, Gillies MC, Zhu L.

title: Schizophyllum commune Enhances Dendrobine Accumulation in Dendrobium nobile in Association with Induced Fungal Cellulolytic Activity and Host Jasmonate Biosynthesis.
abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the mechanism by which Schizophyllum commune elevates dendrobine accumulation in Dendrobium nobile, and verify whether cellulase derived from this fungus triggers jasmonate biosynthesis to mediate the regulation of alkaloid production.MethodsEndophytic fungi were isolated from D. nobile stems via tissue block isolation and identified by ITS sequencing. A plant-fungus symbiotic system was established with axenic plantlets. Dual RNA seq transcriptomic analysis, RT qPCR, pharmacological interventions with methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and the JA biosynthesis inhibitor salicylhydroxamic acid (SHAM) and Extracellular cellulase activities assays was performed.ResultsIn this study, none of 29 endophytic fungal strains from D. nobile stems produced dendrobine independently. Symbiotic screening subsequently identified Schizophyllum commune CY01 1H (SC) as the best strain that significantly increased dendrobine accumulation in D. nobile plantlets. Dual RNA seq revealed that SC colonization substantially activated jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis, accompanied by marked upregulation of the key biosynthetic gene DnLOX2. In contrast, downstream JA-signaling components exhibited an atypical transcriptional pattern, DnJAR was downregulated, whereas DnJAZ was upregulated. These results suggest that SC colonization induces a reconfiguration of JA signaling that may contribute to the maintenance of symbiotic homeostasis. In the fungus, cellulase-encoding genes were significantly induced. Experimental verification that MeJA promoted dendrobine accumulation, whereas SHAM suppressed it, and SC symbiosis partially mitigated this suppression. Stem section assays showed dynamic increases in extracellular cellulase activities (endoglucanase, cellobiohydrolase, β glucosidase), peaking at day 19, with endoglucanase being the highest.ConclusionsThese findings support a cross-regulatory model in which S. commune CY01-1H induces cellulolytic enzyme production during colonization, coinciding with host JA-biosynthetic activation and JA-signaling reprogramming, ultimately enhancing dendrobine accumulation. This study provides integrated evidence from fungal and host transcriptomes and enzymatic assays, expanding our understanding of endophyte-mediated regulation of medicinal plant metabolism. S. commune CY01 1H represents a promising biostimulant for sustainable improvement of dendrobine yield in cultivated D. nobile.
authors: Zhao Y, Ouyang Y, Xiong N, Ji X, Jia Q, Qin L, Xie J, He Y.

title: Genome-Wide Association and Selection Signature Analyses of Hematological and Serum Biochemical Traits in Yunling Cattle.
abstract: Yunling cattle, a native breed native to subtropical regions, exhibit remarkable traits such as heat tolerance, strong immunity, and tick resistance. To characterize the genetic architecture of blood physiological and biochemical traits associated with these adaptations, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) using whole-genome resequencing data from 97 individuals combined alongside 39 blood traits (30 analysed after quality control). Significant association signals were detected for seven traits: albumin (ALB), homocysteine (CYS), white blood cell count (WBC), bilirubin (BIL), indirect bilirubin (I-BIL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LD-CHO), and red cell distribution width (RDW). Notably, loci related to leukocyte parameters overlapped with strong selection signals and were mapped to classical bovine leukocyte antigen (BOLA) genes, including BOLA, BOLA-DQB and BOLA-DQA5, which are located within the MHC region and are known to be involved in immune regulation. For lipid-related traits, the strongest signals were identified near RPL22L1 and SLC7A14 on chromosome 1, while additional associated genes included XPOT, SLC16A7, SCAI, SYT14 and ATP2B2. Additionally, regarding metabolic and protein parameters, NHSL1 showed a strong association with bilirubin; this gene has previously been reported to be associated with hypertension. Red blood cell parameters revealed candidate genes such as NAV3, LSAMP, ACACA, and others linked to erythrocyte variation. For Homocysteine-related traits, CIITA was significantly associated with Homocysteine levels; CIITA is known to be involved in immune regulation. In conclusion, this study provides a genome-wide characterization of the genetic architecture of blood traits in Yunling cattle, identifying several candidate genes (e.g., MOB1B, CIITA and BOLA genes) associated with blood physiological and biochemical traits. These candidate loci provide a foundation for further functional validation; validation in larger and independent populations is needed before any application.

title: A Newly Established Fin Cell Line from Tomato Hind (Cephalopholis sonnerati) and Transcriptome Profiling Characterizing Its Response to Vibrio harveyi Infection.
abstract: The tomato hind (Cephalopholis sonnerati) is an emerging mariculture species increasingly threatened by Vibrio harveyi infection, yet in vitro tools for studying its immune defense remain limited. Here, we established a novel fin-derived fibroblast-like cell line, designated Tomato hind Grouper Fin (TGF), from C. sonnerati using the tissue explant method. TGF cells have been stably subcultured for more than 83 passages in Leibovitz's L-15 medium supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum at 28 °C. Species authentication via mt-co1 barcoding confirmed 99.9% sequence identity, and karyotype analysis revealed a diploid chromosome number of 2n = 48, matching the donor species. TGF cells exhibited robust post-thaw viability (>80%) and were amenable to exogenous nucleic acid delivery, with higher efficiency for siRNA than plasmid DNA. To evaluate immune competence, TGF cells were challenged with V. harveyi, and transcriptomic profiling was performed at 60, 90, and 120 min post-infection. A total of 1876 differentially expressed genes were identified at 120 min. KEGG enrichment analysis revealed sustained activation of Toll-like receptor, NOD-like receptor, NF-κB, TNF, and IL-17 signaling pathways across all time points. The TGF cell line represents a valuable in vitro resource for studying host-pathogen interactions of C. sonnerati.

title: Integrative Analysis of Whole Exome Sequencing and Gene Expression to Uncover Genetic Mechanisms in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. This study aimed to nominate candidate genes and pathways for IBD by integrating exome sequencing and gene expression data. Methods: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed on 10 patients with Crohn's disease (CD). Differential expression was analyzed with GEO2R in an independent RNA-seq dataset (GSE193677; 2490 biopsies from 1162 subjects). Immune-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified with ImmPort, hub genes by protein-protein interaction analysis, and enriched pathways with Enrichr. Missense variants were modeled with AlphaFold 3. Results: WES identified 484 genes with rare coding variants in all 10 patients, and 732 genes were differentially expressed in CD or ulcerative colitis, 234 of them immune-related. Network, pathway, and database filtering prioritized ATM, CSF1R, FN1, and IL11, which together carry eight rare missense variants, with in silico predictions ranging from tolerated to deleterious. Enriched pathways included cytokine and interleukin signaling, and structural modeling predicted conformational changes. Conclusions: ATM, CSF1R, FN1, and IL11 are candidate genes in immune-related pathways in IBD. Because the genomic and expression data came from different cohorts, these genes need replication and experimental validation.
