title: IL-4 Licenses B Cell Activation Through Cholesterol Synthesis
abstract: Abstract  IL-4 is a pleiotropic cytokine that was first identified as a B cell co-mitogen over 30 years ago1. However, how IL-4 signaling mechanistically supports B cell proliferation is incompletely understood. Here, we find that the cholesterol biosynthetic program is transcriptionally upregulated by IL-4 signaling during the early B cell response to influenza virus infection and is required for B cell activation in vivo. Induction of lipid synthesis genes required both STAT6 and SREBP2 transcription factors, allowing IL-4 activated B cells to enter the cell cycle and proliferate in the absence of lipids. Genetic inhibition of de novo cholesterol synthesis via SREBP2 deletion reduced plasmablasts and subsequent germinal center B cell formation at steady state and following influenza infection. SREBP2-deficency blocked IL-4 mediated cell cycle entry, ER expansion, and subsequent proliferation in a cholesterol dependent manner. Further mechanistic studies revealed that ER cholesterol content promoted sustained STAT6 signaling associated with ER expansion and B cell survival. In sum, we demonstrate that the well-known ability of IL-4 to act as a B cell growth factor is through a previously unknown rewiring of specific lipid anabolic programs, relieving sensitivity of cells of environmental nutrient availability.
authors: York A, Steach H, Mattingly J, Skadow M, Wu A, Li M, Wang F, Chen S, Brewer J, Mowel W, Bailis W, Williams K, Bensinger S, Craft J, Flavell R.

title: The growth characteristics and metabolic profiling of Δ 5,7 -sterols and fatty acids in Schizochytrium sp. S31 under different culture conditions
abstract: Abstract    Schizochytrium  is a promising thraustochytrid cell factory for co-producing high-value bioactives; however, its growth and bioactive accumulation depend heavily on culture conditions. This study systematically investigated the growth characteristics and the changes in Δ  5,7  -sterols, fatty acids and astaxanthin of  Schizochytrium  sp. S31 under different concentrations of glucose (0–120 g/L), sea salt (0–130 g/L) and pH (3.5–7.5). Sea salt exerted a markedly stronger influence on sterol profiles and fatty acid contents than glucose or pH. Low salinity (10 g/L), with ergosterol constituting the largest proportion (41%), maximized total fatty acid (41.3% DCW) and DHA (7.3% DCW) contents, whereas higher salinities shifted sterol composition toward C28-Δ  5,7  and increased trace astaxanthin levels. The maximum cell dry weight of 17.4 g/L was obtained at 60 g/L glucose, 20 g/L sea salt and pH 5.5, which was also the optimum condition for the simultaneous accumulation of Δ  5,7  -sterols (50.73 mg/L), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 1097 mg/L) and astaxanthin (0.11 mg/L). Transcriptomic analysis revealed a crosstalk among sterol, DHA and astaxanthin biosynthetic pathways in  Schizochytrium  sp. S31, and low salinity enhanced fatty acid β-oxidation to elevate the acetyl-CoA supply toward the mevalonate (MVA) pathway, while downregulating crtI and crtR to suppress downstream astaxanthin accumulation. Additionally, candidate genes involved in key phytosterols synthesis were identified. These findings provide critical insights into the biosynthetic regulation of sterols, astaxanthin, and DHA in thraustochytrids, highlighting their potential for the co-production of these high-value bioactives.
authors: Zhang X, He P, Liao Y, Peng J, Yuan J, Zhao J.

title: Long-read full-length transcriptome sequencing reveals multilayered sex-associated isoform regulation in thyroid carcinoma
abstract: Abstract  Background  Sex disparities in thyroid carcinoma are well recognized, yet their molecular basis at the transcript isoform level remains poorly understood. We aimed to determine whether sex-associated molecular differences extend beyond gene-level expression to coordinated remodeling of transcript isoforms. Methods  Tumor tissues from ten thyroid carcinoma patients (four males, six females) were profiled by Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) full-length transcriptome sequencing. Gene-level, transcript-level and post-transcriptional analyses, including differential expression, alternative splicing, alternative polyadenylation and differential transcript usage, were integrated. External validation was performed by exon-usage analysis of the TCGA-THCA cohort (505 primary tumors). Results  We identified 14,420 genes and 32,269 transcripts, including 1,064 novel genes and 9,755 novel transcripts. Transcript-level analysis detected 2,052 differentially expressed transcripts, nearly twice the number of differentially expressed genes (1,144), with 627 alterations detectable only at the isoform level. Sex-associated analysis revealed 68 differential splicing events (predominantly exon skipping), 340 alternative polyadenylation events, 94 3′UTR remodeling events and 956 transcripts with altered isoform preference. Integration across layers yielded 56 consistently dysregulated candidates, represented by SNHG5 and PTCSC2. External TCGA-THCA exon-usage analysis reproduced sex-associated signal at JPX and SNHG5 that was undetectable at the gene-expression level. Using GTEx normal thyroid (v8, n = 578; v10, n = 587) and TCGA adjacent-normal tissue (n = 59) as references, only 28 genes (26 in v10) showed sex-biased expression in normal thyroid, almost all sex-chromosomal or immunoglobulin genes, and no autosomal gene passed correction in tumours; 1,917 of the 2,139 sex-associated event genes (89.6%) showed no sex-biased gene-level expression in either normal thyroid or tumour. Conclusions  Sex-associated regulation in thyroid carcinoma is mediated through coordinated changes in transcript abundance and transcript identity, establishing isoform-resolved profiling as an essential complement to conventional gene-level analysis of endocrine tumor heterogeneity.
authors: Dilinigaer D, Rousuli Y, Aini A, Ran D.

title: Splice switching of membrane-bound FLT1 into a soluble protein as a treatment for pathological angiogenesis
abstract: Abstract    Pathological retinal neovascularization is associated with dysregulated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling. Soluble FLT1 (sFLT1), an endogenous VEGF decoy receptor, is generated through alternative 3′-end processing of  FLT1  pre-mRNA. We investigated the cis-regulatory elements that control this process and used splice-switching oligonucleotides (SSOs) to increase sFLT1 production. Two overlapping SSO panels were screened in HEK293FT cells using qPCR and ELISA. We validated lead candidates in CRISPRa-engineered,  FLT1  -enriched Müller glial cells using qPCR, ELISA, and a VEGF-responsive luminescence assay. Proximal SSOs increased sFLT1 without altering total  FLT1  transcript levels, indicating altered RNA processing rather than increased gene expression. Distal SSOs also enhanced sFLT1 by targeting polyadenylation signals. SSO-16 and SSO-19 produced the greatest increases in sFLT1 and significantly attenuated VEGF signaling. These findings identify  FLT1  intron 13 regulatory elements as promising therapeutic targets for retinal vascular disease while preserving  FLT1  expression and supporting targeted modulation of VEGF signaling.
authors: Wazan LE, Kadife E, Harper A, Kumar S, Brownfoot FC, Liu G.

title: Cross-sectional Plasma Metabolomic Profiles across Acute, Recovery-Stage, and Recurrent Ischemic Stroke: A Quality-Control and Multiplicity-Aware Exploratory Study
abstract: Abstract  Background and Purpose: Plasma metabolomics may capture biological heterogeneity across clinically defined ischemic stroke states, but small discovery datasets require careful control of analytical variability, metabolite-annotation uncertainty, and multiple testing. We assessed whether a four-group cross-sectional plasma dataset contained reproducible global or feature-level differences after explicit quality-control filtering and multiplicity correction. Materials and Methods: Plasma samples from 40 participants were compared across healthy control (HC), acute ischemic stroke (AIS), recovery-stage stroke, and recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) groups (n = 10 per group). Positive- and negative-ion untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) feature tables were analyzed separately using the documented detection, transformation, normalization, pooled-quality-control (QC), and imputation workflow. Global structure was assessed by principal component analysis and one-factor PERMANOVA with 1,999 permutations. Feature-wise differences were evaluated by Kruskal-Wallis tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction within ion mode. Results: After QC filtering, 1,605 positive-mode and 872 negative-mode feature rows remained. PCA showed extensive overlap among groups. PERMANOVA did not support a global group effect in positive mode (pseudo-F = 0.988, R² = 0.076, P = 0.486) or negative mode (pseudo-F = 1.168, R² = 0.089, P = 0.117). Although 68 positive-mode and 77 negative-mode features had nominal omnibus P Conclusions: No global or feature-level difference met multiplicity-controlled criteria in this pilot dataset. The nominal signals should therefore be regarded as candidates for targeted chemical confirmation and longitudinal validation rather than as stage-specific or recurrence-associated biomarkers.
authors: liu s, Sun M, Liu H, Wang Y, Zhang F, Li N, Qian T, Zou L, Sun P.

title: Aqueous Humor Proteomic Analysis Identifies Diagnostic Biomarkers for Autoimmune Optic Neuritis
abstract: Abstract  Autoimmune optic neuritis (AON) is an inflammatory optic neuropathy that commonly presents with acute or subacute visual loss. In the early stage, AON may overlap clinically with other optic neuropathies, particularly non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). Although serum and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers can provide diagnostic assistance, they do not directly reflect the local ocular microenvironment. In this study, aqueous humor (AH) was used as a local liquid biopsy source to identify candidate molecules associated with AON. Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics was applied to analyze AH proteins obtained from patients with AON, patients with NAION, and presbyopic surgical controls (CTL group) during anterior chamber paracentesis or surgery. Candidate biomarkers were subsequently quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Proteomic analysis identified 4,264 proteins from 18 samples. Gene Ontology annotation and functional analysis showed that AON-related biological processes were mainly associated with immune responses, ganglioside biosynthesis, glycoprotein biosynthesis, lysosomal function, and protein translation. Candidate protein selection integrated fold change, biological module relevance, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network centrality, and ELISA feasibility, leading to the selection of lactoferrin (LTF), ribosomal protein SA (RPSA), and ATPase H+ transporting V1 subunit A (ATP6V1A) for further validation. The results showed that LTF concentration differed significantly between the AON and CTL groups and demonstrated diagnostic utility in receiver operating characteristic analysis, suggesting that LTF may serve as a potential aqueous humor biomarker for AON. In contrast, RPSA and ATP6V1A did not show stable intergroup differences during validation; nevertheless, the protein translation stress and lysosome-related pathways represented by these molecules suggest corresponding functional alterations in the AH microenvironment of AON. Overall, this study provides an initial characterization of the AH proteomic profile in AON and indicates that AH proteomics may offer a new approach for elucidating local pathological mechanisms and identifying fluid-based diagnostic biomarkers for AON.
authors: mao q, zhang m, huang s, zhang j, luo j, gu h, guan h, ji m.

title: Review on physics of Higgs-R2inflation.
abstract: Higgs inflation, identifying the standard model (SM) Higgs boson as the, causes a unitarity issue during the preheating epoch after inflation in its simplest form, calling for a UV completion. Higgs-inflation serves as a natural candidate for the UV completion of Higgs inflation, providing a consistent framework to describe the inflationary dynamics till the end of reheating. Higgs-inflation contains a new scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, which unitarizes the theory in the same way that the Higgs boson unitarizes the electroweak gauge boson scatterings in the SM. In this short review, we summarize the physics of Higgs-inflation. A particular emphasis is put on its particle physics aspects, such as the unitarity structure, frame-independence, and the renormalization group evolution.
journal: Reports on progress in physics. Physical Society (Great Britain)
authors: Ema Y.

title: Supersonically sprayed Sr-Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>/Fe<sub>3</sub>C textile electrodes as flexible supercapacitors.
abstract: Flexible supercapacitors require electrode materials that simultaneously provide high conductivities, abundant electrochemically active sites, and rapid ion transport pathways. In this study, we developed hybrid Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C/reduced graphene oxide (rGO) electrodes supported on conductive carbonized cotton fabric via a combination of solvothermal synthesis and supersonic cold-spray deposition, followed by controlled annealing. The cold-spray process facilitated the uniform, binder-free deposition of rGO-enwrapped Sr-Fe precursor particles onto temperature-sensitive cotton textiles without structural damage. Subsequent carbonization induced a phase evolution toward a mixed Fe3O4/Fe3C morphology that was strongly coupled with the graphitized carbon matrix. Systematic annealing between 750 and 825 °C revealed that the microstructure, crystallinity, and phase distribution were temperature-dependent. The optimal SF775 electrode was uniformly coated with Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C and rGO on a carbonized cotton fibrous network. The SF775 electrode delivered a maximum areal capacitance of 1050 mF cm-2 at 5 mA cm-2, along with an energy density of 145.8 µWh cm-2 at a power density of 10 mW cm-2. Furthermore, the device exhibited excellent mechanical flexibility and durability, retaining its performance after 1000 bending cycles. These results indicate that high-performance textile-based Sr-Fe3O4/Fe3C electrodes produced via cold-spray deposition and thermal phase evolution are promising candidates for wearable supercapacitors.
authors: Lim W, Kim YI, Lee Y, Joshi B, Samuel E, Aldalbahi A, Periyasami G, Lee MW, Lee HS, Yoon SS.

title: Polyphenol supplementation and skeletal muscle health in older adults: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Sarcopenia is a progressive age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by the decline of muscle mass and function, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Polyphenols have been proposed as candidate modulators of these pathways on mechanistic and preclinical grounds, but whether this plausibility translates into measurable structural and functional benefit in clinical trials remains unresolved. A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook (PROSPERO CRD420251183284) was conducted. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating polyphenol supplementation in adults aged ≥ 55 years for outcomes related to skeletal muscle mass, strength, or physical function. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and because a formal meta-analysis was not feasible given the small number of trials and substantial clinical heterogeneity, effect estimates and measures of uncertainty were tabulated alongside a structured direction-of-effect synthesis, following recommended practice for reviews that cannot pool data quantitatively. Six randomized controlled trials were identified; five had reported outcome data and were included in the synthesis, while a sixth remains an ongoing registered protocol with no results yet available and is reported separately. Interventions included quercetin, epicatechin-rich extracts, tea catechins, cocoa flavonoids, and marine-derived polyphenols, with durations ranging from 4 to 24 weeks among completed trials. Muscle strength improved significantly on between-group comparison in two of five completed trials; effects on muscle mass were inconsistent, with one trial showing a significant group-by-time interaction under a combined polyphenol, amino-acid, and exercise intervention, another showing an attenuated loss without a significant between-group difference, and others showing null or less clearly attributable effects; functional and balance outcomes improved in two of three trials that assessed them. Polyphenol supplementation shows biologically plausible but currently inconsistent effects on skeletal muscle outcomes in older adults; the evidence base remains too small, heterogeneous, and methodologically limited to support therapeutic recommendations. Larger, standardized randomized trials in populations with confirmed sarcopenia, incorporating direct neuromuscular assessment, are required before clinical translation.
authors: Diaz-Vallejo JA, Gonzalez-Correa CH, Padilla CJ.

title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD1-3. Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge4. Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals5, and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts6,7; however, the biological basis of this 'female protective effect' (FPE) has remained unknown8,9. Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST. Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals10, emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

title: Recent developments in downstream processing of novel biotherapeutic modalities.
abstract: There is rising interest in the biopharma industry in exploring next-generation complex therapeutic modalities that offer unique advantages over their traditional counterparts. These include antibody-drug conjugates, nucleic acid-based therapeutics (plasmid DNA and messenger RNA), virus-like particles, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies, and monoclonal antibody (mAb) derivatives such as bispecific antibodies, nanobodies, and antibody fragments. Each of these moieties displays distinct structural, physicochemical, and functional attributes that translate to unique manufacturing challenges. This review showcases major developments over the last 5 years in downstream processing of these next-generation therapeutics, such as chromatographic and nonchromatographic separation strategies, process intensification, and automation and process control. Overall, these advancements indicate that the purification of such biotherapeutics requires an appropriate separation process tailored to modality-specific physicochemical characteristics and cannot be derived from mAb manufacturing expertise; this will be crucial for their scalability and cost-effectiveness.
authors: Rathore AS, Metya S, Yadav P.

title: Endothelial HIF-2α/TFPI signaling contributes to coagulation dysfunction and neurological deficits after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI)-associated coagulopathy is a life-threatening complication characterized by systemic coagulation dysfunction and increased mortality; however, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the potential role of hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (HIF-2α) in endothelial dysfunction and tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI)-associated coagulation imbalance during TBI-associated coagulopathy. Building on our previous transcriptomic analysis identifying TFPI upregulation in trauma-induced coagulopathy, we further explored its upstream regulatory mechanism in a rat TBI model. Notably, integrative analysis revealed partial overlap between the transcriptomic profiles of rat injured cortex and clinical whole-blood samples, both highlighting dysregulated coagulation pathways and converging on TFPI as a key candidate. TBI-induced coagulopathy was characterized by coagulation dysfunction, accompanied by decreased endothelial HIF-2α protein stability associated with calpain activation, with concomitant upregulation of TFPI in cortical tissue. In cultured HUVECs, TNF-α combined with hypoxia/reoxygenation stress induced endothelial HIF-2α protein suppression and TFPI upregulation. Pharmacological stabilization of HIF-2α using dimethyloxalylglycine (DMOG) partially restored coagulation parameters in vivo and attenuated TFPI induction under stress conditions. Mechanistically, structural prediction analysis identified a potential interaction between HIF-2α and the HRE-containing region of the TFPI promoter. Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays further supported the association of HIF-2α with this promoter region. Moreover, AAV-mediated TFPI overexpression partially reversed the protective effects of DMOG-mediated HIF-2α stabilization on coagulation and neurological outcomes. Collectively, these findings suggest that HIF-2α may be involved in the transcriptional regulation of TFPI in endothelial cells under early TBI-associated stress conditions and may contribute to coagulation dysfunction following TBI. This pathway may provide a potential link between endothelial stress responses and trauma-induced coagulopathy.
authors: Wang Y, Huang W, Jiang J, Zou L, Xiang Y, Li B, Chen Q, Huang G, Du D.

title: Beyond M1/M2 dichotomy: Toward an operationally defined, modular framework for macrophage functional states.
abstract: Macrophages are versatile immune cells involved in tissue homeostasis, host defense, inflammation, and disease progression. Their biology has traditionally been interpreted through the M1/M2 paradigm, but single-cell and spatial profiling, lineage tracing, and multi-omics reveal substantially greater heterogeneity. This review organizes macrophage diversity around recurring functional programs: immunosuppressive/regulatory, matrix-remodeling, hypoxia-associated metabolic, IFN-responsive/antigen-presenting, and proliferative. Angiogenic/perivascular activity is treated as a putative program because its status as a distinct transcriptional entity remains uncertain. We introduce an operational framework based on three criteria-co-expression coherence, combinatorial independence, and microenvironmental inducibility-to distinguish candidate functional modules from broader programs. We also conduct an evidence-weighted assessment of these programs, examining their independent variation, contextual coupling, and co-occurrence. Furthermore, we propose a Macrophage Dominance Index (MDI) as a hypothesis-generating numerical framework, with provisional marker sets, weighting, and formula requiring independent validation. Finally, we derive falsifiable predictions and outline experimental, single-cell, spatial, and clinical strategies to test relationships among programs. Overall, available evidence suggests substantial coupling among macrophage functional programs rather than uniformly independent functional axes. Macrophage heterogeneity is therefore better understood as context-dependent combinations of programs, some of which remain unconfirmed as distinct transcriptional modules. Although the framework may inform macrophage biology broadly, most supporting evidence, particularly concerning program relationships, biomarkers, prognosis, and therapeutic implications, derives from tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). Its applicability to non-cancer settings remains to be established. The MDI and proposed predictions are intended to facilitate testable research, not to serve as validated diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic tools.
authors: Jafari A, Vazifedust S, Harmileh KM, Karbasi F, Mazloomi E.

title: Decoding the role of ADAptor2 (ADA2) of HAT complex in autophagy and phospholipid metabolism to maintain ER homeostasis and triterpene regulation.
abstract: In yeast, transcriptional adaptor 2 (ADA2; SAGA complex subunit ADA2), a member of histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complex, regulates transcription through cell signalling, but its precise role in cellular metabolism remains unclear. In this study, genetic loss of ADA2 (ada2Δ) induces squalene (SQ) accumulation, indicating aberrant triterpene metabolism, coupled with endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/nuclear ER (nER) expansion. Lipid analyses of ada2Δ revealed elevated phosphatidic acid (PA) and phosphatidylcholine (PC) levels, indicating disrupted phospholipid metabolism. The expanded ER causes basal autophagy elevation, cellular recycling, and nER phagy, suggesting a regulatory role for ADA2 in autophagy. Downregulation of phosphatidate cytidylyltransferase (CDS1) and inositol-3-phosphate synthase (INO1), coupled with elevated PA and PC in ada2Δ, points to a significant disruption in cytidine-diphosphate-diacylglycerol and phosphatidylinositol pathway. Overexpression of CDS1 or INO1, or the inositol supplementation, in ada2Δ restores SQ, basal autophagy and ER phagy. The observed target of rapamycin Ser/Thr kinase complex (TORC1) activity in ada2Δ is due to the high PA content. Rapamycin-mediated inhibition of TORC1 reduced SQ, PA and ER expansion while increasing lipid droplets. In contrast, a rapamycin-treated ada2Δpah1Δ strain retained high PA, SQ and ER expansion, underscoring the functional role of TORC1-nuclear envelope morphology protein 1 (Nem1)/sporulation-specific protein SPO7 (Spo7)-Pah1 axis. Notably, SQ levels remained unchanged in a rapamycin-treated ada2Δatg39Δ strain, suggesting that loss of nER-phagy receptor, Atg39, impairs the effectiveness of TORC1 inhibition. In conclusion, our data unveiled a critical role for Ada2 in maintaining the intricate relationship between lipid and triterpene/sterol metabolism and connecting autophagy and ER homeostasis.
authors: Rathore A, Priya BG, Nawada NN, Shashank DV, Rao MJ, Anbarasu M, Manjithaya R, Tiwari AK, Ratnasekhar CH, Venkata Rao DK.

title: Targeting P23 by PM534 suppresses glioblastoma via disruption of SFPQ-mediated phase separation.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most lethal human malignancies, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 5% and limited effective therapeutic options beyond standard-of-care regimens, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents and druggable targets. Here, we report that PM534, a marine sponge-derived synthetic compound, potently suppresses GBM malignancy in orthotopic patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and in vitro, with IC50 value of 1.86 nM in patient-derived GBM#P3 cells. Target identification via activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) revealed P23, a co-chaperone of HSP90, as the direct molecular target of PM534. Subsequent LC-MS/MS analysis, molecular dynamics simulation, and site-directed mutagenesis collectively demonstrated that PM534 covalently bond P23 at Cys58 and Cys75. P23 demonstrated significant upregulation in human GBM tissues and orthotopic PDX models, correlating with tumor progression. Mechanistic studies exhibited that P23 interacted with splicing factor proline- and glutamine-rich protein (SFPQ) to regulate liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). Covalent engagement of P23 by PM534 disrupted the interaction of SFPQ with the HSP90/P23 complex, thereby triggering proteasomal degradation of SFPQ and consequently abrogating SFPQ-driven LLPS and oncogenic condensate formation. These findings establish PM534 as a promising drug candidate for clinical GBM therapy and highlight P23 as a therapeutic target in GBM.
authors: Lu X, Wang H, Zhang A, Zhang Q, Cao Q, Hou C, Li Z, Guo C, Li P, Fu Y, Chen A.

title: A Novel Drp1-Golph2 Tether Mediates Mitochondria-Golgi Spatial Association to Orchestrate Mitochondrial Function and Hepatic Lipid Catabolism Across Vertebrates.
abstract: Mitochondria-organelle contact sites are fundamental to cellular homeostasis; however, the molecular mechanisms and physiological significance of mitochondria-Golgi spatial communication remain elusive. To address this, we employed a cross-species approach using hepatocyte models from humans, mice, chickens, and frogs, combined with in vivo and in vitro studies in grass carp fed diets with varying lipid and chlorogenic acid (CGA). This strategy enabled us to systematically delineate the molecular machinery governing mitochondria-Golgi coupling and its role in hepatic lipid metabolism. The key findings were: (1) A candidate cross-species functional module: We identify a novel spatial association between mitochondria and the Golgi apparatus, formed by a direct protein-protein interaction between dynamin-1-like protein (Drp1) (via Leu639) and golgi membrane protein 1 (Golph2). Although Drp1 Leu639 is highly conserved across vertebrates, the corresponding Golph2 interacting site exhibits substantial sequence divergence among species, and this module exhibits functional conservation rather than sequence conservation. (2) A mechanistic link between structure and metabolism: This Drp1/Golph2-mediated mitochondria-Golgi spatial association serves as a critical regulatory node, where its disruption impairs Drp1 phosphorylation and mitochondrial fission, leading to enhanced mitochondrial β-oxidation and altered hepatic lipid metabolism. (3) A nutri-physiological regulatory axis: The nutritional compound CGA alleviates hepatic steatosis by transcriptionally downregulating Drp1 via a peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (pparγ)-binding promoter element, thereby normalizing excessive mitochondria-Golgi juxtaposition. Significantly, this study reveals that Drp1/Golph2-mediated mitochondria-Golgi spatial association represents a regulatory axis with functionally conserved outputs from fish to mammals, establishing this complex as both a fundamental coordinator of mitochondrial dynamics and a promising target for treating hepatic lipid disorders.
authors: Feng GL, Hu NJ, Chi YJ, Zheng FF, Song YF.

title: Diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated fetal immune maturation across multiple immune compartments in rhesus macaques.
abstract: Pregravid obesity is associated with long-term immune alterations in offspring, but the mechanisms linking maternal metabolic state to fetal immune development remain poorly defined. To address this gap, we used a rhesus macaque model of spontaneous, diet-independent pregravid obesity to examine impact of pregravid obesity on fetal immune maturation and function. We profiled immune cell frequency, function, transcriptional programs, and inferred intercellular communication in umbilical cord blood, fetal spleen, and fetal lung using spectral flow cytometry, multiplex cytokine profiling, functional stimulation assays, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Pregravid obesity was associated with altered fetal organ growth, elevated inflammatory mediators, altered immune cell frequencies, and hyperresponsive splenic leukocyte responses to in vitro stimulation. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed a conserved program of innate immune reprogramming across all three compartments, characterized by heightened inflammatory, migratory, and metabolic signatures together with reduced antigen-presentation potential. We also observed impaired T cell maturation with premature effector differentiation and evidence of B cell dysfunction. Computationally inferred cell-cell communication predicted loss of tolerogenic signaling and enhanced proinflammatory pathways across splenic and lung myeloid cells. Together, these findings indicate that diet-independent pregravid obesity drives premature but functionally dysregulated maturation of fetal circulating and tissue-resident immune cells, providing a candidate mechanism for the increased susceptibility to infection, respiratory disease, and immune dysregulation reported in offspring of mothers with obesity. This connection should be tested directly in postnatal studies.
authors: Doratt BM, Wagner S, Avila U, Hodge T, Martin LD, Varlamov O, Messaoudi I.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis identifies a manganese-associated transcriptional signature and a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature in COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling.
abstract: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous respiratory disease involving airway inflammation, emphysema, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manganese exposure has been linked to pulmonary inflammation and oxidative stress, but its molecular association with COPD vascular pathology remains unclear. This study explored a manganese-associated transcriptional signature in COPD and investigated its potential relationship with endothelial cell dysfunction and vascular remodeling.MethodsBulk transcriptomic datasets were used to calculate a manganese-related transcriptional score, identify differentially expressed genes, and characterize WGCNA modules. Manganese-COPD-associated genes were obtained by intersecting manganese-related genes, COPD differentially expressed genes, and manganese-associated module genes. Functional enrichment, PPI analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, diagnostic modeling, and consensus clustering were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to characterize HBEGF expression, endothelial subpopulations, CytoTRACE2 scores, pseudotime dynamics, transcription factor activity, cell-cell communication, and NicheNet ligand-target relationships.ResultsCOPD samples showed significantly higher manganese-related transcriptional scores. A total of 43 manganese-COPD-associated candidate genes were identified and were enriched mainly in pathways related to inflammation, cytokines, immune chemotaxis, and vascular processes. Machine learning identified 14 core diagnostic genes, and the combined model showed good classification performance in the training and validation cohorts. Among these genes, HBEGF showed the highest contribution in the ElasticNet model and was prioritized for downstream analysis. Consensus clustering divided COPD samples into two molecular subtypes with distinct manganese-related scores and functional features. Single-cell analysis suggested that HBEGF was closely associated with endothelial cell alterations, especially venous endothelial cells. Pseudotime and transcription factor analyses suggested a potential JUN/HBEGF regulatory relationship. CellChat and NicheNet analyses further indicated that venous endothelial cell-derived HBEGF may participate in endothelial-smooth muscle cell communication.ConclusionThis study identified an elevated manganese-related transcriptional score in COPD and prioritized HBEGF as a key candidate associated with venous endothelial cell state changes and endothelial-smooth muscle communication. These findings suggest a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature relevant to COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling, which warrants further experimental validation.
authors: Liu Z, Nie L, Zeng H.

title: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from NHANES and mechanistic insights into MECPP-related macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
abstract: BackgroundPhthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.MethodsWe analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).ResultsAmong 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.ConclusionsUrinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.
authors: Liang L, Su S, Niu Q, Rao K, Zhang Y, Chen N, Wang L, Chen Y, Yao P.

title: Dinotefuran aggravates Alzheimer's disease-associated microglial inflammation through the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway.
abstract: Neonicotinoid pesticides are widely used systemic insecticides with increasing evidence of neurotoxicity. However, their potential contribution to Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related neuroinflammation remains poorly understood. In this study, seven representative neonicotinoid pesticides were systematically evaluated by integrating physicochemical characterization, target prediction, pathway enrichment analysis, human AD snRNA-seq, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental validation. Among the seven compounds, dinotefuran was prioritized based on its favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and enrichment in inflammation-related pathways. Integration of target prediction with AD transcriptomic analyses identified CHUK and NFKB1 as key candidate targets associated with NF-κB signaling. snRNA-seq analysis further demonstrated preferential enrichment of NF-κB signaling activity in microglia from AD brains. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported potential interactions between dinotefuran and IKKα (CHUK) as well as NF-κB1 (p50). In Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, dinotefuran further enhanced activation of the CHUK/NFKB1-mediated NF-κB signaling pathway, accompanied by increased expression of IKKα, phosphorylation of IκBα and p65, enhanced NF-κB1 activation, and elevated secretion of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IFN-α, and IFN-β. These pro-inflammatory effects were markedly attenuated by the NF-κB inhibitor BAY11-7082. Collectively, our findings suggest that CHUK/NFKB1-associated NF-κB signaling may contribute to dinotefuran-enhanced inflammatory responses in Aβ-treated BV2 microglia, providing preliminary mechanistic insights into the potential involvement of neonicotinoid pesticides in AD-related neuroinflammation.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
authors: Baibujiafu G, Lin Y, Zhang L, Du L, Yang S, Yu Y, Ainiwaer K, Luo J, Wang X.

title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit. We combined publicly available human transcriptomic resources, genetics-driven causal inference, machine-learning-assisted biomarker screening, mouse-derived single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases, immune-cell deconvolution, and in-silico molecular docking. Twenty migraine-related genes were detected with causal associations to ischaemic-stroke risk. We prioritised three consensus hub genes: CD79A, PKN2, and PRKDC. In stroke patients, CD79A was significantly downregulated, while PKN2 and PRKDC exhibited elevated expression; their reliable diagnostic capacity was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling mapped these hub genes to endothelial, myeloid and glial cell populations residing within a dynamic inflammatory-vascular pathological niche in mouse ischaemic brain lesions. Mechanistic analyses pointed to perturbed mitochondrial energy homeostasis and dysregulated adaptive immune responses as downstream consequences modulated by these hub genes. Molecular-docking simulations demonstrated high-affinity interactions between Tamibarotene, Dirithromycin and the three encoded hub proteins, highlighting these compounds as promising candidates for drug repurposing. Collectively, our multi-omics analysis pinpoints CD79A, PKN2 and PRKDC as migraine-derived causal targets for ischaemic stroke, delivers cell- and spatial-resolved mechanistic perspectives on neurovascular-unit injury, and puts forward lead compounds awaiting further pre-clinical validation.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
authors: Zhang Z, Lin P, Ni H, Li Y, Wei J, Zhang J, Dai Z, Liu Y, Han L, Lin J.

title: Biological Signaling Pathways Associated with Late Tendon Development in Chicken Embryos and Their Dependence on Mechanical Stimulation
abstract: During embryonic and neonatal development, tendons exhibit rapid changes in mechanics and structure, including increases in collagen content, crosslinking, and fibril length. These functional and structural changes are partly dependent on mechanical stimulation. However, the specific mechanobiological mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. The objective of this study was to identify the potential biological mechanisms and pathways driving tendon maturation into load-bearing materials using an embryonic chick model. Using bulk RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor analysis, we produced a transcriptomic profile of chick hindlimb tendons during late embryonic development (E16, E18, and E20) and tendons from rigid and flaccid paralysis-treated embryos. Additionally, we assessed the results from two differential expression analysis models to improve the replicability of our findings. Our results suggest that the largest transcriptomic response occurs between embryonic day 16 and 20, and that among paralysis conditions, rigid paralysis produces the greatest effect relative to controls. Across development, we found positive enrichment in processes related to mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell adhesion, and contractility, and identified candidate pathways upregulated with development, including TGF-β, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Hippo, circadian rhythm, and focal adhesion signaling. In paralysis-treated embryos, our data suggest impairment in extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction events. Specifically, we found that both modes of paralysis are associated with a cellular stress response and downregulation of WNT signaling. Together, our findings identify candidate mechanotransduction pathways that are associated with late tendon maturation and altered by paralysis, which may inform tendon tissue engineering and regenerative approaches.
authors: Canonicco-Castro ML, Konnaris MA, Peterson BE, Buckley NE, Rolfe RA, Murphy P, McCarthy H, Dunne N, Szczesny SE.

title: Chronic Sleep Disruption Activates the Transcriptional Unfolded Protein Response and Induces Compartment-Specific Proteomic Changes in Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT  Sleep disruption (SD) is associated with adverse brain health and increased risk of dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the pathological mechanisms underlying this association are not fully understood. Preclinical studies have shown that acute SD impairs cognition by altering vulnerable synapses (molecular composition, ultrastructure, and function). However, the cumulative effects of chronic SD on the adult brain and its vulnerable synapses, that might contribute to AD risk, remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the impact of chronic SD on brain transcriptomic signatures and subcellular compartment-specific proteomic profiles to identify genes, proteins, and signaling pathways that might confer AD risk. Chronic SD induced a modest transcriptional stress response globally, whereas alterations were more pronounced in the synaptosomal (synapse-enriched P2 fractions) and whole-brain proteomes. Remarkably, chronic SD elicited unique proteomic alterations at the synaptic compartment were distinct from whole-brain effects, including increased proteins involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis, regulation of dendritic spine morphogenesis, and regulation of long-term synaptic depression, compared to increased proteins involved in immune/inflammatory, glial responses and neuronal function at the whole-brain level. Consistent with the chronic SD-induced molecular signatures, we observed subtle ultrastructural changes in vulnerable CA1 hippocampal synapses, including reduced pre-synapse size and decreased synaptic vesicle density, which suggest that chronic SD modifies synaptic transmission and plasticity. Together, our findings indicate that chronic SD differentially impacts the brain and the synaptic proteome, nominating candidate therapeutic targets and signaling pathways for future mechanistic studies of chronic SD and how SD contributes to increased AD risk. Highlights  Brain transcriptomics reveals chronic SD activates the unfolded protein response. Compartment-specific proteomics shows chronic SD drives unique compensatory changes. Chronic SD subtly alters the ultrastructure of vulnerable hippocampal CA1 synapses. We nominate candidate pathways that link effects of chronic SD to AD risk.
authors: Espinosa-Garcia C, Kour D, Srivastava U, Malepati S, Kumar P, Parhizkar S, Tobin B, Jang WE, Kumari R, Campbell B, Stagray J, Henley M, Liu X, Wood LB, Faundez V, Rangaraju S.

title: Cellular composition and the interpretation of candidate RNA readouts of trogocytosis in colorectal cancer
abstract: Background  RNA measurements of genes associated with trogocytosis may reflect cellular composition rather than contact-dependent membrane acquisition. We evaluated an eight-gene candidate module in colorectal cancer (CRC) using expression- and lineage-matched random modules, independent compartment analysis and patient-level inference. A separate rare-transcript definition and cancer-model fitness screens provided complementary analyses. Results  In 62 GSE178341 patients, the module correlated with T-cell fraction (ρ=0.767), but this association was typical of 10,000 matched modules (null median 0.766; one-sided empirical P=0.493; equal-tail two-sided P=0.985). A post hoc closest-10% matching sensitivity gave P=0.571. In 23 independent GSE132465 patients, the tumour-wide correlation was 0.735 (permutation P=0.00060) and the epithelial correlation was 0.376 (P=0.0892). The difference in absolute correlations was 0.359, with a 95% confidence interval of −0.041 to 0.759, leaving attenuation uncertain. Among 43,817 leukocytes, 16  CEACAM5 -positive candidates arose from four patients; 15 had expression ≤2 transcripts per million. Candidate counts were threshold-sensitive. No survival association was detected for the module in two cohorts.  SCD fitness dependency reproduced across CRC organoids and cell lines, whereas adjusted  SCD –  VPS72 and exploratory  ATF3 –  SMYD2 co-dependencies did not. Exploratory  CH25H ,  ATF3 and  FADS2 analyses yielded no Hallmark enrichment meeting the multiple-testing threshold.  Conclusions  Matched-module calibration placed the strong association with T-cell abundance within the range expected for comparable immune-lineage genes. Independent compartment analysis was consistent with a contribution from cellular composition, although attenuation remained uncertain. These results identify the comparison conditions needed to interpret the tested RNA readouts. Linking them to membrane transfer requires event-resolved protein measurements.
authors: Wang J, Sun P, Xu L, Wang Y, Zhu W, Zhang Y, Tang Y, Yang J.

title: Immersion as inference: An active inference account of induced realities and its relation to the two-competitor model
abstract: Immersive technologies are designed for a single target: the human perceptual system. Engineers of virtual and augmented reality have long recognized that a display does not have to replicate the physical world, it only has to provide the inputs that satisfy the senses at the level at which the brain samples them. This engineering intuition is, in fact, a statement about brain function. Here we develop it into a formal account of immersion within the active inference framework. We treat an induced reality (a virtual, augmented, or mixed reality, but also a book or a daydream) as a candidate generative model that competes with the model of the actual reality for the explanation of a shared sensorium and for the control of action. Immersion is then defined as the ensuant belief that the induced reality best explains the current sensory signals and supports the current perceived reality of the winning model, despite any break in immersion by Bayesian model switching driven by a high-precision prediction error that the induced model cannot absorb. Exogenous and endogenous attention, implemented as weights governing stream selection in our earlier two-competitor model, which treated attention as necessary but not sufficient for immersion, appear as two routes of precision allocation: likelihood precision of evolutionarily entrenched sensory events, and precision that follows the expected free energy of policies. Affect and motivation enter through the pragmatic and epistemic value of remaining in the induced reality and through the rate of change of free energy. We show that the two-competitor attentional focus vector and its angle are recovered from the active inference variables, and we reproduce the two scenarios of the original model, a rewarding and a fatiguing activity interrupted by a slamming door, in a minimal simulation. The account links presence, embodiment, cybersickness, and narrative absorption to a single quantity, and it yields concrete predictions for the psychophysiological assessment and closed-loop control of immersion. We discuss implications for neuroergonomic design in which the evolutionarily entrenched core of perception is non-negotiable while its experience-dependent periphery can be trained.
authors: Renz L, GauthierDickey KL, Vibell J, Francis AL, Corona-Strauss FI, Strauss DJ.

title: Neural dynamics become significantly faster and more nonlinear at the peak of information processing
abstract: The temporal scale at which neural populations preserve stimulus information is often treated as fixed, even though population activity changes rapidly during sensory processing. Whether the information-optimal scale changes within a single stimulus-evoked episode, and what determines its evolution, remains unclear. We developed Integration-Split, a decoding-based framework that estimates the time-varying temporal resolution of population spike trains. Across four visual paradigms and throughout the mouse visual hierarchy, the optimal scale contracted after stimulus onset and subsequently re-expanded. This pattern persisted across stimulus temporal frequencies and was largely absent in a hippocampal control. The optimal scale varied inversely with stimulus decodability, reaching its finest resolution when stimulus identity was most accurately decoded. Beyond this association, independently estimating the signal-noise autocorrelation balance across candidate window widths identified the window that maximized the autocorrelation-based signal-to-noise ratio, and this optimal width closely followed the Integration-Split trajectory. Consistent with these findings, stronger nonlinear predictive structure coincided with finer optimal temporal resolution, consistent with the idea that shorter integration windows are needed to preserve informative nonlinear population structure that would otherwise be attenuated by temporal averaging. To test the functional relevance of this organization, we trained a Transformer solely to decode stimulus identity, without providing the optimal temporal-scale pattern or Integration-Split outputs. Its learned attention exhibited a similar contraction-and-recovery profile, and disrupting heads with stronger correspondence produced larger decoding deficits. Together, these findings reveal a dynamically changing, information-optimal temporal scale in population coding, shaped by the evolving balance of signal and noise autocorrelation and by nonlinear population structure, and independently recapitulated in the learned attention of a Transformer trained without temporal-scale supervision.
authors: samiei t, Lokray S, Ahmed HF, Nozari E.

title: AlphaFold 3 Prediction Accuracy and Reliability across RNA Structures and Protein–RNA Interfaces
abstract: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) models RNA and protein–RNA complexes, but when its predictions and confidence metrics can be trusted is unclear. We evaluated AF3 on more than 1,300 protein–RNA complexes and about 270 RNA-only systems, and compared post-cutoff RNAs with pre-cutoff candidates selected by sequence and fold similarity. On structurally novel RNAs, AF3 largely preserves the protein fold, while RNA-fold and interface accuracy drop sharply with little change in predicted RNA confidence score. Input ablations show that protein alignments and templates from RNA-bound proteins govern complex assembly, whereas RNA alignments matter most for single-chain and long RNAs. The most frequent failed interface retains protein-side contacts but places an often-misfolded RNA in the wrong pose. RNA interface confidence only partly distinguishes this error from correct placements. Against CLIP-seq, SELEX and RNAcompete motifs, AF3 usually places the protein against the experimentally observed motif-bearing RNA segment, even where the interface fails, but often not in the native pose. In protein–RNA complexes released in 2026, a score combining AF3 confidence with RNA familiarity and template use ranked RNA chains with accurate folds and correctly placed interfaces better than AF3’s ranking score. Graphical abstract
authors: Tennie IK, Uhl M, Franke JK, Backofen R, Runge F.

title: Disentangling Context-Specific Alzheimer’s Disease Progression Signatures through an Explainable AI Framework
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression involves stage-dependent transcriptional changes that are often masked by dominant cellular and biological variation. Here, we present  ADVISE (Alzheimer’s Disease Variational Isolation of Signal Embeddings) , an interpretable deep generative framework designed to disentangle Braak stage-associated transcriptional signals from background biological variation through separate latent representations. Using explainable AI, ADVISE prioritizes genes and pathways contributing to the disease-specific representation. Applying ADVISE to large-scale single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from the human prefrontal cortex, we identify shared and context-specific signatures of AD progression across global, sex-specific, and cell-type-specific analyses, revealing convergent molecular programs involving synaptic transmission, HSF1-associated proteostatic stress responses, and SLIT/ROBO axon guidance. Notably, ADVISE prioritizes  ROBO2 as a progression-associated candidate in excitatory neurons. Experimental validation using CRISPR activation in hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons demonstrates that  ROBO2 activation reduces the phosphorylated Tau-to-total Tau ratio. ADVISE thus reveals context-dependent molecular signatures of AD progression and bridges human single-cell discoveries with experimental validation of candidate regulators of AD pathology.
authors: Li AW, Qiu W, Arian C, Young JE, Lee S.

title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation–position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-  β response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.
authors: Sasson J, Niasoff B, Karin J, Ezraty Y, Nitzan M.

title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis of Gene Expression Patterns in Neutrophils from Rheumatoid Arthritis and COVID-19
abstract: Background  Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disorder characterised by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, and neutrophils play a key role in its progression. COVID-19 also involves neutrophil hyperactivation that contributes to severe immune responses. Emerging evidence links COVID-19 to increased incidence or exacerbation of RA, potentially through overlapping immune mechanisms. Objective  To compare neutrophil transcriptomic profiles in RA and COVID-19 and identify shared immune pathways and disease-specific features. Methods  Publicly available neutrophil RNA-seq count data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analysed: RA versus healthy controls (GSE116899) and COVID-19 versus healthy controls (GSE212041). A second COVID-19 comparison (severe versus convalescent) was assembled from GSE272381 and GSE227116. Differential expression was analysed with DESeq2, pathway enrichment with fgsea (Hallmark gene sets) and topGO (Gene Ontology biological process and molecular function). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were compared between diseases by direction of change. Results  In RA neutrophils, 11,355 DEGs were identified, of which 90 had an absolute log2 fold change of at least 2 with pConclusions  RA neutrophils show a transcriptional programme enriched for interferon and antiviral-response pathways. Part of the RA signature is shared with COVID-19 neutrophils, while a subset of genes diverges, and this divergence depended on the COVID-19 comparison used. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide candidate genes for experimental validation.
authors: Nawani S, Alam M.

title: Evaluating the Identifiability of Temporal Delay and Response Attenuation in Endometrial Decidualization
abstract: Endometriosis is associated with impaired endometrial decidualization, yet conventional differential expression analyses cannot readily distinguish delayed transcriptional activation from reduced response amplitude. These mechanisms may produce similar expression differences at individual time points while implying distinct biological interpretations. Establishing when they can be distinguished is therefore a computational identifiability problem. We implement an identifiability-aware analysis of temporal displacement and amplitude attenuation in longitudinal transcriptomic responses. The approach combines reference trajectories, constrained amplitude-only and amplitude-plus-delay models, analytical examples of observational equivalence, and simulation-based assessments of mechanism distinguishability. Held-out time-point evaluation and culture-level sensitivity analyses examine the stability of model-dependent conclusions. In GSE246591, a candidate-delay-dependent dynamic-range filter excluded 30.9–38.3% of initially dynamic features under a hypothetical 24-hour shift across four endometrial stromal cultures. A two-component diagnostic separating retained dynamic range from affine shape similarity revealed that small projection residuals can arise from either loss of observable dynamics or similarity of response shapes. These findings demonstrate why a single separation statistic may be insufficient for interpreting temporal identifiability. Complementary independent in vivo analyses provided biological context. In GSE51981, an endometrial progesterone-response-associated transcriptional score was reduced in endometriosis samples (phase-model estimate 0.155, 95% CI 0.222 to 0.088). GSE6364 showed a directionally consistent but statistically inconclusive difference (0.033, 95% CI 0.068 to 0.002). Neither observation independently establishes a temporal delay. Together, these results support selection-aware evaluation of temporal transcriptomic responses, distinguishing structural ambiguity and loss of dynamic signal from evidence of a biological timing change.
authors: Krikun E, Fahmy W, Alkhateeb A.

title: Developmental perturbation of Purkinje cell function induces male-biased core and associated autism spectrum disorder–like phenotypes in adulthood
abstract: Abstract  Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental condition whose etiology remains incompletely understood. Human epidemiological studies have implicated the cerebellum in ASD pathogenesis, and studies in mouse models have provided evidence for a causal contribution of cerebellar dysfunction. However, previous animal studies have largely focused on males and cerebellar manipulations at later developmental stages, with associated features of ASD remaining less explored. To address these gaps, we chemogenetically perturbed Purkinje cell function during early postnatal development in both male and female mice. Developmental Purkinje cell perturbation induced male-biased core ASD-like behavioral phenotypes, including reduced sociability and cognitive inflexibility. Phenotypes related to associated features of ASD, including impaired fine motor learning, altered sensory processing, and sleep abnormalities, were also predominantly observed in males. At the molecular level, bulk RNA sequencing following developmental Purkinje cell perturbation identified candidate sex-dependent transcriptional changes in both the hindbrain and forebrain, suggesting that altered cerebellar activity during development can influence gene expression across distant brain regions. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient early postnatal perturbation of Purkinje cell function can produce diverse core and associated ASD-like phenotypes, predominantly in males, with evidence suggesting transcriptional changes beyond the cerebellum. This study highlights developmental cerebellar dysfunction as a potential contributor to sex differences in ASD vulnerability.
authors: Miwa H, Kamijo S, Hori K, Hoshino M, Ikeda K.

title: Inverse design of chemical perturbations for desired cellular state transitions with GEMGen
abstract: Abstract  Perturbation biology links interventions to resulting cellular changes, providing a basis for understanding and manipulating biological processes. Recent advances in computational modelling have enabled prediction of cellular responses to diverse perturbations. However, many biomedical applications require going beyond response prediction to identify perturbations capable of inducing desired responses, an inverse design problem that remains largely underexplored compared to the forward prediction task. Here we introduce GEMGen, a large language model-based framework for the inverse design of chemical perturbations conditioned on desired cellular state transitions. GEMGen represents transitions as text-based, rank-ordered differential-gene instructions, generates molecular structures autoregressively, and uses a compound-response scorer to prioritize candidates for experimental testing. Across multiple benchmarks, GEMGen recovered small molecules structurally or mechanistically relevant to ground-truth compounds, and also generalized across perturbation modalities by generating chemical interventions from genetic perturbation signatures, outperforming existing perturbation design approaches. Beyond in silico evaluation, when conditioned on transcriptional signatures related to tissue fibrosis, GEMGen yielded eight novel antifibrotic structures from 17 de novo synthesized candidates. Notably, one lead candidate, GEMGen-010, exhibited strong antifibrotic activity in animal models of liver fibrosis without any structural optimization. Together, these results establish GEMGen as an effective approach extending perturbation modeling toward intervention design, broadening the methodology and application scope of perturbation biology.
authors: Shao S, Jiang Q, Ye X, Guo Z, Xia Y, Liu Z, Xu J, Jin P, Ju F, Xia H, Feng S, Liu H, Qin T, Deng P.

title: Matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures reveal astrocyte-centered neuroimmune alterations in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Abstract    Background  Extracellular matrix remodeling and altered tissue mechanics are increasingly implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but links between matrix stiffness and AD pathology remain unclear.  Objective  To identify matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures in AD and characterize their diagnostic potential, functions, cell-type specificity, and intercellular communication patterns.  Methods  Bulk transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus were integrated with literature-derived matrix stiffness-related genes. Differential expression analysis, three machine-learning algorithms, and cross-dataset validation were used to identify candidate genes and construct a multigene classification model. Functional enrichment and immune-cell deconvolution analyses were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to assess cell-type-specific expression, inferred astrocyte trajectories, and predicted cell–cell communication.  Results  Eighty-one differentially expressed matrix stiffness-related genes were identified in AD brain tissue. FREM3, DUSP4, and FAM107A were selected and showed concordant differential expression across discovery and validation datasets. The three-gene model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.963 in the discovery cohort. Gene set enrichment analysis linked all three genes to oxidative phosphorylation, although FAM107A showed an enrichment direction opposite to DUSP4 and FREM3. Immune deconvolution suggested associations with immune-cell signatures. Single-cell analysis identified astrocytes as a major population expressing the three-gene signature. AD astrocytes showed altered pseudotime distributions and stronger predicted communication with immune cells, particularly T cells and macrophages.  Conclusions  FREM3, DUSP4, and FAM107A are candidate matrix stiffness-related transcriptomic signatures in AD and may connect extracellular matrix remodeling with mitochondrial metabolism, immune dysregulation, and astrocyte-associated changes. Independent clinical validation and experimental confirmation are required.
authors: Luo P, Qiao Y, Jin C, Wang Y, Qin Y, Wang Y, Zhang Y.

title: CDK4/6 inhibition exploits the radiobiology of lutetium-177 therapy to induce replication stress and durable senescence
abstract: Abstract    Background  Lutetium-177 (  177  Lu)-based radiopharmaceutical therapy delivers prolonged low-dose-rate irradiation, creating a radiobiological context that differs substantially from conventional external beam radiotherapy (EBRT). We hypothesised that this extended radiation exposure generates distinct therapeutic vulnerabilities and senescence states that can be exploited pharmacologically. Methods  A high-throughput clonogenic screen of 295 small-molecule inhibitors was performed in combination with  177  Lu-DOTATATE and compared with equitoxic EBRT. Candidate interactions were validated using multiple CDK4/6 inhibitors across SSTR2- and PSMA-targeted neuroendocrine and prostate cancer models, including xenografts. Cell-cycle regulation, replisome stability, DNA damage, p21 dynamics, senescence and autophagy-associated nuclear processing were interrogated mechanistically. Results  Drug interactions with  177  Lu-DOTATATE differed substantially from those observed with EBRT, identifying CDK4/6 inhibition as a preferential therapeutic vulnerability of prolonged  177  Lu exposure. Abemaciclib, palbociclib and ribociclib enhanced clonogenic suppression by  177  Lu-DOTATATE, while abemaciclib similarly potentiated  177  Lu-PSMA in human prostate cancer models and improved tumour control in vivo. Therapeutic cooperation was not associated with enhanced Rb inhibition or G1 arrest, but with replisome depletion, replication stress, genotoxicity and durable senescence. Distinct senotypes emerged between tumour models: 22Rv1 cells developed a predominantly sustained p21  high  state associated with persistent growth arrest, whereas CA20948 cells displayed a p21  low  senotype following an early p21 response, accompanied by increased autophagic and nucleophagic features. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy differentially altered these senotypes, indicating that divergent p21-processing states can converge on durable senescence following combined CDK4/6 inhibition and  177  Lu therapy. Conclusions  CDK4/6 inhibition exploits a therapeutic vulnerability created by prolonged  177  Lu irradiation by promoting replication stress and durable senescence rather than conventional cell-cycle arrest. The emergence of distinct p21  high  and p21  low  senotypes identifies senescence heterogeneity as a previously underappreciated determinant of radiopharmaceutical response and provides a mechanistic rationale for combining clinically established CDK4/6 inhibitors with  177  Lu-based therapy.
authors: O'Neill E, Amoroso F, Mosley M, Genestar TH, Nonnekens J, Cornelissen B.

title: An Icariin-Informed Nine-Gene Transcriptomic Signature Identifies Mesenchymal–Stromal Recurrence Risk in Resected Colorectal Cancer: External Validation and Single-Cell Localization
abstract: Abstract    Background  Recurrence after curative resection of colorectal cancer is stratified largely by stage. Icariin, a prenylated flavonoid glycoside from  Epimedium  spp., defines a target space not yet examined as a source of recurrence-associated transcriptomes. Methods  Icariin targets intersected with tumour-versus-normal expression (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582) gave an 84-gene candidate pool; a pre-specified 100-combination screen (10 selectors × 10 models) in GSE14333 (  n   =   226  , 50 events) produced a fixed nine-gene signature. Four conditions fixed before external testing — patient-level independence, a depositor-coded disease-free-survival (DFS) event, the same platform, and the largest event count — selected GSE17536 (  n   =   145  , 36 events). Results  The signature (TIMP1/ SPARC/CLDN1 positive; PCNA/ACADM/ DPEP1/MMP3/CASP7/MMP12 negative) stratified DFS in GSE17536 (C-index 0.734; HR 2.30 per SD,  P   =   2.3  ×  10    −   8    ) and improved on stage, age and sex (  ΔC   +   0.085  , 95% CI 0.023–0.169; likelihood-ratio  P   0.001  ), but under-estimated absolute risk (observed-to-expected 1.90). Pooling the eight deduplicated cohorts (181 DFS events) gave a random-effects HR of 1.53 per SD (95% CI 1.13–2.07,  P   =   0.013  ;  I    2     =   69  %; prediction interval 0.71–3.31). High-risk tumours were mesenchymal/stromal and immune-suppressive; the signal localized mainly to fibroblasts and endothelium through SPARC and TIMP1. A protocol-matched random-pool control placed the signature at the 88th percentile (  P   =   0.118  ), and the stage-dominated TCGA-COAD transfer added no incremental value. Conclusion  The nine-gene signature is an externally validated relative-risk stratification biomarker derived from an icariin-associated candidate space; all results are in silico and await prospective and experimental validation.
authors: Zuo F, Yan J, Jiang M, Luo T.

title: CNGB3 promotes proliferation migration and metastasis in gastric cancer cells
abstract: Abstract    AIM: To investigate CNGB3 as a prognostic biomarker and functional driver of gastric cancer progression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used multi-omics approaches to comprehensively evaluate CNGB3's role in gastric cancer. Transcriptomic and clinical data were retrieved from the TCGA, GTEx, and GEO (GSE84437) databases. Analyzed methods included differential expression analysis between tumor and normal tissues, functional enrichment analysis (GO, KEGG, GSEA), immune infiltration analysis using the ssGSEA algorithm, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression modeling. RESULTS: CNGB3 expression levels in gastric cancer tissues were significantly elevated compared to normal tissues, and even higher in metastatic gastric cancer (p  1), from which 20 hub genes were identified through PPI network construction. Immune infiltration analysis showed substantial differences in immune cell enrichment between high and low CNGB3 expression groups (p Core tip:  Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, and effective molecular biomarkers are needed to improve risk stratification. Through integrated multi-omics analysis, we identify CNGB3—a cyclic nucleotide-gated channel subunit—as a novel gastric cancer biomarker that is upregulated in tumors and linked to poor survival. Functional validation shows CNGB3 drives gastric cancer cell proliferation, migration, and metastasis in vitro. These results position CNGB3 as both a prognostic indicator and a candidate therapeutic target.
authors: Lin H, Lin Y, Zheng S, Yang Z.

title: Transcriptomic and machine learning analyses identify entosis-related key genes and potential regulatory networks in ischemic stroke
abstract: Abstract  Background  Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, while effective therapeutic targets remain limited. Entosis is a non-apoptotic form of cell-in-cell death, but its involvement in IS is unknown. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and differential expression analysis were integrated with machine-learning selection and cross-dataset expression verification to determine key genes. Subsequent analyses included functional enrichment, immune infiltration, construction of molecular regulatory networks, drug prediction, and molecular docking.
