title: Diagnostic performance of serum P85-Ab versus routine laboratory indicators for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: specificity assessment of P85-Ab in multiple control cohorts and its correlation with EBV DNA load.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic value of serum anti-BNLF2b total antibody (P85-Ab) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) compared with routine laboratory indicators, validate its specificity across control cohorts, and explore the correlation between P85-Ab level and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA load.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled 331 participants from Xiangya Hospital of Central South University, comprising 115 patients with NPC, 46 patients with benign nasopharyngeal diseases, 118 healthy controls, and 52 EBV DNA-positive non-NPC individuals. Serum P85-Ab levels were detected. Routine blood parameters, biochemical indicators, and EBV DNA load were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance. The DeLong test was employed to compare differences in area under the curve (AUC), and Spearman's rank correlation analysis was performed to explore the association between P85-Ab level and EBV DNA load.ResultsThe P85-Ab positivity rate in the NPC group was 90.4% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 83.5%-95.1%), whereas all non-NPC controls were negative, yielding a specificity of 100% (95% CI: 92.3%-100.0%). The AUC for P85-Ab (0.949) significantly exceeded those for lymphocyte count (0.749), platelet count (0.668), globulin level (0.777) (all P ConclusionP85-Ab demonstrated 90.4% (95% CI: 83.5%-95.1%) sensitivity and 100% (95% CI: 92.3%-100.0%) specificity for NPC diagnosis, with diagnostic efficacy significantly surpassing both individual and combined routine laboratory indicators. No significant within-group monotonic association was detected between P85-Ab level and EBV DNA load. P85-Ab represents a convenient and reliable serological diagnostic marker for NPC.
journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
authors: Tao Y, Wu Q, Liang Y, Wang K, Huang K, Yi B, Long L.

title: Tilianin counteracts doxorubicin-induced myocardial injury by downregulating mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major clinical limitation of this widely used chemotherapeutic agent. Dracocephalum moldavica L., a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for cardiovascular disorders, contains the flavonoid Tilianin (Til). Although Til exhibits reported cardioprotective properties, whether and how it mitigates DIC remains incompletely understood. In this study, we established DIC models in H9c2 cardiomyocytes and C57BL/6N mice and performed transcriptomic profiling to identify underlying mechanisms. Pharmacological interrogation using mitochondrial modulators (carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone and cyclosporin A) and a ferroptosis inhibitor (ferrostatin-1) revealed that DOX triggers excessive mitophagy, leading to mitochondrial iron release and lipid peroxidation, ultimately driving mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis in cardiomyocytes. Til intervention attenuated DOX-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial injury in vivo and protected H9c2 cells from cytotoxicity in vitro by suppressing overactivated mitophagy and partially restoring iron homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that Til confers cardioprotection against DIC through modulation of the mitophagy-ferroptosis axis, supporting its potential as a candidate agent for managing chemotherapy-related cardiac injury.
authors: Yan M, Yuan Y, Huang C, Liu R, Ruan X, Chen Y, Hong Y, Ma X, Wang L, Guo X, Wang X, Cao W.

title: A TORC1-regulated H3K4me reader preserves promoter chromatin stability, and its degradation promotes meiotic remodeling.
abstract: Histone H3 lysine 4 methylation (H3K4me) is enriched at active promoters and promotes the recruitment of chromatin regulators, yet how cells protect H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin from inappropriate remodeling remains unknown. Here, we show that proteins encoded by the essential genes jmj3 and lid2 in fission yeast function coordinately to preserve promoter chromatin stability by limiting inappropriate H3K4me-dependent NuA4 acetyltransferase chromatin engagement. Decreased NuA4 at the chromatin restricts excessive histone H4 acetylation, SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling, and promoter-associated nucleosome-sized fragile particle (NSFP) destabilization, thereby maintaining transcriptional programs that support vegetative growth. Upon nutrient limitation, TOR complex 1 (TORC1) inactivation triggers Ubc14-Dbl4-dependent degradation of Jmj3 and Lid2, which results in programmed promoter remodeling. Moreover, loss of Jmj3/Lid2 couples meiotic transcriptional reprogramming with Rec12-dependent recombination hotspot activation, ensuring efficient meiotic differentiation. Together, our findings identify a nutrient-responsive mechanism that safeguards H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin while permitting regulated chromatin remodeling during developmental transition.
authors: Yun L, Zhang PC, Zhou K, Wang WT, Zhang KY, Wu YL, Zhu M, Ge HQ, Min T, Suo F, Du LL, Guo W, Sun LL, Wei Y.

title: Metal enrichment and downstream concentration gradients in an agricultural ditch draining a long-term fertilisation experiment.
abstract: Agricultural sediment surveys seldom quantify the downstream extent of metal enrichment. We measured Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn in 24 surface sediment samples below the Palace Leas long-term fertilisation experiment at Cockle Park, UK. Eighteen samples formed a 452.5 m ditch transect, with three samples each from the receiving stream and an adjacent diffuse runoff line. Concentrations declined downstream, with the strongest enrichment near the ditch head. Metal-specific segmented-fit breakpoints were 104 m for Cd (5-95% resampling interval, 78-129 m), 159 m for Co (129-185 m) and 159 m for Cu (104-236 m). These do not establish a shared boundary. Cr and Ni breakpoint positions were poorly constrained. The first 150 m contained 66.3-96.7% of the distance-integrated excess concentration for six metals, an index of profile shape rather than stored metal mass. Cd contributed 73.9% of a partial seven-metal risk index, while Ni exceeded its freshwater probable effect level in one third of samples. As and Hg were not measured, so the screening may underestimate multi-element hazard and cannot establish the overall priority contaminant. Missing grain-size and organic-carbon measurements leave sediment sorting and carrier mixing unresolved. Uniform concentration scaling preserves within-metal spatial contrasts, but absolute concentrations and screening classifications remain conditional on unmeasured digestion recovery. Detection-limit-aware uncertainty was therefore used for risk-score scenarios. The upper reach is a candidate for follow-up monitoring; a 150 m mitigation zone requires validation with sediment-flux and repeated sampling data.
authors: Li Y, Li J, Liu X, Qi Y.

title: Changes in self-reported Long COVID in different variant-dominant phases of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: the influence of vaccination on a diverse Israeli cohort study.
abstract: Purpose of researchLong COVID (LC) risk varies across SARS-CoV-2 variants, but causal inference is complicated by rising vaccine coverage coinciding with viral evolution. We examined how pre-infection vaccination status modified LC risk across different pandemic periods dominated by different variants, to disentangle the contributions of viral evolution and vaccine-induced immunity. In this prospective cohort study of Israeli adults with SARS-CoV-2 infections from July 2021-March 2023, participants completed baseline and follow-up online surveys ≥60 days post-infection. LC was defined as ≥3 symptoms within validated symptom clusters. Infections were assigned to an infection period corresponding to the predominant circulating variant (Wild type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) at onset time. Pre-infection vaccination was categorized as unvaccinated (0-1 doses), partially vaccinated (2 doses), or fully vaccinated (≥3 doses). Generalized estimating equations estimated multivariable risk ratios, adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up time. Among 1715 participants reporting 2018 infections, LC was reported following 30·4% of infections. In models adjusted for vaccination, LC risk did not differ between the Delta and Omicron-dominant periods (aRR 1·01, 95% CI 0·80-1·26). Among partially vaccinated individuals, infections during the Omicron-dominant period carried lower LC risk than during Delta (aRR 0·62, 95% CI 0·40-0·98). LC risk did not differ by variant-dominant periods among unvaccinated or fully vaccinated individuals.Major conclusionsObserved differences in LC risk at various periods of the pandemic dominated by different variants may be largely explained by concurrent increases in vaccine coverage rather than intrinsic changes in variant pathogenicity. Full pre-infection vaccination conferred consistent protection against LC regardless of the period of variant dominance.
authors: Lazar S, Kuodi P, Shibli H, Zayyad H, Wertheim O, Beiruti Wiegler K, Abu Jabal K, Dror AA, Nazzal S, Glikman D, Edelstein M.

title: Composition and bioavailability of dissolved organic matter in a semi-enclosed mariculture bay: Insights from spectral and stable carbon isotope analyses.
abstract: Characterizing the composition, sources, and apparent bioavailability of coastal dissolved organic matter (DOM) is essential for understanding carbon cycling in semi-enclosed mariculture systems. In this study, field observations and laboratory incubation experiments were conducted in the Haizhou Bay (HZB), South Yellow Sea, during July 2024. Using measurements of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration, DOM absorption and three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy, stable carbon isotope (δ13C) analysis, and a Bayesian mixing model, the composition, sources, and microbial transformation of DOM were assessed. Three fluorescent components were identified, including microbial humic-like (C1), tryptophan-like (C2), and terrestrial humic-like (C3) substances. The DOM pool exhibited strong terrestrial characteristics, with the Bayesian model estimating a terrestrial contribution of 73.05 ± 15.55%, mainly associated with riverine inputs. Among fluorescent components, protein-like C2 appeared to represent an apparent bioavailable fraction and was preferentially removed during microbial degradation. Dark incubation experiments revealed a two-phase degradation pattern, with an average short-term microbial degradability of 24.53 ± 9.85%. Microbial processing selectively depleted labile DOM components while increasing the relative contribution of humic-like fluorescence, aromaticity, and humification degree. Higher apparent BDOC values near aquaculture zones suggested potential local modulation by aquaculture activities, although terrestrial inputs and microbial community differences may also contribute. This study highlights terrestrial dominance, selective microbial transformation, and the complex regulation of DOM cycling in semi-enclosed mariculture bays.
authors: Yan R, Xie L, Zhang G, Yang B, Yang B, Lu D, Kang Z, Zhou J, Yan Y, Xia J.

title: CDH3-directed immunotherapy targets basal-like hormone receptor negative prostate cancer and breast cancer.
abstract: Basal-like double-negative prostate cancer (DNPC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) are aggressive tumors with few targeted treatment options, raising the question of whether a shared, druggable cell-surface antigen can be leveraged for effective immunotherapy. Here, we integrated analyses of independent bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets with mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies to evaluate CDH3 (P-cadherin) as a candidate target in basal-like disease. CDH3 expression was consistently enriched in basal-like subtypes across prostate and breast cancer cohorts and was preferentially expressed in basal epithelial tumor compartments. Mechanistically, CDH3 expression was governed by a YAP1-WNT5A/ROR2 signaling axis, linking basal subtype gene expression to non-canonical Wnt signaling. To exploit this target, we evaluated both a CDH3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) and CDH3-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. The ADC exhibited antigen-dependent internalization and cytotoxicity in vitro and reduced metastatic tumor burden in vivo. CDH3 CAR-T cells showed antigen-specific activation and tumor cell killing in vitro and improved tumor control and survival in metastatic prostate and breast cancer xenograft models, with additional benefit when combined with PD-1 blockade (nivolumab). Together, these findings establish CDH3 as a clinically relevant and therapeutically actionable target and support CDH3-directed ADC and CAR-T strategies for aggressive, basal-like DNPC and TNBC.

title: Rhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves ameliorates chronic atrophic gastritis via immunomodulation and apoptosis regulation.
abstract: ObjectiveChronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous inflammatory‑atrophic gastric disorder with limited effective therapies. Although Traditional Chinese medicine shows multi‑target benefits for CAG, the bioactivity of rare medicinal plant Aquilaria sinensis remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify anti‑inflammatory components from Aquilaria sinensis leaf extract and clarify the compound's anti‑CAG effects and mechanism.MethodsAnti‑inflammatory constituents were screened. Macrophages stimulated by LPS and MNNG‑injured GES‑1 cells were used to assess cell viability, inflammation, cell‑cycle, proliferation and apoptosis. Transcriptomic‑proteomic profiling predicted candidate pathways. An MNNG‑combined rat CAG model was established; gross gastric observation, H&E, AB‑PAS, Masson staining, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry and qPCR were performed.Resultsrhamnoside exhibited the strongest anti‑inflammatory activity. It reduced IL‑1β, IL‑6 and TNF‑α secretion and suppressed apoptosis in LPS‑treated macrophages, and triggered S‑phase cell‑cycle arrest in MNNG‑damaged GES‑1 cells. Omics analyses pinpointed PI3K/Akt as the core regulatory pathway. In vivo animal experiments demonstrated that rhamnoside dose‑dependently alleviated gastric gland atrophy, intestinal metaplasia and lamina propria fibrosis; it elevated PI3K/Akt signals, down‑regulated pro‑apoptotic BAX/caspase‑3, up‑regulated anti‑apoptotic BCL‑2, and normalized CAG‑associated gene transcription in gastric mucosa.ConclusionRhamnoside from Aquilaria sinensis leaves protects against CAG by regulating immunity and inhibiting apoptosis via PI3K/Akt signaling, which provides a potential candidate for CAG experimental therapy.
authors: Zhang W, Yue B, Zhi Y, Lv N, Sun D, Wang Y, Wang X.

title: Bcl11a preserves hematopoietic stem cell function in culture by restraining Ncf1-dependent ROS.
abstract: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is limited by culture-induced oxidative stress, yet the upstream transcriptional drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we show that the transcription factor Bcl11a is rapidly and persistently downregulated during HSC culture and that this decline drives functional deterioration. Bcl11a was both required and sufficient to maintain quiescence, clonogenic activity, and serially transplantable HSC function. Mechanistically, Bcl11a directly represses a Nox2 NADPH oxidase gene module, including Ncf1, encoding the p47phox organizer subunit; Ncf1 deletion reduced ROS and partially rescued the defects of Bcl11a-deficient HSCs. Rapamycin-but not the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine-restored Bcl11a expression, suppressed Ncf1 and ROS, and improved HSC function, identifying Bcl11a as a candidate effector linking mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibition to redox control. This axis was conserved in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, revealing a druggable transcriptional vulnerability of cultured HSCs and a framework for improving ex vivo-expanded grafts.
authors: Xu X, Zhang L, An Y, Wang J, Ding X, Xie J, Yu Y.

title: miR-8485 by Targeting ITGAM Expression Alleviates Cognitive Impairment Induced by Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: ObjectivePost-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major complication of ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to explore the role of miR-8485 in PSCI and its underlying molecular mechanism.Methods84 PSCI patients and 90 post-stroke cognitively normal (PSCN) patients were included. Serum miR-8485 and ITGAM expression were examined via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The diagnostic efficacy of miR-8485 was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Risk factors of PSCI were determined via logistic regression analysis. An in vitro PSCI cell model was constructed through oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Cell viability, apoptosis and inflammatory factor levels were determined by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, flow cytometry and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The oxidative stress was evaluated by measuring superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA) and catalase (CAT) levels. The interaction between miR-8485 and ITGAM was verified by dual-luciferase reporter assay.ResultsmiR-8485 was downregulated in PSCI patients, and ROC analysis showed that it could differentiate PSCI patients from PSCN patients. Downregulated miR-8485 expression was associated with PSCI disease severity. In OGD/R-treated human microglial cells (HMC3), upregulation of miR-8485 increased cell viability, suppressed inflammatory responses and oxidative stress, and inhibited apoptosis. ITGAM was the target of miR-8485. Overexpression of ITGAM partially reversed the protective effect of miR-8485 upregulation in OGD/R-induced HMC3 cells.ConclusionmiR-8485 alleviates OGD/R-induced inflammatoty responses and oxidative stress via targeted inhibition of ITGAM expression. The miR-8485/ITGAM axis may serve as a key regulatory pathway and a potential therapeutic candidate for further investigation in PSCI.
journal: Journal of geriatric psychiatry and neurology
authors: Shen W, Gao L, Liu G, Li Z, Li J.

title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Armillaria gallica to Selenium: Bioaccumulation, Biotransformation, and Growth Promotion.
abstract: AimsArmillaria gallica is a medicinal fungus and key symbiont for Gastrodia elata cultivation. This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent effects of exogenous selenium (Se) on mycelial growth, Se accumulation and biotransformation, antioxidant regulation, and transcriptional responses in A. gallica.Methods and resultsDose-response experiments showed that 20 mg L-1 Na2SeO3 optimally promoted mycelial biomass (47% increase) and Se accumulation (837.53 mg kg-1), with 99.71% of Se in organic forms, predominantly associated with polysaccharides and proteins. Physiological assays revealed enhanced SOD, POD, CAT, and GPx activities and reduced MDA content under Se treatment. Transcriptomic profiling identified extensive gene remodeling in ion transport, redox metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, glutathione metabolism, and MAPK signaling pathways, with qRT-PCR validating key DEG expression patterns.ConclusionsAppropriate Se concentration promotes A. gallica growth and enhances antioxidant capacity through coordinated transcriptional and metabolic regulation. The strong Se accumulation and biotransformation capacity position A. gallica as a promising candidate for Se biofortification and for developing Se-enriched Gastrodia elata via the Armillaria-Gastrodia symbiotic system.
authors: Liu J, Du J, Zhang X, Gao M, Ai L, Song Y, Qiao Y, Xie X.

title: Transformer-Guided Co-Optimization of Mutation Prioritization and Thermodynamic Probe Design for Mutation Detection.
abstract: The design of sequence-selective DNA probes has long been limited by a decoupled workflow in which target selection proceeds without considering the physicochemical determinants of probe performance, such as thermodynamic stability and mismatch discrimination. Here, we establish an iterative computational design strategy that unifies mutation prioritization with chemical probe design. A custom transformer model extracts diagnostic attribution scores of mutations from 1,782 samples, generating semantic maps to guide probe placement. Candidate designs undergo in silico thermodynamic screening based on differential binding free energy. Probes failing to satisfy the integrated criteria of thermodynamic discrimination, diagnostic attribution, and population frequency are further evaluated by refining their spatial configuration to co-optimize thermodynamic discriminability and clinical relevance. This iterative process converges on an 8-plex targeted panel. Wet laboratory validation confirms 0.03% variant allele frequency detection with low assay cost and short turnaround time. Clinical testing on 375 samples achieves AUROC values of 0.96 for tissue and 0.90 for plasma. This work provides a potential chemical framework for nucleic acid probe design that could be explored in other molecular diagnostic systems.
authors: Zhang Y, Xue B, Zhang L, Zhao L, Su X, Song H, Zuo X, Yang X, Jin C, Wang Y, Fan C, Song P.

title: Transcriptional Regulatory Crosstalk Between Heat Stress and Nitrogen-Sulfur Nutrition in Plants.
abstract: Plant responses to high temperature depend on the nutritional state in which the stress occurs. Nitrogen and sulfur shape this state through photosynthetic capacity, protein synthesis, nitric oxide production, and thiol redox buffering, while heat alters nutrient uptake and assimilation. We review how nitrate and sulfate nutrition interact with heat responses through direct transcriptional cross-regulation, metabolite- or redox-mediated regulation, and convergence on shared processes. Nitrate provides the clearest transcriptional link: in Arabidopsis, the nitrate-responsive transcription factor NLP7 regulates HSFA2 and HSFA3, encoding heat stress transcription factors that sustain chaperone expression and acquired thermotolerance, and rice NLP3 binds the HsfA3 and HsfA7 promoters under heat. Nitrate reductase-derived nitric oxide modulates HSF activity, and warm temperature represses the nitrate transporter and sensor NRT1.1 through the transcription factor HY5. For sulfur, evidence comes mainly from glutathione-deficient mutants, glutathione application and hydrogen sulfide donors, which alter heat-responsive transcription factors and antioxidant genes; whether sulfate supply acts through these routes, and how sulfate sensing and the sulfate-limitation regulator SLIM1 contribute, remain unresolved. Comparing published Arabidopsis transcriptomic meta-analyses, we identify genes responding to heat and to nitrate or sulfate and propose candidate regulators. In crops, nitrogen maintains photosynthesis under heat but does not consistently protect yield.
authors: Soto-Rauch G, Saez AR, Salvo A, Canales J.

title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
abstract: BackgroundMaladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.MethodsIntegrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.ResultsWe identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.ConclusionsAARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.
authors: Huang X, Zhang J, Zeng Q, Lin M, Bai J, Feng H, Liu J, Sha Z, Peng T, Lv Y, Zhang X, Li S, Li T, Qu J, Shao S, Liu Q, Liang S, Yang K, Tang H, Zhang Z, He Y, Duan Z, Kong D.

title: 2D and 3D antiproliferative properties of Schiff base and reduced Schiff base palladium(II) complexes in doxorubicin-resistant colorectal cancer cells.
abstract: To further investigate the structural features and antiproliferative properties of Pd(II) complexes containing halogenated ligands, one Schiff base and two reduced Schiff base complexes, I2PyPd, Cl2Pic(R)Pd, and BrClPic(R)Pd (Pic = 2-picolylamine; Py = 2-(2-pyridyl)ethylamine), were synthesized and characterized spectroscopically. The molecular structure of Cl2Pic(R)Pd was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, revealing a distorted square-planar Pd(II) center coordinated by a bidentate N,N-chelating ligand and two chloride ions. DFT calculations supported the experimental structure. Electronic absorption spectra, corroborated by TD-DFT analysis, indicated low-energy transitions assigned to 1LC for I2PyPd and 1MLCT for Cl2Pic(R)Pd and BrClPic(R)Pd. Biological evaluation showed that I2PyPd was inactive, whereas Cl2Pic(R)Pd and BrClPic(R)Pd exhibited significant antiproliferative activity. Cl2Pic(R)Pd displayed broad cytotoxicity across all tested cancer cell lines, while BrClPic(R)Pd demonstrated pronounced activity against doxorubicin-resistant HCT116-DoxR cells with limited toxicity toward other cancer cells and normal fibroblasts, indicating enhanced selectivity. Consistent results were obtained in 3D HCT116-DoxR spheroids, where BrClPic(R)Pd remained the more promising candidate despite higher IC50 values. Mechanistic studies revealed that both active complexes induced apoptosis and autophagy, with minimal necrosis. Cl2Pic(R)Pd increased intracellular ROS levels, suggesting an oxidative stress-mediated mechanism, whereas BrClPic(R)Pd reduced ROS while maintaining strong cytotoxicity, indicating a ROS-independent mode of action. Molecular docking studies showed that both complexes interact with the drug-binding cavity of ABCB1/P-gp and the DNA minor groove, supporting a dual mechanism involving modulation of multidrug resistance and DNA targeting. BrClPic(R)Pd exhibited slightly stronger binding, consistent with its superior activity against resistant cancer cells.
authors: Amiri Rudbari H, Forooghi K, Kazemi Z, Salas B, Sahihi M, Cuevas-Vicario JV, Cordeiro S, Valente R, Baptista PV, Blacque O, Fernandes AR.

title: dsRNA: mechanisms of gene expression regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic potential.
abstract: Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) has long been recognized as a viral pathogen-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immunity. However, dsRNA is increasingly recognized as a regulatory RNA species involved in RNA homeostasis, gene expression, and cell fate determination. In this review, we discuss canonical dsRNA-dependent mechanisms, including RNA interference (RNAi), with particular emphasis on nuclear RNAi, and dsRNA-sensing networks, together with broader RNA-RNA duplex-associated regulatory processes. We also consider structurally distinct RNA-DNA hybrids that functionally converge with dsRNA-responsive innate immune pathways. We further examine how dysregulation of dsRNA production, processing, sensing, and clearance contributes to cancer, autoimmune disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases, and how these mechanisms can be therapeutically exploited. Collectively, these insights establish a conceptual framework for understanding the roles of dsRNA in physiological regulation, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic applications.
authors: Liu S, Zhe C, Hou J, Fang Y, Yang H, Chen Y, Wu S, Xiang Q, Zhang Y, Fang J, Zhou Y, Li L, Xiao B.

title: Bromeliad Brocchinia reducta, a rare carnivorous monocot, is a holocarnivorous plant secreting its own digestive enzymes.
abstract: Carnivorous bromeliad Brocchinia reducta is a rare carnivorous plant. As a monocot, it is the youngest and most distantly related to the remaining ∼800 dicot carnivorous plant species. Although considered carnivorous for more than 40 years, it is believed that it does not secrete digestive enzymes and relies on microorganism-mediated digestion. Here we investigated the digestive physiology of B. reducta by measuring enzyme activity and using LC-ESI-MS/MS in response to feeding. We found prey-induced pH regulation and digestive capacity with secreted hydrolytic enzymes (e.g., aspartic protease, type I and III chitinase, GDSL hydrolase) similar to those found in other carnivorous lineages. Although the enzyme activity is rather low and comparable to the members of the carnivorous Sarraceniaceae family, the active prey response and presence of secreted enzymes placed B. reducta among truly holocarnivorous plants. Our results showed that a nutrient-poor environment exerts the same selective pressures on even distantly related plants and, through the process of convergent evolution, leads to the co-option of the same proteins for digestive function.
authors: Pavlovič A, Rotreklová M, Chamrád I, Lenobel R.

title: Integrative transcriptome meta-analysis distinguishes compatibility and incompatibility in rice-Xanthomonas interaction.
abstract: Diseases caused by the Xanthomonas oryzae pathovars are important constraints for global rice productivity. Despite being a well-studied pathosystem, the transcriptional mechanisms distinguishing resistance from susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we present a systems-level meta-analysis of more than a hundred publicly available rice-Xanthomonas transcriptome datasets. Using appropriate analysis pipelines, stringent filtering criteria and metadata integration, we identified rice functions that distinguish disease resistance and susceptibility with temporal resolution. Compatible interactions were characterized by early activation of abscisic-acid biosynthetic and signaling genes, and extensive transcriptional plasticity associated with susceptibility gene activation. In contrast, incompatible interactions displayed a restrained transcriptome reprogramming, enrichment of phenylpropanoid and aromatic-amino-acid biosynthetic pathways, and enrichment of an AP2/ERF-GCC-box regulatory module. Transient over-expression of three conserved infection-responsive genes, OsJAZ11, OsSYP131b, and OsMYB45, modestly enhanced defense gene expression and reduced lesion length caused by X. oryzae pv. oryzae in rice leaves, thus providing a proof-of-concept relevance of the candidates to rice-Xoo interaction. We also developed RiceXtra, an openly available database hosting the analyzed data (http://tdb.ccmb.res.in/RiceXtra), for exploring gene expression patterns during rice-Xanthomonas interactions. Overall, our study proposes a mechanistic framework connecting hormonal signalling and transcriptional plasticity with disease outcome, offering a foundation for engineering durable disease resistance.
authors: Cg G, Malukani KK, Gaur N, M S, Patel HK, Sonti RV.

title: Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis couples septum assembly to cell separation in  Schizosaccharomyces pombe
abstract: ABSTRACT  Ceramides are precursors of complex sphingolipids and bioactive membrane lipids. In the fission yeast  Schizosaccharomyces pombe , they are produced by a ceramide synthase with two catalytic subunits, Lac1 and Lag1, which are redundant but not functionally equivalent: only Lac1 is required for normal growth and cell size. Why Lac1 has this unique role, and how ceramide synthesis contributes to cell morphogenesis, remain unknown. Here, we show that Lac1 couples septum assembly to cell separation. Cells lacking Lac1 die predominantly during cell separation and build septa with a thinner primary layer and markedly thicker secondary layers, accompanied by altered deposition of β-(1,3)-glucans and galactomannan. These defects are not rescued by osmotic stabilization. The essential glucan synthase Bgs4 is mislocalized to cytoplasmic granules, and total β-(1,3)-glucan synthase activity is partially reduced. Nevertheless, Ags1, Bgs1 and Bgs4 accumulate to higher levels and persist almost twice as long at the division site, indicating defective clearance rather than delivery of the septum-synthesis machinery. Plasma membrane sterol distribution remains unaffected. To accurately impair ceramide synthesis, we isolated thermosensitive  lac1-ts alleles in a  lag1 Δ background. Their substitutions cluster in the conserved TRAM/LAG1 domain. Metabolic labeling showed that these alleles reduce ceramide synthesis at the restrictive temperature. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that two substitutions perturb distinct contacts with C26-CoA, while Lac1-M167T loses its endoplasmic reticulum localization. Acute inactivation recapitulates the deletion phenotype, causing septum accumulation and cell death. Together, our findings establish that Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis is required for the orderly completion of septum assembly and cell separation.
authors: Serrano A, Gómez-Delgado L, Hanaoka K, Matsunaga K, Funato K, Cortés JCG, Ribas JC, Alcaide-Gavilan M, Flor-Parra I, Lucena R.

title: A respiratory microdomain links ubiquinone biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase in an apicomplexan mitochondrion lacking Complex I
abstract: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) is a major entry point for NADH-derived electrons and an important site of redox regulation in most eukaryotes. However, apicomplexan parasites, including  Toxoplasma gondii , lack CI, raising a fundamental question of how mitochondrial respiration is organized in these parasites. Here, we identify a parasite-specific mitochondrial microdomain that physically and functionally couples ubiquinone (UQ) biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase (SDH). Using proximity labeling, membrane-based yeast two-hybrid analyses, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitations, and blue native PAGE, we show that UQ biosynthesis proteins associate with parasite-specific SDH subunits and co-migrate as a high-molecular-weight assembly. Knockdown of TgCoq4, a component of the UQ biosynthesis pathway, reduced SDH activity, and adding exogenous UQ to the assay did not restore it, indicating that UQ availability is not sufficient for efficient succinate oxidation. FCCP stimulates malate- and TMPD/ascorbate-supported respiration to maximal capacity but fails to do so with succinate as the substrate. This result, combined with reactive oxygen species (ROS) data, suggests that succinate causes over-reduction of the UQ pool, limiting further electron flow. We also find that CIII associates with the UQ synthesis machinery, suggesting a larger protein assembly. Together, these findings reveal that UQ biosynthesis and electron transport are physically and functionally integrated in  T. gondii , defining a previously unrecognized organization of mitochondrial respiration in an organism lacking CI.
authors: Baierna B, Moreno SN.

title: ANABOLIC FAILURE, NOT CATABOLIC ACTIVATION, UNDERLIES GLYCOGEN DEPLETION IN CERVICAL CARCINOGENESIS: A MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS
abstract: Background  Cervical epithelium loses its glycogen as disease grade rises, an observation old enough to underpin iodine-based visual screening, but which arm of glycogen metabolism accounts for the loss has not been established. The expectation from cancer metabolism is catabolic: that stored glycogen is mobilised and glycolysis activated. Methods  We analyzed 238 specimens from four publicly available cohorts across three sample types: 128 laser-capture-microdissected epithelial samples, 35 bulk-tissue samples, and 75 exfoliated cytology samples in two sets (44 and 31; GSE27678). We prespecified a 33-gene panel comprising four modules: glycogen synthesis, glycogen degradation, glycolysis, and squamous differentiation. For each specimen, we calculated module scores using single-sample gene set enrichment. Differential expression was assessed with limma, pathway enrichment with fgsea, and classification performance with bootstrap confidence intervals for ROC curves. We documented all analytical decisions and their rationale. Results  Synthesis and differentiation fell with grade in all four cohorts, while degradation and glycolysis stayed at their normal-tissue baseline. All seven differentiation genes were reduced in carcinoma and all seven occupied the top 5.1% of the ranked transcriptome, with CRNN the most down-regulated of 21,755 genes. Synthesis failed selectively, through GYS2 and PPP1R3C only, with the ubiquitous synthase GYS1 unchanged. The glycolytic module separated from normal epithelium at no grade (p 0.45 to 0.62), classified CIN3 or worse at an area under the curve of 0.569 with an interval spanning chance, and showed no enrichment in carcinoma. Synthesis separated from normal first, at CIN2, and differentiation at CIN3. The composite index tracked grade in the discovery cohort (Spearman rho 0.652,  p 7.9×10  -17 ), but offered no discriminatory advantage over its differentiation component alone (0.832 against 0.832).  Conclusions  Glycogen depletion in cervical carcinogenesis reflects failure of a tissue-restricted synthetic axis, GYS2 and PPP1R3C, within a collapsing squamous differentiation programme, not catabolic activation. Measuring all four candidate mechanisms on one scale in the same specimen is what allows the catabolic explanation to be excluded rather than merely left untested. The pattern holds across two array chemistries and three specimen preparations, including the exfoliated cytology that screening already collects, and the synthesis and differentiation modules together are the molecular counterpart of what iodine staining reports. These are transcript-level findings and define no clinical threshold.
authors: Ajayi OO, Odigie EB, Adesite SO, Erameh TO, Archibong AM, Eziagu UB.

title: Endogenous PROM1 activation redistributes liver cancer cells along a preexisting differentiation axis
abstract: Summary  CD133 is widely used as a marker of stem-like cells in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its functional contribution remains incompletely defined. In PLC/PRF/5 cells, acute CRISPR activation of endogenous PROM1 suppresses hepatic programs, whereas PROM1 knockdown elicits an opposing hepatocyte-identity response, together defining a PROM1-responsive transcriptional axis. Single-cell profiling shows that this axis is preexisting and tracks endogenous PROM1 heterogeneity, separating a hepatocyte-like, PROM1-low compartment from a PROM1-enriched, less hepatocyte-like compartment. Sustained PROM1 activation reduces the hepatocyte-like compartment and shifts the population toward intermediate positions along this axis. Related transcriptional patterns are detectable in an independent HuH-7 dataset and a human HCC case. Endogenous ALFA tagging identifies candidate CD133-associated proteins. Together, these findings support CD133 as an active contributor to tumor-cell state redistribution, extending its role beyond a mere marker of stem-like populations.
authors: Schneider T, Kaneko K, Vogl M, Utpatel K, Immel A, Hirsch D, Raggi C, Spinola Lasso E, Evert M, Feng G, Calvisi DF, Scheiter A.

title: Apelin signaling controls neuroendocrine homeostasis via Atoh8-dependent transcriptional regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT  Apelin is a pleiotropic peptide hormone with established roles in cardiovascular function, angiogenesis, and metabolism, but its contribution to neuroendocrine development and function remains poorly understood. Here, using genetic loss-of-function and inducible gain-of-function approaches in zebrafish, we show that Apelin signaling is dosage-sensitive and required for normal development, reproductive capacity, and physiological homeostasis. Both  apelin deficiency and  apelin overexpression disrupted embryonic development and reduced adult lifespan, while exhibiting markedly reduced fertility in both sexes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed broad changes in neuroendocrine, hormonal, stress-response, and inflammatory genes with young adult mutant expression profiles resembling those of aged wild-type fish. Both loss and excess of Apelin also disrupted hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis development, reducing hypothalamic thyrotropin-releasing hormone-expressing cells, pituitary gonadotropic cell populations, and thyroid gland volume. Transcriptomic analyses identified  atoh8 , encoding a basic helix–loop–helix transcription factor, as a candidate effector of Apelin signaling. Apelin expression increased  atoh8 expression during early embryogenesis, whereas atoh8 mRNA partially rescued developmental defects in apelin mutants, including hypothalamic and pituitary markers, and thyroid volume. Conversely,  atoh8 crispants displayed thyroid and pituitary abnormalities, supporting a role for Atoh8 in neuroendocrine development. Together, these findings establish Apelin signaling as a dosage-sensitive regulator of zebrafish development and tissue homeostasis and identify Atoh8 as a functional downstream effector that partially mediates Apelin-dependent HPT axis formation. This work links peptide hormone signaling to neuroendocrine development and provides a framework for investigating its broader contributions to vertebrate physiology, reproduction and aging.
authors: Menard R, Neog A, Halluin C, Bonnet F, Madelaine R.

title: CrJAMs are transcriptional repressors of the monoterpenoid indole alkaloid pathway in  Catharanthus roseus
abstract: Catharanthus roseus produces monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (MIAs) in response to the defense hormone jasmonate (JA). In  Arabidopsis , JA regulates defense processes through MYC2 and JA-Associated MYC2a-like transcription factors (JAMs). Here we characterize two previously identified  C. roseus JAMs, CrJAM2 and CrJAM3, as regulators of MIA biosynthesis.  Functional screens using viral-induced gene silencing and transient promoter activity assays showed that CrJAMs repress the MIA pathway; silencing both  CrJAM2 and  CrJAM3 increased expression of MIA pathway genes and MIA levels while their individual overexpression repressed promoter activity. To assess their activity broadly across MIA regulatory and biosynthetic genes, we generated  C. roseus hairy root cultures either constitutively overexpressing individual  CrJAMs or  CRISPR-Cas9 creating mutations in multiple  CrJAMs , and profiled their expression by RNA-Seq.  CrJAM2 overexpression decreased expression of most MIA biosynthetic genes relative to the  GUS control, while double mutant lines showed increased basal expression of these genes relative to non-targeting controls. Notably, methyl JA treatment perturbs this equilibrium, reversing these trends at 24 hrs in both  CrJAM overexpression and mutant lines relative to basal conditions.  In summary, CrJAMs broadly repress MIA regulatory and biosynthetic gene expression and together with CrJAZ and CrMYC2a regulates MIA biosynthesis. Summary sentence  We characterize two previously identified  Catharanthus roseus JAMs; CrJAM2 and CrJAM3 regulate overlapping and unique genes and broadly repress the expression of monoterpenoid indole alkaloid regulatory and biosynthetic genes.
authors: Breselge S, Traverse KKF, Cole-Osborn LF, Sathitloetsakun S, Dürr K, Wang J, Childs KL, Cram EJ, Lee-Parsons CW.

title: Hmox1/CO regulates retina regeneration via modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and induction of  vaspb  in zebrafish
abstract: Müller glia (MG) in the zebrafish retina retain a latent stem cell capacity that is absent in mammals, yet the injury responsive signals that drive this reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify heme oxygenase-1 (Hmox1), the stress-inducible, rate-limiting enzyme of heme catabolism, as a previously unrecognized regulator of this process. Following injury,  hmox1a is selectively and rapidly induced among the heme oxygenase gene family, localizing to photoreceptors with expression peaking during the MG proliferation window. Pharmacological inhibition and morpholino mediated knockdown of Hmox1 dysregulate the acute inflammatory response, impair Müller glia-derived progenitor cell (MGPC) proliferation, and produce lasting deficits in retinal lamination, establishing Hmox1 as a potentially non-redundant, early-acting node required for structural recovery. Exogenous delivery of carbon monoxide (CO), a bioactive Hmox1 metabolite, partially rescues each of these phenotypes, functionally implicating CO as a key downstream effector. Mechanistically, Hmox1/CO signalling stabilizes β-catenin likely via transcriptional repression of the Wnt antagonist  dkk1b . This stabilized β-catenin is enriched at a predicted Tcf7l2 site in the promoter of  vaspb , which encodes an actin binding protein and is newly identified here as an injury-induced Wnt target gene. Bioinformatic and functional analyses further implicate Nfe2l2a (Nrf2) as a candidate intermediary bridging Hmox1/CO to Wnt regulation, with putative antioxidant response elements identified within the  dkk1b locus. Together, these findings outline a putative Hmox1→CO→Nrf2⊣  dkk1b →β-catenin→  vaspb relay coupling redox biology to Wnt-dependent glial reprogramming. Notably, HO-1 is similarly induced in stressed mammalian retina, yet Wnt/β-catenin activation fails to sustain regeneration, positioning the Hmox1/CO axis as a candidate target for future investigation in mammalian retina regeneration.
authors: Sherpa RD, Sen A, Chaudhuri AG, Hui SP.

title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Innate Immune Responses to  Toxoplasma gondii  in Bat Cells
abstract: Bats exhibit remarkable tolerance to numerous viral infections, a phenotype associated with distinctive adaptations in innate immune and inflammatory pathways. Whether these adaptations also shape responses to nonviral intracellular pathogens remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the interaction between the protozoan parasite  Toxoplasma gondii and epithelial cell lines derived from the black flying fox (Pteropus alecto). We found that both type I and type II strains of  T. gondii readily invaded and replicated in bat cells, demonstrating a high degree of cellular permissiveness to infection. Surprisingly, transcriptomic analysis revealed remarkably limited early host responses despite progressive intracellular parasite replication. A pronounced transcriptional response emerged only at later stages of infection, coinciding with extensive parasite replication and cellular damage, and was characterized by changes in genes associated with inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation, and tissue remodeling. Together, these findings reveal an unusual interaction between bat cells and an intracellular protozoan pathogen, characterized by efficient parasite replication and markedly delayed host transcriptional activation. Our results suggest that distinctive regulation of cellular responses to intracellular infection may extend beyond viral pathogens and represent a broader feature of bat immune biology.
authors: Yarovinsky P, Kwok SF.

title: CTLA-4 checkpoint signalling modulates germinal centre dynamics and antibody avidity during  Borrelia burgdorferi  infection in mice
abstract: Borrelia burgdorferi , the causative agent of Lyme borreliosis, persists in mammalian hosts despite robust activation of innate and adaptive immunity. A hallmark of murine infection is the production of low-avidity antibodies, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying this defective humoral response remain poorly understood.  Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of draining lymph node cells from Borrelia-infected mice at days 7 and 14 post-infection, comparing transcriptional profiles with those from mice immunised with heat-killed Borrelia or with a potent germinal centre-inducing protein immunisation. Borrelia infection induced a rapid germinal centre response, however, light zone B cells displayed diminished expression of co-stimulatory and T-B cell interaction molecules while maintaining core germinal centre identity markers, suggesting impaired positive selection. T follicular helper cells upregulated multiple inhibitory checkpoint receptor genes, most prominently Ctla4, alongside an active germinal centre engagement programme. Foxp3⁺ regulatory T cells upregulated genes associated with follicular-homing and suppressive function, including those implicated in CTLA-4-mediated trans-endocytosis. To test whether inhibitory signalling contributes to the impaired humoral response, infected mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4 blocking antibody. CTLA-4 blockade significantly increased plasma cell numbers and enhanced both the magnitude and avidity of  Borrelia - specific IgG responses, including the induction of complement-fixing IgG2a. These findings reveal that CTLA-4-dependent inhibitory signalling contributes to defective antibody quality during  Borrelia infection, identifying a mechanism by which dysregulated T cell responses may facilitate impaired humoral control of a persistent spirochaetal pathogen.  Authors summary  Borrelia burgdorferi , the bacteria that cause Lyme borreliosis, can persist in the body for long periods despite triggering a strong immune response. One puzzling feature of this infection is that the antibodies produced are often of poor quality and do not bind the bacteria effectively.  To investigate why, we examined individual immune cells in lymph nodes of  Borrelia -infected mice and compared them with cells from mice that received non-living  Borrelia or a vaccine- like immunisation known to generate strong antibody responses. Although  Borrelia infection rapidly triggered the formation of structures that normally help the immune system refine and improve antibodies, key communication signals between immune cells were reduced. At the same time, both helper and regulatory T cells showed increased activity of molecular pathways that act as brakes on immune responses. One such brake, controlled by a molecule called CTLA-4, appeared particularly important. When we blocked CTLA-4 during infection, mice produced more antibody-secreting cells and generated antibodies that had improved functional properties.  Our findings identify a mechanism that limits antibody quality during  Borrelia infection and help explain how the bacteria can evade effective immune control and persist in the host.
authors: Mäkinen V, Alinikula J, Fair-Mäkelä R, Sundqvist P, Salmi M, Mattila P, Pietikäinen A, Hytönen J.

title: Microbial Consortia from Chilean Salt Flats Drive Coupled Gypsum Dissolution and Mineralization in the Absence of Evaporation: Experimental Evidence
abstract: Microbial consortia actively modulate mineralogical processes in polyextreme environments, yet biological mechanisms are often excluded from evaporite evolution models. Here, we investigated gypsum surface dissolution and secondary mineral nucleation driven by microbial mats and natural brines from three Andean salt flats (Salar de Llamara, Salar de Pajonales, and Salar de Gorbea) across 90-day incubation experiments. Synthesized gypsum crystals were exposed to inoculated media and sterile brines (abiotic controls) under controlled conditions, and analyzed using SEM-EDS and epifluorescence microscopy. Results demonstrate that microbial colonization dual-modulates gypsum dynamics: while apparent microbially-mediated boring formed rounded cavities, extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrices acted as diffusion barriers that buffered abiotic dissolution. Furthermore, EPS promoted localized supersaturation and authigenic mineral nucleation, yielding fibrous eugsterite and globular Mg-silicates across all sites, alongside site-specific phases such as dumbbell-shaped calcite, allotriomorphic halite (Pajonales), and lenticular alunite (Gorbea). Abiotic controls exhibited simpler parageneses and angular dissolution along cleavage planes without filling. Specific bio-induced textures, including EPS-infilled pores, dumbbell calcite, Mg-Si globules, and alveolar eugsterite, represent potential morphological biosignatures relevant to astrobiology. Our findings demonstrate that purely abiotic geochemical models are insufficient to describe brine evolution, underscoring the critical necessity of integrating geomicrobiological interactions into evaporite formation frameworks.
authors: Orellana I, Tebes C, Demergasso C, Cabestrero Ó.

title: Analysis of HPV Genotype Distribution, Viral Load Profiles, and Their Relationship With Cervical Pathology Among Women in Samarkand Region (2023-2025)
abstract: Abstract  Introduction:  Persistent infection with high-risk oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary cause of cervical cancer development. Objective  To evaluate the prevalence of various HPV genotypes, describe genotype-specific viral load patterns, and determine their relationship with patient age and cervical cytological changes among women in the Samarkand region. Methods  In a cross-sectional study (2023–2025), cervical epithelial samples from 535 women (aged 19–56 years) were analyzed. Genotyping of 21 HPV types and quantification of viral load (expressed in \(\:\text{l}\text{g}\) copies of DNA/10⁵ cells) were performed using real-time PCR. Cytological status was classified according to The Bethesda System (TBS, 2014) in cohorts with monoinfection (n = 73) and mixed infection (n = 20). Results  Out of 116 HPV-positive cases, HPV 16 was unconditionally dominant (24%). An atypically low prevalence of HPV 18 (3%) was observed alongside a high detection rate of non-vaccine types: HPV 56 (6%), 51 (5%), and 58 (4%). No statistically significant correlation was found between patient age and viral load (p > 0.05). A significant overall association was revealed between HPV genotype and cytological status (χ²=97.06; df = 68; p = 0.012). HPV 58 demonstrated the highest pathogenetic potential (OR = 12.11; 80% of cases were ASC-US, 20% were ASC-H) and was never detected in normal cytology (NILM). No direct linear correlation was found between viral load level and lesion severity: peak loads were recorded in NILM cases, whereas the only severe case (HSIL, associated with HPV 68) presented with a low viral load (2.7 lg copies/10⁵ cells). Conclusion  The regional epidemiological profile is determined by the dominance of HPV 16 and a high circulation of high-risk non-vaccine strains (56, 51, 58). Viral load exhibits immense genotype-specific variability and does not directly correlate with the severity of cytological changes, highlighting the necessity of integrating multi-genotype PCR testing and cytological screening.
authors: Yarmukhamedova GK, Kan SV, Dushanova GA, Ziyadullayeva GZ, Khalilova SA, Yarmukhamedova MK.

title: Neuroscience Research: Before and After the Evolution of Optogenetics
abstract: Abstract  In an article titled “Thinking about the Brain,” published in a special issue of Scientific American devoted to the Brain in September 1979, Francis H.C. Crick wrote: “Reflecting on itself, the human brain has uncovered some marvelous facts. What appears to be needed for understanding how it works is new techniques for examining it and new ways of thinking about it.” He made several important observations about the technological limitations of the time, noting that electrodes cannot readily distinguish different types of neurons. Light could be an ideal signal to turn firing on and off in an alert animal (Crick 1999; Crick 1979). This conceptual blueprint was eventually realized experimentally through the groundbreaking work of Hegemann, Nagel, Deisseroth, and their colleagues, who harnessed the microbial channelrhodopsins to achieve fast, genetically targeted, light-driven control of neuronal activity (Boyden et al. 2005; Nagel et al. 2002; Nagel et al. 2003). Over the past two decades, optogenetics has become a mainstay of circuit neuroscience and is now emerging as a potential therapeutic approach. In light of the 2026 Nobel Prize awarded to optogenetics, this perspective narrates the evolution of neuroscience research before and after the advent of optogenetics, and summarizes how this technology has transformed our approaches to studying the brain.
authors: Pandey S, Abraham NM.

title: Sustained HBsAg Loss and Marked Reversal of Liver Cirrhosis in a Patient with Antiviral-Resistant Chronic Hepatitis B: A Case Report with 13-Year Follow-up
abstract: Abstract    Background  Achieving sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss and reversing established cirrhosis is considered extremely challenging, especially in patients with prior antiviral resistance. We report a case of marked reversal of liver cirrhosis and sustained HBsAg loss in a patient with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) who previously failed standard antiviral therapy.  Case Presentation  A 60-year-old male patient was diagnosed with CHB in 2006 and developed cirrhosis after 6 years of standard antiviral therapy at a top-tier hospital. In February 2012, his liver stiffness (FibroScan) was 19.9 kPa, with HBV DNA at 1.47×10^7 IU/ml. He subsequently received combined Chinese-Western medicine ("Neo-Chinese Medicine") treatment. After 7 years and 2 months of treatment, his liver function normalized, HBV DNA became undetectable, and FibroScan decreased to 5.1 kPa. Notably, the patient achieved HBsAg loss and Pre-S1 antigen negativity. All medications were discontinued in April 2019. By November 2020, despite the patient developing hyperlipidemia and steatohepatitis due to lifestyle factors, imaging and elastography confirmed a marked reversal of cirrhosis (FibroScan: 6.2 kPa, normal portal vein diameter of 12 mm) without disease progression. Long-term follow-up up to 2025 consistently showed sustained HBsAg negativity (Conclusion  This case demonstrates that Neo-Chinese Medicine can achieve marked reversal of cirrhosis and sustained functional cure in patients with antiviral-resistant CHB. The durability of these outcomes after treatment discontinuation suggests a fundamental restoration of the hepatic microenvironment and the depletion of the viral reservoir.
authors: Li w.

title: Native-to-fibril structural remodelling reveals an amyloid-selective transthyretin epitope for AI-guided binder design
abstract: Abstract  Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis involves conversion of the native tetramer into cross-$\beta$ fibrils, creating potential targets for conformation-selective binders. Full-assembly solvent-accessibility analysis of 30 patient-derived fibril structures, spanning wild-type TTR and ten hereditary variants, identifies increased exposure of an N-terminal region adjacent to Cys10. Using a common normalisation reference, mean relative solvent accessibility for residues 11--15 is 0.089 in native TTR and at least 0.168 in fibrils. Modification mapping, saturation-mutagenesis stability predictions and steric PTM models provide molecular context. BoltzGen and RFAntibody generate candidate binders, and sequence-only Boltz-2 counter-predictions place selected nanobodies at the Pro11/Met13/Lys15 region in fibril-derived constructs but at distal surfaces in native-state constructs. Vitreous-fibril designs also engage cardiac-fibril constructs, suggesting cross-tissue epitope recognition. These results support structure-guided candidate prioritisation, while fibril geometry, binding affinity and disease-state selectivity require experimental validation.
authors: Lomoio U, Carbonari V, Roncada P, Urbani A, Lio' P, Veltri P, Guzzi PH.

title: Verifiable Deep Learning: Smart Contract--Enabled Model Integrity and Provenance on Distributed Ledgers
abstract: Abstract  Deep learning artifacts undergo long and mutable lifecycles in which datasets, preprocessing pipelines, checkpoints, evaluation configurations, and deployed versions may be controlled by different actors. Hash anchoring makes individual bytes tamper-evident but does not establish that a checkpoint was derived from authorized data or that its alleged computation actually occurred. We present ProofWeave, a provenance-coupled verification specification that treats model evolution as a typed, policy-constrained transition system. Each transition binds content commitments, authenticated parent references, version rules, and explicit evidence obligations; the proposed contract state machine admits only policy-valid transitions. We distinguish full computational proofs, conditioned on a sound external proving backend, from probabilistic committed-step audits with a finite-population detection bound. For transparent evaluation we implement a local integrity prototype, not a live blockchain or zero-knowledge proof service. Seven deterministic integrity fault types are assessed across three public datasets; four nested validators cover 2, 4, 6, and 7 of the nine broader threat classes discussed. To expose an essential security boundary, we additionally perform 105 real MLP training runs over seven random seeds and five controlled training-label corruption rates. Hash/signature microbenchmarks and Merkle trees of up to 65,536 leaves characterize local scaling. A controlled Monte Carlo audit study quantifies probabilistic detection under committed-step sampling, separately from the local measurements. The evidence supports preliminary provenance-check correctness and quantifies its limits; it does not establish on-chain costs or end-to-end verifiable neural training.
authors: Wu F, Yuan B, Wang Y.

title: Experimental Synthesis, Characterization, and Numerical Device Simulation of Hydrazinium–Methylammonium Mixed Lead Bromide Perovskites for Solar Cell Applications
abstract: Abstract  Mixed-cation lead bromide perovskite thin films and powders with composition HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 (x = 0.0, 0.20, 0.40) were synthesised via solution-processed spin-coating and comprehensively characterised to elucidate the role of methylammonium (MA+) incorporation in hydrazinium (HA+) lead bromide perovskites. XRD analysis revealed a progressive hexagonal-to-tetragonal phase transition with increasing MA+ content, accompanied by crystallite size reduction from 86.68 ± 5.99 nm to 61.26 ± 11.59 nm and concurrent increases in dislocation density and microstrain. SEM confirmed morphological evolution from agglomerated nanoparti cles (88.61 ± 23.43 nm) in pristine HAPbBr3 to a refined homogeneous nanostructure (72.41 ± 16.40 nm) in HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3, while EDX confirmed stoichiometric compositions and successful A-site cation mixing. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy verified co incorporation of both cations within the intact PbBr4− 6 octahedral framework. UV–Vis spectrophotometry revealed direct bandgaps of 2.9565, 2.9339, and 2.3075 eV for x = 0, 0.20, and 0.40, respectively, demonstrating continuous bandgap tunability via a two-stage mechanism of chemical A-site perturbation and phase-transition-driven bandgap collapse. Urbach energy decreased monotonically from 0.2112 to 0.1902 eV, indicating progressive band-edge quality improvement. Hall effect measurements showed carrier mobility increasing from 71.86 to 143.2 cm2 V−1 s−1 and conductivity from 1.078×10−5 to 2.278×10−5 Ω−1 cm−1 for HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3. Using experimentally determined parameters, seventeen solar-cell architectures (SC1–SC17) were evaluated by SCAPS-1D simu lation, employing HAPbBr3 and HA0.8MA0.2PbBr3 as electron transport layers and HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 as the absorber layer. The highest PCE of 32.18% was achieved by Cs2InSbCl6-based devices (SC3 and SC8) with NiO hole transport layers, while HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 single-absorber cells (SC11–SC13) attained the highest fill factors (>82%) among all architectures. Temperature (300–420 K) and back-contact work function (4.8–6.0 eV) analyses confirmed the thermal robustness and contact tolerance of the devices, establishing HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 as a promising candidate for next-generation tandem photovoltaic applications.

title: LINC00641 Expression and a Predicted LINC00641-Associated RNA Network in Multiple Sclerosis
abstract: Abstract  Background  Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease characterized by demyelination and neurodegeneration. Long non-coding RNAs may contribute to gene-regulatory changes in MS, but the involvement of LINC00641 has not been investigated. Methods and Results  LINC00641 expression was measured by quantitative real-time PCR in peripheral blood samples from 48 patients with MS and 48 healthy controls. LINC00641-associated mRNAs were retrieved from ENCORI and integrated with differential-expression analysis of the GSE137143 RNA-seq dataset. Protein-interaction analysis, functional enrichment, miRNA-target prediction, and receiver operating characteristic analyses were then performed. LINC00641 was significantly upregulated in MS and showed case-control discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.74). Six LINC00641-associated genes—DDX5, HNRNPC, THRAP3, YY1, SUPT16H, and HP1BP3—were significantly upregulated in the RNA-seq dataset, with individual AUC values of 0.64–0.71. A logistic-regression model combining the six genes showed an AUC of 0.806. Eleven predicted miRNAs were shared among the six genes, and enrichment analysis linked the gene set mainly to RNA splicing, mRNA processing, and chromatin organization. Conclusions  LINC00641 is upregulated in MS, and integration of experimental expression data with transcriptomic and network analyses identifies a LINC00641-associated RNA signature linked to RNA-processing pathways. These findings support independent validation and functional investigation of LINC00641 and the associated network as candidate molecular biomarkers and regulators in MS.
authors: Sadeghi¹˒³ N, Salehi² Z, Hojati³ Z, Salehi Z.

title: Integrative Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals POLQ as a Prognostic Biomarker and Immunotherapeutic Target in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract  DNA polymerase theta (POLQ) mediates microhomology-mediated end joining and represents a synthetic lethal target for homologous recombination deficient cancers, yet its pan-cancer clinical, immunoregulatory and predictive functions are poorly defined. Multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, cBioPortal, TIMER2.0 and GSCA were used for pan-cancer profiling of POLQ expression, mutations, prognosis, immune signatures. Drug sensitivity correlation analysis together with in silico molecular docking simulations were applied to predict potential binding between POLQ and candidate therapeutic agents. Differential gene expression analysis and functional enrichment were further investigated in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC). POLQ was overexpressed in most malignancies, associated with advanced stages and poor survival. Gene amplification drove its upregulation. POLQ expression showed significant correlations with immune cell infiltration, tumor mutation burden, and microsatellite instability. The strong negative correlations between POLQ expression and responses to multiple chemotherapeutic agents, with molecular docking predicted potential direct interactions between vincristine, paclitaxel, docetaxel and the POLQ protein. In UCEC, high POLQ activated DNA replication, cell cycle and ATR-dependent DNA damage pathways. POLQ is a pan-cancer prognostic and therapeutic biomarker. In UCEC, it accelerates tumor progression via DNA damage and cell cycle dysregulation and reshapes immune microenvironment, supporting POLQ-targeted precision immunotherapy especially for endometrial cancer.
authors: Du B, Wang C, Lv Y, Wang Q, Wang F, Li J, Gao H, Chang R, Li H.

title: Increased Zoonotic Risk Posed by Emerging Haemagglutinin Variants of Clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza Virus
abstract: Abstract  High pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) remain a major threat to animal and human health. The clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx panzootic has been marked by increasing cross-species adaptation, including outbreaks in dairy cattle. The surge in mammalian infections in both wild and captive populations heighten concerns about zoonotic and pandemic potential. Here, we analyse haemagglutinin (HA) evolution in clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx viruses from 2020 to 2025, focusing on key residues within the receptor-binding domain. We identify HA E185K (mature H5 HA numbering; E189K in H3 numbering) as a novel immune escape mutation that confers increased binding to avian- and human-type sialic acid receptors. Strikingly, this mutation is increasingly prevalent in cattle-derived H5N1 viruses and enhances binding to human-like receptors. However, ferret studies demonstrated that whilst pathogenicity of the E185K virus was comparable to the cattle derived isolate, the E185K mutation did not confer transmission to direct or indirect contact ferrets. Our results reveal a mechanism linking immune escape with expanded receptor specificity, highlighting a potential pathway for mammalian adaptation. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance of evolving H5Nx viruses to mitigate emerging zoonotic threats.

title: Fucosyltransferase 4 as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in osteosarcoma: a multi-dataset transcriptomic and structural bioinformatics analysis
abstract: Abstract    Background  Osteosarcoma, the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and young adults, has a poor prognosis in metastatic or recurrent disease. Fucosyltransferase 4 (  FUT4  ) mediates fucosylation and has been implicated in several cancers, but its role in osteosarcoma remains unclear. Methods  Using two public Gene Expression Omnibus microarray cohorts (GSE36001, GSE16088), we assessed  FUT4  expression and diagnostic performance by limma-based differential analysis and ROC curves with AUC estimation, and profiled function through GO, KEGG, GSEA and GSVA. We further constructed protein-protein interaction and transcription factor/microRNA/drug regulatory networks, characterized immune-cell signatures by ssGSEA, and prioritized candidate binding compounds by DrugCLIP virtual screening followed by AutoDock Vina docking. Results  FUT4  transcripts were significantly down-regulated in osteosarcoma in both cohorts (GSE36001, p FUT4  -associated genes were enriched in ossification, osteoblast differentiation and extracellular matrix-related terms. GSEA linked high  FUT4  to epithelial-mesenchymal transition and inflammatory-response signatures, and exploratory GSVA suggested differences in cytoskeletal, apoptotic and Wnt/beta-catenin signalling between  FUT4  -low and  FUT4  -high subgroups, which also showed distinct immune-cell correlation patterns. Structure-based screening prioritized ST50926609 as the lead candidate  FUT4  -binding compound (Vina score = − 7.35 kcal/mol). Conclusions  Collectively, these computational findings support  FUT4  as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in osteosarcoma, but they remain hypothesis-generating and require validation in clinical cohorts, cell and animal models.

title: Circular RNA in Lipid Nanoparticles: From Molecular Engineering to First-in-Human Testing
abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) were, until a decade ago, a by-product of transcriptome profiling. They are now drug candidates. A covalently closed backbone removes the termini that exonucleases and cap-dependent decay require, and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) turn that molecular property into a pharmacological one by carrying the RNA into the cytoplasm of a chosen cell. Between 2021 and 2026 the field moved from reporter-gene proof of concept to nine first-in-human programmes, five of which encode a CD19 chimeric antigen receptor and one of which has completed. We argue that the central question is no longer whether circRNA can be made and delivered, but which of its claimed advantages survive in vivo, and at what cost in manufacturing complexity. We examine performance determinants at three coupled levels, the molecule, the particle and the biological context, and set out the manufacturing, analytical and regulatory problems that will decide whether circularity becomes a general platform property or a niche solution.
authors: Zhao Y, Cheng H, Zhou S, He L, Xiu C, Huang B, Lu X.

title: Isoform Remodeling Along the Human Monocyte-to-Macrophage Differentiation Axis
abstract: Tissue-resident macrophage diversity has been mapped at the gene-expression level, and alternative splicing has been catalogued across immune lineages [1,2]; isoform behavior along the monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation axis remains unexamined. Analyzing a 17-gene immune panel across BLUEPRINT differentiation series and GTEx v8, we identify an MSR1 isoform switch with complete donor-level separation (short-isoform fraction 0.844–0.914 in monocytes versus 0.291–0.541 in six macrophage samples; exact permutation p = 0.024) — a switch from the dominant-negative SR-AIII scavenger-receptor isoform to functional SR-AI/II receptors — with equally supported PTPRC, MYD88, and IRAK1 remodeling, whereas an IL1B canonical-fraction rise is donor-heterogeneous (p = 0.114). LY96 (MD-2) is induced ~17-fold during differentiation, yet the functionally decisive antagonist/agonist isoform ratio is not resolved by standard short-read annotation — a methodological gap for immune isoform studies. CD14/CD163 show dosage regulation without isoform switching: CD163 peaks in LPS-driven M1 macrophages and, in human brain, marks border-associated macrophages rather than microglia. A 62-gene cytoskeletal panel nominates septin-family isoform divergence as a candidate mechanism of the ramified-to-amoeboid morphology spectrum, with PTBP1/hnRNP/SRSF programs as candidate executors of immune-side switching. Differentiation-coupled isoform remodeling is thus a component of macrophage identity.
authors: Wang X, Chen H, Li D, Shen C.

title: Polysaccharides in modern therapeutics: structural diversity, delivery platforms, and antitumor applications.
abstract: Polysaccharides, as structurally diverse and biologically versatile natural macromolecules, have long been recognised for their indispensable roles in immune regulation, intercellular communication, and tissue architecture. Their intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability, and chemical modifiability position them at the interface between small-molecule drugs, biologics, and functional biomaterials. This review provides a systematic overview of the biological characteristics, historical evolution, and clinical applications of polysaccharide-based drugs, with an emphasis on marketed products and advanced clinical candidates. We critically discuss recent progress in polysaccharide-based delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, hydrogels, and polysaccharide-drug conjugates, highlighting how molecular design - such as molecular weight control, glycosidic linkage configuration, and functional group substitution - governs pharmacological activity and targeting performance. Particular attention is given to antitumor applications, where natural and chemically modified polysaccharides (e.g. selenized, phosphorylated, and sulphated derivatives) exert multitarget effects through cell cycle arrest, apoptosis induction, tumour microenvironment remodelling, and immunomodulation. Despite significant advances, challenges related to structural heterogeneity, batch-to-batch variability, and incomplete structure-activity relationship elucidation continue to hinder clinical translation. By integrating structural precision with mechanistic clarity, polysaccharide-based drugs are poised to evolve from supportive agents into rationally designed, next-generation therapeutic platforms.
authors: Wang X, Li Y, Li X, Zhang Y, Yu C, Guo J, Li K, Wang H.

title: Low-Titre ANA Late-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Presenting With Pleural Effusion and Markedly Elevated Pleural Adenosine Deaminase Mimicking Tuberculous Pleuritis.
abstract: Pleural effusion with markedly elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA) levels is commonly associated with tuberculous pleuritis but may occur in other conditions. We report a case of low-titre ANA late-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting with pleural effusion and markedly elevated ADA levels mimicking tuberculosis. A 78-year-old man with pneumoconiosis presented with fever, cough, and progressive pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis revealed lymphocyte-predominant exudative effusion with markedly elevated ADA levels. Tuberculous pleuritis was initially suspected, but microbiological tests were negative. The patient developed thrombocytopenia, renal dysfunction, and altered consciousness. Immunological findings showed hypocomplementemia and elevated anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies despite low-titre ANA. Corticosteroid therapy led to rapid improvement, confirming the diagnosis of late-onset SLE. Clinicians should consider autoimmune diseases when tuberculosis is not microbiologically confirmed.
authors: Inoue S, Tatsuta M, Tatsutani T, Ueda S, Wakamatsu K, Kawasaki M.
