title: Long-term fertilizer-derived chloride inputs suppress nitrification and alter nitrogen supply patterns in a temperate agricultural brown soil
abstract: Chloride-containing fertilizers, especially those used as accompanying components in nitrogen fertilizers, are widely applied into the soil for agricultural production. However, the long-term impacts of this chloride input on nitrification and inorganic nitrogen supply remain poorly understood. Here, in order to determine whether long-term chloride-containing fertilization is associated with soil acidification, suppressed potential nitrification rate, altered ammonia-oxidizing microbial communities, and a shift in inorganic nitrogen supply patterns, we used a 35-year field experiment in Northeast China to compare chloride-free, low chloride, and high chloride fertilization regimes under equal total N, P, and K inputs. The results showed that High chloride treatments were associated with lower soil pH, although the direct effect of chloride on pH was not statistically significant in the path model, suggesting that ammonium-based fertilization itself is a major contributor to acidification in this system. Linear mixed models (LMM) further verified the significant effects of chloride addition and soil pH on PNR and the abundance of ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms. Our results suggest chloride may suppress soil nitrification via two hypothesized pathways: putative direct inhibitory effects of chloride, and an indirect pathway mediated by chloride-associated shifts in soil pH that may suppress ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms. Together, these two pathways facilitate the accumulation of ammonium-N relative to nitrate-N. High chloride treatments suppressed ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), and the abundance of AOA decreased by up to 72%. Amplicon sequencing of harvest-stage soil samples demonstrated that high chloride input altered the diversity and community composition of ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms, and reduced maize grain yield. Our findings reveal that combined application of potassium chloride and chloride-containing nitrogen fertilizers exacerbates soil acidification and substantially disturbs soil nitrification as well as ammonia-oxidizing microbial communities. Such disturbances reshape soil inorganic nitrogen supply patterns within this long-term brown-soil agroecosystem.

title: Seed development shapes the diversity, succession, and functional potential of endophytic bacterial communities in Camellia oleifera
abstract: Camellia oleifera is a significant woody oil crop with considerable commercial, nutritional, and ecological importance. The developmental processes of seed endophytic bacterial populations are inadequately understood. This study used 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing to analyze the diversity, community structure, and predicted functions of endophytic bacteria in C. oleifera seeds across four developmental stages: early fruit-set (YC1), young fruit (YC2), early mature (YC3), and late mature (YC4). A total of 907,440 raw reads were obtained, and 874,097 effective sequences were retained across 12 sequencing samples, which were taxonomically assigned to 41 phyla, 112 classes, 258 orders, 448 families, 994 genera, and 1,602 putative species-level ASVs. The predominant phyla were Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Actinobacteriota, and Bacteroidota, with Pseudomonas, Methylobacterium-Methylorubrum, and the uncultured lineage 1174-901-12 as the prevalent taxa. Alpha- and beta-diversity analyses showed distinct stage-specific community succession: YC1-YC3 exhibited greater richness and diversity, whereas YC4 showed a decline in both. PICRUSt2-based prediction of COG functional categories showed that functions related to energy production and conversion (C), amino acid transport and metabolism (E), inorganic ion transport and metabolism (P), translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis (J), and cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis (M) were relatively abundant. These results provide a microbiological foundation for comprehending seed development and identifying functional strains in C. oleifera.

title: A quantitative microbial risk assessment of Escherichia coli O157:H7 in sheep meat in Saudi Arabia
abstract: BackgroundEscherichia coli O157:H7 is an important foodborne pathogen associated with severe clinical outcomes. It has been detected in sheep and sheep meat in Saudi Arabia. However, quantitative estimates of exposure and illness risk under the Saudi food-supply context remain limited.MethodsA probabilistic quantitative microbial risk assessment model was developed for sheep meat. Seven fixed initial contamination levels were evaluated, ranging from −3 to 3 log10 CFU/g. Each level was simulated under two storage scenarios: recommended refrigeration (1–5 °C) and a plausible temperature distribution. Saudi consumption and supply patterns were maintained across scenarios.ResultsAcross the seven contamination levels, both the probability of illness and modeled annual incidence increased with initial concentration. At 3 log10 CFU/g, the median probability of illness was 1.50 × 10−9 under recommended storage and 3.40 × 10−9 under plausible storage. Median annual incidence was zero cases per 100,000 under both scenarios when rounded to the nearest whole case. Factor-fixing sensitivity analysis identified the probability of illness from a single organism as the most influential parameter, followed by internal cooking temperature.ConclusionThe modeled results suggest that population-level risk is associated with a subset of high-exposure scenarios observed within the simulation. Variation across storage and cooking conditions is reflected in the distribution of outcomes.

title: Study on the nutrient spatiotemporal changes and multi-habitat microbial succession in a decoupled largemouth bass–garlic chive aquaponics system
abstract: The decoupled aquaponics system was an important model of circular agriculture and represents a mature circular agricultural framework, yet integrated studies simultaneously tracking nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and microbial communities in water, sediment, substrate and fish gut remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a three-month continuous monitoring (July to September 2024) of a triplicate indoor decoupled aquaponics system combining largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) and garlic chives (Allium tuberosum) in northern Chinese greenhouses. Nutrient dynamics (total nitrogen, TN; total phosphorus, TP; total potassium, TK) were quantified monthly in aquaculture water, sedimentation tank mud and cultivation substrate, while microbial community structure, succession and putative functions were characterized via 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, canonical correspondence analysis (CCA), variance partitioning analysis (VPA) and PICRUSt2 functional prediction. The results were as follows: (1) The three modules formed a characteristic “water transport → mud accumulated → substrate consumption” nutrient cascade, with nutrient reserves ordered as mud > substrate > water. (2) TN in water increased by 237.60% over the cultivation period, indicating a latent risk of eutrophication. Microbial communities exhibited strong habitat partitioning, with Proteobacteria as the shared dominant phylum across environmental media, while fish gut harbored a temporally dynamic assemblage shifting from Fusobacteriota (83.11% in July) to Firmicutes (73.31% in September), forming a distinct “environmental versus host” bistable zonation. (3) VPA revealed that TN and TP synergistically regulated mud microbiota (27.70% interaction), whereas TK independently structured substrate communities (19.95% independent contribution), ranking as the strongest single-nutrient driver (K > N > P). (4) PICRUSt2-based functional prediction indicated metabolism as the core function across all habitats, with complementary profiles—sediment for nutrient sensing, substrate for stable transformation, water for temporal adaptation, and gut for host-specific nutrition. These provide species-specific nutrient–microbe linkage data, synchronous four-habitat temporal dynamics, and quantitative partitioning of N/P/K effects, offering actionable baselines for structural optimization, seasonal nutrient regulation and targeted microbial modification in decoupled aquaponics facilities.

title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis in premature ovarian insufficiency and polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective cohort observational study
abstract: BackgroundPremature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) are two major reproductive endocrine disorders associated with impaired ovarian function and infertility. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis has been implicated in both conditions, direct comparisons of their microbial and functional characteristics remain limited.MethodsIn this prospective cohort study, 102 women of reproductive age, including patients with PCOS and POI as well as healthy controls (NG), were recruited between March 2024 and March 2025. Gut microbial profiles were initially characterized by 16S rDNA amplicon sequencing in 101 fecal samples, and 90 fecal samples (30 per group) were subsequently subjected to metagenomics sequencing for comprehensive taxonomic and functional analyses. Differential taxa, microbial functions, and their associations with baseline characteristics were evaluated.ResultsBoth PCOS and POI exhibited gut microbial dysbiosis characterized by reduced abundances of Bacteroides compared with healthy controls. Distinct disease-specific microbial signatures were identified. The PCOS microbiome was enriched in Escherichia coli, together with functional pathways associated with energy metabolism, lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, biofilm formation, antimicrobial resistance, and environmental adaptation. In contrast, the POI microbiome was characterized by enrichment of Gemmiger, Subdoligranulum, and Clostridiales-related taxa, accompanied by enhanced aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis, fatty acid biosynthesis, glucuronate metabolism, and carbohydrate utilization pathways. Correlation analyses further demonstrated close associations between disease-specific microbial taxa, microbial functions, and host metabolic and reproductive hormone profiles.ConclusionPCOS and POI share common features of gut microbial dysbiosis but exhibit distinct taxonomic and functional signatures. These findings provide new insights into microbiome-associated mechanisms underlying female reproductive endocrine disorders.

title: Karst wetland reclamation increases the proportion of inorganic sulfur in total sulfur: associations with sulfate-reducing bacteria abundance and soil enzyme activity
abstract: Karst wetlands are fragile and critical ecosystems for soil sulfur biogeochemical cycling. In this study, six typical land-use types in the Huixian karst wetland of Guilin, southern China, were selected to investigate the variations in soil physicochemical properties, four inorganic sulfur fractions, soil enzyme activities, and sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) abundance across 0–40 cm soil profiles. The results showed that wetland reclamation significantly reduced soil pH, soil organic carbon (SOC), silt content, total nitrogen, and total sulfur, while increasing soil bulk density, electrical conductivity (EC), and redox potential (Eh). Reclamation reduced the content of total inorganic sulfur, while elevating its proportion in total sulfur; water-soluble sulfur dominated the inorganic sulfur pool. The composition of inorganic sulfur fractions differed markedly across land-use types. Reclamation increased SRB abundance but inhibited soil enzyme activities. Correlation analysis indicated that soil enzyme activities were negatively correlated with inorganic sulfur contents in abandoned land, whereas positive correlations were observed in other land-use types. Close internal correlations existed among different inorganic sulfur fractions. Soil pH and SOC were associated with greater inorganic sulfur accumulation, while Eh showed an inhibitory association. SOC, Eh, EC, pH, and silt content were the key environmental factors associated with SRB abundance and soil enzyme activities. Collectively, wetland reclamation reduced absolute concentrations of both total inorganic sulfur (TIS) and total organic sulfur (TOS), and preferential loss of TOS increased the TIS/TS ratio, altered sulfur transformation processes, and were accompanied by higher SRB abundance and lower soil enzyme activity. This study reveals the responses of soil sulfur biogeochemical processes to land-use conversion in subtropical karst wetlands and provides insights into sulfur cycle regulation under wetland disturbance.

title: ST-26 serotype V Group B Streptococcus: an unexpected lineage among maternal carriage strains and neonatal infection in Gabon
abstract: BackgroundTo investigate the burden of neonatal Group B Streptococcus (GBS) infection, we conducted a prospective study at a regional hospital in Gabon.MethodsConsecutive parturients and their newborns were enrolled in this study. Vaginal swabs were collected and cultured to test for GBS colonization. Blood cultures were obtained from newborns presenting clinical signs suggestive of infection during the first 28 days of life. All GBS strains underwent whole-genome sequencing.ResultsA total of 203 newborns and 197 mothers were enrolled. One newborn developed GBS disease, corresponding to an incidence of 4.93 cases per 1,000 live births. Vaginal GBS colonization was detected in 28 parturients (14.2%). Seven colonizing strains (25.0%) and the neonatal strain belonged to clonal complex CC26.ConclusionThese initial data on the molecular epidemiology of maternal GBS colonization and neonatal infection in Gabon reveal an unexpected contribution of CC26 strains, a lineage that has been rarely reported in this context.

title: The ulvanolytic capacity of the seaweed associated bacterium Aliiglaciecola sp. SL4
abstract: Polysaccharide utilization loci (PULs) enable marine heterotrophic bacteria to access the complex carbohydrates that constitute a major reservoir of fixed carbon in seaweed biomass. Here, we identify and characterize two enzymes from a novel ulvan utilization locus (uPUL) from the genome of Aliiglaciecola sp. SL4 (GlaSL4), an epiphytic bacterium isolated from an Ulva species of green macroalgae. Genome analysis revealed a dedicated ulvan degradation system encoding a suite of carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) and auxiliary enzymes predicted to carry out ulvan depolymerisation and downstream oligosaccharide processing. Biochemical validation of the polysaccharide lyase GlaPL25a and the unsaturated glycoside hydrolase GlaGH105 confirmed their activities and broader roles as key initiating enzymes in the ulvan utilization pathway. These findings provide experimental evidence linking a previously uncharacterized uPUL to ulvan degradation, advancing our understanding of marine carbon cycling and expanding the repertoire of enzymes available for algal biomass conversion and the generation of value-added ulvan oligosaccharides.

title: Global research landscape and emerging trends in intervertebral disc degeneration and the gut microbiota: a multi-database bibliometric and knowledge mapping analysis
abstract: ObjectiveTo characterize the global research landscape and thematic evolution of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) and gut microbiota using multi-database bibliometric analysis and knowledge mapping, and to identify major research hotspots and emerging trends.MethodsThis study employed a bibliometric and knowledge-mapping design. We searched the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus for relevant English-language original articles and reviews from database inception to July 31, 2026. We merged records retrieved from the two databases. After removing duplicates, screening for relevance, and standardizing data, we performed bibliometric and knowledge mapping analyses using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and bibliometrix. We analyzed research output, collaboration networks, co-citation relationships, and keyword evolution.ResultsWe included 385 publications from 58 countries and 224 journals. The annual number of publications showed an overall upward trend, with more rapid growth after 2020. China and the United States led contributions, while the United States played a central role in the international collaboration network. European Spine Journal published the most articles. Co-citation and keyword analyses showed that research interest gradually shifted from local disc infection, clinical phenotypes, and inflammatory mechanisms toward gut microbiota dysbiosis, the gut–disc axis, and potential causal relationships. “Gut microbiota” and “Mendelian randomization” showed the two strongest keyword bursts, both during 2024–2026. The “gut–disc axis” emerged as a burst keyword in 2025. Recent studies have also drawn increasing attention to the NLRP3 inflammasome and pyroptosis.ConclusionResearch on IDD and the gut microbiota is increasingly integrating local pathological mechanisms with the gut microbial ecosystem. The gut–disc axis, inflammation-related cell death, and causal inference have emerged as important research priorities requiring further validation. However, bibliometric trends alone cannot establish biological causality or therapeutic effectiveness. Future studies should integrate longitudinal population studies, genetic causal inference, and functional experiments to clarify potential causal relationships and evaluate the therapeutic relevance of microbiome-targeted interventions.

title: Environmental drivers of microbial community dynamics in a cool-water aquaponics system
abstract: Aquaponic systems represent an integrated water-efficient approach to food production by combining recirculating aquaculture with hydroponic plant cultivation. Performance and stability of these systems depend not only on fish and plant interactions but also on the structure and function of associated microbial communities, which regulate nutrient cycling and water quality. Microbial communities play a central role in the stability and performance of aquaponic systems, yet the relative importance of temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and environmental drivers remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated microbial consortia and production characteristics in six replicate aquaponic systems with cool/cold water fishes, including rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) and yellow perch (Perca flavescens, all female) to cultivate lettuce (Lactuca sativa) and kale (Brassica oleracea), and investigated microbial community structure across production cycles and system compartments using high-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA gene and multivariate ecological analyses. DNA samples were collected from fish tank water during the initial control cycle and from key aquaponic compartments, including circulating water, rhizosphere, biodeposits, and biofilters, during three subsequent harvesting cycles. Across all four cycles, a core microbiome was observed, with 136 shared taxa. Microbial communities were consistently structured at the system level where each system supported a distinct microbial assemblage. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed that microbial community composition was significantly influenced by both production cycle and compartment with temporal effects emerging as a dominant driver of variation. Observed shifts in microbial communities were closely associated with temperature and pH gradients. Significant but comparatively weaker differences were observed among individual AP systems, fish species, and plant species. These results indicate that microbial community structure was shaped primarily by temporal succession across production cycles, with additional contributions from spatial structuring and biotic factors. These findings provide insight into ecological processes governing aquaponic microbiomes and highlight the importance of managing environmental conditions to promote system stability and performance.

title: Expression, purification and broad-spectrum antibacterial characterization of Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage PPAT endolysin
abstract: The prevalence of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria poses a serious threat to clinical anti-infective therapy, and bacteriophage-encoded endolysins have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics due to their high efficiency and low risk of resistance development. In this study, the endolysin gene lysPPAT from Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteriophage PPAT was cloned and heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli, and the recombinant protein was successfully purified. Bioinformatic analysis revealed that LysPPAT contains a conserved phage lysozyme domain without transmembrane regions or signal peptides, consistent with typical endolysin characteristics. In vitro assays demonstrated that LysPPAT exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against a subset of tested Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens, including clinically resistant strains of P. aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Escherichia coli, and Staphylococcus aureus, even in the absence of outer membrane permeabilizers. The optimal enzymatic activity was observed at 37 °C and pH 8.0. Scanning electron microscopy and peptidoglycan degradation assays confirmed that LysPPAT directly disrupts bacterial cell walls, with degradation activity against P. aeruginosa peptidoglycan comparable to that of lysozyme. Molecular docking revealed stable hydrogen bond interactions between LysPPAT and peptidoglycan, with a docking score of −4.56 kcal·mmol−1. Amphipathic α-helices were predicted to be the structural basis for outer membrane penetration. Additionally, LysPPAT significantly reduced mature P. aeruginosa and S. aureus biofilms biomass. Collectively, LysPPAT represents a novel broad-spectrum endolysin with great potential for combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.

title: Contrasting microbial and environmental associations link water availability to soil multifunctionality in the rhizosheath and bulk soil of Eremopyrum distans
abstract: IntroductionChanges in water availability can alter soil resources and microbial communities, but whether association structures linking water availability to soil multifunctionality (SMF) differ between the root–soil interface and bulk soil remains unclear.MethodsWe subjected Eremopyrum distans to five water treatments over one growing season and assessed dimension-weighted and threshold-based SMF, together with bacterial, fungal and protistan community attributes, in the rhizosheath and bulk soil.ResultsDimension-weighted SMF generally increased across the imposed water-treatment gradient. At higher functional thresholds, W + 25 supported more functions at high levels, particularly in bulk soil. After accounting for water treatment, microhabitat and their interaction, C- and N-related functions were associated mainly with microbial diversity, whereas P-related functions and high-threshold SMF were more closely associated with network complexity and the community-stability proxy. Piecewise structural equation models indicated that, in the rhizosheath, soil moisture was associated with SMF primarily through modeled indirect associations involving integrated microbial diversity, network complexity and the community-stability proxy. In bulk soil, the positive direct association of soil moisture and the negative direct association of soil pH with SMF were more prominent. Formal paired-bootstrap comparisons showed that most corresponding paths did not differ between microhabitats, although selected path differences were detected across SMF thresholds.ConclusionWater availability was associated with SMF through microhabitat-dependent association structures. Microbial community organization was more closely associated with SMF in the rhizosheath, whereas local environmental conditions retained stronger direct associations with SMF in bulk soil. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing rhizosheath and bulk-soil microhabitats when evaluating soil functional responses to changing water availability.

title: Genotypic drug resistance characteristics and their clinical guiding value in people living with HIV
abstract: ObjectiveGenotypic drug resistance testing plays a critical role in guiding antiretroviral therapy (ART) for people living with HIV (PLWH). However, current studies lack a stratified quantitative framework to evaluate its clinical utility, which hinders the precise translation of resistance data into routine practice.MethodsIn this study, 274 PLWH who underwent HIV genotypic drug resistance testing were enrolled to characterize drug resistance profiles, subtype-specific resistance heterogeneity, resistance transmission clusters, and metabolic features, with particular emphasis on grading the clinical utility of genotypic resistance.ResultsThe overall drug resistance rate was 24.09%, predominantly involving non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) and nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs). The three major locally circulating recombinant subtypes showed distinct resistance spectra and active transmission of resistant strains, whereas subtype-specific metabolic variations were confounded by demographic and immunological factors rather than resistance mutations. Notably, graded genotypic resistance guidance values were closely associated with clinical outcomes: stronger guidance values corresponded to better virological suppression and CD4 recovery, whereas weaker guidance values were associated with poorer prognosis.ConclusionsThis stratified evaluation framework improves the interpretation of genotype-phenotype discordance in resistance assessment, helps refine standardized resistance evaluation criteria, supports individualized ART decision-making, and provides real-world evidence for optimizing clinical management strategies and targeted HIV treatment policies.

title: Updated occurrence, habitat associations, and genomic resources of syngnathids in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia
abstract: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. Across 32 dives at seven reef sites, we recorded 54 occurrence records belonging to four species: Hippocampus kuda, H. comes, Doryrhamphus janssi, and Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus. Species differed in their observed habitat associations, while size–depth relationships varied among species. A brooding male and two juvenile seahorses provided evidence of local reproductive activity during the survey period. To establish baseline genomic resources for Malaysian syngnathids, we generated high-quality PacBio HiFi genome assemblies for six individuals from three species, with genome sizes ranging from 0.45–0.61 Gbp and BUSCO completeness scores of 92.3–98.8%. The assemblies were characterized through repeat annotation, protein-coding gene prediction, orthology analysis, and phylogenomics. Complete mitochondrial genomes were generated for all six individuals. These genomic resources provide a foundation for future comparative and population genomic studies of genetic diversity, connectivity, and evolutionary relationships. Together, the ecological observations and genomic resources provide a baseline for future standardized monitoring and conservation research on Malaysian syngnathids.

title: Empirical screening of sesamol, melatonin, and spermidine combinations on growth, biochemical composition, and antioxidant responses of Nitzschia closterium under low-salinity stress
abstract: Low-salinity stress, frequently caused by spring rainfall and estuarine fluctuations, is a major constraint on the large-scale cultivation of marine diatoms and can disrupt their growth, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism. Nitzschia closterium is a marine diatom with high nutritional value and strong potential for producing PUFAs such as EPA and DHA, and it is also widely used as a live feed in aquaculture. However, effective mitigation strategies for low-salinity stress in this species remain limited, and the effects of multiple exogenous regulators remain poorly understood. In this study, an L9(34) orthogonal design was used to evaluate nine combinations of sesamol (SL), melatonin (MT), and spermidine (SPD) on growth, biochemical composition, and antioxidant responses of N. closterium at salinity 5. Responses varied among the tested combinations and endpoints. Among the nine combinations, 30 mg·L−1 SL + 20 mg·L−1 MT + 150 mg·L−1 SPD (A2B2C3) produced favorable results for several measured parameters, including higher total lipid (26.8%) and PUFA (55.28%) relative to the low-salinity control, as well as elevated SOD and CAT activities. The lowest MDA content among the additive treatments was observed under a different combination (A2B1C2). Range analysis indicated that SPD had the strongest influence on growth rate, chlorophyll a, total lipid, EPA, PUFA, soluble sugar, and antioxidant enzyme activities within the tested matrix, whereas SL showed the largest range for MDA reduction and DHA. Because the orthogonal design contained only non-zero levels and did not include additive-free or single-additive treatments, the results are interpreted as an empirical comparison of the nine tested combinations rather than evidence of synergistic or coordinated action. Further dose-range expansion, independent verification, and cultivation-scale assessment are required before practical application can be recommended.

title: Influence of Soluble and Mineral Sources of Cobalt on Methanogenesis and Growth in Methanosarcina barkeri Fusaro and Methanococcus maripaludis S2
abstract:
Mode of methanogenesis and sulphur source affected cobalt (availability and biosynthetic demand in cultures of Methanosarcina barkeri Fusaro and Methanococcus maripaludis S2. Both strains reductively dissolved cobaltoan pyrite, (Co,Fe)S2, as a source of iron, Co and sulphur and assimilated the mobilized Co as cobalamide cofactors. These findings provide insight into factors that influence Co demands in methanogens and show that mineral sources of Co that prevail under sulphidic conditions commonly inhabited by methanogens are bioavailable.

ABSTRACT
Cobalt (Co) is a required component of cofactors and coenzymes in all life and has a pronounced role in the one carbon metabolism of methanogens. However, methanogens often inhabit sulphidic environments where Co precipitates and is incorporated into low solubility mineral phases, such as pyrite (FeS2). Here, we initially examined the influence of Co availability on the growth kinetics of (1) Methanosarcina barkeri with different methanogenesis substrates and (2) Methanococcus maripaludis with different sulphur sources. We then investigated Co acquisition from cobaltoan pyrite [(Co,Fe)S2]. Co demand was highest in M. barkeri grown on methanol/acetate relative to hydrogen/carbon dioxide or methanol only and in M. maripaludis grown with sulphide relative to cysteine or cysteine/thiosulphate. Methanol/acetate‐grown M. barkeri and formate‐grown M. maripaludis grew with (Co,Fe)S2 as well as with soluble sources of Co, Fe and S. Both strains required direct contact to reduce and solubilize Fe and S from (Co,Fe)S2. Further, M. barkeri grown with (Co,Fe)S2 produced an equal amount of cobamides relative to cells provided with soluble Co, Fe, and S. These findings indicate that the availability of methanogenesis substrates and sulphur sources influence Co requirements for methanogens and that these organisms can acquire Co, Fe and S from (Co,Fe)S2.

title: Genomic, spatial, and evolutionary insights into a dominant Mycoplasmatota symbiont colonizing the body wall of deep-sea holothurians
abstract: AbstractSubcuticular bacteria (SCB) are widespread symbionts of echinoderms and often dominate the body-wall microbiome, suggesting their important roles in host physiology. However, their diversity, metabolic properties, and host associations remain poorly characterized. Here, we report a novel dominant SCB lineage associated with deep-sea holothurians, Scotoplanes spp. collected from the Northwest Pacific. We recovered two high-quality genomes, including a 649-kb complete circular genome, and propose a new genus and species, “Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola,” within Mycoplasmatota. The two genomes show a highly reduced metabolic repertoire, lacking central pathways including glycolysis. In contrast, acidic cell-surface-associated proteins, including large proteins exceeding 5000 amino acids, accounted for 27.6% of the complete genome and clustered near defense islands. Localized genome plasticity in these regions, revealed by a comparison between the two closely related genomes, suggests a possible mechanism for the diversification of cell-surface proteins at the host-symbiont interface. “Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola” occupied 76.4%–98.9% of the body-wall microbiome of the Scotoplanes specimens. Fluorescence in situ hybridization analysis confirmed that these bacteria formed aggregates on the epidermal side of the body wall. Overall, this study provides genome- and spatially resolved views of dominant SCB in holothurians and offers evolutionary insights into host-interface diversification in the deep-sea holothurian body wall.

title: RNA sequencing depth guidelines for the study of alternative splicing
abstract: AbstractA key parameter in the experimental design of RNA-seq projects is the choice of sequencing depth. Considering a limited budget, one needs to find a trade-off between the number of samples and the sensitivity of the analysis, particularly concerning lowly expressed genes. While previous studies have proposed a lower bound for the comprehensive analysis of differential gene expression, for the analysis of alternative splicing, it has only been proposed for human adipose tissue. However, alternative splicing differs across tissues and conditions. We analyzed publicly available and newly generated deep-sequenced paired-end RNA-seq samples (between 150 and >500 million reads, read length 50–150 bp) from human buffy coat cells and diverse sets of tissues, including gluteal subcutaneous fat, heart, and hypothalamus. Our results show that the sequencing depth typically used in published cohorts is not sufficient to comprehensively capture the landscape of alternative splicing. This motivates the use of deeper sequencing or long-read technologies in future studies. Toward this goal, we offer guidelines and a website (https://sequencing-depth4splicing.com/) for choosing a suitable sequencing depth.

title: The balance between R-loops and RNAPII occupancy determines the outcome of transcription–replication conflicts
abstract: AbstractMaintaining genome integrity requires the precise coordination of replication and transcription. While R-loops are known to cause transcription–replication conflicts (TRCs), the precise nature of the barrier, whether it is the RNA:DNA hybrid itself, the stalled RNA Polymerase II (RNAPII), or a combination of both, remains elusive. Using live-cell imaging in yeast to monitor a single R-loop prone locus in real time, we demonstrate that wild-type replisomes traverse R-loop enriched transcription units with high efficiency. We find that while R-loops initially repress transcription, replisome passage prompts a robust recovery of transcription activity. Indeed, we discover that R-loops serve a critical regulatory function by suppressing excessive RNAPII occupancy. In an RNAPII mutant with high DNA affinity, the enzymatic removal of R-loops leads to a pile-up of RNAPII molecules, creating a barrier to replication, more severe than the R-loops themselves. Thus, our findings reveal a dual nature of R-loops: while they can be obstacles and repress transcription, they can also serve as a physiological buffer that prevents the formation of high-density RNAPII ‘trains’. These findings establish that the precise regulation of both R-loop levels and RNAPII density is critical for preventing harmful TRCs and maintaining genome stability.

title: Truncated APC regulates alternative splicing by interacting with DDX21 in colorectal cancer
abstract: AbstractTruncating mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene—a key driver of colorectal cancer (CRC) initiation—frequently lead to the production of a truncated APC protein (Trunc-APC). However, its post-transcriptional roles and oncogenic potential remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that Trunc-APC functions as an RNA-binding protein, directly associating with pre-mRNA via its N-terminal 1–169 amino acid region to regulate widespread alternative splicing (AS) in CRC cells. Specifically, Trunc-APC promotes exon inclusion in ARHGEF11, producing an oncogenic isoform that is associated with enhanced Bcl-xL/BAX complex formation and reduced apoptosis. Mechanistically, Trunc-APC interacts with the RNA helicase DDX21 and facilitates SF3B complex recruitment to pre-mRNA, thereby modulating splicing patterns. Notably, treatment with the splicing inhibitor Madrasin significantly reduced tumor burden in ApcMin/+ CRC mice, indicating strong antitumor efficacy. Collectively, these findings establish Trunc-APC as a novel regulator of alternative splicing and a promoter of CRC progression, and highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting the Trunc-APC/DDX21/SF3B axis in CRC.

title: A RARγ–SMARCA5 chromatin-remodeling axis stabilizes AR luminal programs and opposes lineage plasticity in prostate cancer
abstract: AbstractIn prostate cancer (PCa), epigenomic mechanisms drive resistance to androgen receptor (AR) signaling inhibitors, such as enzalutamide (enza). We tested whether retinoic acid receptor gamma (RARγ) shapes the epigenome to direct AR transcription, promote luminal identity, and limit enza resistance. RARγ restoration in enza-resistant 22Rv1 cells induced a large RARγ complex containing its coactivator TACC1 and the chromatin remodeler ISWI ATPase SMARCA5. RARγ restoration expanded and redistributed the AR cistrome toward active promoters, enhancers, and unique super-enhancers and increased the overlap with H3K27ac. RARγ restoration also increased SMARCA5 promoter-proximal binding that overlapped with G2/M-enriched AR cistrome, linking AR redistribution to cell cycle-associated chromatin engagement, including at luminal genes. In 22Rv1 and LNCaP C4-2 (also enza-resistant), RARγ restoration directed the AR transcriptome toward luminal differentiation. A miR-96 antagomir (targeting RARγ) mirrored the impact of RARγ restoration. RARγ antagonized the actions of the master lineage regulator ONECUT2 at the cistrome and transcriptome level and these antagonized genes were significantly associated with alternative lineages in murine PCa models of lineage plasticity and enza responsiveness and lineage plasticity in human PCa cohorts. These findings identify RARγ as a regulator of a chromatin remodeling mechanism that sustains luminal AR programs and opposes therapeutic resistance.

title: Bipartite DNA-binding domain of transcription factor BCL11B binds clustered short DNA sequence motifs
abstract: AbstractB-cell leukemia/lymphoma 11B (BCL11B), despite its name, is a key regulator of T-cell development, lineage specification, and T-cell malignancies. BCL11B contains a bipartite DNA-binding domain composed of two C2H2 zinc finger arrays: low-affinity ZF2-3 and high-affinity ZF4-6. These arrays recognize similar six-nucleotide motifs, TG(n)CC(n), as seven of the eight DNA base-contacting residues are conserved between them. The most conserved interactions involve the central GG dinucleotides, recognized by arginine and lysine residues at the key base-interacting positions of ZF3 and ZF5. We determined eight crystal structures of ZF2-3 bound to 12- or 20-base pair DNA duplexes containing either one or two binding motifs. The structures reveal that ZF2-3 recognizes DNA with remarkable configurational flexibility, binding motifs on either the same or opposite DNA strands with variable spacing in three relative orientations: head-to-tail (or tail-to-head), head-to-head, and tail-to-tail. Analysis of BCL11B ChIP-seq peaks revealed a strong enrichment of 1-bp-spaced, same-orientation TGACC(c/t) motif pairs. We also examined six neurodevelopmental disorder-associated missense variants affecting DNA base-contacting residues. Substitutions that replace bulky, positively charged arginine or lysine with smaller or hydrophobic amino acids weaken DNA-binding affinity and specificity, whereas substitutions between asparagine and lysine alter base recognition preferences.

title: Strand-displacement amplification reduces structure-induced PCR bias and preserves structurally diverse aptamers during SELEX
abstract: AbstractStable secondary structures are important for aptamer folding and target recognition, but they can introduce structure-dependent amplification bias during Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX), with G-quadruplexes (G4s) representing the most demanding case. Here, we introduce strand-displacement SELEX (SD-SELEX), which employs a polymerase with robust 5′→3′ strand-displacement activity to improve the amplification of structured templates. Comparative analyses showed that SD polymerase efficiently amplified hairpin- and G4-forming templates, whereas Taq polymerase exhibited structure-dependent amplification variability. In parallel thrombin SELEX experiments, SD-SELEX achieved 37-fold greater structural preservation and 65-fold higher batch-to-batch reproducibility than Taq-SELEX over 11 rounds. High-throughput sequencing further showed that SD-SELEX maintained G4 motif representation and progressively enriched the known 15-mer thrombin-binding aptamer through round 8, after which it was gradually replaced by newly identified G4 variants, whereas Taq-SELEX progressively depleted these sequences. SD-SELEX also identified novel G4 aptamers with affinities comparable to that of the reference aptamer, whereas representative Taq-SELEX candidates generally showed weaker binding. A parallel selection against VEGF-165 showed the same divergence, with SD-SELEX retaining structurally complex sequences and a previously reported functional motif that were progressively lost under Taq. Thus, SD-SELEX primarily improves aptamer discovery by reducing structure-induced amplification bias and preserving structurally diverse functional candidates, rather than by substantially increasing affinity alone.

title: Gut Bacteriome Modulation in Rhipicephalus microplus Under Biotic Stress From Metarhizium anisopliae and Anaplasma marginale
abstract:
(A) Ticks exposed to Metarhizium anisopliae and Anaplasma marginale showed enriched SCFA‐producing bacteria, restructured microbial networks and greater robustness under combined stress. Co‐exposure increased functional profiles and KEGG orthologl abundance, with A. marginale exerting a dominant influence. (C) In silico removal of the pathogen revealed a persistent ecological imprint on network structure, preventing network reversion and suggestingg that simultaneous biotic stressors affect bacteriome stability.

ABSTRACT
Understanding how multiple biotic stressors shape host‐associated bacteriomes is essential for predicting ecological outcomes. This study examined interactions among the cattle tick Rhipicephalus microplus, the pathogen Anaplasma marginale and the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae. Across treatments involving fungal exposure alone or combined with A. marginale, the gut bacteriome comprised 698 ASVs, of which 28.2% formed a stable core dominated by Bacteroidota and Bacillota. Fungal‐associated stress drove functional shifts, including enrichment of SCFA‐producing taxa such as Akkermansia muciniphila and Lachnospiraceae, indicating reorganization preceding major taxonomic changes. Co‐occurrence networks were restructured under fungal and combined pressures, showing high connectivity, predominance of negative correlations and antagonistic interactions driven by keystone taxa like Prevotella. The combined‐stressor network showed greater robustness, cohesion and communication efficiency than single‐stressor conditions. Functional predictions revealed conserved metabolic profiles, yet co‐exposure increased functional diversity and gene abundance, with A. marginale exerting dominant influence. In silico removal of A. marginale from the co‐exposure condition indicated a persistent ecological imprint, preventing reversion to the basal fungal‐only configuration and retaining structural traces of prior colonization. Overall, simultaneous pathogen–fungus pressures reorganize microbial networks, tightening interactions and enhancing stability, underscoring the dual role of M. anisopliae as a biocontrol agent and potential modulator of bacteriome resilience.

title: Succession of Microbial Communities and Identification of Indigenous PAH‐Tolerant Bacteria Under Multiple PAH Stresses in Mangrove Sediments From Maowei Sea, Guangxi, China
abstract:
Significantly discrepancies in microbial communities across different PAH substrates and enrichment cycles (p 
Significantly discrepancies in microbial communities across different PAH substrates and enrichment cycles (p < 0.01) were observed, with Pseudomonadota (33.2%–99.9%), Bacillota (0%–48.3%), and Actinomycetota (0.1%–33.7%) dominating PAH-tolerant bacteria. Notably, Labrys sp. F3-1, Acinetobacter sp. B1-5, and Sphingomonas sp. N2-15 represent novel acidophilic, mesophilic, and (moderately) halophilic strains that can tolerate phenanthrene, anthracene, and pyrene, respectively, as their sole carbon and energy sources.

ABSTRACT
Elucidating microbial community shifts under polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) stress and screening indigenous PAH-tolerant microbial resources are valuable for exploring potential bioremediation strategies for PAH-contaminated mangrove ecosystems. In this study, surface sediments were collected from mangrove wetlands of the Maowei Sea, Guangxi, China. Three rounds of successive 7-day enrichment cultures were performed with gradually elevated PAH concentrations using phenanthrene, anthracene, and pyrene as target carbon substrates, followed by isolation and taxonomic identification of PAH-adapted bacteria. The results demonstrated that microbial community diversity decreased with increasing enrichment rounds and varied significantly among different PAH substrate treatments. ANOSIM confirmed significant differences in community structure across enrichment cycles and PAH treatments (p < 0.01), consistent with the ordination patterns revealed by Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS). The PAH-adapted microbial communities were predominantly dominated by Pseudomonadota (33.2%–99.9%), Bacillota (0%–48.3%), and Actinomycetota (0.1%–33.7%). In total, 17 indigenous PAH-tolerant bacterial strains belonging to eight genera within the phylum Pseudomonadota were isolated, with representative strains affiliated with Labrys, Sphingomonas, and Acinetobacter. Within the tested physiological gradient ranges, Labrys sp. F3-1 and Acinetobacter sp. B1-5 exhibited optimal growth at pH 5.0, 40°C, and 15‰ salinity, while Sphingomonas sp. N2-15 showed the best growth performance at pH 5.0, 25°C, and 4‰ salinity. Growth assays under PAH pressure further verified that these three isolates could survive and proliferate in PAH-amended selective media under the tested laboratory conditions. This study provides indigenous PAH-tolerant bacterial resources and fundamental community-level insights for future investigations on microbial-based remediation of PAH-polluted mangrove sediments. Notably, the high PAH concentrations applied during laboratory enrichment (100–500 mg/L) were substantially higher than in situ environmental levels; the observed microbial responses and strain physiological traits reflect adaptive characteristics under extreme laboratory selective pressure and should be cautiously extrapolated to natural mangrove ecosystems.

title: LRPPRC deficiency impairs trophoblast function through disrupted phosphatidylinositol metabolism in recurrent pregnancy loss.
abstract: Study questionIs leucine-rich pentatricopeptide repeat-containing protein (LRPPRC) involved in the development of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and, if so, what is the potential mechanism?Summary answerLRPPRC deficiency impairs trophoblast viability and promotes apoptosis and oxidative stress through disruption of phosphatidylinositol (PI) metabolism, and low preconception serum PI (18:1/18:1) levels are associated with subsequent miscarriage in women with RPL.What is known alreadyRPL is commonly associated with impaired trophoblast function. LRPPRC works as a multifunctional protein that regulates a myriad of biological processes, including energy metabolism.Study design, size, durationThe investigation included re-analysis of a public transcriptomic dataset, functional experiments in trophoblast cell models, lipidomic profiling of first-trimester human villous tissues obtained from 11 clinically healthy pregnant women and 11 patients with RPL, and analysis of preconception serum lipids in a cohort of 63 women with a history of RPL, who were prospectively followed for subsequent pregnancy outcomes resulting in 32 normal deliveries and 31 cases of early pregnancy loss.Participants/materials, setting, methodsBioinformatics screening of the public transcriptomic dataset GSE76862 was first conducted to identify candidate genes dysregulated in RPL villous tissues. Following the identification of LRPPRC, its functional role was investigated through siRNA-mediated knockdown in the human trophoblast cells, specifically assessing the resultant effects on cell viability, apoptosis, and oxidative stress levels. To elucidate the downstream molecular pathways, transcriptomic analysis of the LRPPRC-depleted cells was performed. Subsequent Gene Ontology analyses revealed a significant enrichment of candidate differentially expressed genes that are involved in the phospholipid biosynthetic process. In parallel, comprehensive lipidomic profiling of human villous tissue samples from both RPL patients and matched controls was carried out using mass spectrometry to validate bioinformatic predictions at the metabolite level. To explore translational potential, the preconception serum levels of lipids, including PI species, were measured in a cohort of women with a history of RPL and statistically correlated with their subsequent pregnancy outcomes. Finally, direct functional rescue experiments were executed by exogenously supplementing PI (18:1/18:1) to the culture medium of LRPPRC-deficient trophoblast cells to determine if this intervention could reverse the observed phenotypic impairments.Main results and the role of chanceLRPPRC was downregulated in RPL villous tissues. Functional validation in trophoblast cells demonstrated that knockdown of LRPPRC suppressed viability and increased apoptosis/oxidative stress. Transcriptomics and lipidomics converged on the phospholipid biosynthetic pathway as a key downstream process. Total lipids and specific phospholipids were decreased in RPL villous tissues. Low preconception serum PI (18:1/18:1) levels predicted subsequent miscarriage in the RPL cohort. Exogenous PI (18:1/18:1) supplementation reversed the cellular defects caused by LRPPRC deficiency.Large scale dataThis study analyzed the publicly available transcriptomic dataset GSE76862 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repository.Limitations and reasons for cautionThe analysis of preconception serum lipids was performed in a cohort of 63 women with a history of RPL. This sample size remains relatively limited, primarily due to the current availability of patients with documented follow-up pregnancy outcomes.Wider implications of the findingsOur results reveal a pivotal role for PI in the pathogenesis of RPL and highlight its potential as a mechanistic biomarker and therapeutic target.FundingThis study was supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (82171657 and 81971384) and Shanghai First Maternity and Infant Hospital Basic Research Special Fund (2025A08).DisclosuresThe authors have declared no conflict of interest.Trial registration numberN/A.
authors: Wang C, Yang H, Li M, Li W, Wu X, Jin L, Xu XH.

title: Increased replication-associated single-stranded DNA promotes formaldehyde-induced mutagenesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
abstract: Formaldehyde (FA) is an environmentally abundant and endogenously produced aldehyde that has been shown to cause DNA damage, mutagenesis, and carcinogenesis. Several studies have demonstrated that FA induces guanine mutations resulting in a mutation signature like SBS40. In this work, we use Saccharomyces cerevisiae to demonstrate that replication defects generating single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) caused by the downregulation of the major replicative polymerases results in elevated FA mutagenesis. We found that loss of Mrc1 (CLASPIN) resulted in a high accumulation of ssDNA and FA mutagenesis, and that these phenotypes were not dependent on Mrc1's checkpoint activity. Loss of DNA-protein crosslink repair results in elevated FA sensitivity with no alteration to mutagenesis, likely due to the inability of the fork to bypass unprocessed protein adducts. Finally, we show that FA-induced mutagenesis is dependent on Pol ζ-mediated translesion synthesis, while deficiencies in the template switching pathway do not alter error-free bypass of FA adducts. Overall, our work points toward replication-associated ssDNA as a major substrate for FA-induced damage and elucidates the pathways that function to prevent FA mutagenesis at replication forks.
authors: Blouin T, McGuinness C, Marshall K, Bazzle C, Saini N.

title: Contrasting time- and concentration-dependent cellular and photosynthetic responses of the freshwater alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii to inorganic mercury and methylmercury.
abstract: Mercury (Hg) is a global pollutant threatening ecosystems, mainly via methylmercury (MeHg) biomagnification in food webs. Microalgae are the primary entry point, yet the toxicity of its different forms in them is still understudied. This study compared, for the first time, the time-dependent effects (3-96 hr) of inorganic Hg (IHg) and MeHg at concentrations of 10-5-10-8 g/L on the green microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. Flow cytometry and chlorophyll fluorescence revealed contrasting physiological and photosynthetic responses. Inorganic Hg was more toxic at 3 hr than MeHg, reducing growth, photosynthetic efficiency, and chlorophyll autofluorescence, and increasing mortality. Effects of IHg decreased over time, with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mortality below control by 96 hr. In contrast, MeHg at 10-5 g/L caused sustained growth inhibition, elevated ROS, increased chlorophyll autofluorescence, and cell death beyond 24 hr. Differences in energy dissipation and photosystem II recovery further indicated distinct toxicity targets. At lower concentrations, both forms triggered time- and concentration-dependent responses, including transient growth inhibition, stimulation, and ROS changes, likely reflecting hormesis and metabolic trade-offs. These responses may affect growth, photosynthesis, and ROS processes. They highlight the need for time-resolved assessments to capture adaptation-toxicity thresholds. This study strengthens the understanding of Hg toxicity in primary producers and its ecotoxicological risks.
authors: Cosio C, Rioult D, Barjhoux I, Gaveau N.

title: A novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification method for screening detection of genetically modified cotton.
abstract: BackgroundLimited domestic cotton production in Japan has led to large amounts of cottonseed being imported for food and feed. Consequently, genetically modified (GM) cotton seeds have been introduced into the country, and a qualitative method is required for the detection of unauthorized GM cotton.ObjectiveThe aim of this study is to develop a testing method that is simpler, more rapid, and more cost-effective than the conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) technique.MethodsA novel method was developed for the screening detection of unauthorized GM cotton seeds using loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) to target the 35S promoter of the cauliflower mosaic virus (P35S), neomycin phosphotransferase II (NPTII), and the endogenous cotton gene stearoyl acyl carrier protein desaturase (sad1).ResultsThe method LOD was determined to be ≤0.1%, which is equivalent to the corresponding LOD achieved using the conventional PCR method. A simpler detection method based on single-stranded tag hybridization on a chromatographic printed-array strip system (denoted as DNA chromatography) was also developed. This method allowed visual detection of the amplification of multiple DNA samples at the LOD level.ConclusionCompared with the conventional PCR approach, the developed detection method is cost-effective, rapid, and simple.HighlightsThe method facilitates the analysis of GM crops and will be expected to help prevent the unintended spread of GM crops into the environment.
authors: Matsumoto M, Onishi M, Minegishi Y, Takabatake R.

title: Investigating interspecies correlation estimation models to predict chronic toxicity of insecticides and fungicides to honey bee larvae using nonbiting midge data.
abstract: Interspecies correlation estimations (ICEs) are typically limited to predicting acute toxicity values between species that live in the same habitat. In this article, we investigate the relationship between an aquatic insect and a terrestrial insect with respect to their chronic sensitivity to insecticides and fungicides. Chronic toxicity values-namely, no observed effect concentration (µg active substance/L) for the nonbiting midge Chironomus riparius and no observed effect dose (µg active substance/larva) for the honey bee Apis mellifera-were obtained from various databases, regulatory documents, and the open literature. Most of the data originated from regulatory studies. The derived correlation equations for the two insect species are based on bound endpoints from a total of 52 substances (25 insecticides, 27 fungicides; unbound endpoints could not be used). By applying the statistical criteria for identifying robust ICE models, two models were identified-one for insecticides and one for insecticides and fungicides combined-while fungicides alone did not fulfill the criteria. The obtained models can be used to predict honey bee larval chronic toxicity (no observed effect dose) from nonbiting midge chronic toxicity data (no observed effect concentration) and vice versa. The developed ICE models are unique for two reasons: they predict across different habitats (i.e., aquatic and terrestrial), and they are applicable for chronic toxicity. The models can provide toxicity estimations without experimental testing, which is especially helpful in the case of honey bees, which cannot be tested year-round.
authors: Weltje L, Savaliya D.

title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Identify NFKBIE as a Candidate Gene Associated with IS-II Neutrophil Differentiation in Lung Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: ObjectivePeople undergoing lung transplantation may develop lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), in which neutrophils contribute to the inflammatory response. However, the molecular features associated with distinct neutrophil states remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate molecular features associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil state, with particular attention to NFKBIE, an NF-κB inhibitor.MethodsWe integrated bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Candidate genes were identified using co-expression analysis and machine-learning methods. We further examined cell-cell communication and the association of NFKBIE with neutrophil states using pseudotime analysis and computational gene perturbation. We validated NFKBIE expression in a mouse model of LIRI using RT-qPCR and Western blotting and assessed lung injury by histological examination.ResultsA total of 553 differentially expressed genes and a key disease-associated module containing 4,456 genes were identified, with predominant enrichment in inflammation- and immunity-related pathways (eg, TNF and NF-κB). Five overlapping candidate transcriptomic markers, CXCL3, CYLD, NFKBIE, SLC30A1, and KBTBD8, were identified. The five-gene model showed strong discrimination in the discovery cohort (AUC = 0.986) and also showed strong discrimination in the separate GSE127003 validation dataset (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.996-1.000). Single-cell analysis showed that neutrophils were the largest annotated cell population in both CIT and post-reperfusion samples, whereas the IS-II neutrophil subtype was markedly enriched after reperfusion; NFKBIE was most highly expressed in IS-II neutrophils. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further indicated that elevated NFKBIE expression was associated with a later differentiation state toward the IS-II phenotype, while computational NFKBIE perturbation predicted alterations in several perturbation-associated genes. In vivo validation confirmed that both NFKBIE mRNA and protein levels were upregulated in lung tissue after reperfusion.ConclusionThe five-gene transcriptomic model showed reproducible discriminatory performance in a separate validation dataset. NFKBIE was consistently associated with the IS-II neutrophil state across multiple computational analyses, while in vivo experiments confirmed its increased expression after reperfusion. These findings nominate NFKBIE as a candidate gene associated with IS-II neutrophil differentiation and provide a hypothesis-generating basis for further functional investigation.
authors: Huang XT, Zhou M, Fu Y, Zhang N, Jin Y, Jiang X, Gao J, Zhang Z, Li Y, Wen ZM.

title: Chicken invariant chain-Vti1b association and changes in autophagy-related proteins.
abstract: Antigen processing and presentation are key steps by which the host recognizes pathogens and initiates adaptive immune responses. This process relies not only on MHC molecules and associated chaperones but also on the coordinated activity of endosomal trafficking, membrane fusion, and autophagy-related processes. In this study, we focused on chicken invariant chain (chIi) and chicken Vti1b (chVti1b) to examine their association and changes in autophagy-related protein levels. Confocal microscopy was used to examine the subcellular localization of chVti1b in HD11 cells and its colocalization with chIi. Co-IP and pull-down assays were used to assess chIi-associated proteins and the contribution of the CLIP region, while LC-MS/MS and AlphaFold3/HDOCK analyses were used to identify and prioritize candidate associations. Western blot was used to detect autophagy-related markers and chicken Tax1-binding protein 1 (chTAX1BP1) protein expression, and RT-qPCR was used to analyze the transcript levels of selected immune-related genes. The results showed that chVti1b was mainly localized to late endosomes and showed marked colocalization with chIi in HD11 cells. This colocalization was associated with the formation of larger chIi/chVti1b-positive vesicular structures. Reciprocal co-IP supported an interaction between overexpressed chIi and chVti1b in human 293T cells, and CLIP deletion resulted in undetectable co-IP signals in this system. In rapamycin-treated HD11 cells, co-expression of chVti1b and chIi was associated with a 58% decrease in p62, a 34% increase in LC3-II, and a 121% increase in chTAX1BP1 protein levels relative to the empty-vector control. ChVti1b knockdown reduced the transcript levels of BF2, BLB, IFN-γ, and chIi, whereas chVti1b overexpression increased the transcript levels of BLB, IFN-γ, and chIi but had no significant effect on BF2. Together, these findings support an interaction between chIi and chVti1b and show that their co-expression is associated with changes in autophagy-related protein levels in rapamycin-treated HD11 cells.
authors: Liu C, Shen Y, Zhang X, Wang H, Li J, Liu H, Chen F.

title: Integrated multi-tissue transcriptomic and network analyses reveal systemic crosstalk governing the onset of lay in Wuhua Yellow chickens.
abstract: The onset of lay in poultry is a systemic transition requiring tight neuroendocrine-metabolic coordination. Although indigenous breeds retain valuable genetic diversity and resilience, their multi-tissue regulatory architecture remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomes across four key tissues (hypothalamus, pituitary, ovary, and liver) in Wuhua Yellow chickens at pre-laying (16 weeks) and peak-laying (32 weeks) stages, combining weighted gene co-expression network analysis, ligand-receptor inference, and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) validation. Results support a coordinated HPO-liver expression program rather than isolated organ responses. Systemic prolactin (PRL) induction was coupled with hepatic PRLR upregulation (log2FC = 4.23), coinciding with massive hepatic induction of yolk precursors: VTG1 (log2FC = 18.28), VTG2 (log2FC = 6.60), and APOB (log2FC = 3.31). Reciprocal downregulation of pituitary lipoprotein receptors (VLDLR and LRP2) suggested a possible feedback-related route consistent with peripheral metabolic status. WGCNA identified tissue-specific hub genes associated with a functional division of labor across the axis, including hypothalamic (ADGRL3, NRXN1), pituitary (EYA1), ovarian (MAD2L1, PLK1), and hepatic (HGFAC, PAH) modules. Significant negative inter-module correlations between liver and central/gonadal tissues (r = -0.48 to -0.68, P < 0.05) highlighted a systemic trade-off reallocating resources toward yolk synthesis. Targeted qPCR confirmed strong stage-dependent changes in core signaling and yolk-precursor genes (PRL, VTG1, VTG2, APOB, and SPP1) and a significant peak-lay decrease in hepatic PAH, whereas other representative hubs (NRXN1, EYA1, and PLK1) tracked RNA-seq trends. Overall, this multi-tissue framework provides a transcriptomic-based framework for understanding stage-dependent transcriptional coordination of reproductive activation in an indigenous chicken and nominates expression-level candidate genes for further genetic and functional validation toward improving egg production while preserving native genetic diversity.
authors: Xu YJ, Wang YX, Weng ZX, Zou YN, Li WN, Chen JB, Du BW, Huang XH.

title: Identification of Candida spp. in denture wearers by two amplicon-based molecular typing techniques.
abstract: ObjectiveAlthough molecular methods such as quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction with High-Resolution Melting Curve (qPCR-HRMC) analysis and Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) enable accurate identification of Candida spp., their application to denture samples remains limited. This study applied qPCR-HRMC and PCR-RFLP to identify Candida species in denture wearers with and without denture stomatitis.DesignBiofilm samples from denture wearers with and without denture stomatitis (n = 40) were collected using swabs and ultrasound, followed by DNA extraction and qPCR-HRMC for direct Candida identification. All samples were cultured on CHROMagar Candida for presumptive identification. When direct identification was not possible, cultured isolates were subjected to qPCR-HRMC. For PCR-RFLP, purified amplicons were digested with a restriction enzyme, and electrophoretic banding patterns were compared with reference strains. Cohen's kappa coefficient (κ) evaluated the agreement between qPCR-HRMC and CHROMagar Candida.ResultsqPCR-HRMC successfully identified Candida albicans and Candida tropicalis directly from denture biofilms colonized by a single species. In contrast, identification of Nakaseomyces glabratus, Candida dubliniensis, and mixed-species colonization required prior cultivation. Substantial agreement was observed between CHROMagar™ Candida and qPCR-HRMC (κ = 0.826), with 100% sensitivity for C. albicans and high specificity for N. glabratus (97%) and C. tropicalis (100%). PCR-RFLP showed limited discriminatory capacity.ConclusionsqPCR-HRMC proved effective for the direct detection of C. albicans and C. tropicalis in denture biofilms, whereas identification of other species and mixed-species colonization required prior cultivation. PCR-RFLP was not suitable for Candida identification in these samples.
authors: Vega-Chacón Y, Savadkouhi AG, Bonani A, Mima EGO.

title: Genetic dissection of soybean cyst nematode HG type 2.5.7 resistance reveals a multilocus architecture and favorable alleles from both parents.
abstract: Soybean cyst nematode (SCN; Heterodera glycines) is a major pathogen affecting soybean production worldwide. Understanding the genetic architecture of SCN resistance can facilitate the identification and utilization of favorable resistance alleles. We investigated resistance to SCN HG type 2.5.7 using an F₂ population (n = 184) and a recombinant inbred line (RIL; F₂:₇, n = 323) population derived from Longken336 × Kangxian12, together with seven additional F2 populations. The eight F₂ populations exhibited broad transgressive phenotypic segregation, including progeny with female index (FI) values extending beyond the corresponding parental range. QTL analysis identified six FI-associated loci in the Longken336 × Kangxian12 F₂ population on chromosomes 6, 7, 8, 11, 17, and 18, explaining 4.9-17.0% of the phenotypic variance, with one exceeding the permutation-derived significance threshold. High-density mapping in the RIL population identified resistance-associated loci across 17 chromosomes, with individual loci explaining 2.8-33.5% of the phenotypic variance. Seven QTL were consistently detected across both RIL evaluations, including four that exceeded the corresponding permutation-derived significance thresholds in both RIL evaluations. QTL regions colocalizing with the known resistance loci Rhg1 and Rhg4 were detected, along with favorable alleles contributed by both parental, including the phenotypically susceptible Longken336. Transcriptomic profiling identified contrasting infection-responsive expression patterns in both parental genotypes and prioritized candidate genes within selected QTL regions. These results highlight differences in QTL detection between the F2 and RIL populations and support a multilocus basis for resistance to SCN HG type 2.5.7, with favorable alleles contributed by both parental backgrounds.Supplementary informationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s11032-026-01735-9.
journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
authors: Huang M, Jiang Y, Chang D, Guo L, Zhou C, Wang M, Tian Z, Li C, Wang C.

title: Systematic analysis reveals an Mln1-dependent trade-off between metabolic flexibility and thermotolerance in  Cryptococcus neoformans
abstract: During infection, fungal pathogens must adapt to multiple environmental challenges, including changes in temperature, nutrient availability, and immune stress. Although transcriptional regulators are central to these adaptations, how individual regulators contribute to distinct environmental responses and how these responses are functionally interconnected remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the functions of infection-associated transcription factors under distinct host-relevant conditions in  Cryptococcus neoformans . Integrating in vivo expression profiling with infectivity data from signature-tagged mutagenesis, we prioritized 24 transcription factors, 12 of which were induced under host-mimicking conditions. Initial functional analyses revealed distinct roles for these transcription factors in adaptation to temperature, carbon, and nitrogen availability. Further characterization of Mln1, a fungal basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, uncovered an unexpected connection between carbon source adaptation and thermotolerance. Mig1-dependent repression limited  MLN1 expression in the presence of glucose, whereas Mln1 accumulated in the nucleus in the presence of trehalose or ethanol, but not glucose. Loss of  MLN1 impaired carbon-starvation gene expression and growth on non-preferred carbon sources, particularly trehalose. Conversely,  mln1 Δ cells accumulated more intracellular trehalose and exhibited enhanced thermotolerance, yet showed reduced melanization, titan cell formation, virulence in  Drosophila , and brain fungal burden in mice. Together, these results suggest that Mln1 contributes to metabolic flexibility and fungal virulence while differentially influencing thermotolerance. More broadly, these findings highlight a potential physiological trade-off between nutrient utilization and stress resistance, suggesting that these adaptive processes may be interconnected in fungal pathogens.
authors: Yu S, Lee M, Yang S, Cha H, Won D, Kim D, Choi J, Yu S, Seo R, Lee K, Lee J, Lee W, Lee D, Bahn Y.

title: Expression of tardigrade intrinsically disordered proteins in  C. elegans  reveals variable effects on aging and stress
abstract: Tardigrades survive extreme environmental stress by expressing intrinsically disordered proteins that stabilize cellular structures during cryptobiosis. Because these proteins protect cells from desiccation, oxidative stress, and DNA damage, they have attracted interest as potential therapeutics to enhance stress resilience in other organisms. However, most studies have relied on cultured cells or germline expression, leaving their effects in somatic tissues largely unexplored. Here, we generated  Caenorhabditis elegans strains expressing four tardigrade intrinsically disordered proteins, Damage Suppressor (DSUP), cytoplasmic-abundant heat-soluble (CAHS), mitochondrial-abundant heat-soluble (MAHS), and Ramazzottius varieornatus late embryogenesis abundant (RvLEAM), throughout somatic tissues. Surprisingly, constitutive expression of each protein reduced lifespan, impaired motility and reproduction, and failed to improve resistance to most environmental stressors. DSUP toxicity was tissue- and developmental stage-dependent, indicating that both spatial and temporal expression influence its physiological effects. Despite these detrimental phenotypes, several proteins reduced protein aggregation during desiccation-associated stress, demonstrating context-dependent protective effects. Together, our findings reveal that tardigrade stress proteins impose physiological tradeoffs in vivo and underscore the importance of evaluating candidate stress-protective proteins in physiologically relevant somatic models before therapeutic translation.  Summary Statement  Constitutive somatic expression of tardigrade stress proteins impairs aging and stress resilience while providing context-dependent protection during desiccation in  C. elegans .

title: Integrated Multiomic Analysis Reveals an EBV-Associated MIF-SPP1<sup>+</sup> Macrophage Axis Linking Tumor Stemness and Immune Dysfunction in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.
abstract: Elucidating how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) shapes tumor-immune interactions is important for improving therapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This multi-cohort analysis integrates single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data with multiplex immunofluorescence and functional assays. Single-cell profiling identifies stemness-associated epithelial states and enrichment of SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in EBV+ NPC. SPP1+ TAM abundance is associated with stemness-associated epithelial features and dysfunctional T-cell states, while high MIF and SPP1+ macrophage signatures are associated with shorter progression-free survival. Within the EBV+ spatial cohort, SPP1+ TAMs co-occur with stemness-associated tumor cells, exhausted CD8+ T cells, and regulatory T cells in Niche 5, which is more frequent in non-response tumors following chemoimmunotherapy. Functional experiments show increased MIF expression and secretion by EBV+ epithelial cells. MIF inhibition attenuates conditioned-medium-induced monocyte migration and SPP1-associated TAM-like programming, whereas recombinant MIF reproduces these effects. Conversely, macrophage-derived SPP1 increases stemness-associated marker expression and tumorsphere formation in EBV+ epithelial and tumor models. It also impairs primary CD8+ T-cell proliferation, effector function, and cytotoxic activity while increasing exhaustion-associated markers; CD44 blockade partially reverses these effects. Collectively, these findings support an EBV-associated MIF-SPP1 macrophage-tumor/T-cell crosstalk model linking stemness-associated epithelial phenotypes with immune dysfunction and adverse clinical outcomes.

title: Integrated analysis of mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA expression profiles and regulatory relationships during longissimus dorsi muscle development in Lufeng cattle.
abstract: Lufeng cattle (Bos taurus) are an indigenous breed of southern China with strong environmental adaptability but limited meat production performance. To characterize postnatal skeletal muscle development, longissimus dorsi samples were collected at 3 days, 4 months, and 24 months of age for integrated mRNA, lncRNA, and circRNA sequencing. Nine libraries generated 545,665,884 clean reads, identifying 21,483 mRNAs, 1688 lncRNAs, and 18,147 circRNAs. Across pairwise comparisons, 1568 non-redundant differentially expressed mRNAs, 107 lncRNAs, and 305 circRNAs were detected. Functional analyses highlighted protein translation, extracellular matrix organization, muscle contraction, chromatin organization, cell cycle, and energy metabolism. Integrated co-expression and protein interaction analyses prioritized candidate molecules including INHA, IGF2, and TMEM52. RT-qPCR confirmed expression trends broadly consistent with RNA-seq. These results provide a transcriptomic resource and candidate molecules for further investigation of skeletal muscle development in Lufeng cattle.
authors: Niu Q, Feng G, Yang X, Luo Y, Yang S, Deng M, Sun B, Guo Y, Liu G, Liu D, Li Y.
