title: Dendrobium officinale extract ameliorates Alzheimer's disease by modulating PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes: An integrated study combining feature-based molecular networking, network pharmacology and multi-omics.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder with limited effective treatments. Dendrobium officinale Kimura & Migo (D. officinale) has been traditionally used for dementia, but its active constituents and mechanisms remain unclear.Aim of the studyThis study aimed to systematically characterize the chemical constituents of D. officinale extract (DOE) and elucidate its anti-AD mechanisms using an integrated pharmacological strategy.Materials and methodsThe chemical composition of DOE was analyzed using UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN). Target prediction and pathway analysis were performed using a network pharmacology approach. Therapeutic effects were evaluated in 5×FAD mice using behavioral and histopathological assays. Mechanistic validation was further conducted using transcriptomics, proteomics, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and molecular docking.ResultsSixty-five components were identified, with apigenin, naringenin, rutin and oxyresveratrol as major identified constituents. Integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology analyses highlighted the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes as potential mechanisms underlying the anti-AD effects of DOE. In 5×FAD mice, DOE markedly improved cognitive deficits, alleviated hippocampal neuronal injury, reduced Aβ plaque deposition, and suppressed astrocytic and microglial activation. Mechanistically, DOE significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of Pi3k, Akt, and Mtor, reduced AKT and mTOR phosphorylation, and showed a trend toward decreased PI3K phosphorylation. DOE also reduced p62 accumulation and increased the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, suggesting an improvement in autophagy-related processes. Molecular docking further demonstrated favorable binding affinities of major identified constituents toward key targets, particularly AKT1 and PIK3CA.ConclusionDOE ameliorates AD-related pathological changes, potentially through modulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and improvement of autophagy-related processes. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting the potential of D. officinale as a multi-target therapeutic candidate for AD.
authors: Fu J, Liang Z, Wang F, Xiong F, Wang X, Sun J, Zhan J, Hu K, Gao H.

title: CRYAB as a key mediator of Xianlian Jiedu Decoction-induced suppression of colorectal cancer stemness.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceXianlian Jiedu Decoction (XLJDD) has long been used clinically in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). Our preliminary work indicated that XLJDD exerts anti-CRC activity by attenuating inflammation, restoring gut microbiota balance, and modulating signaling pathways such as CXCR2/PI3K/AKT. However, the bioactive constituents and the precise molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly defined. The present study sought to clarify the active components and mechanisms of XLJDD in CRC, thereby providing a scientific basis for its further therapeutic application.Aim of the studyThis study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of XLJDD on tumor stemness in CRC and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.Materials and methodsAn orthotopic CRC mouse model was established and treated with XLJDD for 21 days. The chemical constituents of XLJDD were characterized by UPLC-MS/MS, and treatment-related metabolic alterations were profiled by plasma metabolomics. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to identify differentially expressed genes, which were validated by Western blot and immunohistochemistry. In vitro, HCT116 and HT29 cells were evaluated for proliferation, sphere-forming capacity, stemness-marker (CD44/CD133) populations by flow cytometry, and protein expression by Western blot. CRYAB-knockdown cell lines were generated to assess proliferation (CCK-8), apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, and stemness-marker expression. Transcriptome sequencing combined with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) was performed across treatment groups (NC, NC + XLJDD, CRYAB-KD, CRYAB-KD + XLJDD) to define the downstream signaling pathways regulated by XLJDD.ResultsXLJDD significantly suppressed tumor growth in the orthotopic CRC model. Plasma metabolomics revealed clear separation between groups, with reduced phenylalanine and glycerophospholipid metabolism and enhanced energy metabolism in XLJDD-treated mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumors identified cancer-cell clusters with high CRYAB and ALDH3A1 expression that were markedly suppressed following XLJDD treatment. In vitro, XLJDD reduced proliferation, sphere formation, CD44+/CD133+ populations, and stemness-marker expression. CRYAB knockdown impaired proliferation, induced apoptosis and G1-phase arrest, and attenuated stem-like features in CRC cells. Transcriptomic profiling with IPA identified STC1 as a downstream target of CRYAB, with the CRYAB-STC1 axis closely linked to the core stemness transcription factors OCT4, SOX2, and NANOG.DiscussionThese findings indicate that XLJDD constrains CRC stemness through a CRYAB-driven regulatory program rather than a single isolated target. By coupling CRYAB to STC1 and the OCT4/SOX2/NANOG network, the study connects XLJDD's anti-tumor activity to a defined stemness axis and positions CRYAB as a tractable node within it. Because CRYAB knockdown both reproduced and reinforced the anti-stemness effect of XLJDD, the data suggest that XLJDD acts, at least in part, by downregulating CRYAB, offering a mechanistic rationale that extends beyond its previously reported anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects.ConclusionThis study demonstrates for the first time that XLJDD suppresses CRC tumor stemness by targeting the CRYAB-STC1 axis. By integrating metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation, this work provides new evidence that XLJDD regulates cancer stemness and offers experimental support for its therapeutic potential in CRC.
authors: Chen H, Fan Y, Xu C, Yan Q, Shen W, Cheng H, Lai Y, Sun D.

title: The impact of PROgnostic SIgnatures in stage II colon cancer patients enrolled in the phase III clinical trial TOSCA: the PROSIT study.
abstract: BackgroundAdjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) indication in stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) remains challenging, as clinical, pathological, and ctDNA inadequately predict benefit. Immune infiltration correlates with outcome, yet transcriptional signatures have not been systematically evaluated in prospective trial cohorts. We aimed to identify a prognostic transcriptional signature in high-risk stage II CRC patients treated with ACT within the TOSCA trial.MethodsFrom the TOSCA trial, 124 high-risk stage II patients were selected using a matched case-control design, with matching based on center, pT stage, ACT regimen, and treatment duration. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on FFPE samples. MSI status was inferred bioinformatically. Prognostic associations were assessed using log-rank tests and multivariable Cox models adjusting for MSI status and tumor sidedness.ResultsSeventy-two samples met RNA quality criteria. Median follow-up was 70.9 months; 40% were right-sided, 60% received FOLFOX, 54% 3-month ACT, and 19% were MSI-high. Transcriptomic analyses highlighted immune-regulatory and TGF-β/stromal programs associated with outcome. A biologically defined Immune Exclusion (IE) phenotype, characterized by low ICR and high Hallmark TGF-β signaling, was observed in approximately 28% of patients and was associated with shorter DFS (HR=2.22, p = 0.036). This association persisted after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness (HR=2.47, p = 0.018). A reduced seven-gene IE signature (rIE) was subsequently derived and was also associated with shorter DFS after multivariable adjustment (HR=2.83, p = 0.012).ConclusionThe IE phenotype and its reduced rIE signature were associated with shorter DFS in high-risk stage II colon cancer and represent exploratory candidate prognostic biomarkers requiring validation in independent cohorts.Statement of translational relevanceIdentifying stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) patients who will relapse despite standard adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) remains an unmet clinical need. Current clinicopathological and ctDNA-based approaches do not fully resolve risk stratification in this setting. In this study, whole-transcriptome profiling of high-risk stage II CRC from the prospective TOSCA trial identified an Immune Exclusion (IE) signature associated with significantly shorter disease-free survival, which remained associated with DFS after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness. These findings provide a biological framework for further validation in independent cohorts and for future hypothesis-generating studies aimed at refining risk stratification and exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.
authors: Puccini A, Ferrando L, Frige G, Rulli E, Nano E, Bergamo F, Pastorino A, Martelli V, Pessino A, Garuti A, Bedognetti D, Ballestrero A, Labianca R, Maiello E, La Verde N, Bernardini I, Corsi DC, Zaniboni A, Aprile G, Pietrantonio F, Torri V, Fassan M, Lonardi S, Zoppoli G, Mazzarella L, Sobrero AF, TOSCA (Three or Six Colon Adjuvant) investigators.

title: Behavioural and contextual correlates of reported or committed uptake of Dry Flood-Proofing and Flood Barriers: Evidence from two distinct cross-sectional cohorts surveyed around the 2022 Eastern Australian floods.
abstract: Riverine floods generate residential losses in Australia, yet many flood-prone households do not implement property-level mitigation measures. This study examines behavioural and contextual covariates associated with reported or committed uptake of Dry Flood-Proofing and Flood Barriers. Data came from cross-sectional cohorts surveyed before (n = 311) and after (n = 97) the early-2022 eastern Australian floods, collectively covering four states. Reported or committed uptake combined self-reported implementation with stated near-term commitment. Protection Motivation Theory guided behavioural variable organisation; pre-2022 coding and scaling rules were applied unchanged to the post-2022 cohort. Logistic models used 396 complete cases (311 pre-2022 and 85 post-2022), with inference clustered across 58 postcode-based area groups. Because both cohorts contributed to pooled estimation, wave-stratified diagnostics were apparent rather than external validation. Self-efficacy and response efficacy were consistently associated with both outcomes. Perceived implementation capability was prominent among the Dry Flood-Proofing point estimates, and perceived measure effectiveness among the Flood Barriers point estimates. Flood-risk communication was positively associated with both outcomes. Threat-appraisal point estimates differed by measure and survey context, whereas prior-flood-experience interactions were imprecise. The small post-2022 modelling sample and wave-specific estimation instability limited inference. In exploratory bounded-shift analyses, hypothetical 0.20 increases in perceived implementation capability for Dry Flood-Proofing and perceived measure effectiveness for Flood Barriers corresponded to mean model-implied probability differences of 0.083 and 0.078. These non-causal contrasts do not demonstrate intervention responsiveness or targeting efficiency. The findings support measure-specific analysis and identify practical information, implementation capability, and perceived effectiveness as candidates for prospective programme evaluation.
authors: Fouladi Semnan A, Maqsood T.

title: Multi-omic profiling reveals coordinated remodeling of inflammatory glial states and oligodendrocyte-myelin homeostasis by BoNT/A in CCI-induced neuropathic pain.
abstract: This study investigated inflammation-associated microglial states, cross-glial inflammatory signaling and spinal myelin abnormalities after CCI, and evaluated their response to BoNT/A administered after pain hypersensitivity had developed. Male rats underwent CCI and received intrathecal BoNT/A on D7. Behavioral phenotyping was integrated with spinal transcriptomics, proteomics, scRNA-seq, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, TEM, conditioned-medium transfer, TNF-α challenge, and in vitro and in vivo IL-1β add-back. CCI produced persistent mechanical, thermal, and cold hypersensitivity together with shifts in inflammation-associated microglial states and transcriptional programs, increased spinal NF-κB/NLRP3-caspase-1-IL-1β-related proteins, an enhanced C3-associated astrocytic response, and abnormalities in OLIG/OPC states and myelin structure. BoNT/A attenuated inflammatory readouts, was associated with higher OLIG2 and MBP signals, and reduced the apparent severity of myelin ultrastructural abnormalities. Single-cell analyses described cell-state patterns, while CellChat prioritized candidate microglia-astrocyte interactions. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated microglia increased astrocytic C3, whereas BoNT/A pretreatment reduced this effect; IL-1β add-back increased C3 and attenuated OLIG2/MBP improvement. TNF-α challenge increased several inflammatory readouts despite continued BoNT/A exposure. BoNT/A given after hypersensitivity onset dampened spinal inflammation and improved myelin-related measures. IL-1β add-back supported a functional link between the inflammatory glial milieu and C3/OLIG2/MBP.
authors: Zhou WM, Zhang K, Dong YB, Zhang SB, Ran R, Wang ZQ, Zhao GH, Zhou KS, Ma YC, Nan W, Zhang HH.

title: Exploring the role and mechanism of methionine metabolism in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps based on bioinformatics analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveChronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches.MethodsCRSwNP transcriptomic datasets (GSE136825, GSE179265) and single-cell data (GSE276503) were obtained from GEO database. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, differential expression analysis using limma, and Weighted Gene co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) were performed to identify methionine metabolism-related candidate genes. Three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with SHAP interpretation screened core genes. Functions and mechanisms were explored through single-gene GSEA, ceRNA network construction, transcription factor prediction, immune infiltration analysis, and pseudotime trajectory analysis. Potential therapeutic drugs were identified via molecular docking.ResultsAmong 14 candidate genes, CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1 were identified as core genes with excellent diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.85). SHAP analysis revealed CSTB and IGFBP3 as disease risk-promoting factors, while TCN1 showed protective effects. Single-cell analysis demonstrated all three genes were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells with significant differential expression patterns. They were enriched in primary immunodeficiency pathways and significantly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly M2 macrophages and activated dendritic cells. Molecular docking identified five potential therapeutic drugs including ambroxol, carbamazepine, and curcumin with favorable binding energies.ConclusionMethionine metabolism participates in CRSwNP pathogenesis by regulating CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1, affecting epithelial cell function and immune microenvironment. These genes represent promising biomarkers for diagnosis and potential therapeutic targets, providing theoretical basis for developing metabolic-immune intervention strategies in CRSwNP management.Level of evidence: 3
authors: Lin D.

title: Integrating Immunogenetics, Single-Cell Transcriptomics, and AI-Assisted Drug Discovery Reveals CXCL10-Associated Immune Remodelling in Breast Cancer.
abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy shaped by genetic alterations and cytokine-mediated immune interactions. However, integrative characterization of cytokine-related regulators using genetic, single-cell, and computational approaches remains limited. This study aimed to identify genetically supported cytokine-related candidates in breast cancer, characterize their immune and cellular contexts, and explore their potential regulatory and therapeutic relevance. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to identify differentially expressed cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction-related genes, followed by two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), functional enrichment, immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, CellChat analysis, in silico gene perturbation, AI-assisted compound screening, and molecular docking. A total of 882 differentially expressed genes and 20 cytokine-related candidates were identified. MR provided the most consistent support for CXCL10, with genetically predicted higher expression associated with increased breast cancer risk (OR = 1.112, 95% CI: 1.026-1.206, p = 0.010). PRLR was significant only in the IVW analysis and was therefore considered a candidate requiring further validation. The CXCL10/PRLR model achieved an AUC of 0.810 (95% CI: 0.774-0.846) for discriminating breast cancer from normal samples. CXCL10 was predominantly associated with immune-cell populations, interferon-related programs, and predicted chemokine communication. In silico perturbation, AI-assisted screening, and docking further generated computational hypotheses regarding CXCL10-associated regulation and candidate compounds. CXCL10 represents a genetically supported immune-associated candidate in breast cancer. Overall, the findings are computational and hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts and experimental models.
authors: Wang H, Li Y, Chen Y, Chen H, He Y, Zhou Y.

title: Structure-guided engineering of medium- and long-chain triglycerides:​Fermentation-assisted biosynthesis, structural control and future perspective.
abstract: Medium- and long-chain triglycerides (MLCTs) are triacylglycerols (TAGs) that have medium-chain fatty acids (MCFAs) and long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) linked together on a single glycerol backbone. The positioning of the components, such as the MCFA-LCFA-MCFA (MLM-type) positioning, can affect lipase-mediated hydrolysis, release of fatty acids (FAs), absorption and metabolic behavior, however, structure-function relationships requires experimental validation. This review presents a comparison between chemical interesterification, lipase-catalyzed interesterification and fermentation-assisted biosynthesis of MLCT. Chemical interesterification will redistribute fatty acyl groups, but offers​ limited positional control, while lipase-catalyzed synthesis provides more positional selectivity but is susceptible to acyl migration. Fermentation-​assisted biosynthesis is a prospective approach that connects FA chain-length control, acyl-CoA supply and TAG assembly more strongly. However, there is currently more evidence that strongly supports the production of tailored FAs by microbes than demonstrated positional control of MLCT molecular species. Structural validation requires intact TAG molecular species analysis, positional analysis, and stereospecific analysis. An integrated framework combining applications of structural analysis, selective biocatalysis, fermentation optimization, metabolic engineering and functional evaluation is proposed.
authors: Naseem A, Zhang L, Sun S.

title: Protein Quality Control Systems in Neurodegeneration-Chaperones, Cytoskeleton, and the Pathogenic Transition of Tau.
abstract: Maintenance of protein homeostasis is essential for neuronal survival, and its disruption is a defining feature of neurodegenerative diseases. Neurons are particularly vulnerable to proteostatic stress due to their post-mitotic nature, long lifespan, and dependence on cytoskeletal integrity for structural stability, intracellular transport, and synaptic function. In tauopathies and related neurodegenerative disorders, misfolded proteins and aggregation-prone proteins burden the cellular quality-control systems, leading to cytoskeletal destabilization, synaptic dysfunction, and progressive neuronal loss. This review is organized around a central question: for a given tau species, defined by its isoform, post-translational modifications, and assembly state, what determines its fate? We examine how molecular chaperone networks, including HSP100, HSP90, HSP70, J-domain proteins (JDPs), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), and the Prefoldin-CCT pathway, regulate the folding, disaggregation, sequestration, and degradation of pathogenic tau. We highlight how these chaperone networks influence key proteostasis checkpoints, determine whether tau refolds, is degraded, or is redirected toward toxic aggregation, and how these outcomes impact microtubule stability and neuronal function. Drawing on studies in yeast, Drosophila, mammalian models, and human tissues, we develop two key conclusions. First, chaperone activity is not uniformly protective against tauopathies; its effects depend on the tau species, cellular context, and disease stage. Second, because the cytoskeleton is both a chaperone client and an essential component of intracellular clearance pathways, tau pathology and proteostasis failure can reinforce one another. Finally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies and challenges in targeting chaperone networks to restore proteostasis while avoiding unintended neurotoxic consequences.
authors: Bisht A, Pippadpally S, Kumar V.

title: Functional Characterization of Isoflavonoid Synthase CYP736D1 Mediating Oxidative Aryl Migration in a Non-leguminous Plant, Iris germanica (Iridaceae).
abstract: Isoflavonoids are a specialized subclass of flavonoids predominantly distributed in the Fabaceae, where they fulfill essential ecophysiological roles as antimicrobial phytoalexins and symbiotic signal molecules. During their biosynthesis, 2-hydroxyisoflavanone synthase [also called isoflavonoid synthase (IFS)], a cytochrome P450 (P450) of the CYP93C subfamily, catalyzes the oxidative aryl migration of (2S)-flavanones. While various species in the genus Iris (Iridaceae, monocots) are also prolific isoflavonoid producers, the biosynthetic mechanisms in these non-leguminous plants have remained elusive. To identify the Iris IFS, we utilized an established adventitious-root culture system for Iris germanica and employed functional expression-fractionation screening of its cDNA library in yeast cells. This sequence-independent strategy successfully identified CYP736D1 as the enzyme mediating the characteristic skeletal rearrangement of naringenin to form 2-hydroxyisoflavanone. CYP736D1 showed higher in vitro and in vivo catalytic activities than CYP93C2, owing to its higher substrate affinity, kinetic efficiency, and protein stability. The IFS activity was highly specific to naringenin; reactions with other flavanones (liquiritigenin, hesperetin, and pinocembrin) primarily yielded corresponding flavone or 3-hydroxyflavanones. The reaction mechanism of CYP736D1 is considered to be essentially identical to that of CYP93C, but the amino acid residues of CYP93C critical for the IFS activity are not conserved in CYP736D1. Thus, IFS proteins in the Fabaceae and Iridaceae likely evolved from different ancestral P450s and independently acquired the ability to construct the isoflavonoid skeleton through parallel evolution. Bioconversion and transgenic experiments demonstrated that CYP736D1 is a promising tool for biotechnological isoflavonoid production in heterologous systems.
authors: Akashi T, Yoshida J, Nakao T, Uchida K, Uchiyama H, Ayabe SI, Aoki T.

title: Serum Vitamin D Levels do not Affect Susceptibility to EBV Infection – A Mendelian Randomization Study
abstract: Introduction  Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) infection and low serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) levels are strongly associated with multiple sclerosis (MS). We investigated whether genetically proxied serum vitamin D levels are causally linked to EBV infection, assessed by serology and detectable EBV DNA, using Mendelian randomisation (MR). Methods  We conducted two-sample cis-MR using genetic instruments associated with serum 25OHD concentrations, restricted to variants near genes implicated in vitamin D metabolism. Outcomes included EBV seropositivity, antibody responses to four EBV antigens, detectable EBV DNA in blood and saliva, and MS case status as a positive control. Results  Genetically proxied vitamin D levels had no clear effect on EBV seropositivity (odds ratio per standard deviation (SD) increase in rank-based inverse-normal transformation (RINT) 25OHD: 1.76, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83–3.73) or antibody responses to EBV antigens. No significant associations were observed with detectable EBV DNA in blood (beta 0.02, 95% CI −0.004 to 0.04) or saliva (beta 0.02, 95% CI −0.23 to 0.26). In contrast, genetically proxied vitamin D levels were associated with reduced MS risk (odds ratio per SD increase in RINT 25OHD 0.67, 95% CI 0.54–0.84). Discussion  We found no clear evidence that genetically proxied vitamin D levels causally influence EBV serological responses or detectable EBV DNA in blood or saliva. The protective association with MS supports previous genetic evidence. These findings suggest that vitamin D and EBV may influence MS risk through distinct pathways, although effects specific to early-life vitamin D exposure remain possible.
authors: Stanley J, Davey Smith G, Hamilton F, Hamilton F.

title: APH-1A and CDK5 Expression Correlates with Tau Hyperphosphorylation and Its Attenuation by Brahmi and Donep-M in STZ induced Alzheimer’s Disease Model
abstract: Abstract  Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressively characterized neurodegenerative condition marked by molecular instability, neuronal dysfunction and abnormal tau buildup. Identification of disease-associated molecular signatures that can be experimentally validated in neuronal models may provide biologically relevant biomarkers and targets for therapeutic intervention. Here, we employed an integrated transcriptomic and cellular approach to identify and validate biomarkers associated with AD pathology. Differential transcriptomic analysis of (AD versus control) samples was used to prioritize candidate genes, followed by experimental validation in a streptozotocin (STZ) induced SH-SY5Y cells. Among the selected genes, anterior pharynx defective 1A (APH-1A) and cyclin dependent kinase (CDK5) were experimentally validated and further correlated to tau pathology by quantifying phosphorylation of tau at serine 396 (p-Tau Ser396) using confocal fluorescence microscopy. Complementary atomic force microscopy (AFM) was employed to characterize STZ-associated cellular morphological alterations. STZ exposure induced an AD-like neuronal phenotype characterized by associated cellular structural abnormalities. Importantly, co-treatment with (Brahmi) attenuated STZ-associated tau Ser396 phosphorylation and improved the cellular phenotype. The effects of Brahmi were further compared with those of established anti-Alzheimer’s drugs, Donep-M (Donepezil and Memantine) together, which similarly reduced p-Tau Ser396-associated alterations. The concordance between molecular biomarker validation and imaging-based phenotypic responses warrants further investigation of underlying molecular mechanisms. Collectively, our findings establish a transcriptome-to-cellular validation framework in which APH-1A and CDK5 represent experimentally supported AD-associated biomarkers. This integrated strategy provides a foundation for connecting human AD molecular signatures with measurable neuronal phenotypes and evaluating potential therapeutic interventions.
authors: Hathi UPS, Kumar A, Arora J, Kateriya S.

title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanisms of Yinxieping Tablets in Psoriasis Treatment Based on Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Experimental Validation.
abstract: IntroductionPsoriasis is a prevalent immune-mediated chronic inflammatory skin disease, with a pathology defined by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and immune cell infiltration. Yinxieping Tablets (YXPT), a traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting solely of rosin, have been clinically used to alleviate psoriatic symptoms. However, their underlying mechanisms of action remain to be fully elucidated.MethodsWe established an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and systematically screened the potential targets and pathways of YXPT using integrated network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning, transcriptome sequencing, and molecular docking. Key findings were experimentally validated by Western blot and qPCR in a psoriasis-like mouse model.ResultsYXPT treatment improved psoriasiform skin lesions and was associated with lower lesional Ki67 expression and serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels; high-dose YXPT also reduced the spleen index. Integrated analyses identified six candidate genes (BCL2, LYN, SYK, CCR2, AURKA, and ADRB2), with CCR2 emerging as the sole overlap with RNA-seq-derived genes. CCR2-based gene-set analysis showed enrichment of PI3K/Akt- and NF-κB-related pathways. Following YXPT treatment, lesional CCR2 protein and mRNA levels, phosphorylation of PI3K, Akt, p38, and p65, and mRNA levels of PI3K, Akt, p38, ERK1/2, and p65 were lower than in the IMQ group.ConclusionYXPT ameliorated psoriasis-like skin lesions in the IMQ mouse model, accompanied by lower CCR2 expression and changes in PI3K/Akt, MAPK, and NF-κB pathway components. These findings nominate CCR2 as a candidate for further study, while its causal role and relationship to the signaling changes remain to be established.
authors: Zhu Z, Ma L, Sun D, Li W, Zhao J.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis and Experimental Validation Identify ATF3 as a Mesangial Cell-Associated Candidate Regulator in IgA Nephropathy.
abstract: BackgroundIgA nephropathy (IgAN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease marked by mesangial proliferation, inflammation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and progressive renal injury. This study aimed to identify IgAN-associated genes and evaluate the relevance of activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) to mesangial cell activation.MethodsPublic bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression, co-expression network, machine learning, and immune infiltration analyses. Single-cell RNA sequencing, mesangial cell-specific high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and single-cell regulatory network inference were used to assess cell type-specific expression and regulatory activity. The findings were further evaluated using Nephroseq and an aggregated IgA1-stimulated human mesangial cell model with ATF3 knockdown.ResultsIntegrated analysis identified 47 shared differentially expressed genes and a 12-gene candidate set with reduced expression in IgAN. ATF3 was prioritized as a mesangial cell-associated candidate and showed reduced expression and regulon activity in the analyzed single-cell dataset. Nephroseq analysis showed lower glomerular ATF3 expression in IgAN-related kidney disease samples; ATF3 expression was positively associated with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively associated with serum creatinine and proteinuria. Aggregated IgA1 reduced ATF3 expression in human mesangial cells, whereas ATF3 knockdown further increased inflammatory cytokine expression and proliferative activity.ConclusionReduced ATF3 expression is associated with IgAN-related mesangial cell activation. ATF3 may represent a mesangial cell-associated candidate regulator that warrants further mechanistic and clinical validation.
authors: Liang M, Gan X, Shadekejiang H, Hong H, Li X, Xia T, Wang J, Zhang X, Lu C.

title: RIFTT: Robust Identification of Fusion genes in Tumor Transcriptomes.
abstract: BackgroundFusion genes serve as crucial biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy, yet many detection tools lead to high false-positive rates and poor consensus. We developed RIFTT, a pipeline for Robust Identification of Fusion genes in Tumor Transcriptomes which integrates Arriba and FusionCatcher, two state-of-the-art fusion callers, together with novel scoring metrics (Promiscuity Score, Fusion Transcript Score, and Robustness Score).ResultsBenchmarking on TCGA-LAML, BeatAML, and LL-100 datasets demonstrated RIFTT's ability to reduce the number of candidates by up to 95% compared to single callers. At the same time, it preserves high-confidence events, outperforming both the nf-core/rnafusion pipeline and an Arriba/FusionCatcher consensus approach. RIFTT also identified novel high-evidence candidates, including a previously unreported recurrent fusion in acute myeloid leukemia.ConclusionPackaged in a Singularity container for ease of use across computing environments, RIFTT provides standardized visual and annotated tabular outputs to support downstream analysis in research workflows and clinical molecular diagnostics. RIFTT is freely available at https://github.com/pkerbs/RIFTT .
authors: Kerbs P, Latzko L, Mansmann U, Unger K, Greif PA, Vosberg S.

title: One Health approach to Babesia and Bartonella species: occupational zoonotic infections in veterinary workers and their families.
abstract: This study investigated the presence of Babesia, Bartonella, and Borrelia spp infection in an extended veterinary family. Between May 2023 and August 2025, 8 individuals enrolled in an Institutional Review Board-approved observational study. Serological evidence of Bartonella spp exposure and molecular evidence of Babesia, Bartonella, and Borrelia spp infection were assessed. Among other symptoms, at least half of the study participants reported chronic fatigue, headaches, anxiety, depression, and difficulty remembering. On the basis of PCR amplification and DNA sequencing, infection with Babesia odocoilei, Babesia divergens-like MO-1, Babesia gibsoni, or Babesia microti was confirmed in 4 individuals. Three other individuals were PCR positive for Piroplasmida/Apicomplexa DNA. Four individuals were seroreactive to 1 or more Bartonella spp and 6 individuals were Bartonella PCR positive in blood, serum, or enrichment blood cultures. Six individuals had at least 1 Borrelia partition detected by digital PCR; however, efforts in our laboratory to confirm Borrelia digital PCR positivity by DNA sequencing were not successful. Similar to this extended veterinary family, previous studies have documented that veterinarians and veterinary workers may be occupationally at risk for exposure to Bartonella spp. On the basis of the results of this study, veterinary workers may also be at risk for infection with Babesia spp and potentially other Piroplasmida/Apicomplexa organisms. The potential that chronic intravascular or endotheliotropic infections with vector-borne pathogens contributes to multisystem illnesses in veterinary workers deserves future research considerations, which, on a clinical, epidemiological, and microbiological basis, will require sequential lifetime studies.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
authors: Breitschwerdt EB, Maggi RG, Kaufman D, Dillon-McBride J, Kingston E.

title: Immune and tumor-intrinsic signatures are associated with resistance and response to PD-1 blockade in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: BackgroundAnti-PD-1 therapy has significantly improved clinical outcomes in patients with advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC); however, approximately half of patients fail to respond. This study aimed to investigate molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance and to identify predictive biomarkers.MethodsWhole transcriptome profiling was performed using HTG EdgeSeq technology on pre-treatment cSCC samples. Clinical data and treatment outcomes were correlated with gene expression profiles, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed in relation to response. Moreover, promising targets were further analyzed at the protein level via immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry.ResultsTumors from patients achieving disease control showed a distinct immune-active transcriptional profile characterized by interferon-associated signaling, enhanced antigen presentation pathways, and cytotoxic immune activity. Consistently, IFN-γ and cytolytic activity signatures were higher in patients with favorable clinical outcomes. CIBERSORTx-based deconvolution demonstrated marked interpatient heterogeneity, with T cells, macrophages, and NK cells representing major components of the immune infiltrate, but no major differences in overall immune cell composition between patients with early and late/no progression. Histopathological assessment revealed a tendency toward higher immune cell infiltration in patients achieving disease control. Notably, elevated gene expression of SLC7A5 and SOX2 was associated with poor response and early progression. Also, at protein level, higher SLC7A5 expression was associated with early progression, whereas SOX2 showed a more heterogeneous pattern, with particularly high expression in a subset of progressive tumors.ConclusionOur data provide hypothesis-generating evidence that a combination of immune-related and tumor-intrinsic novel molecular markers is associated with response to anti-PD-1 therapy in advanced cSCC, thereby identifying promising candidate biomarkers, which require validation in larger independent cohorts.
authors: DeTemple VK, Beikirch M, Ulama AC, Bergmann M, Bredemeier S, Schacht V, Sachse M, Mohr P, Gambichler T, Gutzmer R, Schaper-Gerhardt K.

title: From Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease to Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Mediterranean Diet.
abstract: The knowledge structure and evolution of Mediterranean diet and fatty liver disease research from 1992 - 2025 were systematically characterized through bibliometric analysis, with additional examination of the terminological transition from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). A comprehensive bibliometric and knowledge graph analysis was performed on 725 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (1992-2025) using the bibliometrix R package, CiteSpace, and VOSviewer. Annual publication output increased rapidly from 2014 onward. Italy, Spain, and the United States led in the number of publications. Spanish research institutions were prominently represented among the most productive institutions. Nutrition-related journals dominated publication output, whereas hepatology journals, such as Hepatology and the Journal of Hepatology, occupied a central role in the cited literature. Keyword and topic analyses showed a shift from early nutrient-focused themes toward metabolic mechanisms and, more recently, clinical and lifestyle management. NAFLD transitioned from a motor theme (2005-2015) to a basic theme (2016-2025), while MASLD emerged as a recent research theme. Coronary heart disease research was a key focus during 2001-2020, whereas management-related research emerged as a rising hotspot beginning in 2022. Overall, the field evolved from nutrient-focused to management-oriented research, with terminology shifting from NAFLD to MASLD and current frontiers emphasizing clinical translation, gut microbiota, and multi-target mechanisms.
authors: Ding Y, Liu Q, Mao M, Feng B, Huang Y.

title: Mitochondrial Metabolism-Related Candidate Signatures in Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Spectrum: An Exploratory Integrative Bioinformatics Study.
abstract: ​Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a progressive valvular disorder in which the role of mitochondrial metabolism remains incompletely understood. This exploratory study aimed to identify mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MIMMRGs) associated with CAVD-spectrum valve remodeling. GSE83453 was used as the training dataset, and GSE51472 was used for expression-direction validation. Both datasets contain biologically and phenotypically heterogeneous groups of diseased valves. CAVD-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were integrated with MIMMRGs, followed by functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), expression validation, immune infiltration analysis, transcription factor analysis, drug and compound prediction, and molecular docking. A total of 909 DEGs and 1,234 MIMMRGs were identified, yielding 67 candidate genes enriched in metabolic and biosynthetic processes. ACADL and TDO2 were identified as candidate biomarkers and exhibited consistent expression differences between CAVD and normal samples in both datasets. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated the involvement of chemokine-related and immune-regulatory pathways. Four immune cell types differed between the CAVD and normal groups, and ACADL and TDO2 exhibited opposite correlations with naive B cells. HNF4A, STAT3, and AR were predicted to be common transcriptional regulators. Molecular docking indicated favorable in silico interactions between doxorubicin and ACADL and between dexamethasone and TDO2. In conclusion, ACADL and TDO2 are candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism and immune-related processes in heterogeneous CAVD-spectrum valve lesions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require independent clinical and experimental validation.
authors: Yang M, Gui Y, Qian H, Zhang D.

title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomics with Tissue Validation Prioritizes MMP1 in Diabetic Foot Ulcer.
abstract: Cellular sources of reproducible transcriptomic changes in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated differential-expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) gene screening, exploratory machine-learning feature selection, two external bulk-transcriptomic datasets, single-cell analysis, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) network analysis, and patient-tissue quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and western blotting. In GSE199939 (10 DFU and 11 control samples), 3,691 differentially expressed genes were identified, and the WGCNA blue module was strongly associated with DFU (r = 0.97, p = 5 × 10-13). Intersecting the differentially expressed genes, blue-module hub genes, and 1,062 DPN-related genes yielded 77 candidates. CCL7, CHEK1, MKI67, MMP1, MMP13, and TRPV2 were supported by at least two feature-selection methods; complete separation in support vector machine recursive feature elimination raised concerns about discovery-cohort overfitting. MMP1 showed the largest discovery-cohort expression change (log2 fold change = 9.854; adjusted p = 1.24 × 10-29). In the merged GSE68183/GSE80178 matrix, MMP1 had an adjusted p of 0.0159 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.981. In GSE134431, MMP1 expression was nominally higher in DFU than in non-ulcerated diabetic foot skin (p = 0.0225; adjusted p = 0.135; AUC = 0.808). Analysis of 69,944 cells from 24 samples showed the highest mean MMP1 expression in fibroblasts, with higher sample-level expression in DFU fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and endothelial cells. Patient-tissue assays showed higher MMP1 mRNA abundance in four matched pairs (paired test on ΔCq, p = 3.04 × 10-5) and higher protein abundance in three matched pairs (paired p = 0.0107). Statistical replication was incomplete. Findings suggest a fibroblast-centered matrix-remodeling association, subject to limitations from transcripts per million (TPM) input in count-based discovery analysis, incomplete single-cell preprocessing records, and small tissue-assay cohorts. Causality and clinical utility remain unestablished.
authors: Zhou M, Zeng Y, Xie H, Kong Y.

title: Expanding the conjugation toolbox of DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters with biotin-streptavidin.
abstract: DNA-stabilized silver nanoclusters (DNA-AgNCs) combine molecular-scale dimensions with sequence-dependent optical properties, making them promising candidates for bioimaging applications. However, strategies for site-specific conjugation of DNA-AgNCs remain comparatively limited. Here, we expand the conjugation toolbox of DNA-AgNCs through biotin functionalization of previously developed single-stranded DNA-AgNC containing a [Ag16Cl2]8+ cluster. Incorporation of biotin either at 3' end or in the middle of the sequence, enabled selective immobilization of the resulting biotinylated DNA-AgNCs on streptavidin-coated poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) microparticles. Importantly, biotin functionalization and subsequent particle attachment largely preserved the characteristic optical properties and fluorescence lifetimes of the DNA-AgNCs, while control experiments showed negligible nonspecific binding of the non-biotinylated DNA-AgNCs. These results demonstrated that biotin-streptavidin interaction provides a robust strategy for the modular functionalization of DNA-AgNCs without compromising their photophysical properties, opening opportunities for their integration into future bioimaging and sensing applications.
authors: Rück V, Lind SW, Mollerup CB, Vosch T.

title: CpxR-CpxS two-component system exacerbates development of antibiotic resistance in  Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa , as a member of the ESKAPE pathogens, is well known for its ability to develop multidrug resistance following antibiotic therapy. Overexpression of the efflux pumps, often caused by dysfunction of related transcriptional factors, is well known as a common mechanism underpins multidrug resistance. Previous work showed direct regulatory link of CpxR-CpxS, an OmpR-EnvZ family two-component system, with the expression of the predominant MexAB-OprM efflux pump in  P. aeruginosa . However, the contribution of this regulatory link to the development of antibiotic resistance has not been fully elucidated. In this work, it has been shown that deletion of  cpxR , but not  cpxS , reduces the emergence of multidrug resistant colonies almost 1000 times lower compared to the parental wild type  P. aeruginosa PA14 following sub-lethal antibiotic exposure, suggesting that apart from CpxS, other sensory component(s) or pathway(s) can also mediate CpxR activity in the development of antibiotic resistance in  P. aeruginosa . We further demonstrate that when glucose is used as the sole carbon source, it leads to increased expression levels of  mexA and reduced antibiotics susceptibilities in the PA14Δ  cpxS strain in a  cpxR dependent manner. GtrS, another EnvZ family sensor kinase, but not the well-known AckA-Pta pathway, mediates this glucose effects. Both  in vivo and  in vitro evidences support that GtrS can activate CpxR in a cross-talk manner in the absence of CpxS. Besides  gtrS , at least four other sensor kinase genes (  envZ ,  tctE ,  phoR and  colS ) can exert activation effect upon CpxR in the PA14Δ  cpxS strain. Having the risk of multiple way to antibiotic resistance development,  cpxS null mutations can be emerged in  P. aeruginosa clinical isolates. Since many OmpR-EnvZ family two-component system have been shown to be engaged in antibiotic resistance, its potential risk of exacerbating antibiotic resistance in ESKAPE pathogens has been discussed.
authors: Tian Z, Tian A, Ko KS, Wang Y.

title: More insights into the dynamic assembly and rotation of the archaellum motor machinery
abstract: Archaea use the archaellum for swimming motility. Rotation of the archaellum is driven by the ATPase ArlI and the membrane platform protein ArlJ. Structural studies suggest that conformational changes in ArlI power the rotation of ArlJ. However, how ATP hydrolysis is converted into rotation remains poorly understood. Using single-molecule total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy, we show that dimeric ArlJ forms a complex with ArlI. Combining conservation analysis, AlphaFold3 predictions and co-purifications, we identified conserved ArlJ residues required for interaction with ArlI, including a structurally rigid loop and the critical residue R341 at the ArlI interface. Motility assays in  Haloferax volcanii confirmed these findings. Together, these findings support a model in which a dimeric ArlJ is interacting with ArlI via conserved residues to generate torque.
authors: Joest M, Wüllner F, Schimpf J, Vollmar L, Steyer E, Kumariya R, Hugel T, Albers S.

title: Metal-Organic Frameworks for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes in Aqueous Batteries: Structure-Interface-Performance Relationships: A Critical Review.
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs), with intrinsic advantages such as environmental friendliness, cost-effectiveness, and high theoretical capacity, have emerged as promising candidates for energy storage systems. However, the zinc anode in ZIBs faces several challenges, including dendrite formation, the hydrogen evolution reaction, corrosion, and surface passivation. These processes are strongly coupled rather than independent failure modes. To address these challenges, functional-material-based strategies involving electrode architecture, interface engineering, separator modification, and electrolyte regulation have been developed to improve the reversibility of the Zn metal anode. This review summarizes a structure-interface-performance framework for understanding MOF-enabled stabilization of Zn metal anodes. Four implementation routes are systematically examined and compared: MOF protective coatings, MOF-based three-dimensional hosts, MOF-modified separators, and MOF-containing liquid, gel, or solid-state electrolytes. Particular attention is paid to the relationships between pore aperture, framework chemistry, zincophilic sites, conductivity, mechanical integrity and five major interfacial functions: homogeneous nucleation, selective deposition, zincophilic regulation, accelerating Zn2+ desolvation, and interfacial shielding against water and detrimental anions. Representative studies are critically assessed by considering the trade-offs between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity, interfacial protection and transport resistance, and long-duration laboratory cycling and practical Zn utilization, allowing to develop predictive design principles for MOF-enabled aqueous Zn metal batteries.
authors: Liu S, Maisuradze M, Giorgetti M.

title: Current strategies and challenges in vaccine platforms for Newcastle Disease Virus.
abstract: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) remains one of the most economically devastating pathogens affecting poultry production. Despite decades of vaccination efforts, NDV continues to circulate and remain endemic across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, posing persistent threats to food security, rural livelihoods, and international trade. This review comprehensively examines the current landscape of NDV vaccine platforms, their immunological mechanisms, and the multifaceted challenges limiting their efficacy. We critically evaluated conventional platforms, including lentogenic live attenuated vaccines and oil-adjuvanted inactivated formulations, highlighting their contributions to disease control while addressing their inherent limitations including cold-chain dependence, maternal antibody interference, incomplete cross-protection against heterologous genotypes, and the absence of differentiating infected from vaccinated animals (DIVA) capability. We then examined next-generation approaches, including recombinant vector platforms, virus-like particles, DNA and mRNA vaccines, and AI/ML-informed antigen design, assessing each against its actual stage of development, from vaccines already in commercial use to platforms that remain preclinical or theoretical, rather than treating design capability as equivalent to field-ready deployment. Finally, we addressed regulatory, manufacturing, and logistical barriers to vaccine deployment in low-resource settings, including a dedicated feasibility assessment and platform-comparison table for smallholder-dominated, endemic regions. Integrating these technological advances with robust surveillance, biosecurity, and supportive policies will be essential for achieving sustainable NDV control and advancing toward eradication.
journal: Tropical diseases, travel medicine and vaccines
authors: Amoia CF, Misinzo G, Munir M.

title: Interfacial Vacancy Engineering in CdS-CeO<sub>2</sub> S-Scheme Heterojunctions for Efficient Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution and Wastewater Remediation.
abstract: A hydrothermal-calcination route combined with an in situ oil-bath deposition process was designed to construct CdS nanoparticle-decorated CeO2 nanorod heterostructures. The intimate interfacial contact between the two components, along with the presence of sulfur vacancies in the CdS lattice, was corroborated by x-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. The resulting heterostructure, with an optimal composition, shows substantially improved photocatalytic performance in visible-light-driven H2 generation and the decomposition of various organic contaminants, including dyes, antibiotics, and phenolic derivatives. A suite of characterization techniques-including photoluminescence spectroscopy, transient photocurrent measurements, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and radical quenching assays-was employed to probe the charge dynamics. The results reveal that the S scheme charge transfer mechanism, working in concert with vacancy engineering, facilitates charge-carrier separation and migration while retaining the robust redox capacity inherent to both semiconductors. Collectively, these findings establish defect engineered CdS/CeO2 heterojunctions as a versatile and promising candidate for simultaneous solar-to-chemical energy conversion and water purification.
authors: Chu H, Li W, Fang X, Gao Y, Wu C, Lin S, Xu M, Li T, Peng L.

title: Dynamic structural adaptation of a conserved interaction hotspot in the respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F.
abstract: Protein interaction sites must maintain structural integrity while accommodating conformational fluctuations and sequence perturbations. Molecular determinants that distinguish locally adaptable residues from structurally constrained positions within conserved interfaces remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate this problem using the prefusion respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F as a model system, focusing on a conserved interaction hotspot proximal to the MEDI8897-binding interface. An integrated computational framework combining evolutionary conservation, structure-based energetic analysis, residue interaction networks, and molecular dynamics simulations was used to characterize mutation-dependent structural responses. Analysis of 1848 RSV F sequences revealed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot comprising C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Despite conservation, saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed pronounced heterogeneity in calculated energetic response to substitution. P205R and N208R produced highly unfavorable calculated energetic effects, whereas I206R exhibited an approximately neutral energetic response. Residue interaction network analysis identified I206 as topologically central residue with the highest betweenness and closeness centrality within the hotspot. Aggregate MD sampling comprised three independent 500-ns simulations for each of seven systems, yielding 10.5 μs of total simulation time. All systems retained the overall prefusion architecture over the simulated timescale but exhibited distinct local and interprotomer responses. N208R produced the strongest local perturbation, including increased hotspot flexibility and reduced interprotomer contact occupancy. In contrast, P205R maintained restrained local dynamics despite its energetic penalty, whereas I206R preserved a broadly wild-type-like dynamic profile. These findings indicate that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide complementary information for characterizing mutation-induced structural adaptation.
authors: Kaushik R, Re S.

title: YAP/AP-1 activation in sebocytes promotes CCL5-dependent perifollicular macrophage recruitment in rosacea.
abstract: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder in which macrophages have been increasingly implicated, yet the spatial basis and local cues of their recruitment remain poorly defined. Given the prominent perifollicular inflammatory changes in rosacea, we investigated whether sebocytes contribute to macrophage recruitment and the underlying mechanisms. Multiplex immunofluorescence combined with distance-stratified quantification demonstrated a preferential perifollicular distribution of macrophages around pilosebaceous units (PSUs) in human rosacea lesions. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses identified the C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5)-C-C motif chemokine receptor 5 (CCR5) axis as a candidate mediator of sebocyte-macrophage crosstalk. Silencing CCL5 by small interfering RNA and CCL5 neutralization attenuated sebocyte-driven macrophage migration in vitro and reduced macrophage accumulation in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis of sebocytes further linked CCL5 expression to activation of Yes-associated protein (YAP)/activator protein-1 (AP-1) signaling. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of YAP or AP-1 reduced CCL5 expression in sebocytes and alleviated erythema and macrophage infiltration in vivo. Furthermore, untargeted lipidomics uncovered profound metabolic reprogramming in sebocytes, characterized notably by the accumulation of cholesteryl esters. Bidirectional interventions via simvastatin and cholesterol loading confirmed that this lipid remodeling acts as an upstream driver of YAP nuclear translocation. Overall, our study identifies a PSU-centered inflammatory niche in rosacea and implicates lipid-driven, YAP/AP-1-associated sebocytic CCL5 upregulation in perifollicular macrophage recruitment, providing a rationale for further exploring sebocyte- and pilosebaceous unit-directed therapeutic strategies in rosacea.
authors: Liu J, Yang J, Zhou W, Ruan Z, Chen C, Li C, Feng C, Yan J, Liao C, Zhang H, Liu X, Cao Y, Xu D, Zhang C, Wang X, Wang P, Zeng Q.

title: Mitigation of imprinted antibody responses against COVID-19 in highly vaccinated older adults.
abstract: Despite higher clinical risk of severe COVID-19, contemporary data on antibody durability and breadth in older adults receiving multiple COVID-19 booster vaccines remain limited amid ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron JN.1 descendants and the divergent BA.3.2 saltation variant. We studied a clinically vulnerable cohort of 43 older adults (median age = 85 years, IQR 75-88, 40% female). Using pseudotyped and surrogate virus neutralization-based assays, we demonstrate that JN.1 and KP.2 vaccinations six months apart elicit high-potency neutralization across all studied JN.1-lineage variants but not BA.3.2.2, where titers were 2-3-fold lower. Waning of serum neutralizing activity was modest between vaccine doses, suggesting sustained immunity. Importantly, the half-life of serum neutralization against Wu-1 (179 days) was substantially longer than JN.1 subvariants (43.7-70.1 days), consistent with Wu-1-specific imprinted responses. Furthermore, BA.3.2.2 neutralizing antibody half-life was prolonged at 107 days, implicating imprinted ancestral variant-targeting antibodies having some activity against BA.3.2.2. While absolute neutralization titers remained highest against ancestral Wu-1 due to multiple historical exposures, recall responses after the KP.2 vaccine revealed a shift in immunodominance. Neutralization against full-length Wu-1 spike was not boosted, whereas all JN.1 descendants and BA.3.2.2 showed significant boosts, indicating partial alleviation of immune imprinting. These data indicate that in the elderly, protective neutralizing antibody responses against recent variants of concern can be achieved, with reduction of immune imprinting and waning through biannual, strain-updated booster vaccines. Imprinted antibodies against ancestral variants may still be relevant for protection against highly immune evasive variants such as BA.3.2.2, highlighting that careful characterization of population-level COVID-19 humoral immunity remains warranted.

title: Estrogen-driven PDK4-MYH9 phosphorylation promotes mitochondrial fission and osteogenic commitment of mesenchymal stem cells.
abstract: IntroductionPostmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP), driven primarily by estrogen deficiency, represents a major public health challenge. Although estrogen's anti-resorptive effects are well established, the direct osteogenic actions by which it regulates the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) remain poorly understood.ObjectivesThis study aimed to elucidate a novel mechanism by which estrogen regulates osteogenic differentiation in MSCs and to identify key downstream molecular events.MethodsWe employed single-cell RNA sequencing to profile the transcriptional landscape of osteoporotic MSCs. The pro-osteogenic effects of estradiol (E2) were validated in ovariectomized mice and primary mouse bone marrow-derived MSCs through in vitro differentiation assays and mitochondrial functional analyses. Downstream targets of estrogen receptor were identified by integrating CUT&Tag-seq with transcriptomic data and validated using conditional knockout mice. Protein interactions and phosphorylation sites were mapped via co-immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, and mitochondrial morphology assays.ResultsOsteoporotic MSCs displayed concurrent impairments in osteogenic differentiation and mitochondrial function. E2 stimulated mitochondrial fission, enhanced maximal respiration, and induced DRP1 translocation to mitochondria. The combined evidence from our CUT&Tag-seq, RNA-seq, and the additional CUT&Tag-qPCR and ERα knockdown data supports the conclusion that Pdk4 is a direct transcriptional target of ERα. This finding is further corroborated by the compromised osteogenesis observed in conditional Pdk4 knockout mice. Mechanistically, PDK4 catalyzed MYH9 phosphorylation at serine 1943, thereby facilitating DRP1 recruitment to mitochondria and subsequent fission. Both pharmacological inhibition of PDK4 and introduction of the phosphorylation-deficient MYH9 S1943A mutant abolished the E2-induced effects. Notably, Pdk4 overexpression in ovariectomized mice reversed bone loss in the absence of exogenous estrogen.ConclusionThis study identifies an unrecognized ERα-PDK4-MYH9 signaling axis through which estrogen drives mitochondrial fission to promote osteogenic differentiation of MSCs. These findings expand the current understanding of estrogen's skeletal actions by revealing a pro-osteogenic effect on MSCs, and suggest PDK4 as a potential candidate for therapeutic exploration in PMOP.

title: Integrative multi-omics and multi-trait analysis prioritizes regulatory mechanisms and genes for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: BackgroundMetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent condition that progresses from simple steatosis to advanced fibrosis, significantly affecting liver function and systemic health. Despite its widespread impact, therapeutic options remain limited, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive exploration to identify potential therapeutic targets.MethodsWe developed an analysis pipeline anchored on liver gene expression, integrating differential meta-analysis of transcriptomic data across three MASLD stages, transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR), and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) to identify candidate genes potentially involved in MASLD progression. We further prioritized these genes using a scoring system that incorporated gene expression-clinical phenotype correlation meta-analysis, proteome-wide association studies (PWAS), and external genetic data from the GWAS Catalog and ExPheWAS. In addition, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis was performed to characterize the expression patterns of prioritized genes across liver cell types and disease stages.ResultsBy integrating transcriptomic, genetic, and phenotypic evidence, we prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD. snRNA-seq analysis of liver cells from healthy to cirrhotic stages revealed stage- and cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes. Through experimental validation in a lipid overload hepatocyte model, we confirmed a role for MLIP in lipid metabolism. To facilitate community access and data exploration, these data were organized and deposited into a publicly accessible interactive web portal (www.masldportal.net).ConclusionsOur integrative, liver expression-anchored multi-omics framework prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD and highlighted MLIP as a functional modulator of hepatocellular lipid accumulation. These results provide a systematic foundation for understanding MASLD biology and for guiding future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.
journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
authors: Feng Z, Chen F, Xiao J, Du A, Deng J, Wu S, Zhang Y, Li X, Zheng A, Li H.

title: Green-synthesized nanoparticles for sensing: From molecular mechanisms to next-generation sensing platforms.
abstract: Green synthesis has emerged as a sustainable and mechanistically versatile strategy for fabricating nanomaterials with tunable physicochemical and interfacial properties for advanced sensing applications. Unlike conventional synthesis routes that depend on toxic chemicals, harsh reaction conditions, and post-synthetic functionalization, green synthesis integrates nanoparticle formation, stabilization, defect generation, and surface engineering within a biomolecule-rich environment. Biological entities such as plant extracts, microorganisms, proteins, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and polyphenols act as reducing and capping agents, producing intrinsically functionalized nanostructures with enhanced biocompatibility and sensing performance. Recent studies demonstrate that biomolecule-mediated synthesis strongly influences nucleation kinetics, morphology evolution, defect chemistry, electronic structure, plasmonic behaviour, and interfacial charge transfer, which collectively govern sensitivity, selectivity, and signal amplification in sensing systems. This Review critically discusses the mechanistic foundations of green nanoparticle synthesis and their use in electrochemical, fluorescence, colorimetric, SERS, and photoelectrochemical sensing platforms. Emphasis is placed on morphology engineering, defect-mediated electronic modulation, biomolecular corona formation, heterojunction design, and nano-bio interface engineering. Current challenges related to reproducibility, scalability, and mechanistic understanding are also highlighted, alongside future opportunities involving AI-assisted synthesis optimization and sustainable next-generation sensing architectures.
authors: Bachhar V, Joshi V, Wu CH, Lin WC, Tsai CI, Duseja M, Chang-Chien GP, Kogularasu S.

title: Rainfall-runoff duration shapes divergent water quality and microbial assembly patterns in a drinking water reservoir.
abstract: Under climate change, the frequency of extreme rainfall events is increasing. However, how rainfall-runoff duration shapes water quality dynamics and microbial ecological processes in drinking water reservoirs remains poorly understood. Using Jinpen Reservoir as a case study, this study investigated ecological responses to contrasting short- and long-duration rainfall-runoff events by integrating water quality monitoring, microbial community analysis, community assembly assessment, and functional potential prediction. Short-duration rainfall-runoff resulted in rapid pulse inputs of allochthonous nutrients and organic matter, leading to transient deterioration of water quality. In contrast, long-duration continuous rainfall-runoff promoted enhanced water renewal and vertical mixing, coinciding with improved water quality conditions during the later stage of the event. Microbial communities exhibited distinct response patterns under contrasting rainfall-runoff regimes. Short-duration rainfall-runoff induced transient microbial community fluctuations and maintained higher community evenness, whereas long-duration rainfall-runoff was linked to persistent microbial community reorganization, altered microbial association networks, increased community richness, a higher proportion of specialist taxa, and stronger environmental filtering signals. Redundancy analysis (RDA) and Mantel tests revealed that nitrogen, phosphorus, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), CODMn, and turbidity were key environmental factors associated with microbial community variation. PICRUSt2-based functional prediction further indicated that long-duration rainfall-runoff was linked to enhanced predicted microbial functional potential, particularly for nitrogen cycling-related functional pathways. Overall, this study reveals that rainfall-runoff events with different durations correspond to distinct ecological response modes, with prolonged disturbances associated with stronger environmental coupling and microbial community reorganization. These findings advance our understanding of reservoir microbial responses under changing precipitation regimes and provide scientific insights for adaptive management of drinking water reservoirs under climate change.
authors: Chen S, Yan C, Luo Z, Jiao Y, Huang T.

title: Glabridin inhibits senescent CAF-mediated proliferation, migration, and invasion of colorectal cancer cells by suppressing the expression and secretion of MMP1/3/12.
abstract: BackgroundCancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) critically regulate colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but the contribution of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-induced senescent CAFs to CRC malignancy and whether this stromal response can be pharmacologically restrained remain unclear. This study investigated whether Glabridin (Gla) attenuates the pro-tumorigenic activity of 5-FU-induced senescent CAFs.MethodsPrimary human CRC-derived CAFs were exposed to 5-FU to establish a senescence model, which was validated by SA-β-Gal staining, EdU assay, cell-cycle analysis, γ-H2AX immunofluorescence, p53/p21 detection, and SASP marker analysis. Drug-free conditioned media (CM) collected from control, 5-FU-treated, and 5-FU plus Gla-treated CAFs after drug withdrawal and medium replacement were applied to RKO and SW480 cells to assess proliferation, migration, and invasion. Transcriptomic and integrative analyses were used to identify candidate SASP factors, followed by RT-qPCR and ELISA validation.Results5-FU induced a stable senescent phenotype in primary CAFs and enhanced SASP factor expression. CM from senescent CAFs promoted CRC cell proliferation, wound closure, and invasion. MMP1, MMP3, and MMP12 were identified as candidate senescence-associated secretory factors and were upregulated in 5-FU-induced senescent CAFs. Gla significantly suppressed 5-FU-induced MMP1/3/12 mRNA expression and reduced the cell number-normalized secretion of these MMPs in senescent CAF-CM. Functionally, CM from 5-FU plus Gla-treated CAFs exhibited weaker pro-tumorigenic effects than 5-FU-CM.ConclusionsGla attenuates the pro-tumorigenic activity of 5-FU-induced senescent CAFs, at least in part by suppressing MMP1/3/12 expression and secretion. These findings suggest that Gla may help mitigate chemotherapy-associated stromal remodeling in CRC.
authors: Wang M, Li F, Liang Y, Su L, Yang L.

title: LILRB3 as an ulcerative colitis-associated molecular biomarker: integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental validation.
abstract: ObjectiveUlcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Although macrophage-mediated inflammation is associated with UC progression, its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to identify UC-associated molecular biomarkers and explore their roles in immune dysregulation.MethodsBulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multi-algorithm machine learning. The machine-learning model was evaluated in independent validation cohorts, and a nomogram was subsequently constructed and evaluated in an additional colonic-tissue cohort. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, pseudotime analysis, and scTenifoldKnk-based virtual knockout were used to investigate hub genes. RT-qPCR, WB, and IHC validated the findings in a DSS-induced mouse model and clinical samples, while siRNA-mediated LILRB3 knockdown was performed in THP-1-derived macrophages.ResultsDifferential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 55 candidate genes. Through screening of 127 machine-learning algorithm combinations, DPP10, LILRB3, MTMR11, and SLC6A14 were identified as UC-associated molecular biomarkers. A separately constructed logistic regression nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.989. LILRB3 was predominantly expressed in myeloid cells, particularly M1 macrophages, and was associated with inflammatory immune cell infiltration. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that LILRB3⁺ M1 macrophages exhibited active intercellular communication involving MHC-II-CD4 and other inflammation-related signaling pathways. Experimental validation showed increased PirB expression in the colonic tissues of DSS-induced colitis mice and elevated LILRB3 expression in human UC colonic tissues. Knockdown of LILRB3 in THP-1-derived macrophages significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β mRNA expression.ConclusionLILRB3 is a candidate UC-associated molecular biomarker in colonic tissue and may be associated with proinflammatory macrophage remodeling and myeloid immune dysregulation, warranting mechanistic investigation.
authors: Yang B, Sun D, Liu Z, Zhou L.

title: The Prevalence of Occult Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Immunized Children Born to Mothers Who Are Hepatitis B Carriers.
abstract: PurposeOccult hepatitis B virus infection is characterized by the presence of hepatitis B virus DNA despite the undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of occult hepatitis B virus infection in children born to hepatitis B surface antigen-positive mothers who received complete immunoprophylaxis.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 99 children. All received hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis B immune globulin within 24 hours after birth. Serological markers and serum hepatitis B virus DNA were assessed in children aged 9 months to 15 years.ResultsAll children were negative for hepatitis B surface antigen and serum hepatitis B virus DNA. The prevalence of serum-detectable occult hepatitis B virus infection was 0% (95% confidence interval: 0-3.6%). Anti-hepatitis B surface antibody seropositivity (≥ 10 IU/L) was observed in 66.7% of the children. Four children older than 24 months were positive for anti-hepatitis B core IgG antibody and anti-hepatitis B e antibody, possibly reflecting previous exposure without evidence of active infection. In these children, serum hepatitis B virus DNA remained negative at the initial assessment and at the 6- and 12-month follow-up assessments.ConclusionNo serum-detectable occult hepatitis B virus infection cases were identified. Complete immunoprophylaxis appears effective in this population; however, larger prospective studies with serial hepatitis B virus DNA testing are needed.
authors: Yardibi YS, Ustundag GH.

title: WGCNA and single-cell analysis identify FLG, DSG3 and DSG1 as melanoma-associated hub genes and their modulation by Dinaciclib.
abstract: Melanoma is one of the most aggressive skin cancers, and its molecular heterogeneity continues to present challenges for diagnosis and treatment. Identification of molecular alterations associated with melanoma progression may provide clinically relevant biomarkers and therapeutic insights. In this study, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were integrated across melanoma transcriptomic datasets to identify disease-associated gene modules and hub genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis and prognostic modelling were subsequently used to characterize candidate desmosomal genes. WGCNA identified melanoma-associated modules enriched in keratinization, epidermal differentiation, and desmosome-related processes, with FLG, DSG1, and DSG3 emerging as prominent hub genes. Their prognostic relevance was evaluated in the TCGA-SKCM cohort using LASSO-Cox and multivariable survival analysis, while single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate their cellular distribution. The analysis revealed distinct cellular expression patterns, with DSG3 showing expression within melanoma cells, whereas FLG and DSG1 were predominantly associated with keratinocyte populations. Pharmacological validation using Dinaciclib in A375 and SK-MEL-28 melanoma cells demonstrated reduced cell viability and increased accumulation of cells in the G2/M phase, accompanied by reduced expression of FLG, DSG1, and DSG3. Molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of Dinaciclib with FLG and DSG3. Collectively, these findings identify a melanoma-associated desmosomal gene program with prognostic relevance and demonstrate that Dinaciclib treatment modulates the expression of these genes in melanoma cells.
authors: Khan B, Imtiyaz K, Athar A, Nasar MA, Abbasi B, Aslam A, Rizvi MMA.
