title: 3,4-Dimethoxyacetophenone ameliorates epileptogenesis by suppressing BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 expression in a pentylenetetrazole-induced kindling model of epilepsy.
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological condition that affects approximately 50 million individuals worldwide. Current treatments mainly alleviate symptoms and have substantial adverse effects, with about 1/3 of patients not responding to existing medications. This underscores the urgent need for new drugs that can overcome these challenges. According to recent studies, the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) pathway play an important role in epileptogenesis. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and c-fos are also involved in neuronal excitability and seizure-induced neuronal changes. The purpose of the present study was to examine the anticonvulsant and antiepileptogenic activities of 3,4-dimethoxyacetophenone (3,4-DMA) in the acute seizure and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling models of epilepsy and to elucidate related molecular changes of BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 signaling pathways. 3,4-DMA was first evaluated in an acute seizure model, followed by a kindling model of epilepsy in mice. The effects of 3,4-DMA on BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were assessed by quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). The results showed that 3,4-DMA significantly reduced seizure scores in a PTZ-induced kindling model. BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were significantly upregulated in both the cortical and hippocampal tissues in PTZ-control mice. Conversely, treatment with 3,4-DMA attenuated this overexpression in the cortex and hippocampus. In conclusion, 3,4-DMA has antiepileptogenic effect as evidenced by a reduction in the expression of BDNF, c-fos and the JAK-2/STAT-3 pathway components. So, it can be a promising therapeutic candidate in the treatment of epilepsy. However, future studies measuring p-JAK-2 and p-STAT-3 will be required to confirm pathway activation status.
authors: Ali SB, Jamal M, Ayub M, Nisar U, Malhi SM, Faizi S, Simjee SU, Iriti M.

title: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate exacerbates psoriasis-like skin inflammation and is associated with interleukin-17A signaling and S100A9/FABP5 upregulation in keratinocytes.
abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that has been implicated in immune and inflammatory dysregulation, but its potential role in psoriasis-related skin inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we integrated bioinformatics, network toxicology, and machine-learning analyses to identify candidate genes associated with DEHP-exacerbated psoriasis-like inflammation, followed by experimental validation in in vivo and in vitro models. Public transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to screen differentially expressed genes and prioritize key candidates. S100A9 and FABP5 were identified as high-priority genes by machine learning and were further examined in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and in DEHP-treated HaCaT keratinocytes. Our results showed that DEHP exposure exacerbated IMQ-induced psoriasiform skin inflammation in mice and was associated with increased expression of S100A9, FABP5, and IL-17A-related inflammatory markers in mouse skin. In HaCaT cells, DEHP treatment was also associated with increased S100A9/FABP5 expression under the tested conditions. These exploratory findings suggest that DEHP exposure may exacerbate psoriasis-like skin inflammation and is associated with increased keratinocyte S100A9/FABP5 expression and IL-17A-related signaling. Translation to human psoriasis remains uncertain. Further functional studies are needed to clarify the causal role and mechanistic significance of this pathway.
authors: Fan L, Wang J, Wang K, Xue Y, Mai Z, He Z, Huang M, Fang M, Fu Y, Li Y, Liu X, Sun W.

title: Gramine limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
abstract: Alcohol-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ferroptosis-related damage. NADPH oxidase 1 (NOX1), together with its regulatory GTPase Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1 (RAC1), forms a regulatory module that governs redox signaling. Yet small molecules that engage NOX1 and suppress these coupled injury programs remain insufficiently defined. Here, we identified gramine as a candidate NOX1-engaging compound and delineated its protective mechanism in ethanol-associated hepatocellular injury. Alcohol challenge induced a hepatic NOX1/RAC1 response, recapitulated in ethanol-injured hepatocytes. Silencing Nox1 or Rac1 blunted ethanol-driven injury phenotypes, limiting injury-associated enzyme release, reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential disturbance, mitochondrial network disruption, and DNA fragmentation while partially preserving glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Molecular docking predicted a gramine-NOX1 interaction, a cellular thermal shift assay supported target engagement, and cycloheximide chase analysis showed gramine accelerated NOX1 protein turnover. In ethanol-exposed hepatocytes, gramine conferred concentration-associated protection, improving cell viability, and reducing injury-associated enzyme release, lipid droplet signals, and DNA fragmentation. Post-ethanol gramine treatment reduced injury-associated enzyme release. NOX1 overexpression undermined gramine-mediated protection and reinstated ferrous iron accumulation, glutathione redox imbalance, reactive oxygen species production, mitochondrial dysfunction, and damage-associated signaling. Erastin weakened gramine-mediated protection, implicating inhibition of ferroptotic responses in the protective mechanism. In alcohol-gavaged mice, gramine reduced hepatic NOX1 abundance, serum injury markers, Fe2+ levels, lipid accumulation, and lipid peroxidation-associated changes, while preserving GPX4 abundance and limiting histopathological injury. These findings support gramine as a NOX1-engaging small molecule that limits alcohol-associated liver injury by suppressing NOX1-linked ferroptotic responses and mitochondrial dysfunction.
authors: Zhang Y, Su L, Cheng H, Wei W, Xu W, Bao X, Lu C.

title: Withaferin A induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells via ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 axis.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide with a high mortality rate, and conventional chemotherapy faces significant limitations due to drug resistance and severe adverse effects. Natural products represent promising alternative therapeutic agents. In this study, withaferin A (WA), a major bioactive compound derived from Withania somnifera, was investigated for its anticancer activity in GC. We found that WA inhibited the growth and migration of GC cells while inducing both apoptosis and ferroptosis. WA dose-dependently suppressed GC cell proliferation and colony formation. Mechanistically, WA induced apoptosis through ROS accumulation, resulting in mitochondrial depolarization, increased expression of BAX/BAD, and decreased expression of Bcl-2. Meanwhile, WA triggered ferroptosis by promoting ubiquitin-dependent degradation of GPX4, depleting GSH, increasing lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, and activating the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling axis to elevate Fe2⁺ accumulation. Western blotting and transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that WA regulated apoptosis- and ferroptosis-related proteins and activated the Keap1/Nrf2 pathway. In vivo, WA significantly suppressed tumor growth in a xenograft model without causing apparent systemic toxicity, indicating its therapeutic potential for GC treatment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that withaferin A is a potent and promising natural compound that induces apoptosis and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells through ROS-mediated mitochondrial damage and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling pathway, respectively, highlighting its potential as a candidate therapeutic agent for cancer treatment.
authors: Liu Y, Tang Y, Xie D, Zhang Q, Hu Z, Bai L, Feng S.

title: Individualized structural brain network and transcriptomic characterization of heterogeneity in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a heterogeneous metabolic disorder that also affects the brain, yet prior neuroimaging studies have predominantly focused on group-level comparisons, obscuring interindividual variability in brain structural organization. To capture this heterogeneity, we constructed individualized differential structural covariance networks for 156 individuals with T2DM using 148 healthy controls as a normative reference. Unsupervised clustering based on these individualized networks revealed two neuroanatomical subtypes with distinct network configurations. Most subtype-differentiating edges showed higher values in one subtype, whereas a smaller set of edges, primarily involving the basal ganglia and cerebellum, showed higher values in the other. Integration with transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas identified genes spatially associated with subtype-related differences. These genes were enriched in processes including receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and glycerolipid metabolism, with preferential expression in the striatum and cerebellum. Together, these findings characterize interindividual variation in brain structural covariance in T2DM and identify candidate molecular processes associated with the observed subtype differences.
authors: Wang H, Xu J, Wu Y, Du X, Zhang Y, Zhai Y, Zhang Z, Wu Q, Lei M, An Q, Cai W, Peng Y, Liu F, Zhang Q.

title: Sinensetin inhibits choroidal neovascularization by downregulating the MAPK/ERK pathway.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceSinensetin (SIN), a characteristic polymethoxyflavone abundant in Citrus species, is isolated from Citrus peel (Chenpi), a medicinal material widely applied in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) to activate blood circulation and ameliorate blood stasis-associated ocular disorders. Accumulating pharmacological evidence confirms that SIN exerts prominent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic bioactivities. It is capable of suppressing pathological angiogenesis in zebrafish and endothelial cell models, which renders SIN a promising candidate for angiogenic ocular diseases. Nevertheless, its therapeutic efficacy against choroidal neovascularization (CNV) remains largely uninvestigated.Aim of the studyThis study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effects of SIN on CNV and to dissect the underlying mechanism, specifically focusing on its modulation of FGF1-mediated MAPK/ERK signaling.Materials and methodsThe anti-CNV effect of SIN was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo. In vivo, a laser-induced CNV model was established in Brown Norway (BN) rats, and SIN was administered via intravitreal injection; CNV severity was assessed by FITC perfusion, OCT, HE staining, and Western blot. In vitro, human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) were treated with CNV-mimicking ARPE-19 human retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19) conditioned medium; the effects of SIN on migration and angiogenesis were evaluated by scratch, transwell, and tube formation assays. Combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were employed to screen key targets and pathways, and mechanistic validation was performed using the ERK agonist PMA and inhibitor U0126.ResultsIn the laser-induced CNV rat model, intravitreal injection of SIN significantly reduced CNV area and thickness and suppressed the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway, effects that were reversed by the ERK agonist PMA. Consistently, in vitro experiments confirmed that SIN dose-dependently reversed the enhanced migration and tube formation of HUVEC induced by CNV-mimicking conditioned medium. Multi-omics analysis identified FGF1 as a shared candidate downstream mediator of SIN, with SIN downregulating FGF1, VEGF-A, HIF-1α, and p-ERK1/2 expression. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the ERK inhibitor U0126 mimicked the anti-angiogenic effect of SIN, whereas the ERK agonist PMA abolished its inhibitory activity, suggesting that SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling.ConclusionsCollectively, this study demonstrates that citrus-derived SIN exerts anti-CNV effects, at least in part, through suppression of MAPK/ERK signaling, while additional pathways identified by multi-omics may also contribute. These findings highlight SIN as a promising natural product for the treatment of CNV-related ocular diseases, with FGF1 identified as a potential mediator underlying its anti-angiogenic action.
authors: Han GJ, Du Y, Wu XX, He YX, Lu J, Wang WJ, Peng H.

title: Analytical instability and aqueous degradation of carbapenem antibiotics: formation of β-lactam-retaining transformation products.
abstract: Carbapenems are last-resort antibiotics used to treat severe infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. Despite their clinical importance and documented consumption, they remain largely undetected in environmental monitoring studies. This study investigated whether the lack of detection of carbapenems in environmental studies reflects analytical limitations, rapid degradation, or both. Sensitive LC-MS/MS methods were developed for selected carbapenems and used to assess compound stability under analytical and environmentally relevant conditions. All investigated carbapenems exhibited limited stability, with degradation strongly accelerated by methanol. Under environmentally relevant conditions, parent compounds degraded rapidly in river water, biofilm-containing water, and UV-exposed water, with little difference between treatments. High-resolution LC-MS/MS analysis revealed formation of multiple transformation products (TPs) retaining an intact β-lactam ring. Meropenem generated four β-lactam-retaining TPs, and faropenem generated four, several of which remained detectable long after disappearance of the parent compounds. These findings help explain the lack of detection of carbapenems in environmental surveys and demonstrate that disappearance of parent compounds does not necessarily imply elimination of β-lactam-containing structures. The persistence of β-lactam-retaining TPs suggests that environmental exposure and associated selective pressure may persist after parent carbapenems have degraded, highlighting the need for further investigation of their biological activity and potential role in antimicrobial resistance.
authors: Martinez I Quer A, Toussaint A, Jessen E, Kisielius V.

title: Multi-omics reveals evolution from CD7-negative T cell dysregulation to EBV-positive LPD after CD7 CAR-T therapy.
abstract: EBV activation specifically occurs in a subset of patients following CD7 CAR-T therapy, subsequently leading to EBV-positive lymphoproliferative disorder (EBV+ LPD), descriptively referred to as post-CD7 CAR-T lymphoproliferative disorder (PCLD) in this study. To comprehensively characterize PCLD, we employed single-nucleus RNA sequencing, ATAC sequencing, and Stereo-seq to perform multi-omic spatial profiling of PCLD, and compared it with classical post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), EBV-negative diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV- DLBCL) and normal lymph nodes. Infiltrating T cells in PCLD are uniquely characterized by CD7 negativity, exhibiting limited proliferation upon infection stimulation and impaired antiviral activity against EBV. Macrophages are recruited in an attempt to sustain viral clearance; however, the Macro_IDO1 subset emerges as the dominant macrophage population, exhibiting an immunosuppressive phenotype marked by elevated IDO1 expression. Spatially, macrophages, predominantly Macro_IDO1, aggregate to form an immunosuppressive niche that restricts T-cell infiltration and is enriched for inhibitory ligand-receptor interactions, including the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. T-cell function is further compromised, enabling sustained EBV infection of B cells and driving malignant transformation. EBV-driven B cells undergo plasmacytic differentiation and sustained proliferation, actively remodeling the microenvironment. This study provides a comprehensive molecular characterization of lymphoproliferative disorder following CD7 CAR-T therapy, elucidates spatial tumor-immune interactions, mechanisms of EBV-driven B-cell transformation and potential intervention strategies.
authors: Huang M, Jiang Y, Ye F, Yu F, Zhang M, Jiang Y, Fu S, Feng J, An J, Li Y, Zhao H, Wei G, Liu C, Liu L, Huang H, Zhang M, Hu Y.

title: Dissolved organic matter uptake balances carbon budgets of Red Sea bivalves and ascidians.
abstract: Benthic suspension feeders have long been thought to depend solely on particulate organic matter (POM) for their nutritional needs. Our research, conducted in the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), shows that the available concentration of planktonic carbon in the reef water is too low to meet the metabolic demands (measured through in situ oxygen uptake) of common bivalves (Spondylus sp. and Chama pacifica) and ascidians (Polycarpa mytiligera and Halocynthia spinosa). In situ measurements confirmed a concentration-dependent uptake of bulk dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and protein-like dissolved organic compounds (fDOM, analyzed via spectrofluorometry) by Spondylus sp. and P. mytiligera, suggesting that DOC uptake may balance their carbon budgets. Stable isotope (δ13C) mixing models indicate that reef-derived DOC (mean δ13C = -18.4 ± 0.7‰) emerges as the primary carbon source for bivalves (57% of their body composition), far surpassing contributions from particulate sources (26% from POC > 100 µm and 14% from POC < 100 µm). While ascidians still rely primarily on POM (60 to 71%), DOC plays an essential role as a supplementary food source (23 to 29%). These results challenge the prevailing assumption that POM is the exclusive food source for these organisms. Given the widespread presence of bivalves and ascidians in benthic habitats, our findings highlight their ability to bypass the microbial loop and directly utilize dissolved organic compounds, prompting a reevaluation of current benthic carbon budgets.
authors: Diga R, Amit T, Mueller B, Genin A, Carlson CA, Yahel G.

title: Dynamics of TFIIH and Spt4/5 during the transition from transcription initiation to elongation.
abstract: The transition of RNA polymerase II from initiation to elongation requires the timely exchange of many factors. Some initiation factors and elongation factors contact the same RNA polymerase II surfaces in an apparently mutually exclusive manner. For example, space occupied by the initiation factor TFIIH and elongation factor Spt4/5 (also known as DSIF) are predicted to overlap. To determine whether Spt4/5 actively displaces TFIIH, or binds only after TFIIH dissociates, labeled yeast nuclear extracts were combined with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to observe their dynamics in real time. TFIIH categorically dissociates before Spt4/5 arrives, with a clear interval in between when neither factor is present. Therefore, Spt4/5 binding is not required to dissociate TFIIH from RNA polymerase II.
authors: Portman JR, Torrens K, Giordano GG, Jeon J, Chung J, Friedman LJ, Gelles J, Buratowski S.

title: Antigenic landscape of a highly mutated SARS-CoV-2 spike in ongoing viral evolution.
abstract: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme-metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.
authors: Turelli P, Eray E, Raclot C, Trono D, Antanasijevic A.

title: An EjSPT-EjTCP4-EjRR8 Regulatory Module Links Cytokinin Homeostasis and Cell Proliferation to Fruit Growth in Loquat.
abstract: Fruit size is a key determinant of crop yield and commercial value. Here, we investigated fruit development in two loquat cultivars with contrasting fruit sizes. Through hormone quantification, cytological analyses, and transcriptome profiling, we found that cytokinin-related changes were closely associated with loquat fruit-size variation, and further identified EjRR8 as a key regulatory gene. Gain- and loss-of-function analyses indicated that EjRR8 modulates cytokinin accumulation and cell proliferation, thereby contributing to fruit growth. Furthermore, we identified EjSPT and EjTCP4 as upstream transcription factors of EjRR8. Yeast one-hybrid, Dual-Luciferase, and EMSA assays showed that both factors directly bind to the EjRR8 promoter, while functional validation demonstrated that they positively affect cytokinin accumulation. Notably, EjSPT and EjTCP4 physically interacted and synergistically activated EjRR8 expression, forming a regulatory module that links transcriptional control with cytokinin-related responses and cell proliferation. These findings reveal an EjSPT-EjTCP4-EjRR8 module associated with cytokinin accumulation, cell division and fruit-size variation. This study provides a molecular framework for breeding loquat cultivars with larger fruits and offers broader insights into the regulation of fruit development in woody crops.
authors: Deng Y, Zhang K, Yang Z, Liu C, Ding Y, Yao Q, Feng C, Luo X, Zhang H, Wang Y, Deng Q, Li Y.

title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
abstract: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness. In antibody sequencing, it improved recovery of peptides spanning the variable-constant boundary, deamidation calls, and assembly, while preserving recall of hypervariable regions inaccessible to database search. Peptide priors thus bring reference knowledge into DNPS without limiting discovery.
authors: Khan S, Klaproth-Andrade D, Bruns Y, Wilhelm M, Gagneur J.

title: Hepatic stellate cells drive hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-dependent metabolic rewiring and proliferation in hepatocellular carcinoma cells
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most prevalent primary liver cancer in adults and represents the third most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. With limited treatment options, HCC remains a major global health problem. The majority of HCC develops in a cirrhotic liver, where the tumor microenvironment (TME) is enriched in fibroblasts derived from activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Cell-cell interactions in TME play an important role in metabolic reprogramming, which is increasingly recognized as a crucial driver in HCC proliferation. The tumor-promoting and metabolic effects of HSCs on HCC cells however remain incompletely characterized. Understanding how HSC-HCC interaction regulates HCC proliferation can lead to identification of novel therapeutic targets. Here, we established a Transwell co-culture model of HSCs and HCC cells to investigate how HSC-HCC interactions regulate HCC metabolism and proliferation. Using isotope tracing metabolomics, we show that co-culture with HSCs increases proliferation of HCC cells by rewiring glucose metabolism to increase glycolysis and  de novo synthesis of nucleotides. Transcriptomic and immunofluorescence staining analyses revealed that HSCs upregulate hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) signaling in HCC cells, which contributes to metabolic rewiring and HCC proliferation. We further identified H  2 O  2 as a candidate crosstalk signal that could mediate HSC-dependent activation of HIF signaling in HCC cells. Together, these findings reveal a previously overlooked modulatory role of HSC-HCC interaction in metabolism-driven HCC progression. Targeting these pathways may represent a promising strategy to improve HCC treatment.
authors: Rijlaarsdam DJ, Chang J, Helms JB, Zaal EA, Berkers CR.

title: Transcriptional differences between repeatedly recultured and freshly induced embryogenic calli reveal candidate developmental regulators
abstract: Peanut (  Arachis hypogaea L.) is an economically important oilseed and food legume, yet genetic transformation remains challenging because of genotype dependence and the lengthy tissue-culture and regeneration process. A better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying callus development and proliferation could help identify candidate morphogenic genes and developmental regulators (DRs) for peanut improvement. Here, we used RNA sequencing to compare embryogenic calli from the cultivar Georgia Green that had been maintained for three months (new callus; NC) or repeatedly subcultured for four years (old callus; OC). The two callus types displayed distinct morphologies: NC was pale cream, expanded, and cauliflower-like, whereas OC was more yellow, compact, and nodular. We identified 1,141 genes significantly upregulated in NC and 2,086 in OC (adjusted  p  2). Transcription factors were prominent among 13 categories of differentially expressed genes, including members of the AP2/ERF, WOX, GRAS, LBD, and NAC families, several of which are known DRs in other crops. qRT-PCR analysis of seven selected genes strongly corroborated the RNA-seq results (  r = 0.944;  R 2 = 0.891). Highly upregulated candidates included C2H2/BED-type zinc-finger proteins, calreticulin/calnexin, a glycine-rich protein, a late embryogenesis abundant protein, glycoside hydrolases, and SWEET sugar transporters. These findings provide a resource for investigating callus development in peanut and prioritize candidate genes for functional validation and future improvement of transformation and regeneration systems.
authors: Ingole H, Saripalli G, Rustgi S.

title: Nascent transcription profiling identifies H3K36 methylation as a custodian of the somatic transcriptome
abstract: Faithful gene expression not only requires activation of productive transcription units, but also suppression of aberrant initiation within or between gene bodies. In  Saccharomyces , Set2-mediated H3 lysine-36 methylation (H3K36me) recruits a deacetylase complex that removes acetylation deposited behind elongating RNA polymerase II, preventing cryptic initiation. Whether metazoans require Set2 or the K36 residue itself for this function has been difficult to test. Here, we combined PRO-seq, RNA-seq, and chromatin profiling in  Drosophila wing imaginal discs to define individual contributions of Set2, H3.2K36 and H3.3K36 to transcriptome fidelity. Intragenic initiation events are abundant but largely unresponsive to loss of K36 methylation. Aberrant initiation instead concentrates in repetitive, extragenic chromatin, co-marked by H3K9me2/3 and H3K36me2 but depleted of H3K36me3, a dual heterochromatin signature that is also conserved in mammals. Within this compartment, piRNA clusters, germline-restricted genes, and LTR and LINE retrotransposons are aberrantly activated in somatic tissue. A K36R substitution in  H3.2 , but not in  H3.3 , derepresses these loci to a far greater extent than deleting  Set2 , which retains K36me2 but cannot deposit K36me3. Thus, metazoan H3K36 safeguards the somatic transcriptome principally within heterochromatin, rather than within gene bodies.
authors: Sultana H, Vandadi V, Salzler HR, Baluapuri A, Ponkiya D, Hirth AK, Vernesoni GC, Goldman SR, Adelman K, Matera AG.

title: Cervical lymph node B cell subset resists depletion and sustains lytic Epstein Barr-virus signature in patients with multiple sclerosis
abstract: B cells have arisen as key in multiple sclerosis (MS) pathogenesis by the high efficacy of B cell depleting CD20 monoclonal antibodies and by the identification of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) as a prerequisite factor. We previously demonstrated an expansion of memory and double negative (DN) B cells in the deep cervical lymph nodes (dcLNs) of newly diagnosed patients with MS (pwMS), with DN B cells showing a molecular signature consistent with lytic EBV infection. Effect of anti-CD20 therapies for pwMS require sustained administration, which led us to hyhenhesize that incomplete effects on the dcLNs, a natural site for lymphocyte priming towards the central nervous system (CNS), might be sustaining the pathology. Using single-cell transcriptomics and paired sampling, we characterized the effects of anti-CD20 therapies on dcLNs compared to circulation and to other therapies. We observed switched (SM) and unswitched (USM) memory B cells to be depleted uniquely by anti-CD20 in both dcLNs and circulation, whereas DN B cells of the dcLNs were not. Moreover, EBV lytic signature was retained in DN B cells during anti-CD20, and using clonal trajectory we saw that the DN B cells continued to contribute to the plasmablast differentiation within dcLNs. EBV targeting of expanded memory CD8 T cells, as well as CD8 T cell exhaustion, were retained during anti-CD20 therapy within the dcLNs. Our findings suggest a sustained, EBV-driven process in pwMS during anti-CD20 in the CNS-targeting priming dcLNs, with therapeutic implications to be investigated further. One Sentence Summary  Cervical lymph nodes show sustained, EBV-driven pathology in multiple sclerosis during anti-CD20 therapy unseen in peripheral blood.
authors: Babal YK, Sarkkinen J, Ahvenainen E, Susi A, Saarela M, Kurdo G, Laakso SM.

title: World Wide Eyes: Social Media Assisted Wildlife Research. Assessing Supplementary Feeding Areas for Eastern Australian Humpback Whales as a Case Study
abstract: ABSTRACT  Humpback whales typically adopt a “feast-and-famine” strategy, feeding intensively at high-latitude summer feeding grounds while fasting throughout migration. However, increasing reports of feeding at mid-latitudes suggest that some individuals may supplement their energetic requirements along migratory corridors. Detecting and monitoring these emerging behaviours remains challenging because conventional marine mammal surveys are often spatially and financially constrained. Here, we used passive citizen science by systematically compiling humpback whale feeding records from publicly shared Facebook and Instagram posts and the citizen-science platform Happywhale to investigate feeding events of the Eastern Australian population over five consecutive migration seasons (2020– 2024). A total of 256 feeding records were collected, revealing three recurrent candidate Supplementary Feeding Areas (SFAs): the Sapphire Coast (New South Wales), Port Phillip and Bass Strait (Victoria), and southeast Tasmania. Feeding events occurred across multiple migratory months, involved both solitary whales and groups, and included both krill and schooling fish as prey, with lunge feeding representing the predominant feeding strategy. Comparison of passive and active citizen-science sources showed that social-media records substantially increased the number of documented feeding events and more frequently allowed feeding behaviour to be identified. The temporal recurrence of feeding events across five consecutive migration seasons supports the hypothesis that some behaviours traditionally interpreted as opportunistic feeding may instead represent recurrent supplementary feeding. Overall, this study demonstrates the value of passive citizen science as a cost-effective complement to conventional monitoring programmes for detecting large-scale behavioural changes and identifying candidate supplementary feeding areas in migratory humpback whales.
authors: Marzorati G, Valsecchi E.

title: Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection Using CNN-LSTM with Confidence-Aware Automated Pseudo Label Generation
abstract: Abstract  Video anomaly detection in surveillance environments is a challenging problem due to the lack of large-scale frame-level annotations and the high cost of manual labeling. Traditional fully supervised approaches are not scalable in real-world scenarios, while existing weakly supervised methods often rely on noisy bag-level labels and lack fine-grained supervision. In this work, we propose a weakly supervised video anomaly detection framework based on automatically generated pseudo labels. Unlike existing approaches that rely solely on video-level annotations, our method constructs a multi-stage pseudo labeling pipeline that integrates motion-based foreground estimation, object-level detection, and pixel-level segmentation. Specifically, motion regions are first extracted using MOG2 background subtraction. Then YOLOv8 is applied to detect candidate objects in motion-activated frames, followed by SAM-based segmentation to refine object boundaries at pixel level. These signals are fused to generate clip-level pseudo labels with confidence scores. To handle noise in automatically generated labels, we introduce a confidence-aware weighting mechanism and a temporal consistency regularization term. Furthermore, a lightweight CNN-LSTM architecture is employed, where ResNet18 is used as a frozen feature extractor to significantly reduce computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Experimental evaluation on the UCF-Crime dataset demonstrates that the proposed method achieves an AUC of 0.80 and an F1-score of 0.78 under a reproducible multi-run evaluation protocol. The source code and generated pseudo labels will be made publicly available upon publication.
authors: Jalali S, Boostani R.

title: Debriefing and Structured Reflection after Communicative Tasks in Second Language and ESP Learning: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review with VOSviewer Bibliometric Mapping (2000–2026)
abstract: Abstract  Background.  Simulations, role plays, and other communicative tasks are central to second language (L2) and English for Specific Purposes (ESP) teaching. Experiential-learning and simulation theory treat the reflective phase that follows such tasks (debriefing, guided reflection, self-review) as the place where experience becomes learning. No review has yet synthesised what is known about this post-performance phase in L2 learning. Methods.  Following PRISMA 2020, three Boolean queries were run in OpenAlex (2000–2026). A documented rule-based screen produced a bibliometric corpus of 888 records, which was mapped in VOSviewer 1.6.21 through term co-occurrence, overlay, and co-citation analyses. From this corpus, 405 candidates were screened against eligibility criteria for empirical studies in which L2 learners engaged in a structured reflective phase after an oral or interactive task. Included studies were coded for context, design, reflective modality, and outcomes, appraised with an MMAT-informed rubric, and synthesised narratively by modality. Results.  Forty-three studies (46 reports) met the criteria. They used five reflective modalities: structured debriefing (10 studies), post-task transcription (10), guided self-reflection or self-assessment (15), recording-based self-review (9), and peer or multi-source feedback with reflection (13). The most consistent controlled evidence concerned accuracy gains from transcription and guided reflection between task repetitions, although one randomised study found no added benefit. Evidence for structured debriefing of simulations and role plays rested mainly on qualitative, survey, and action-research designs. Only 12 of the 88 corpus records that mentioned debriefing described it as a pedagogical phase after an L2 task. Co-citation analysis showed that the field draws on experiential, task-performance, task-based-pedagogy, and interaction/noticing traditions, but not on the simulation-debriefing literature. Conclusions.  Post-performance reflection in L2 learning is promising, but the evidence is fragmented and methodologically uneven. A five-phase reflective cycle (performance, evidence capture, structured reflection, calibration, and feedforward) is proposed to guide practice and a research agenda that prioritises controlled comparisons of debriefing formats, interactional and professional outcomes, and transparent reporting.
authors: Shokirov BI, Sharipova CA, Kuchkarov BM.

title: Integrated Analysis of Pyroptosis-Energy Metabolism Identifies a Prognostic Immunometabolic Signature in Lung Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract  Background  Pyroptosis and energy-metabolic reprogramming are closely linked to tumor progression and immune dysfunction, but their integrated relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains incompletely defined. We aimed to characterize the pyroptosis–energy metabolism (PEM) landscape of LUAD and identify PEM-associated candidate biomarkers. Methods  TCGA-LUAD and two independent GEO cohorts (GSE31210 and GSE32863) were integrated for transcriptomic analyses. WGCNA, consensus clustering, Cox/LASSO modeling, functional enrichment, regulatory network construction, immune profiling, and gene-level prognostic and diagnostic analyses were performed. Expression of the six signature genes was further assessed by RT–qPCR in 19 paired LUAD and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Results  Twenty-eight PEM module genes were identified, and consensus clustering defined three molecular subtypes with distinct survival outcomes. A six-gene signature comprising ADORA1, CRTAC1, IL1A, PCSK9, TLR2, and TREM2 significantly stratified overall survival in TCGA-LUAD, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs of 0.690, 0.649, and 0.627. High-risk tumors showed lower stromal and immune scores, higher tumor purity and tumor mutation burden, and distinct immune-cell infiltration patterns. RT–qPCR showed significantly lower expression of CRTAC1, IL1A, and PCSK9 in tumor tissues, whereas ADORA1, TLR2, and TREM2 did not differ significantly between paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Conclusion  This study identified a six-gene PEM-related signature associated with overall survival and the tumor immune environment in LUAD. CRTAC1 showed the most consistent evidence across transcriptomic datasets, survival analyses, diagnostic evaluation, and paired clinical tissues, with lower expression in tumors and higher expression associated with better survival. These findings support further investigation of CRTAC1 and the other signature genes as biomarkers related to pyroptosis, energy metabolism, and immune regulation in LUAD.
authors: Luo K, Guo G, Liu H, Huang W, Gao X, Shi Y, Han Y, Han S, Meng M, Zheng B.

title: SeAMT1;2a and SeAMT1;2b from the halophyte Salicornia europaea play dual roles in ammonium transport and salt tolerance
abstract: Abstract    Aims  Ammonium (NH₄⁺) is an essential nitrogen nutrient for plant growth, but excessive NH₄⁺ from fertilizer application and aquaculture wastewater poses eutrophication risks in waterbodies. The halophyte  Salicornia europaea  can efficiently remove NH₄⁺ from wastewater, yet the molecular mechanisms governing its ammonium uptake remain largely elusive. This study aimed to identify and functionally characterize ammonium transporter (AMT) genes in  S. europaea  and to assess their roles in NH₄⁺ uptake and salt tolerance. Methods  We identified six AMT genes—  SeAMT1;1  ,  SeAMT1;2a  ,  SeAMT1;2b  ,  SeAMT1;3  ,  SeAMT1;4  , and  SeAMT3;1  —in  S. europaea  , determined their expression patterns and subcellular localization, and characterized their functions in ammonium transport and salt tolerance using transgenic yeast and Arabidopsis. Results  Among the six AMT genes,  SeAMT1;1  and  SeAMT1;3  were shoot-predominantly expressed genes, whereas  SeAMT1;2a  and  SeAMT1;2b  were root-expressed and transcriptionally induced by both nitrogen starvation and salt stress. Functional analyses revealed that SeAMT1;2a and SeAMT1;2b are the two major AMTs mediating high-affinity and low-affinity ammonium transport in  S. europaea  . Moreover, these two transporters also confer salt tolerance independent of NH₄⁺ uptake, with SeAMT1;2a exhibiting K⁺ transport activity that likely contributes to maintaining cellular K⁺ homeostasis under salinity. Furthermore, the high NH₄⁺ affinity of SeAMT1 transporters, which enables them to function effectively despite Na⁺ competition, allows  S. europaea  to sustain nitrogen acquisition even under highly saline conditions. Conclusions  Our findings provide new insights into SeAMT-mediated ammonium transport and salt tolerance in this halophyte, with promising potential for phytoremediation.
authors: Ma J, Ou Z, Chandrasekaran U, Yao Y, Xiao X.

title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa CntM-Dependent Upregulation of Staphylococcus aureus cntA Enhances Fitness During Co-Infection
abstract: Abstract    Background  Staphylococcus aureus  frequently occurs in polymicrobial infections, but how co-infecting species influence its in vivo fitness requirements remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how  Pseudomonas aeruginosa  affects  S. aureus  fitness during co-infection. Results  We combined murine systemic mono-infection and co-infection models with transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq). Ninety genes met the fitness-gene criteria only during co-infection and were significantly enriched in the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter pathway. Among genes assigned to this pathway,  cntA  , encoding the substrate-binding component of the Cnt metal acquisition system, showed the strongest depletion. Deletion of  cntA  caused no detectable fitness defect during mono-infection but reduced  S. aureus  fitness and tissue burdens during co-infection. In Zn-supplemented chemically defined medium, Δ  cntA  also showed reduced growth relative to the wild-type strain during co-culture with  P. aeruginosa  . Co-culture with  P. aeruginosa  increased  S. aureus cntA  transcription, but co-culture with  Acinetobacter baumannii  or  Klebsiella pneumoniae  did not. Physical separation of  S. aureus  and  P. aeruginosa  in a Transwell system did not prevent the increase in  cntA  transcription, and cell-free co-culture supernatant retained this ability. Deletion of the  P. aeruginosa  pseudopaline biosynthetic gene  cntM  markedly reduced the  P. aeruginosa  -associated increase in  cntA  transcription. Conclusions  We identify  cntA  as a fitness determinant for  S. aureus  during co-infection with  P. aeruginosa  .  P. aeruginosa  upregulates  cntA  transcription through the CntM-dependent pseudopaline biosynthetic pathway, thereby enhancing the fitness of  S. aureus  in the coexistence environment. These findings link metal-acquisition responses to interspecies adaptation during polymicrobial infection and further suggest that this cross-species regulation of metal acquisition may offer a potential therapeutic target for polymicrobial infections.
authors: He T, Zhou J, Li G, Rao Y, Tan Y, Yang Y, Shang W, Peng H, Hu Z, Li M, Zhao Y, Rao X.

title: Where do the gains come from? A component analysis of a spatial-decomposition memetic algorithm for large geometric traveling salesman problems
abstract: Abstract  Geometric traveling salesman problems (TSP) with thousands to hundreds of thousands of points arise in printed circuit board (PCB) drilling and VLSI layouts. We present a hierarchical spatial-decomposition memetic algorithm (HSD-MA) that combines Morton and nearest-neighbor seeding, a Lamarckian evolutionary core with order crossover, a three-tier local search (neighbor-list 2-opt, 2.5-opt node shift and segment-insertion 3-opt over 1-hop and 2-hop Delaunay candidates) and, for more than 5,000 points, a $k$-means decomposition whose clusters are solved in parallel. Distances are computed on the fly, so memory grows linearly with the instance size. We then ask which components matter, using controlled experiments in which all methods share the same compiled local search kernels. On ten instances with 30 runs each, HSD-MA is significantly better than genetic, particle swarm and ant colony hybrids that use 2-opt only, but not better than the same frameworks equipped with the three-tier local search. An iterated local search without population, given the same time per run, finds significantly shorter tours on the four instances with 1,173 or more points and is worse only on the two smallest; with 16 times more generations the difference shrinks but does not reverse. Given the same time, the iterated local search is also better than the decomposition branch on instances with 7,397 and 33,810 points; the decomposition pays off only on the largest instance tested, with 104,814 points. Seeding and the kick have no significant effect, and nearest-neighbor candidates work as well as Delaunay candidates, so the gains over 2-opt-based memetic algorithms come from the local search, not from the population. HSD-MA solves all 102 Waterloo VLSI instances, up to 744,710 points, with a mean gap of $5.88\%$ on the 25 largest and a peak working set of 0.9 to 1.2~GiB on the largest. LKH-3, run on the same machine, finds much better tours in every configuration we tested, and GA-EAX does so on the small instances given a few seconds; the only advantage of HSD-MA is that it needs a third to a fifth of the wall-clock time of the quickest LKH-3 configuration on large instances. In a simulated drilling case study, HSD-MA shortens the cycle time by less than $1\%$ relative to a nearest-neighbor tour improved by 2-opt.
authors: Vu M.

title: Single-Cell Dissection of Microglial Dysfunction in Diabetes-Associated Neurodegenerative Vulnerability.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms linking type 2 diabetes to increased neurodegenerative risk remain poorly defined. Given the critical involvement of microglial dysfunction in neurodegeneration, we constructed a temporal single-cell atlas integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles of microglia from diabetic (db/db) and control (db/m) mice across the lifespan. We delineated a nonlinear, diabetes-specific pathological trajectory characterized by early inflammatory activation, a mid-stage inflection in neurodegeneration-associated signaling and metabolic stress, and late-stage dysfunction. Chromatin accessibility profiling revealed early and persistent epigenomic priming of neurodegeneration-associated pathways, accompanied by stage-specific enhancer rewiring. Pseudotime analysis identified a disease-associated microglial (DAM) state as a candidate transition node, characterized by biased polarization and accelerated maturation under diabetic conditions. Targeted validation using freshly isolated microglia and primary microglial cultures further supported the early expansion of the DAM population, a bias toward homeostatic-to-DAM activation, and Arhgap15-dependent regulation of phagocytic activity. Together, these findings identify microglial states and candidate regulatory pathways that may link diabetes to neurodegenerative vulnerability.
authors: Zhang J, Yau TK, Tse J, Li TH, Hu D, Zhao YJ, Chan TF.

title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra-ortho-Substituted Dibenz[c,e]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase.
abstract: Atropisomeric dibenz[c,e]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium-sized ring. Tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter- and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure-guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED-04-M3) that delivers various tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram-scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.
authors: Zhou Z, Yan Y, Fan S, Yao Z, Wang W, Li K, Qiao T, Huang L, Yang Z, Fu H.

title: 4'-Hydroxywogonin Attenuates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Suppressing Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT Signaling.
abstract: 4'-Hydroxywogonin, a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanism in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-tumor effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin and its regulatory role in Gas6/Axl-associated signaling. Human HCC cells were used to evaluate proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, senescence, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, molecular docking, and thermal shift analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanism, and antitumor efficacy and safety were further examined in a mouse xenograft model. 4'-Hydroxywogonin significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing G1-phase arrest, apoptosis, and senescence. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses identified Axl as a key affected target. 4'-Hydroxywogonin reduced Gas6 and Axl expression, suppressed PI3K/AKT activation, and downregulated cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between 4'-hydroxywogonin and Axl, which was supported by thermal shift analysis. Axl overexpression partially rescued the inhibitory effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin, suggesting involvement of Axl-dependent and additional pathways. In vivo, 4'-hydroxywogonin markedly reduced tumor growth with efficacy comparable to sorafenib and without evident hepatotoxicity. These findings indicate that 4'-hydroxywogonin suppresses HCC progression, at least in part, through inhibition of the Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, supporting its further development as a natural therapeutic candidate.
authors: Chen CY, Chen CC, Yeh CT, Chan CW, Chu YD, Leu YL, Satange RB, Chou LF, Chuang WY, Hsueh C, Shieh TM, Wang TH.

title: Time-to-transformation transcriptomic modeling identifies oral squamous cell carcinoma-initiation and SPP1-integrin niche programs in oral leukoplakia.
abstract: Oral leukoplakia and other oral potentially malignant disorders carry heterogeneous risks of subsequent oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), whereas conventional clinicopathological factors have limited ability to discriminate individual risk and event timing. We developed a time-to-transformation transcriptomic score (TT-score) in the longitudinal GSE26549 cohort, including 86 participants and 35 subsequent oral-cancer events. A 12-gene TT-score was derived using multimethod feature selection and Cox-GLMNET modeling, and the full development pipeline was evaluated by 20 repeated five-fold nested cross-validations. Strict internal validation yielded a mean out-of-fold C-index of 0.740 (95% confidence interval, 0.679-0.801), with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUCs) of 0.731, 0.771, and 0.811 at 2-, 3-, and 5-yr, respectively. Full-pipeline outcome permutation analysis supported the non-random nature of the observed risk-ranking signal. Across external progression-axis cohorts, direct stage associations of the fixed TT-score were cohort-dependent, whereas TT-score-related epithelial proliferation, invasion, hypoxia/metabolic, OSCC-initiation-like, and SPP1-related microenvironmental programs showed more consistent stage-associated trends. Single-cell analyses and published spatial-atlas signatures further contextualized these programs. Overall, the TT-score captured a transcriptomic risk state associated with the timing of subsequent oral cancer and provides a candidate framework for independent longitudinal validation and targeted assay development.
authors: Guo Z, Shi Y, Zhang X, Wu Q.

title: Exploring Barriers, Facilitators, and Strategies for the Etiological Management of Sexually Transmitted Infections in Brazil: A Qualitative Study Using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).
abstract: BackgroundIn Brazil, syndromic management remains the standard approach for male urethral discharge despite the growing need for etiological diagnosis. This study explored barriers, facilitators, and implementation strategies for adopting the etiological approach using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).MethodsA qualitative study was conducted through semi-structured online interviews with health professionals. Interview transcripts were analyzed deductively using the CFIR Codebook and inductively to identify emerging themes.ResultsFrom March to April 2023, 15 professionals from all Brazilian regions were interviewed: five clinicians, five laboratory professionals, and five public health managers. Major barriers for implementing the etiological approach included limited systematic epidemiological data, the absence of rapid immunochromatographic STI tests, limited workforce capacity, and high staff turnover. Key facilitators were timely diagnosis and treatment of asymptomatic infections, targeted therapy based on pathogen identification, and antimicrobial resistance surveillance through biological sample collection. Proposed strategies involved phased introduction, with both approaches initially coexisting: syndromic treatment for symptomatic cases with sample collection to identify the causative agent, discussion of results during follow-up consultations, and screening of asymptomatic cases. Additionally, interviewees recommended mandatory STI notification for standardized data generation, awareness raising, and public policy planning. They also emphasized the need for national meetings on STIs beyond syphilis, HIV, and viral hepatitis.ConclusionsAlthough the syndromic approach remains necessary in Brazil, health professionals demonstrated readiness to implement the etiological approach and identified practical strategies to support its integration into STI prevention and control programs.

title: Supraoptimal Mycorrhizal Colonisation Elicits Defence and Depletes Rhizosphere Inhabiting Massilia in Mild Salt‑Stressed Maize: A Split‑Root Comparison of Locally Colonised Roots.
abstract: Environmental conditions, such as light availability, affect the growth‑promoting effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis. However, how the root‑rhizosphere continuum responds when mycorrhizal structures become unsuitable due to environmental deterioration remains unresolved. Using a split‑root system under mild salinity and low light, we generated two AM colonisation states (moderate and supraoptimal) and focused on roots with similar colonisation rates to compare local responses under different whole‑plant symbiotic backgrounds. Supraoptimal colonisation reduced the mycorrhizal growth response compared with moderate colonisation, and this reduction was uncoupled from ion homoeostasis. Root transcriptomics and rhizosphere exudates revealed that supraoptimal colonisation induced jasmonate/ethylene‑mediated defence responses, downregulated carbon transporter genes, and shifted exudation from symbiosis‑supporting lipids/terpenoids toward defence‑related amino acid derivatives. Consequently, supraoptimal colonisation reduced beneficial bacteria, notably Massilia, and simplified co‑occurrence networks. We propose a model in which salt stress and low light drive a host‑mediated "defence‑symbiosis" trade‑off, reducing the mycorrhizal growth response under supraoptimal AM colonisation. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for optimising AM applications in saline systems.
authors: Wang C, Zheng G, Chen Y, Zhang L, Li X, Ning P, Quan M, Wang D, Xie Z.

title: A BmMYB14-UGT Regulatory Module Contributes to Dammarane-Type Triterpene Biosynthesis in Bacopa monnieri.
abstract: Bacosides, a key glycosylated dammarane-type triterpenes of Bacopa monnieri, exhibit diverse pharmacological activities, yet the enzymatic and regulatory mechanisms governing their biosynthesis remain underexplored. In this study, we functionally characterized the methyl jasmonate-inducible glycosyltransferase UGT94AV1 and demonstrated its ability to glycosylate diverse triterpenoid substrates, with the highest catalytic efficiency observed for ginsenoside RH2. Recombinant UGT94AV1 demonstrated a capacity for sequential glycosylation by efficiently catalyzing the transfer of a glucose moiety to the aglycone core, i.e., jujubogenin and pseudojujubogenin, derived from the periodate oxidation of bacoside A, and its corresponding monoglycosides. Overexpression of UGT94AV1 in B. monnieri enhanced the accumulation of jujubogenin-derived bacosides, while its knockdown reduced their levels. Further, transcriptome analysis has identified BmMYB14 co-expressing with UGT94AV1 and the previously characterized UGT79A18. Overexpression of BmMYB14 significantly upregulated UGT79A18 and UGT94AV1, whereas silencing of BmMYB14 markedly reduced their transcript levels. The expressions of UGT94AV1 and UGT79A18 in BmMYB14 OE and KD lines were consistent with enhanced accumulation of bacosides in OE lines and reduced in KD lines. Yeast one-hybrid and dual-luciferase assays using the promoter regions of UGT94AV1 and UGT79A18 further demonstrate that BmMYB14 transcriptionally regulates UGT79A18 and UGT94AV1, and hence contributes to the dammarane-type triterpene biosynthesis in Bacopa monnieri.
authors: Kumar S, Singh N, Joshi A, Pandey DK, Lahane V, Upadhyay R, Yadav AK, Pandey R, Tyagi S, Shukla RK.

title: HHV-6 Encephalitis Presenting With Severe SIADH and CO₂ Narcosis in Non-Transplant Smoldering Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) encephalitis is best recognized after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation but can also occur in non-transplant immunocompromised patients. Hyponatremia and syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) may precede or accompany HHV-6 encephalitis. Severe SIADH as an early dominant clue in non-transplant patients with smoldering adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) is not fully described. CASE REPORT A 55-year-old woman with smoldering ATLL received systemic corticosteroid therapy for clinically diagnosed human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1)-associated uveitis and was admitted for progressive pulmonary infection. Bronchoscopic specimens revealed polymicrobial infection, including Nocardia and Actinomyces; invasive pulmonary aspergillosis was also clinically suspected. Although pulmonary findings improved with antimicrobial and antifungal therapy, she developed nausea, acute impairment of consciousness, and severe SIADH-associated hyponatremia. Serum sodium decreased to 113 mmol/L, and consciousness did not adequately improve after sodium correction. Cerebrospinal fluid obtained by lumbar puncture on hospital day 13 showed HHV-6 DNA positivity (1.0×10³ copies/mL). Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral cortical and limbic abnormalities, supporting a clinical diagnosis of HHV-6 encephalitis. Ganciclovir was initiated on hospital day 15 along with sodium correction, tolvaptan, and supportive care. The patient subsequently developed hypercapnic respiratory failure and CO₂ narcosis requiring mechanical ventilation. Her neurologic and respiratory status gradually improved, and she was discharged on hospital day 53. CONCLUSIONS In non-transplant patients with ATLL, corticosteroid exposure, and opportunistic infection, severe SIADH accompanied by new neurologic symptoms can be an early clue to HHV-6 encephalitis. Early recognition and prompt initiation of antiviral therapy may help to improve neurologic outcomes.
journal: The American journal of case reports
authors: Tateishi K, Yanagihara T, Kawabata R, Kinoshita E, Miyazaki T, Tateishi Y, Koga K, Hamasaki M, Fujita M.

title: Synergistic induction of apoptosis in human prostate cancer PC3 cells by silver-coated cerium oxide nanoparticles: unveiling the role of ROS-mediated p53-associated apoptotic signaling and antioxidant system depletion.
abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) represents a formidable clinical challenge due to intrinsic defects in apoptotic execution, elevated baseline antioxidant capacity, and rapid resistance to standard chemotherapy. Herein, we report the rational design, template-directed synthesis, and antineoplastic evaluation of silver-coated cerium oxide core-shell nanoparticles (Ag@CeO2 NPs) derived from a cerium-based metal-organic framework (Ce-UiO-66) for targeted intervention in androgen-independent prostate carcinoma. Uniform Ce-UiO-66 MOF nanoparticles were thermally converted via controlled calcination (550 °C, 3 h) into porous cubic fluorite nanoceria (CeO₂) cores, followed by in situ surface nucleation and reduction of a metallic silver (Ag⁰) nanoshell stabilized by polyvinylpyrrolidone. The physicochemical properties were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, FESEM, EDX mapping, DLS, and Zeta potential analysis. In vitro anticancer efficacy was evaluated in human androgen-independent PC-3 prostate cancer cells and normal human fibroblasts (HFF-1). Cellular viability, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) enzymatic kinetics, apoptosis-related transcriptomics (p53, Bax, Bcl-2 via qRT-PCR), and p53 protein levels (ELISA) were systematically quantified. PXRD and Scherrer analysis confirmed the formation of pure, face-centered cubic fluorite CeO₂ (Cerianite-(Ce), Fm3̄m, *a* = 5.4110 Å) with an average primary crystallite size of 7.27 ± 0.36 nm (7.44 nm for the (111) reflection), alongside characteristic reflections of metallic Ag. FESEM, DLS, and electrophoretic measurements revealed spherical, cauliflower-like hierarchical clusters with a hydrodynamic diameter (Z-average) of 111.68 nm, narrow polydispersity (PDI = 0.2860), and stable negative surface charge (ζ = - 14.96 mV). The Ag@CeO2 NPs displayed pronounced, tumor-selective cytotoxicity, yielding an IC₅₀ of 32.14 µg/mL against PC-3 cells while sparing normal HFF-1 fibroblasts (IC₅₀ = 171.6 µg/mL, > 5.3-fold selectivity window). Mechanistically, the nanocomposite triggered a severe, concentration-dependent intracellular ROS burst (*p* < 0.0001 at 30 µM) accompanied by the functional collapse of the cellular antioxidant barrier through profound suppression of SOD (*p* < 0.01) and CAT (*p* < 0.0001) activities. This unmitigated oxidative crisis was associated with increased TP53 transcript levels and increased p53-associated protein signals as measured by ELISA (*p* < 0.0001), which coincided with upregulated Bax, downregulated Bcl-2, and elevated the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio (*p* < 0.001), consistent with activation of mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. Ag@CeO2 NPs function as a potent, tumor-selective pro-oxidant nanotherapeutic platform capable of overriding endogenous antioxidant defenses, enhancing p53-associated apoptotic signaling and promoting mitochondrial apoptotic responses, suggesting that Ag@CeO2 NPs may serve as a potential candidate for further investigation in prostate cancer nanomedicine.
authors: Al-Awassi H, AlAbdulhadi SAS, Aslam A, AlMoshary M, Alrefaei GI, Al-Qahtani SA, Barnawi J.

title: Synergistic regulation of temperature and primary knock-on atom energy on irradiation damage evolution in tantalum: a molecular dynamics study.
abstract: Tantalum is a candidate material for advanced nuclear systems, but its irradiation damage mechanisms remain unclear. Using molecular dynamics with the UNEP-v1-Ziegler Biersack Littmark machine-learning potential, we simulated body-centered cubic Ta under 1-50 keV PKA irradiation at 300-900 K. Results show that threshold displacement energy decreases with temperature and exhibits anisotropy. Defect evolution displays strong energy-temperature coupling: low-energy cascades (⩽5 keV) follow monotonic displacement chain behavior, while high-energy cascades (⩾15 keV) are governed by competition between thermal spike formation and energy dissipation. Interstitial clusters outnumber vacancy clusters due to low migration energy and 〈111〉 diffusion. Cascade morphology controls final damage accumulation by modulating defect spatial distribution. These atomic-scale insights provide theoretical foundations for accurate damage modeling and radiation-resistant material design.
journal: Journal of physics. Condensed matter : an Institute of Physics journal
authors: Wang K, Teng J, Zhang L, Wang S, Jia X, Cheng H, Qian P.

title: Molecular Detection Tools for the Powdery Mildew Genus Podosphaera.
abstract: Powdery mildews are caused by obligate biotrophic fungi that pose a significant threat to a broad range of economically important crops across a diverse range of plant families. However, conventional morphological characterization and PCR-based identification using the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region often lack the resolution necessary to differentiate closely related species within Erysiphaceae, limiting the precision of current diagnostic approaches. In this study, we developed species-specific TaqMan quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) assays targeting the nuclear gene glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) to detect Podosphaera shepherdiae (North American strawberry powdery mildew) and P. leucotricha (apple powdery mildew) in environmental samples. To evaluate assay specificity, powdery mildew specimens representing multiple genera were collected between 2020 and 2024 from diverse hosts across Michigan, California, New York, Oregon, and Washington (U.S.A.) and were sequenced. The qPCR assays exhibited high specificity and sensitivity, with detection limits of 10 pg of DNA and 100 gene copies for P. shepherdiae, and 5 pg of DNA and 10 gene copies for P. leucotricha, with no cross-reactivity with other collected powdery mildew species. Application of the P. shepherdiae assay to a Fragaria × ananassa 'Annapolis' infection time course confirmed consistent detection at both early (5 days postinoculation) and later stages of infection. In silico TaqMan qPCR assays for additional powdery mildew taxa were developed using GAPDH sequences obtained from a broad panel of genera within the family Erysiphaceae. Additionally, we document four novel host-pathogen associations that are being reported globally for the first time. These assays provide a robust molecular toolset for early detection and monitoring of powdery mildew fungi, supporting improved management, enabling accurate species identification, and advancing species-specific diagnostics within the Erysiphaceae.
authors: Thompson SR, Bradshaw M, Naegele RP, Miles LA, Miles TD.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis with Interpretable Machine Learning Prioritizes Candidate Biomarkers for Bladder Cancer.
abstract: IntroductionBladder cancer is the most prevalent malignancy of the urinary tract. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers for bladder cancer through an integrated multi-omics analysis.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and proteomic datasets were analyzed to characterize cellular populations and identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and proteins (DEPs). Candidate genes were prioritized using four machinelearning algorithms, with model interpretation performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was conducted to explore associated pathways, whereas Enrichr/DSigDB enrichment and molecular docking were performed to investigate potential therapeutic compounds and compound-gene interactions. A five-gene SVM model was externally validated in the independent bulk transcriptomic cohort GSE13507. The expression levels of the candidate genes were further evaluated in bladder cancer cell lines.ResultsFifteen major cell populations were identified. Exploratory analyses highlighted endothelial perivascular stromal cells and inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts as cell populations of interest, with predicted intercellular communication patterns suggesting potential roles in the bladder cancer microenvironment. Moreover, 7 genes/proteins showed concordant upregulation and 122 downregulation across all three datasets, and these candidates were subsequently subjected to machine- learning analysis. CFD, WNT2B, MAPK13, ABLIM1, and PRKAR2B were prioritized as five candidate genes for bladder cancer, and their expression patterns and potentially associated pathways were further evaluated in bladder cancer samples and cell lines. Among the four evaluated algorithms, SVM demonstrated the highest reported internal holdout-set AUC of 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and was selected for SHAP interpretation. In the independent GSE13507 cohort, the five-gene SVM model achieved an AUC of 0.815 (95% CI: 0.752-0.877). Molecular docking suggested potential interaction poses between Rifaximin and CFD, and between MAPK13 and NG- 25/XMD13-2.DiscussionThe integration of multi-omics data with an interpretable SHAP-based model provides an exploratory framework for prioritizing candidate bladder cancer biomarkers and generating hypotheses for subsequent biological and clinical validation.ConclusionThis multi-omics study identified candidate biomarkers and exploratory compoundgene associations for bladder cancer. These findings require validation in additional independent multicenter cohorts and functional studies before clinical application.
authors: Guan H, Liu X, Hong T, Li H, Liu G, Zhang Y, Hong X.

title: Neuroprotective Effects of Natural Products: Innovative Therapeutic Strategies for Preventing the Progression of Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders are serious conditions characterized by progressive neuronal degeneration, which leads to cognitive decline, motor dysfunction, and other neurological problems, severely impairing daily activities and quality of life. These diseases involve multiple biological pathways, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and abnormal protein folding. Given the multifactorial nature of neurodegenerative diseases, neuroprotective approaches targeting multiple mechanisms hold great promise for prevention and treatment. Natural products derived from plants, microorganisms, and marine organisms are renowned for their excellent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities and show great potential in preventing neurodegenerative diseases. Unlike synthetic compounds, these naturally sourced bioactive compounds offer a variety of therapeutic targets due to their diverse structures and biological activities. This review provides a systematic overview of 125 newly identified neuroprotective natural products derived from plants, microorganisms, and marine organisms in 2025, with a comprehensive summary of their origins, chemical architectures, and biological activities. These collected natural products are categorized into seven classes based on their structural features: terpenoids (42.4%, 53/125), alkaloids (19.2%, 24/125), glycosides (10.4%, 13/125), lignans (9.6%, 12/125), phenols (6.4%, 8/125), flavonoids (6.4%, 8/125), and other miscellaneous compounds (5.6%, 7/125). Accumulating evidence indicates that natural products hold great promising potential for preventing and slowing the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.
authors: Zou Y, Gong C, Pan C.

title: Integrative bioinformatics, single-cell, and machine learning analyses identify OIP5-AS1 as a pro-oncogenic ceRNA hub in gastric cancer.
abstract: Despite advances in treatment, gastric cancer prognosis remains poor, necessitating the discovery of reliable molecular biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study investigates the long non-coding RNA OIP5-AS1 as a candidate oncogenic regulator through an integrated strategy combining bioinformatics, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, and experimental assays. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed substantial intratumoral heterogeneity across tumor layers, while integrative network analysis and machine learning prioritized OIP5-AS1 as a potential regulatory hub associated with disease progression, characterized by putative interactions with miR-20a-5p and downstream dysregulation of targets such as ZBTB4. Additional model-level prognostic contributions were observed for miR-155-5p and PTEN, although these were not included in the proposed ceRNA axis. The machine learning models further supported the discriminatory and prognostic relevance of OIP5-AS1-related features, and examination of a 30-patient clinical cohort confirmed its significant, grade-dependent overexpression in tumor tissues. Functional experiments in AGS gastric adenocarcinoma cells demonstrated that siRNA-mediated silencing of OIP5-AS1 effectively induces apoptosis, evidenced by altered BAX/BCL2 ratios and flow cytometry, while simultaneously inhibiting cancer cell migration. Collectively, these findings position OIP5-AS1 as a candidate oncogenic regulator and putative ceRNA hub in gastric cancer pathogenesis, highlighting its potential utility as a candidate prognostic biomarker and a promising avenue for targeted therapeutic intervention. However, definitive clinical utility and direct molecular binding require further validation.
authors: Askari N, Shafieipour S, Hadizadeh M.

title: The "Invisible Killer" of Neurodegeneration: Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Neurodegenerative Disorders, Mechanisms, Emerging Pathways and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease (PD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), Huntington's disease (HD), multiple sclerosis (MS), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) place substantial burden on global public health. Mounting evidence identifies mitochondrial dysfunction as a central contributor to neuronal damage and progressive brain functional decline. As a narrative review, this work aims to dissect mitochondrial‑associated pathological features across these major neurodegenerative disorders, summarize under‑recognized emerging mechanisms, and highlight translational bottlenecks for mitochondrial‑targeted therapies. Mitochondria sustain neuronal survival by mediating oxidative‑phosphorylation‑driven energy production, biomolecule biosynthesis, calcium homeostasis, reactive oxygen species (ROS) metabolism, and apoptotic regulation. In PD, aggregated α‑synuclein (α‑syn) damages respiratory‑chain complex I, perturbs mitochondrial dynamics and blocks PINK1/Parkin‑dependent mitophagy. In AD, amyloid‑β together with hyper‑phosphorylated tau (p-Tau) impairs respiratory complex activity, axonal mitochondrial trafficking and mitophagic clearance. Mutant huntingtin induces multiple mitochondrial lesions in HD, while inflammation‑triggered oxidative stress secondarily compromises mitochondrial function in MS. Pathogenic mutations in ALS disrupt respiratory‑chain assembly, mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy. Beyond classic mitochondrial defects including respiratory‑chain impairment, dynamic imbalance and defective mitophagy, emerging mechanisms such as mitocytosis, mitochondrial aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetase (mt‑aaRS) dysfunction and mitochondria‑associated membrane (MAM) disruption are discussed. Mitochondrial dysfunction drives neurodegeneration via energy exhaustion, aggravated oxidative stress, pathological protein aggregation and excessive neuronal apoptosis. We further recapitulate mitochondrial‑oriented therapeutic approaches including small‑molecule regulators, mitophagy activators, mitochondrial biogenesis promoters, gene‑editing strategies and mitochondrial transplantation. Notable translational obstacles remain, including limited blood‑brain‑barrier penetration of candidate drugs, narrow therapeutic time‑window post‑symptom onset, and prominent disease heterogeneity. By synthesizing basic experimental findings and pre‑clinical and clinical trial progress, this review provides updated insights into the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases and facilitates the development of precise mitochondrial‑targeted therapeutic regimens.
authors: Cao S, Liu T, Cheng X, Tian X, Wei J.

title: Aptamers in Brucellosis: Diagnostic Advances, Current Challenges and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Brucellosis, caused by Brucella species, is a major zoonosis with global health and economic burdens. Conventional diagnostics suffer from slow culture, biosafety risks, cross-reactivity, and equipment dependence. Aptamers, synthetic single-stranded oligonucleotides selected via Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX), offer promising alternatives to antibodies. This review focuses primarily on recent advances in aptamer-based diagnostic technologies for brucellosis. The success of Brucella-specific aptamers is largely attributed to the development of whole-cell-based SELEX strategies and counter-selection against non-target bacteria, which help overcome the complexity of the Brucella outer membrane and improve target specificity. Brucella-specific aptamers such as B20 (KD = 40.179 pM), B21 (KD = 184.396 pM), and WS-6 (KD = 16.23 nM) exhibit high affinity and specificity. Integrated into biosensors, they enable detection limits as low as 1.5×101 CFU/mL (colorimetric) and 27 cells/mL (surface plasmon resonance). While aptamer-nanoparticle conjugates also show therapeutic potential against intracellular infections via immun4omodulation, this aspect remains secondary and requires further validation, and toxicity concerns remain. Despite progress, clinical validation, matrix interference, and regulatory hurdles persist. Future directions include multi-target aptamers, nanomaterial integration, and point-of-care translation. This review underscores the central role of aptamers in brucellosis diagnosis, with complementary therapeutic potential.
