title: Dynamic changes in volatile profiles of fu brick tea during storage and a predictive model for aging year.
abstract: This study investigated the dynamic evolution of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in Jingyang Fu brick tea during storage. Using GC-IMS and HS-SPME-GC-MS, we characterized the VOC profiles, identifying 291 volatiles, among which 36 key compounds (including α-ionone, trans-β-ionone, and methyl salicylate) were pinpointed as responsible for the distinctive fungal-floral aroma that intensified with storage time. Sensory evaluation revealed a progressive shift from fresh to mellow fungal and aged characteristics. Key fungal-floral compounds exhibited synchronous variations with processing-derived metallic elements. Based on the identified VOCs, we developed the first predictive model for determining storage year using machine learning (PLSR and SVM). The model achieved a classification accuracy of 0.889 and high regression precision (R2 > 0.87). This work provides fundamental insights into the aroma evolution of Fu brick tea during aging and offers a robust tool for quality control.
authors: Wang Y, Zhang S, Sun X, Zhou B, Zhang J, Yang M, Ma D, Zhang G, Wu T, Yuan Y, Feng K, Yue T.

title: A temporal coupling hypothesis for chemoresistance in canine DLBCL and osteosarcoma: stress signalling and microRNA regulation.
abstract: Acquired chemoresistance remains a major clinical problem in canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and osteosarcoma. Existing canine studies identify established resistance-associated features, including drug efflux, altered apoptosis, DNA repair, epigenetic change, and microRNA (miRNA) dysregulation, and support selected stress-response components as biologically relevant. However, the available canine evidence does not establish a chemotherapy-induced temporal sequence linking early stress signalling to later miRNA regulation. Likewise, the YAP-DDX17-Microprocessor relationship is supported by mechanistic evidence from mammalian/human systems but has not been demonstrated as a chemotherapy-induced coupling mechanism in canine tumours. This Opinion Paper therefore presents a testable temporal coupling hypothesis rather than a validated canine mechanism. The hypothesis asks whether early treatment-induced stress responses reproducibly precede and are associated with later miRNA regulation, and whether any such relationship reflects mechanistic dependence. YAP-DDX17-Microprocessor is considered one experimentally tractable but unvalidated candidate bridge, not a required component of the broader hypothesis. The article distinguishes established canine evidence from cross-species evidence and theoretical inference, and outlines the longitudinal and perturbational studies needed to test the hypothesis while accounting for pharmacokinetics, miRNA biogenesis, and tumour-microenvironment effects before clinical translation.
authors: Akbari-Ardabili S.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.
authors: Liu H, Li X, Li M, Jiu J, Zhao Y, Li D, Zhang J, Yan L, Li S, Li R, Du G, Li JJ, Du Y, Liu W, Zhao B, Wang B.

title: Integrated metabolomic characterization of refrigerated storage stability and aroma development in a Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP-315-fermented milk beverage.
abstract: Metabolic changes associated with quality stability and flavor evolution in refrigerated live-culture fermented milk beverages remain poorly characterized. In this study, a live-culture fermented milk beverage produced using Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LP-315 (LP-315) was evaluated during fermentation and 21 days of storage at 4 °C using physicochemical, sensory, and metabolomic analyses. It showed limited post-acidification, retained viable counts above 107 CFU/mL on day 21, and maintained favorable sensory quality throughout storage. Temporally varying non-volatile metabolites predominantly comprised amino acids, carbohydrates, and organic acids, mapping mainly to arginine and proline metabolism, galactose metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Among 52 temporally varying volatile metabolites, ethyl nonanoate, acetylfuran, and furanones increased transiently during early storage. Integrated analyses associated carbohydrate utilization, amino acid conversion, organic acid metabolism, and lipid-derived compound transformations with flavor and quality trajectories. These findings support LP-315 as a candidate starter for live-culture fermented milk beverages with favorable stability during refrigeration.
authors: Jiao Y, Liu L, Yuan J, Wang J, Chen Y, Zha M.

title: Identification of mitophagy-related genes with diagnostic value in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis using bioinformatics analysis.
abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. We integrated GEO transcriptomic datasets to identify 839 differentially expressed genes and 33 differential mitophagy-related genes via differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Machine learning identified six candidate diagnostic biomarkers, SLIRP, BLVRB, ATP6V1F, COX5B, TMEM14A, and TRMT112, with moderate-to-good discriminatory capacity across cohorts. xCell analysis revealed extensive renal immune remodeling in FSGS with expanded pro-inflammatory cells, diminished naive T cells and Tregs, and tight correlations between hub genes and immune profiles. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis suggested a trend of downregulation of hub genes in FSGS podocytes, alongside suppressed transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial energy metabolism and mitophagy-related pathways. qRT-PCR and western blot validated their downregulation at the whole-renal-tissue level in FSGS mouse models. These six genes may serve as diagnostic candidates and provide research clues for exploring mitophagy mechanisms in FSGS.
authors: Ma J, Ma T, Zhang Y, Wei H.

title: LCK regulates apoptosis and intercellular communication networks in neuroblastoma.
abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most common solid malignancy of childhood with poor prognosis in high-risk patients. The tumor microenvironment, particularly the metastatic bone marrow niche, plays a critical role in disease progression. Lymphocyte-specific protein tyrosine kinase (LCK) is essential for T cell function and implicated in apoptosis induction by anticancer drugs, yet its role in neuroblastoma remains unclear. This study investigated LCK expression changes in neuroblastoma cells following doxorubicin treatment, examined molecular interactions between LCK and doxorubicin, and elucidated LCK's role in the tumor immune microenvironment. Differential LCK expression was analyzed across control, non-metastatic and metastatic neuroblastoma samples using single-cell transcriptomics. CellChat framework mapped immune cell interaction networks. LCK expression was evaluated before and after doxorubicin treatment, and molecular docking assessed direct binding between LCK and doxorubicin. CellChat revealed significantly altered communication between T cells and hematopoietic progenitors in metastatic samples, with increased interactions associated with LCK-expressing cells. Molecular docking suggested a potential interaction between doxorubicin and the LCK kinase domain. Chromosomal localization of LCK at 1p32-35, frequently deleted in aggressive neuroblastomas, underscores its clinical relevance. LCK expression changes were associated with doxorubicin response and apoptosis-related transcriptional changes. These findings suggest LCK as a candidate biomarker for predicting treatment response and a potential target for further investigation in neuroblastoma. Experimental validation is required to establish the functional role of LCK in this context.
authors: Tafazoli A, Askari N, Jafarinejad Farsangi S.

title: Emerging concepts in the diagnosis and treatment of fracture-related infections.
abstract: Fracture-related infections (FRIs) remain a significant challenge in orthopaedic trauma, as they are a consistent source of poor patient outcomes and elevated health care costs. FRIs have traditionally been diagnosed using findings from physical examination, blood tests, and advanced imaging, and the mainstay of treatment has been bony debridement, removal of hardware, and local and systemic antibiotic therapy. Although patients with FRIs were historically treated with IV antibiotics, randomized clinical trials have since demonstrated that oral antibiotics can be just as effective while mitigating the risks associated with prolonged IV antibiotics. Emerging biomarkers for infection, including molecular methods such as transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and next-generation sequencing, offer the ability to more precisely identify infection from a wider range of microbes. Fluorescence-guided debridement surgery presents a strategy to better visualize infected tissue and decrease surgeon reliance on subjective intraoperative findings. The purpose of this review is to present emerging tools and treatment algorithms that might be able to increase the accuracy and precision with which FRIs are diagnosed and managed.
journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
authors: Pedrick E, Certain L, Yoon R, Natoli RM, Gitajn IL, Tang Y, Bateman LM, Jiang S, Slobogean G, O'Toole RV, Elliott J, Wixted J, Haller J.

title: Genetic Insights into the Potential Causal Role of LIPA and LTA4H in Vitiligo: A Single-Cell Integrative Analysis.
abstract: BackgroundVitiligo is a complex autoimmune skin disorder characterized by the loss of melanocytes, imposing a significant psychosocial and economic burden on affected individuals. Despite the identification of numerous susceptibility loci through GWAS, translating these findings into clinical insights remains challenging as the cell-type-specific causal genes and their regulatory mechanisms are largely unexplored. Identifying these specific drivers is crucial for developing targeted precision therapies.MethodsWe employed an integrative framework combining single-cell eQTL data and vitiligo GWAS summary statistics to identify cell-type-specific causal genes. Potential causal relationships were evaluated using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analysis. Functional significance was explored via GO/KEGG enrichment. Finally, the prioritized candidates were validated using PBMC scRNA-seq dataset.ResultsMR analysis identified several cell-type-specific causal transcripts. Beyond the established HLA-DRB1 in NK recruiting cells (β=1.84, pfdr 0.7) confirmed shared causal variants at these loci. Functional enrichment highlighted lysosomal metabolism and antigen presentation. External validation (GSE231794) confirmed that HLA-DRB1 was significantly up-regulated in patient NK recruiting cells, while LIPA and LTA4H expression were markedly diminished in patients, aligning consistently with our genetic estimates.ConclusionThis study provides genetic insights into the potential involvement of LIPA and LTA4H in vitiligo. These findings suggest that a deficiency in these metabolic-immune regulators within specific myeloid subsets may contribute to the disease's pathogenesis, highlighting them as potential targets for further functional investigation and precision intervention. Future studies should focus on in vivo and in vitro functional validation of these genes to further elucidate their precise roles in melanocyte stability and their potential as therapeutic targets for precision intervention.
authors: Zhang Z, Lu H.

title: Adaptive immune plasticity in MASH: Functional states, pathological consequences, and regulatory mechanisms.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by both metabolic stress and immune dysregulation. A growing body of evidence suggests that adaptive immune cells exhibit significant functional plasticity during the progression and resolution of MASH. CD8+ T cells can assume various states, including pathogenic cytotoxicity, functional exhaustion, and tissue repair; CD4+ T cells exhibit enhanced Th1/Th17 programming, reduced Treg stability, and a functional shift toward Th17/Treg; and B cells undergo remodeling between regulatory, pro-inflammatory, and antibody-effect states. These functional states determine disease outcomes through distinct effector mechanisms. The cytotoxicity and inflammatory factors of pathogenic T cells promote hepatocyte damage, metabolic dysregulation, and hepatocyte stellate cell activation, while B-cell antigen presentation, cytokine, and antibody responses further amplify inflammation and fibrosis; conversely, Tregs, Bregs, and tissue-resident CD8+ T cells with reparative functions can limit inflammation or promote the resolution of fibrosis. Adaptive immune plasticity is, in turn, continuously shaped by the hepatic metabolic environment, in which glycolipid and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming determine the metabolic basis of different functional states, while metabolite-driven epigenetic remodeling stabilizes corresponding transcriptional programs. Microbiome components and metabolic signals originating from the gut-liver axis further regulate the state of T and B cells within the liver. Consequently, the functional states of adaptive immune cells, their pathological effects, and their metabolic regulation collectively constitute a critical immunometabolic network linking metabolic dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and the progression of fibrosis, providing a unified mechanistic framework for understanding the sustained progression of MASH and tissue repair.
authors: Yu X, Yang Y, Bai L.

title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Multi-Omics, and Mendelian Randomization Reveal Ferroptosis-Related Molecular Subtypes and a Genetically Supported Causal Candidate in Psoriasis.
abstract: BackgroundFerroptosis contributes to inflammatory skin diseases, but its role in psoriasis remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated multi‑omics analysis combining single‑cell transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, consensus clustering, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to characterize ferroptosis‑related molecular features, intercellular communication, immune microenvironment remodeling, molecular subtypes, and causal biomarkers in psoriasis.MethodsSingle‑cell RNA‑seq data (GSE151177) were analyzed to quantify ferroptosis activity across cell populations and infer intercellular communication networks. Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE30999, GSE78097) were integrated for differential expression and machine‑learning feature selection with SHAP interpretation. Consensus clustering, immune infiltration, functional enrichment, and drug repurposing analyses were performed. Cis‑eQTLs from eQTLGen (n=31,684) served as instruments for two‑sample MR with psoriasis GWAS from FinnGen (13,667 cases, 395,092 controls).ResultsMacrophages/monocytes and fibroblasts showed the highest ferroptosis scores. MIF signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44, MIF-CD74/CXCR4, MIF-ACKR3) dominated keratinocyte outgoing communication. Transcriptomic integration yielded 72 overlapping ferroptosis-related genes; machine learning identified eight feature genes (CD24, EFNB2, DDX39A, NDRG4, GPRC5A, S100A8, PRSS8, ITPKC). CD24 (AUC=0.979) and S100A8 (AUC=0.974) exhibited top diagnostic performance. Consensus clustering stratified patients into two subtypes (C1, C2); all eight genes were highly expressed in C1, while C2 showed upregulated phagocytic but downregulated innate immune pathways. Drug enrichment suggested MS-275, genistein, and β-adrenoceptor agonists as potential ferroptosis-modulating compounds. MR demonstrated that only PRSS8 eQTL had a nominally significant causal association with psoriasis risk (P ConclusionOur multi‑omics study delineates the ferroptosis‑related landscape in psoriasis, identifies MIF signaling as a key keratinocyte communication axis, establishes a high‑performance diagnostic model with eight feature genes, defines two distinct immune‑metabolic subtypes, and provides genetic evidence supporting PRSS8 as a putative causal biomarker for psoriasis susceptibility, offering novel insights and potential ferroptosis‑based biomarkers and therapeutic targets for psoriasis.
authors: Xu M, Zuo Y, Liu H, Jia H, Liu X.

title: Candidozyma auris in hospital setting: Molecular characterization of clinical and environmental strains.
abstract: BackgroundCandidozyma auris is a yeast that has a strong ability to adapt, can cause serious invasive infections and contaminate various surfaces.MethodsAfter cases of C. auris have occurred in patients hospitalized in a healthcare facility of Apulia region, Italy, clinical and environmental surveillance was implemented. The aim of this study is to perform genotypic and phenotypic characterization between clinical and environmental isolations. In August and September 2024, in three hospital wards, axillary-inguinal swabs were performed on hospitalized patients; environmental monitoring was carried out simultaneously to detect C. auris in air and surfaces.ResultsC. auris strain was isolated from the blood culture and peritoneal fluid of a patient, and identified using mass spectrometry. Swabs were performed on surfaces in the patient's room using sterile swabs, analyzed by molecular method. Active and passive sampling of air was conducted. Out of the 194 surface swabs, C. auris DNA was detected in 50 samples. Passive air sampling identified C. auris in 33.3% of plates in Intensive Care patient areas. In the Infectious Diseases Unit, a sample tested positive. Active air sampling didn't detect C. auris. 66 patients were screened, all of which resulted negative for C. auris. Swabs collected from two patients were positive. All isolates were susceptible to amphotericin B, anidulafungin and resistant to fluconazole. Amino acid substitutions were identified in the ERG11 and TAC1B genes.ConclusionsViable C. auris was detected in a small number of environmental samples and was genetically closely related to isolates from the corresponding patients.
journal: Journal of infection and public health
authors: Caggiano G, Triggiano F, Fioriti S, D'Achille G, Rochira N, Diella G, Spagnuolo V, Lopuzzo M, Dalfino L, Stufano M, Sartini M, Cristina ML, Grasso S, Di Lorenzo A, Tafuri S, Barchiesi F, Morroni G.

title: Unraveling pyrethroid-induced multisystem toxicity in fish: a review of pathways, drivers, and countermeasures.
abstract: Pyrethroid pesticides, widely applied in agriculture and public health, frequently contaminate aquatic ecosystems and pose substantial risks to teleost fish due to their lipophilicity and bioaccumulation potential. This review synthesizes recent advances in understanding pyrethroid-induced multisystem toxicity in teleosts, covering neurotoxicity via voltage-gated sodium channel disruption, cardiovascular impairment, reproductive and endocrine disruption, immunotoxicity, and metabolic dysfunction. Oxidative stress emerges as a common mediator across these effects. Toxicity is modulated by abiotic factors (temperature, salinity, sediment organic matter), biotic factors (species, developmental stage, sex), and co-exposure with other contaminants. Detoxification strategies include physical/chemical remediation, microbial biodegradation, and nutritional or immunomodulatory interventions that enhance endogenous antioxidant defenses. Despite progress, critical knowledge gaps remain regarding chronic low-level exposure, metabolite toxicity, transgenerational epigenetic effects, and climate-change interactions. Future research should integrate molecular, organismal, and environmental data to develop predictive risk assessment frameworks and field-applicable mitigation measures, ensuring sustainable pyrethroid use while safeguarding fish health and aquatic biodiversity.
authors: Xu M, She S, Yang S, Fei H.

title: Amplified toxicity of the dinoflagellate Amphidinium carterae in Artemia franciscana under climate warming and nitrogen enrichment.
abstract: Climate warming and nutrient imbalance in coastal areas are considered key drivers of harmful algal blooms formation, yet their influence on the toxicity of these harmful organisms remains poorly understood. This study investigated the lethal and sub-lethal effects of the toxin-producing dinoflagellate A. carterae on the brine shrimp Artemia franciscana using different exposure matrices (live cells, cell lysates and cell-free supernatants), two temperature regimes (19 and 24 °C), and nitrogen-enriched conditions. Mortality assays revealed clear dose-response relationships, with cell lysates being markedly more toxic than live cells, indicating that most bioactive compounds are intracellular. In contrast, exposure to live cells caused significant sub-lethal effects, including a dose-dependent reduction in swimming activity, with behavioural impairment occurring at concentrations considerably below lethal thresholds. A binary exposure experiment demonstrated that elevated temperature (24 °C) significantly amplified sub-lethal toxicity of A. carterae, resulting in reduced motility, and increased lipid peroxidation and DNA damage on A. franciscana. Similar responses were observed when A. carterae was grown under nitrogen-enriched conditions. LC-HRMS analysis revealed the presence of amphidinol-related compounds and cytotoxic macrolides, supporting a membrane-active mode of action underlying the observed effects. Overall, these findings demonstrate that A. carterae induces significant sub-lethal effects in a model organism A. franciscana at cell densities comparable to those reported during A. carterae proliferations, and suggest that climate warming combined with nitrogen-enriched conditions may increase the hazard potential of this dinoflagellate under future coastal conditions. These results highlight the importance of incorporating sub-lethal endpoints and multi-stressor scenarios into hazard and risk assessment of harmful algal blooms under future coastal conditions.
authors: Rissel T, Morão IFC, Moutinho A, Correro MM, David H, Shiels K, Novais SC, Lemos MFL, Amorim A, Simões T.

title: BrABA2 mutation conferred glossy leaf via epicuticular wax crystal disruption in Chinese cabbage.
abstract: Leaf glossiness is an important quality trait affecting the commercial value of Chinese cabbage. Identifying the genes controlling the glossy leaf trait in Chinese cabbage is crucial for cultivar improvement. In this study, we characterized a glossy leaf mutant wdm19 isolated from an EMS-mutagenized population of the doubled haploid line 'FT'. Scanning electron microscopy revealed the absence of epicuticular wax crystal on the mutant leaf surface, accompanied by significantly increased water loss and chlorophyll leaching rates. GC-MS analysis confirmed a marked reduction in total cuticular wax load in wdm19 compared with 'FT'. Genetic analysis indicated that the glossy leaf phenotype was controlled by a single recessive nuclear gene. By combining MutMap analysis with KASP genotyping, BraA08g002170.3.5C was identified as the candidate gene named BrABA2, which is orthologous to AtABA2 and is involved in abscisic acid biosynthesis. A single nucleotide substitution (G to A) was detected at position 304 bp downstream of the TAG stop codon within the 3' UTR of BrABA2, which significantly reduced its expression at both transcript and protein levels. Heterologous complementation in Arabidopsis confirmed that the aba2 mutant phenotype could be restored by overexpressing BrABA2. Our findings demonstrated that mutation of BrABA2 led to the glossy leaf phenotype in Chinese cabbage.
authors: Zhao N, Song G, Yang G, Li X, Liu C, Feng H, Liu Z.

title: Extracting candidate motif patterns for multiple RNA modifications using direct RNA sequencing.
abstract: RNA modifications have emerged as key regulators of virtually all aspects of RNA biology, driving growing interest in computational approaches for their transcriptome-wide detection. For some RNA modifications, the search space can be reduced by exploiting characteristic sequence motifs, as exemplified by the canonical DRACH motif associated with m⁶A. However, comparable sequence preferences remain largely unknown for most other RNA modifications, making systematic motif discovery considerably more challenging. Here, we applied exponential population analysis to direct RNA sequencing data from HEK293T cells and peripheral human blood to identify candidate motif patterns for pseudouridine (Ψ), inosine (I), and 5-methylcytosine (m⁵C). Our results demonstrate that exponential population analysis provides a systematic framework for identifying candidate motif patterns from nanopore-derived RNA modification predictions, thereby prioritizing sequence contexts for future biological validation.
authors: Alagna N, Miedema J, Basiony Y, Gerber S.

title: Transcriptomic and long non-coding RNA profiling suggests molecular mechanisms underlying skin color variation in common carp (Cyprinus carpio).
abstract: Skin color is an economically important trait in cultured fish, but the transcriptional basis of orange pigmentation in the FFRC No. 2 strain of common carp (Cyprinus carpio) remains unclear. This study compared messenger RNA and long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression in dorsal skin from five orange and five gray six-month-old full siblings. Transcriptome sequencing, differential-expression and functional-enrichment analyses, target-gene prediction, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction validation were performed. In orange relative to gray skin, 1014 genes and 519 lncRNAs were differentially expressed. Differentially expressed genes were enriched in melanin biosynthesis, melanocyte differentiation, melanosome organization, tyrosine metabolism, and melanogenesis. Most melanogenesis-associated genes, including tyr, tyrp1a, tyrp1b, mc1r, mreg, pmel, and kita, were down-regulated in orange fish, whereas asip and slc7a11 were up-regulated. Up-regulated genes were also enriched in lipid-metabolism-related processes and pathways. Target prediction identified 2346 potential relationships between differentially expressed lncRNAs and genes, comprising 48 cis and 2298 trans relationships; 48 lncRNAs were linked to 20 pigmentation-associated genes. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction results were consistent with the sequencing data. These results suggest that a possible switch from eumelanin to pheomelanin production may be the cause of orange coloration. The predicted lncRNA-gene regulatory networks provide valuable candidate targets for future functional studies and molecular breeding in common carp.
journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
authors: Fu J, Zhu W, Luo M, Wang L, Gong Y, Dong Z.

title: Identification of ceruloplasmin-binding anticancer peptides linked to cancer cell reprogramming in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) progression is strongly influenced by tumour-cell plasticity and dynamic transcriptional reprogramming, which contribute to heterogeneity, treatment resistance and metastatic progression. This study developed an integrated computational framework to identify anticancer peptides that interact with molecular candidates associated with CRC reprogramming. Experimentally reported colon/colorectal cancer-associated anticancer peptides were curated and filtered according to physicochemical stability, predicted toxicity and haemolytic potential. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE132465 were analysed using tumour-normal differential expression, reprogramming-related Hallmark signatures and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, followed by protein-protein interaction, functional enrichment, immune-infiltration and machine-learning analyses. Ceruloplasmin (CP) emerged as the strongest internally consensus-stable candidate, being selected by at least two machine-learning feature-ranking methods in 73.3% of bootstrap iterations, while its differential expression was independently supported in TCGA-COAD/READ. Twelve prioritised peptides were subsequently evaluated by interface-guided HADDOCK docking, and six leading complexes were subjected to three independent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations. FLAK26VAM produced the most favourable HADDOCK score and the highest hydrogen-bond occupancy, whereas FLAK93B showed the most consistent overall post-docking profile, including lower structural deviation, greater conformational compactness and the most favourable MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA energy estimates. HAL-1/20, HAL-1/9 and FLAK50Q7 also showed favourable complementary structural characteristics. Free-energy landscape analysis further supported the presence of defined low-energy conformational states in the prioritised complexes. Collectively, these findings identify CP as an externally supported CRC-associated candidate and prioritise FLAK26VAM and FLAK93B as complementary lead peptide candidates, with FLAK93B showing the strongest overall support when dynamic stability and post-MD energetics are considered. Thus, this study provides an integrated computational framework that links CRC reprogramming biology with peptide-target prioritisation, highlighting ceruloplasmin and selected anticancer peptides as candidates for further experimental validation.
authors: Rehman A, Li T, Shaikh AL, Hassan SSU, Pan J.

title: Heat stress elevates intracellular H₂O₂ and induces Tiron-attenuated gene expression in mouse skeletal muscle.
abstract: Changes in intracellular hydrogen peroxide concentration ([H2O2]i) serve as a key signal regulating cellular adaptation. In response to heat stress, increased ROS production and upregulation of antioxidant-related genes have been observed in skeletal muscle in vitro. However, the specific temperature dependence of [H2O2]i changes induced by heat, as well as the quantitative relationship with induced gene expression, remain unclear. This investigation tested the hypothesis that the increase in [H2O2]i during heat stress regulates antioxidant-related gene expression. To measure [H2O2]i, the highly H2O2-sensitive HyPer7 fluorescent protein was expressed in the tibialis anterior (TA) muscle of male C57BL/6J mice. The temperature dependence of [H2O2]i was determined via in vivo imaging during a 30-min heating protocol from 30°C to 40°C. Furthermore, one hour after maintaining the muscle temperature at 40°C for 30 minutes, the TA was excised, and gene expression was evaluated using transcriptomic analysis. It was found that raising the temperature of the TA from 30°C to 40°C for 20 minutes resulted in a 28% increase in [H2O2]i (p 2O2]i increase was significantly suppressed by the antioxidant Tiron (i.e., 14%). Transcriptome analysis revealed that 22 heat-induced genes were attenuated by Tiron; these were strongly enriched in Gene Ontology terms related to "unfolded protein binding". Transcription factor predictions identified HSF1 as a candidate upstream regulator of this Tiron-attenuated gene set. In conclusion, heat stress in vivo increases [H2O2]i in a temperature-dependent manner, and this redox change contributes to the induction of cell protection-related genes.
authors: Kano R, Nehashi R, Toba S, Sato S, Shirakawa H, Poole DC, Kano Y, Hoshino D.

title: Attractor Landscapes and Network Dynamics of iPSC-Derived Neural Stem Cell Plasticity: A Complexity-Theoretic Benchmark of Cell-Fate Transitions
abstract: Cell fate decisions are often studied as static transcriptomic snapshots even though differentiation is intrinsically a complex dynamical, multistable, and plastic process. To better elucidate cell fate plasticity dynamics, we developed a complexity-theoretic and machine learning framework to model neural stem cell state-transitions using a two-time point single-cell RNA-sequencing subset of GSE138121 (iPSC-derived motor neurons). The primary cohort comprised 1,960 quality-controlled cells from the Batch A control iPSC line at days 12 and 18, represented by 815 genes and 62 metacells. Ten neural/progenitor states were annotated and contrasted with NNMF and Leiden communities. We integrated forward-in-time metacell transport, quasi-potential landscapes, basin and dwell-time analysis, Spearman and Kauffman Random Boolean Networks, BDM perturbation analysis, and 5-fold cross-validation of classical machine learning and deep learning models. Transition kernels showed broad funneling toward the neuroblast/immature-neuron state. The continuous attractor landscape resolved four basins, while the 180-node, 1,080-edge Boolean Kauffman abstraction produced 18 attractors, basin entropy of 2.75 bits, and Derrida one-bit sensitivity of 1.69, indicating damage amplification rather than directly demonstrated critical point. Consensus steering prioritized ONECUT2, ZFP36L1, DCX, HOXB2, TMEM123, TUBA1A, ENO1, ELAVL4, MAP1B, and MLLT11. ESN/reservoir computing yielded the lowest latent endpoint MAE (0.138), while CTM and Transformer achieved the lowest transition-kernel RMSE after validation-selected blending with a training-only state/time prior (0.0402 and 0.0404). These results support a complex systems view of iPSC-derived neural differentiation as trajectories through a multi-basin state-space, linking attractor geometry, network topology, and explainable AI to generate testable candidates for cell fate control and reprogramming.
authors: Uthamacumaran A.

title: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems: A Survey and an Evaluation Audit
abstract: In 2026 a new kind of recommender research appeared: large language model (LLM) agents that propose changes to a recommender's configuration or source code, train the changed model, and keep what the evaluation says is better. Within ten months, more than thirty such systems were reported, from open-source research harnesses to production loops at Google, Meta, Amazon, Alibaba, Kuaishou, Tencent and NetEase. This survey organises them, together with search-space AutoML and the agentic recommenders that update their own memory or weights, along two axes: what the loop changes and which signal decides whether a change survives. Because a self-evolving system is only as good as the signal it selects on, we then audit how 27 configuration- and code-level recommender systems are evaluated, coding each paper's full text against nine criteria. Three of the 27 evaluate with full-catalogue ranking. Of the 17 that select candidates offline, nine do not say which data split makes the decision, two select on the data they report, and three state that the test set was used once. None reports its headline result with the spread over repeated evolution sessions, and none runs an equal-budget random search over its own edit space; the few studies that measure transfer to held-out data find that part of the selected gain, sometimes most of it, does not survive. Four systems report that their agent inflated the metric or leaked the target, caught by a human or by monitoring rather than by the acceptance rule. We distil these findings into a reporting standard and describe recforge, an open benchmark under development that implements the API side of a sealed-test, full-ranking, equal-budget protocol.
authors: Yang S, Shi Z.

title: Progress and perspectives in nitrogenase engineering in plants and yeast.
abstract: Crop productivity relies on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers, which entail significant economic and environmental costs. Engineering crop plants to produce nitrogenase allowing them to acquire nitrogen from the atmosphere offers a transformative approach to sustainable agriculture. However, engineering the nitrogenase pathway into eukaryotic cells poses significant challenges due to the enzyme metal clusters, high energy demands, and extreme sensitivity to oxygen. This review summarizes recent advances in nitrogenase engineering in yeast and plants. Progress has been made using a stepwise modular approach and a functional validation pipeline for core and ancillary nitrogenase proteins. Key milestones include recovery of NifH with in vitro activity from mitochondria and chloroplasts, production of NifB that is active upon isolation or after in vitro cluster reconstitution, production of NifB-co in yeast mitochondria, in vitro FeMo-co biosynthesis using proteins purified from yeast mitochondria, and recovery of nitrogenase components from transgenic rice with activity demonstrated in vitro. Complete nitrogenase activity in engineered yeast or plants has not yet been demonstrated. We discuss the importance of organelle targeting, the exploitation of natural diversity and engineered proteins, and synthetic biology tools for the assembly of multigene pathways. Finally, we present the main remaining obstacles, such as the assembly of functional NifDK in plants, integration with host metabolism and coordinated regulation, and we outline the prospects for the development of nitrogen-fixing crops.
authors: Paganelli Á, Curatti L, González-Guerrero M, Burén S, Rubio LM.

title: Development of cinnamyl derivatives as antibiotic-potentiating agents.
abstract: Here, we report the discovery and optimization of 1-cinnamylpiperazine derivatives as antibiotic-potentiating agents inspired by the known RND efflux pump inhibitor 1-(1-naphthylmethyl)piperazine (NMP). A structurally diverse series of analogues was synthesized and evaluated for intrinsic antibacterial activity, cytotoxicity, and ability to potentiate antibiotic activity against Escherichia coli. Most derivatives showed low intrinsic antibacterial activity, consistent with an adjuvant mode of action. In combination assays, several compounds enhanced the antibiotic activity of erythromycin and linezolid, with halogenated derivatives showing the strongest potentiating effects. Compound 27 displayed the broadest potentiation profile, showing synergistic interactions with five of the seven tested antibiotics, namely linezolid, novobiocin, fusidic acid, pyridomycin, and clindamycin. Notably, it showed a superior potency to the structurally related reference inhibitor NMP. Experiments with AcrAB-TolC-deficient E. coli mutants, together with dye accumulation (Hoechst 33342) and membrane-permeabilization assays, suggested that 1-cinnamylpiperazine derivatives modulate efflux-associated resistance in a manner distinct from NMP, with increased membrane permeability likely contributing to their overall potentiating effect. Beyond planktonic cultures, compound 27 also potentiated erythromycin and linezolid against mature E. coli biofilms. These findings identify 1-cinnamylpiperazines as promising antibiotic adjuvant scaffolds for further optimization against drug-resistant Gram-negative infections.
authors: Hympanova M, Kufa M, Muckova L, Prchal L, Janousek J, Finger V, Kovar O, Cizkova J, Jagob J, Mansfeldova A, Marek J, Soukup O, Roh J, Korabecny J.

title: Development of cosmeceutical nanoemulsion formulation containing peptide acting on neurotransmitters and evaluation of its efficacy.
abstract: External factors such as oxidative stress and ultraviolet (UV) radiation increase reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cause the skin to age faster. Recently, peptides have been frequently preferred in nanoformulation development to prevent these effects. This study aimed to develop a nanoemulsion formulation of Syn-Ake peptide that reduces wrinkles by affecting neurotransmitters and to evaluate its efficacy by in silico and in vitro methods. In this context, the anti-aging activity of Syn-Ake peptide was evaluated by molecular docking and MD simulation. Then, nanoemulsion formulations of the peptide were produced using ultrasonic homogenization method and stability and characterization studies were conducted. The in vitro safety of the formulation was evaluated by genotoxicity and cytotoxicity studies. The cell regenerative effect of the formulation was evaluated by scratch test. Additionally, the protective effect of its formulation against H2O2-UV-induced skin damage was evaluated at both the cellular and DNA levels. Finally, the antioxidant activity and the collagenase inhibitory activity of the formulation was evaluated. Our findings showed that the peptide strongly interacted with p-38 MAPK and PI3K-AKT signalling pathways, as well as stromelysins and gelatinases. The most stable formulation was determined among the formulations developed with different production procedures. The formulation was determined to be non-genotoxic, cytocompatible and to have cell regenerative properties. It was also evaluated that the formulation was protective against H2O2-UV-based damage, showed antioxidant activity and collagenase inhibitory activity. The formulation of Syn-Ake peptide in nanoemulsion was evaluated to have promising potential as an anti-aging product candidate with a high efficacy and safety profile.Supplementary informationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05090-6.
authors: Gok B, Budama-Kilinc Y, Kecel-Gunduz S.

title: An integrated One Health surveillance approach to Dirofilaria spp.: Linking mosquito xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis and veterinary epidemiology.
abstract: Dirofilaria immitis and Dirofilaria repens are mosquito-borne filarioid nematodes of veterinary and public health importance whose distribution is expanding across Europe. This study developed an integrated One Health surveillance framework combining mosquito monitoring, molecular xenomonitoring, blood-meal analysis, and veterinary epidemiological data to assess Dirofilaria circulation and transmission dynamics. During the 2025 transmission season, mosquitoes were collected by the University of Parma in urban and peri-urban areas and by the Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale della Lombardia ed Emilia-Romagna (IZSLER) in rural areas. Female mosquitoes were morphologically identified and analysed in pools by Real-time PCR for D. immitis and D. repens DNA. Positive pools were screened for West Nile virus, Usutu virus, and insect-specific flaviviruses in order to detect possible co-infection parasite-virus. Blood-fed mosquitoes were individually analysed by mitochondrial 12S and 16S rRNA sequencing to identify vertebrate hosts. Veterinary practices across Emilia-Romagna were surveyed for canine and feline dirofilariosis during 2024-2025. Overall, 11,225 females belonging to eight species were collected and 181 pools analysed. D. immitis predominated in urban collections, whereas D. repens was more frequent in peri-urban and rural areas. Aedes albopictus was the principal positive species in urban environments, while Aedes caspius predominated in rural settings. Humans were the predominant blood-meal host, followed by dogs, horses, cattle, and birds. Veterinary and vector surveillance showed poor agreement, indicating complementary epidemiological information. These findings highlight complex transmission patterns and support integrated One Health surveillance to improve risk assessment and guide evidence-based prevention and control strategies for Dirofilaria and other vector-borne zoonoses.
authors: Vismarra A, Fozzer M, Genchi M, Tenga A, Semeraro M, Calzolari M, Grisendi A, Bazzocchi C, Kramer L, Stocchero C, Cafiso A.

title: Schaftoside from galgeuntang as a multi-target class I histone deacetylase inhibitor: Integrated molecular docking, dynamics, and systems pharmacology analysis.
abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are enzymes that remove acetyl groups from lysine residues of histone proteins, playing a critical role in gene expression regulation. Particularly, Class I HDACs (HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8) are implicated in cancer development and have attracted significant interest as therapeutic targets. However, developing isoform-selective HDAC inhibitors remains challenging. We screened 1625 phytocompounds from the Korean herbal formulation Galgeuntang using the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology database. After applying drug-likeness filtering, 235 compounds underwent molecular docking against HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8. Schaftoside emerged as the sole candidate engaging all three isoforms, with binding energies of -115.1, -103.8, and -135.5 kcal/mol, respectively. ADMET profiling, quantitative cytotoxicity predictions across multiple cancer cell lines, and in silico gene expression analysis were then performed. One hundred nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable complex formation and PCA-based free energy landscape analysis revealed well-defined conformational minima for each complex. Schaftoside exhibited potent predicted cytotoxicity against hematological and gastrointestinal malignancies (selectivity Index: 8.7-18.6), including the cisplatin-resistant A2780cisR ovarian carcinoma line. In silico transcriptomic profiling predicted downregulation of oncogenic drivers (MYC, STAT3, AKT1) with concurrent upregulation of tumor suppressors (TP53, CDKN1A) and suppression of the HDAC machinery itself. ADMET profiling revealed high aqueous solubility but limited membrane permeability, indicating that structural optimization will be required. Schaftoside therefore constitutes a promising multi-target Class I HDAC inhibitor scaffold, warranting experimental validation through enzymatic assays, histone acetylation analysis, and cell-based cytotoxicity testing.
authors: Shah FH, Cho JS, Lee SH, Jo YR, Huh SJ, Chung HJ, Jung J, Jeong NY.

title: Carbazole derivatives as privileged scaffolds for kinase inhibition: advances in design, therapeutic applications and mechanisms.
abstract: Protein kinases are regarded as the most pursued drug targets in inflammatory diseases and oncology, and the carbazole scaffold has emerged as a versatile core for their inhibition owing to its planar, rigid tricyclic framework, which efficiently accommodates the kinase hinge region. This review consolidates the design and biological exploration of carbazole analogues and fused carbazole derivatives, including pyrrolocarbazole, indolocarbazoles, carbazole carboxamides, and various others, as inhibitors of several kinase families. These carbazole derivatives have been evaluated against VEGFR (Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptor), EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor), CDK (Cyclin-Dependent Kinase), PIM (Proviral Integration Site for Moloney Murine Leukemia Virus), MAPK (Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase), BTK (Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase), ALK (Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase), JAK/STAT (Janus Kinase/Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription signaling pathway), CHK (Checkpoint Kinase), and CK (Casein Kinase) protein kinases. Despite chemical versatility, these therapies remain constrained due to acquired resistance via non-gatekeeper and gatekeeper mutations, nonselective kinase inhibition, poor solubility, and metabolic vulnerability, collectively leading to poor oral bioavailability. Looking forward, structure-based carbazole derivative design for better ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) profile, allosteric and covalent inhibitor development are some of the gaps that need to be covered in future drug discovery.
authors: Munawar S, Saif MJ, Khan SG, Zahoor AF, Parveen B, Hafeez F, Said MA.

title: Polyethylene glycol 35 preserves endothelial barrier integrity by stabilizing the glycocalyx and intercellular junctions.
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is a hallmark of numerous inflammatory and ischemic conditions, characterized by increased permeability, disruption of intercellular junctions and endothelial glycocalyx (eGCX) degradation. In the present study, we investigated the ability of polyethylene glycol 35 (PEG35) to preserve endothelial barrier integrity in cultured human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) exposed to inflammatory, thrombotic, hypoxia-mimetic and eGCX-disrupting stimuli. PEG35 mitigated the loss of cellular metabolic activity induced by apoptotic and hypoxia-mimetic stress. Functionally, PEG35 attenuated stimulus-induced increases in FITC-dextran permeability and helped maintain trans-endothelial electrical resistance (TEER) under pro-inflammatory and eGCX-disrupting agents. PEG35 also reduced LDH release and maintained higher TEER values in endothelial cells exposed to plasma collected from pancreas transplant recipients after reperfusion, which contained increased circulating levels of the endothelial glycocalyx component syndecan-1. Mechanistically, PEG35 reduced NFĸB p65 nuclear translocation under thrombin, TNFα, and hyaluronidase stimulation and attenuated inflammatory and endothelial activation-related transcriptional responses. PEG35 also modulated intercellular junction gene expression in a stimulus and target-dependent manner, helped maintain occludin and claudin-5 protein expression under selected injurious conditions, and limited the loss of eGCX-associated syndecan-1 and heparan sulfate staining after enzymatic degradation. Collectively, these findings support a multifactorial endothelial-protective effect of PEG35 involving preservation of endothelial surface layer, maintenance of junctional integrity and attenuation of inflammatory signalling. These results identify PEG35 as a potential vasoprotective candidate for conditions involving acute endothelial barrier injury.
authors: Llaves-López A, Barnat-Cabrera Q, Manso-Álvarez P, Ferrer-Fàbrega J, Casal C, Folch-Puy E.

title: Cellular diversity of the developing chick trigeminal ganglion at single-cell resolution.
abstract: BackgroundThe trigeminal ganglion (TG) integrates sensory input from the face and jaw and is derived from two embryonic cell populations: neural crest and cranial placode. These populations interact during TG development to coordinate specification, differentiation, and organization, but the molecular characteristics of the heterogeneous cell populations within the developing TG remain poorly defined.ResultsWe performed single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of chick TG at HH17, generating a high-resolution dataset of ~87,000 cells representing diverse neuronal and non-neuronal populations. Subclustering and RNA velocity analysis of Isl1+ neuroblasts resolved distinct developmental trajectories associated with neural crest- and cranial placode-derived populations converging toward neuronal differentiation. A Sox10+ neural crest-associated population progressively acquired neuronal characteristics, while a distinct placode-associated trajectory exhibited loss of epithelial gene expression during neuronal maturation. We additionally identified lineage-enriched long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), including MIR137HG, which was strongly enriched in Isl1+ neuroblasts and spatially validated across TG development.ConclusionsOur study provides a single-cell atlas of the developing chick TG that resolves transcriptional heterogeneity and developmental states within its neural crest- and placode-derived populations. These data identify candidate molecular signatures associated with sensory neuronal differentiation and provide a resource for investigating the mechanisms governing trigeminal gangliogenesis.
journal: Developmental dynamics : an official publication of the American Association of Anatomists
authors: Arul Nambi Rajan A, Hutchins EJ.

title: Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BackgroundWe aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort.MethodsProteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication.ResultsMR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users.ConclusionsOur genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
authors: Huang P, Tang H, Feng Z, Stergiakouli E, Gaunt TR, Zheng J, Lu Y.

title: Identification of a Novel EBF1-Expressing Disease-Associated Arterial Subpopulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
abstract: BackgroundPulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating disease with a poor prognosis. However, only a limited number of palliative interventions are currently available. To address this unmet need, it is essential to understand the molecular causes of PAH by identifying unique disease-associated populations and their key molecular regulators during disease progression.MethodsWe constructed a single-cell multiome data set at 4 distinct time points during the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) using endothelial cells isolated from the Sugen5416/hypoxia rat model. We assessed the conservation of novel disease-associated endothelial cells by reanalyzing previously reported single-cell RNA sequencing data from human patients with PAH. We validated the functional importance of EBF1 (early B-cell factor 1) in PAH by performing in silico simulations and an in vivo knockdown mediated by a pulmonary endothelium-targeting associated virus.ResultsWe found that PH progression gradually altered the transcriptional and epigenetic landscape of the pulmonary endothelium in a stage-specific manner, leading to the emergence of a novel disease-associated arterial endothelial population expressing EBF1. A similar endothelial subset was present in human patients with PAH. Immunofluorescence revealed that EBF1 expression was elevated in both human and rat lungs during PH progression. In silico simulations suggested that EBF1 is required for the pathogenic state, and the associated virus-mediated in vivo knockdown of Ebf1 ameliorated the pathological hallmarks of PH, including right ventricular systolic pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, when delivered either before the onset of PH or after its establishment.ConclusionsWe identified EBF1 as a key transcriptional regulator of a novel disease-associated population in both humans and rats. We further demonstrated that inhibiting EBF1 within the pulmonary endothelium ameliorates the pathological features of PH, suggesting that EBF1 and its transcriptional targets represent a novel and promising therapeutic avenue for PAH.
authors: Choi W, Lee D, Lee A, Yun E, Choi SY, Lee G, Ju S, Pak B, Kim M, Cho H, Yi K, Shao Z, Zhang G, Jun YS, Choi J, Simons M, Wang S, Kim J, Park J, Jin SW.

title: Progress in synergistic nanoengineering regulation of cathode and anode interfaces in high-performance aqueous zinc-iodine batteries.
abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine (Zn-I2) batteries are considered promising candidates for large-scale energy storage, owing to the abundant resources of zinc anodes, high theoretical capacity, excellent safety, as well as the fast reaction kinetics and low cost of iodine (I2) cathodes. However, their application is still limited by coupled failure at the cathode and anode interfaces. On the cathode side, polyiodides easily cause shuttle effects, self-discharge, and active I2 loss, while the anode faces core issues such as dendrite formation, hydrogen evolution, corrosion and deposition of by-products. Meanwhile, the migration of polyiodides and OH-/pH disturbances induced by anode side reactions amplify each other, further accelerating battery degradation. Electrolyte additives, due to their structurally designable nature, low dosage, and good compatibility, can synergistically regulate both the cathode and anode interfaces, making them an effective strategy to mitigate coupled failures. This review systematically summarizes the research progress of additives with different molecular configurations in aqueous Zn-I2 batteries, focusing on their structural characteristics, dual-interface mechanisms, and performance. The review also discusses challenges in mechanistic evidence, evaluation standards, adaptability to complex working conditions, and molecular design, and envisions the development direction of additives for Zn-I2 batteries with high loading, long lifespan, and multi-electron reactions.
authors: Chen X, Chen L, Lin C, Liu M, Huang Z, Luo F, Zhou W, Chen Q, Zeng L.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Pharmacology Identifies IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG as Candidate Targets of Cortex Dictamni in Atopic Dermatitis.
abstract: Cortex Dictamni has been used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for inflammatory skin disorders, but its potential molecular targets in atopic dermatitis (AD) remain incompletely characterized. Active compounds and predicted targets of Cortex Dictamni were retrieved from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform and integrated with bulk-transcriptomic differential-expression data and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Protein-protein interaction, functional-enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA)-based immune-cell and pathway analyses were performed with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Molecular docking was used to predict luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2 binding poses, and candidate-gene expression was assessed in TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT keratinocytes treated with low concentrations of purified dictamnine. Eighteen active components yielded 170 predicted targets; 88 overlapped with AD-related genes, and 43 of these were differentially expressed. Intersecting 366 cell-type-specific differentially expressed genes with 42 targets identified IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG. IRF1, PTGS2, and TNF were upregulated in specific immune-cell populations, whereas IFNG was downregulated in natural killer cells. Ribosome-pathway enrichment was observed across five immune-cell types. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, immune-signature correlations were gene-specific and bidirectional, whereas Hallmark-pathway correlations were nonsignificant. Docking predicted possible binding poses for luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2. In TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT cells, 6.25 and 12.5 µM dictamnine reduced all four mRNAs, whereas 12.5 µM dictamnine alone had no significant effect. Collectively, IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG were nominated as potential Cortex Dictamni-associated targets in AD, and low-dose purified dictamnine provided preliminary mRNA-level support. These findings do not establish crude-herb efficacy or direct target-compound interactions and require protein-level, mechanistic, in vivo, and clinical validation.
authors: Feng R, Liu X, Wei J, Ma T.

title: A Bibliometric and Visualized Analysis of Global Trends in Gut Microbiota and Metabolic Syndrome Research.
abstract: The relationship between the gut microbiota and metabolic syndrome (MetS) has attracted increasing attention, but the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and evolution of this field remain insufficiently characterized. English-language articles and reviews published in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2015 to 2025 were retrieved, based on the final search and data export conducted on April 18, 2026. Using the predefined search strategy and database filters, 2,473 records were retrieved and analyzed using CiteSpace 6.4.R1, VOSviewer 1.6.20, and SCImago Graphica 1.0.35 to evaluate publication trends, collaboration networks, knowledge structures, research hotspots, and emerging frontiers. Annual publication output increased from 72 articles in 2015 to 333 in 2025 and peaked at 334 in 2021. The country/region collaboration network comprised 97 nodes and 134 links, with a density of 0.0288. China and the United States were the leading contributors, while the United States occupied a prominent bridging position. Instituto de Salud Carlos III, Zhejiang University, Harvard Medical School, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences were major institutional contributors. Nieuwdorp M was the most productive author, whereas Cani PD was the most frequently co-cited author. Nutrients was the most productive journal, publishing 170 articles. Keyword analysis identified MetS, gut microbiota, obesity, inflammation, and insulin resistance as the principal research themes. "Diet induced obesity" showed the strongest early keyword burst (strength = 9.02; 2015-2019), whereas probiotics, dysbiosis, and clinical trials emerged as recent research frontiers. While metabolic and inflammatory mechanisms remained prominent, microbiota-targeted interventions and clinical translation gained increasing research attention in recent years.
authors: Xu M, Wang C, Wu Y, Zhu W, Yu Q.

title: Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Prioritizes Candidate Paraptosis-Related Genes in Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy.
abstract: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is among the most disabling complications of diabetes, but its molecular features and underlying biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Paraptosis, a non-canonical form of programmed cell death characterized by endoplasmic reticulum/mitochondrial swelling and cytoplasmic vacuolization, is associated with endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial stress, processes that are also implicated in diabetic neuropathy, but its potential involvement in PDPN remains unclear. This study applied an exploratory integrative strategy that combined peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic data from 12 patients with PDPN and 12 healthy controls, together with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from human peripheral nerve tissue (GSE266026), comprising samples from patients with DPN and traumatic limb amputation (TLA) comparators. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with a paraptosis-related gene set, and were prioritized using LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest. The biological context of the prioritized genes was further explored through immune infiltration analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization, single-cell characterization, and scTenifoldKnk-based computational virtual knockout analysis. Fifteen paraptosis-related differentially expressed genes were identified, with a significantly elevated paraptosis-related score in PDPN. AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 were prioritized by all three machine-learning methods. Computational immune-cell deconvolution estimated increased the estimated neutrophil abundance and decreased the estimated CD8⁺ T-cell and resting memory CD4⁺ T-cell abundance in PDPN blood, with distinct correlations between the three candidate genes and inferred immune-cell profiles. Mendelian randomization provided evidence consistent with a potential association between genetically proxied higher AKT1 expression and diabetic polyneuropathy risk. Single-cell analysis revealed cell type-specific expression patterns of the three candidate genes, while computational virtual knockout analyses predicted gene-regulatory perturbations involving immune-inflammatory, neuronal structural, and cell-adhesion pathways within the respective network backgrounds. This exploratory integrative analysis prioritizes AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 as candidate paraptosis-related genes associated with PDPN and provides a biological context for further mechanistic and experimental investigation.
authors: Zhang Z, Gao Z, Liu J, Jin Q, Aerman A, Kou L, Kong C, Cai S, Yang W, Wang Q, Zhang L.

title: The Modified Nipple-Areola Preservation Procedure: An Evolution of the Technique After 10 Years of Experience.
abstract: BackgroundThe nipple-areola preservation (NAP) procedure was introduced by the authors in 2015 as a way to increase the survivability of the native skin breast envelope and nipple-areola complex (NAC) in patients undergoing nipple-preserving mastectomies. By undermining the central mastectomy flap 2 weeks before the planned mastectomy, the skin and NAC benefit from the delay phenomenon, resulting in improved vascularity and survivability. In addition, the NAP allows the breast surgeon to identify subareolar malignant extension and sentinel lymph node status before mastectomy and reconstruction. After 10 years of experience with this procedure, the authors have streamlined the technique, resulting in fewer complications and allowing nipple repositioning at the time of the initial operation. With this modified technique, the NAP can be performed on patients with ptotic breasts, allowing for improved cosmetic and oncological results.MethodsThis is a retrospective study of 45 female patients who underwent the modified NAP procedure followed by definitive reconstruction with perforator-based flaps.ResultsPatients had a mean age of 46 years and a body mass index of 27 kg/m2. Results demonstrate the procedure's efficacy in NAC preservation, with only 1 patient experiencing a minor hematoma. One patient developed skin flap necrosis affecting a portion of the areola, whereas another had unilateral nipple necrosis.ConclusionsOverall, the modified NAP offers improved NAC survival compared with the standard nipple-sparing mastectomy and allows patients with ptotic breasts who may not be candidates for nipple-sparing mastectomy to undergo nipple preservation while maintaining oncological principles.
journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
authors: Mentz JA, Martinez CA, Shen M, Zaghloul TM, Boutros SG.

title: YAP Fuels Cerebral Cavernous Malformations by Regulating KLF4 Transcriptional Activity and Protein Stability.
abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs), which frequently predispose patients to strokes or seizures, primarily arise from endothelial specific loss-of-function mutations in the CCM genes, and occasionally accompanied by gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA and MAP3K3. While the Hippo pathway is a well-established regulator of tissue homeostasis, its emerging relevance in vascular pathology particularly its precise role in CCM pathogenesis remains poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that CCM gene deficiency suppresses endothelial Hippo signaling, as evidenced by diminished LATS activity, alongside concomitant elevation of YAP expression and nuclear translocation in both human and mouse CCM lesions. Notably, endothelial-specific deletion of Yap mitigates CCM lesion formation, reinforces endothelial junctions, enhances inflammatory resistance, and decreases KLF4 protein levels in a CCM mouse model. Conversely, intracranial Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated inhibition of LATS or activation of YAP promoted CCMs formation under Ccm2 deficiency. Mechanistically, under the dual coordination of negative regulation by LATS and positive regulation by MAP3K3, YAP orchestrates KLF4 transcriptional activity and protein stability. This is achieved through a direct interaction with KLF4 that shields it from β-TrCP-mediated proteasomal degradation, thereby driving CCM progression. Collectively, our findings unveil a novel dimension to Hippo pathway regulation and underscore YAP as a pivotal driver of CCM pathogenesis.
authors: Ye T, Zheng Q, Hu Z, Fan H, Sun Z, Li X, Mo H, Chang C, Xu Y, Wang K, Fang D, Song H.

title: Elucidation and reconstitution of the poplar salicortin biosynthetic pathway.
abstract: Salicinoids are specialized benzenoid (C6-C1) metabolites characteristic of the Salicaceae family. Although salicinoids have long been recognized as effective defense compounds and pharmacologically active constituents in willows and poplars, the biosynthetic pathway underlying their formation remains largely unresolved. Through integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses of black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) roots, we identified candidate genes involved in salicinoid biosynthesis belonging to the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase family 92 (CYP92) and the progesterone 5β-reductase/iridoid synthase-like enzyme (PRISE) family of short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases. Co-expression of all identified candidate genes, together with the previously characterized glycosyltransferase gene PtUGT71L1, acyltransferase gene PtACT47, and cinnamic acid-CoA ligase gene PtCNL5, in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in the production of salicortin, the most abundant salicinoid in poplar. Further characterization of the P450 candidates revealed that two enzymes catalyze ortho-hydroxylation of both aromatic rings of the proposed salicortin precursor, benzyl benzoate, while two other P450s catalyze the subsequent oxidative dearomatization of the benzoic acid-derived ring of benzyl benzoate. The resulting dieneone intermediate is converted by PRISE enzymes via a 1,4-reduction to form the characteristic 1-hydroxy-6-oxocyclohex-2-en-1-carboxylic ester moiety of salicortin. Functional redundancy among the identified CYP92 and PRISE enzymes may reflect the central role of these compounds in plant defense.
authors: Lackus ND, Ma D, Nakamura Y, Luck K, Gordon H, Reichelt M, Alam RM, Paetz C, Constabel CP, Gershenzon J, Köllner TG.

title: A five-gene mitochondrial-lipid metabolism signature for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis identified by machine learning and validated in independent cohorts.
abstract: BackgroundMitochondrial dysfunction and lipid metabolism dysregulation represent early key events in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet integrated transcriptomic signatures combining these two biological processes for AD diagnosis remain poorly defined.ObjectiveThis study aimed to construct and validate a mitochondrial-lipid metabolism (MLM) gene-based diagnostic classifier for AD using machine-learning approaches and explore its underlying biological mechanisms.MethodsTwo public GEO datasets GSE5281 (training) and GSE28146 (independent validation) were included. Candidate MLM genes were retrieved from MSigDB. Differentially expressed MLM genes were screened by limma, followed by two-step feature selection with LASSO regression and random forest. Four machine-learning algorithms were compared. Model performance was evaluated by AUC, calibration, decision-curve analysis and subgroup analysis across AD severity. GSVA and hypergeometric test were applied for mechanistic exploration.ResultsA five-gene signature (SDR16C5, EGR1, ASAH2B, HIP1R, CKMT1B) was finally identified. Logistic regression model achieved 5-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.953 in training cohort and AUC = 0.892 (95%CI:0.768-1.000) in validation cohort. The signature maintained high diagnostic accuracy across incipient, moderate and severe AD stages. Hypergeometric test demonstrated significant MLM-set enrichment (p = 3.85 × 10-5). GSVA revealed close correlations between this signature with oxidative stress, synaptic dysfunction and apoptosis pathways.ConclusionsThis validated five-gene MLM signature exhibits favorable diagnostic performance for AD and reflects disturbed mitochondrial-lipid metabolic network. It provides a promising transcriptomic biomarker for AD diagnosis.
authors: Liu B, Wu J, Liu J, Mo Y, Lin G, Zhang Y, Wei C, Tao R.

title: scHGNN: A single-cell gene regulatory network inference method based on heuristic graph neural networks.
abstract: The construction of gene regulatory networks based on single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq) data provides crucial technical support for decoding cell fate determination mechanisms at the single-cell level, elucidating molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression, and developing targeted therapeutics. Existing methods for constructing GRNs often rely excessively on gene expression features, struggling to achieve an effective balance between local direct regulatory signals and global multi-step regulatory pathways. This imbalance results in insufficient utilization of topological information within the network structure. Therefore, this study proposes a heuristic graph neural network-based GRN inference model (scHGNN). scHGNN integrates multi-order neighbor topological information into learnable weights through unified heuristic matrix and link prediction modules, thereby balancing local and global regulatory relationships. This approach effectively fuses gene expression features with network structural information to achieve precise inference of latent regulatory links within gene regulatory networks. Across GRN inference tasks using benchmark networks of varying gene scales and diverse origins, scHGNN consistently outperforms existing mainstream methods on key evaluation metrics. Furthermore, in target gene prediction cases for key transcription factors such as TP53, OTX2, and FOXP1, the model achieved validation rates as high as 76%-84% in the hTFtarget database. This not only supports its accuracy in identifying known regulatory relationships but also indicates its potential to identify high-confidence candidate regulatory interactions for further biological investigation. Collectively, these results demonstrate that scHGNN holds significant application value in elucidating gene regulatory mechanisms and exploring the molecular basis of related diseases.
authors: Zhang T, Teng X, Zhang H, Zhao Z, Li Y, Dong B, Wang G.

title: Single-Cell Resolution Mapping Reveals Cell Death-Associated Stress Programs and Osteogenic-Chondrogenic Differentiation Imbalance in Subchondral Bone Mesenchymal Stem Cells of Knee Osteoarthritis.
abstract: BackgroundKOA is a degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive cartilage degradation and subchondral bone remodeling. Subchondral bone MSCs orchestrate tissue homeostasis through osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation, yet the mechanisms underlying their lineage imbalance in OA pathogenesis remain poorly understood.MethodsWe reanalyzed publicly available human tibial-plateau subchondral-bone single-cell RNA-sequencing and bulk-expression datasets using library-aware integration, donor-paired regional pseudobulk summaries, diffusion pseudotime, candidate cell-cell interaction analysis, and weighted gene co-expression analysis. Quantitative RT-PCR in four ATCC cell lines (NHAC, SW1353, MG-63, and U2OS) assessed ferroptosis-related gene expression (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, and TFRC). Immunofluorescence with COL2A1 co-staining and Western blotting assessed protein-level changes across four experimental groups (Control, OA, OA + OE-GPX4, and OA + si-GPX4).ResultsAfter quality control, 25,885 of 31,090 cells were retained and assigned to 12 marker-supported display labels. The single-cell analysis defined eight molecular program modules, whereas the bulk analysis identified six data-derived coexpression blocks. Donor-paired regional analyses characterized observed composition and expression differences, and diffusion pseudotime organized 749 mesenchymal/perivascular stromal cells without establishing lineage conversion. Bulk OA-versus-Normal analysis identified 1,805 differentially expressed genes, and the exploratory cross-platform comparison showed no global monotonic correspondence (Spearman rho = 0.009, p = 0.282). Quantitative RT-PCR showed lower GPX4 and SLC7A11 and higher ACSL4 and TFRC in OA-like chondrocytes, whereas osteosarcoma lines showed higher GPX4, SLC7A11, and TFRC. Immunofluorescence and Western blotting showed corresponding GPX4, SLC7A11, and ACSL4 changes across the four experimental groups, with COL2A1 co-staining providing a matrix-associated readout.ConclusionsIntegrated single-cell and bulk analyses identified regional transcriptional patterns, stromal-state ordering, and stress-associated programs in subchondral bone. In vitro assays supported ferroptosis-related protein changes in OA-like chondrocytes. These findings provide candidate mechanisms for further functional testing but do not establish lineage conversion or causal relationships.
authors: Ye Z, Zhu M, Dai F, Zhou Z.
