title: BactFlow: a graphical workflow for bacterial genome assembly and annotation
abstract:
Background
                     Bacterial genome reconstruction increasingly uses short-read, long-read, and hybrid sequencing strategies. However, coordinating read processing, genome assembly, quality assessment, and downstream characterization across these data types can require substantial bioinformatics expertise.
                  
                     Results
                     We developed BactFlow (https://github.com/farhadm1990/bactflow), an open-source interactive app for bacterial single isolate genome assembly and downstream analysis. It supports Nanopore and PacBio long reads, Illumina short reads, and Nanopore-Illumina data for hybrid assembly. A single local browser interface integrates read processing and quality assessment, genome assembly, and post-assembly analysis, with run-status monitoring. BactFlow combines genome-quality assessment, taxonomic classification, gene annotation, plasmid prediction, and interactive genome visualization. We demonstrated four assembly routes using publicly available Nanopore, Illumina, and PacBio datasets, as well as Nanopore-Illumina hybrid assembly.
                  
                     Conclusions
                     After initial setup on Linux, BactFlow can be launched with a single command line using Docker, Apptainer/Singularity, or Conda. Users can then configure and run analyses through the user interface (UI) without manually invoking each bioinformatics tool. The integrated interface supports bacterial isolate genome analysis across multiple sequencing strategies.

title: Track display jockey (trackDJ): a user-friendly R package for visualization of epigenomic data
abstract:
Background
                     Visualization of epigenomic data such as coverage tracks, peak calls, and chromatin interactions is a critical task in genomic data analysis. Although genome browsers such as the Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) and the UCSC Genome Browser permit user-friendly exploration of genomic tracks, they are not optimized for fully programmatic and reproducible generation of publication-quality figures. In contrast, existing programmatic tools lack a user-friendly interface and require extensive configuration.
                  
                     Results
                     We present trackDJ (Track Display Jockey), an R package for visualization of epigenomic data. trackDJ prioritizes usability by favoring convention over configuration; it provides high-level plotting functions with sensible defaults, aiming to allow users with minimal programming experience to generate clear, publication-quality figures with relatively little coding. Within a unified plotting framework, users can stack and align multiple data types, including coverage tracks, peak annotations, chromatin loops, and gene annotations. trackDJ allows users to select plotted genomic regions by coordinates or by gene name, enabling rapid visualization without knowledge of precise locus boundaries.
                  
                     Conclusions
                     trackDJ complements existing epigenomics toolkits by providing a user-friendly, reproducible alternative to interactive genome browsers for epigenomic visualization. By enabling scripted generation of clean, customizable genomic illustrations, trackDJ readily integrates into R-based analysis workflows to streamline the creation of publication-quality figures.

title: LoRA-BERT: a natural language processing model for robust and accurate prediction of long non-coding RNAs
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are key regulators in many biological processes. While they share some sequence features with messenger RNAs (mRNAs), lncRNAs have distinct functions, opening new research opportunities. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing have made it easier to detect lncRNAs, and deep learning methods are increasingly used to classify these transcripts. Although these methods have significantly improved the efficiency of identifying lncRNAs, they often lack robustness, and the prediction accuracy tends to vary significantly depending on the quality of the transcript. To tackle this issue, we introduce LoRA-BERT, a novel lncRNA prediction algorithm built on the bidirectional encoder representation from transformers (BERT). LoRA-BERT is designed to effectively capture information at the nucleotide level that is important for lncRNA classification, leading to more robust and accurate prediction outcomes that are not significantly affected by the quality of the input transcript. Through performance evaluations on comprehensive benchmarks, we demonstrate that LoRA-BERT outperforms existing schemes in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. Especially, unlike other methods, LoRA-BERT retains good predictive capability for partial transcripts, a critical feature that makes it applicable for reliable lncRNA prediction even when the sequencing depth is relatively low. Availability and implementation: The code repository is available at https://github.com/Nick-Jeon/LoRA_BERT.

title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics
abstract:
by Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu, Siwen Zhang, Yiwen Du, Hong Li, Lanming Chen, Lu Xie

Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notably, Sphinx offers improved computational efficiency and scalability. Across lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen datasets, Sphinx robustly identifies cell types and spatial functional units, including tertiary lymphoid structures. We also explored the application of Sphinx to paired high-resolution spatial transcriptomics datasets, illustrating its potential applicability. Sphinx provides a flexible and efficient framework for spatial proteomics, enabling robust characterization of spatial organization and tissue microenvironments.

title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
abstract:
by Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li, Haohua Wang

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data. Validation on synthetic data with known ground-truth parameters confirms high inference accuracy in low-to-medium activation regimes and shows that recovery of BS and productive BF becomes increasingly condition-dependent as the ON-state probability approaches saturation; under different recovery criteria, the condition-specific upper Pon limit for simultaneously recovering BS and productive BF varies with cell number and capture efficiency. Applied to a mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) dataset, PhysInfer reconstructs a transcriptional dynamic manifold across the 2,137-gene secondary BIC analysis set, showing cross-gene variation in fitted burst frequency and burst size. A model-specific stationary likelihood combined with zero-count anchoring improves robustness to zero-heavy observations. The adaptive topology module further identifies a distinct subset of genes with stable support for an effective sequential 3-state representation, revealing distributional structure beyond that captured by standard 2-state fitting. PhysInfer thus provides a robust, topology-adaptive, and interpretable solution for characterizing transcriptional kinetic patterns from static single-cell transcriptomic snapshots.

title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics
abstract:
by Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez, Gustavo Deco, Yonatan Sanz Perl

A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. We hypothesize that a key signature of this balance is the presence of memory effects, which arise when a brain region’s future activity depends not only on its current state, but also on past information fed back from the wider network. Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation–dissipation theorem (FDT). We first apply this framework to whole-brain models fitted to human neuroimaging data, demonstrating that the brain’s memory structure reflects its underlying connectivity. We then extend the analysis to individualized models of subjects during wakefulness and deep sleep. Memory effects are consistently stronger in wakefulness, indicating richer inter-regional dependencies and more integrated dynamics. These findings establish local memory as a dynamical marker of brain state and position the FDTest as a principled tool for probing the hidden structure of neural dynamics.

title: Concordance of flow cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection with human papillomavirus DNA testing and cervical cytology in a cervical cancer screening cohort.
abstract: Overexpression of viral oncogenes E6 and E7 of high-risk (HR)-human papillomavirus (HPV) plays a key role in the progression to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cancer. Detection of E6/E7 mRNA may help distinguish between transient and transforming infections, thus improving cervical cancer screening accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the association of E6/E7 mRNA expression with HR-HPV infection, cervical cytology, and histologically confirmed cervical lesions and to compare its agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology. A total of 526 women undergoing cervical cancer screening between January 2023 and May 2025 were enrolled. E6/E7 mRNA expression was assessed using flow cytometry with the HPV OncoTect 3Dx E6/E7 mRNA assay and compared with HR-HPV DNA testing, cervical cytology, and available histopathologic findings from biopsy specimens. Among 526 samples, eight (1.5%) tested positive for E6/E7 mRNA, compared to 30 (5.7%) HR-HPV DNA-positive and 17 (3.2%) abnormal cytology results. Median E6/E7 mRNA expression was higher in HR-HPV- positive cases and in cytologically abnormal cases. Almost perfect agreement was observed between E6/E7 mRNA results, HR-HPV DNA testing, and cytology. Histopathologic follow-up was available for nine women with cytological abnormalities ≥low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, including four CIN2 and five CIN1 cases. E6/E7 mRNA expression was markedly elevated in one CIN2 case associated with HPV16 infection (37.51%), while two CIN1 cases demonstrated high mRNA expression despite negative HPV DNA results. Flow-cytometric E6/E7 mRNA detection showed high overall agreement with HPV DNA testing and cytology in this screening cohort. Larger prospective studies with comprehensive histologic follow-up are needed to determine its clinical utility.

title: Integrated anatomical, biochemical and transcriptomic analysis provide new insights into the photosynthetic regulation and source capacity of Coffea arabica under prolonged differential shading.
abstract: Shade cultivation is generally considered more suitable for coffee growth and development. However, to date, systematic studies on the response of Coffea arabica under multi-gradient shading conditions remain scarce, and, in particular, no comprehensive analysis of the molecular regulatory mechanisms has been reported. This study focused on evaluating the phenotypic, photosynthetic physiological, energy metabolic, and molecular responses of Coffea arabica under four shade conditions (25%, 40%, 65%, and 90% shade degree), with no-shade condition as the control. The results indicate that shading induced leaf size and color adjustment but exhibited a distinct threshold effect, whereas palisade tissue and spongy tissue showed significant structural plasticity across treatments. Coffee exhibited optimal photosynthetic performance under light- and moderate-shade (25%-40% shading), with the net photosynthetic rate reaching 16.443 μmol m-2·s-1. Under severe shade (90% shading), despite pronounced non-stomatal limitations, high light use efficiency sustained energy output and redox-related metabolic balance, with selective accumulation of TCA cycle intermediates and an apparent shift toward fermentative metabolism, as indicated by lactate accumulation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the number of differentially expressed genes increased markedly with shade intensity, with functional enrichment predominantly in pathways such as ribosome, starch and sucrose metabolism, and plant hormone signal transduction. WGCNA identified six co-regulatory networks containing 38 candidate hub genes associated with ribosome biogenesis repression, organellar metabolic reprogramming, auxin transduction, and redox homeostasis maintenance. These findings reveal a shade adaptation syndrome of Coffea arabica as a facultative shade species, providing an integrative phenotypic, physiological, metabolic, and molecular framework for shade management optimization in coffee agroforestry systems.
authors: Yu H, Fu X, Hu F, Bi X, Li Y, Li Y, Gao X.

title: Metabolic reprogramming by caloric restriction enhances acute phase virological control and reduces chronic inflammation during SIV infection.
abstract: Nutrient metabolism influences HIV-1 replication, antiviral immunity, and chronic inflammation, yet remains difficult to leverage therapeutically. Using a non-human primate model of HIV-1, we modulated metabolism through caloric restriction (CR). Four months of 30% CR was safe and induced metabolic reprogramming in rhesus macaques. Compared with ad libitum-fed animals, CR reduced gut mucosal CCR5+ CD4+ T cell frequencies. Following SIV infection, CR reduced acute viremia, dampened type I interferon signaling, and enhanced CD8+ T cell cycling in lymphoid tissues. CR-associated protection coincided with glycolytic upregulation, supporting an early reduction in viremia that waned over time. Following antiretroviral therapy, CR limited gastrointestinal immune activation, improved tricarboxylic acid cycle flux, and reduced plasma sCD14 and TNF-related molecules. Blood SIV DNA remained unchanged, suggesting GI inflammation can be decoupled from viral persistence. These findings demonstrate that dietary intervention can limit lentiviral pathology while revealing the temporally constrained nature of glycolysis in supporting antiviral responses.
authors: Suresh Babu N, Perdios C, Hallmets M, Brown AT, Coleman C, Fennessey CM, Allers C, Moström MJ, Khare P, Zhang C, Smith BT, Golden NA, Myers A, Doyle-Meyers L, Blaney A, Blair RV, Saied AA, Colman R, Keele BF, Le A, Palmer CS, Mudd JC.

title: A Translation Protocol for Cross-Paradigm Dialogue: Decomposing the Meridian Doctrine Within the Evolutionary Information Layering Framework
abstract: The biomedical sciences and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) describe the same body in vocabularies that have long been mutually unintelligible, and both sides bear the cost: biology discards a rich, structured corpus of clinical phenomenology, while TCM lacks a mechanistic idiom it can defend without ontological commitment. Here we propose a translation protocol built on the Evolutionary Information Layering (EIL) framework, which describes biological coordination as superimposed informational layers, from ancient bioelectric and connective-tissue coordination (Layer 0) to neural amplification and cortical control. The protocol enforces four rules: operationalization of every classical term (R1), bidirectional symmetry of translation (R2), explicit confidence grading of every mapping (R3), and ontological neutrality toward qi (R4). Using the meridian doctrine as a demonstration case, we decompose ten classical terms across EIL layers, assigning each component a candidate carrier, an evidence grade, and falsifiable predictions, and we work three examples—deqi, propagated sensation along channels, and acupoint specificity—in detail. EIL's masking principle—fast neural signals overshadowing slower ancestral coordination channels—explains why quiet, low-noise observation could detect phenomena that instrumentation optimized for neural signals filters out. The framework claims neither the substantial existence of qi nor clinical efficacy; its test is whether biologists can derive predictions from classical statements, and whether TCM practitioners recognize their doctrine, undistorted, in translation.
authors: Hu D.

title: Hormetic Biphasic Effects of MSC-Derived Extracellular Vesicles: From Preconditioning and Redox Homeostasis to Calcium Dysregulation and Apoptosis
abstract: Extracellular vesicles released by mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC-EVs) are increasingly viewed as candidates for cell-free neuroprotection, but their dose-response behavior in ischemic settings is poorly defined. Using rat hippocampal neuroglial cultures, we asked whether MSC-EVs can reproduce a hypoxia-like preconditioned state and how vesicle concentration shapes cell fate. EVs isolated from human placental MSCs by differential centrifugation were applied for 24 h at 2.4×108–2.4×109 particles/mL. Low-dose EVs (2.4×108) strengthened hypoxic preconditioning, attenuated OGD-induced global Ca2+ elevations, improved survival and metabolic activity, and shifted transcription toward anti-apoptotic (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL), neurotrophic (Gdnf), antioxidant (Sod1, Cat, HO-1), and pro-survival (Hif1α, Stat3) programs while lowering basal ROS. High-dose EVs (9.6×108 and above) reversed these effects: preconditioning was lost, Ca2+ oscillations became uncontrolled and progressed to overload, ROS rose, and pro-inflammatory (Tnfα, Il-1β) and pro-apoptotic (Caspase-3) genes were induced. Thus, MSC-EVs act within a narrow hormetic window, exerting protective effects at low doses and harmful effects at high doses; this constraint must inform therapeutic dosing.
authors: Turovsky EA, Turovskaya MV, Zinchenko VP, Yurin A, Sukhikh GT, Silachev DN.

title: Profile-First Model Selection for Specialized Image Annotation: A Handball Knowledge Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
abstract: Selecting vision-language models to annotate specialized-domain images requires evidence that general-purpose benchmarks may not provide: current domain knowledge, correct domain con-cepts, and restraint where the image is inconclusive. We present a profile-first protocol for pre-deployment evaluation and instantiate it as the Handball Knowledge Benchmark (HKB). HKB separately evaluates productive terminology, rules and tactics, and both general and hand-ball-specific interpretation of images. Diagnostics cover rule currency, answer-order robustness, fabrication and warranted abstention. A provider-diverse judge panel with provider-aware recusal scores open-ended responses. Among the 19 ranked multimodal candidates, GPT-5.6 Sol led all four dimensions (G1 0.97, G2 98.8%, G3 8.22/7.98), but below it ranks order depended on dimension weighting. Diagnostics exposed mismatches hidden by aggregate scores: high rules accuracy coex-isted with superseded rule knowledge, reliable sport recognition with scarce warranted abstention under ambiguity, and near-identical general visual scores with a 1.6-point gap in handball-specific interpretation. Results were stable across judges and aggregation rules. Under an illustrative deci-sion rule, six admissible candidates differed about threefold in inference cost. Therefore, we suggest displaying domain competencies as a profile and not as a rank, while the protocol can be transferred to other domains by replacing the handball content.
authors: Hrga I, Ivasic-Kos M.

title: Anti-Melanogenic Potential of Phenolic Fractions from Naematelia aurantialba: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background:  Naematelia aurantialba has a solid research foundation in cultivation and polysaccharide chemistry, yet the systematic characterization of its low-molecular-weight phenolic constituents lags behind, and direct evidence linking them to melanogenesis regulation is lacking. Methods: Following the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA), we conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and CNKI (from inception to September 2026); 81 studies were included and appraised within three evidence tiers and a methodological/translational reference framework. Results: N. aurantialba contains extractable and quantifiable phenolic and flavonoid constituents, its extracts exhibit chemical antioxidant activity, and processing and fermentation strategies can influence phenolic parameters; however, the evidence stops at chemical occurrence and antioxidant screening, with no compound-level confirmation, human tyrosinase or melanocyte model validation, or human pigmentation endpoint data retrieved, and analogous evidence from Sanghuangporus and Ganoderma cannot be directly extrapolated owing to species specificity. Conclusions: N. aurantialba phenolic fractions should be positioned as a candidate resource for anti-melanogenesis research rather than a proven whitening ingredient; priority should be given to phenolic-targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) annotation, bioassay-guided fractionation, recombinant human tyrosinase assays, and cytotoxicity-corrected melanocyte models.
authors: Zhang L, Hu Q, He M, Li B, Sun Y, Yang B.

title: Spatially Convergent Encoding of Linked Data Through Assembled DNA Nanostructures.
abstract: DNA-based storage is a promising candidate for next-generation data media, providing a powerful strategy for preserving digital information in molecular formats. As information complexity increases, multiple DNA molecules are often used to encode related data elements, but their independent distribution can compromise information linkage during amplification-based readout. Although microdroplet PCR reduces amplification bias through spatial compartmentalization, stochastic partitioning of individual DNA molecules may hinder the recovery of associated information. Here, we present a Y-shaped DNA nanostructure system that integrates multiple related DNA sequences into a single molecular scaffold, enabling physical co-localization of linked information before compartmentalization. The Y-shaped architecture serves as a unified input unit for microdroplet PCR, allowing coordinated amplification and accurate recovery of associated data within individual droplets. By maintaining molecular linkage during processing, this strategy improves the uniformity of DNA-encoded linked information recovery. Overall, this system provides a programmable framework for DNA data organization and droplet-based retrieval of linked information.
authors: Huang Y, Ran X, Jiang M, Song Y.

title: In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics.
abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions.
authors: Yang E, Aceves-Salvador J, Castrillon C, Herrmann US, Akama-Garren EH, Carroll MC, Moffitt JR.

title: Association of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and characterization of a stroke related five gene immune signature: an exploratory study.
abstract: BackgroundDietary fiber intake has been associated with cerebrovascular health, motivating investigation of its relationship with inflammation and stroke-related immune expression.MethodsWe combined NHANES population analyses with whole blood microarray and single-cell transcriptomic analyses to examine dietary associations and characterize a stroke-related gene signature. NHANES analyses included 34,928 adults from 2005 to 2018, including 1,348 with self-reported stroke history. Associations were examined using fully adjusted survey-weighted logistic regression, with a sensitivity analysis using two-day mean intake. Candidate genes were selected using GSE16561 and external gene resources, followed by LASSO selection and external validation in 46 GSE58294 participants. Single-cell analysis included 91,176 cells from three paired donors.ResultsEach unit increase in ln(fiber intake + 0.1) was associated with an odds ratio of 0.755 (95% confidence interval 0.663 to 0.861) for stroke history. Analysis of two-day mean intake showed a consistent association, with an odds ratio of 0.601 (0.499 to 0.723). Higher fiber intake was also associated with lower NLR, MLR, SIRI, and CRP levels. Of 15 candidate genes, LASSO retained CD163, PAK1, FOS, PTGS2, and HDAC4. The model achieved an external area under the curve of 0.964 (0.916 to 1.000). Single-cell analysis localized CD163, PAK1, and PTGS2 predominantly to monocytes and conventional dendritic cells. FOS showed broad expression, whereas HDAC4 was relatively enriched in naive CD4 T cells.ConclusionsThese findings identify inverse associations of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and systemic inflammatory markers, together with a discriminative five-gene blood signature and its cellular distribution, providing directions for further investigation of nutritional and immune processes in stroke.
journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
authors: Zhang C, Zhang J.

title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods.
abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail 'Viviparus' sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. High-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography and microfossil extraction reveal key ecological adaptations: obligate ovoviviparity with up to 16 embryonic shells showing an axial developmental size gradient within the maternal body whorl, female-biased sexual size dimorphism, and continuous indeterminate growth. Analyses of gastrointestinal residues and taphonomic associations further indicate trophic flexibility (epilithic microalgal grazing, suspension feeding, and detritivory) alongside opportunistic microhabitat use within articulated unionid bivalves. This high-fidelity preservation-retaining delicate embryonic shells, intact protoconchs, and organic residues-is linked to a distinctive taphonomic window, wherein alkaline ash from palaeo-wildfires is inferred to have buffered ambient freshwater acidity, mitigating post-mortem carbonate dissolution. Our findings demonstrate that modern-type viviparid reproductive and feeding adaptations were already established by the Early Cretaceous, illustrating how wildfire-mediated geochemical buffering can preserve rare biological records in Mesozoic limnic ecosystems.
authors: Yoshimura T, Nakayama K, Asato K, Noda Y, Fujimoto H, Nakagawa Y, Legrand J, Ikeda M, Sasaki T.

title: Luteolin Alleviates Renal Fibrosis in Diabetic Kidney Disease via Activation of the Cx32-Nrf2 Signaling Axis.
abstract: Luteolin (Lut) is a flavonoid found in many medicinal plants, and previous studies have shown that it can slow the progression of diabetic kidney disease (DKD), although the mechanism is incompletely defined. This study asked whether Lut protects against DKD by acting on the connexin32 (Cx32)-Nrf2 signaling axis to suppress ferroptosis and partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Renal fibrosis, oxidative stress, EMT, and ferroptosis related markers, as well as Cx32/Nrf2 expression were assessed in db/db mice and high glucose (HG)-induced NRK-52E cells. Microdissected human kidney transcriptomes were obtained from GEO and analyzed in R. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to test whether Lut interacts with Cx32. siRNA knockdown was used to test whether Cx32 is required for its effects. Lut improved renal function, reduced fibrosis, lowered ROS, EMT, and ferroptosis in db/db mice and HG-induced NRK-52E cells. Additionally, Cx32 and Nrf2 protein levels were reduced, which was restored by Lut treatment. And overexpression of Cx32 promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation. In human diabetic kidney transcriptomes, Cx32 and Nrf2 transcripts changed reciprocally and were inversely correlated across two independent cohorts, supporting Cx32 as a candidate upstream node. Molecular docking indicated that Lut binds to the ARG22 and THR18 residues of Cx32, and CETSA showed that Lut increased the thermal stability of Cx32. Knockdown of Cx32 abolished Nrf2 activation by Lut. Therefore, we concluded that Lut attenuates renal fibrosis in DKD by activating the Cx32-Nrf2 signaling axis.
authors: Liang S, Nong Q, Chen Y, He Y, Feng T, Chen G, Zhang Q, Liu Z, Ou G, Tang D, Jiao Y, Chen Z.

title: DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-based compound, ameliorates MASLD by restoring metabolic-redox homeostasis and promoting hepatic lipid remodeling.
abstract: BackgroundMetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a highly prevalent chronic liver disorder for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Autophagy is a fundamental intracellular degradation and recycling process that maintains hepatic homeostasis by regulating lipid metabolism and mitigating lipid-induced cellular stress, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for MASLD.Approach and resultsThrough an in vitro reporter-based screening of a chemical compound library, DTC1225, a novel benzothiazole-derived compound was identified as an autophagy activator that inhibited mTORC1 signaling, promoted transcription factor EB nuclear translocation, activated the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and enhanced autophagic flux. Functionally, DTC1225 reduced lipid droplet accumulation in steatotic HepG2 cells and differentiated 3 T3-L1 adipocytes, accompanied by alterations in autophagy-related markers and gene expression, and attenuation of MASLD-associated cellular injury. In a 4-month fructose, palmitate, and cholesterol diet-induced mouse model of MASLD, DTC1225 alleviated hepatic injury, modulated autophagic machinery, improved lipid metabolic profiles, restored redox homeostasis, and attenuated early-stage hepatic fibrosis. Hepatic lipidomics analysis further revealed that DTC1225 induced selective structural lipid remodeling, shifting the lipidome toward longer-chain and more unsaturated species, with a preferential enrichment of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids-containing lipids, which may contribute to attenuated lipotoxicity and modulation of membrane fluidity.ConclusionsDTC1225 ameliorates MASLD-associated hepatic pathology through multifaceted mechanisms involving coordinated modulation of autophagy-related pathways, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, accompanied by favorable hepatic lipid remodeling. These findings provide a critical rationale for further development of DTC1225 as an innovative therapeutic candidate for MASLD and its associated complications.
authors: Zhang S, Selvaraj B, Kim YE, Lee H, Farzand S, Nguyen QNS, Lim SM, Pae AN, Yang HO, Bian Y, Lee G, Lee JW, Kim J.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of PM2.5 ovarian toxicity: pulmonary particulate instillation associates with leukocyte infiltration and impaired granulosa cholesterol biosynthesis.
abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure impairs female reproductive capacity and accelerates follicular depletion, yet ovarian responses remain poorly illustrated at single-cell resolution. To evaluate early multicellular alterations following exposure, we combined a mouse model of repeated pulmonary PM2.5 instillation with single-cell transcriptomic profiling and in situ histological validation. We found that pulmonary PM2.5 instillation expanded the ovarian immune compartment through B-lineage lymphocyte and neutrophil infiltration, whereas resident macrophages adopted a C1qa-enriched scavenger profile without canonical NLRP3 inflammasome activation. At the intercellular interface, immune-derived TGF-β1 and TNF signals engaged somatic receptors and elevated downstream JAK-STAT pathway activity across recipient ovarian somatic cells. Specifically, in follicular granulosa cells, immune-somatic signaling suppressed the cholesterol-biosynthesis program independently of autonomous inflammatory stress, accompanied by matrix remodeling in stromal fibroblasts. Furthermore, dynamic trajectory modeling and in silico perturbation prioritized STAT1 as a candidate regulator of follicular deviation toward atretic fates. Concordantly, in situ multiplex immunofluorescence, TUNEL, and immunohistochemical assays verified parenchymal leukocyte localization, somatic Phospho-STAT1 nuclear engagement, preserved granulosa HMGCR expression, and follicular granulosa apoptosis in intact ovaries. In summary, our findings indicate that pulmonary PM2.5 instillation disrupts ovarian homeostasis through leukocyte infiltration, granulosa sterol suppression, and STAT1-associated follicular atresia.
authors: Zhang L, Zheng Y, Shi X, Li N, Tian J, Duan S.

title: Abamectin and mancozeb at environmentally relevant concentrations: comparative ecotoxicity versus a Trichoderma asperellum biopesticide.
abstract: The increasing replacement of synthetic pesticides by microbial biopesticides requires robust evidence of environmental safety, particularly under water contamination scenarios with potential implications for drinking water. This study compared commercial formulations based on Trichoderma asperellum, mancozeb, and abamectin at environmentally realistic concentrations, using an integrated battery of bioassays with Allium cepa (cytotoxicity, cytogenotoxicity, and cellular biomarkers), Lactuca sativa (phytotoxicity), and aquatic organisms (Artemia salina and Daphnia similis for acute toxicity and Raphidocelis subcapitata for chronic toxicity). Overall, the synthetic pesticide formulations exhibited more pronounced and biologically disruptive effect profiles, whereas the T. asperellum-based biopesticide formulation showed a lower magnitude of toxic responses and no evidence of genotoxicity under the tested conditions, although detectable cellular changes occurred. These findings support the use of multi-parameter and multi-species approaches to discriminate risk profiles and highlight the need to incorporate bioassays into the assessment of pesticide contamination relevant to drinking-water quality.
authors: Ventura de Souza V, Fraga LR, Ferreira JD, Vergilio CDS, Trujillo FA, da Silva Souza T.

title: Glycosaminoglycan-Induced Macrophage Reprogramming Orchestrates Pro-Regenerative Crosstalk with Fibroblasts.
abstract: Macrophages and fibroblasts play central roles in coordinating inflammation and tissue repair, whilst dysregulation of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk drives pathological outcomes such as chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), key components of the extracellular matrix (ECM), interact with cytokines and growth factors that modulate macrophage polarisation and direct fibroblast activity, making them attractive candidates for developing immune-instructive biomaterials. However, the optimal GAG compositions that promote macrophage-mediated repair and fibroblast-driven ECM remodelling remain unclear. Here, we report an unbiased screening of 82 surface-adsorbed GAG combinations to identify candidates capable of modulating macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Leveraging cytokine profiling, surface marker immunostaining, gene expression, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical clustering, we identified 'hit' GAG combinations that induced distinct, non-canonical macrophage activation programmes characterised by coordinated inflammatory and regulatory signalling, alongside enhanced fibroblast proliferation. Shortlisted formulations were validated using expanded biological replication, orthogonal phenotypic, transcriptional and functional analyses, assessment in macrophage-fibroblast co-culture systems, and in an in vivo diabetic wound model. These data demonstrated that 'hit' GAG formulations modulated macrophage functional activation states, promoted collagen and ECM synthesis, facilitated vascular and lymphatic vessel formation, and accelerated wound closure. Complementary metabolomic profiling using OrbiSIMS and molecular formula prediction (MFP), revealed macrophage metabolic reprogramming as a potential mechanism underlying these pro-healing effects. Collectively, this study established an unbiased methodology for discovering immune-instructive GAGs in supporting pro-healing responses for potential wound-healing applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are key extracellular matrix components with significant potential to regulate immune responses. However, their immunomodulatory effects are highly context-dependent, varying with sulfation pattern, molecular composition, and the local microenvironment, making it challenging to identify GAG combinations that consistently promote pro-regenerative immune responses and tissue repair. Here, we developed an unbiased combinatorial screening platform to systematically identify GAG combinations that reprogram macrophages toward pro-regenerative functional states. The selected GAG combinations enhanced macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in vitro and improved diabetic wound healing in vivo by promoting collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and lymphatic remodelling. OrbiSIMS metabolomics further revealed macrophage metabolic reprogramming associated with these regenerative responses. This work establishes a generalizable discovery framework for identifying immune-regulatory GAG formulations and provides new design principles for developing extracellular matrix-inspired immunomodulatory biomaterials for regenerative medicine.
authors: Du Q, Mace K, Wong KFC, Lawler K, Kotowska A, AlRomaihi RA, Latif A, Hook AL, Ghaemmaghami AM.

title: Reprogramming flavonoid glycosylation by bridging advanced biocatalysis and systems synthetic biology.
abstract: Flavonoid glycosides exhibit profound pharmacological and nutritional value, yet their industrial-scale acquisition is severely hampered by low abundance in plant extracts and the stereochemical complexity of chemical synthesis. Synthetic biology offers a sustainable alternative, while the deployment of natural plant uridine diphosphate-dependent glycosyltransferases (UGTs) is intrinsically bottlenecked by low catalytic efficiency, poor stability, and severe intracellular metabolic competition. This review systematically explores the paradigm shifts in the biomanufacturing of these complex molecules, highlighting how the methodological evolution in UGT discovery has evolved from traditional sequence homology to multi-omics and AI-driven predictive models. Multidimensional engineering of UGTs spanning from active-site remodeling to distal allosteric regulation and computational-design is elucidated to precisely manipulate catalytic efficacy, enzyme stability, substrate promiscuity, and catalytic regioselectivity. Bridging the gap between optimized biocatalysts and robust microbial cell factories requires critical systems metabolic engineering strategies, including the rewiring of intracellular UDP-sugar flux, the elimination of catabolic sinks, and the deployment of spatiotemporally decoupled microbial consortia. Cell-free synthesis cascades offer a highly controllable alternative to circumvent in vivo physiological constraints. A strategic roadmap for future research emphasizes AI-driven de novo enzyme design, autonomous single-cell dynamic regulation, and the valorization of lignocellulosic biomass to achieve unprecedented atom economy. Ultimately, this integrated framework provides a scalable, multidimensional blueprint for the sustainable and green biomanufacturing of high-value flavonoid glycosides.
authors: Zhang J, Zhang J, Pan Y, Liu G, Yao Y.

title: Contrasting effects of Ca<sup>2+</sup>, Zn<sup>2+</sup>, and Fe<sup>2+</sup> on uranium uptake in rice (Oryza sativa L.): ionomic and transcriptomic evidence.
abstract: Uranium contamination in agricultural soils threatens crop safety, but the mechanisms regulating uranium uptake in rice (Oryza sativa L.) remain poorly understood. This study investigated these mechanisms using a hydroponic experiment that examined the effects of Ca²⁺, Zn²⁺, and Fe²⁺ availability under uranium stress through growth, uranium accumulation, ion homeostasis, and transcriptome analyses. Fe²⁺ deficiency severely inhibited growth and intensified uranium toxicity. Ca²⁺ deficiency reduced root uranium content to 10.4% of that in the U-alone treatment, followed by Zn²⁺ deficiency. Uranium stress disrupted Ca²⁺ and Fe²⁺ homeostasis, which was partially restored by exogenous ion treatments. Transcriptome analysis showed that doubled Fe²⁺ and Ca²⁺ deficiency induced the largest sets of differentially expressed genes, enriched in iron transport/oxidative stress responses and cell wall modification, respectively. Correlation analysis identified candidate genes associated with root uranium content. These findings suggest that Ca²⁺, Zn²⁺, and Fe²⁺ availability is associated with changes in uranium uptake through putative pathways such as cell wall modification and transporter competition. The candidate genes identified here require functional validation, and further studies are needed to determine whether they can inform molecular breeding strategies for reducing uranium accumulation in rice.
journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
authors: Liu C, Zhang S, Guo D.

title: A tumor-responsive p53-loaded nanovesicle system for senescence induction and immune microenvironment reprogramming.
abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) critically regulates the balance between antitumor immunity and immune evasion. Although cellular senescence can promote immune-mediated tumor clearance through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), this mechanism is frequently compromised by loss of p53 function, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Consequently, strategies capable of restoring p53 activity while harnessing intact immune-responsive pathways are urgently needed. Integrated transcriptomic analyses provided a computational basis for this therapeutic strategy. Bulk RNA-seq demonstrated that, in TNBC, the downstream SASP-immune activation axis remains largely preserved, whereas the upstream p53-SASP coupling is disrupted, supporting the concept that exogenous p53 restoration may effectively re-engage immune programs. Single-cell RNA-seq further revealed that p53-functional malignant cells exhibit enhanced tumor-immune communication and immune-recognition signals, reinforcing the feasibility of p53 reactivation to remodel the TIME. Guided by these insights, we engineered a dual-functional, tumor-responsive nanovesicle system for p53 delivery. Escherichia coli was genetically modified to express p53, and p53-loaded outer membrane vesicles (OMV@p53) were coated with a biomimetic calcium phosphate shell via bionanomorphic mineralization, yielding acid-responsive nanovesicles (Ca@OMV@p53; 200-300 nm). This coating enhanced biocompatibility and enabled pH-triggered release within the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. In vitro, Ca@OMV@p53 efficiently induced tumor cell senescence and promoted M1 macrophage polarization. In vivo, treatment markedly increased intratumoral infiltration of M1 macrophages and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, accompanied by elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines and sustained immune activation. Together, this study demonstrates that p53-restoration via a tumor-responsive nanodelivery system can synergistically induce senescence and immune-mediated tumor clearance. By integrating systems-level bioinformatics with experimental nanomedicine, our work establishes a rational framework for senescence-based immunomodulatory cancer therapy.

title: Senescence induces clonal failure of hepatocyte plasticity and reshapes regenerative lineages.
abstract: Background & aimsTelomere dysregulation is a central driver of cellular senescence and chronic liver disease. Yet how physiological telomeric attrition, rather than uniform telomere loss, leads to hepatic functional decline remains unclear. We therefore investigate how resolvable telomere dysfunction reshapes liver regeneration.MethodsAn adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR-based strategy was developed to induce resolvable telomeric breaks in mouse hepatocytes while preserving endogenous telomere maintenance. Clonal dynamics, lineage tracing, and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling were used to characterize senescent hepatocyte behavior during chronic liver injury. Human cirrhotic liver samples were analyzed to assess the relationship between hepatocyte telomere length and intermediate cellular states. An in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte plasticity under telomere stress.ResultsTelomere-induced senescence did not substantially impair hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic function, but induced a clonal imbalance shaped by telomerase expression. Lineage tracing and single-nucleus transcriptomics demonstrated that senescent hepatocytes exhibited impaired hepatocyte-to-ductal metaplasia during chronic injury, with limited entry into the dedifferentiated state and failure to fully activate the ductal program. This incomplete transition disrupted epithelial composition and exacerbated the ductular reaction. Analyses of human cirrhotic livers revealed an association between preserved telomere integrity and bipotent hepatocyte states. Furthermore, the in vivo CRISPR screen identified regulators of hepatocyte dedifferentiation under telomere stress.ConclusionsThese findings identify senescence as a barrier to hepatobiliary clonal balance rather than a direct trigger of hepatocyte loss. Telomere dysfunction thereby promotes pathological epithelial remodeling during chronic liver injury.Impact and implicationsTelomere shortening is a common feature of chronic liver disease, but how it functionally contributes to regenerative failure remains incompletely understood. Our study shows that telomere dysfunction does not simply compromise hepatocyte survival or basal metabolic capacity. Instead, senescence acts as a clonal and lineage-selective constraint that limits hepatocyte plasticity and alters which cells contribute to regeneration. These findings provide a mechanistic link between telomere attrition, loss of regenerative diversity, and progressive liver dysfunction, and suggest that preservation of hepatocyte plasticity may be an important determinant of regenerative capacity in chronic liver disease.
authors: Zheng Q, Chen J, Hu X, Zhang Y, Yu S, Sun N, Zhu QY, Zhao B, Xu X, Lin S.

title: Intermolecular disulfide bond formation promotes Hsp42 higher-order assembly and shapes client selection in yeast.
abstract: Cellular redox homeostasis plays a critical role in regulating protein function, including chaperone activity, through reversible oxidation of cysteine and methionine residues. Previously, we found that budding yeast cells experiencing redox imbalance due to inactivated thioredoxin reductase (trr1Δ) activate the heat shock response and induce hyperaccumulation of the small heat shock protein/sequestrase Hsp42 with misfolded proteins. Building on that finding, this study identified cysteine 127 (C127) within Hsp42 as a redox-active residue that becomes oxidized in trr1Δ cells, upon treatment with the powerful oxidant hydrogen peroxide, or by exposure to the cysteine crosslinker divinyl sulfone (DVSF). In trr1Δ cells, C127 oxidation promoted intermolecular disulfide bond formation and contributed to Hsp42 homo-oligomerization. We show that stable oligomerization requires both the prion-like domain (PrLD) and C127 oxidation. While Hsp42-GFP formed prominent persistent foci in trr1Δ cells, replacement of C127 with non-thiol reactive serine decreased foci formation. Furthermore, the C127S mutation diminished Hsp42 oligomerization and sedimentability. Immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry analysis revealed that Hsp42 in trr1Δ cells preferentially associated with mitochondrial precursor proteins accumulated in the cytoplasm, as well as oxidation-reduction enzymes. The observed client selectivity was altered by the C127S mutation that diversified the spectrum of Hsp42-associated proteins. Collectively, these findings identify Cys127 as a redox-active switch that regulates Hsp42 assembly, foci formation, stability, and client specificity in response to oxidative stress.
authors: Duong LD, Escobar-Osorio D, Saltzman AB, Morano KA.

title: A930024E05Rik is a hypoxia-upregulated lncRNA that facilitates atrial fibrosis by sponging let-7 miRNAs to modulate collagen expression in cardiomyocytes.
abstract: Hypoxia-induced atrial fibrosis plays a central role in the development and progression of atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the involvement of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in this process is not fully defined. This study aimed to identify hypoxia-responsive lncRNAs and investigate their functional roles in hypoxia-mediated fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomic profiling of HL-1 atrial cardiomyocytes under hypoxic conditions, followed by bioinformatic prediction and molecular validation, including luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, RNA immunoprecipitation, and gain- and loss-of-function analyses, were performed to delineate the downstream effects. Among lncRNA candidates, A930024E05Rik was markedly upregulated by hypoxia and inversely associated with let-7 miRNA expression. Further analyses demonstrated that A930024E05Rik physically interacts with let-7a and let-7e, is enriched in let-7-dependent gene-silencing machinery, and modulates the expression of collagen genes, COL1A1 and COL3A1. Functional assessments demonstrated that A930024E05Rik enhances collagen production by alleviating let-7-mediated repression, as evidenced by reciprocal effects of gene silencing and overexpression. In conclusion, these findings support a competing endogenous RNA mechanism in which A930024E05Rik modulates let-7 miRNA availability to control collagen expression in hypoxic cardiomyocytes, highlighting potential avenues for the application of this A930024E05Rik-let-7 regulatory axis on AF management.
authors: Ting KH, Su SC, Chu HJ, Tang CH, Yang SF, Ueng KC.

title: Curdione restores brain-spleen axis-mediated Th1/Th2 immune homeostasis via modulation of LCN2 to alleviate CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevanceCurcuma wenyujin Y.H.Chen & C.Ling supplies both Curcumae Rhizoma (the rhizome) and Curcumae Radix (the root tuber). Curcumae Radix is documented in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia (2020) for moving qi, relieving depression and clearing the heart, and is used in classic formulas such as Baijin Wan to treat depression-like syndromes. Curdione is a major sesquiterpenoid constituent of this species.Aim of the studyThis study aimed to investigate the mechanism underlying curdione-mediated amelioration of depressive-like behaviors in CUMS-exposed mice, and to elucidate the core role of LCN2 and the brain-spleen axis in this process.Materials and methodsA CUMS-induced mouse depression model was established, with interventions including splenic sympathetic denervation (SDN) and administration of the LCN2 inhibitor ZINC00640089. Assessments were conducted via behavioral tests (OFT; EPMT; TST; MWM), histopathology, ELISA, flow cytometry, qRT-PCR, Western blot and transcriptomics.ResultsCUMS exposure significantly induced depressive-like behaviors, hippocampal neuronal injury, splenic atrophy and Th1/Th2 immune deviation (elevated IFN-γ, decreased IL-4 and IL-5) in mice, which were effectively reversed by SDN. Curdione ameliorated depressive-like behaviors, and restored Th1/Th2 balance. Transcriptomic screening and experimental validation identified LCN2 as a candidate key mediator; curdione significantly downregulated its aberrant overexpression in both the hippocampus and spleen. Pharmacological inhibition of LCN2 mimicked the antidepressant and immunomodulatory effects of curdione.ConclusionCurdione exerts antidepressant effects by indirectly modulating LCN2 to restore brain-spleen axis-mediated Th1/Th2 immune homeostasis. These findings not only support the involvement of LCN2 in the pathogenesis of depression, but also validate the therapeutic potential of modulating neuro-immune crosstalk mediators, supporting the development of curdione as a promising natural antidepressant agent. Our findings further provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional antidepressant use of Curcuma wenyujin.
authors: Huang L, Huang J, Wang Y, Shen B, Tang X, Lai C, Gao Y.

title: Coupling corncob fractionation with covalent enzyme assembly for resveratrol biosynthesis from lignin-derived p-coumaric acid.
abstract: Lignin is an abundant renewable source of aromatic carbon, yet its biological valorization remains limited by poor coordination between biomass fractionation and microbial pathway design. We combined urea-KOH (UK) fractionation with pathway-entry optimization and SpyTag/SpyCatcher-mediated enzyme assembly to match the recovery of lignin-derived precursors with microbial resveratrol biosynthesis. UK fractionation released 191.97 ± 7.42 mg p-coumaric acid (p-CA) per g Klason lignin and retained cellulose-rich solids suitable for saccharification. Purified lignin-derived p-CA and glucose-rich hydrolysate from the same corncob were then used as the aromatic precursor and principal carbon source, respectively. In E. coli, replacing plant 4-coumarate: CoA ligase with a lignin-catabolic feruloyl-CoA synthetase improved p-CA activation. Tests using matched vector backgrounds showed that reactive SpyTag/SpyCatcher pairs formed complex-sized species without increasing the soluble abundance of either enzyme. In reconstituted cascades, this assembly increased resveratrol formation and reduced p-coumaroyl-CoA exposure, even though upstream-enzyme activity remained unchanged. These results are consistent with tighter coupling between the cascade enzymes. Following optimization, 5-L fed-batch fermentation produced 803.85 ± 10.06 mg L-1 resveratrol. Exploratory structural modelling and molecular dynamics simulations suggested closer enzyme-pair arrangements and smaller ligand displacements in several assembled models, offering a possible explanation for the improved cascade coupling. The resulting process combines complementary corncob fractions for resveratrol production through coordinated fractionation and pathway engineering.
authors: Zhang Z, Gao L, Ali MY, Haq WU, Li W, Ma S, Zhan L, Wu X, Zhu D.

title: Short-term exposure to 2,3,6,7-tetrachlorocarbazole induces early serum metabolic disturbance and hepatic lipid remodeling in mice.
abstract: Polyhalogenated carbazoles (PHCZs), particularly 2,3,6,7-tetrachlorocarbazole (2367-CCZ), are emerging dioxin-like contaminants with bioaccumulation potential, but their early mammalian metabolic effects remain insufficiently understood. Here, male mice were orally exposed to 2367-CCZ for 7 days, and early molecular responses were examined using serum metabolomics followed by liver lipidomics. Untargeted serum metabolomics was first applied to capture systemic metabolic signatures, including lipid-associated metabolic changes. To further resolve hepatic lipid remodeling, a DDA-derived and manually curated liver lipid annotation library was constructed and then used to support high-throughput DIA(HDMSE) lipidomics across exposure groups. No overt changes in body or organ weights were observed, whereas serum metabolomics revealed glutamate/glutathione-related and lipid-associated metabolic responses, with glutathione metabolism showing the strongest nominal serum pathway-level signal. The DDA library-assisted liver lipidomics workflow identified 60 candidate differential lipids and highlighted glycerophospholipid-centered hepatic lipid remodeling as the primary liver response. Additional changes in sphingolipid-related lipids, neutral lipids, oxidized fatty acids, and authentic-standard-confirmed decreases in alpha-linolenic acid and eicosapentaenoic acid further indicated hepatic lipid remodeling and impaired fatty acid homeostasis. Together, these serum and liver omics data indicate early hepatometabolic perturbation and hepatic lipid remodeling in the absence of detectable changes in body or organ weights.
authors: Li X, Zeng Q, Tao W, Guo Z, Zhao B.

title: A tumor biology-informed interpretation of TNM 9 in HPV-associated OPSCC.
abstract: BackgroundThe 9th edition of the TNM classification (TNM-9) refines anatomical staging in head and neck cancer, maintaining p16-based categorization for HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). However, anatomical extent alone does not capture key biological and host-related determinants of clinical behavior.MethodsIn this concept-driven synthesis, we integrate TNM-9 anatomy with evidence on transcriptional viral activity, p16 discordance, nodal morphology including imaging-defined extranodal extension (iENE), immune microenvironment, and host modifiers such as smoking and comorbidity. We propose a layered integrative framework that preserves TNM-9 structure while contextualizing tumor biology. The review is based on a selective synthesis of key translational and clinical studies identified through literature searches and expert knowledge, without a formal systematic approach.ResultsTNM-9 improves anatomical prognostic stratification at the population level, but identical anatomical stages encompass biologically heterogeneous entities. HPV RNA expression distinguishes biologically favorable tumors from p16+/HPV-inactive disease. iENE retains prognostic relevance in HPV-associated OPSCC, although its radiological appearance may partly reflect immune-associated stromal remodeling and cystic nodal morphology rather than invasive behavior alone. Smoking exposure, comorbidity burden, and immune-related host factors modify survival independent of tumor extent, explaining different outcomes within identical TNM stages.ConclusionsTNM-9 should be interpreted as an anatomical framework supplemented by biological and host factors. A multidimensional understanding enhances clinical applicability, avoids overtreatment of biologically favorable disease and highlights high-risk phenotypes concealed by anatomy alone. This perspective supports precise, biology-informed risk assessment in HPV-associated OPSCC. .
authors: Hoffmann M, Tribius S.

title: Synergistic enhancement of chromium bioleaching by Oceanobacillus profundus and groundnut oil cake an optimized approach.
abstract: Heavy metal contamination, particularly hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)), poses severe environmental and public health risks due to its high toxicity, persistence, and carcinogenicity. Conventional remediation techniques are often expensive, inefficient, and environmentally unsustainable. This study investigates an eco-friendly and cost-effective bioleaching approach using the halophilic, metal-tolerant bacterium Oceanobacillus profundus coupled with groundnut oil cake (GOC) as a nutrient amendment to enhance chromium solubilization from contaminated soil. The Box-Behnken design (BBD) of response surface methodology (RSM) was applied to optimize key parameters, including incubation time, GOC concentration, and shaking rate. Optimal conditions 60 h incubation, 3% GOC, and 180 rpm resulted in a maximum chromium bioleaching efficiency of 45.4%. Sequential extraction analyses revealed a significant shift of chromium from residual and oxide-bound forms toward more labile carbonate-bound fractions, indicating enhanced mobility and bioavailability. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic use of O. profundus and GOC effectively accelerates chromium bioleaching while transforming its geochemical speciation, offering a sustainable strategy for remediating chromium-contaminated environments.
authors: Mani A, Narayanan M, Praburaman L.

title: Probing the biomolecular design space with generative modeling.
abstract: Discovering new-to-nature biomolecules requires navigating a design space that has only been sparsely explored. Traditional paradigms such as rational design, directed evolution, and high-throughput screening have enabled the development of many successful functional biomolecules, but are significantly limited when given an unseen target or novel function, where there is no starting point for design. Generative modeling offers a way to approximate the continuous manifold underlying observed biological data, enabling the sampling of new candidates beyond any finite dataset while remaining within the support of viable, functional biomolecules. Here, we outline recent progress in generative biomolecular design through an algorithmic lens, bridging theoretical foundations with its extensions and applications in truly de novo and controllable biomolecular design.
authors: Tang S, Zhang Y, Chatterjee P.

title: CD74 links MHC class II risk to tumor immune microenvironment remodeling across the Sjögren-to-lymphoma axis.
abstract: IntroductionSjögren's syndrome creates a lymphoma-prone inflammatory niche and confers one of the highest autoimmune risks of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Yet the genetic and cellular mechanisms that remodel this pre-neoplastic niche into a tumor-supportive immune microenvironment remain unclear. We integrated human genetics, single-cell transcriptomics and functional cell biology to identify an actionable mediator of this transition.MethodsWe combined bidirectional Mendelian randomization, directionality filtering, MHC-exclusion sensitivity analyses (chromosome 6: 25-35 Mb), colocalization and summary-based HLA fine-mapping. Single-cell RNA sequencing of salivary gland and splenic marginal-zone lymphoma was used to localize genetic risk, reconstruct cross-disease B-cell states and infer intercellular signaling. Mechanistic dependence was tested in IFN-γ-stimulated Raji B-lymphoma cells, and clinical relevance was evaluated in a public chronic lymphocytic leukemia cohort.ResultsGenetic liability to Sjögren's syndrome increased marginal-zone/MALT, diffuse large B-cell and overall non-Hodgkin lymphoma risk, and effects collapsed after MHC exclusion and resolved to the class II 8.1 ancestral haplotype. Single-cell analysis localized risk to salivary B cells and revealed disease-associated remodeling toward a lymphoid, MIF-rich, CD74-receiving microenvironment, with plasma cells as the largest MIF source. HLA-class-II/CD74 programs increased along the Sjögren-to-lymphoma B-cell trajectory. In Raji cells, MIF activated AKT/NF-κB/BCL-xL signaling and viability. ISO-1 or CD74 knockdown suppressed the pathway and increased cleaved PARP, whereas AKT activation partially rescued signaling and viability. Higher CD74 expression marked adverse outcome in an external B-cell malignancy cohort.ConclusionConvergent genetic, single-cell and perturbation evidence positions CD74 as a candidate organizer of a lymphoma-supportive immune microenvironment linking inherited MHC class II risk to B-cell survival. The MIF-CD74 axis provides a translational tumor-microenvironment target that requires tissue-level and prospective validation.
authors: Liu S, Li M, Wang Y, Xia X, Wang P, Ni Z, Li Q, Teng Q, Han W, Liu J, Wang X, Yu S, Zhang H, Meng X, Zhong F, Wang H.

title: Host resistance and pathogen aggressiveness vary along an elevation gradient in a wild plant-pathogen interaction.
abstract: Diversity in host resistance and pathogen virulence is ubiquitous in nature, determines infection outcomes, provides the raw material for antagonistic (co)evolution, and is fundamental to epidemiological dynamics. Yet empirical data on spatiotemporal variation of host and pathogen abundances together with measures of host resistance and pathogen virulence are rare. To address this gap, we surveyed host abundance and pathogen prevalence in four populations of a plant host and its specialist fungal pathogens along an elevation gradient. Using one of the pathogen species, we experimentally tested whether host resistance, pathogen virulence and aggressiveness vary among the study populations. Our measurements of infection success and severity across several hundred plant-pathogen pairs showed significant variation in both host resistance and pathogen aggressiveness among the populations, with resistance decreasing and aggressiveness increasing with elevation. Further, the high-elevation pathogen population produced the most severe infection on their local host population, whereas the low-elevation pathogen population produced the least severe infections on their local host populations. Our results reveal contrasting patterns between pathogen prevalence and key host and pathogen traits among populations along an environmental gradient, highlighting that shifts in pathogen distributions may reshape epidemiological and evolutionary dynamics between hosts and pathogens.
journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
authors: Rechsteiner M, Halliday FW, Giolai M, Wagner A, Laine AL.

title: Heartland Virus Disease in the United States, 2018-2024.
abstract: Heartland virus (HRTV), a tick-borne virus, was first discovered as a cause of human disease in Missouri in 2011. Heartland virus disease presents similarly to other tick-borne infectious diseases, with acute febrile illness accompanied by thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and elevated liver enzymes. In 2018, diagnostic testing for HTRV disease by reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction, IgM microsphere immunosorbent assay, and plaque reduction neutralization test became routinely available at the CDC. We describe the demographics and geographic distribution of patients tested for evidence of HRTV disease, and we note the clinical outcomes of patients with HRTV disease identified during 2018-2024. Of 279 patients tested, we identified 38 patients with laboratory evidence of HRTV disease (median of 5 patients per year). Patients resided in 13 states located in the eastern, southeastern, and central United States. All patients were ages 50 years old and older, 29 (76%) were male, and most (n = 36; 95%) had illness onset during April to September. Among patients with HRTV disease, 92% were hospitalized, and 13% died. Compared with patients with no evidence of HRTV disease, HRTV disease patients were older (median age = 68 versus 51 years old, P <0.05) and more limited in their geographic distribution. Through routine diagnostic testing, the number of HRTV disease cases identified in the United States has more than doubled, but the disease remains relatively uncommon. Continued surveillance and increased awareness among clinicians and public health officials can help improve understanding of the epidemiology and public health burden of HRTV disease.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
authors: Padda H, Baker M, Beddo M, Smith M, Hedges S, Popovitch J, Lindemann S, Petro E, Moncayo AC, Fisher T, Coughlin J, Richardson K, White J, Mason K, Schafer A, Broyhill J, Fitzpatrick KA, Laven J, Panella A, Velez J, Lehman J, Gould CV, Staples JE.

title: What do we really know about human immunometabolism in inflammatory disease?
abstract: Cellular metabolism is now recognised as an active regulator of immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. However, much of this conceptual framework derives from in vitro systems and animal models that may not fully reproduce human physiology or disease. Many studies of human immune metabolism are constrained by artificial culture conditions, tissue dissociation, limited pathway coverage, and a reliance on static measurements that do not directly quantify metabolic flux in vivo. Interpretation is further complicated by the use of blood samples as a surrogate for diseases that arise in specialised tissues, such as synovium, gut, and skin, and by the influence of systemic physiology, including hepatic substrate regulation, adipose tissue, endocrine and neuronal signalling, and the gut microbiota. In this review, we examine what current experimental approaches can infer about immune metabolism in humans, with a focus on immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Oncology provides a valuable methodological precedent through its use of tissue sampling, spatial profiling, and stable isotope tracing, while also illustrating the challenges of assigning metabolic activity to individual cell populations within heterogeneous tissues. We propose five priorities for the field: move beyond blood to inflammatory tissue; complement static abundance with dynamic, stable isotope flux analysis; integrate single cell, spatial, and imaging modalities; incorporate carefully designed human metabolic perturbations; and account for the wider systemic and pre-analytical context. The next phase of human immunometabolism should move from pathway annotation in reductionist models towards dynamic, tissue-resolved, and clinically anchored studies of immune cell metabolism in vivo.
authors: Gunawardana S, Romero Arocha S, Clarke AJ.

title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
abstract: BackgroundKeloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.MethodsWe integrated network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, external transcriptomic validation, and qRT-PCR to investigate candidate molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.ResultsA total of 127 shared candidate targets between pyrethroid insecticides and keloid were identified, mainly enriched in MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and FoxO signaling pathways. Three machine-learning algorithms prioritized VCAM1 and FGFR1. In GSE145725, both genes showed significant differential expression and high dataset-level discriminatory performance. In the integrated external validation cohort generated from GSE90051 and GSE158395, VCAM1 remained significantly upregulated and showed good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.869), whereas FGFR1 showed weaker external support (AUC = 0.677) without significant differential expression. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the structural plausibility of selected pyrethroid-target interactions, particularly theta-cypermethrin with VCAM1. Single-cell analysis characterized the cell-type-specific distribution of candidate genes, while virtual gene perturbation suggested a putative VCAM1-SOCS3 regulatory relationship. qRT-PCR further showed that 20 μM cypermethrin exposure for 24 h significantly increased VCAM1 mRNA expression in KEL FIB cells.ConclusionVCAM1 emerged as the most consistently supported candidate linking cypermethrin exposure with keloid-associated molecular alterations, while the predicted VCAM1-SOCS3 relationship requires further mechanistic validation.
authors: Wang Z, Yang C, Wang W, Zhang Z, Sun Z, Diao Z.

title: MFMNet: Adaptive tri-layer graph pyramid with cross-scale attention router for synergistic drug prediction.
abstract: Background and objectiveExperimental screening of synergistic anticancer drug pairs is time-consuming, while effectively integrating complementary molecular graph representations with cell-line-specific information remains challenging for computational drug-synergy prediction.MethodsWe developed MFMNet with a Tri-Layer Graph Pyramid (TGP) comprising GCN, GIN, and GAT branches for extracting complementary molecular graph representations. A Cross-Scale Attention Router (CSAR), implemented as an adaptive feature-wise gating mechanism, integrates the graph representations before they are combined with drug embeddings and cell-line transcriptomic features for synergistic drug-pair prediction.ResultsIn the initial five-fold cross-validation analysis, MFMNet achieved a mean five-fold AUROC of 0.9301 ± 0.0036. Under the stricter fold-matched evaluation protocol, the full MFMNet backbone achieved an AUROC of 0.9227 ± 0.0055 and a PR-AUC of 0.9127 ± 0.0084, with statistically significant improvements over XGBoost, DeepDDS-GCN, and DeepDDS-GAT after Holm correction.ConclusionsMFMNet provides a computational framework for synergistic drug-pair prediction by integrating complementary molecular graph representations with drug and cell-line features. The results support its use for computational prioritization of candidate synergistic drug combinations. All reported performance estimates refer to record-level five-fold cross-validation within the O'Neil dataset; generalization to entirely unseen drugs and cell lines requires further study.
authors: Wang L, Sun L, Pan J, Shao G, Shi G, Zhang G, Shi Y, Jin L.

title: Integrated transcriptomic analysis and machine learning identify AURKA and CENPM as candidate biomarkers in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
abstract: BackgroundFocal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a leading cause of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and progression to end-stage renal disease, but existing therapeutics and diagnostics are limited. Therefore, reliable diagnostic biomarkers that contribute to FSGS therapy and diagnostics are urgently needed.MethodsGene expression data for FSGS (GSE104948; 37 samples: 16 FSGS vs 21 controls) were obtained from GEO. A weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was employed. Key genes within significant modules were identified using Support Vector Machine Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE), random forest (RF), and cytoHubba Maximal Clique Centrality (MCC). Functional enrichment analyses were executed, while diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Immune cell infiltration (ICI) levels were quantified using CIBERSORT, and validation was conducted with an independent external dataset (GSE129973; 20 FSGS vs 20 controls).ResultsThe green-yellow module demonstrated robust association with the FSGS phenotype, from which 39 candidate genes were selected. Integration of RF, SVM-RFE and cytoHubba analyses pinpointed two primary hub genes: AURKA, which was recovered consistently across cross-validation folds, and CENPM, a less consistently recovered candidate. Functional enrichment underscored the involvement of these genes in pivotal biological processes, particularly mitosis and regulation of the cell cycle. Analysis of immune infiltration revealed significant shifts in the immune microenvironment (IME) of FSGS, correlating elevated expression of AURKA and CENPM with altered ICI patterns. ROC curve analyses showed the diagnostic performance of these genes, with AURKA achieving an AUC of 0.95 and CENPM 0.94 in the training dataset (independent validation: AURKA AUC 0.797, CENPM AUC 0.720). These results showed a consistent direction of change between FSGS patients and healthy controls in an independent validation cohort.ConclusionUsing a combined analytical approach involving WGCNA, machine learning (ML) algorithms, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, this study identified AURKA and CENPM as exploratory tissue-based candidate biomarkers for FSGS, with AURKA being the more robustly supported of the two; both require functional validation and independent confirmation before any therapeutic application can be considered.
authors: Lin X, Huang G, Sun Q, Zhang X.

title: Characterization of monoterpene and sesquiterpene synthases from Nardostachys jatamansi.
abstract: Nardostachys jatamansi essential oil possesses various pharmaceutical activities and is widely applied in the cosmetic and perfume industries. It mainly comprises monoterpenoids and sesquiterpenoids. In this work, 21 monoterpene and sesquiterpene synthase candidates were identified from N. jatamansi via transcriptome analysis. Five of them were functionally characterized by in vitro reactions and in vivo experiments, including four sesquiterpene synthases and one monoterpene synthase. The structures of their products were determined by NMR analysis and comparison with authentic reference standards and with mass spectra from the NIST Mass Spectral Library. All of these enzymatic products can be found in N. jatamansi. This work lays a foundation for bioproduction of N. jatamansi essential oil.
journal: Journal of Asian natural products research
authors: Ji QG, Lin PC, Gao K, Zi JC.
