title: Chromosome 14q loss is associated with adverse survival and a distinct transcriptional phenotype in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.
abstract: PurposeIn IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, prognostic biomarkers beyond MGMT promoter methylation remain limited. Chromosome 14q contains candidate tumor suppressors, yet the significance of arm-level 14q loss in molecularly defined glioblastoma is unclear.MethodsArm-level 14q status was inferred from coordinated 14q expression (Gaussian-mixture model) in bulk RNA sequencing of 215 Japanese IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and validated against methylation-array copy number (n = 42). Associations with outcome and transcriptional programs were evaluated and assessed in CGGA (n = 74) and TCGA (n = 139) using the discovery-cohort threshold.ResultsRNA-seq-based calls agreed with array copy number in 40/42 cases (κ = 0.90). 14q loss (87/215, 40.5%) was associated with shorter overall (p = 0.0053) and progression-free survival (p = 0.0175), remaining prognostic in the prespecified multivariable model (hazard ratio 1.44, 95% confidence interval 1.02-2.01; p = 0.036). 14q loss and MGMT promoter hypomethylation were prognostically complementary (four-group p ConclusionRNA-seq-inferable 14q loss identifies a clinically adverse subgroup of Japanese IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, is complementary to MGMT promoter methylation, and is associated with a proliferation-high, oxidative-phosphorylation-low transcriptional state. The absence of this association in TCGA underscores the need for validation in additional population-diverse cohorts before clinical implementation.
authors: Higa N, Yokoyama S, Akahane T, Hamada T, Yonezawa H, Makino R, Takajo T, Matsuo K, Kirishima M, Kitazono I, Fujioka Y, Hatae R, Kuga D, Nagasaka S, Suzuki K, Yamamoto J, Yoshimoto K, Tanimoto A, Hanaya R.

title: Ferroptosis-associated macrophages suggest a potential ACSL1-PGE2-stromal iron homeostasis-related axis in endometriosis.
abstract: BackgroundEndometriosis (EMs) is characterized by chronic inflammation, recurrent bleeding, oxidative stress, and disrupted local iron homeostasis. Although macrophages are important components of the immune microenvironment in EMs, their ferroptosis-related heterogeneity and potential association with iron homeostasis remain unclear. This study investigated ferroptosis-associated macrophages (FAMs) and their potential involvement in immune-iron homeostasis coupling in EMs.MethodsPublicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data were used to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in eutopic endometrial samples from women with EMs and disease-free controls. Differential expression, functional enrichment, donor-level, pseudobulk, pseudotime ordering, and inferred cell-cell communication analyses, together with independent bulk RNA sequencing, were used to prioritize candidate regulators. In vitro experiments included ferroptosis-related phenotype induction, ACSL1 knockdown, PGE2 quantification, EP2 receptor blockade, and iron-loading and chelation assays.ResultsFAMs were preferentially enriched in the EMs group and exhibited elevated ferroptosis-related transcriptional activity. Integrative transcriptomic and donor-level analyses supported the prioritization of acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 1 (ACSL1) as a candidate metabolic regulator. Ferrostatin-1 treatment significantly attenuated erastin-induced lipid peroxidation and cellular injury. ACSL1 knockdown markedly attenuated ferroptosis-related alterations and PGE2 secretion in macrophages. In endometriotic stromal cells, PGE2 treatment downregulated FTH1 expression, upregulated SLC40A1 expression, and elevated extracellular Fe³⁺ levels; these changes were partially reversed by EP2 receptor blockade. Iron chelation treatment significantly attenuated FAC-induced lipid peroxidation and cellular injury in macrophages.ConclusionThe findings support a proposed macrophage-stromal interaction axis linking ACSL1-PGE2-associated signaling, stromal iron homeostasis-related changes, and extracellular iron loading, with potential intervention points involving ACSL1, PGE2/EP2 signaling, and iron homeostasis.
authors: Wang J, Liu M, Luo X, Zhang Y, Ding J.

title: LC-MS determination of dopaminergic catecholamines in tissues and biofluids using streamlined sample preparation and heterocyclic NHS-ester derivatization.
abstract: The accurate quantification of endogenous catecholamines within the dopaminergic pathway plays a crucial role in neurochemical and clinical diagnostics. However, this process is severely hindered by rapid analyte oxidation and complex matrix interferences. This study introduces a comprehensive bioanalytical strategy that connects structural chemical modification with streamlined sample processing. First, the influence of various heterocyclic scaffolds on derivatization agent synthesis, chemical stability, chemoselectivity, and mass spectrometric (MS) ionization enhancement was systematically evaluated. This evaluation identified β-CCarb-NHS as the most promising candidate. To complement this chemical platform, a simple sample preparation workflow was developed. Catecholamines were stabilized directly during sample homogenization using 0.02% formic acid (FA), followed by a rapid liquid-liquid extraction (LLE) utilizing water, ACN, and chloroform. This approach achieved effective deproteination and lipid removal while eliminating the need for solid-phase extraction (SPE) or time-consuming solvent evaporation. Utilizing deuterium-labeled internal standards throughout, the integrated method was fully validated for 11 target catecholamines across mammalian brain tissue, human serum, and urine. The workflow demonstrated excellent accuracy (86-116%), precision (99%), yielding competitive limits of detection (3-217 nM) from a minimal 1 µL injection volume. Finally, the practical utility of the protocol was demonstrated by successfully profiling endogenous baseline levels in real human serum, urine, and river nutria brain tissue. The simple, robust, and cost-effective nature of this workflow makes it ideal for the analysis of large sample sets.
authors: Hofmanova T, Divis F, Miko M, Lisa M, Cifkova E, Andrys R.

title: Population pharmacokinetic analysis of lamivudine (3TC) in HIV-exposed neonates and pediatric participants living with HIV-1 from the IMPAACT 2019 and PETITE studies.
abstract: Lamivudine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor widely used in combination antiretroviral therapy for the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus infection. Accurate dose selection in neonates and young children remains challenging because of rapid developmental changes in renal clearance. We updated an existing pediatric population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model, previously developed using data from 210 participants across five studies, by incorporating a maturation function and integrating pharmacokinetic data from two additional studies, IMPAACT 2019 (n = 55) and PETITE (n = 24, all neonates), for a total of 289 participants aged 0.0137 (~5 days) to 19.1 years. Unlike the prior model, which did not include a maturation function, the refined PopPK model incorporates a sigmoid Emax maturation function on clearance (postmenstrual age at which clearance reaches 50% of its mature [adult] value (TM50) 51.4 weeks postmenstrual age; Hill coefficient 4.81), reflecting developmental immaturity of clearance mechanisms in early life. The PopPK model retained a one-compartment structure with first-order absorption and linear elimination. Estimation of allometric exponents for body weight further improved model fit, and inter-individual and inter-occasion variability were included in clearance, volume, and absorption rate constant. Model performance was assessed using standard goodness-of-fit diagnostics and visual predictive checks, which demonstrated good agreement between observed and model-predicted concentrations across the pediatric age and weight range. In conclusion, incorporation of a maturation function on clearance successfully extended the pediatric lamivudine PopPK model to term neonates and infants, with parameter estimates remaining consistent with the original model, supporting model-informed dose selection in this understudied population.
authors: Costa ACC, Lin Y-W, Chandasana H, Collins J, Bekker A, Cressey TR, Brooks KM, Deprez I, Cheung SYA, Bush M, Mehta R, IMPAACT 2019 Team, PETITE study Team.

title: SSR42 enhances the hemolytic capacity of Staphylococcus aureus by stabilizing the hla mRNA.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus utilizes a complex regulatory network to precisely control a vast array of virulence factors and facilitate infection. One such regulator, the long regulatory RNA SSR42, is emerging as a key modulator of virulence factor abundance and pathogenesis. Previous work has shown that a primary role for SSR42 is controlling hemolytic behavior through the positive regulation of alpha-toxin (hla/Hla). Herein, we confirm that loss of SSR42 limits hemolytic capacity due to reduced Hla production. Others have suggested that this occurs through the SaeRS two-component system; however, using epistasis experiments, we reveal that SSR42 and SaeRS function independently to control Hla activity. Using a two-plasmid system optimized to detect regulatory RNA-mediated control in gram-positive bacteria, we demonstrate that SSR42 directly enhances Hla production through the hla 5' untranslated region. Using interaction prediction and targeted mutagenesis, we identify a discrete site upstream of the hla ribosome-binding site that is required for SSR42 binding and hemolytic activity. Transcriptional arrest experiments further show that SSR42 stabilizes the hla mRNA, increasing its half-life, and promoting downstream toxin production. Finally, electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirm a specific interaction between SSR42 and the hla 5' UTR. Collectively, these findings establish SSR42 as a major post-transcriptional regulator of S. aureus virulence and reveal a novel RNA-mediated mechanism that promotes alpha-toxin production through stabilization of the hla transcript.
authors: Jobson M-E, Tomlinson BR, Jackson JK, Shaw LN.

title: Soil antibiotic resistance genes at the One Health interface: Evidence trajectories, dissemination risks, and risk-based management.
abstract: Soils serve as reservoirs and transmission interfaces for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), which can function as mobile genetic contaminants by persisting and replicating within microbial hosts and propagating via horizontal gene transfer (HGT). However, evidence linking mitigation mechanisms to environmental risk reduction remains insufficiently synthesized. Here, we integrate bibliometric trajectory analysis with mechanistic synthesis, using 2,309 Web of Science Core Collection records published between 2008 and 2026 to identify research trajectories, knowledge structures, and emerging mitigation fronts. The field has shifted from occurrence surveys and source identification toward intervention-oriented control, accelerating markedly after 2019. Foundational knowledge centers on soil resistome dynamics, mobile genetic element (MGE)-mediated HGT, and contaminant-driven co-selection. Current fronts highlight biochar-mediated regulation, manure and compost management, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-driven or photocatalytic inactivation of extracellular deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and ARG responses under co-contamination by antibiotics, heavy metals, and microplastics. Beyond mapping research trends, this review constructs a three-tier mitigation framework spanning extracellular DNA deconstruction and sequestration, MGE-mediated transfer inhibition, and system-level microecological restructuring through source management and soil amendment. Future work should integrate absolute gene loads, host identity, ARG-MGE linkage, transfer frequency, soil biogeochemical context, and field-scale ecological rebound into mechanistically grounded and ecologically defensible evaluation frameworks that assess reductions in ARG dissemination risk alongside effects on soil function, ecological resilience, and organic resource circularity.
authors: Ding H, Zhu Y, Zhu L, Xiu Z, Liu F, Huang D, Wang M.

title: Advances in electrocatalyst design for the ammonia oxidation reaction.
abstract: The transition towards a hydrogen (H2)-based economy is significantly constrained by challenges associated with its storage, transportation, and supply-chain infrastructure. These limitations arise from hydrogen's low volumetric energy density and the need for energy-intensive compression or cryogenic liquefaction. To circumvent these issues, liquid-phase energy carriers such as methanol, ethanol, and ammonia have emerged as attractive alternatives, offering significant benefits, including higher energy density, ease of storage and handling, and compatibility with existing fuel distribution infrastructure. Among the available candidates, ammonia (NH3) has gained considerable attention, particularly for applications in direct ammonia fuel cells (DAFCs). Ammonia has a high hydrogen content (~17.6 wt%) and a relatively high volumetric energy density, enabling efficient hydrogen storage without prior reforming or extraction. Despite these advantages, the practical implementation of DAFCs is hindered by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR). In addition, strong adsorption of reaction intermediates on catalyst active sites leads to catalyst poisoning, thereby reducing turnover frequency and overall cell performance. In this review, we present recent advances in electrocatalyst development and engineering strategies to improve AOR activity and durability in DAFC systems. Particular emphasis is placed on the evolution of catalyst materials, spanning platinum-group-metal (PGM)-based systems to hybrid PGM/non-PGM architectures and fully non-PGM catalysts. Furthermore, key design principles, including electronic structure modulation, surface and interface engineering, compositional optimization, and AI/ML approaches, are discussed to provide fundamental insights into AOR electrocatalysts. Finally, we outline the current challenges and highlight future research directions towards the development of next-generation electrocatalysts for efficient and durable DAFC operation in this review article.
authors: Rajeev C, Jefin F, U AK, Sethi A, Shahid LM, Bhat SD, Agarwal H, Dhavale VM.

title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units—cells, bins or multicellular spots—into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p-values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene–gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p-values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.
authors: Wang H, Cao F, Shen H, Liu Y, Yan G.

title: EWSR1::ATF1 hyperactivation via TRIM11 depletion triggers lethal metabolic rewiring in clear cell sarcoma
abstract: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is an ultra-rare and aggressive soft tissue sarcoma driven by the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion oncoprotein. Currently, no effective and well-tolerated treatment options are available to CCS patients. Direct inhibition of fusion transcription factors is precluded by the absence of defined ligand-binding pockets, whereas their abundance is under the control of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), offering an alternative avenue for biology-guided treatment. Here we show the abundance of EWSR1::ATF1 is tightly regulated by the UPS, and that release of this constraint is lethal to CCS cells. A reporter-based CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen of UPS components identified TRIM11 as an E3 ligase that regulates turnover of EWSR1::ATF1, which it recognises as a neosubstrate without altering wild-type EWSR1 or ATF1. Depletion of TRIM11 increased nuclear fusion protein abundance, amplified the fusion-driven transcriptional programs and reduced viability. Proteomic analysis identified the cataplerotic enzyme phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1), a direct EWSR1::ATF1 target, as the key mediator of lethal effects of fusion hyperactivation. Extracellular flux analysis, isotope tracing and quantitative metabolomics revealed excessive cataplerotic carbon withdrawal and impaired oxidative phosphorylation as the underlying mechanism. In patient tumors, high PCK1 expression associated with metastatic transcriptome programs and disease presentation, as well as shorter survival. Taken together, we report that hyperactivation of EWSR1::ATF1 opens a metabolic vulnerability, establishing TRIM11 as an actionable dependency and PCK1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker in CCS.

title: User-Informed Design of a Psychological Support Social Pet Robot for Community-Dwelling People With Long-Term Physical Disabilities: A Formative Study
abstract: Background:  Community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities may experience pain that interferes with daily and social activities and is associated with poorer mental wellbeing. A home-based psychological support social pet robot could offer mood check-ins, companionship, supportive interaction, and mindfulness guidance for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities. Preliminary evidence is needed to understand their preferences and translate them into candidate design requirements. Objective. This study aimed to identify preliminary needs and preferences to inform a psychological support social pet robot for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities, offering mood check-ins, companionship, and mindfulness guidance at home. Methods. We conducted a 3-phase formative user-informed design study comprising initial concept development, qualitative target user interviews, and a design workshop. Six community-dwelling adults with long-term physical disabilities took part in the interviews, and one participant also answered the workshop questions by telephone. Four authors used modified workshop materials to synthesize the interview findings and separate responses into an early product plan. Results. Qualitative content analysis of the interview transcripts produced 5 themes. These were emotional support, soft touch and appearance, mindfulness delivery, context of use, and ease of use and accessibility. Participants expressed preferences about companionship, touch, use settings, and interaction effort. The author workshop combined these findings with author and technical judgments to develop candidate requirements for dialogue and mindfulness delivery. The resulting psychological support concept combined mood check-ins and companion-oriented interaction with flexible mindfulness guidance. The design also needed to consider pain and daily routines. After the workshop, the authors developed a physical proof-of-concept prototype. It implemented only part of the candidate requirements and included additional author or technical choices. Conclusions. For this small community-dwelling sample, target user input showed that home use, physical access, companionship, and flexible support were important. Mindfulness was one component of the broader psychological support role, alongside mood check-ins and optional companion interaction. The prototype illustrates but does not validate the early requirements. Further studies should include people with a wider range of long-term physical disabilities and test usability, accessibility, privacy, and nursing value. Keywords. social pet robots; user-informed design; psychological support; mindfulness; long-term physical disabilities; community dwelling; user centered design; human robot interaction; mental health; qualitative research
authors: Lu Y, Chen X, Hui R, Dai Y, Mei X, So H, Li C, Tao X, Li Y.

title: CDC123 variants associated with developmental abnormalities alter CDC123-eIF2 subunit interactions and impair protein synthesis
abstract: The translation initiation factor eIF2 is an essential regulator of cellular protein synthesis with direct links to human physiology and development. Composed of eIF2α, β, and γ subunits, eIF2 heterotrimer assembly requires the activity of its dedicated chaperone and the essential protein, CDC123. Accordingly, CDC123 is a key determinant of protein synthesis and cell growth. Previous research has demonstrated that variants in eIF2γ impair neurodevelopment, and CDC123 variants of uncertain significance have recently been reported for pediatric patients with neurologic findings. However, the potential pathogenicity, and cell and molecular impacts of these clinically relevant CDC123 variants remains entirely unexplored. In this work, we describe four unrelated families with pediatric patients that present with neurodevelopmental delays, hypotonia, and motor dysfunction. The probands are heterozygous for three novel CDC123 missense variants. The potential pathogenicity of the variants is comprehensively assessed through appraisal of CDC123 variant allele frequencies, protein conservational analyses, structural modeling, and functional assays in both humanized yeast and human cell-based model systems. Cellular and biochemical studies indicated that the variants are damaging to CDC123 activity, altering CDC123-eIF2 subunit interactions and leading to reduced cell growth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the CDC123 variants display dominant-negative effects on yeast cell growth and protein synthesis, rather than causing haploinsufficiency. Together, our findings provide the first link between CDC123 missense variants and human disease and highlight that CDC123-mediated eIF2 heterotrimer formation is essential for human development.
authors: Erb A, Misciagna A, Rodriguez-Martinez A, Gasser B, DeFilippo C, Gillam A, Beleford D, VanNoy G, Young-Baird S.

title: Closing the reference gap for Australo-Papuan rodents: a 431-mitogenome library for environmental DNA and species discovery
abstract: As biodiversity declines at an unprecedented rate, rapid and scalable approaches to monitoring species are increasingly needed, particularly in poorly known and highly threatened groups. Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly enabling high-throughput monitoring to inform conservation. However, species-level monitoring through eDNA relies on comprehensive reference databases and short, species-discriminating ‘mini-barcode’ loci, resources that are lacking for many taxa. The application of eDNA for species-level monitoring is therefore constrained by these gaps. Here, we use Australo-Papuan rodents (subfamily Murinae: tribe Hydromyini) as a model system to address these limitations, given their high species diversity, conservation concern, and distribution across geographically complex regions. Among animals, eDNA monitoring typically depends on mitochondrial markers. Leveraging taxonomically-verified museum specimens, we develop a 431-mitogenome reference library representing ~72% of described species diversity, and use this database to assess the species-level resolution of candidate mini-barcodes. We show that common 12S rRNA mammalian eDNA markers cannot reliably discriminate between Hydromyini species (resolving 23-33% of tested species). In contrast, a Rodentia-specific Cytb marker resolves 66% of tested species, and two novel ATP6 Hydromyini markers, presented here, resolves 93% through a multi-locus approach. This reference library represents a >40-fold increase in available complete mitogenomes for Australo-Papuan rodents, enabling eDNA monitoring in this highly threatened group. More broadly, we demonstrate the value of pairing comprehensive reference resources with empirical marker assessment to reveal where eDNA based approaches may fail to distinguish species. Understanding these limitations is essential to realising the promise of eDNA as a reliable tool for species-level monitoring and conservation.
authors: Drury C, MacDonald A, Moritz C, Rowe K, Roycroft E.

title: Innateness is (still) an orienting principle for language development
abstract: How humans come to acquire language has been a persistent object of philosophical and scientific inquiry, in part because it bears on fundamental questions about the nature of human cognition.Classically, this field of inquiry has centered innateness as a critical component of language acquisition, traditionally characterizing innate capability in terms of richly specified, biologically endowed linguistic structure, such as Universal Grammar. Contemporary theories have evolved considerably from these earlier formulations and now present several differing candidates for innateness in language. Throughout this evolution, though, questions of innateness have remained central to theories of language acquisition, even as the nature of those questions has shifted in response to new sources of evidence. In this Perspective, we consider evidence from three complementary sources of evidence—linguistic diversity, human social interaction, and language models (LMs)—that together inform the question of what children must bring to the task of language learning. We conclude by identifying desiderata for theories of language acquisition that seek to specify the nature, scope, and explanatory role of innate contributions to language development.
authors: Singh L, Casillas M, Allen SEM, Frank MC, Rowland CF.

title: The global population genetics of GPNMB-associated amyloidosis cutis dyschromica: ancestry-specific variation and likely underdiagnosis
abstract: Abstract    Amyloidosis cutis dyschromica (ACD) is a rare recessive pigmentary disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function (LoF) variants in  GPNMB  . Almost all reported patients are East or Southeast Asian, and it is unknown whether this reflects allele distribution or ascertainment. Using gnomAD v4.1, I identified 114 high-confidence predicted LoF (pLoF) variants on the MANE Select transcript and estimated carrier frequencies and expected biallelic prevalence across ancestry groups. Carrier frequencies were highest in Ashkenazi Jewish (1 in 251) and East Asian (1 in 261) individuals, followed by non-Finnish Europeans (1 in 358) and Admixed Americans (1 in 422). Under Hardy–Weinberg proportions, about 183 people in Mexico (95% interval 141–344) and about 40 Ashkenazi Jews worldwide (25–68) are expected to carry biallelic pLoF alleles. A literature audit found no reported ACD cases of Latin American or Ashkenazi Jewish origin, against at least 100 reported patients worldwide. The Ashkenazi burden is driven by a single founder splice-donor allele, c.367+2T>C (57 of 80 gnomAD copies). In Admixed Americans, 70% of pLoF alleles are shared with Europeans and 30% come from four alleles essentially absent elsewhere. Heterozygous pLoF carriers in 394,841 UK Biobank exomes showed no association across 4,529 traits, consistent with recessive inheritance. Variants that disrupt the essential MITF binding site of the  GPNMB  proximal promoter (MCS3) were rare, but one, 7-23246653-A-T, is confined to African and Admixed American chromosomes and is a candidate for functional testing. These results indicate that ACD is likely underdiagnosed in Latin America and among Ashkenazi Jews, and that  GPNMB  belongs on diagnostic panels for pigmentary disorders beyond East Asia.
authors: Garcia-Elfring A.

title: Hydrogen peroxide, chlorine, and peracetic acid disinfectants outperform quaternary ammonium compounds against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa wet and dry surface biofilms
abstract: Abstract      Background:    Wet and dry surface biofilms (WSB and DSB), are a recognized source for healthcare-associated infections (HAI), and effective cleaning and disinfection regimens are critical to reducing HAI risk for patients. Disinfectant efficacy against biofilms on dry surfaces, however, remains poorly characterized relative to that against planktonic organisms.    Methods:    The bactericidal efficacy of eight EPA-registered hospital-grade, one-step cleaner-disinfectants was assessed against WSB and DSB of  Staphylococcus aureus  (ATCC 6538) and  Pseudomonas aeruginosa  (ATCC 15442)  .  Biofilms were grown in a CDC biofilm reactor following EPA-MLB-SOP-MB-19-06 and, for DSB formation, dehydrated at 25 and 21  o  C for  S. aureus  and  P. aeruginosa  respectively for 24, 48, and 72 h intervals to reflect recommended cleaning frequencies for healthcare surfaces. Biofilms were challenged with each disinfectant at its label-specified contact time following EPA-MLB-SOP-MB-20-04. Efficacy was expressed as log  10  CFU/cm  2  reduction, and experiments were performed in triplicate.    Results:    Hydrogen peroxide-, chlorine- and peracetic acid-based disinfectants demonstrated significantly greater efficacy than quaternary ammonium-based products against  S. aureus  biofilms (P .  Desiccation time significantly impacts bactericidal efficacy of  P. aeruginosa  biofilms (P S. aureus  . There is greater disinfectant efficacy against  P. aeruginosa  biofilms with the addition of a solvent to a quaternary ammonium product.    Conclusions:    Our findings indicate that current planktonic-based registration testing may overstate real-world disinfectant performance against the biofilm-embedded organisms healthcare facilities are realistically working to control, and that this gap varies by chemistry, organism, and how long a biofilm has been allowed to persist before disinfection.
authors: Horn CM, Spray HN, Garris AJ, Teska PJ, Oliver-Jischke H.

title: Herbal, Dietary, and Non-Prescription Medication Use and Spontaneous Abortion: A Case–Control Study with Exploratory Analysis of Pineapple-Associated Molecular Targets
abstract: Abstract  Background  Herbal remedies, selected foods, and non-prescription medications are widely used during pregnancy despite limited evidence regarding their safety. This study examined associations between first-trimester consumption of these products and spontaneous abortion among Iranian women. An exploratory transcriptomic extension investigated predicted pineapple-associated targets and MAPK-related patterns in endometrial datasets from women with recurrent pregnancy loss. Methods  In this multicenter case-control study (May 2023–March 2024), 377 women aged 18–45 years were recruited from three prenatal clinics in Tehran, including 167 women with physician-confirmed spontaneous abortion and 210 controls with at least one live birth and no history of abortion. Data on demographic, reproductive, and first-trimester exposure to 45 herbal products, foods, and non-prescription medications were collected using a structured questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with correction for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR). To explore underlying mechanisms, predicted pineapple-associated targets were intersected with lists of differentially expressed genes from GEO datasets (GSE165004 and GSE26787), followed by pathway enrichment analysis. These findings were further assessed using decidual single-cell data to evaluate the common-scale MAPK footprint, and branch-expression. Results  In total, 29.97% of participants reported consuming at least one of the evaluated herbal or food items during the first trimester. After adjustment for confounders and multiple comparisons, pineapple consumption was associated with a higher odds of spontaneous abortion (aOR 2.95, 95% CI 1.55–5.64; FDR adjusted P = 0.0276). Twenty candidate genes were shared between the lists of abortion-associated and pineapple-related targets, including six MAPK-associated genes. Additionally, single-cell analysis suggested that the pooled MAPK footprint was lower in abortions. Conclusion  Pineapple consumption was associated with higher odds of spontaneous abortion. Exploratory molecular analyses suggested MAPK pathways as a candidate pathway for future investigation, although experimental validation is required to confirm these findings.
authors: Saeedinia R, Rafiepoor H, Sahebi L, Amini F, Jafarabady K, Hemmat A, Heidary Z.

title: Benchmarking the Elastic Tensors of Silicon Polymorphs Across Three Density Functional Theory Databases Disconfirms a Predicted Auxetic Candidate
abstract: Abstract  We benchmark the structural and elastic properties of silicon polymorphs (diamond-Si, BC8-Si, R8-Si, Ibam-Si, and phases identified through high-throughput screening) across three independent computational databases: Materials Project, AFLOW, and JARVIS-DFT. Calibrating against the one phase with a complete experimental elastic tensor (diamond-Si), all three databases show a consistent 9-10% systematic underestimate of the bulk modulus relative to experiment, quantifying a known GGA-PBE limitation across three unrelated codes and workflows. We retrieve and cross-validate the complete elastic tensors of BC8-Si and R8-Si for the first time in a consolidated, source-traceable dataset, confirming both phases mechanically stable and finding BC8-Si to be the most elastically isotropic entry among fifteen independently characterized silicon structures on a symmetry-independent anisotropy index. An apparent auxetic silicon candidate identified by high-throughput screening (derived Poisson ratio -0.181) is shown, via a direct Born-stability-criterion violation in its full elastic tensor, to be mechanically unstable rather than a genuine effect -- illustrating a general pitfall of screening on isotropic averages alone. A component-by-component comparison of the full elastic tensor across eighteen matched AFLOW-JARVIS structures reveals that this agreement is not uniform: two of six diagonal constants, C44 and C66, show median disagreements of 13% and 19% respectively, an order of magnitude larger than the 2-4% typical of normal-stress and off-diagonal constants. This disagreement is absent in cubic structures and present in every non-cubic structure examined; re-pairing C44 against C66 collapses the discrepancy to a few percent in four independent cases, consistent with an axis-labelling convention difference between the two databases rather than a physical one, though genuine structural non-equivalence between matched entries cannot be fully excluded. Mapping the elastic-property space of silicon polymorphs in the style of Ashby materials-selection charts, we find that structural compactness predicts bulk stiffness but has no detectable power to predict ductile-versus-brittle character, a decoupling replicated independently across two of the three databases. We document a genuine, unresolved discrepancy of 11-12% between databases in the bulk modulus of β-Sn-Si, illustrating that cross-database benchmarking remains necessary even for a well-studied elemental system. All underlying data, including full elastic tensors, structure identifiers and evidence-level annotations, are made available in a source-traceable database.
authors: aourag h.

title: Functional transcriptomic profiling ofVeillonella parvula in oral microenvironments of patients with oral cancer: A cross-sectional study. Veillonella parvula Transcriptomics in Oral Cancer
abstract: Abstract    Background.  Oral squamous cell carcinoma is a pathology associated with microbial dysbiosis.  Veillonella parvula  modulates the microenvironment by facilitating the maturation of complex biofilms; its role in carcinogenesis could therefore be decisive. Objectives.  To determine the active biological processes of  Veillonella parvula  in saliva, dental plaque, and tumor tissue samples from patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma. Methods  This cross-sectional study analyzed dental plaque, saliva, and tumor tissue from 10 oral squamous cell carcinoma patients. Following quality control (FastQC/Trimmomatic), Veillonella parvula was identified using Kraken and reference databases. Transcriptomic analysis (BLAST, STRING, KEGG) was performed on normalized data for differential abundance, clustering, PCA, and pathway enrichment. This approach characterized gene functions and identified tumor-associated signatures across microenvironments in a 69-word methodology. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION  Not applicable. This study was observational and did not involve a clinical intervention.
authors: Erira A, Polania JFN, Guevara LAC, Tosse FT, Robayo DAG.

title: Uncertainty Aware Prediction of Near Complete Brilliant Green Photodegradation over CaTiO 3 Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Kinetic Modeling
abstract: Abstract    Brilliant Green (BG) is a persistent cationic dye that can harm aquatic environments by reducing light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, altering microbial activity, and causing toxicity. Because BG degradation depends on interacting operating conditions, accurate prediction and optimization remain challenging. In this study, we analysed 90 previously published CaTiO  3  photocatalytic observations using an integrated machine-learning and kinetic framework. Twelve regression models Extra Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, XGBoost, HistGradientBoosting, SVR, GPR, KNN, Elastic Net, Ridge, and PLSR were optimized using Bayesian search and evaluated through five-fold cross-validation and held-out testing. XGBoost achieved the strongest individual performance, with mean CV R  2  of 0.9844 and test R  2  of 0.9796. An XGBoost-GPR hybrid improved test R  2  to 0.9809, with RMSE and MAE of 3.4058 and 2.4556, respectively. SHAP analysis identified degradation time as the most influential predictor. Since measured removal reached only 89.53%, direct models could not reliably predict near-complete degradation. Therefore, pseudo-first-order rate constants were modeled using SVR. The framework identified a 2:7 CaCO  3  /TiO  2  ratio, 200 mg catalyst, and 10 ppm BG for 99.9% removal in 275.6 min. Bootstrap uncertainty analysis yielded a median time of 251.7 min.
authors: Khan MAH, Islam MM, Rahman S.

title: A single-cell and bulk transcriptome meta-analysis reveals RYR2 as a key biomarker and potential regulator in Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Abstract  Intracellular calcium release channels, including ryanodine receptors (RYRs) and inositol trisphosphate receptors (ITPRs), regulate calcium signalling essential for insulin secretion by pancreatic islet β-cells. However, alterations in their expression in type 2 diabetes (T2D) remain unclear. Here, we screened 1.3 million single-cell RNA sequencing transcriptomes and performed a meta-analysis of 464,713 transcriptomes from human islet α-, β-, or δ-cells across 22 independent studies from n=235 individuals with, at risk of, or without diabetes. We identified RYR2 as the predominant RYR isoform in human pancreatic islet β-cells, with significantly increased expression in T2D, compared to prediabetes and non-diabetes states. Bulk RNA sequencing of n=381 human islet samples from our own and publicly available datasets confirmed RYR2 abundance and enrichment of RYR2-212 (ENST00000714022.1) splice variant in human islets. These findings suggest that elevated β-cell RYR2 expression may contribute to islet dysfunction in T2D, identifying RYR2 as a candidate biomarker and potential therapeutic target to guide personalised strategies for diabetes management.
authors: Hardikar A, Hardikar H, Wong W, Kanta S, Shekhawat R, Papanicolaou A, Islam MS, Prasad R, Joglekar M.

title: Morphological and transcriptomic dynamics of flower development in Phyllostachys reticulata
abstract: Abstract    Background  The prolonged and often unpredictable flowering cycles of bamboos have limited studies of their reproductive development. In  Phyllostachys reticulata  , the relationships among inflorescence organization, floral organogenesis, gametophyte development, and tissue-specific transcriptional programs remain unclear. We combined morphological observations, serial histological sections, and PacBio and Illumina transcriptome sequencing to characterize floral development, establish a reference transcriptome resource, and identify candidate regulators. Results  Morphological and histological observations revealed distinct spatial patterns of floret initiation and maturation. Floret primordia were initiated sequentially from the apex toward the base of the spikelet, whereas basal florets developed faster than apical florets. Floral organs differentiated centripetally, successively forming the lemma, palea, lodicules, stamens, and carpel. Male gametophyte development culminated in bicellular pollen, with collapsed pollen grains occurring alongside well-developed pollen in mature anthers. Female development produced seven-celled, eight-nucleate Polygonum-type embryo sacs. Integration of PacBio long-read and Illumina short-read sequencing generated a reference transcriptome comprising 259,726 non-redundant protein-coding sequences. Expression analysis identified 33,765 differentially expressed transcripts among six tissue types, with lemmas and paleae exhibiting the most similar expression profiles. Co-expression analysis identified modules associated with leaves, outer floral organs, stamens, and carpels. Thirty-eight candidate ABCDE(G)-class MADS-box transcripts exhibited divergent tissue-associated expression patterns. Homologs of established flowering regulators differed in expression between leaves from flowering and non-flowering branches, encompassing photoperiodic signaling, florigen-associated pathways, and floral meristem identity regulation. Conclusions  This study establishes an integrated morphological and transcriptional framework for floral development in  P. reticulata  , distinguishing spatial developmental patterns and identifying candidate transcriptional programs associated with flowering status and floral organ differentiation. The reference transcriptome provides a sequence resource for investigating reproduction in this species and comparing conservation and divergence in bamboo floral development. Future functional studies could clarify the roles of key candidates in floral development and seed formation.
authors: Li Y, Huang X, Liu H, Wang C, Peng J, Zhang W, Guo C, Wang M.

title: Nuclear proteomics identifies TEAD4 as an IFN-γ-responsive regulator of pathogenic synovial fibroblast programs
abstract: Abstract  Difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA) remains a major unmet clinical challenge despite advances in targeted therapies. Recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies identified synovial fibroblast (SF) subsets associated with multidrug-resistant disease states. Transcriptome-based inference approaches have been used to further characterize pathogenic fibroblast subsets by identifying candidate master transcriptional regulators. However, their accuracy is limited by the context-dependent relationship between transcription factors and their target genes. Here, we applied nuclear proteomics using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) to identify transcription factors regulated in cytokine-stimulated rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts (RASFs). Nuclear DIA-MS identified TEAD4 as a transcription factor selectively induced by IFN-γ signaling. Transcriptomic and functional analyses demonstrated that TEAD4 regulates gene programs associated with multidrug-resistant fibroblast subsets, including TGF-β-associated fibroblast activation programs. Comparative perturbation analyses showed that TEAD family members exhibit both redundant and distinct functions and regulate transcriptional programs that only partially overlap with those controlled by YAP/TAZ. Pharmacologic inhibition of TEAD activity suppressed fibroblast proliferation and migration in vitro and attenuated arthritis severity in the collagen-induced arthritis model without impairing antigen-specific immune responses. Together, these findings identify TEAD signaling as a therapeutically targetable pathway in rheumatoid arthritis and provide a mechanistic framework linking inflammatory and profibrotic fibroblast activation.
authors: Saito T, Sato M, Horie K, Nakahara T, Da R, Li S, Yamamoto A, Noda S, Hosoya T, Takahara Y, Sugimoto K, Endo K, Koga H, Sekiya I, Kawakami E, Yasuda S.

title: From Finite Embodied Capabilities to Autonomous Knowledge and Method Evolution
abstract: Autonomous intelligent systems should be able to acquire knowledge and improve their own learning capabilities through continuous interaction with the environment. However, existing approaches often rely on predefined tasks, fixed learning methods, or externally provided training data, limiting their ability to grow autonomously from minimal initial capabilities. In this paper, we propose a finite-capability-driven autonomous learning framework that actively utilizes sensing, movement, interaction, learning, and thinking to acquire new experiences. The framework transforms experiences into reusable knowledge, applies acquired knowledge to improve task execution, and reinvests saved resources into further learning. It also enables experience-driven evolution of learning and thinking methods through candidate generation, evaluation, and selective retention. Persistent activity scheduling integrates these mechanisms into a continuing autonomous learning process. Results from complementary simulation experiments show that active embodied exploration discovers 25.5 versus 9.7 objects without movement, improves recognition Macro-F1 from 0.588 to 0.634 through active perception, increases cross-object transfer accuracy from 78.82% to 86.54% through rule reuse, and reduces task execution cost by 21.09% compared with a fixed method.
authors: Su H.

title: Neural Adhesion Gene Expression in Suicide: A Bilateral Study of IgLONs in the Human Anterior Midcingulate Cortex with Genetic and Transcriptomic Context
abstract: Genetic association studies have implicated neural adhesion-related genes in suicidal behaviour and related psychiatric phenotypes, whereas postmortem brain transcriptomic studies have yielded heterogeneous findings with limited support after multiple-testing correction. We synthesized genetic evidence and examined IgLON expression in bilateral anterior midcingulate cortex (aMCC) samples from 14 suicide and 10 non-suicide donors. RT-qPCR measured eight transcripts from five IgLON genes, including alternative promoter-derived transcripts of LSAMP, NTM and OPCML. We additionally reanalysed published dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) expression data and examined public transcriptomic datasets. The genetic synthesis identified several adhesion-related candidate genes, while exploratory DLPFC reanalysis suggested potentially informative promoter-specific differences in LSAMP expression. In the aMCC, NEGR1 expression was lower in the right hemisphere of suicide donors (suicide/non-suicide ratio = 0.54; FDR-adjusted q = 0.027), but not significantly different in the left. Directional NEGR1 asymmetry also differed between groups (q = 0.026), although this result was sensitive to covariate adjustment and the scope of multiple-testing correction. Blood ethanol adjustment minimally changed effect estimates. No other aMCC transcript or public transcriptomic comparison showed FDR-significant differences. Our findings support anatomically focused, bilateral and transcript-specific investigation of neural adhesion genes in larger, independent cohorts.

title: miR-155 expression associates with pathogenic circulating follicular helper T-cell phenotype in myasthenia gravis.
abstract: IntroductionMyasthenia gravis (MG) is an antibody-mediated autoimmune disease targeting neuromuscular junctions. We previously reported that ICOS-high expressing circulating follicular T cells (ICOShighcTfh) are expanded in MG and are associated with the disease severity. Although it is unknown what influences the skew of Tfh in MG, one of the candidates is microRNA (miRNA), especially miR-146a and miR-155, which were reported to be associated with accumulation and function of Tfh.MethodsTwenty-four MG patients positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody and 12 HS were enrolled. The expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were analyzed by a real-time PCR system in association with the cTfh phenotype in MG. To further examine cell-type-specific MIR155HG expression, publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from MG patient PBMCs were analyzed.ResultsThe expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 were significantly higher in MG than HS. The level of miR-155 but not miR-146a level showed significant correlation with the frequency of ICOShighcTfh. scRNA-seq analysis revealed that MIR155HG was most highly expressed in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell cluster characterized by elevated CXCR5, ICOS, PDCD1, and IL21, which was expanded in MG relative to HS (24% vs. 18%), supporting the PBMC-level miRNA findings. miR-155 levels decreased after immunotherapy, paralleling the reduction of ICOShighcTfh in MG.ConclusionElevated miR-155 expression is associated with pathogenic activation of circulating Tfh cells in MG, supported by single-cell transcriptomic evidence of MIR155HG enrichment in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell population.
authors: Ashida S, Ochi H, Fujii C, Hamatani M, Mizuno T, Kondo T.

title: Innateness is (still) an orienting principle for language development
abstract: How humans come to acquire language has been a persistent object of philosophical and scientific inquiry, in part because it bears on fundamental questions about the nature of human cognition.Classically, this field of inquiry has centered innateness as a critical component of language acquisition, traditionally characterizing innate capability in terms of richly specified, biologically endowed linguistic structure, such as Universal Grammar. Contemporary theories have evolved considerably from these earlier formulations and now present several differing candidates for innateness in language. Throughout this evolution, though, questions of innateness have remained central to theories of language acquisition, even as the nature of those questions has shifted in response to new sources of evidence. In this Perspective, we consider evidence from three complementary sources of evidence—linguistic diversity, human social interaction, and language models (LMs)—that together inform the question of what children must bring to the task of language learning. We conclude by identifying desiderata for theories of language acquisition that seek to specify the nature, scope, and explanatory role of innate contributions to language development.
authors: Singh L, Casillas M, Allen SEM, Frank MC, Rowland CF.

title: Andrographolide, A Plant-Based Dietary Bioactive Nutritional Health Compound, Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Acute Lung Injury by Inhibiting Ferroptosis Through the STAT3/P53 Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Andrographolide (AG) is a plant-derived bioactive diterpenoid compound with potential applications in nutritional science and clinical nutrition. This study investigated whether AG attenuates hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury (HALI) by inhibiting ferroptosis via the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3)/tumor protein P53 (P53) signaling pathway. Male C57BL/6 mice were used to establish a hyperoxia-induced lung injury model, and the protective effects of AG were compared with those of the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1). Lung histopathological changes, the lung wet-to-dry (W/D) weight ratio, reactive oxygen species (ROS), ferrous iron (Fe2+), glutathione (GSH), inflammatory cytokines, and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression were assessed. Network pharmacology and functional enrichment analyses were performed to identify potential targets of AG, followed by validation in MLE-12 lung epithelial cells and mouse models. Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, and the expression of phosphorylated STAT3 (P-STAT3), total STAT3, P53, and GPX4 was examined by western blotting. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) was used to investigate the interaction between STAT3 and P53. Hyperoxia induced marked lung injury, inflammatory cell infiltration, increased pulmonary edema, and alterations in ferroptosis-related indicators. Both AG and Fer-1 attenuated lung injury and reduced ferroptosis-associated changes. Network pharmacology analysis identified 79 potential targets associated with HALI, with STAT3 emerging as a core candidate target. In MLE-12 cells, AG attenuated ferroptosis-associated changes, whereas the STAT3 phosphorylation activator Colivelin TFA attenuated these protective effects. Co-IP confirmed an interaction between STAT3 and P53, and Colivelin TFA also weakened the protective effects of AG in the mouse model. These findings suggest that AG may alleviate HALI by inhibiting ferroptosis through modulation of the STAT3/P53 signaling pathway, providing experimental evidence for its potential as a plant-derived bioactive compound for further investigation in hyperoxia-induced lung injury.
authors: Xia Q, Liu X, Qin S, Feng B, Yu K, Ren Y.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis identifies key regulatory genes involved in lignin biosynthesis in Heracleum moellendorffii.
abstract: Lignin is a major component of secondary cell walls and plays essential roles in mechanical support and stress resistance. In Heracleum moellendorffii Hance, a medicinal and aromatic plant resource under artificial cultivation, petioles undergo progressive firming and lignification during development. Here, we combined anatomical observation, cell-wall and biochemical measurements, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and heterologous functional analysis to characterize developmental lignification. Microscopic observations and firmness measurements revealed progressive structural changes accompanied by increased lignin deposition from the early to late developmental stages. Targeted metabolite analysis showed developmental remodeling of the monolignol-related metabolite pool, with the relative proportion of coniferyl alcohol increasing during petiole maturation. Integrated RNA-seq and metabolite analyses prioritized Hm4CL2, HmCCR2, and HmCAD2 as candidate structural genes associated with lignin biosynthesis. Stable heterologous expression of these genes in tobacco was associated with altered vascular anatomy and changes in measured monolignol-related compounds. These findings provide a developmental framework for lignification in H. moellendorffii and identify candidate genes for future manipulation of lignification, pending direct functional validation in this species.
authors: Zhang X, Peng L, Lin Y, Gong S, Zhang H, Zhang M, Ma D, Yu J, Zhou A, Qiao K, Wang J.

title: A robust coordinated molecular response following trauma promotes recovery and protects against chronic pain and neuropsychiatric symptoms
abstract: The biological mechanisms governing recovery versus chronicity of adverse posttraumatic neuropsychiatric sequelae (APNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized longitudinal molecular changes among trauma survivors across ten APNS domains, including pain, anxiety, and depression. Recovery across these diverse clinical outcomes was associated with a shared, temporally coordinated transcriptional signature, characterized by early innate immune activation, subsequent homeostatic and wound-healing processes, and later adaptive immune responses. In contrast, chronic APNS trajectories exhibited limited transcriptional remodeling. We derived and externally validated an RNA-based Recovery Score (RRS) capturing the shared molecular response underlying recovery. Higher RRS was associated with greater clinical recovery, elevated peritraumatic cortisol, and lower cumulative stress exposure. Drug-response profiling identified candidate compounds predicted to mimic recovery-associated transcriptional changes. Together, these findings support posttraumatic recovery as an active biological process and identify shared molecular pathways that may be harnessed to prevent multiple adverse posttraumatic outcomes.

title: Generative design of de novo AAV vectors with unique serological profiles
abstract: More than 5000 monogenic diseases are potentially curable by replacing a single defective gene with one that functions normally. Currently, the only clinically approved vector able to effectively deliver a therapeutic gene to a target tissue is Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAVs). However, despite decades of work, only a handful of gene replacement therapies have been approved, and many patients remain ineligible for even those. A major barrier to broad adoption of AAV therapies is pre-existing immunity to AAVs, mediated by neutralizing antibodies (nAbs). It is potentially possible to change exposed capsid surfaces in AAV capsids to avoid nAb recognition. However, traditional techniques such as rational design and directed evolution only allow modest changes. AAV function becomes compromised long before full nAb avoidance is achieved. Recent advances in protein design by generative modelling provide a new way to overcome this problem by learning AAV design constraints from natural sequences. We built a variational autoencoder that could learn these sequence constraints and generate functional AAV capsid proteins de novo. More than 255 designs were synthesized and tested in vitro in two design sets, with one set dedicated to exploring uncertain regions of the sequence space. Between the two campaigns, seven designs transduced human cells with >50% efficiency, of which four avoided nAb neutralization (NT50 < 1:50) in all human sera that were reactive to AAV. In one of these designs, sequence identity to the nearest natural AAV sequence was 18% divergent. Given the radical sequence diversity and its unique serological profile, this new capsid design would represent the first ever AAV serotype designed de novo.
authors: Garton M, Chiesa G, Lyu S, Nguyen M, Benjamin J.

title: Protein Expression to Functional Interaction: Evaluating Evidence for Therapeutic Targets in Cancer
abstract: Protein abundance helps identify candidate cancer targets. Their therapeutic relevance depends on the protein’s molecular state, its role in the tumor, and how the treatment acts on it. This review synthesizes evidence from quantitative proteomics, protein interaction mapping, structural analysis, genetic perturbation, and pharmacological studies. Preclinical examples involving epidermal growth factor receptor trafficking, hexokinase 2 scaffolding, chromatin complex assembly, and protein turnover illustrate how localization, binding partners, and post-translational modifications shape protein function. Studies of targeted degraders and molecular glues show why target engagement, ubiquitin ligase recruitment, and protein loss require separate verification. Clinical responses to revumenib in genetically defined acute leukemias support targeting the menin–KMT2A interaction, while acquired MEN1 mutations reveal a mechanism of resistance. Trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-low breast cancer illustrates a distinct use of protein expression to guide patient selection when the target serves as a delivery antigen. We propose a framework that evaluates protein expression, physical interaction, functional dependence, drug mechanism, and clinical benefit as distinct forms of evidence. The framework matches validation experiments and patient-selection biomarkers to the therapeutic modality. Confidence in a target is greatest when independent evidence connects the proposed mechanism to a cancer-relevant effect at achievable and tolerable drug exposures.
authors: Ayaz M.

title: Titin-Mimetic Phase Separation Enables a High-Performance Dielectric Elastomer for Artificial Muscles.
abstract: Dielectric elastomers (DEs) are promising candidates for soft robots to achieve efficient electromechanical conversion and lightweight integration. However, conventional homogeneous DE networks face multiple inherent contradictions among compliance, robustness, and dielectric performance due to the lack of differentiated structural design at the molecular scale. Inspired by the hierarchical responsiveness of titin, we present a phase-separated fluorinated polyacrylate DE that achieves synergistic optimization of electrical and mechanical properties while exhibiting excellent self-healing capability. The proposed elastomer achieves a maximum actuation strain of 235% and an ultrahigh specific energy density of 386 J kg-1 approximately 9.65 times that of natural muscle. As such, our work demonstrates a remarkably comprehensive performance among contemporary advancements. We further demonstrate a biomimetic swimming robot that achieves efficient aquatic locomotion, highlighting the potential of our DE as a suitable candidate for high-performance artificial muscle.
authors: Du C, Yin L, Chen Y, Yang X, Dang ZM, Pang Z, Li S, Fan Q, Liu H.

title: Differential Expression of Selected miRNAs in CD44-Enriched Cell Populations of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: BackgroundOral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a clinically challenging malignancy characterized by marked biological heterogeneity, high recurrence rates, and limited progress in survival outcomes. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as key post-transcriptional regulators involved in carcinogenesis and cancer progression, yet their expression patterns within phenotypically distinct tumor cell subpopulations, particularly CD44+ cancer stem cells-like (CSC-like), remain insufficiently characterized.ObjectiveThis study investigated the expression of five candidate miRNAs (hsa-miR-26a-5p, hsa-miR-31-5p, hsa-miR-133a-5p, hsa-miR-491-3p, and hsa-miR-532-3p) in OSCC on multiple levels: public dataset analysis, whole-tissue expression profiling, and evaluation within sorted CD44+ and CD44- primary cell populations.ResultsTCGA-HNSC dataset analysis revealed upregulation of hsa-miR-31-5p and hsa-miR-532-3p (p + and CD44- cells were isolated from primary OSCC cultures (n = 5 primary cultures). hsa-miR-133a-5p, hsa-miR-491-3p, and hsa-miR-532-3p were significantly less expressed in CD44+cells than in CD44-cells (p = 0.0142, p = 0.0015 and p = 0.0002), indicating that their downregulation characterizes the CD44+-enriched fraction. These findings suggest that the tumor-suppressive miRNAs hsa-miR-133a-5p, hsa-miR-491-3p, and hsa-miR-532-3p are selectively dysregulated within CSC-like cells, potentially contributing to stemness-associated signaling and therapy resistance.ConclusionOverall, this study integrates bioinformatic, tissue-level, and cell-specific analyses to identify miRNAs implicated in CSC-like biology in OSCC, highlighting their potential as biomarkers and targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at eradicating chemotherapy-resistant CSC-like populations.
journal: Journal of oral pathology & medicine : official publication of the International Association of Oral Pathologists and the American Academy of Oral Pathology
authors: Karisik MJ, Zeljic K, Konstantinovic V, Dozic B, Nikolic N, Mitic D, Milasin J.

title: 1-Deoxynojirimycin Alleviates Osteoporosis via Promoting LRP5 Signaling in Osteoblasts and BMSCs.
abstract: Osteoporosis is the most common bone disease worldwide, and natural bioactive products that promote osteogenesis are a therapeutic strategy to prevent osteoporosis. 1-Deoxynojirimycin (DNJ) is the major bioactive small molecule in mulberry with anti-diabetic properties, but its effect on osteoporosis treatment remains largely unexplored. This study aims to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of DNJ on osteoporosis, with a particular emphasis on its ability to promote osteogenesis pathways. We investigated the bone anabolic ability of DNJ in two well-recognized osteoporosis models: ovariectomy-induced and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced osteoporosis. DNJ prevented estrogen deficiency and HFD-induced bone loss, resulting in increased osteoblast number and inhibited osteoclast number, supporting its therapeutic potential for osteoporosis. Consistent with these in vivo results, in vitro experiments showed that DNJ promoted osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization of primary BMSCs and osteoblasts without affecting primary osteoclast differentiation. Mechanistic studies revealed that DNJ increased osteoblastic mineralization by directly binding to the extracellular domain of the transmembrane protein LRP5, thus promoting the Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis to activate the transcription of osteogenesis-related genes in osteoblasts. Taken together, our study demonstrated that DNJ plays a critical role in activating the LRP5/β-catenin pathway, suggesting its potential as a candidate for osteoporosis prevention and treatment.
authors: Sun K, Li Y, Zhao K, Xu J, Tower RJ, Shen M, Zhang W, Xiong W, Li K, Li B, Zhang Q.

title: Potential Mechanisms of Jingtong Granules in Cervical Degeneration: An Integrative Multiomics and Computational Study.
abstract: Jingtong Granules is a widely used Chinese patent medicine approved by China's National Medical Products Administration for cervical spondylotic radiculopathy, but its systems-level mechanism remains insufficiently defined. This study investigated its potential mechanisms in cervical degeneration using a staged integrative framework. Candidate targets were screened and evaluated using transcriptomic, genetic, and structural evidence. Intersecting compound targets from four databases with cervical-spondylosis-associated genes identified 40 multi-source-supported drug-disease targets and 17 hub genes. The hub module was dominated by inflammatory cytokines, matrix-remodeling molecules, and central signaling regulators, with enrichment concentrated in PI3K-Akt, TNF, IL-17, and AGE-RAGE signaling. MMP9 showed the strongest pathway association, exploratory blood-discriminative potential, and nominal genetic support for spondylosis risk. AKT1 was the highest-degree signaling hub, and molecular dynamics simulations supported the stability of its quercetin and kaempferol complexes. Single-cell analysis placed the hub module in relevant disc-cell populations. However, these findings may be confounded by age because patient and control age ranges did not overlap. Overall, this study prioritizes an AKT1/MMP9-centered inflammatory and extracellular-matrix-remodeling module as a patient-grounded candidate mechanism of Jingtong Granules in cervical degeneration. Experimental validation in adequately powered disease-specific cohorts is warranted.

title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics reshape microbial respiratory responses to warming.
abstract: Earth System Models project a strong positive carbon-climate feedback from microbial respiration, the largest biotic carbon flux to the atmosphere. Yet experimental studies show that under sustained warming, the thermal sensitivity of microbial respiration often attenuates, through mechanisms that are debated and absent from models. I propose that attenuation is an emergent eco-evolutionary property: evolutionary temperature compensation lowers baseline respiratory rates within lineages; species sorting shifts biomass toward lineages with lower baseline rates; and species interactions reshape the aggregate response, all conditioned by substrate. The pace of these trait and compositional changes relative to warming determines how quickly attenuation develops. Embedding these dynamics in trait-based models could improve carbon-climate projections.
authors: Yvon-Durocher G.

title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation strategy to achieve the functional cure for chronic hepatitis B? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BackgroundFunctional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed. Included studies were prospective, experimental and observational studies, including data on outcomes after NA discontinuation in HBV DNA negative patients with positive HBsAg, involving at least 20 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir, published from 2008 to February 2026, written in English language.ResultsA total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I2=83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg ConclusionsThese results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.
authors: Pisaturo M, Grimaldi P, Onorato L, Cacace C, Coppola N.

title: Monocyte-macrophage transcriptional features in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: An exploratory prognostic signature and the potential role of DDX39A.
abstract: The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment contributes to poor outcomes in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By integrating single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE196756), TCGA data, patient-level pseudobulk analysis, and independent single-cell validation (GSE160269), we identified 315 monocyte-macrophage-associated candidate genes and developed a 10-gene prognostic signature. The signature showed exploratory risk-stratification potential in TCGA and GSE53624 cohorts. Immune infiltration analyses suggested increased myeloid and M2 macrophage-associated signals in high-risk patients. DDX39A knockdown suppressed ESCC cell migration and invasion while increasing apoptosis. Further experiments revealed associations among DDX39A expression, Wnt/β-catenin-related signaling, WISP1 secretion, and macrophage M2-associated phenotypes. Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory molecular framework for investigating ESCC prognosis and suggest a potential role for DDX39A-associated signaling in tumor-macrophage interactions.
authors: Cao S, Duan L, Lun S, Gao Z, Wang X, Li Y.

title: Nonylphenol-responsive MIR200CHG modulates colorectal cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion through EPS8L1.
abstract: BackgroundNonylphenol (NP), an environmental endocrine disruptor, has been associated with changes in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell proliferation and motility. The contribution of NP-responsive long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to these effects remains unclear.ObjectiveTo investigate the role of MIR200CHG in NP-associated CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and examine its relationship with EPS8L1 expression and ERK1/2 phosphorylation.MethodsMIR200CHG and EPS8L1 expression was examined in public CRC datasets and six paired CRC and adjacent noncancerous tissue specimens. After assessing MIR200CHG responses to NP at 10-7, 10-6, and 10-5 M for 24 h, 10-6 M was selected for subsequent cell experiments. MIR200CHG gain- and loss-of-function experiments were used to examine CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion; E-cadherin, N-cadherin, and vimentin protein expression was assessed by western blotting. Candidate MIR200CHG-associated genes were screened using ENCORI. Dual-luciferase reporter assays and actinomycin D mRNA-stability assays were performed to evaluate the post-transcriptional regulatory relationship between MIR200CHG and EPS8L1. Reciprocal rescue experiments were used to assess the functional contribution of EPS8L1, and ERK1/2 phosphorylation was examined by western blotting. In vivo, subcutaneous HCT116 xenografts were used to evaluate tumor growth under MIR200CHG knockdown with or without NP treatment.ResultsMIR200CHG and EPS8L1 expression was higher in the CRC tumor tissues, consistent with the expression patterns observed in public CRC datasets. NP increased MIR200CHG expression in CRC cells. In cultured CRC cells, MIR200CHG overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas knockdown reduced these phenotypes. These changes were accompanied by decreased E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin and vimentin after overexpression, with the opposite pattern after knockdown. Dual-luciferase reporter assays supported site-dependent regulation of EPS8L1, while actinomycin D assays indicated that MIR200CHG enhances EPS8L1 mRNA stability. EPS8L1 knockdown attenuated, whereas EPS8L1 overexpression restored, the MIR200CHG-associated phenotypes. MIR200CHG knockdown reduced subcutaneous xenograft growth, while NP treatment increased growth within the knockdown setting. Changes in ERK1/2 phosphorylation accompanied MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 manipulation.ConclusionNP-responsive MIR200CHG contributes to CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Reporter, mRNA-stability, and rescue experiments support EPS8L1 as a downstream regulator of these cellular responses. ERK1/2 phosphorylation changes were associated with MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 manipulation, while the xenograft findings support a role for MIR200CHG in primary tumor growth.
authors: Dai L, Wan L, Zhang N, Wang B, Zhong Y, Yang X.

title: The IgG4ward! Foundation guidelines on the treatment of IgG4-related disease.
abstract: IgG4-related disease is a chronic, immune-mediated, systemic condition that presents as tumour-like masses. Since publication of the last international consensus statement on the treatment of IgG4-related disease in 2015, the related literature has expanded considerably, with two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials published within the past 2 years. This foundation of evidence for treatment decisions justified new, dedicated treatment guidelines. 62 investigators-comprising 52 physicians, one medical reference librarian, eight patients, and one caregiver from 15 countries across six continents-were assembled to form a treatment guidelines group. The physicians had a broad range of specialties and patient representation spanned the full spectrum of organ involvement. The treatment guidelines group generated 183 candidate questions, which were consolidated into 40 final questions approved by the IgG4ward! Advisory Board. These questions formed the basis of a systematic literature search, led by a medical reference librarian, which informed the development of 28 treatment statements. Supporting evidence for each statement was independently graded using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence framework. The 52 physicians voted electronically on their level of agreement with each statement; consensus required more than 80% to agree or strongly agree with the statement, and was reached for 22 of the 28 statements. The evidence base reflects marked recent progress due to the publication of phase 3 clinical trials, although most statements still rely on low-level evidence. This effort provides cohesive, consensus-based guidelines from a geographically and professionally diverse group of experts in IgG4-related disease, reflecting the evolution in the field since 2015. Despite this progress, important knowledge gaps remain, and are highlighted to guide future research.

title: Marine water quality in a binational coastal zone: Integrated assessment of pollution from Tijuana to Rosarito beaches.
abstract: Water quality and beach sediment particle-size characterization are essential for assessing pollution, particularly at recreational beaches where contamination may pose human health risks. This study evaluates physicochemical, microbiological, and sediment characteristics at 13 coastal sites in Tijuana and Rosarito, Baja California, Mexico, within the broader San Diego- Tijuana binational environmental context. Conducted through the community science project "One Cast, One Community," supported by the San Diego Foundation. The investigation included three sampling campaigns between September 2023 and February 2024, yielding 39 water samples. Water quality measurements included pH, temperature, redox potential (ORP), zeta potential (pZ), Total Nitrogen (TN), Total Phosphorus (TP), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), and microbiological tests for enterococci. High enterococci concentrations (49% of samples over 200 MPN/100 mL) were relevant because people are in direct contact with water at recreational beaches. A weighted mathematical index of physicochemical parameters, the water quality index (WQI), showed that 38 of the 39 samples were in poor to extremely poor condition, attributed to mixed runoff (stormwater and unexpected sewage spills) along the Mexican coast. The beach sediment analysis included particle-size distribution, indicating a predominance of sandy soil and the rainy season's impact on particle-size distribution. The sediment samples showed a trend toward slightly moderate alkalinity. The particle-size distribution results indicated that most samples were classified as poorly graded sand (SP), reflecting a uniform grain-size distribution and high permeability. During the rainy season, larger rocks appeared, suggesting cliff erosion along the coastline.
authors: Mercado-Hernández SM, Morales-Salcido DF, Díaz-López M, González-Olachea SA, Castellanos-Armendáriz DC, Hernández-Ovalle K, Oropeza-Guzmán MT.
