title: Identification and Biological Evaluation of Fisetin as a Novel DYRK1B Inhibitor in Ovarian Cancer with Apoptotic and Ferroptotic Effects.
abstract: BackgroundDYRK1B kinase has emerged as an important regulator of tumor survival, quiescence, and chemotherapy resistance, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Natural compounds are well-known for their anticancer properties and are being studied extensively for their ability to modulate cancer-related signaling pathways.PurposeThis study aimed to screen and identify a natural compound that functions as a DYRK1B inhibitor and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic candidate for ovarian cancer treatment.Methods and resultsWe used virtual screening, in-silico molecular docking and in-vitro kinase assay to identify fisetin as a potential DYRK1B inhibitor exhibiting an IC50 of 1.2 μM. Subsequent validation through in-vitro analysis on ovarian cancer cell lines revealed a reduced phosphorylation of DYRK1B downstream targets, characterized by decreased p27 phosphorylation at (Ser 10) and increased cyclin D1 expression, indicating cell cycle re-entry of quiescent cells following effective inhibition of DYRK1B. This inhibition further triggered DNA damage and apoptosis by the accumulation of γ-H2AX, followed by the cleavage of caspase 3 and PARP. To further investigate the mechanistic role of fisetin, RNA-seq was performed, which showed an enrichment of the ferroptosis pathway. The validation of ferroptosis-associated RNA-seq data using qPCR and Western blot analysis confirmed the upregulation of transferrin receptor (TFRC) and downregulation of the iron exporter SLC40A1, leading to iron accumulation. In addition, GPX4, a crucial protein that inhibits ferroptosis by preventing lipid peroxidation, was also found to be decreased. Lipid Peroxidation assay by C11-BODIPY confirmed an increase in lipid ROS, which was effectively reversed by the treatment with ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1.ConclusionIn summary, our results revealed that fisetin is an effective DYRK1B inhibitor that further induces ovarian cancer cell death via apoptosis and also modulates ferroptosis associated pathways, underscoring the therapeutic potential of fisetin in ovarian cancer treatment.
authors: Sam A, Peng CH, Hsu KC, HuangFu WC.

title: Immunotherapy for gliomas: from checkpoint blockade to vaccines, cellular therapy, local immune engineering and combinations.
abstract: Purpose of reviewImmunotherapy has transformed the treatment of many malignancies but has not yet produced comparable improvements in survival for patients with gliomas. This review examines the biological rationale for immunotherapy across molecularly defined gliomas, lessons from unsuccessful immune checkpoint inhibitor trials, and emerging strategies including vaccines, adoptive cellular therapies, bispecific T-cell engagers, immunocytokines, innate immune modulators, oncolytic viruses, and approaches to improve delivery within the central nervous system.Recent findingsRandomized studies have established that programmed death-1 (PD-1) blockade alone is insufficient for unselected patients with glioblastoma. Treatment resistance reflects multiple interacting barriers, including low and heterogeneous antigen expression, limited T-cell infiltration, T-cell dysfunction, immunosuppressive myeloid populations, corticosteroid exposure, and treatment-associated lymphopenia. Importantly, these features differ across glioma subtypes. Recent studies demonstrate that vaccines directed against clonal IDH1 and H3K27M mutations can generate durable antigen-specific immunity, while locoregionally delivered chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cells targeting IL13Rα2, EGFR/EGFRvIII, GD2, and B7-H3 can produce rapid and occasionally durable tumor regression. Oncolytic viruses and immunocytokines provide complementary approaches to remodeling the glioma microenvironment.SummaryThe principal challenge in glioma immunotherapy is no longer demonstrating that immune cells can recognize and kill glioma cells but converting immune recognition into durable tumor control. Future progress will likely depend on matching therapy to molecular subtype, targeting multiple or clonal antigens, optimizing immune-cell trafficking and persistence, modifying the suppressive microenvironment, and longitudinally monitoring tumor and immune evolution.
authors: Owens E, Chandar MS, Khasraw M.

title: Single nucleotide polymorphisms of the CALB1 are associated with egg quality traits in chickens.
abstract: Eggshell quality is an important economic trait in egg-laying poultry. As a cytoplasmic soluble calcium-binding protein, CALB1 (Calbindin-D28k) binds Ca²⁺, modulates calcium ion transport and mediates diverse calcium-related physiological processes. In this study, 560 eggs from Jining Bairi Chickens were used as experimental materials. Twenty-five SNPs were detected in the 5' regulatory region of CALB1. Association analysis of all 25 SNPs identified 10 loci significantly associated with egg quality, among which six SNPs (-919, -879, -725, -682, -541, and -516) were significantly associated with eggshell quality: -725 was associated with eggshell thickness; -682 was associated with eggshell ratio; -919, -879, -541 and -516 were associated with egg shape index. AliBaba 2.1 prediction showed that mutations -879 (C→T), -682 (C→G) and -516 (A→G) changed transcription-factor-binding types, whereas -725 (A→G) did not, and such binding-pattern variations may regulate CALB1 expression. MethPrimer 1.0 predicted one CpG island within the 1040- bp 5' regulatory segment, yet none of the six shell-quality-related SNPs fell inside this island. In conclusion, these six 5' regulatory sites of CALB1 show potential as candidate molecular markers for eggshell quality in Jining Bairi chickens.
authors: Ma X, Shen G, Zhang Q, Wang W, Tang H.

title: Sangmei Zhike Granules alleviate type 2 inflammation in allergic asthma via the TLR4/PI3Kγ/NF-κB axis: insights from UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS, network pharmacology, and experimental validation.
abstract: BackgroundAllergic asthma is a common allergen-driven phenotype of asthma with a high prevalence. Current first-line therapies are limited by poor treatment adherence, frequent relapse after discontinuation, and heterogeneous therapeutic responses. Sangmei Zhike Granules (SMZK), a traditional Chinese medicine formula formulated to dispel wind, diffuse the Lung, and nourish yin, have demonstrated therapeutic efficacy against allergic asthma; however, their underlying mechanisms remain unclear.ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify the lung-distributed constituents of SMZK and elucidate their mechanisms of action against allergic asthma.MethodsUltra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS) was used to characterize the chemical constituents of SMZK and identify SMZK-derived prototype compounds in rat lung tissue. Network pharmacology analysis was subsequently performed based on the screened prototype compounds to predict potential targets and signaling pathways. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced rat model of allergic asthma was established, and the therapeutic effects of SMZK were evaluated using pulmonary function testing, histopathological examination, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The predicted signaling pathway was further validated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting (WB), and ELISA.ResultsA total of 812 chemical constituents were identified in SMZK, and 41 SMZK-derived prototype compounds were detected in rat lung tissue. Network pharmacology analysis of 26 prototype compounds that met the screening criteria identified IL6, MAPK8, ESR1, SRC, STAT3, TNF, MAPK3, MAPK1, and RELA as key targets, with the PI3K-Akt and Toll-like receptor signaling pathways emerging as major candidate pathways. SMZK improved pulmonary function, alleviated pulmonary inflammatory cell infiltration, and attenuated type 2 airway inflammation. Mechanistically, SMZK downregulated the expression of TLR4 and PI3Kγ and inhibited NF-κB p65 activation, thereby suppressing the TLR4/PI3Kγ/NF-κB signaling axis and ameliorating type 2 airway inflammation.ConclusionThe lung-distributed constituents of SMZK may attenuate type 2 airway inflammation in allergic asthma primarily by suppressing the TLR4/PI3Kγ/NF-κB signaling axis.
journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
authors: Luo J, Li K, Huang G, Gong X, Cui H, Ren P.

title: ATP Dyshomeostasis and Cellular Senescence: A Potential Mechanistic Nexus in Degenerative Skeletal Diseases.
abstract: Degenerative skeletal diseases are chronic disorders characterized by progressive deterioration, maladaptive remodeling or repair failure within bone, articular cartilage, intervertebral disc (IVD) and osteochondral tissues, which exhibit different but related states of bioenergetic dysfunction, oxidative stress-induced injury, persistent inflammation and disruption of tissue homeostasis. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) homeostasis, a central metabolic regulator of cell activity and tissue homeostasis, is typically perturbed in degenerative microenvironments together with mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory stimulation and non-physiological mechanical loading conditions, while cellular senescence may also coexist with purinergic dysregulation, oxidative stress and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) damage that favor senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-mediated inflammatory amplification. Mechanistically, ATP dyshomeostasis includes at least three distinct processes: decreased intracellular ATP availability representative of bioenergetic failure, extracellular ATP release serving as a damage-associated signal through P2 receptors and the conversion of extracellular ATP to adenosine by ectonucleoside triphosphate diphosphohydrolase 1 (CD39)/ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73) with subsequent P1 receptor signaling. This Review surveys the link between ATP dyshomeostasis and cellular senescence as an integrative framework across osteoporosis, osteoarthritis (OA), intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), degenerative spinal diseases, osteophyte formation and osteonecrosis, before discussing its relevance to disease progression, defective tissue repair and therapeutic translation. While ATP signaling is not intrinsically harmful, its effects are highly cell type- and receptor subtype-specific and depend on ATP concentration and disease stage. Much of the existing evidence remains either associative or preclinical, and direct causal relationships linking ATP dyshomeostasis, cellular senescence and degenerative disease progression are not yet established. Disease-specific validation in human tissues and clinical settings is sparse, especially outside OA and IDD. Greater clarity around these context-specific interactions may elucidate shared pathogenic mechanisms and inform candidate metabolic, senescence-targeted and precision-stratification approaches for future evaluation.
authors: Li Z, Lin W, He Y, Song Z, Xue Y, Wang W, Jiang Z, Wang K, Li Y, Zhang H, Gao Q.

title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temporal dynamics of colorectal carcinogenesis, the evolution of molecular classification systems, including their computational and machine-learning foundations and emerging image-based prediction approaches, molecular drivers and the tumor microenvironment (TME) of CRC by summarizing the most investigated molecular pathways involved in CRC pathogenesis and their role as biomarkers for early CRC diagnosis based on the three main molecular mechanisms of colorectal carcinogenesis: chromosomal instability (CIN), microsatellite instability (MSI), and CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). Importantly, emerging evidence reveals that the TME acts as an important factor in driving CRC progression by regulating the immune system through dynamic cellular and molecular interactions. In particular, tumor metabolic reprogramming and microbiota-driven alterations act as major drivers of therapy resistance and immune escape. Combining these mechanisms will enhance biomarker discovery and aid in developing precision medicine for patients with CRC. This review also highlights the regulatory roles of key signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tumor protein p53 (TP53), and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling, during CRC initiation and progression, while further addressing current targeted therapies and emerging precision-based and experimental therapeutic strategies.
authors: Aldeyarbi S, Elhanafy E, Saber-Ayad M, Abu Almaaty AH, Sagheer A, Hassan MK.

title: Next-generation CAR-NK therapies: molecular engineering strategies for solid tumors.
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are innate lymphocytes that exert cytotoxic activity against malignant and virus-infected cells without prior antigen sensitization. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-engineered NK (CAR-NK) cells combine CAR-dependent tumor-antigen recognition with endogenous NK-cell receptor-dependent cytotoxicity against stress-induced ligands and tumor cells with reduced HLA class I expression. Clinical studies of allogeneic CD19 CAR-NK cells have reported antitumor responses without notable cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, or graft-versus-host disease. CAR-NK cells also support allogeneic manufacturing for off-the-shelf cellular therapy. NK-associated intracellular domains including DAP10, DAP12, 2B4, and CD3ζ, cytokine expression using IL-15 or IL-21, and gene editing of inhibitory molecules have been incorporated into CAR-NK designs. PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 and JAK-STAT signaling, glycolytic metabolism, mitochondrial activity, and transcriptional control contribute to CAR-NK cytotoxic function. Recent CAR-NK studies have also examined inhibitory-receptor editing, chemokine receptor expression, and metabolic engineering to improve cytotoxic activity, intratumoral infiltration, and resistance to hypoxia and immunosuppressive signaling in solid tumors. This review examines the molecular mechanisms involved in NK-cell activation and metabolism and evaluates molecular engineering strategies for next-generation CAR-NK therapy in solid tumors.
authors: Kim ME, Lim Y, Lee JS.

title: Integrated Machine Learning and Experimental Validation Identify Shared Aging-Related Molecular Signatures in Alzheimer's Disease and Osteoporosis.
abstract: BackgroundAging is a key biological driver implicated in the initiation and progression of both Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Osteoporosis (OP). However, the shared aging-related molecular alterations underlying these disorders remain incompletely understood.MethodsTranscriptomic datasets of AD and OP, together with curated aging-related genes (ARGs), were systematically collected. Differential expression analysis was conducted using the limma algorithm, followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify disease-associated gene modules. Multiple machine learning algorithms were subsequently employed to prioritize candidate biomarkers, and model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Immune infiltration profiles were characterized via CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) was conducted to validate the expression of six core candidate genes.ResultsIntegrated analysis identified 228 aging-related genes shared by AD and OP. EGR1, NFKBIA, UQCRC2, RB1, CREBBP, and NDUFV1 were selected based on the comparative performance of 130 machine learning models for disease prediction. Enrichment analyses linked these genes to cellular senescence, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and cell-cycle regulation, suggesting convergent aging-related alterations in AD and OP. RT-qPCR analysis in the D-galactose-induced senescence models revealed cell-type-specific expression patterns: all six genes were significantly altered in HT22 cells, whereas EGR1, NFKBIA, UQCRC2, and NDUFV1 were significantly altered in MC3T3-E1 cells, with no significant changes observed in RB1 or CREBBP. Moreover, they exhibited robust diagnostic potential, as reflected by nomogram analyses, and showed significant correlations with immune cell infiltration profiles.ConclusionThis study elucidates shared aging-related genes linking AD and OP. The six identified hub ARGs demonstrate significant immunological relevance and diagnostic value. Collectively, these findings offer novel insights into shared pathogenic mechanisms and highlight potential targets for integrated therapeutic strategies.
authors: Guo X, Guo Z, Peng T, Pan J, Zhang M, Ye X, Wen J, Liu X, Li Y, Lin X.

title: Natural and Synthetic Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase Inhibitors for Therapeutic Applications.
abstract: Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase (DHODH) is an important mitochondrial enzyme that plays a key role in the catalysis of an important step in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis, which in turn supports DNA and RNA production. This enzyme is highly conserved across different organisms, including humans, protozoan parasites, and bacteria, although subtle differences in its structure make it possible to selectively inhibit this enzyme. In recent years, this enzyme has emerged as a promising target in the development of therapeutic agents against different diseases, including cancer, autoimmune diseases, and malaria. Various natural and synthetic compounds have shown promise as inhibitors of this enzyme. While natural inhibitors such as lapachol (1), piperine (5), and baicalein (6) provide a starting point in terms of chemical structure, synthetic inhibitors such as GSK983 (20), Brequinar (21), Teriflunomide (22), Vidofludimus (35), BAY 2402234 (36), and Tenovin (40) achieve high potency and specificity against the human enzyme. In the context of malaria treatment, selective inhibitors such as DSM265 (37), DSM267 (38), and DSM421 (39) selectively inhibit Plasmodium falciparum DHODH with minimal cross-reactivity to the human enzyme. This review outlines the conservation and variability in the structure of this enzyme in different organisms, and the mode of interaction with inhibitors, as well as the different strategies that have been adopted to develop potent and selective inhibitors of this enzyme with minimal side effects in the context of cancer, autoimmune diseases, and malaria treatment.
authors: Sures PL, Tan CY, Choo YM.

title: [Not Available].
abstract: Immediate implant-based breast reconstruction (IBBR) has become a key component of surgical breast cancer management. Available evidence supports its oncologic safety, with no detrimental effect on overall survival, disease-free survival, or local recurrence, while improving quality of life and reducing the psychological burden of mastectomy. Its main advantage lies in preservation of the native skin envelope, allowing maintenance of skin quality, pigmentation, and, to some extent, sensitivity, even within an evolving reconstructive pathway that may later include autologous conversion. Patient selection relies on the combined assessment of oncologic criteria, breast morphology, and anticipated adjuvant treatments. Ideal candidates are patients with small- to medium-volume breasts, minimal or no ptosis, and well-vascularized mastectomy flaps. Nipple-sparing mastectomy is the preferred option when oncologic safety criteria are met, whereas large and/or ptotic breasts require tailored strategies, including skin-reducing mastectomy or staged sequential approaches. In our practice, direct-to-implant prepectoral reconstruction is used almost systematically, combined with matrix support, most often with resorbable synthetic meshes. Tissue expanders are rarely used, includingin patients expected to receive postmastectomy radiotherapy, as our preferred strategy is to irradiate the definitive implant when needed. In the event of unfavorable evolution, implant revision or secondary conversion to autologous reconstruction may be proposed. Recent technical innovations, including minimally invasive endoscopic and robot-assisted approaches, may further improve aesthetic outcomes while reducing surgical morbidity.
journal: Annales de chirurgie plastique et esthetique
authors: Mathieu O, Honart JF, Leymarie N.

title: Recurrent cerebrospinal fluid herpesvirus PCR positivity: a retrospective analysis of inter-positive intervals.
abstract: Introduction. Herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2 (HSV-1 and HSV-2) and varicella-zoster virus (VZV) are established causes of central nervous system infection, whereas human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) DNA may be detected in more heterogeneous contexts. However, longitudinal patterns of recurrent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) PCR positivity remain poorly characterized.Hypothesis/Gap statement. When the same herpesvirus is detected in CSF on different dates, the meaning of the interval between positive results is uncertain. Its observed distribution may also depend on retesting opportunities and changes in testing practice.Aim. To describe inter-positive intervals across five herpesvirus targets and assess how their interpretation changes with operational cut-offs and calendar-period testing patterns.Methodology. We retrospectively analysed qualitative CSF PCR results for five herpesviruses from 16 March 2010 to 30 March 2026. Recurrent positivity required at least two distinct positive dates per patient-virus pair. First-to-last intervals were classified at 30 days, with exploratory cut-offs of 14, 60 and 90 days. Calendar-period analyses used FilmArray Meningitis/Encephalitis panel introduction on 10 November 2020 as the boundary and period-specific positive pairs as denominators.Results. Among 19,959 interpretable target-level results (994 positive), 33 recurrent pairs were identified: HHV-6 (18), VZV (7), HSV-1 (5), HSV-2 (2) and cytomegalovirus (1). The median first-to-last inter-positive interval was 11 days (interquartile range, 4-185; range, 1-864). Nineteen intervals were <30 days and 14 were ≥30 days; HHV-6 accounted for 10 longer pairs, all pre-implementation, limiting target-specific interpretation. The HHV-6 versus non-HHV-6 comparison was not significant (10/18 versus 4/15; two-sided Fisher's exact P=0.158). Within-period recurrent positivity was 24/771 (3.1%) in the pre-implementation calendar period and 8/176 (4.5%) in the post-implementation period; corresponding HHV-6 recurrent positivity was 17/302 (5.6%) and 1/84 (1.2%).Conclusion. Recurrent CSF herpesvirus PCR positivity showed heterogeneous target composition and inter-positive intervals. These data cannot distinguish clustered retesting, persistence, reactivation or chromosomal integration. Interpretation requires prior testing history and linked clinical or quantitative virological data.
authors: Kim JY, Jung BK, Jeon JS, Kim JK.

title: Cell Wall Engineering of Kluyveromyces lactis for Efficient Extracellular Production of Bovine Chymosin.
abstract: Bovine chymosin, an essential milk-clotting enzyme widely utilized in cheese production, was successfully expressed in the generally recognized as safe yeast Kluyveromyces lactis GG799. The recombinant strain SKB was initially constructed. Subsequently, 15 genes involved in the cell wall biosynthesis pathway were knocked out to evaluate their effects on chymosin release. Notably, the double-deletion strain SKB7 (ΔKLLA0_C00803g, ΔKLLA0_F20031g), involving two genes encoding a protein involved in the regulation of cell wall structure/stress response and a cell wall protein, exhibited a 4.5-fold increase in chymosin activity (498 SU/mL) in shake-flask. In fed-batch fermentation, strain SKB7 achieved a high chymosin activity of 4469 SU/mL after 96 h in a 5 L bioreactor. Transcriptomic analysis reveals distinct gene expression in strain SKB7 compared with SKB-3, representing enhanced metabolic robustness and growth potential. This study demonstrates that cell wall engineering is an effective strategy for improving chymosin production in K. lactis.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
authors: Song Y, Zhou J, Xie D, Wang J, Meng C, Dong J, Han R, Ni Y.

title: Polysaccharide A1 from Bran-Fried Atractylodes lancea Regulates Cyclophosphamide-induced Intestinal Immune Injury in Mice via the Faecalibaculum rodentium-Mediated IAA-AHR/RORC Axis.
abstract: Cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury is often characterized by gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolite imbalance. Bran-fried Atractylodes lancea polysaccharide (FALP-A1) protects against cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury by significantly modulating Faecalibaculum rodentium abundance. However, the mechanism of FALP-A1-mediated F. rodentium regulation remains unclear. Ex vivo digestion confirmed FALP-A1 is stable in the simulated upper gastrointestinal tract, while fermentation showed it is degradable and enriches F. rodentium. Nontargeted fecal metabolomics of in vivo mice co-treated with the FALP-A1 and Faecalibaculum rodentium, together with ex vivo coculture systems, identified Indoleacetic acid (IAA) as a potential metabolite. We further validated that IAA protects the intestinal barrier in cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury by modulating nuclear transcription factor RORC mRNA expression. However, these effects were reversed by an AHR inhibitor. This study elucidates the central role of "FALP-A1-F. rodentium-IAA-AHR/RORC" axis in protecting against cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury, providing evidence for pharmacological potential of FALP-A1 and indole-3-acetic acid.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
authors: Nie W, Xiao Y, Zhong L, Wu K, Wang D, Liu Y, Qu L.

title: Transcriptome Analysis Revealed a Key Sugar Transporter CitSWEET15 and Its Regulatory Network for Sugar Accumulation in Citrus Fruit.
abstract: Sugar accumulation is a major determinant of citrus fruit quality, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated the dynamic changes in sugars and organic acids during the development of 'Ehime 38' citrus fruit and explored the regulatory mechanisms of sugar accumulation through integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and functional analyses. Fruit maturation was accompanied by increased sugar accumulation and reduced organic acid levels, reshaping the sugar-acid balance for flavor formation. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis identified CitSWEET15, encoding a plasma-membrane-localized sucrose transporter, as a key candidate. Transient overexpression of CitSWEET15 promoted the accumulation of sucrose, glucose, and fructose in fruit. Furthermore, CitLBD18 directly bound to the CitSWEET15 promoter and activated its transcription, establishing a CitLBD18-CitSWEET15 regulatory module associated with sugar accumulation. These findings provide new insights into the transcriptional regulation of sugar accumulation in citrus fruit and identify potential molecular targets for improving fruit quality.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
authors: Liu J, Li X, Kou Y, Huang P, Li Y, Qiu X, Zhao L, Zhu F, Wang S, Zhong D, Zhang M, Wang X, He J.

title: Drug Design and Discovery: The Long Road From Hansch Analysis to Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: The present article traces the long journey of the historical evolution and transformation of QSAR from its early days to its current role in drug discovery. It begins with the breakthrough created by the introduction of data analysis and highlights the major advances achieved throughout its development. Changes in molecular representation resulted in an explosion of molecular descriptors, while the rapid accumulation of large amounts of data demanded the application of elaborated statistical techniques. Today, machine learning and artificial intelligence have become integral components of pharmaceutical research, supporting every stage of the drug discovery pipeline, from target identification and hit discovery to lead optimization and the prediction of ADMET properties. At the same time, strict prerequisites have been established to ensure the development of QSAR models capable of reliable and robust predictions. Model validation, applicability domain, and model interpretability are fundamental principles of robust QSAR modeling. These principles are closely related to the distinction between local and global models, reflecting the trade-off between predictive performance, generalizability, and mechanistic interpretability. Finally, multi-objective optimization is discussed, as an approach to address the complex and often conflicting requirements, associated with successful drug candidates and decision-making throughout the drug discovery pipeline, including library design.
authors: Tsantili-Kakoulidou A.

title: PAM-Free Programmable Enzymatic Cascade Design Enabling Highly Sensitive CRISPR/Cas12a Lateral Flow Assay for Foodborne Pathogen Detection.
abstract: CRISPR/Cas12a-assisted nucleic acid assays have shown great potential for rapid pathogen detection. However, their implementation in lateral flow assays remains constrained by strict protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements and low-contrast, signal-off readouts. To effectively address these limitations, we present a new PAM-free programmable enzymatic cascade-enabled CRISPR/Cas12a lateral flow assay (PAEC-LFA) for highly sensitive foodborne pathogen detection. In this strategy, target amplification products are enzymatically digested to generate programmable single-stranded DNA activators, enabling PAM-independent Cas12a activation and flexible target recognition. Upon activation, Cas12a exhibits efficient trans-cleavage activity, which subsequently triggers terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT)-mediated extension, forming an enzymatic cascade that amplifies signal output and generates a high-contrast signal-on readout on lateral flow assays. Integrating RPA and enzymatic digestion with PAM-free Cas12a-TdT signal amplification into two sequential one-pot modules simplifies the workflow, minimizes contamination risk, and maintains effective amplification performance. Under optimized conditions, PAEC-LFA achieved detection limits of 1.05 CFU/mL for Salmonella and Staphylococcus aureus, and 3.13 CFU/mL for Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Visual detection limits in spiked food samples reached 10 CFU/mL for all three pathogens. This work establishes a generalizable PAM-free enzymatic cascade framework for highly sensitive CRISPR/Cas12a lateral flow assays, advancing practical pathogen detection in food safety applications.
authors: Chen Q, Chen Z, Peng Y, Wang H, Xu H, Yao B, Fatima N, Chen W.

title: Dimethyl Sulfoxide/H<sub>2</sub>O Cosolvent Reconstructs Fe<sup>2+</sup> Solvation Sheath and Breaks Water H‑Bond Network for Stable Aqueous Iron Metal Batteries.
abstract: Aqueous iron metal batteries are promising candidates for safe and low-cost stationary energy storage, but their practical application remains hindered by poor Fe anode reversibility due to hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), by-product formation, and poor low-temperature operation. Herein, a dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)-water cosolvent electrolyte is developed to address these challenges through simultaneous reconstruction of the Fe2+ solvation sheath and disruption of the intrinsic hydrogen-bond network among water molecules. Molecular dynamics simulations and spectroscopic characterization reveal that DMSO preferentially coordinates with Fe2+ ions, displacing water molecules from the primary solvation sheath and substantially reducing interfacial water activity. This solvation restructuring effectively suppresses parasitic HER and the associated irreversible formation of FeSO4(OH)·3H2O by-products, as confirmed by X-ray diffraction and in situ optical microscopy. As a result, the optimized electrolyte (DMSO/H2O = 2:8) enables stable Fe plating/stripping with a compact electrode morphology, achieving over 350 h of cycling stability in Fe//Fe symmetric cells at 1 mA cm-2, and demonstrating a significantly enhanced Coulombic efficiency. Furthermore, the disruption of the hydrogen-bond network by DMSO depresses the freezing point of the electrolyte from -2.8 to -20.9 °C, endowing the Fe//PBA full cell with stable cycling for over 400 cycles at -20 °C.
authors: Li L, Liang M, Shangguan E, Wang L, Niu Y, Gao S.

title: Automated Perovskite Film Fabrication with High-Resolution Data Acquisition and Machine Learning Analysis.
abstract: Lead halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics; nevertheless, fabrication of the perovskite photoactive layer remains highly intricate with film formation strongly modulated by various processing and environmental factors. Here, we report an environment-controlled, robot-assisted platform for automated thin-film fabrication designed to quantify and visualize perovskite crystallization in situ. Beyond precise control of each processing step, the system captures dynamic phenomena spanning subsecond color evolution and millisecond antisolvent droplet behavior while simultaneously recording slower environmental parameters (temperature, humidity/moisture, and concentrations of oxygen and volatile organic compounds). For optoelectronic assessment, we implemented time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) measurements together with photoluminescence intensity quantification by using a complementary automated evaluation system. By combining machine-learning regression with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) analysis, we identify the environmental parameters that most impact film properties and propose a feedback strategy to refine data and extract precise effects of process factors. A comparative study of a two-cation perovskite, (FAPbI3)0.87(MAPbBr3)0.13, and a three-cation perovskite, FA0.85MA0.10Cs0.05PbI3, further reveals markedly different sensitivities to environmental factors (FA, formamidinium; MA, methylammonium), in particular, temperature and resultant phase transition kinetics during thermal annealing. Based on the ML analysis and feedback, we tuned the antisolvent droplet velocity and obtained the maximized power conversion efficiency of 24.4%. Notably, this manual device fabrication was consistent with the results obtained by the automated system. This work establishes a practical route to stable, quantitative, and mechanistically informed investigation of solution-processed photovoltaic films.
authors: Kado R, Iwai F, Nishikubo R, Ishiwari F, Saeki A.

title: Nanoscale Immune Activator for Enhancing CD8+ T Cell Infiltration in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: The infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment is a well-established determinant of immunotherapy efficacy and patient prognosis. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing this process and the therapeutic strategies capable of modulating it remain largely unexplored. Here, we identify HCC-IN-247 as a candidate compound that enhances IFNβ-driven CD8+ T cell infiltration both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the long noncoding RNA LINC02084 directly interacts with the transcription factor GLIS1 and facilitates its recruitment to the IFNβ promoter. HCC-IN-247 was identified through screening to target the LINC02084-GLIS1 binding interface, thereby stabilizing this RNA-protein complex. Stabilization of the complex significantly enhances IFNβ transcription, which in turn upregulates CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression and promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration. Furthermore, this study engineered a nanoparticle-based delivery system, designated Lip@RA@BSA-PD-L1/IN-247, for the codelivery of HCC-IN-247 and the anti-PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in HCC treatment. These nanoparticles exhibited robust tumor-specific accumulation and elicited potent synergistic antitumor activity against HCC in mice. Collectively, our findings establish HCC-IN-247 as an activator of the tumor immune microenvironment and provide a preclinical basis for a combined immunotherapeutic approach to HCC.
authors: Zhang D, Peng D, Wang X, Gao Y, Liu Z, Yang R, Wei T, Li C, Gao C, Jiang Z, Miao H, Li P, Qi X.

title: Unveiling Phase-Dependent Fe-O Bond-Guided Nitrate Reduction at Biocathodes: Balancing Interfacial Reactivity and Iron Bioavailability.
abstract: Iron oxides are widespread in anoxic water environments, yet how their structures regulate microbial nitrate reduction remains unclear. Here, we reveal that phase-dependent Fe-O bond characteristics guide denitrification in bioelectrochemical system (BES) by balancing lattice-iron bioavailability and interfacial electrochemical reactivity at biocathodes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that surface Fe-O bond covalency was associated with the thermodynamic barrier to lattice-iron release. α-Fe2O3, with the most negative ICOHP, exhibited the strongest Fe-O bonding and restricted iron release, thereby limiting microbial iron acquisition and downstream Fe-S cluster assembly. In contrast, γ-Fe2O3 and γ-FeOOH exhibited higher surface electroactivity but suffered from structural instability, evidenced by phase transformation, cell encrustation, and elevated microbial mortality. With mixed valence and balanced Fe-O bonding characteristics, Fe3O4 achieved the highest denitrification efficiency (17.8-fold enhancement over its abiotic control), which enabled direct Fe(II) uptake via the FeoAB system, bypassing siderophore-dependent acquisition and simultaneously activating both TonB-mediated iron acquisition and Fur-flavin-regulated respiratory pathways. This dual-pathway activation supported enhancement in biomass growth, intracellular electron transfer, and Fe-S cluster-dependent enzymatic activity. These findings help establish Fe-O bond characteristics as a key structural factor for Fe-N coupling and offer a structural perspective for rational design of iron-oxide-based nitrate-removal technologies.
authors: Xing Y, Kong Z, Wang H, Man S, Huang B, Yan Q.

title: MOF-303-Functionalized Glass Fiber Separator Enabling Synergistic Ion Flux Regulation and Desolvation Modulation for Durable Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries.
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. However, their practical deployment remains hindered by interfacial instability of the Zn anode, including dendritic growth, hydrogen evolution, and parasitic byproduct formation. Here, an aluminum-based metal-organic framework-functionalized glass fiber separator (MOF-303-GF) is developed to regulate Zn2+ transport and deposition chemistry in AZIBs. With the porous framework and abundant zincophilic binding sites of MOF-303, the modified separator reconstructs the local ion transport environment, improves electrolyte wettability, and delivers a high ionic conductivity of 22.6 mS cm-1 together with a Zn2+ transference number of 0.46. More importantly, MOF-303-GF homogenizes the interfacial electric field and Zn2+ concentration distribution, facilitates desolvation-coupled charge transfer, and induces preferential Zn deposition along the Zn(002) plane, thereby effectively suppressing dendrite growth and side reactions. As a result, the Zn symmetric cell achieves highly reversible Zn plating/stripping for over 3700 h at 2.0 mA cm-2, while the Zn∥Cu cell exhibits a Coulombic efficiency of 99.0%. When paired with a sodium vanadate (NaV3O8, NVO) cathode, the Zn||NVO full cell delivers improved cycling stability and retains 58.5% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. We show an effective separator engineering strategy for coupling ion flux homogenization with interfacial reaction regulation, providing new insights into the design of durable AZIB systems.
journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
authors: Dong H, Wang Y, Wang D, Wang G.

title: Active Learning Enables Discovery of Asymmetric Dual-Atom Catalysts for Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrocatalysis.
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia requires a delicate balance between nitrate activation, hydrogen delivery, suppression of competing hydrogen evolution, and stabilization of the catalytic metal centers. Such coupled requirements make the rational design of dual-atom catalysts challenging, particularly when the two metal sites and their coordination environments contribute differently to the reaction. Here, we establish an interpretable active-learning framework to navigate the chemical space of asymmetric dual-atom catalysts and uncover the physicochemical origins of their performance. Rather than learning an empirical activity score, the framework predicts individual DFT-derived properties from readily accessible elemental and structural descriptors and uses uncertainty-aware sampling to iteratively explore previously uncharted metal-pair and coordination environments. Model interpretation reveals distinct roles of the two metal sites in regulating nitrate activation and hydrogen adsorption, and identifies moderate electronic asymmetry coupled with mixed N/O coordination as a favorable design regime. Guided by these principles, active learning efficiently explores an expanded library of 1050 structures and progressively identifies candidates beyond the initial chemical space. Prospective DFT validation highlights Mo-Ta/N3O3-C, Mo-Nb/N3O3-C, and Mo-Nb/N5O1-C as promising catalysts, whose performance arises from a balanced combination of reaction thermodynamics, adsorption selectivity, and structural stability. These findings establish a transferable strategy for designing multifunctional dual-atom sites and demonstrate how interpretable, closed-loop learning can transform catalyst screening from property prediction into mechanism-guided materials discovery.
journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
authors: Xu Z, Niu G, Shi Z, Yan G, He X, Zhang Y, Deng Q, Wang F.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals transcriptional dynamics underlying maize ligule development.
abstract: The maize ligule arises from the preligule band (PLB) at the leaf blade-sheath boundary and provides a tractable system for investigating how boundary-associated positional cues direct local cell-fate specification and tissue outgrowth. Although key genes involved in ligule development have been identified and cell-resolved profiles are available for stages after PLB formation, how PLB acquires ligule identity and initiates outgrowth remains unclear at the cellular level. Here, we have used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to profile maize ligular regions at the preligule band and ligule outgrowth stages. The atlas resolved major cell populations and identified a ligule population supported by established marker genes, published laser microdissection transcriptomes, and RNA in situ hybridization. Pseudotime trajectory and co-expression network analyses resolved two sequential transcriptional programs corresponding to ligule initiation and subsequent outgrowth. ZmIDD30 was identified as a promising candidate transcriptional regulator, and molecular assays showed that it bound to the promoters of ZmPIN1c and ZmVG1 and activated their transcription, suggesting potential links to auxin transport and lipid metabolism during ligule development. Overall, these findings define a cell-resolved transcriptional progression in which a localized epidermal domain at the blade-sheath boundary progressively acquires ligule identity and progresses toward outgrowth.
journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
authors: Wei F, Xia M, Galbraith DW, Huang J, Song CP, Pan J, Yang X, Sun G.

title: Synergistic Assembly of High-Symmetry Motifs Enhances Nonlinear Optical Response in the Chromium-Based Thiophosphates ACrP2S7 (A = K, Rb, Cs).
abstract: Transition-metal chalcogenides represent promising candidates for nonlinear optical (NLO) materials, yet Cr-based ones remain largely unexplored owing to the challenge of simultaneously achieving suitable electronic structures and noncentrosymmetric structures. Herein, we report the reactive flux assisted solid-state synthesis of a series of thiophosphates ACrP2S7 (A = K, Rb, Cs) and systematically investigate their structural chemistry and optical properties. All compounds crystallize in the polar monoclinic space group C2 and feature a layered structure composed of distorted [CrS6] octahedra and [P2S7] dimers, which cooperatively construct low-symmetric [CrP2S11] motifs. Structural analysis reveals that the polar structure can be derived from the centrosymmetric CrPS4 through symmetry breaking via insertion of A+ ions. The band gaps of ACrP2S7 are tunable in the range of 1.22-1.27 eV, and the second-harmonic generation measurements confirm that ACrP2S7 represents the first Cr-based chalcogenide exhibiting significant NLO activity (0.3-0.8 × AgGaS2). This work suggests that Cr-based thiophosphates can also be explored as promising infrared NLO materials.
authors: Wang B, Su LH, Zhang YX, Wu ZC, Du QY, Ran MY, Guo SP.

title: DBNAMP: A Chemically Curated Database of Noncanonical Antimicrobial Peptides with Standardized Molecular Representations.
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising anti-infective agents, yet conventional sequence-centered resources often inadequately represent noncanonical residues, stereochemical variations, terminal modifications, cyclization, lipidation, stapling, and peptidomimetic scaffolds, limiting chemically meaningful annotation, comparison, and structure-activity relationship analysis. Here, we present DBNAMP, a manually curated and chemically explicit database of AMP-like entities containing residue-level noncanonical features, molecular-level covalent modifications, or both; it currently comprises 1,859 curated entries, including 1,421 entries with computed representative three-dimensional conformers and 129 standardized controlled-vocabulary records for noncanonical residues and peptide modifications. Among 537 source-level ambiguity-audit records, 84 remained unresolved after review, of which 82 retained at least one uppercase X character. Only one such record was included in the final release. Each DBNAMP entry integrates sequence, chemical annotation, antimicrobial activity, target organisms, physicochemical descriptors, molecular representations, structural information, and literature or patent provenance. In addition to browsing, filtering, and data download, DBNAMP enables chemically informed exploration of related peptide entities through standardized molecular representations and incorporates a lightweight SMILES-based prioritization module for preliminary ranking of candidate molecules. By bridging sequence-level peptide annotation and chemically explicit molecular representation, DBNAMP supports chemoinformatics analysis, structure-activity relationship studies, virtual screening, and computer-aided design of chemically diverse AMP candidates and is freely accessible at https://dbnamp.cn/.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
authors: Liang T, Li B, Hong X, Yang L, Li J.

title: Senescence-Associated Loss of α-Synuclein in Brain Microvascular Endothelium Compromises Tight Junctions and Disrupts Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is an early feature of brain aging, but the endothelial mechanisms preserving barrier resilience remain unclear. Although we have reported α-synuclein (SNCA) supports vascular endothelial homeostasis, its role in the brain microvascular endothelium is unknown. Because SNCA loss suppresses eNOS/NO signaling and promotes endothelial β-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) induction, we investigated whether senescence-associated SNCA decline drives BACE1-dependent BBB injury. Replicative senescence in human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) reduced SNCA expression. siRNA-mediated SNCA depletion induced a senescence-like state with increased β-galactosidase activity, CDKN2A/p16 and TP53/p53 induction, and decreased SIRT1, eNOS, and glypican-1. SNCA-deficient HBMECs showed impaired proliferation and migration, loss of occludin and ZO-1, increased permeability, and elevated BACE1 expression and activity; BACE1 co-silencing restored junctional proteins and normalized permeability. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling excluded most classical BACE1-regulatory mechanisms and instead implicated coordinated disruption of the NO-sGC-cGMP axis, consistent with the partial rescue by the NO donor SNAP. Amyloid-β42 oligomers sensitized SNCA-deficient monolayers to barrier injury at concentrations that left control monolayers unaffected. Global SNCA-knockout mice exhibited multiregional BBB leakage, reduced occludin, ZO-1, and claudin-5, and p53 immunoreactivity confined to CD31-positive microvessels. This phenotype was present in young adulthood and was reproduced in aged wild-type mice, which showed reduced SNCA in isolated brain microvessels. These findings identify senescence-associated endothelial SNCA loss as a candidate contributor to brain microvascular barrier vulnerability, describing an endothelial stress pathway in which SNCA insufficiency is associated with BACE1-dependent tight junction destabilization in the aging brain.

title: HDAC3 drives type II alveolar epithelial barrier dysfunction via MKP1 deacetylation in radiation-induced lung injury.
abstract: Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is a key biological macromolecule involved in protein acetylation and inflammatory signalling. Although its biological functions are well recognised, the molecular mechanisms through which HDAC3 regulates stress-induced responses of alveolar epithelial cells during early-stage radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) remain incompletely understood. In this study, using AT2-specific HDAC3 conditional knockout mice as well as primary mouse AT2 and A549 cell models, we found that radiation markedly upregulates HDAC3 expression, whereas HDAC3 knockdown alleviates radiation-induced disruption of the alveolar epithelial barrier. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that HDAC3 influences barrier integrity by modulating MAPK-mediated inflammation and apoptosis. Pharmacological intervention with the selective HDAC3 inhibitor RGFP966 also demonstrated that HDAC3 inhibition mitigates radiation-induced oxidative stress imbalance. Mechanistically, HDAC3 deacetylates MKP1, enhancing p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) phosphorylation, promoting FBJ murine osteosarcoma viral oncogene homolog (c-Fos) expression, and activating activator protein-1 (AP-1), thereby driving downstream inflammatory signalling. Collectively, our findings support a role for the HDAC3-MKP1-p38 MAPK-c-Fos/AP-1 axis in regulating inflammatory responses in AT2 cells and highlight HDAC3 as a potential molecular target for mitigating alveolar epithelial injury in early-stage RILI.
authors: Li B, Li N, Xiong R, Zuo Y, Liu Y, Luo G, Zhang W, Xiao Z, Wu L, Peng M.

title: Identification of the Glycosaminoglycan Metabolism-Related Protein IDUA Associated With Tumor Progression and Prognosis in ccRCC.
abstract: ObjectiveThis study investigated the expression, prognostic significance, and functional role of α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).MethodsWe performed two-sample Mendelian randomization using eQTL and ccRCC GWAS data. We analyzed transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. We constructed a prognostic nomogram integrating IDUA expression with clinicopathological variables. We used ESTIMATE and CIBERSORT algorithms to evaluate immune infiltration and examined correlations between IDUA and immune checkpoint genes. We knocked down IDUA in 786-O and ACHN cells using shRNA and assessed proliferation, invasion, and migration via MTT, Transwell, and wound-healing assays.ResultsIDUA was significantly overexpressed in ccRCC tumors versus normal tissues. High IDUA expression correlated with advanced stage, higher T stage, and poor overall survival. Multivariate Cox regression confirmed IDUA as an independent prognostic factor (HR = 1.614, p ConclusionIDUA serves as an independent prognostic biomarker in ccRCC, promotes tumor aggressiveness, and may modulate the immune microenvironment. These findings support IDUA as a potential therapeutic target and a candidate predictor for immunotherapy response in ccRCC.
authors: Cao Z, Yan S, Chu W, Yuan H, Shen Z, Bi L, Peng L.

title: The Rice CBP60 Protein OsCBP609 Interacts With Pik1-H4 and Supports Salicylic Acid-Responsive Immunity Against Magnaporthe oryzae.
abstract: Plant immunity depends on coordination between immune receptors and hormone-responsive transcriptional networks, yet how CBP60 proteins contribute to disease resistance in monocots remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized OsCBP609, a rice CBP60 family protein involved in resistance to Magnaporthe oryzae. Expression of OsCBP609 was responsive to M. oryzae infection and defence-related signals, and the encoded protein localized to the nucleus and exhibited transcriptional activation. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption of OsCBP609 increased lesion development and fungal biomass following infection with multiple M. oryzae isolates. Transcriptome profiling showed that loss of OsCBP609 was associated with altered expression of genes involved in plant-pathogen interactions and hormone-related signalling pathways during infection. Although basal salicylic acid (SA) levels were elevated in the oscbp609 mutant, SA-responsive defence transcription was attenuated, and exogenous SA failed to restore resistance to the wild-type level, supporting a role for OsCBP609 in the transcriptional response to SA. OsCBP609 physically interacted with the NLR protein Pik1-H4 in the nucleus, and co-expression of the two proteins produced significantly higher reporter activity than expression of either protein alone. Disruption of OsCBP609 in a Pik-H4 near-isogenic line also reduced blast resistance, supporting a functional contribution of OsCBP609 to Pik-H4-associated immunity. Together, these results identify OsCBP609 as a CBP60 transcriptional regulator that supports SA-responsive defence and Pik-H4-associated resistance to rice blast.
authors: Xie H, Wei D, Li J, Lin C, Zou X, Li R, Hou Y, Jiang X, Chen C, Guo T, Wang J.

title: Rewiring of oncogenic pathways confers carfilzomib resistance in multiple myeloma and is reversed by Rap1 inhibition.
abstract: Resistance to carfilzomib, a second-generation proteasome inhibitor, represents a major barrier to effective treatment in multiple myeloma (MM). To uncover actionable vulnerabilities in drug-resistant cells, we establish two carfilzomib-resistant MM models and perform an in-depth molecular characterization of resistance-associated transcriptomic reprogramming. Comparative pathway analyses reveal consistent activation of survival-promoting signaling networks, including the Rap1, MAPK, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Guided by these findings, we systematically evaluate targeted inhibitors and identify GGTI-298, an agent that disrupts Rap1 signaling, as the most effective compound. In vivo , GGTI-298 significantly curtails tumor growth in xenograft models derived from both parental and resistant MM cells without causing detectable systemic toxicity, underscoring its therapeutic potential and safety. Mechanistically, treatment with GGTI-298 leads to downregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2 along with a concomitant reduction in the proliferation marker Ki-67. Moreover, GGTI-298 reprograms oncogenic signaling and transcriptional circuits, markedly suppressing MYC- and E2F-dependent gene expression while activating pro-apoptotic pathways such as the p53 axis. These effects are particularly evident in resistant cells, suggesting a selective vulnerability conferred by resistance-driven pathway rewiring. Collectively, our findings highlight the Rap1 signaling axis as a critical mediator of carfilzomib resistance and position GGTI-298 as a promising candidate for overcoming therapeutic failure in MM, providing a strong rationale for further clinical development of Rap1-targeted strategies in relapsed or refractory disease settings.
authors: Qin L, Hu R, Shi Y, Li Q, Gao G, Zhang X, Cheng C, Li B, Zhuang W.

title: Quorum-Sensing-Mediated Extracellular Electron Transfer Enables Hydrogel Morphogenesis.
abstract: Engineered living materials seek to capture the sensitivity, responsiveness, and programmable characteristics of biological systems. One emergent property of living systems is genetically driven spatial patterning, which controls cell differentiation and the development of complex multicellular organisms. Inspired by this capability, we use bacteria to spatially control material assembly. In our system, extracellular electron transfer (EET) flux from Shewanella oneidensis drives hydrogel synthesis via copper-catalyzed radical polymerization. We first construct a recombinant quorum-sensing system in S. oneidensis that allows for cell-cell communication between "sender" and "receiver" cells through an autoinducer. We then examine controlled gene expression and EET-driven chemical transformation in various synthetic consortia. Via diffusion through agarose, we examine 2D patterns of gene expression relative to localized sender cell populations and demonstrate controlled hydrogel crosslinking in predictable patterns. Finally, we apply computational methods and NOT logic in "receiver" cells toward more complex patterns of gene expression. Our results highlight the potential of bacteria to program material systems with life-like properties, including self-assembly, environmental responsiveness, and patterned differentiation.
authors: Miniel Mahfoud IE, Damani VS, Partipilo G, Liu AY, Keitz BK.

title: Age and sex-related changes in the human rapid eye movement sleep microstructure.
abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep alternates between two states-phasic and tonic-defined by the presence or absence of transient neurophysiological events such as REMs. These states exhibit distinct neural activity and putative underlying function, yet their evolution along with aging remains unknown. Retrospective polysomnographic data from 627 healthy participants (290 females and 337 males), aged 18-80 years and drawn from five databases, were analyzed to characterize age- and sex-related changes in the REM sleep microstructure. REM sleep macrostructure declined with age, paralleled by a reduction in phasic REM duration. In addition, the proportion of phasic REM sleep as well as the number and density of eye movements decreased with advancing age. We found sex-related differences in these trajectories, with a steeper decline in phasic REM percentage and REM density in women. Spectral analyses mainly confirmed previously reported differences in power between phasic and tonic states and further revealed differential age-related changes, i.e. while spectral power in tonic REM increased in higher frequency bands, phasic REM exhibited a progressive slowing of electroencephalographic (EEG) activity across the lifespan. This large-scale, multicohort analysis provides a comprehensive characterization of REM sleep microstructure across aging and between sexes in healthy participants, constituting an important step toward its potential as a biomarker candidate in psychopathological and neurodegenerative disorders. Statement of Significance Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep alternates between phasic and tonic states, which differ in neural activity and are thought to support distinct functions. However, how these states evolve across the human lifespan remains largely unknown. Using a large multicohort dataset of 627 healthy individuals, we show that aging is associated with a reduction in phasic REM sleep, reflected by decreases in phasic REM percentage and REM density. These declines were steeper in women than in men. Spectral analyses further revealed a slowing of electroencephalographic activity occurring specifically in phasic REM sleep. Together, these findings provide a large-scale characterization of age- and sex-related trajectories of REM sleep microstructure, highlighting changes distinct from global sleep architecture.
authors: Bertin C, Jeanne R, Bourgin J, Leoncini-Janin É, Wunderlin M, Züst MA, Hot P, Eichenlaub JB.

title: Scaffold compound T4015 attenuates pulmonary fibrosis via suppressing JAK/STAT and NF-κB signaling.
abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a life-threatening interstitial lung disease characterized by scarring and inflammation in lung tissues. Aberrant activation of the JAK/STAT and NF-κB signaling pathways is critical in initiating and sustaining the inflammatory processes that drive fibrotic progression. In this study, we identify a novel small-molecule compound, T4015, a 4-indolyl-2-phenylaminopyrimidine derivative, as a dual-pathway inhibitor targeting both JAK/STAT and NF-κB signaling. Dual-luciferase reporter assays demonstrate the potent inhibitory activity of T4015 against these pathways. T4015 effectively suppresses the phosphorylation of STAT3, JAK1, and TYK2 induced by IL-6 and IFN-γ, while suppressing LPS-induced NF-κB activation in macrophages. Transcriptome sequencing and pathway enrichment analyses further confirm that T4015 downregulates multiple inflammation-related signaling cascades, including the JAK/STAT, NF-κB, TNF, IL-17, and Toll-like receptor pathways. In a mouse model of bleomycin-induced PF, T4015 treatment significantly improves survival, attenuates collagen deposition, and reduces the expression of pro-inflammatory and profibrotic markers such as IL-6, CCL2, and COL1. Molecular docking and target prediction analyses suggest that T4015 exhibits strong binding affinity for multiple kinases within the JAK/STAT and NF-κB networks, including JAK1, TYK2, JAK2, JAK3, RIPK1, IRAK1/4, TAB1, and ZAP70. Collectively, these results highlight T4015 as a promising therapeutic candidate for PF through its simultaneous inhibition of the JAK/STAT and NF-κB signaling pathways.
authors: Zhang M, Xu H, Liu S, Xu X, Yin J, Zhang X, Zhang X, Yang X, Liu X, Yin B, Zhou M, Wang L, Zhang M, Liu H, Jiang W, Song Q, Yang J.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies JUN as a candidate regulator associated with follicular development in Hainan Wenchang hens.
abstract: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing of the advantage follicles (AVF) revealed significant transcriptional differences between high-yield and low-yield laying Hainan Wenchang hens (HYLH, LYLH). Follicular developmental normal (FDN)​ hens exhibited higher egg production rates, whereas follicle developmental arrest (FDA)​ individuals showed markedly lower laying performance. Preovulatory follicular arrest is primarily associated with the AVF selection. Consequently, single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to investigate the differences in AVF between FDN and FDA groups. We identified 13 distinct cell clusters, with particular focus on the granulosa cells (GCs) given their critical role in follicle development. Comparative analysis identified 167 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in GCs between FDN and FDA hens. JUN was selected for subsequent functional investigation based on exploratory analyses of the single-cell transcriptomic data. This suggests that JUN may be associated with follicular development and egg-laying performance. A JUN overexpression plasmid was constructed and transfected into primary GCs isolated from follicles. The CCK-8 assay was used to assess cell viability, and it was found that JUN overexpression enhanced GC viability. Compared with the control group, the JUN overexpression group showed significantly higher concentrations of GnRH, FSH, and LH and a significantly lower concentration of testosterone (TESTO) in GC culture supernatants, as measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, transcriptome sequencing was performed on JUN overexpressing GCs. Differential expression analysis identified numerous genes involved in cell proliferation, immune regulation, and metabolic processes. Collectively, this study suggests that JUN, identified through single-cell transcriptomic profiling, may enhance GCs viability and was associated with altered hormone concentrations in GC culture supernatants. These findings provide novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying differences in egg-laying performance between HYLH and LYLH and may offer potential targets for improving reproductive efficiency in poultry.
authors: Zhang Y, Tang H, Cai G, Zhao H, Li H, Lin M, Tai Y.

title: Multistage screening and fraction-knockout validation of pancreatic lipase inhibitors from Ganoderma lucidum using counter-current chromatography.
abstract: This study combined pancreatic lipase inhibition-guided screening with high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC) to screen and isolate pancreatic lipase-inhibitory constituents from Ganoderma lucidum. Eleven candidate lipid-lowering constituents were tentatively identified in G. lucidum, and one lanostane-type triterpenoid, ganoderol A, was isolated. A preparative separation strategy integrating extract-layer recombination with two-stage HSCCC purification was established for the efficient separation of ganoderol A from G. lucidum. Mixtures of extracts prepared at different ratios from petroleum ether (P), ethyl acetate (E), n-butanol (B), and water (W) were screened to evaluate pancreatic lipase inhibitory activity. The E/P extract mixture at 1:4 (w/w), which exhibited the highest inhibition, was ultimately selected for preparative separation. Using a colorimetric method, two biphasic solvent systems, n-hexane/ethyl acetate/acetonitrile/water (7:4:3:6, v/v/v/v) and n-hexane/acetonitrile/water (7:3:0.5, v/v/v), were selected. The first-stage HSCCC separation yielded 146.91 mg of fraction 7 from 320.73 mg of the E/P extract mixture (1:4 w/w). Subsequently, a second-stage separation yielded 4.21, 9.61, and 6.82 mg of fractions 2, 5, and 6, respectively, with corresponding IC50 values of 21.67, 58.38, and 31.04 μg/mL. The compound isolated from fraction 6 was identified by 1H and 13C NMR as the lanostane-type triterpenoid ganoderol A, with a purity of 94.05%. Ganoderol A was isolated from G. lucidum using high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC) for the first time and showed pancreatic lipase inhibition, with an IC50 of 31.04 μg/mL. LC-QTOF-MS/MS profiling of fractions 2 and 5 yielded 11 tentative constituent annotations. Their identities and individual pancreatic lipase inhibitory activities remain to be confirmed.
authors: Bai J, Zhu X, Wang J, Kong Y, Du Y, Liu W, Tong S.

title: C/EBPδ in autoimmunity: Linking inflammation and tissue protection.
abstract: C/EBPδ, encoded by CEBPD, regulates inflammatory and stress responses across immune and tissue compartments. This narrative review examines its relevance to autoimmune diseases, distinguishing disease-model perturbation from cellular mechanisms, human associations and contextual studies. Whole-animal Cebpd deletion supports involvement in experimental arthritis, while renal studies reveal contrasting effects across inflammatory and fibrotic models. Evidence in other autoimmune settings varies in experimental scope. Protective findings in intestinal epithelium, pancreatic β cells and psoriasis-related systems challenge a uniform inhibitory strategy. We propose a framework linking C/EBPδ activation, transcriptional programme selection and functional consequences: expression alone does not determine whether its activity is pathogenic or protective. Therapeutic development requires demonstrated target dependency, selective engagement and delivery, and assessment of protective and host-defence functions. The review identifies priorities for testing C/EBPδ as a context-dependent candidate target rather than an established treatment across autoimmune diseases.
authors: Hu Y, Chen J, Liu Y, Li C, Wu B, Ding L.

title: Structural modeling supports an interaction between the Drosophila Estrogen-Related Receptor and Sima/HIF1α.
abstract: The Drosophila Estrogen-Related Receptor (dERR) is an orphan nuclear receptor that regulates developmental metabolism, yet the protein cofactors that modulate its activity remain poorly defined. Here, we used the AI-based FlyPredictome platform to identify candidate dERR interaction partners and evaluate their predicted structural interfaces. Among the highest-confidence interactors is the transcription factor Sima, which represents the Drosophila ortholog of HIF1α - an interaction that was reciprocally identified in Sima/HIF1α interaction datasets. Structural modeling predicted binding between the dERR ligand-binding domain and a conserved LXXLL motif in Sima/HIF1α. Notably, the predicted dERR-Sima/HIF1α interaction interface includes residues previously shown to be essential for in vitro binding, providing independent support for this protein-protein interaction.
authors: Feng Y, Tennessen JM.

title: Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses reveal key genes and pathways associated with egg-laying rate in the late laying phase of Chinese yellow-feathered quails.
abstract: Egg production is a core indicator for laying‑poultry productivity, and reduced egg yield in the late laying phase severely harms farming economic returns. Although some quails retain high egg production within flocks experiencing late‑phase production decline, the molecular mechanisms behind divergent laying performance remain unclear. This study conducted integrated ovarian transcriptome and serum metabolome analyses on late‑laying Chinese yellow‑feathered quails with contrasting laying performance. Transcriptomics identified 751 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 205 up‑, 546 down‑regulated), enriched in steroid hormone biosynthesis, PPAR signaling, retinol metabolism and neuroactive ligand‑receptor interaction.PPI network analysis further picked out 8 candidate core genes that were upregulated in the low-yield group, including F2, FGA, AHSG, SERPINC1, APOH, FGG, FGB, and AMBP. Metabolomics detected 141 differentially expressed metabolites (DEMs; 87 up‑, 54 down‑regulated), mainly enriched in bile acid biosynthesis, steroid biosynthesis and ABC‑transporter pathways. Multi‑omics integration revealed strong correlations between these key genes and DEMs; taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA) was negatively correlated with the above genes. The integrated analysis suggests that changes in bile acid and lipid metabolism may be associated with ovarian coagulation-related processes and injury responses, jointly contributing to differences in laying performance among quails during the late laying period. The candidate genes and metabolites identified in this study provide leads for further investigation of ovarian functional changes during this period and may inform future research on the selection of high-producing individuals and nutritional interventions.
authors: Wang C, Tian T, Sun H, Liu Y, Zeng F, Liu S, Lu Y, Shi B.

title: An LLM-based Technique for Detection of Code Clones Across Open Source Microservice Repository Forks
abstract: Abstract  Aim: Understanding code reuse and divergence in open-source microservice projects is crucial to assessing software evolution and community-driven software development. As repositories are forked and modified, it becomes difficult to trace how much of the original code persists and whether or not these forks create a unique project or retain the same functionality as the original. In this study, we leveraged Large Language Models to identify code clones and analyzed code clone distribution in open-source microservice projects. Method: We used a RAG framework based on LLMs to semantically compare code at the service level. This allowed us to detect not only direct clones, but also functionally equivalent segments that have been refactored. In order to identify a feasible LLM pipeline for analyzing clone types and distribution, we tested three candidate LLMs and four prompt techniques on the IBM CodeNet dataset of Type-4 clones. We then used the best-performing pipeline to identify the code clones in pairs of primary and forked open-source microservices projects. Results: We found the code-specific Codestral-22B LLM with a few-shot continuous prompting technique to be the most accurate in detecting Type-4 code clones, with a precision of 0.74 but a recall of only 0.60. Our analysis of 22 microservice repositories with this technique showed that Type-1 clones are most prevalent, followed by Type-3 clones. Semantic comparison revealed patterns of reuse and divergence not captured by syntax-based tools. Conclusion: Semantic code analysis using LLMs provides deeper understanding of code evolution in forks of microservice projects. Code-specific LLMs significantly outperformed multimodal models but remain unsuitable for production use due to high false negative rates.
authors: Kemman J, Nakum S, Bakhtin A, Esposito M, Cerny T, Lenarduzzi V, Taibi D.

title: Identification, Expression Analysis, and Functional Characterization of the Main Nitrate Transporter Genes of the NPF, NRT2, and NAR2 Families in the Salt-Tolerant Barley Hordeum marinum Huds
abstract: Soil salinization is a widespread abiotic stress factor that significantly limits the growth, development, and productivity of plants. One of the effects of salt stress on plants is a disruption in mineral nutrient uptake, particularly due to the competition between nitrate and chloride anions for the root ion transport systems. In this study, we identified key genes in the salt-tolerant barley Hordeum marinum that regulate nitrate uptake from the soil solution and encode membrane proteins of the NPF, NRT2, and NAR2 families. When the expression profiles of nitrate transporter genes in H. marinum and H. vulgare were compared, differences were found in the response of NPF family genes to the addition of NaCl to the medium: in H. marinum, transcription of the HmNPF6.3B1 gene was significantly induced, whereas the expression level of orthologous genes in H. vulgare was almost independent of the NaCl concentration in the medium. Changes in the expression of nitrate transporter genes are consistent with data on the accumulation of nitrate and chloride anions in the organs of H. marinum and H. vulgare and indicate a greater ability of H. marinum, compared to H. vulgare, to maintain nitrate influx and limit chloride entry under salt stress conditions. Using the bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) method, the interaction of NRT2 family proteins of H. marinum with the HmNAR2.3 protein was detected, and using a heterologous expression system based on the yeast Ogataea parapolymorpha, the nitrate transport activity of the HmNPF6.3B1 protein was demonstrated.
authors: Nedelyaeva OI, Khramov DE, Volkov VS.

title: ZIF-8/Graphene Oxide Nanocomposite Modified Electrode for Electrochemical Detection of Trimethylamine as a Freshness Indicator in Crayfish
abstract: Trimethylamine (TMA) is a characteristic spoilage marker generated during the late stage of microbial metabolism in crayfish, and its rapid detection is of great significance for ensuring the safety of aquatic products. In this study, a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) and graphene oxide (GO) nanocomposite (ZIF-8@GO) was synthesized via a room-temperature stirring method and subsequently modified onto a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) surface to construct an electrochemical sensor for TMA detection. The composite material and the modified electrode were systematically characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Under optimized conditions, differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) was employed to evaluate the sensor response toward TMA. The oxidation peak current exhibited a good linear relationship with TMA concentration in the range of 5–105 μM, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.79 μM (S/N = 3) and a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 5.97 μM (S/N = 10). The sensor displayed excellent reproducibility with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 0.89% (n = 5), and outstanding long-term stability with an RSD of 1.03% after 10 days of storage. Furthermore, the sensor exhibited superior anti-interference capability against common coexisting ions and organic substances. When applied to the detection of TMA in real crayfish samples, the recoveries ranged from 96.56% to 101.32% with RSDs below 3%, and the results were in good agreement with those obtained by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). The proposed sensor is facile to prepare, rapid in response, and cost-effective, offering a new technical approach for the on-site rapid screening of crayfish freshness.
authors: Duan S, Liao C, Zhao J, Zhang Y, Liu Y, Wang Q, Dai H.
