title: Circuit organization of Tac2-expressing neurons from established functions to testable hypotheses.
abstract: Tac2-expressing neurons participate in behavioral and neuroendocrine functions through regionally specialized circuits. Building on a 2021 review of the Tac2/neurokinin B (NKB) pathway, we examine how cell- and projection-specific studies have refined this organization. Fear-memory and isolation-stress studies provide convergent evidence for NKB-neurokinin 3 receptor (NK3R) signaling, whereas other studies establish functions of Tac2-expressing populations without demonstrating peptide dependence. We distinguish interventions targeting neurons, the Tac2-encoded peptide, NK3R, and NK3R-expressing cells, and assess classical-transmitter evidence separately. We then integrate descriptive Allen Brain Cell Atlas MERFISH visualizations with regional circuit knowledge to formulate hypotheses for the medial habenula, dorsal tegmental nucleus, and spinal trigeminal nucleus interpolaris. Established reinforcement in a Tac2-driver-defined habenular subset motivates tests of output specialization; tegmental and trigeminal expression patterns motivate hypotheses about orientation-arousal coupling and sensory gating. Atlas annotations identify candidate molecular phenotypes, not validated transmitter release or behavioral functions. Together, the literature supports a region- and state-dependent account of Tac2-expressing populations and defines where additional molecular evidence is needed to establish NKB-NK3R mechanisms.
authors: Zhang Z, Hu S, Cao H, Mu M.

title: Regulatable in vivo gene expression via adaptamers.
abstract: Precise, reversible control of transgene expression is essential for safe and durable gene therapy, yet current inducible systems remain difficult to translate in vivo due to large size, limited induction duration, and dependence on immunogenic regulators. Here, we present the adaptamer (adenosine deaminases acting on RNA [ADAR]-modulatable aptamer), a compact (<120 base pair) RNA switch that couples FDA-approved small-molecule-responsive aptamers with endogenous ADAR-mediated RNA editing to regulate expression. Ligand binding stabilizes a double-stranded RNA structure that recruits ADAR to convert a stop codon into a sense codon, restoring downstream protein translation. This cleavage-free, post-transcriptional mechanism enables precise, small-molecule-dependent modulation without exogenous protein machinery. We demonstrate that adaptamers are highly functional across multiple cell lines, including human T cells. In mice, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered adaptamer-controlled FGF21 expression induced metabolic remodeling, reversing obesity and hepatic steatosis. This minimal, programmable system offers a clinically compatible approach for tunable genetic medicines and safe deployment of pleiotropic and dose-limited proteins.
authors: Bryant J, Herron L, Doctor Y, McRae F, Wang J, Hirsch T, Portell A, Kumar S, Mali P.

title: Absence of Validated and Candidate Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 Markers of Artemisinin Resistance and Low Frequency of a Pfcoronin Mutation in Igombe, Mwanza Region, Tanzania.
abstract: Tanzania recently identified partial artemisinin resistance in the Kagera region bordering Rwanda and Uganda, where resistance is established. Monitoring neighboring regions is critical to guide containment strategies. We, therefore, conducted molecular surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 (pfk13) and Plasmodium falciparum actin-binding protein coronin (pfcoronin; P76S) mutations in Igombe in Mwanza region. In a health facility-based cross-sectional study in 2025, P. falciparum DNA from patients with uncomplicated malaria was analyzed using polymerase chain reaction, Sanger sequencing, and allele-specific melting curve assays. Among 121 sequenced isolates, no validated or candidate pfk13 mutations were detected. The nonsynonymous, nonvalidated pfk13 variant N489K occurred in 2.5%. The pfcoronin P76S mutation was observed at low prevalence (3.6%). Despite proximity to Kagera hot spots, validated pfk13 markers have not yet been established in the Mwanza region. The presence of pfcoronin P76S, albeit at low levels, requires careful monitoring. Continued molecular surveillance is essential to support the early detection and containment of emerging artemisinin resistance in Tanzania.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
authors: Marwa KJ, Oliveira R, Mwaiswelo RO, van Loon W, Mockenhaupt FP.

title: Germline pharmacogenetic variants associated with trastuzumab deruxtecan-induced interstitial lung disease in advanced breast cancer: PROCURE project.
abstract: BackgroundTrastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has demonstrated substantial clinical benefit in patients with advanced human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive and HER2-low breast cancer. However, treatment-related adverse events-particularly interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis-represent a clinically relevant limitation. While UGT1A1 polymorphisms influence toxicity with other topoisomerase I inhibitor-based therapies, their role in T-DXd-related toxicity appears limited. The PROCURE project aimed to investigate germline pharmacogenetic variants beyond UGT1A1 associated with T-DXd-induced ILD.Materials and methodsThe PROCURE project is a multicenter translational study conducted across 26 Spanish institutions. Germline DNA from patients with advanced HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer treated with T-DXd was genotyped using the Infinium Global Diversity Array enriched for pharmacogenomic variants. A candidate gene approach was applied to 14 genes involved in drug metabolism, transport, pharmacodynamics, and immune-mediated drug hypersensitivity. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with ILD/pneumonitis.ResultsA total of 290 patients with clinical and genotyping data were included in the analysis. The median age was 58 years (range, 34-94 years). After a median follow-up of 18.3 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 15.4-20.5], the cohort registered 33 ILD cases (incidence of 11.4%). The strongest association signals mapped to variants within the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) region, with the top single nucleotide polymorphism near HLA-F (rs9258213; OR 6.8, 95% CI 2.6-17.9, P = 9.5 × 10-5). Additional associations were observed in SLCO1B1 and CYP3A4, genes involved in T-DXd transport and metabolism.ConclusionsThis study identifies host genetic variation within the HLA locus and drug pharmacokinetic pathways as potential contributors to T-DXd-induced ILD in patients with advanced breast cancer. Although no definitive pharmacogenomic predictor was identified, these findings provide insights into the biological mechanisms underlying this toxicity and support further investigation of pharmacogenomic biomarkers to improve risk stratification and guide personalized T-DXd therapy.
authors: Arenas A, Saura C, Alva-Bianchi M, de Nicolás-Hernández J, Gion M, Cejalvo JM, Llabrés E, Cortés J, Falcón A, Pernas S, López de Sa A, Vidal M, Hinojo C, Curiel T, Cruz J, Martínez V, Cantos B, Echarri MJ, Gallegos I, Bueno C, Vargas AM, Escrivá-de-Romaní S, Fullana B, Cobos MA, Joval-Ramentol L, Ortiz-Heras P, Pascual T, Valdivia C, Villacampa G, Ciruelos E, Rodriguez-Antona C, Sánchez-Bayona R.

title: Dynamic Expression Quantitative Trait Locus Mendelian Randomization in Activated CD4-Positive T Cells Nominates SMDT1 and CMTM7 as Candidate Genes in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is largely refractory to immune checkpoint blockade. Conventional Mendelian randomization (MR) using steady-state expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) may miss regulatory effects that emerge during CD4 + T-cell activation. We used a two-stage genetic framework. Fixed-effect meta-analysis across four PDAC GWAS served as an exploratory cross-cohort discovery screen, followed by GCST90041814 as the ancestry-matched European primary analysis. Associations were assessed by colocalization, summary-data-based MR with HEIDI testing, and DICE/eQTLGen replication. Paired sample-level pseudobulk analysis evaluated tumor-adjacent CD4 + T cells. Bulk transcriptomic, mediation, virtual perturbation, survival and phenome-wide analyses were treated as exploratory. The pooled discovery screen identified 67 genes at FDR < 0.05; 65 also showed concordant effect directions across all four cohorts and constituted the main discovery set. In the European primary analysis, 66 of 1247 genes had nominal p < 0.05, but none survived cohort-wide FDR correction. SMDT1 (European OR = 0.603, 95% CI 0.412-0.884, p = 0.009, FDR = 0.754) and CMTM7 (European OR = 1.208, 95% CI 1.026-1.424, p = 0.023, FDR = 0.754) retained directionally consistent nominal associations and were prioritized as exploratory candidates. In six paired GSE212966 samples, pseudobulk changes were directionally consistent but not significant (SMDT1 log2FC = -0.381, p = 0.250; CMTM7 log2FC = 0.493, p = 0.199). Dynamic CD4 + T-cell eQTL MR nominates SMDT1 and CMTM7 as candidate genes associated with PDAC susceptibility. The pooled discovery evidence and directionally consistent nominal European associations support prioritization, but no gene survived FDR correction in the European analysis. Transcriptomic and downstream functional findings remain exploratory and require experimental validation.
authors: Wang H, Wang B, Duan X, Jiao G, Chen M, Guan X, Cao J, Cui L, Li H, Li Z.

title: Cinchonidine Ameliorates Traumatic Brain Injury-Related Neurobehavioral Deficits via the SRC/RAF1/NF-κB Pathway to Attenuate Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
abstract: Cinchonidine (CD), a metabolite derived from gut microbiota, shows promise in protecting against traumatic brain injury (TBI), where mitochondrial dysfunction is a key driver of secondary damage. Using a mouse model of controlled cortical impact (CCI) and an in vitro primary neuron injury model, CD administration resulted in improved physiological status (weight recovery, stabilized heart rate) and behavioral outcomes (increased travel distance and speed) in TBI mice. Histological analysis showed reduced hippocampal neuronal damage, decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin‑1β, interleukin‑6, and tumor necrosis factor‑α), and upregulated blood-brain barrier tight-junction proteins (Claudin-5, Occludin, zonula occludens‑1). Mitochondrial function was improved, evidenced by increased mitochondrial DNA copy number, elevated expression of translocase of outer mitochondrial membrane 20 and cytochrome c oxidase subunit IV, and restoration of mitochondrial membrane potential. In addition, CD attenuated TBI-induced changes in mitochondrial dynamics and biogenesis, restoring the phosphorylated dynamin-related protein 1 (p-DRP1)/DRP1 ratio and the expression of mitofusin 1/2 (MFN-1/2) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), while reducing mitochondrial DRP1. Network pharmacology identified proto‑oncogene tyrosine‑protein kinase Src (SRC) as a key target, validated by stable binding in molecular docking and drug affinity responsive target stability assays. Furthermore, cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated a direct interaction between CD and SRC. CD treatment suppressed the activation of the SRC/RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase (RAF1)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling axis, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of SRC and p65, along with decreased expression of RAF1 and cleaved Caspase-3. Crucially, SRC knockdown mimicked CD's protection, while SRC overexpression abolished its benefits. These findings suggest that CD ameliorates post-TBI mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage by inhibiting SRC kinase activity and its downstream RAF1/NF-κB signaling pathway. Thus, CD may represent a promising SRC-targeted neuroprotective strategy for TBI.
authors: Tang H, Huang J, Sun C.

title: MicroRNAs and polymorphisms influencing MICA immune modulation.
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs that play a central role in post-transcriptional gene regulation. They act mainly by interacting with sequences located in the 3' untranslated regions (3'UTRs) of messenger RNAs (mRNAs), thereby influencing mRNA stability and translation. Through these mechanisms, miRNAs contribute to the fine-tuning of multiple biological pathways, including immune activation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular stress responses. Among the genes involved in immune surveillance, the major histocompatibility complex class I polypeptide-related sequence A (MICA) has emerged as an important target for post-transcriptional regulation due to its role as a ligand for the activating receptor NKG2D (natural killer cell group 2-D), which is expressed in natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes. MICA is highly polymorphic, and several allelic variants differ in sequence composition, structural organization, and expression patterns, potentially influencing miRNA-mRNA interactions. Growing evidence suggests that miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA contributes to immune modulation in cancer, viral infections, and autoimmune disorders, particularly through mechanisms associated with immune evasion and altered NKG2D signaling. In addition, genetic polymorphisms and structural variations within regulatory regions, especially within the 3'UTR, can alter miRNA binding affinity by creating, disrupting, or modifying target sites. This mini review discusses the current understanding of miRNA-mediated regulation of MICA, emphasizing the impact of allelic diversity and regulatory polymorphisms on post-transcriptional control. Furthermore, it highlights current knowledge gaps and future perspectives regarding allele-specific regulation.
authors: Nicoletti MB, Ferraz IM, Moço AC, da Cruz Castelli E, Castro CFB.

title: A gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation.
abstract: BackgroundThe pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking.MethodsWe integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the gutMGene database. A gut microbiota-metabolite-host score (GMS) was constructed via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal small molecule.ResultsWe identified seven microbiota-metabolite-host hub genes (FOS, JUN, IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune activation subtype and an inflammatory-metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota-metabolite signalling drives RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their respective target proteins.ConclusionThis study establishes a GMS based on the gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut-joint axis.
authors: Sun XF, Yang YJ, Li CL, Huang T, Wang Q, Yu Q.

title: Transcriptomics analysis and experimental assay to screen prognostic genes of N6-methyladenosine RNA methylation related to cuproptosis in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Cuproptosis and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation have been identified as significant factors in cancer. Consequently, we seek to uncover m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that are correlated with cuproptosis-related genes (CRGs) in colorectal cancer (CRC) and develop an effective prognostic model. Based on public datasets, differential expression analysis, correlation analysis, and machine learning were conducted to identify prognostic genes. Subsequently, a prognostic model was constructed and validated. Furthermore, independent predictive markers were found through the use of clinical characteristics and risk score, to establish a prognostic nomogram. Prognostic gene expression in CRC and normal samples was evaluated using reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). According to the prognostic genes, potential drugs for CRC were predicted using artificial intelligence drug design (AIDD) and computer-aided drug design (CADD). A prognostic model was developed utilizing 7 m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that were significantly correlated with CRGs (MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, CDC25C, XRN2, COX5A, and FBXL5) in CRC. Survival analysis uncovered a notable contrast in survival outcomes between the high- and low-risk groups. The nomogram constructed based on age, stage, T stage, and risk scores demonstrated good predictive ability. RT-qPCR results showed that MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, and CDC25C were upregulated in CRC samples, while COX5A was downregulated, consistent with the bioinformatics analysis results. Furthermore, 186 candidate drugs targeting COX5A were identified, 153 of which showed better predicted binding affinity than the positive-control ligand 3,5‑diiodo‑L‑thyronine. Our analysis sets the groundwork for a more comprehensive comprehension of the fundamental molecular pathways involved in CRC.
authors: Sun D, Liu Z, Chen M, He Y, Zeng X, Li D, Wang W.

title: Epidemiological Evolution of HIV in Pakistan (1987-2026): From High-risk Populations to Emerging Pediatric Cases.
abstract: Purpose of reviewThis narrative review examines the evolving epidemiology of HIV in Pakistan from 1987 to 2026, focusing on temporal trends among key populations, geographic hotspots, emerging pediatric infections, and health-system gaps affecting epidemic control.Recent findingsEvidence indicates a persistent concentrated epidemic, with the highest burden among people who inject drugs and continuing transmission among sex workers, transgender populations, and prisoners. HIV transmission remains geographically heterogeneous, with major urban hotspots in Karachi and cities across Punjab. Recent pediatric outbreaks have introduced an important healthcare-associated dimension, with unsafe medical practices and weaknesses in infection prevention and control emerging as major concerns. Pakistan's HIV epidemic remains concentrated but is becoming increasingly complex. Persistent transmission among key populations, geographic expansion, pediatric infections, and substantial gaps in diagnosis, treatment, and viral suppression highlight the need for strengthened surveillance, prevention, infection control, and continuity of HIV care.
authors: John A, Faridi TA, Iqbal N.

title: PRKAR2A/RIIα as a candidate spatial cAMP-PKA signal router in triple-negative breast cancer metastasis: evidence boundaries, competing models and decisive experiments.
abstract: Metastatic relapse remains the principal lethal event in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet the contribution of PRKAR2A, which encodes the type IIα regulatory subunit (RIIα) of protein kinase A (PKA), remains unresolved. RIIα creates a mechanistic duality: it restrains catalytic PKA within the holoenzyme while recruiting type II PKA to A-kinase anchoring protein (AKAP) microdomains. A targeted critical narrative search identified no eligible published study in the searched sources that causally linked PRKAR2A to a TNBC metastasis endpoint. Direct evidence is limited to four association or detection contexts: PRKAR2A mRNA differed at the adjusted-significance boundary between pathological complete response and residual disease but was not retained in the final consensus predictor; its transcript was induced in a lipid-adapted TNBC heterospheroid state without gene-specific perturbation; RIIα was detected in mitochondria-endoplasmic-reticulum contact fractions whose local PKA activity controlled calcium transfer and apoptosis without isolating RIIα; and PRKAR2A entered a multigene prognostic signature without independent or cell-resolved validation. AKAP2 depletion altered focal-adhesion signalling, invasion, primary-tumour growth and lung signal, but neither the operative PKA regulatory subunit nor a burden-independent metastatic effect was established. These boundaries support four competing interpretations: PRKAR2A may be a driver, compensatory brake, localisation determinant or passenger state marker. Decisive tests require inducible depletion, near-endogenous domain-resolved rescue, compartment-targeted PKA reporters, endogenous complex mapping and stage-resolved metastasis assays. Until then, RIIα is best treated as a candidate spatial signal router rather than a validated biomarker or therapeutic target.
authors: Muzaffar T, Saha B.

title: Suppressing radiocesium uptake and root-to-shoot translocation in crops: Molecular, agronomic, and ecological strategies.
abstract: Radiocesium (r-Cs: 137Cs) from the Fukushima Daiichi accident and earlier nuclear fallout remains a long-term contaminant in agricultural soils. It poses an ongoing threat to global food safety because crops readily absorb it as a potassium analog. This review synthesizes a decade of mechanistic, agronomic, and ecological advances in suppressing r-Cs uptake and root-to-shoot translocation. First, the impact of soil mineralogy, particularly clay fixation, on initial r-Cs bioavailability is examined. At the molecular level, r-Cs influx is governed by a shared calcium-signaling hub linked to potassium status. Consequently, optimizing potassium fertilization can transcriptionally silence the principal uptake genes. Furthermore, controlling xylem loading and managing internal sodium interactions directly restrict r-Cs translocation, protecting edible plant parts. Supplementary countermeasures, including plant-microbe symbioses, porous soil amendments, and targeted genetic exclusions, are also evaluated. To ensure long-term agricultural resilience, multi-site field trials and the molecular dissection of translocation pathways must be prioritized in future research. Ultimately, sustainable crop production requires integrating biological and agronomic strategies rather than relying solely on intensive potassium fertilization.
authors: Rahman I, Khan BM, Hossen I, Rahman Z.

title: The AMPK kinase Sak1 activates separase and promotes its nuclear localization during mitosis.
abstract: Accurate chromosome segregation during mitosis requires the precise regulation of separase, a protease that cleaves cohesin to trigger the separation of sister chromatids. Here, we identify the AMPK-activating kinase Sak1 as a novel regulator of separase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Using a suppressor screen, we discovered a hypermorphic SAK1-E50K allele that restored separase activity and nuclear localization in esp1-2 and pds1Δ mutants. We demonstrated that Sak1 phosphorylates separase independently of Snf1 activation, enhancing its enzymatic function and promoting nuclear accumulation. Loss of Sak1 delays Cdc14 activation and phenocopies FEAR pathway defects, establishing Sak1 as a mitotic regulator. Extending these findings to humans, we demonstrated that human separase and the tumor suppressor kinase LKB1, which is homologous to Sak1, physically associate. This finding reveals an evolutionarily conserved regulatory link between LKB1 and separase, highlighting the kinase-protease interplay as a critical mechanism for ensuring faithful mitotic progression.
authors: Vaquero-Pelaz D, Rodriguez-Rodriguez JA, Ilinca MC, Casas-Fernández E, Picard A, Del Caño-Ochoa F, Vernia I, Gabaldón T, Juanes MA, Queralt E.

title: Mechanisms by which cannabidiol promotes peripheral nerve regeneration.
abstract: AbstractCannabidiol, a cannabis-derived non-psychoactive compound, possesses neuroprotective potential; however, the specific mechanisms by which it promotes peripheral nerve repair remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the neurorepair effects of cannabidiol, focusing on the regulation of nerve injury and repair through the "gut-nerve axis." We used a sciatic nerve crush model, combined with multi-omics analyses and molecular validation, to investigate and verify the mechanisms underlying cannabidiol mediated peripheral nerve injury repair both in vivo and in vitro. Following peripheral nerve injury, the abundance of the probiotic Akkermansia muciniphila was significantly reduced. cannabidiol treatment restored Akkermansia muciniphila abundance and was accompanied by increased levels of 3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in both the serum and injured sciatic nerve. Oral administration of cannabidiol promoted PNI repair by improving the morphology of the injured nerve, increasing the static sciatic index in mice, and alleviating gastrocnemius muscle atrophy. Importantly, antibiotic-induced dysbiosis significantly attenuated the therapeutic efficacy of cannabidiol, whereas Akkermansia muciniphila supplementation restored these neuroregenerative effects. Mechanistically, transcriptomic sequencing indicated that 3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid effectively inhibited MAPK signaling activation in Schwann cells, thereby reducing the secretion of inflammatory factors and alleviating inflammation to create a favorable microenvironment for repair of peripheral nerve injury. Exogenous 3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid supplementation similarly promoted recovery of peripheral nerve injury. This study reveals, for the first time, a novel "cannabidiol-Akkermansia muciniphila-3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid-mitogen-activated protein kinase axis" that plays a pivotal role in peripheral nerve repair. These findings deepen our understanding of the neuroprotective mechanisms of cannabidiol and provide an important theoretical foundation for developing novel therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiome to promote repair of peripheral nerve injury.
authors: Li J, Xin Y, You W, Zhou J, Wu Z, Fang X, Zhang W.

title: mGem: Innate immune sensing of HIV-1 transcription in myeloid cells-a tale of two transcription start sites.
abstract: Suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART) in people with HIV (PWH) arrests progression to AIDS and onward viral transmission. However, viral transcription from integrated HIV-1 proviruses persists on treatment and is linked to markers of chronic immune activation, contributing to the accelerated development of comorbidities in PWH. Of particular interest are persistent responses in long-lived tissue-resident myeloid cells, which direct tissue-level inflammatory processes through cytokine secretion and interactions with other immune cell populations. Here, we review recent findings on viral nucleic acid sensing events in HIV-infected myeloid cells to shed light on possible mechanisms of persistent inflammation resulting from chronic HIV-1 transcription in myeloid cells in PWH.
authors: Hughes IK, Gummuluru S.

title: DENV-NS1 drives novel microRNAs to disrupt cerebral endothelial barrier functions.
abstract: Dengue virus non-structural protein 1 (DENV-NS1) plays a key role in the vascular leakage associated with severe dengue; however, the molecular mechanisms by which NS1 induces endothelial dysfunction remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify a new aspect of the pathogenic strategy: the post-transcriptional reprogramming of host endothelial cells via microRNAs (miRNAs) in NS1-induced DENV pathogenesis. Small RNA sequencing and subsequent bioinformatic analysis identified novel miRNA-gene regulatory networks responsive to DENV-NS1 in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. Multiple dysregulated novel miRNAs were identified as potential regulators of critical antiviral components (STAT1, SOCS1-6, OAS1), suggesting suppressed interferon signaling. Downregulation of identified novel miRNAs targeting IL-6, IL-10, IL-1α, IL-17A, CXCR4, and CXCR5 indicates increased pro-inflammatory cytokine production and chemokine-driven immune cell recruitment, thereby worsening endothelial inflammation and vascular leakage. The simultaneous targeting of cytoskeletal regulators (RAC1, ROCK1/2) and tight junction proteins (CLDN1, CLDN2, CLDN16, CLDN22) suggests a two-phase disruption of endothelial stability, characterized by cytoskeletal remodeling and compromised tight junction integrity as a bystander effect of DENV-NS1. The downregulation of several miRNAs targeting XIAP, MDM2/4, and SMAD family genes established the involvement of novel miRNAs in apoptosis regulation and TGF-β/SMAD-mediated endothelial cell signaling. Our findings suggest that DENV-NS1 alters endothelial miRNA networks, leading to reduced antiviral immunity, increased inflammation, and compromised vascular integrity. This study identifies novel miRNA-mediated regulatory nodes that could function as therapeutic targets to prevent or mitigate dengue-associated vascular leakage.
authors: Apoorva, Singh SK.

title: Structural identification of endogenous Escherichia coli proteins from heterogeneous cryo-electron microscopy datasets.
abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) can resolve multiple structurally distinct macromolecules (for example unintended host-derived proteins that remain during recombinant protein purification) within a heterogeneous specimen. Here, cryo-EM was initially performed to investigate an oligomeric form of recombinant human 2-oxoglutarate- and iron-dependent oxygenase domain-containing protein 1 (OGFOD1) purified from Escherichia coli. However, image classification and 3D reconstruction revealed OGFOD1-incompatible particle populations. Combined cryo-EM and mass spectrometry identified these particles as three endogenous E. coli proteins: the bifunctional enzyme ArnA, guanosine triphosphate cyclohydrolase I (GTP cyclohydrolase I) and glycerol dehydrogenase (GlyDH). Their structures were reconstructed at overall resolutions of 3.24, 3.00 and 3.02 Å, respectively, revealing expected hexameric, decameric and octameric protein assemblies. Structural comparisons with previously reported crystallographic and cryo-EM structures showed that the overall oligomeric architectures and active-site configurations were highly conserved; however, local conformational differences were observed in specific regions. Despite substantial differences in total molecular mass, the three protein assemblies had comparable predicted hydrodynamic radii, which plausibly explained their partial coelution during size-exclusion chromatography. These results show that rigid, symmetric endogenous complexes can dominate heterogeneous cryo-EM datasets and highlight the value of systematic analysis of off-target particle populations.
journal: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
authors: Kim S, Yeo H, Kim J, Jeong H, Shin DH, Youn HD, Lee BI.

title: Hepatitis-Associated Aplastic Anemia in Children and Adolescents: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Hepatitis-associated aplastic anemia (HAAA) is a rare but life-threatening subtype of acquired aplastic anemia (AA) that predominantly affects children and adolescents, characterized by bone marrow failure developing weeks to months following acute hepatitis. Although HAAA accounts for a small proportion of AA cases, it presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and remains poorly understood. Most cases are seronegative, with no identifiable viral pathogen, supporting an immune-mediated pathophysiology. Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated cytotoxic T-cell activation, reduced regulatory T-cell function, and a shared immune target within hepatic and hematopoietic tissues. HAAA follows a variable course of hepatitis and pancytopenia, which necessitates a high index of suspicion and thorough evaluation to exclude inherited and secondary causes of bone marrow failure. Management strategies are largely extrapolated from severe AA and include supportive care, immunosuppressive therapy with antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. While outcomes have improved with modern therapy, relapse, treatment failure, and clonal evolution remain challenges. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnostic approach, treatment options, and outcomes of pediatric HAAA, highlighting critical gaps in evidence and the need for prospective studies to guide risk stratification and therapy optimization.
authors: Liao E, Subedi S, Kasper V, Fassel H.

title: When do starch-polyphenol complexes qualify as type 5 resistant starch? A critical evidence framework from molecular assembly to colonic utilization.
abstract: Starch-polyphenol complexes are increasingly explored for modulating starch digestibility, developing low-glycemic-index foods, and improving polyphenol stability and delivery. Some systems have been described as type 5 resistant starch (RS5) or RS5-like based on V-type crystalline signals, increased resistant starch content, or reduced glucose release. However, these outcomes alone are insufficient for RS5 assignment because they may also arise from surface adsorption, non-inclusion networks, substrate shielding, enzyme inhibition by free or released polyphenols, or food-matrix effects. This review critically assesses the evidence required to describe starch-polyphenol systems as V-type starch-polyphenol complexes with demonstrated enzymatic resistance and examines their relationship to the proposed non-lipid extension of RS5. Evidence from molecular assembly, structural characterization, processing-induced rearrangement, resistance to enzymatic digestion, polyphenol release, colonic fermentation, and physiological relevance is integrated. V-type or V-type-like inclusion provides the strongest structural basis for identifying a V-type starch-polyphenol complex, whereas surface-bound complexes, non-inclusion networks and covalent derivatives require different mechanistic descriptions. Mechanistic attribution should include removal and quantification of unbound polyphenols, physical-mixture and washed-complex controls, and enzyme-inhibition kinetics. A tiered evidence framework is proposed to classify these systems as putative RS5, RS5-like complexes, polyphenol-bound resistant starch candidates, enzyme-inhibition-dominated systems, or non-RS mixtures.
journal: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
authors: Su K, Xiao W, Han S, Yang X, Zheng Z.

title: VoroTIDE: Protein domain segmentation through independent hierarchical searches using Voronoi tessellation and physical self-containment
abstract: Protein domains are commonly regarded as structurally separated, functionally relevant, and evolutionarily separable units. Although classification systems may assign different domain boundaries to the same structure, structural separation remains a shared criterion, and many domain parsers assess it through inter-residue distances, contact numbers, or contact densities. However, the Voronoi contact area, which is widely used to study protein-protein interactions and predict contact sites, has seen limited use in domain parsing. There are two potential challenges to this problem. First, unlike in protein-protein interaction, partitions are not known in advance and must be identified before their interface can be evaluated. Second, the contact area depends on fragment size and internal packing, making it difficult to compare candidate partitions. Here, we introduce VoroTIDE (Voronoi-based Two-way Independent Domain Exploration), a domain parser based on all-heavy-atom Voronoi contact areas. By normalizing the contact area for fragment size and internal packing, and incorporating residue hydropathy, we define a pairwise self-containment score F. VoroTIDE applies F in two independent hierarchical searches: top-down recursive splitting until no admissible division remains, and bottom-up merging of elementary structural units until the entire structure becomes a single fragment. Intermediate partitions from both searches are ranked by a global partition quality score G, derived on the same principle. On two CATH-ECOD consensus benchmarks, under balanced evaluation, VoroTIDE achieved the strongest performance among all tested criterion-based parsers and was comparable to Chainsaw, the best-performing deep learning method tested. These results show that the Voronoi-based criterion can yield competitive domain parsing.
authors: Le KQ, Postic G, Angel E, Tahi F.

title: Heimdall SNAREs reveal an ancestral architecture of eukaryotic SNARE complexes
abstract: SNARE proteins are central to eukaryotic cell biology, where they drive membrane fusion by assembling into four-helix bundles that bring opposing membranes into close proximity. Their ubiquitous role in intracellular membrane trafficking raises fundamental questions about their evolutionary origin and the emergence of eukaryotic cellular complexity. Here, we characterize SNARE-like proteins from Heimdallarchaeota, a lineage within the Asgard archaea that is closely related to eukaryotes. We show that a Heimdall SNARE forms a stable homotetrameric four-helix bundle in solution and determine its structure by X-ray crystallography. Strikingly, the Heimdall complex closely resembles eukaryotic SNARE complexes in its overall architecture and core organization, despite being composed of four identical subunits. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal conserved physical features of the bundle alongside distinctive properties of its central 0-layer. These findings demonstrate that the characteristic four-helix architecture of SNAREs predates the emergence of eukaryotic cells and provide structural insight into the evolution of the membrane fusion machinery.
authors: Bentahar I, Yadav D, Hacisuleyman A, Fasshauer D.

title: RARRES2 promotes glycolytic reprogramming and malignant phenotypes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
abstract: Abstract    Background  : Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is a metabolically driven malignancy characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming, with enhanced glycolysis representing a key feature. However, the relationship between glycolytic activation and ccRCC progression remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize glycolytic activity in the ccRCC tumor microenvironment and identify a key biomarker associated with glycolytic reprogramming.  Methods:  Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE156632 and bulk transcriptomic data from the TCGA-KIRC cohort were analyzed. Single-cell analyses were performed to investigate the association between glycolytic activity and tumor epithelial cells within the tumor microenvironment, as well as related intercellular communication patterns. Bulk transcriptomic analyses were used to evaluate the clinical relevance of glycolysis-related features. Machine-learning algorithms combined with SHAP interpretation were applied to identify candidate biomarkers and construct diagnostic models. In vitro experiments were conducted in ccRCC cells to validate the functional role of RARRES2 in glycolysis and malignant progression.  Results:  Tumor epithelial cells exhibited significantly elevated glycolysis scores in the ccRCC microenvironment. Highly glycolytic tumor epithelial cells showed enhanced outgoing signaling, particularly through the MIF-CD74/CXCR4 axis, and were associated with poorer prognosis, increased immune infiltration, and activation of hypoxia-related pathways. A stable five-gene signature was identified from 11 candidate genes, and the SVM classifier achieved the best diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.982). SHAP analysis highlighted RARRES2 as a consistent positive contributor. Functional experiments further demonstrated that RARRES2 knockdown suppressed proliferation, colony formation, and migration of ccRCC cells, reduced glucose consumption, ATP production, and lactate production, and downregulated the mRNA expression of glycolysis-related genes, including HK2, LDHA, PKM2, and GLUT1 (PConclusions:  Multi-omics and machine-learning analyses identified RARRES2 as a glycolysis-associated biomarker in ccRCC and incorporated it into a diagnostic model. In vitro validation furthe demonstrated that RARRES2 contributes to glycolytic reprogramming and malignant phenotypes in ccRCC cells, supporting its potential role in the metabolic progression of ccRCC.
authors: Chen L, Chen Y, Li Y, Li Y, Gao J, Liu X, Ruan X, Ma S, Sharma A, Schmidt-Wolf IG.

title: Construction and validation of a prognostic model for genes associated with myeloid differentiation in liver hepatocellular carcinoma: bulk RNA sequencing combined with Mendelian randomization and single-cell RNA sequencing
abstract: Abstract    Background:  Myeloid cell differentiation is closely related to the tumour microenvironment and tumour progression, but specific genes and mechanisms have not been investigated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Therefore, this study developed a prognostic model for myeloid cell differentiation in HCC.  Methods:  HCC transcriptomic data and myeloid cell differentiation-related genes (MCDRGs) were sourced from public databases. Candidate genes, derived from the intersection of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and MCDRGs, underwent Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify MR feature genes causally linked to HCC. Regression and machine learning analyses then identified prognostic genes and established a risk model. A nomogram integrating the risk score with independent prognostic factors was subsequently constructed and validated. Furthermore, prognostic genes were further investigated through functional enrichment, gene mutation, immune escape correlation, and drug sensitivity analyses. Single-cell analysis revealed their expression on key cell clusters. Finally, expression in clinical samples was verified by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).  Results:  Seven genes (FECH, CDKN2B, CAMK4, NBEAL2, RASGRP4, GPR171, EIF6) were identified as prognostic and used to construct a risk model, with high-risk group (HRG) patients showing significantly worse survival. A validated nomogram integrated T stage and risk score. Enrichment analysis revealed differential pathway enrichment (e.g., complement and coagulation cascades, fatty acid metabolism) between risk groups. Moreover, prognostic genes were shown to be correlated with immune escape, and CDKN2B had the highest mutation frequency. Single-cell analysis identified T cells as key cells and the expression of GPR171 showed an upward-downward-upward trend. Finally, RT-qPCR confirmed significant upregulation of CDKN2B, EIF6, NBEAL2, and FECH (P Conclusions:  This study uncovered 7 myeloid differentiation-related prognostic genes in HCC, offering new insights for its research and treatment.
authors: Lin Z, Xu L, Liu Z, Huang X, Ran Y, Chen D, Zhang W, Huang Z.

title: Computationally guided inhibition of the HIF-1α–CBP/p300 coactivator interface suppresses hypoxia signaling in Caki-1 renal carcinoma cells
abstract: Abstract  Hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) drives adaptive transcription through recruitment of the homologous coactivators CBP and p300, but this interface remains difficult to modulate with small molecules. We combined virtual screening of approximately 250,000 ZINC natural-product-like compounds against the CBP CH1 domain (PDB 1L8C), molecular docking and a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation to identify candidate interface binders. SIHC926 (ZINC000097971950) remained within the predicted pocket, and MM/PBSA analysis produced a negative total binding-free-energy estimate dominated by favourable van der Waals contributions. In a homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence assay using the p300 CH1 domain, SIHC926 inhibited HIF-1α–coactivator association with an IC₅₀ of 1.88 µM, compared with 4.72 µM for YC-1. SIHC926 also inhibited hypoxia-response-element-dependent transcription (IC₅₀ 2.52 µM), reduced Caki-1 cell viability under hypoxia (reported GI₅₀ 2.29 µM), decreased vascular endothelial growth factor secretion, increased Annexin V-positive apoptosis and elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species. These findings nominate SIHC926 as a candidate scaffold for modulating HIF-1 coactivator recruitment. Direct intracellular target engagement, coactivator selectivity, complete compound characterization and validation in additional renal carcinoma models remain necessary.
authors: Gahtani¹ RM, Mesfer Mohammad Al Shahrani1, Zaman¹ GS.

title: Development and validation of a three-marker urine DNA methylation assay complementary to mpMRI for pre-biopsy risk stratification of clinically significant prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract    Background  Current prostate cancer (PCa) diagnostic strategies remain limited in accurately identifying clinically significant disease while avoiding unnecessary biopsy. This study aimed to develop and independently validate a non-invasive urine DNA methylation assay using naturally voided, non-digital rectal examination (non-DRE) urine and assess its complementary value with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥ 2). Methods  The biomarker discovery phase was initiated using microarray-based DNA methylation profiling to screen for tumor-specific alterations, and the candidate regions were subsequently validated by bisulfite-pyrosequencing in the same tissue specimens. Three prioritized markers–  CDYL  ,  EMX2  , and  LRRC4–  were incorporated into a linear target enrichment quantitative methylation-specific PCR assay. Marker-specific thresholds optimized in a training cohort (n = 33) were locked and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of men undergoing biopsy for suspected PCa (n = 97). All participants underwent pre-biopsy mpMRI and standard prostate biopsy. Of the 97 validation patients, 89 were evaluable for combined-modality analysis, while 8 were excluded due to missing mpMRI scans. Results  In the training cohort, the assay achieved 100% sensitivity and 31.6% specificity for csPCa. In the independent validation cohort, standalone assay performance yielded 75.9% sensitivity and 44.2% specificity. Among the 89 patients evaluable for both modalities (49 csPCa, 40 no-csPCa), mpMRI alone (PI-RADS ≥ 4) showed a sensitivity of 69.4%. title: Toward Sensory Homeostasis in Autism: Comparative Evaluation of a Recurrent Signal-to-Memory Hierarchy
abstract: Background:  /Objectives: The signal-to-memory (S2M) hierarchy links Ca²⁺-signal construction and decoding to transcriptional and chromatin changes that may modify subsequent neuronal responsiveness and support sensory homeostasis: adaptation to familiar input while preserving sensitivity to meaningful change. We assessed evidence for its involvement in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) pathogenesis and implications for therapeutic target validation. Methods: The prespecified S2M-44 core was compared with 11 monogenic ASD mouse models, an ASD protein-association network, and 106 schizophrenia-prioritized genes. Exact overlap, molecular association, and functional correspondence were distinguished; broader ASD-gene context and four extension candidates were evaluated separately. Results: Four mouse-model genes matched the core, all transcriptional or chromatin regulators. The protein network represented 27 core proteins, including both IP₃ receptors, ITPR1 and ITPR3, recovered as interactors. Separately reported KDM6B and SETD5 studies demonstrated rescue of downstream neuronal defects, with selected behavioral rescue in the SETD5 model. The schizophrenia set shared one core gene and implicated related signaling operations. Conclusions: These findings strengthen the case for pathogenic involvement of connected S2M operations and prioritize IP₃R-mediated Ca²⁺ release for molecular target validation. Demonstrating target-dependent restoration of signaling and adaptive responsiveness across genetically distinct models would establish a mechanistic foundation for drug discovery.

title: Selective gas adsorption by novel pocket-like supramolecular coordination cages based on sulfonylcalix[4]arene-supported cobalt(II) and nickel(II) tetranuclear clusters and 4,4'-sulfonyldibenzoate linkers.
abstract: Rational design of the nanoporous metal-organic cages (MOCs) with tunable shapes, cavity sizes and adsorption properties is a tremendously important and emerging field, enabling the development of new, highly efficient molecular systems for the separation, storage, and transport of specific target guests. Herein, we report the synthesis and solid-state characterization of two novel isoreticular MOCs displaying a pocket-like shape, resulting from the linkage of two tetranuclear shuttlecock-like [MII4] sub-building units (M = Co and Ni), supported by sulfonylcalix[4]arene (SO2CA) in a cone conformation and four 4,4'-sulfonyldibenzoate linkers. Overall, the presence of 12 -SO2- groups, connected by 16 aryl units, allows the obtained supramolecular assemblies to be considered highly electron-deficient molecules, which are particularly appealing candidates for application as selective adsorbents. These coordination compounds, displaying pores of two distinct types with sizes of ca. 3 Å and 7 Å and BET surface areas of 271 and 409 m2 g-1 for Co- and Ni-based MOCs, respectively, demonstrate selective adsorption capacity towards industrially important gases and CO2, which is observed for the first time for SO2CA-supported MOCs of the pocket-like type.
authors: Volodin PA, Shutilov ID, Ovsyannikov AS, Kovalenko KA, Litvinov IA, Ivshin KA, Gubaidullin AT, Solovieva SE, Fedin VP, Antipin IS.

title: Excitonic-engineered bismuth oxyhalide nanosheets with superior performance for environmental photocatalysis.
abstract: The escalating severity of global environmental pollution and energy crises demands innovative and sustainable remediation technologies. Solar-driven photocatalysis offers a green solution, and bismuth oxyhalide (BiOX, X = Cl, Br, I) nanosheets have emerged as promising candidates because of their layered structure, tunable band gaps, and internal electric fields. This review summarizes recent progress in excitonic engineering of BiOX nanosheets, including synthesis, characterization, pollutant removal performance, and structure-property relationships. We show that surface asymmetry weakens excitonic effects and switches O2 activation from 1O2 to ˙O2-, enabling efficient organic synthesis. Surface boronizing induces staggered band alignment and oxygen vacancies for selective NO oxidation to nitrate. Homogeneous B doping manipulates bulk excitons and surface defects for selective, ultrastable CO2 photoreduction, while van der Waals gap engineering reduces exciton binding energy and creates active defect sites for pure-water CO2-to-CO conversion. Nitrogen doping enables spatial charge separation for simultaneous CO and HClO production from seawater. Moiré superlattice construction destabilizes surface Bi-Cl bonds and reinforces interlayer coupling for methane chlorination. Ag single-atom modification creates Cl-Ag1-Cl sites for superior O2 activation and NO oxidation. Finally, we discuss challenges and opportunities for practical pollution control and environmental remediation.
authors: Guo F, Liao M, Song Q, Li H.

title: Microbiome evidence-guided construction of a defined microbial consortium for light-aroma Baijiu fermentation and flavor development.
abstract: Natural fermentation systems harbor microbial resources, but translating microbiome information into cultivable and controllable defined communities remains challenging. We integrated 74 metagenomic datasets from light-aroma Baijiu-associated Daqu and fermented grains with metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) functional profiles and independent 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon time series to propose four candidate functional roles: substrate conversion, acid/acyl-precursor formation, alcoholic fermentation, and aroma formation. Metagenomic profiling revealed community heterogeneity, whereas MAG analysis showed widespread genetic potential for starch conversion and lactic- and acetic-acid-related metabolism. Amplicon data revealed genus-level temporal distributions of Bacillus, Weissella, Wickerhamomyces, and Saccharomyces. Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, Weissella confusa, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Wickerhamomyces anomalus were selected from the available laboratory culture collection as candidate representatives of these roles. A three-factor Box-Behnken design optimized the two bacterial inoculum volumes and the combined yeast volume, with the yeast ratio fixed at 1:1 (v/v). For 500 g of substrate, inoculation volumes were 7 mL for B. amyloliquefaciens, 20 mL for W. confusa, 41 mL for S. cerevisiae, and 41 mL for W. anomalus, yielding 2.28 ± 0.12 g/L ethyl acetate (HPLC). During 28 d of solid-state fermentation, starch, reducing sugars, acidity, and volatile profiles changed, with 51 volatile compounds detected. The final base Baijiu contained 33 volatile compounds, including 13 with odor activity values (OAVs) >1, of which 11 were also detected by gas chromatography-olfactometry (GC-O). These findings support a role-guided route from natural fermentation microbiome evidence to a defined consortium with measurable fermentation and flavor phenotypes.
authors: Li H, Zhang X, Liu J, Chen X, Liao B, Zhang Y, Li W, Sun B, Li X.

title: Nocardioides candidus sp. nov. and Sphingomonas crocea sp. nov., isolated from soil of Inwang Mountain.
abstract: Two novel strains, designated MH1T and IW22T, were isolated from soil of Inwang Mountain, Seoul, Republic of Korea. The nearly complete 16S rRNA gene sequences of strains MH1T and IW22T were 1,521 and 1,485 bp, respectively. Strain MH1T showed the highest sequence similarity to Nocardioides pelophilus THG-T63T (98.22%), Nocardioides stalactiti 1.0914T (98.20%) and Nocardioides humilatus BN130099T (98.02%). Strain IW22T showed the highest similarity to Sphingomonas spermidinifaciens 9 NM-10T (97.94%), Sphingomonas baiyangensis L-1-4 w-11T (97.94%) and Sphingomonas yantingensis 1007T (97.58%). Phylogenomic analysis based on 81 conserved core genes and average amino acid identity supported the placement of the two strains within the genera Nocardioides and Sphingomonas, respectively. The average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values between the novel strains and their closest relatives were below the species delineation thresholds. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the presence of distinct biosynthetic gene clusters, including terpene, polyketide and peptide-associated clusters, suggesting potential ecological adaptation to soil environments. The DNA G+C contents of strains MH1T and IW22T were 71.5 and 64.5 mol%, respectively. The major fatty acids of strain MH1T were iso-C16 : 0 and C18 : 1  ω9c, whereas those of strain IW22T were C16 : 0, C18 : 1  ω7c and summed feature 3 (C16 : 1  ω6c and/or C16 : 1  ω7c). Based on polyphasic taxonomic evidence, strains MH1T and IW22T represent novel species of the genera Nocardioides and Sphingomonas, respectively, for which the names Nocardioides candidus sp. nov. and Sphingomonas crocea sp. nov. are proposed.
journal: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology

title: Pasteurella vulneris sp. nov., mainly obtained from large cats.
abstract: Twenty-four strains mainly from lions, tigers and human wounds inflicted by these animals and strains from birds, elephants and a bite wound in a calf were investigated. As a consequence, the new species Pasteurella vulneris is proposed based on the phenotypic and genotypic similarity of strains, as well as differences to the other species of the genus. Monophyly was confirmed by partial 16S rRNA and rpoB gene sequence comparisons. The intra-species identity of P. vulneris 16S rRNA gene sequences was 99-100%, and the identity to strains of Pasteurella multocida was 99% or less. The identity to taxon 46-like of Bisgaard was 96-98%, to taxon 46 of Bisgaard 97-98%, and identities to Pasteurella stomatis, Pasteurella dagmatis, Pasteurella canis and Pasteurella oralis were within the range of 95-97%. The whole genomic sequences of ten strains obtained in a previously published study and analysed by the type strain genome server showed the highest digital DNA-DNA hybridization of 31% to the genome of the type strain of P. multocida and 59-93% between strains of P. vulneris. Average nucleotide identity was 95-98% between members of the new species with 87% to the type strain of P. multocida. Colonies of P. vulneris on bovine blood agar were regular, smooth, convex, opaque, greyish, non-haemolytic and circular after 24 h of incubation at 37 °C. Mucoid colonies are observed for some strains. Analysis of isolates by MALDI-TOF MS clustered them close together and separated them from other Pasteurella species, allowing discrimination and making this the method of choice for identification. The G+C content of the type strain HIM 1004-6 T isolated from a chipmunk (=Schmid351T=CCUG 77952T=DSM 118578T) is 40.78 mol%, calculated from the whole genome.
journal: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology
authors: Christensen H, Larsen J, Kuhnert P, Angen Ø, Henton MM, Buys A, Foggin C, Bisgaard M.

title: Carbon-Fixation Potential in Zhuqueibacterota from a Central Indian Ridge Hydrothermal Vent Extends beyond Zhuqueibacterales, Tracking Habitat Rather Than Lineage
abstract: Abstract  Background Deep-sea hydrothermal vent fields are biological hotspots sustained by chemosynthetic primary production rather than photosynthesis. The Onnuri Vent Field (OVF), discovered in 2018 on the Central Indian Ridge, exhibits an unusual diffuse-flow regime and supports a distinct faunal community, yet its microbial contributors to primary production remain incompletely characterized. Zhuqueibacterota (formerly Ca. KSB1) is an uncultured bacterial phylum long considered strictly heterotrophic, although a recent study proposed that a single order within this phylum, Zhuqueibacterales, can perform carbon fixation via the Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle. Because CBB-competent Zhuqueibacterales had not previously been reported from deep-sea hydrothermal vents, whether Zhuqueibacterota inhabiting the OVF belong to this order, and whether their capacity for carbon fixation extends to this environment, remained unexamined. Results Comparative shotgun metagenomic analysis of sediment from the OVF and two co-located chimney-type vent fields, Edmond and Solitaire, revealed a prokaryotic community at the OVF marked by the near-absence of Epsilonproteobacteria, the typically dominant chemolithoautotrophic primary producers at hydrothermal vents. Metagenome-assembled genome analysis identified Zhuqueibacterota as a lineage with high relative abundance unique to the OVF, encoding the complete gene set for carbon fixation via non-canonical CBB cycle variants. Zhuqueibacterota-derived RuBisCO sequences accounted for 7.2% of total RbcL sequences at the OVF, the second-largest contribution after Gammaproteobacteria. This carbon-fixing genome belonged to Oceanimicrobiales rather than Zhuqueibacterales, the order previously reported as the sole lineage capable of the CBB cycle. Phylogenetic analysis showed that possession of Form I RuBisCO, and thus the potential for active CBB cycle operation, tracked with isolation habitat rather than taxonomic lineage across the phylum, a pattern corroborated by global mapping of Zhuqueibacterota-derived RbcL sequences against environmental metagenomes. Conclusions The identification of a carbon-fixing Zhuqueibacterota genome within Oceanimicrobiales, rather than the previously implicated Zhuqueibacterales, demonstrates that CBB cycle capacity within this phylum cannot be inferred from order-level taxonomy alone. Instead, the association between Form I RuBisCO possession and isolation habitat, corroborated by global metagenomic mapping, indicates that habitat exerts a stronger influence on carbon-fixation potential than phylogenetic lineage in Zhuqueibacterota. These findings identify Zhuqueibacterota as an unrecognized contributor to carbon fixation in deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems.
authors: Park M, Kim YJ, Lee J, Yu J, Han G, Lee J, Kwon KK.

title: Homology-aware average nucleotide identity estimation at scale with TurboANI
abstract: Here we introduce TurboANI, a fast homology-aware average nucleotide identity (ANI) estimation algorithm that implements the seed-chain-quasi-alignment scheme using SIMD seeding, compact indexing, lightweight chaining, and cache-friendly bitset sliding minwise hashing, achieving up to ~40,000-fold speedup over the alignment-based ANI algorithm with near-perfect agreement. TurboANI is also >40-fold faster than the state-of-the-art FastANI and ten-fold faster than skani while maintaining better accuracy. In the sensitive mode, it has a ten-fold higher true-ANI recovery rate than skani.
authors: Zhao J, McDonald D, Patel L, Wang C, Gonzalez A, Knight R.

title: The leader-trailer helix of pre-16S rRNA increases the speed and efficiency of 30S subunit biogenesis in Escherichia coli.
abstract: Leader-trailer helices of precursor rRNAs are ubiquitous in bacteria and archaea and are crucial for ribosome biogenesis in Escherichia coli. Here, using an orthogonal ribosome system, we investigate whether an engineered protein-aptamer bridge can functionally substitute for the leader-trailer helix (hLT) of pre-16S rRNA in E. coli. We find that components of such a bridge, and even the 3' aptamer array component alone, can increase 30S subunit formation in the absence of hLT. Loss of RNase R or mutations of the degradosome (RNase E, PNPase, or RhlB) also boost 30S biogenesis in the absence of hLT. Quantification of orthogonal 16S rRNA suggests that these alterations act by stabilizing pre-16S rRNA molecules lacking the leader or trailer, giving sufficient time for rRNA folding to occur. In all cases, 16S rRNA level correlates with 30S subunit activity; however, the active fraction of 30S particles formed is substantially higher in the presence of hLT than in its absence. Notably, the complete set of aptamer-bridge components can fully stabilize pre-16S rRNA lacking hLT but fails to increase the active fraction of 30S particles formed. These findings suggest that hLT enhances both the speed and efficiency of 30S subunit formation in the cell.
authors: Warner BR, Fredrick K.

title: Comparative evaluation of molecular assays for detection of Orientia tsutsugamushi in patients with acute febrile illness in Western Odisha
abstract: Abstract  Scrub typhus is an important cause of acute febrile illness in India, but diagnosis may be difficult because molecular detection of Orientia tsutsugamushi and the host antibody response occur over different phases of infection. We compared four molecular assays targeting three genomic regions in 71 hospitalized patients with acute undifferentiated fever in Western Odisha. All patients were tested by IgM ELISA and by TSA-56 quantitative PCR (qPCR), 16S rRNA qPCR, 16S rRNA conventional PCR (cPCR), and GroEL cPCR. Using IgM ELISA as the reference comparator, 16S rRNA qPCR showed the strongest overall performance, with 78.6% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, 88.7% accuracy and substantial agreement (κ = 0.758). TSA-56 qPCR showed 67.9% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, 84.5% accuracy and κ = 0.661. GroEL cPCR showed 78.6% sensitivity, 81.4% specificity, 80.3% accuracy and κ = 0.592, whereas 16S rRNA cPCR had the lowest sensitivity (50.0%), accuracy (74.6%) and agreement (κ = 0.434). Comparative ROC analysis showed the highest AUC for 16S rRNA qPCR (0.870), followed by TSA-56 qPCR (0.816), GroEL cPCR (0.800) and 16S rRNA cPCR (0.703). These findings suggest that real-time PCR, particularly 16S rRNA qPCR, may provide useful complementary information to serology for scrub typhus detection. The results should be interpreted as agreement with an IgM ELISA comparator rather than definitive diagnostic accuracy.
authors: Panda RK, Dash PM, Rao BM, Mohanty SR, Behera AK.

title: Comparative analysis of gut and skin microbiota from the coastal and non-coastal populations in Tamil Nadu using 16S rRNA gene sequencing: a pilot study.
abstract: BackgroundThe human gut and skin microbiota play a vital role in maintaining physiological balance and immune function. Factors such as age, diet, geography, and genetic factors influence their composition, and disruptions can contribute to metabolic alterations and chronic diseases. Coastal populations are exposed to environmental pollutants and experience disrupted gut microbial balance, impaired epithelial barrier integrity, and possibly dysbiosis-associated inflammatory responses. In this study, we aim to analyze microbiome diversity in coastal and non-coastal populations of Tamil Nadu, India, using 16S rRNA sequencing.MethodsFecal and skin swab samples were collected from 75 participants, 57 from coastal regions and 18 from non-coastal regions. DNA was extracted, and using the Illumina MiSeq platform, the 16S rRNA sequencing was performed. The alpha and beta diversity analyses compared the fecal and skin microbiota diversity and composition.ResultsThe study revealed that Firmicutes dominated the gut microbiota in both coastal and non-coastal groups, with higher abundances of Bacilli and Clostridia in the coastal group. In skin swabs, Firmicutes and Proteobacteria were predominant, with different clustering patterns observed in coastal samples. Beta diversity analyses revealed overlapping but distinct microbial communities between the two groups.ConclusionThis pilot study highlights differences in gut and skin microbiota between coastal and non-coastal populations. However, further study with a larger sample size is required to better understand the impact of environmental exposures on human health.
authors: Thangamani RA, Jayachandran J, Jayavel A, Ponnaiya SKM, Mitra A, Shanmugam P, Radhakrishnan A, Banerjee A, Duttaroy AK.

title: Prevalence, molecular characterization, and factors associated with hemotropic Mycoplasma infection in domestic cats (Felis catus) in the semi-arid region of Paraíba, Brazil.
abstract: Hemotropic mycoplasmas are bacteria that parasitize the surface of erythrocytes and may cause clinical alterations of varying severity in felines. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, identify factors associated with infection, and molecularly characterize the circulating species in cats from the semi-arid region of Paraíba, Brazil. A total of 354 cats from the municipality of Sousa were evaluated through clinical and epidemiological assessment and blood sampling for molecular detection of 'Candidatus Mycoplasma haemominutum' (CMhm), Mycoplasma haemofelis (Mhf), and 'Candidatus Mycoplasma turicense' (CMt) by PCR targeting the 16S rRNA gene. Selected samples were subjected to Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. The overall prevalence of hemotropic mycoplasmas was 36.2% (128/354), with CMhm being the most frequent (31.4%), followed by Mhf (4.8%) and CMt (3.7%); coinfection with CMhm and Mhf was observed in 3.7% of the animals. In the multivariable analysis, age over four years and the presence of lymph node abnormalities were identified as factors associated with positivity. BLASTn showed 99.72-100% sequence identity; phylogenetic analysis grouped five sequences with CMhm references and one with CMt references, while the 16S rRNA fragment could not distinguish M. haemofelis from M. haemocanis. These findings expand the knowledge of the molecular epidemiology of these agents in the semi-arid region of Paraíba and reinforce the importance of their investigation in routine diagnostics, as well as the need for further studies on their genetic diversity, transmission, and clinical relevance.

title: Tenacibaculum profundi sp. nov., Tenacibaculum aquaeponti sp. nov. and Tenacibaculum profundicola sp. nov. isolated from seawater samples of the western Pacific Ocean.
abstract: Three Gram-staining-negative, rod-shaped, yellow-pigmented, strictly aerobic bacterial strains, designated C7A-26P2T, ZS6-P6T and C14-20M1T, were isolated from seawater samples of the western Pacific Ocean. All strains were able to grow in the presence of 1.0-6.0% NaCl, at pH 6.0-8.0 and at 10-37 °C. Phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences indicated these strains belong to the genus Tenacibaculum, with strain C7A-26P2T closest to Tenacibaculum xiamenense Wj-1T (97.9% sequence similarity), ZS6-P6T closest to Tenacibaculum jejuense CNURIC013T (98.7%) and C14-20M1T closest to Tenacibaculum mesophilum NBRC 16307T (96.4%). Genome sizes were 3.8 Mb (G+C content 30.8 mol%) for C7A-26P2T, 4.0 Mb (G+C content 30.1 mol%) for ZS6-P6T and 4.6 Mb (G+C content 33.0 mol%) for C14-20M1T, with average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values with other Tenacibaculum species below 87.9 and 34.8%, respectively. Cellular fatty acid profiles identified C15 : 0 iso, summed feature 3 (C16 : 1  ω7c/C16 : 1 ω6c), C18 : 0 and C15 : 1 iso G as the predominant fatty acids for C7A-26P2T; summed feature 3 and C16 : 0 as the major fatty acids for ZS6-P6T; and C15 : 0 iso and summed feature 3 as the major fatty acids for C14-20M1T. The respiratory quinone detected was MK-6 for all strains. The major polar lipids of these three strains were phosphatidylethanolamine, glycolipid, aminolipid and phospholipid. Based on phenotypic, chemotaxonomic and genomic characteristics, strains C7A-26P2T, ZS6-P6T and C14-20M1T were identified as three novel species within the genus Tenacibaculum, for which the names Tenacibaculum profundi sp. nov., Tenacibaculum aquaeponti sp. nov. and Tenacibaculum profundicola sp. nov. are proposed; the type strains are C7A-26P2T (=MCCC M21464T=NBRC 117451T), ZS6-P6T (=MCCC M21515T=NBRC 117453T) and C14-20M1T (=MCCC M24271T=NBRC 117450T), respectively.

title: An integrated analytical strategy combining UPLC-QTOF-MS-based metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing to explore the mechanism of Shenqi Jieyu decoction in coronary heart disease complicated by depression in ApoE<sup>-/-</sup> mice.
abstract: Coronary heart disease combined with depression (dual-heart disorder) exhibits high morbidity and poor prognosis, lacking safe unified therapeutic agents. Shenqi Jieyu Decoction (SQJY) relieves depressive and cardiovascular symptoms in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) patients, yet its underlying multiple potential mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an ApoE-/- mouse model of dual-heart disorder was induced via high-fat diet combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Behavioral testing, aortic pathological staining, hippocampal neurochemistry, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics of serum and cecal contents were integrated with 16S rRNA sequencing, establishing an integrated multi-omics workflow to examine the potential modulatory effects of SQJY and to explore its possible mechanism. Behavioral and pathological assays indicated that SQJY alleviated atherosclerosis and depression-like phenotypes, elevated hippocampal 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), dopamine (DA) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and suppressed neuroinflammatory cytokines. 16S sequencing suggested SQJY remodeled dysregulated gut microbiota toward a more balanced profile. Metabolomics identified disturbed sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism as important metabolic signatures that H-SQJY group corrected more extensively in cecal content (68 of 265 metabolites) than in serum (8 of 103). Phylogenetic Investigation of Communities by Reconstruction of Unobserved States 2 (PICRUSt2)-based prediction of microbial functions was integrated, and Spearman correlation analysis showed significant associations between predicted microbial functions, differential gut microbes and lipid metabolites. Collectively, SQJY showed concurrent potential cardioprotective and antidepressant effects, possibly through restoring gut microbial homeostasis and modulating lipid metabolic disorders. These correlative and predicted findings provide preliminary evidence for the potential application of SQJY in dual-heart disorder.

title: EMtrace: offline nanopore metagenomics on a laptop for rapid viral diagnostics, genome recovery and 16S profiling
abstract: Nanopore sequencers produce reads within minutes, but metagenomic analysis remains challenging where internet access is limited, data are sensitive or computing resources are modest. EMtrace is an offline pipeline that runs on a laptop during sequencing: it classifies MinKNOW reads, estimates taxon abundance by expectation-maximization (EM) and assembles reference-based consensus genomes. We benchmarked it against five virome and four 16S rRNA tools on simulated, mock-community and clinical data. On field isolates and 16 SARS-CoV-2 clinical samples, EMtrace had the highest species-level F1 score (1.00 and 0.97) and one false-positive species, against 3-7 for the comparators. It recovered divergent viruses as completely as ViMOP, and low-titre field libraries more completely, at ≥99.7% identity. In replayed runs, it identified the target virus in the first 4,000-read batch (5-13 min). With a shared 16S reference, EMtrace reported two to three times fewer false-positive species than Emu.

title: Clinical Manifestations and Diagnostic Challenges of Human Taeniasis in a Low-Prevalence Setting: An Eight-Case Series from South Korea, 2019-2025.
abstract: In South Korea, a low-prevalence setting for taeniasis, the clinical recognition of this infection remains challenging. Eight patients diagnosed with taeniasis at Chosun University Hospital between January 2019 and July 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical characteristics, exposure history, and results from stool microscopy, serologic testing, and molecular analyses, including multiplex polymerase chain reaction and 18S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequencing, were analyzed to evaluate clinical presentation and diagnostic performance in routine clinical practice. Clinical manifestations were generally mild and nonspecific, and most patients sought medical attention only after spontaneously passing proglottids. A history of consuming raw or undercooked beef was the most common route of exposure. Conventional diagnostic methods, including stool microscopy and serological testing, had limited utility, with stool microscopy successfully used to detect Taenia eggs in only two of six tested patients. Additional molecular analyses in the present study, including multiplex polymerase chain reaction and 18S rRNA sequencing, improved diagnostic confirmation and provided supportive phylogenetic evidence for species relatedness within the genus Taenia, including clustering of seven isolates near Taenia saginata reference sequences and one isolate near Taenia asiatica reference sequences. However, these approaches still lacked sufficient resolution for reliable species-level differentiation. These findings highlight that in low-prevalence settings, the major diagnostic challenge is no longer detecting taeniasis itself but reliably differentiating species, particularly excluding Taenia solium, which may affect decisions regarding further evaluation for cysticercosis or neurocysticercosis.

title: Metabolite-Mediated Rhizosphere-Endosphere Microbiome Shapes Genotype-Dependent Cadmium Accumulation via Coupled Chemical Immobilization and Microbial Detoxification.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) contamination threatens food safety, yet genotype-dependent Cd accumulation at the soil-root interface remains poorly understood. We integrated physiological profiling, metabolomics, density functional theory (DFT), and 16S rRNA sequencing to compare two amaranth cultivars, Quanhong (QH, low-Cd) and Liuye (LY, high-Cd). QH showed greater shoot biomass (6.84 g/plant) and stronger Cd exclusion (root/shoot Cd: 0.12/0.08 mg/kg), whereas LY developed a larger root system (1.42 vs 0.71 g/plant) and accumulated more Cd (0.26/0.16 mg/kg). QH promoted conversion of exchangeable Cd into stable residual fractions and enriched humic-like dissolved organic matter and 9-Oxo-ODE, which showed strong predicted Cd2+ binding (-22.34 kcal/mol), supporting its potential role in Cd immobilization. QH showed stronger host-associated microbial selection, enriching Bacillus and Streptomyces associated with sulfur metabolism and thiol-mediated metal sequestration, together with greater diversity and stability of root endophytes. These findings indicate coordinated chemical and microbial regulation contributing to the low-Cd phenotype of QH.
